verses.text:
कच्चिन्न किंचिद् भरते कुमारे प्रियदर्शने।
शत्रुघ्ने वा महासत्त्वे मातृणां वा ममाशुभम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I hope no offence has been committed by me against Prince Bharata of pleasing aspect or Śatrughna possessing great valour or against my mothers. (14)

verses.text:
अतोषयन् महाराजमकुर्वन् वा पितुर्वचः।
मुहूर्तमपि नेच्छेयं जीवितुं कुपिते नृपे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Unable to please the Emperor or failing to do my father’s bidding and in the event of His Majesty being angry with me I would not survive even for an hour or so. (15)

verses.text:
यतोमूलं नरः पश्येत् प्रादुर्भावमिहात्मनः।
कथं तस्मिन् न वर्तेत प्रत्यक्षे सति दैवते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How can a man fail to be devoted to his father, his veritable and living deity, to whom he owes his own birth in this world? (16)

verses.text:
कच्चित्ते परुषं किंचिदभिमानात् पिता मम।
उक्तो भवत्या रोषेण येनास्य लुलितं मनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Or, has my father been told by you through vanity or anger a harsh word, by which his heart has been stung to the quick? (17 )

verses.text:
एतदाचक्ष्व मे देवि तत्त्वेन परिपृच्छतः।
किंनिमित्तमपूर्वोऽयं विकारो मनुजाधिपे॥ १८॥
verses.m: “What is this unprecedented agitation in the mind of the Emperor due to? Pray, point this out correctly to me, inquisitive as I am, O godly lady?” (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी राघवेण महात्मना।
उवाचेदं सुनिर्लज्जा धृष्टमात्महितं वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Questioned thus by the high-souled Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Kaikeyī, for her part, who had grown utterly impudent, made the following bold reply, which was calculated to advance her own interest : (19)

verses.text:
न राजा कुपितो राम व्यसनं नास्य किंचन।
किंचिन्मनोगतं त्वस्य त्वद्भयान्नानुभाषते॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The king is neither angry nor is there any anguish troubling him, O Rāma ! There is, however, something in his mind, which he is not disclosing to you for fear of paining you. (20)

verses.text:
प्रियं त्वामप्रियं वक्तुं वाणी नास्य प्रवर्तते।
तदवश्यं त्वया कार्यं यदनेनाश्रुतं मम॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Words do not proceed from his mouth to tell you, his darling, something disagreeable to you. That which has been promised by him to me must, however, be implemented by you. (21)

verses.text:
एष मह्यं वरं दत्त्वा पुरा मामभिपूज्य च।
स पश्चात् तप्यते राजा यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having granted me a boon in the past and thereby honoured me, this illustrious monarch now repents in the same way as any other common man. (22)

verses.text:
अतिसृज्य ददानीति वरं मम विशाम्पतिः।
स निरर्थं गतजले सेतुं बन्धितुमिच्छति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Having given a pledge to me in the words ‘I grant you a boon’ the celebrated monarch seeks in vain to construct a dam across a stream whose water has already flown. (23)

verses.text:
धर्ममूलमिदं राम विदितं च सतामपि।
तत् सत्यं न त्यजेद् राजा कुपितस्त्वत्कृते यथा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Truth is the root of piety—this is a fact well-known even to the righteous, O Rāma ! Beware lest the king should forsake that truth, angry as he is with me for your sake. (24)

verses.text:
यदि तद् वक्ष्यते राजा शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम्।
करिष्यसि ततः सर्वमाख्यास्यामि पुनस्त्वहम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “If you undertake to implement whatever the king says, whether it is good or evil for you, in that case, of course, I shall reiterate everything to you. (25)

verses.text:
यदि त्वभिहितं राज्ञा त्वयि तन्न विपत्स्यते।
ततोऽहमभिधास्यामि न ह्येष त्वयि वक्ष्यति॥ २६॥
verses.m: “In case that which has been uttered by the king does not fall flat on you, then alone I shall give it out to you. In no case is he going to open his lips before you.” (26)

verses.text:
एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्या समुदाहृतम्।
उवाच व्यथितो रामस्तां देवीं नृपसंनिधौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: Distressed to hear the afore-mentioned words uttered by Kaikeyī, Śrī Rāma for his part spoke as follows to the said queen in the presence of the Emperor : (27)

verses.text:
अहो धिङ् नार्हसे देवि वक्तुं मामीदृशं वचः।
अहं हि वचनाद् राज्ञः पतेयमपि पावके॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Oh ! how shameful it is for me to hear such words expressing doubt about my devotion to my father ! You ought not to speak such words to me, O glorious lady ! At the bidding of my father I am actually prepared to leap into fire. (28)

verses.text:
भक्षयेयं विषं तीक्ष्णं पतेयमपि चार्णवे।
नियुक्तो गुरुणा पित्रा नृपेण च हितेन च॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Commanded by the Emperor, who is my teacher, father and friend, all in one, I might as well swallow deadly poison and take a plunge into the ocean. (29)

verses.text:
तद् ब्रूहि वचनं देवि राज्ञो यदभिकांक्षितम्।
करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामो द्विर्नाभिभाषते॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, speak out what you have got to say, O glorious lady ! I shall do that which is coveted by the king and give my plighted word for it. Know that Rāma does not speak twice.” (30)

verses.text:
तमार्जवसमायुक्तमनार्या सत्यवादिनम्।
उवाच रामं कैकेयी वचनं भृशदारुणम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: To the said Śrī Rāma, who always spoke the truth and was richly adorned with guilelessness, the ignoble Kaikeyī addressed the following exceptionally cruel words : (31)

verses.text:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे पित्रा ते मम राघव।
रक्षितेन वरौ दत्तौ सशल्येन महारणे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Formerly in the course of a conflict between gods and demons, O scion of Raghu, a couple of boons were granted to me by your father, who had been rescued by me in a major battle when a shaft which remained dug into his body and was extracted afterwards by me. (32)

verses.text:
तत्र मे याचितो राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्।
गमनं दण्डकारण्ये तव चाद्यैव राघव॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “As against those boons the king was solicited by me this very day to acquiesce in the installation as Prince Regent of Bharata and your departure to the Daṇḍaka forest, O scion of Raghu ! (33)

verses.text:
यदि सत्यप्रतिज्ञं त्वं पितरं कर्तुमिच्छसि।
आत्मानं च नरश्रेष्ठ मम वाक्यमिदं शृणु॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “If you want to prove your father and yourself to be true to your promises, O jewel among men, please listen to the following exhortation of mine: (34)

verses.text:
संनिदेशे पितुस्तिष्ठ यथानेन प्रतिश्रुतम्।
त्वयारण्यं प्रवेष्टव्यं नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Be faithful to the word of your father: as promised by him, you ought to retire to the woods for nine years and five. (35)

verses.text:
भरतश्चाभिषिच्येत यदेतदभिषेचनम्।
त्वदर्थे विहितं राज्ञा तेन सर्वेण राघव॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “And let Bharata be consecrated with all the material that has been got together by the king for your consecration, O scion of Raghu ! (36)

verses.text:
सप्त सप्त च वर्षाणि दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः।
अभिषेकमिदं त्यक्त्वा जटाचीरधरो भव॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Forgoing the forthcoming installation and ensconced in the Daṇḍaka forest, wear matted locks and the bark of trees for seven and seven years. (37)

verses.text:
भरतः कोसलपतेः प्रशास्तु वसुधामिमाम्।
नानारत्नसमाकीर्णां सवाजिरथसंकुलाम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Let Bharata rule with an iron hand over this globe which is owned by Daśaratha, the king of Ayodhyā, and is full of precious stones of various kinds and crowded with chariots driven by horses. (38)

verses.text:
एतेन त्वां नरेन्द्रोऽयं कारुण्येन समाप्लुतः।
शोकैः संक्लिष्टवदनो न शक्नोति निरीक्षितुम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Overwhelmed with compassion for you due to this circumstance of having granted a couple of boons in my favour, this monarch cannot even gaze at you, his face withered from grief. (39)

verses.text:
एतत् कुरु नरेन्द्रस्य वचनं रघुनन्दन।
सत्येन महता राम तारयस्व नरेश्वरम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Implement this pledge of the Emperor, O delight of the Raghus ! By vindicating his outstanding veracity, pray, deliver the Emperor from a delicate situation.” (40)

verses.text:
इतीव तस्यां परुषं वदन्त्यां
न चैव रामः प्रविवेश शोकम्।
प्रविव्यथे चापि महानुभावो
राजा च पुत्रव्यसनाभितप्तः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Even though Kaikeyī spoke unkindly as above, Śrī Rāma did not yield to grief at all. The king, however, even though he was possessed of great strength of mind, felt sore distressed, afflicted as he was by the agony of impending separation from his dear son. (41)

verses.text:
तदप्रियममित्रघ्नो वचनं मरणोपमम्।
श्रुत्वा न विव्यथे रामः कैकेयीं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the destroyer of his enemies, did not feel distressed to hear that message, which was so unpleasant to hear and was like death itself, and spoke to Kaikeyī as follows : (1)

verses.text:
एवमस्तु गमिष्यामि वनं वस्तुमहं त्वितः।
जटाचीरधरो राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Amen ! Honouring the promise made by the king and wearing matted locks and the bark of trees, I will undoubtedly proceed from Ayodhyā to the forest to take up my abode there. (2)

verses.text:
इदं तु ज्ञातुमिच्छामि किमर्थं मां महीपतिः।
नाभिनन्दति दुर्धर्षो यथापूर्वमरिंदमः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I, however, desire to know wherefore His Majesty, who is capable of chastising his enemies and is himself hard to assail, does not welcome me as before. (3)

verses.text:
मन्युर्न च त्वया कार्यो देवि ब्रूमि तवाग्रतः।
यास्यामि भव सुप्रीता वनं चीरजटाधरः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Nor should displeasure be shown by you to me, O queen, because I am putting this question to you. Wearing the bark of trees and matted locks, I will certainly proceed to the forest. Be fully pleased with me. (4)

verses.text:
हितेन गुरुणा पित्रा कृतज्ञेन नृपेण च।
नियुज्यमानो विस्रब्धः किं न कुर्यामहं प्रियम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Enjoined by the Emperor, who is my friend, preceptor and father, all in one, and appreciates a service done to himself, what kindly act shall I not do unhesitatingly to him? (5)

verses.text:
अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहते मम।
स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “One mental anguish, however, galls my heart, viz., that His Majesty should not personally speak to me about Bharata’s installation. (6)

verses.text:
अहं हि सीतां राज्यं च प्राणानिष्टान् धनानि च।
हृष्टो भ्रात्रे स्वयं दद्यां भरताया प्रचोदितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “For, commanded by you, I would myself joyfully part with, in favour of Bharata, not only the kingdom of Ayodhyā and my personal property but even Sītā, my wedded wife, nay, my beloved life itself. (7)

verses.text:
किं पुनर्मनुजेन्द्रेण स्वयं पित्रा प्रचोदितः।
तव च प्रियकामार्थं प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “How much more gladly shall I part with all these when enjoined by my father, the Emperor himself, and that too with intent to please you and in order to honour the pledge given by him to you? (8)

verses.text:
तथाश्वासय ह्रीमन्तं किं त्विदं यन्महीपतिः।
वसुधासक्तनयनो मन्दमश्रूणि मुञ्चति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Therefore, reassure to that effect the bashful monarch. But why should it be that the Emperor gently sheds tears with his eyes riveted on the ground? (9)

verses.text:
गच्छन्तु चैवानयितुं दूताः शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः।
भरतं मातुलकुलादद्यैव नृपशासनात्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Nay, let messengers proceed this very day on horses possessing a swift speed under orders of the king in order to bring Bharata from his maternal uncle’s home.(10)

verses.text:
दण्डकारण्यमेषोऽहं गच्छाम्येव हि सत्वरः।
अविचार्य पितुर्वाक्यं समा वस्तुं चतुर्दश॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Here do I actually proceed with quick steps without fail to the Daṇḍaka forest in order to live there for fourteen years, without calling in question the command of my father.” (11)

verses.text:
सा हृष्टा तस्य तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा रामस्य कैकयी।
प्रस्थानं श्रद्दधाना सा त्वरयामास राघवम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: The wicked Kaikeyī felt rejoiced to hear that reply of Śrī Rāma. Confident of his departure to the forest, she urged in the following words Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, to look sharp : (12)

verses.text:
एवं भवतु यास्यन्ति दूताः शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः।
भरतं मातुलकुलादिहावर्तयितुं नराः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Let it be so ! Messengers and other men shall depart on horses possessing a swift speed to bring back Bharata here from his maternal uncle’s abode. (13)

verses.text:
तव त्वहं क्षमं मन्ये नोत्सुकस्य विलम्बनम्।
राम तस्मादितः शीघ्रं वनं त्वं गन्तुमर्हसि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I do not in any case deem it advisable for you to tarry any longer, keen as you are to depart for the woods, O Rāma ! Therefore you ought to proceed quickly to the forest from this place. (14)

verses.text:
व्रीडान्वितः स्वयं यच्च नृपस्त्वां नाभिभाषते।
नैतत् किंचिन्नरश्रेष्ठ मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “That the king does not speak to you himself, shy as he is in asking you, his pet son, to relinquish the throne and leave Ayodhyā, matters little, O jewel among men ! So, let this compunction be banished from your mind. (15)

verses.text:
यावत्त्वं न वनं यातः पुरादस्मादतित्वरम्।
पिता तावन्न ते राम स्नास्यते भोक्ष्यतेऽपि वा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “So long as you do not depart posthaste from this city, your father, O Rāma, would neither bathe nor have his meals.” (16)

verses.text:
धिक्कष्टमिति निःश्वस्य राजा शोकपरिप्लुतः।
मूर्च्छितो न्यपतत् तस्मिन् पर्यङ्के हेमभूषिते॥ १७॥
verses.m: Drawing a deep audible breath with the words “What a shame ! How painful !” on his lips, the king, overwhelmed with grief, dropped down unconscious on that couch inlaid with gold. (17)

verses.text:
रामोऽप्युत्थाप्य राजानं कैकेय्याभिप्रचोदितः।
कशयेव हतो वाजी वनं गन्तुं कृतत्वरः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Raising up the king, Śrī Rāma too, when urged on face to face by Kaikeyī, made haste to proceed to the forest even as a horse lashed with a whip. (18)

verses.text:
तदप्रियमनार्याया वचनं दारुणोदयम्।
श्रुत्वा गतव्यथो रामः कैकेयीं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing that unpalatable and poignant remark of the impolite lady, Śrī Rāma, who was unknown to anguish, spoke to Kaikeyī as follows : (19)

verses.text:
नाहमर्थपरो देवि लोकमावस्तुमुत्सहे।
विद्धि मामृषिभिस्तुल्यं विमलं धर्ममास्थितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I do not desire to live in the world as a slave to material gains. Know me to be devoted to immaculate righteousness like the Ṛṣis. (20)

verses.text:
यत् तत्रभवतः किंचिच्छक्यं कर्तुं प्रियं मया।
प्राणानपि परित्यज्य सर्वथा कृतमेव तत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Whatever is agreeable to my adorable father and capable of being accomplished by me even at the cost of my life has veritably been accomplished in everyway. (21)

verses.text:
न ह्यतो धर्मचरणं किंचिदस्ति महत्तरम्।
यथा पितरि शुश्रूषा तस्य वा वचनक्रिया॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Indeed there is no greater piety than or even as good as service to one’s father or doing his bidding. (22)

verses.text:
अनुक्तोऽप्यत्रभवता भवत्या वचनादहम्।
वने वत्स्यामि विजने वर्षाणीह चतुर्दश॥ २३॥
verses.m: “At your command, though not directly enjoined by my revered father, I shall live in a lonely forest on this globe for fourteen years. (23)

verses.text:
न नूनं मयि कैकेयि किंचिदाशंससे गुणान्।
यद् राजानमवोचस्त्वं ममेश्वरतरा सती॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Surely you do not cognize any good point in me since you had to speak to my father about such a trivial thing, though you have greater authority over me even than my father, O princess of Kekaya ! (24)

verses.text:
यावन्मातरमापृच्छे सीतां चानुनयाम्यहम्।
ततोऽद्यैव गमिष्यामि दण्डकानां महद् वनम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Pray, bear with me till I take leave of my mother, Kausalyā, and win Sītā to consent. Then I shall proceed to the great forest of Daṇḍaka this very day. (25)

verses.text:
भरतः पालयेद् राज्यं शुश्रूषेच्च पितुर्यथा।
तथा भवत्या कर्तव्यं स हि धर्मः सनातनः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “An attempt should be made by you to see that Bharata protects the kingdom from internal disorder and foreign aggression and serves his aged father; for such is the eternal code of morality.” (26)

verses.text:
रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा भृशं दुःखगतः पिता।
शोकादशक्नुवन् वक्तुं प्ररुरोद महास्वनम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Sore distressed to hear Śrī Rāma’s utterance, and unable to speak because of grief, his father for his part wept bitterly at the pitch of his voice. (27)

verses.text:
वन्दित्वा चरणौ राज्ञो विसंज्ञस्य पितुस्तदा।
कैकेय्याश्चाप्यनार्याया निष्पपात महाद्युतिः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Bowing at the feet of his royal father, who was lying unconscious even then, as well as of the ignoble Kaikeyī, Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of immense glory, departed. (28)

verses.text:
स रामः पितरं कृत्वा कैकेयीं च प्रदक्षिणम्।
निष्क्रम्यान्तःपुरात् तस्मात् स्वं ददर्श सुहृज्जनम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Going clockwise round his father as well as Kaikeyī and coming out of the said gynaeceum, the celebrated Śrī Rāma saw his friends standing at the gate. (29)

verses.text:
तं बाष्पपरिपूर्णाक्षः पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम ह।
लक्ष्मणः परमक्रुद्धः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Highly enraged, Lakṣmaṇa, who enhanced the joy of his mother Sumitrā, followed at his heels, so the tradition goes, his eyes brimful with tears. (30)

verses.text:
आभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं कृत्वा रामः प्रदक्षिणम्।
शनैर्जगाम सापेक्षो दृष्टिं तत्राविचालयन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Going clockwise round the vessel containing the requisites for the projected consecration, Śrī Rāma moved slowly along without casting his eyes on it, keen as he was to leave the place. (31)

verses.text:
न चास्य महतीं लक्ष्मीं राज्यनाशोऽपकर्षति।
लोककान्तस्य कान्तत्वाच्छीतरश्मेरिव क्षयः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Loss of sovereignty, however, did not detract in the least from his extraordinary splendour because of his being naturally pleasing of aspect, any more than the waning of the orb of the moon, distinguished by its cool rays, which is delightful to the world, detracts from the latter’s charm. (32)

verses.text:
न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्।
सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥ ३३॥
verses.m: No change of mood was perceived in him—any more than in a master-Yogī, who surpasses all common men because of his having risen above all pairs of opposites—even though he was ready to retire to the woods and was renouncing the sovereignty of the entire globe. (33)

verses.text:
प्रतिषिध्य शुभं छत्रं व्यजने च स्वलंकृते।
विसर्जयित्वा स्वजनं रथं पौरांस्तथा जनान्॥ ३४॥
धारयन् मनसा दुःखमिन्द्रियाणि निगृह्य च।
प्रविवेशात्मवान् वेश्म मातुरप्रियशंसिवान्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Forbidding the use of the beautiful umbrella as well as of a pair of richly adorned chowries and sending away his own people, the chariot and the citizens, nay, inhibiting his agony caused by the agony of his own people with his mind and controlling his senses, Śrī Rāma, who had full mastery over his self, entered his mother’s apartments in order to break the unpalatable news to her. (34-35)

verses.text:
सर्वोऽप्यभिजनः श्रीमान् श्रीमतः सत्यवादिनः।
नालक्षयत रामस्य कंचिदाकारमानने॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Everyone around him, who looked smart, did not notice any change in the looks of the glorious and truthful Śrī Rāma. (36)

verses.text:
उचितं च महाबाहुर्न जहौ हर्षमात्मवान्।
शारदः समुदीर्णांशुश्चन्द्रस्तेज इवात्मजम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, who was noted for his self-control, did not shed his characteristic and native joy any more than the autumnal moon with its intensely bright rays loses its natural splendour. (37)

verses.text:
वाचा मधुरया रामः सर्वं सम्मानयञ्जनम्।
मातुः समीपं धर्मात्मा प्रविवेश महायशाः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Duly honouring all men with his suave speech, the highly illustrious Śrī Rāma, whose mind was given to piety, entered the presence of his mother. (38)

verses.text:
तं गुणैः समतां प्राप्तो भ्राता विपुलविक्रमः।
सौमित्रिरनुवव्राज धारयन् दुःखमात्मजम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Controlling the agony caused in his mind by the interruption of Śrī Rāma’s installation and the news of his impending exile, his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa son of Sumitrā, who had attained equality with Śrī Rāma by virtue of his excellences and was possessed of great prowess, followed him. (39)

verses.text:
प्रविश्य वेश्मातिभृशं मुदा युतं
समीक्ष्य तां चार्थविपत्तिमागताम्।
न चैव रामोऽत्र जगाम विक्रियां
सुहृज्जनस्यात्मविपत्तिशङ्कया ॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Entering the palace of Kausalyā, which was full of immense joy at the projected installation of Śrī Rāma, Śrī Rāma did not undergo any change of mood at all even on perceiving that loss of worldly fortune, that had come upon him at this moment, for fear of bringing about the loss of life of his near and dear ones. (40)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रे निष्क्रामति कृताञ्जलौ।
आर्तशब्दो महान् जज्ञे स्त्रीणामन्तःपुरे तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: The moment Śrī Rāma, a veritable tiger among men, issued forth from the gynaeceum, with joined palms, a loud and pathetic lament arose from the mouth of the ladies of the gynaeceum: (1)

verses.text:
कृत्येष्वचोदितः पित्रा सर्वस्यान्तःपुरस्य च।
गतिश्च शरणं चासीत् स रामोऽद्य प्रवत्स्यति॥ २॥
verses.m: “The same Śrī Rāma who used to attend to all the affairs of the gynaeceum unenjoined by his father and who was our resort and protector till now will go into exile today ! (2)

verses.text:
कौसल्यायां यथा युक्तो जनन्यां वर्तते सदा।
तथैव वर्ततेऽस्मासु जन्मप्रभृति राघवः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, has since his very birth ever been attentive to us precisely to the same degree as he is to his mother, Kausalyā. (3)

verses.text:
न क्रुध्यत्यभिशप्तोऽपि क्रोधनीयानि वर्जयन्।
क्रुद्धान् प्रसादयन् सर्वान् स इतोऽद्य प्रवत्स्यति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “He who did not feel angry even though spoken harshly to, avoided words provoking anger in others and appeased all who were angry with him, will go into exile from this place today ! (4)

verses.text:
अबुद्धिर्बत नो राजा जीवलोकं चरत्ययम्।
यो गतिं सर्वभूतानां परित्यजति राघवम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Alas ! This foolish king of ours, who is forgoing Śrī Rāma, the support of all living beings, is bringing destruction to the entire living creation.” (5)

verses.text:
इति सर्वा महिष्यस्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः।
पतिमाचुक्रुशुश्चापि सस्वनं चापि चुक्रुशुः॥ ६॥
verses.m: In this way all those queens not only decried their husband but also wailed loudly like cows bereft of their calves. (6)

verses.text:
स हि चान्तःपुरे घोरमार्तशब्दं महीपतिः।
पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः श्रुत्वा व्यालीयतासने॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing the frightful and piteous wail in the gynaeceum, the king, who was sore stricken with grief over the impending separation from his eldest son, actually hid himself under the bed-sheets in the couch for sheer shame and woe. (7)

verses.text:
रामस्तु भृशमायस्तो निःश्वसन्निव कुञ्जरः।
जगाम सहितो भ्रात्रा मातुरन्तःपुरं वशी॥ ८॥
verses.m: Deeply afflicted to find his near and dear ones plunged in grief, Śrī Rāma, who was noted for his self-control, proceeded, for his part, to his mother’s apartments alongwith his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, drawing a deep audible breath like an elephant. (8)

verses.text:
सोऽपश्यत् पुरुषं तत्र वृद्धं परमपूजितम्।
उपविष्टं गृहद्वारि तिष्ठतश्चापरान् बहून्॥ ९॥
verses.m: He saw seated at the entrance of the section of the gynaeceum, reserved for Kausalyā, the aged and most respected chief of porters and many other porters standing. (9)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वैव तु तदा रामं ते सर्वे समुपस्थिताः।
जयेन जयतां श्रेष्ठं वर्धयन्ति स्म राघवम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: The moment they beheld Śrī Rāma, all flocked to his side and hailed the scion of Raghu, the foremost of the victorious, with shouts of victory. (10)

verses.text:
प्रविश्य प्रथमां कक्ष्यां द्वितीयायां ददर्श सः।
ब्राह्मणान् वेदसम्पन्नान् वृद्धान् राज्ञाभिसत्कृतान्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having passed through the first gate, he saw at the second elderly Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Vedas and highly respected by the Emperor. (11)

verses.text:
प्रणम्य रामस्तान् वृद्धांस्तृतीयायां ददर्श सः।
स्त्रियो बालाश्च वृद्धाश्च द्वाररक्षणतत्पराः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Bowing low to the aforesaid elders Śrī Rāma beheld at the third gate females and girls as well as aged men intent upon guarding the entrance. (12)

verses.text:
वर्धयित्वा प्रहृष्टास्ताः प्रविश्य च गृहं स्त्रियः।
न्यवेदयन्त त्वरितं राममातुः प्रियं तदा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Felicitating the prince on his projected installation as Prince Regent and entering the chamber occupied by Empress Kausalyā, the women, who felt extremely delighted to behold Śrī Rāma, promptly broke the delightful news to Śrī Rāma’s mother on that occasion. (13)

verses.text:
कौसल्यापि तदा देवी रात्रिं स्थित्वा समाहिता।
प्रभाते चाकरोत् पूजां विष्णोः पुत्रहितैषिणी॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having passed the night in religious observances, Queen Kausalyā for her part had started offering worship to Lord Viṣṇu, seated in the orb of the sun, at day break, wishing well of her son. (14)

verses.text:
सा क्षौमवसना हृष्टा नित्यं व्रतपरायणा।
अग्निं जुहोति स्म तदा मन्त्रवत् कृतमङ्गला॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having performed some propitious rites, Kausalyā, who was clad in silk and was ever given to sacred observances, was causing oblations to be poured by the priests into the sacred fire at that time with the chanting of sacred texts. (15)

verses.text:
प्रविश्य तु तदा रामो मातुरन्तःपुरं शुभम्।
ददर्श मातरं तत्र हावयन्तीं हुताशनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Entering forthwith the beautiful chamber of Kausalyā, his mother, Śrī Rāma actually saw there his mother causing oblations to be poured into the sacred fire. (16)

verses.text:
देवकार्यनिमित्तं च तत्रापश्यत् समुद्यतम्।
दध्यक्षतघृतं चैव मोदकान् हविषस्तथा॥ १७॥
verses.m: He also saw kept ready at hand for the worship of the gods there curds, unbroken grains of rice and ghee as well as balls of sweetmeat and oblations to be poured into the sacred fire. (17)

verses.text:
लाजान् माल्यानि शुक्लानि पायसं कृसरं तथा।
समिधः पूर्णकुम्भांश्च ददर्श रघुनन्दनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, further beheld parched grains of paddy, white flowers, milk boiled with rice and sugar, rice cooked with sesame seeds, sticks of sacrificial wood and jars full of rice. (18)

verses.text:
तां शुक्लक्षौमसंवीतां व्रतयोगेन कर्शिताम्।
तर्पयन्तीं ददर्शाद्भिर्देवतां वरवर्णिनीम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: He saw the fair-complexioned Kausalyā clad in white silk and emaciated through persevering in fasting and gratifying the Deity with an offering of water. (19)

verses.text:
सा चिरस्यात्मजं दृष्ट्वा मातृनन्दनमागतम्।
अभिचक्राम संहृष्टा किशोरं वडवा यथा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Overjoyed to behold her son, the delight of his mother, come to her after a long time, she went forward to meet him as a mare would run to meet her foal. (20)

verses.text:
स मातरमुपक्रान्तामुपसंगृह्य राघवः।
परिष्वक्तश्च बाहुभ्यामवघ्रातश्च मूर्धनि॥ २१॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, stood clinging to his mother with his arms placed round her neck as she approached him and was in return folded in her arms and smelt at the head as a token of motherly affection. (21)

verses.text:
तमुवाच दुराधर्षं राघवं सुतमात्मनः।
कौसल्या पुत्रवात्सल्यादिदं प्रियहितं वचः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Out of affection for her son, Kausalyā addressed the following delightful and at the same time wholesome words (a rare combination) to her son, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was hard to assail : (22)

verses.text:
वृद्धानां धर्मशीलानां राजर्षीणां महात्मनाम्।
प्राप्नुह्यायुश्च कीर्तिं च धर्मं चाप्युचितं कुले॥ २३॥
verses.m: “May you attain the age and renown of ancient royal sages of virtuous conduct and possessing a noble soul, and acquire virtue worthy of your race ! (23)

verses.text:
सत्यप्रतिज्ञं पितरं राजानं पश्य राघव।
अद्यैव त्वां स धर्मात्मा यौवराज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Please go and see, O scion of Raghu, your royal father, who is true to his promise. That pious soul is going to install you in the office of Prince Regent this very day.”(24)

verses.text:
दत्तमासनमालभ्य भोजनेन निमन्त्रितः।
मातरं राघवः किंचित् प्रसार्याञ्जलिमब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
स स्वभावविनीतश्च गौरवाच्च तथानतः।
प्रस्थितो दण्डकारण्यमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥ २६॥
देवि नूनं न जानीषे महद् भयमुपस्थितम्।
इदं तव च दुःखाय वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणस्य च॥ २७॥
verses.m: Merely touching the seat offered by the Empress, when invited to breakfast, and distending a bit the hollow of his joined palms, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) began to speak as follows. Nay, about to start on his long journey to the Daṇḍaka forest, Śrī Rāma who was modest by nature and was likewise bent low with reverence, proceeded to take leave of his mother in the following words : “Surely you do not know, O godly lady, that a great calamity is imminent. What I am going to reveal to you will cause you agony no less than to Sītā, a princess of Videha, and to Lakṣmaṇa. (25—27)

verses.text:
गमिष्ये दण्डकारण्यं किमनेनासनेन मे।
विष्टरासनयोग्यो हि कालोऽयं मामुपस्थितः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “I am just going to proceed to the Daṇḍaka forest; what shall I do with this bejewelled seat? Time has now arrived for me to occupy a mat of Kuśa grass . (28)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वत्स्यामि विजने वने।
कन्दमूलफलैर्जीवन् हित्वा मुनिवदामिषम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Indeed for fourteen years I shall actually live in a lonely forest, subsisting like ascetics on bulbs, roots and fruits and giving up royal fare. (29)

verses.text:
भरताय महाराजो यौवराज्यं प्रयच्छति।
मां पुनर्दण्डकारण्यं विवासयति तापसम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “The Emperor is conferring the office of Prince Regent on Bharata and exiling me to the Daṇḍaka forest as an ascetic, on the other hand. (30)

verses.text:
स षट् चाष्टौ च वर्षाणि वत्स्यामि विजने वने।
आसेवमानो वन्यानि फलमूलैश्च वर्तयन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “As such I shall live in a lonely forest for six years and eight, wearing the barks of wild trees and living on fruits and roots.” (31)

verses.text:
सा निकृत्तेव सालस्य यष्टिः परशुना वने।
पपात सहसा देवी देवतेव दिवश्च्युता॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing this unpalatable news, the said queen fell all at once to the ground like a bough of a fir tree in the forest severed with an axe, and lying unconscious shone like a goddess fallen from heaven. (32)

verses.text:
तामदुःखोचितां दृष्ट्वा पतितां कदलीमिव।
रामस्तूत्थापयामास मातरं गतचेतसम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Seeing his mother, who did not deserve suffering, fallen unconscious like a banana tree, Śrī Rāma for his part lifted her up. (33)

verses.text:
उपावृत्योत्थितां दीनां वडवामिव वाहिताम्।
पांसुगुण्ठितसर्वाङ्गीं विममर्श च पाणिना॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Nay, he brushed the dust with his own hands off the person of his distressed mother, who had all her limbs covered with it like a mare that had been made to carry a heavy load and had just risen after rolling on the ground. (34)

verses.text:
सा राघवमुपासीनमसुखार्ता सुखोचिता।
उवाच पुरुषव्याघ्रमुपशृण्वति लक्ष्मणे॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Stricken with agony, Kausalyā, who deserved happiness, spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, a tiger among men, standing by her side, within the hearing of Lakṣmaṇa : (35)

verses.text:
यदि पुत्र न जायेथा मम शोकाय राघव।
न स्म दुःखमतो भूयः पश्येयमहमप्रजाः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Had you not been born, my son, this would have certainly caused grief to me in the shape of issuelessness, O scion of Raghu ! Even if childless, I would not have experienced the present agony caused by separation from a grown up and married son, greater than the former. (36)

verses.text:
एक एव हि वन्ध्यायाः शोको भवति मानसः।
अप्रजास्मीति संतापो न ह्यन्यः पुत्र विद्यते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Indeed there is only one mental anguish for a barren woman—the feeling that she is issueless; there is certainly no other agony to her, my son ! (37)

verses.text:
न दृष्टपूर्वं कल्याणं सुखं वा पतिपौरुषे।
अपि पुत्रे विपश्येयमिति रामास्थितं मया॥ ३८॥
verses.m: No good fortune or happiness was enjoyed by me in the past through the effort of my husband. Hope was, however, entertained by me, O Rāma, that with my son in power I might see both in abundance. (38)

verses.text:
सा बहून्यमनोज्ञानि वाक्यानि हृदयच्छिदाम्।
अहं श्रोष्ये सपत्नीनामवराणां परा सती॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Seniormost though I am of all the queens, I shall in my present plight, as separated from you, hear many unpalatable words from my junior co-wives, who will rend my heart thereby. (39)

verses.text:
अतो दुःखतरं किं नु प्रमदानां भविष्यति।
मम शोको विलापश्च यादृशोऽयमनन्तकः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “What can possibly be more painful than this for the fair sex? The kind of grief and lamentation that has now fallen to my lot is unending. (40)

verses.text:
त्वयि संनिहितेऽप्येवमहमासं निराकृता।
किं पुनः प्रोषिते तात ध्रुवं मरणमेव हि॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Even with you by my side, I have been despised; how much more shall I be despised when you are away, O dear child? Surely my death is but inevitable. (41)

verses.text:
अत्यन्तं निगृहीतास्मि भर्तुर्नित्यमसम्मता।
परिवारेण कैकेय्याः समा वाप्यथवावरा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Not esteemed by my husband, I have always been greatly snubbed by him. I have been treated on a par with or even on a lower footing than Kaikeyī’s servants ! (42)

verses.text:
यो हि मां सेवते कश्चिदपि वाप्यनुवर्तते।
कैकेय्याः पुत्रमन्वीक्ष्य स जनो नाभिभाषते॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Whosoever serves me or even speaks kindly to me, would no longer speak to me on perceiving Bharata. (43)

verses.text:
नित्यक्रोधतया तस्याः कथं नु खरवादि तत्।
कैकेय्या वदनं द्रष्टुं पुत्र शक्ष्यामि दुर्गता॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Reduced to a bad plight, my son, how shall I possibly be able to cast my eyes on those lips of Kaikeyī uttering harsh words due to her being constantly angry? (44)

verses.text:
दश सप्त च वर्षाणि जातस्य तव राघव।
अतीतानि प्रकांक्षन्त्या मया दुःखपरिक्षयम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Ten and seven years have been spent by me since you were born for a second time in the shape of investiture* with the sacred thread, keenly desiring the end of woes, O scion of Raghu ! (45)

verses.text:
तदक्षयं महद्दुःखं नोत्सहे सहितुं चिरात्।
विप्रकारं सपत्नीनामेवं जीर्णापि राघव॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Though worn out with age I am unable to suffer for a long time that great agony, in the shape of the contumely of my co-wives, which knows no end, O scion of Raghu ! (46)

verses.text:
अपश्यन्ती तव मुखं परिपूर्णशशिप्रभम्।
कृपणा वर्तयिष्यामि कथं कृपणजीविका॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Unable to behold your countenance possessing the splendour of the full moon, and dragging a wretched existence, how shall I survive, distressed as I already am? (47)

verses.text:
उपवासैश्च योगैश्च बहुभिश्च परिश्रमैः।
दुःखसंवर्धितो मोघं त्वं हि दुर्गतया मया॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “In vain indeed have you been brought up through great hardship with the help of a number of fasts and meditations on the various gods involving much toil, unlucky as I am. (48)

verses.text:
स्थिरं नु हृदयं मन्ये ममेदं यन्न दीर्यते।
प्रावृषीव महानद्याः स्पृष्टं कूलं नवाम्भसा॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “I conclude this heart of mine to be hard enough inasmuch as it does not get riven any more than the bank of a large river like the holy Gaṅgā even though washed by the new waters in the rainy season. (49)

verses.text:
ममैव नूनं मरणं न विद्यते
न चावकाशोऽस्ति यमक्षये मम।
यदन्तकोऽद्यैव न मां जिहीर्षति
प्रसह्य सिंहो रुदतीं मृगीमिव॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Surely there is no death for me nor is there room for me in the abode of Yama (the god of punishment), as is evident from the fact that Death does not feel inclined to carry me away by force as a lion would carry away a wailing doe. (50)

verses.text:
स्थिरं हि नूनं हृदयं ममायसं
न भिद्यते यद् भुवि नो विदीर्यते।
अनेन दुःखेन च देहमर्पितं
ध्रुवं ह्यकाले मरणं न विद्यते॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “My hard heart is most certainly made of steel inasmuch as it does not break under pressure of grief nor is the body, overcome with this anguish, torn into pieces even on falling to the ground. Undoubtedly death does not come out of time. (51)

verses.text:
इदं तु दुःखं यदनर्थकानि मे
व्रतानि दानानि च संयमाश्च हि।
तपश्च तप्तं यदपत्यकाम्यया
सुनिष्फलं बीजमिवोप्तमूषरे॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “This is all the more painful that my sacred observances and gifts as well as courses of self-discipline are of no use and the asceticism practised with intent to do good to my child has proved utterly unfructuous like a seed sown in barren soil. (52)

verses.text:
यदि ह्यकाले मरणं यदृच्छया
लभेत कश्चिद् गुरुदुःखकर्शितः।
गताहमद्यैव परेतसंसदं
विना त्वया धेनुरिवात्मजेन वै॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “If anyone afflicted with great suffering could meet with death at one’s sweet will even before time, I would certainly, like a cow bereft of its calf, depart to the court of Yama in your absence this very day. (53)

verses.text:
अथापि किं जीवितमद्य मे वृथा
त्वया विना चन्द्रनिभाननप्रभ।
अनुव्रजिष्यामि वनं त्वयैव गौः
सुदुर्बला वत्समिवाभिकांक्षया॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Even if there is no death, life without you is of no consequence and, therefore, useless, O Rāma (wearing a moon-like splendour on your countenance) ! Though very feeble, I shall, like a cow following its calf through ardent longing, definitely proceed with you to the forest.” (54)

verses.text:
भृशमसुखममर्षिता तदा
बहु विललाप समीक्ष्य राघवम्।
व्यसनमुपनिशाम्य सा महत्
सुतमिव बद्धमवेक्ष्य किंनरी॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Pondering over the terrible calamity that was going to befall her as a result of her son’s exile and perceiving Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, bound by a sense of duty to his father, Kausalyā, who was unable to bear the intense suffering, wailed a lot even as a Kinnara woman would on finding her son made captive. (55)

verses.text:
तथा तु विलपन्तीं तां कौसल्यां राममातरम्।
उवाच लक्ष्मणो दीनस्तत्कालसदृशं वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Feeling miserable over the situation, Lakṣmaṇa for his part made the following submission, suited to that occasion, to Kausalyā, mother of Śrī Rāma, who was wailing as aforesaid : (1)

verses.text:
न रोचते ममाप्येतदार्ये यद् राघवो वनम्।
त्यक्त्वा राज्यश्रियं गच्छेत् स्त्रिया वाक्यवशंगतः॥ २॥
विपरीतश्च वृद्धश्च विषयैश्च प्रधर्षितः।
नृपः किमिव न ब्रूयाच्चोद्यमानः समन्मथः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “To me either it does not appeal, O worthy lady, that Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, should proceed to the forest relinquishing the royal fortune. Dominated by the words of a woman, the king has become perverse and is full of lust, senile and overpowered by his love for the pleasures of sense. What will he not say, when urged by Kaikeyī? (2-3)

verses.text:
नास्यापराधं पश्यामि नापि दोषं तथाविधम्।
येन निर्वास्यते राष्ट्राद् वनवासाय राघवः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I do not perceive in Śrī Rāma any such offence against the king nor any vice for which Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, should be exiled from the state to take up his abode in a forest. (4)

verses.text:
न तं पश्याम्यहं लोके परोक्षमपि यो नरः।
स्वमित्रोऽपि निरस्तोऽपि योऽस्य दोषमुदाहरेत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I find no such man in the world who may point out Śrī Rām’s fault even in his absence—not even the man who is his deadly enemy or has been vanquished by him. (5)

verses.text:
देवकल्पमृजुं दान्तं रिपूणामपि वत्सलम्।
अवेक्षमाणः को धर्मं त्यजेत् पुत्रमकारणात्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “What man having regard for virtue would forsake without any cause a son who stands on a par with the gods, is guileless, disciplined and fond even of his enemies?(6)

verses.text:
तदिदं वचनं राज्ञः पुनर्बाल्यमुपेयुषः।
पुत्रः को हृदये कुर्याद् राजवृत्तमनुस्मरन्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “What son having an eye to statesmanship would heed such a command of a king who has attained a second childhood in the shape of dotage?” (7)

verses.text:
यावदेव न जानाति कश्चिदर्थमिमं नरः।
तावदेव मया सार्धमात्मस्थं कुरु शासनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Addressing Śrī Rāma, he continued : “Before any individual comes to know this fact of the king having decided to send you into exile, take the reins of administration in your hands with my help after duly installing yourself as Prince Regent. (8)

verses.text:
मया पार्श्वे सधनुषा तव गुप्तस्य राघव।
कः समर्थोऽधिकं कर्तुं कृतान्तस्येव तिष्ठतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Before you standing as death, guarded by me, stationed beside you, bow in hand, who will be able to exhibit greater valour, O scion of Raghu? (9)

verses.text:
निर्मनुष्यामिमां सर्वामयोध्यां मनुजर्षभ।
करिष्यामि शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्यदि स्थास्यति विप्रिये॥ १०॥
verses.m: “If the city of Ayodhyā stands in opposition to you, I shall depopulate the entire city by means of my sharp-pointed shafts, O jewel among men ! (10)

verses.text:
भरतस्याथ पक्ष्यो वा यो वास्य हितमिच्छति।
सर्वांस्तांश्च वधिष्यामि मृदुर्हि परिभूयते॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nay, whosoever is a supporter of Bharata and whoever seeks to advance his interests, I shall kill them all; for he alone who is meek is subjected to contumely. (11)

verses.text:
प्रोत्साहितोऽयं कैकेय्या संतुष्टो यदि नः पिता।
अमित्रभूतो निःसङ्गं वध्यतां वध्यतामपि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “If pleased with Kaikeyī and instigated by her, our royal father, behaves as an enemy, let him be made captive or even got rid of without the least scruple. (12)

verses.text:
गुरोरप्यवलिप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः।
उत्पथं प्रतिपन्नस्य कार्यं भवति शासनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Coercion has to be resorted to even with reference to a father or teacher who being puffed up with pride has ceased to distinguish between what ought to be done and what ought not to be done and has taken to the evil path. (13)

verses.text:
बलमेष किमाश्रित्य हेतुं वा पुरुषोत्तम।
दातुमिच्छति कैकेय्यै उपस्थितमिदं तव॥ १४॥
verses.m: “On what authority or ground, O jewel among men, does he seek to confer on the son of Kaikeyī this kingdom, which has as a matter of right devolved on you? (14)

verses.text:
त्वया चैव मया चैव कृत्वा वैरमनुत्तमम्।
कास्य शक्तिः श्रियं दातुं भरतायारिशासन॥ १५॥
verses.m: “What power has he to bestow royal fortune on Bharata entering into bitter enmity with you as well as with me, O chastiser of foes?” (15)

verses.text:
अनुरक्तोऽस्मि भावेन भ्रातरं देवि तत्त्वतः।
सत्येन धनुषा चैव दत्तेनेष्टेन ते शपे॥ १६॥
verses.m: Turning again to Kausalyā he said : “I swear to you by my bow as well as by the merit attained by me through truthfulness, charity and worship of gods that I am truly devoted to my eldest brother with the core of my heart, O godly lady ! (16)

verses.text:
दीप्तमग्निमरण्यं वा यदि रामः प्रवेक्ष्यति।
प्रविष्टं तत्र मां देवि त्वं पूर्वमवधारय॥ १७॥
verses.m: “If Śrī Rāma enters a blazing fire or retires to the forest, know me, O glorious lady, as having already entered the same. (17)

verses.text:
हरामि वीर्याद् दुःखं ते तमः सूर्य इवोदितः।
देवी पश्यतु मे वीर्यं राघवश्चैव पश्यतु॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I shall presently dispel your sorrow by dint of my prowess even as the sun when risen drives away darkness. Let all people as well as Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) witness my valour. (18)

verses.text:
हनिष्ये पितरं वृद्धं कैकेय्यासक्तमानसम्।
कृपणं च स्थितं बाल्ये वृद्धभावेन गर्हितम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I shall kill my aged and wretched father, whose mind is attached to Kaikeyī and who is going through his second childhood as a result of his senility and has accordingly grown contemptible.” (19)

verses.text:
एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः।
उवाच रामं कौसल्या रुदती शोकलालसा॥ २०॥
verses.m: On hearing the aforesaid utterance of the high-minded Lakṣmaṇa, Kausalyā, who was plunged in grief, spoke weeping as follows to Śrī Rāma : (20)

verses.text:
भ्रातुस्ते वदतः पुत्र लक्ष्मणस्य श्रुतं त्वया।
यदत्रानन्तरं तत्त्वं कुरुष्व यदि रोचते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The statement of your younger brother, my son, has been heard by you even as he spoke. Do you now, if it so pleases you, what should be done next in this connection. (21)

verses.text:
न चाधर्म्यं वचः श्रुत्वा सपत्न्या मम भाषितम्।
विहाय शोकसंतप्तां गन्तुमर्हसि मामितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Hearing the unjust command given by my co-wife, you ought not in any case to depart from Ayodhyā leaving me sore stricken with grief. (22)

verses.text:
धर्मज्ञ इति धर्मिष्ठ धर्मं चरितुमिच्छसि।
शुश्रूष मामिहस्थस्त्वं चर धर्ममनुत्तमम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “If, as one who is well-versed in morality, you wish to do what is right, O most pious son, serve you me remaining here and practise thus the highest virtue. (23)

verses.text:
शुश्रूषुर्जननीं पुत्र स्वगृहे नियतो वसन्।
परेण तपसा युक्तः काश्यपस्त्रिदिवं गतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Staying self-disciplined at home in the service of his mother and endowed with supreme asceticism, a son of Kaśyapa attained the position of a Prajāpati, lord of creation, in heaven. (24)

verses.text:
यथैव राजा पूज्यस्ते गौरवेण तथा ह्यहम्।
त्वां साहं नानुजानामि न गन्तव्यमितो वनम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “As the king is worthy of adoration to you, more so am I from the point of view of merit. As such I do not grant leave to you to depart. Hence you should not proceed to the forest from this place. (25)

verses.text:
त्वद्वियोगान्न मे कार्यं जीवितेन सुखेन च।
त्वया सह मम श्रेयस्तृणानामपि भक्षणम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “After my separation from you, I have no longer any use for life and happiness. In your company it is better for me even to live on blades of grass. (26)

verses.text:
यदि त्वं यास्यसि वनं त्यक्त्वा मां शोकलालसाम्।
अहं प्रायमिहासिष्ये न च शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “If you retire to the forest leaving me plunged in grief, I shall take up a vow of fasting unto death; for, in that case I shall no longer be able to survive. (27)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वं प्राप्स्यसे पुत्र निरयं लोकविश्रुतम्।
ब्रह्महत्यामिवाधर्मात् समुद्रः सरितां पतिः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “As a sequel to that offence of yours, my son, you will suffer hellish tortures well-known in the world, even as Ocean, the spouse of deities presiding over the rivers, underwent hellish tortures of the kind suffered as a result of Brahmanicide through unrighteousness in the form of inflicting suffering on his own mother.” (28)

verses.text:
विलपन्तीं तथा दीनां कौसल्यां जननीं ततः।
उवाच रामो धर्मात्मा वचनं धर्मसंहितम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, whose mind was given to piety, thereupon made the following submission, conformable to righteousness, to his afflicted mother, Kausalyā, who was wailing as aforesaid : (29)

verses.text:
नास्ति शक्तिः पितुर्वाक्यं समतिक्रमितुं मम।
प्रसादये त्वां शिरसा गन्तुमिच्छाम्यहं वनम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “I have no courage to flout the command of my father and as such wish to proceed to the forest. I, therefore, solicit your favour in the form of leave to depart with my head bent low. (30)

verses.text:
ऋषिणा च पितुर्वाक्यं कुर्वता वनचारिणा।
गौर्हता जानताधर्मं कण्डुना च विपश्चिता॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “A cow was slaughtered in the past by the learned Sage Kaṇḍu living in a forest, in obedience to the command of his father, even though he knew it to be a sin. (31)

verses.text:
अस्माकं तु कुले पूर्वं सगरस्याज्ञया पितुः।
खनद्भिः सागरैर्भूमिमवाप्तः सुमहान् वधः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “A tragic death was met in the past by the sons of Sagara (numbering sixty thousand), belonging to our race, while digging the earth under the command of their father. (32)

verses.text:
जामदग्न्येन रामेण रेणुका जननी स्वयम्।
कृत्ता परशुनारण्ये पितुर्वचनकारणात्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Mother Reṇukā was beheaded in a forest by Paraśurāma, son of Sage Jamadagni, by means of an axe with his own hand in obedience to the command of his father. (33)

verses.text:
एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिर्देवि देवसमैः कृतम्।
पितुर्वचनमक्लीबं करिष्यामि पितुर्हितम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Their father’s behest has been unhesitatingly carried out by these as well as by many other godlike men, I too shall, therefore, do a good turn to my father, O godly mother ! (34)

verses.text:
न खल्वेतन्मयैकेन क्रियते पितृशासनम्।
एतैरपि कृतं देवि ये मया परिकीर्तिताः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a father’s command is not being carried out by me alone in this case, but it has been done by those as well that have been mentioned by me above, O pious lady ! (35)

verses.text:
नाहं धर्ममपूर्वं ते प्रतिकूलं प्रवर्तये।
पूर्वैरयमभिप्रेतो गतो मार्गोऽनुगम्यते॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “I am not introducing any new sacred practice disagreeable to you. That path alone is being followed by me, which was intended and has been traversed by my forbears. (36)

verses.text:
तदेतत् तु मया कार्यं क्रियते भुवि नान्यथा।
पितुर्हि वचनं कुर्वन् न कश्चिन्नाम हीयते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “That alone which is worth doing on this globe is being done by me in this case, not otherwise. Indeed, as is well-known, nobody doing the bidding of his father is forsaken by virtue.” (37)

verses.text:
तामेवमुक्त्वा जननीं लक्ष्मणं पुनरब्रवीत्।
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Having submitted to his celebrated mother as aforesaid, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those knowing the art of expression as also of all bowmen, then spoke to Lakṣmaṇa as follows : (38)

verses.text:
तव लक्ष्मण जानामि मयि स्नेहमनुत्तमम्।
विक्रमं चैव सत्त्वं च तेजश्च सुदुरासदम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “I know your unsurpassed love for me as also your valour and strength as well as your glory, which cannot be easily approached by others. (39)

verses.text:
मम मातुर्महद् दुःखमतुलं शुभलक्षण।
अभिप्रायं न विज्ञाय सत्यस्य च शमस्य च॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Not knowing the import of truthfulness and self-control, as understood by me, great agony, which is unequalled anywhere is being experienced by my mother, O prince endowed with noble characteristics ! (40)

verses.text:
धर्मो हि परमो लोके धर्मे सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
धर्मसंश्रितमप्येतत् पितुर्वचनमुत्तमम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Indeed, righteousness is paramount in the world and truthfulness is rooted in piety. This command of my father too is supreme in that it is based on righteousness. (41)

verses.text:
संश्रुत्य च पितुर्वाक्यं मातुर्वा ब्राह्मणस्य वा।
न कर्तव्यं वृथा वीर धर्ममाश्रित्य तिष्ठता॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Having plighted one’s word to do the bidding of one’s father, mother or a Brāhmaṇa, O gallant Lakṣmaṇa, he who takes his stand on righteousness should not falsify it. (42)

verses.text:
सोऽहं न शक्ष्यामि पुनर्नियोगमतिवर्तितुम्।
पितुर्हि वचनाद् वीर कैकेय्याहं प्रचोदितः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Since I have been commanded by Kaikeyī to go into exile according to the pledge given to her by my father, O valiant prince, I, constituted as I am, dare not flout her command in any case. (43)

verses.text:
तदेतां विसृजानार्यां क्षत्रधर्माश्रितां मतिम्।
धर्ममाश्रय मा तैक्ष्ण्यं मद्बुद्धिरनुगम्यताम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, give up this unworthy thought of assuming the reins of government even by taking captive or killing the reigning king, deriving its support from military heroism. Take your stand on righteousness and do not resort to severity. Let my resolution of carrying out the royal command, be followed.” (44)

verses.text:
तमेवमुक्त्वा सौहार्दाद् भ्रातरं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
उवाच भूयः कौसल्यां प्राञ्जलिः शिरसा नतः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Having thus admonished his aforesaid younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, out of affection, Śrī Rāma (Lakṣmaṇa’s eldest brother) submitted once more to his mother, Kausalyā, with joined palms and his head bent low as follows : (45)

verses.text:
अनुमन्यस्व मां देवि गमिष्यन्तमितो वनम्।
शापितासि मम प्राणैः कुरु स्वस्त्ययनानि मे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Grant leave, O glorious lady, to me, ready as I am to depart from Ayodhyā to the forest. You are hereby bound with an oath on my life: please perform rites ensuring my welfare in the journey. (46)

verses.text:
तीर्णप्रतिज्ञश्च वनात् पुनरेष्याम्यहं पुरीम्।
ययातिरिव राजर्षिः पुरा हित्वा पुनर्दिवम्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Having honoured my vow of remaining in exile for fourteen years, I shall come back from the forest to Ayodhyā, even as in the former days the royal Sage Yayāti ascended back to heaven after leaving it once. (47)

verses.text:
शोकः संधार्यतां मातर्हृदये साधु मा शुचः।
वनवासादिहैष्यामि पुनः कृत्वा पितुर्वचः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Let grief be fully inhibited in the heart, O mother ! Pray, do not sorrow. Having carried out the behest of my father, I shall return to Ayodhyā from my exile in the forest. (48)

verses.text:
त्वया मया च वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन सुमित्रया।
पितुर्नियोगे स्थातव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Yourself, Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), Lakṣmaṇa, Sumitrā and myself should abide by the injunctions of my father: such is the eternal law of morality. (49)

verses.text:
अम्ब सम्भृत्य सम्भारान् दुःखं हृदि निगृह्य च।
वनवासकृता बुद्धिर्मम धर्म्यानुवर्त्यताम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Removing the materials collected for the installation and restraining the agony in the heart, let my righteous resolution of taking up my abode in the forest be carried out.” (50)

verses.text:
एतद् वचस्तस्य निशम्य माता
सुधर्म्यमव्यग्रमविक्लवं च।
मृतेव संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य देवी
समीक्ष्य रामं पुनरित्युवाच॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid submission of Śrī Rāma, which was fully conformable to the principles of righteousness and was marked with patience and courage, the royal mother regained her consciousness like a dead woman coming to life again and, looking intently on Śrī Rāma, spoke to him once more as follows : (51)

verses.text:
यथैव ते पुत्र पिता तथाहं
गुरुः स्वधर्मेण सुहृत्तया च।
न त्वानुजानामि न मां विहाय
सुदुःखितामर्हसि पुत्र गन्तुम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “By virtue of my having discharged my duty of tending you as well as by virtue of my affection towards you, I am worthy of your adoration in the same way, my son, as your father and I do not grant leave to you to retire to the woods. Therefore, leaving me sore distressed, my son, you ought not to go. (52)

verses.text:
किं जीवितेनेह विना त्वया मे
लोकेन वा किं स्वधयामृतेन।
श्रेयो मुहूर्तं तव संनिधानं
ममैव कृत्स्नादपि जीवलोकात्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “What is to be gained by me through life without you in this world or what joy shall I derive through the other world or through offering, received by the departed in the realm of the manes or even through ambrosia—the food of the gods in heaven if I am transferred to these realms after death? Preferable to me is your presence even for an hour or so than the company or even the governance of the entire living creation !” (53)

verses.text:
नरैरिवोल्काभिरपोह्यमानो
महागजो ध्वान्तमभिप्रविष्टः।
भूयः प्रजज्वाल विलापमेवं
निशम्य रामः करुणं जनन्याः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Hearing, as aforesaid, the piteous wail of his mother, Śrī Rāma grew all the more impetuous (impatient to escape) even as a lordly elephant that has entered a gloomy retreat would, when goaded by men laying the trap to catch it with firebrands. (54)

verses.text:
स मातरं चैव विसंज्ञकल्पा-
मार्तं च सौमित्रिमभिप्रतप्तम्।
धर्मे स्थितो धर्म्यमुवाच वाक्यं
यथा स एवार्हति तत्र वक्तुम्॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Holding firmly to his duty, Śrī Rāma made the following righteous reply, a reply which he alone was capable of making on that occasion, to his mother, who lay almost unconscious, as well as to Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), who was feeling distressed and greatly excited on that occasion : (55)

verses.text:
अहं हि ते लक्ष्मण नित्यमेव
जानामि भक्तिं च पराक्रमं च।
मम त्वभिप्रायमसंनिरीक्ष्य
मात्रा सहाभ्यर्दसि मा सुदुःखम्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Indeed, O Lakṣmaṇa, I know your everlasting devotion to me as well as your prowess. But, failing to read my mind fully, you harass me most painfully alongwith mother. (56)

verses.text:
धर्मार्थकामाः खलु जीवलोके
समीक्षिता धर्मफलोदयेषु।
ये तत्र सर्वे स्युरसंशयं मे
भार्येव वश्याभिमता सपुत्रा॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “Religious merit, material gain and worldly enjoyment—which have been positively concluded to be the means of attaining happiness (the reward of merit ) in the world of mortals—all undoubtedly follow in the wake of righteousness even as one’s wife, if obedient, is conducive to religious merit by being helpful in the discharge of one’s religious obligations such as hospitality to unexpected guests, yields sensuous enjoyment if agreeable and makes for prosperity in the other world by giving birth to a son. (57)

verses.text:
यस्मिंस्तु सर्वे स्युरसंनिविष्टा
धर्मो यतः स्यात् तदुपक्रमेत।
द्वेष्यो भवत्यर्थपरो हि लोके
कामात्मता खल्वपि न प्रशस्ता॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “One should abstain from pursuits in which all the three objects of human pursuit do not find any scope and should undertake that pursuit alone from which follows religious merit; for he who is devoted to material wealth, divorced from righteousness, becomes hateful; while excessive addiction to sensuous enjoyment, incompatible with righteousness, is not commendable either. (58)

verses.text:
गुरुश्च राजा च पिता च वृद्धः
क्रोधात् प्रहर्षादथवापि कामात्।
यद् व्यादिशेत् कार्यमवेक्ष्य धर्मं
कस्तं न कुर्यादनृशंसवृत्तिः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “What man who is not cruel in his dealings would fail to perform as a sacred obligation a duty which his aged father, who is also his preceptor and king, might enjoin him to do, whether from anger, excessive delight or even from concupiscence? (59)

verses.text:
न तेन शक्नोमि पितुः प्रतिज्ञा-
मिमां न कर्तुं सकलां यथावत्।
स ह्यावयोस्तात गुरुर्नियोगे
देव्याश्च भर्ता स गतिश्च धर्मः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, I cannot but duly implement this pledge of my father inasmuch as he is competent to command us both (Bharata as well as myself), O dear brother, and he is the asylum as also the means of happiness in this as well as in the other world of the queen (Kausalyā), whose husband he is and with whom she should live through thick and thin rather than with her son. (60)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् पुनर्जीवति धर्मराजे
विशेषतः स्वे पथि वर्तमाने।
देवी मया सार्धमितोऽभिगच्छेत्
कथंस्विदन्या विधवेव नारी॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “So long as such a husband, who is not only a virtuous king but is staunchly adhering to his path (the path of virtue in the shape of truthfulness, for the sake of which he is abandoning his dearest son and sacrificing his interests), is alive, how can the Empress, like an ordinary widowed woman, who has lost her husband and lives with her son, actually depart from Ayodhyā alongwith me? (61)

verses.text:
सा मानुमन्यस्व वनं व्रजन्तं
कुरुष्व नः स्वस्त्ययनानि देवि।
यथा समाप्ते पुनराव्रजेयं
यथा हि सत्येन पुनर्ययातिः॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “As such, pray, grant leave to me proceeding to the forest, and perform sacred rites ensuring our welfare in the journey, O godly lady, so that on the period of exile being complete, I may come back even as King Yayāti ascended for the second time to heaven by dint of truthfulness. (62)

verses.text:
यशो ह्यहं केवलराज्यकारणा-
न्न पृष्ठतः कर्तुमलं महोदयम्।
अदीर्घकालेन तु देवि जीविते
वृणेऽवरामद्य महीमधर्मतः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “For, I am unable to throw away fame, which is of greater consequence, for the sake of mere sovereignty divorced from righteousness. Life being of such a short duration, O godly lady, I am not going to accept in any case the trivial rulership of the globe through unrighteousness today.” (63)

verses.text:
प्रसादयन्नरवृषभः स मातरं
पराक्रमाज्जिगमिषुरेव दण्डकान्।
अथानुजं भृशमनुशास्य दर्शनं
चकार तां हृदि जननीं प्रदक्षिणम्॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Thus trying to please his mother and having fully taught Lakṣmaṇa, his younger brother, his own philosophy of morality, that jewel among men, positively inclined as he was to proceed to the Daṇḍaka forest by way of an enterprise, mentally went round his aforesaid mother clockwise as a mark of respect. (64)

verses.text:
अथ तं व्यथया दीनं सविशेषममर्षितम्।
सरोषमिव नागेन्द्रं रोषविस्फारितेक्षणम्॥ १॥
आसाद्य रामः सौमित्रिं सुहृदं भ्रातरं प्रियम्।
उवाचेदं स धैर्येण धारयन् सत्त्वमात्मवान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Approaching the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), his beloved brother and well-wisher, who felt distressed through agony and was greatly indignant and was looking with eyes wide open through rage like an infuriated elephant, the said Śrī Rāma, who had mastered his self, spoke to him as follows, restraining his mind with firmness : (1-2)

verses.text:
निगृह्य रोषं शोकं च धैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्।
अवमानं निरस्यैनं गृहीत्वा हर्षमुत्तमम्॥ ३॥
उपक्लृप्तं यदैतन्मे अभिषेकार्थमुत्तमम्।
सर्वं निवर्तय क्षिप्रं कुरु कार्यं निरव्ययम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Curbing your anger against our father and Kaikeyī and grief over my impending exile and embracing uncommon fortitude, nay, ignoring this affront in the form of banishing me and deriving the highest joy from the idea of having helped our father in implementing his plighted word and thereby ensuring his place in the highest heaven, pray, cause to be sent back all the exquisite material that has been got ready for my consecration as Prince Regent and quickly and uninterruptedly accomplish what requires to be done now in the shape of preparations for the journey. (3-4)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे योऽभिषेकार्थे मम सम्भारसम्भ्रमः।
अभिषेकनिवृत्त्यर्थे सोऽस्तु सम्भारसम्भ्रमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Let the same zeal be evinced in preparing for the exile, which implies the cessation of the consecration as was shown in collecting materials for my installation, O darling of Sumitrā ! (5)

verses.text:
यस्या मदभिषेकार्थे मानसं परितप्यते।
माता नः सा यथा न स्यात् सविशङ्का तथा कुरु॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Take steps to ensure that that mother of ours viz., Kaikeyī, whose mind is greatly troubled over the question of my installation, is not filled with apprehension (that I may assume a revolting attitude and refuse to leave the capital). (6)

verses.text:
तस्याः शङ्कामयं दुःखं मुहूर्तमपि नोत्सहे।
मनसि प्रतिसंजातं सौमित्रेऽहमुपेक्षितुम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I cannot afford to ignore even for a while, O darling of Sumitrā, the agony in the form of apprehension aroused in her mind. (7)

verses.text:
न बुद्धिपूर्वं नाबुद्धं स्मरामीह कदाचन।
मातॄणां वा पितुर्वाहं कृतमल्पं च विप्रियम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “I do not remember the least offence ever given by me consciously or unwittingly to my mothers or to my father in this life. (8)

verses.text:
सत्यः सत्याभिसंधश्च नित्यं सत्यपराक्रमः।
परलोकभयाद् भीतो निर्भयोऽस्तु पिता मम॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Let my father—who is ever truthful, true to his promise, truly valiant and afraid of falsehood, which brings disaster in the other world—be rid of fear in the other world by my redeeming the promise made by him to Kaikeyī. (9)

verses.text:
तस्यापि हि भवेदस्मिन् कर्मण्यप्रतिसंहृते।
सत्यं नेति मनस्तापस्तस्य तापस्तपेच्च माम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, so long as this business of installation, is not liquidated, the painful consciousness that his veracity has not been vindicated will lurk in his (father’s) mind too and his agony is sure to distress me as well. (10)

verses.text:
अभिषेकविधानं तु तस्मात् संहृत्य लक्ष्मण।
अन्वगेवाहमिच्छामि वनं गन्तुमितः पुरः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Therefore, having done away with this ceremony of installation, O Lakṣmaṇa, I for my part wish to proceed from this city to the forest soon. (11)

verses.text:
मम प्रव्राजनादद्य कृतकृत्या नृपात्मजा।
सुतं भरतमव्यग्रमभिषेचयतां ततः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Accomplished of purpose as a result of my banishment, let Kaikeyī (the daughter of King Aśwapati) then install her son, Bharata, this very day, without any distraction of mind. (12)

verses.text:
मयि चीराजिनधरे जटामण्डलधारिणि।
गतेऽरण्यं च कैकेय्या भविष्यति मनः सुखम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “On my having proceeded to the forest, clad in the bark of trees and deerskin and wearing a coil of matted locks, the mind of Kaikeyī will be gratified. (13)

verses.text:
बुद्धिः प्रणीता येनेयं मनश्च सुसमाहितम्।
तं नु नार्हामि संक्लेष्टुं प्रव्रजिष्यामि मा चिरम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Surely I ought not to give offence to Providence by crossing His purpose, as it is by him that this idea of sending me away into exile to the forest has been infused into the mind of Kaikeyī through the machination of Mantharā and her mind fully set at rest on the question. I shall accordingly go into exile, let there be no delay. (14)

verses.text:
कृतान्त एव सौमित्रे द्रष्टव्यो मत्प्रवासने।
राज्यस्य च वितीर्णस्य पुनरेव निवर्तने॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Providence alone should be regarded, O son of Sumitrā, as responsible for sending me into exile as well as for taking back from me the sovereignty of Ayodhyā offered to me. (15)

verses.text:
कैकेय्याः प्रतिपत्तिर्हि कथं स्यान्मम वेदने।
यदि तस्या न भावोऽयं कृतान्तविहितो भवेत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How could the resolution of persecuting me by way of sending me into exile enter the mind of Kaikeyī (my own mother) if this idea of hers were not prompted by Providence? (16)

verses.text:
जानासि हि यथा सौम्य न मातृषु ममान्तरम्।
भूतपूर्वं विशेषो वा तस्या मयि सुतेऽपि वा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “For, you already know, O gentle brother, that no discrimination was ever made by me between my mothers in the past nor was any distinction made even by her between her son and myself. (17)

verses.text:
सोऽभिषेकनिवृत्त्यर्थैः प्रवासार्थैश्च दुर्वचैः।
उग्रैर्वाक्यैरहं तस्या नान्यद् दैवात् समर्थये॥ १८॥
verses.m: “As such I cannot hold anything other than the will of Providence responsible for her galling the king with pungent words, hard to utter (even for any other), urging him to stop my installation and sending me into exile. (18)

verses.text:
कथं प्रकृतिसम्पन्ना राजपुत्री तथागुणा।
ब्रूयात् सा प्राकृतेव स्त्री मत्पीड्यं भर्तृसंनिधौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: “How else could she, a princess of gentle disposition and possessing such rare qualities of head and heart utter like an uncouth woman in the presence of her husband words intended to torment me?(19)

verses.text:
यदचिन्त्यं तु तद् दैवं भूतेष्वपि न हन्यते।
व्यक्तं मयि च तस्यां च पतितो हि विपर्ययः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “That which cannot be foreseen is surely a decree of Providence and it cannot be set aside by any among created beings. Evidently, therefore, it is by the will of Providence that the unexpected has befallen me as well as her. (20)

verses.text:
कश्च दैवेन सौमित्रे योद्धुमुत्सहते पुमान्।
यस्य नु ग्रहणं किंचित् कर्मणोऽन्यन्न दृश्यते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Again, what man can dare contend, O son of Sumitrā, with destiny, of which no indication can be found other than the consequence of an act? (21)

verses.text:
सुखदुःखे भयक्रोधौ लाभालाभौ भवाभवौ।
यस्य किंचित् तथाभूतं ननु दैवस्य कर्म तत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Joy and sorrow, fear and anger, gain and loss, birth and death and whatever similar experience comes to a particular individual, that is unquestionably the work of Providence. (22)

verses.text:
ऋषयोऽप्युग्रतपसो दैवेनाभिप्रचोदिताः।
उत्सृज्य नियमांस्तीव्रान् भ्रश्यन्ते काममन्युभिः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Strongly impelled by destiny, even sages practising severe austerities are led astray by concupiscence and anger etc., abandoning their strict observance. (23)

verses.text:
असंकल्पितमेवेह यदकस्मात् प्रवर्तते।
निवर्त्यारब्धमारम्भैर्ननु दैवस्य कर्म तत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Setting aside an undertaking already commenced with the help of requisite materials, that which takes place unexpectedly without any ostensible cause, is undoubtedly the doing of Providence.(24)

verses.text:
एतया तत्त्वया बुद्ध्या संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
व्याहतेऽप्यभिषेके मे परितापो न विद्यते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “In spite of my installation having been interrupted, no agony is experienced by me, who have fully steadied my mind by recourse to this true wisdom. (25)

verses.text:
तस्मादपरितापः संस्त्वमप्यनुविधाय माम्।
प्रतिसंहारय क्षिप्रमाभिषेचनिकीं क्रियाम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Therefore, rid of agony and following my line of thought, cause you the proceedings of installation to be stopped at once. (26)

verses.text:
एभिरेव घटैः सर्वैरभिषेचनसम्भृतैः।
मम लक्ष्मण तापस्ये व्रतस्नानं भविष्यति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “With all these jars containing sacred waters, brought together for my consecration, O Lakṣmaṇa, will be accomplished by my bath at the inauguration of my vow of asceticism. (27)

verses.text:
अथवा किं मयैतेन राज्यद्रव्यमयेन तु।
उद्धृतं मे स्वयं तोयं व्रतादेशं करिष्यति॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Or, what have I to do in reality with this water accompanied in abundance by auspicious articles collected for the installation? Water drawn by me personally will serve to inaugurate my vow of asceticism. (28)

verses.text:
मा च लक्ष्मण संतापं कार्षीर्लक्ष्म्या विपर्यये।
राज्यं वा वनवासो वा वनवासो महोदयः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Moreover, O Lakṣmaṇa, do not give way to remorse over the loss of fortune. To me it matters little whether sovereignty falls to my lot or exile, the latter being of greater consequence (in that it will be free from worries and favourable for asceticism and will afford me an opportunity to redeem father’s pledge given to Kaikeyī). (29)

verses.text:
न लक्ष्मणास्मिन् मम राज्यविघ्ने
माता यवीयस्यभिशङ्कितव्या।
दैवाभिपन्ना न पिता कथंचि-
ज्जानासि दैवं हि तथाप्रभावम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Our youngest mother, Kaikeyī, ought not on any account be suspected of having brought about this interruption in my installation nor our father, both of whom are subject to the control of Providence; for, you know Providence to be possessed of unfailing power.” (30)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणोऽवाक् शिरा इव।
ध्यात्वा मध्यं जगामाशु सहसा दैन्यहर्षयोः॥ १॥
verses.m: Pondering with his head bent low, as it were, while Śrī Rāma spoke as aforesaid, Lakṣmaṇa for his part quickly and suddenly began to swing between dejection at the interruption of Śrī Rāma’s installation and delight over the latter’s steadfast devotion to righteousness. (1)

verses.text:
तदा तु बद्ध्वा भ्रुकुटीं भ्रुवोर्मध्ये नरर्षभः।
निशश्वास महासर्पो बिलस्थ इव रोषितः॥ २॥
verses.m: Nay, knitting his brows at the space between his eyebrows, at that time, Lakṣmaṇa, a jewel among men, hissed like an enraged cobra in a hole. (2)

verses.text:
तस्य दुष्प्रतिवीक्ष्यं तद् भ्रुकुटीसहितं तदा।
बभौ क्रुद्धस्य सिंहस्य मुखस्य सदृशं मुखम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: That frowning aspect of his, which was difficult to gaze on, appeared at that moment like the face of an infuriated lion. (3)

verses.text:
अग्रहस्तं विधुन्वंस्तु हस्ती हस्तमिवात्मनः।
तिर्यगूर्ध्वं शरीरे च पातयित्वा शिरोधराम्॥ ४॥
अग्राक्ष्णा वीक्षमाणस्तु तिर्यग्भ्रातरमब्रवीत्।
अस्थाने सम्भ्रमो यस्य जातो वै सुमहानयम्॥ ५॥
धर्मदोषप्रसङ्गेन लोकस्यानतिशङ्कया।
कथं ह्येतदसम्भ्रान्तस्त्वद्विधो वक्तुमर्हति॥ ६॥
यथा ह्येवमशौण्डीरं शौण्डीरः क्षत्रियर्षभः।
किं नाम कृपणं दैवमशक्तमभिशंससि॥ ७॥
verses.m: Violently shaking his forearm precisely as an elephant would shake its proboscis, and flinging his neck horizontally as well as upwards on his body, and gazing obliquely with a corner of his eye, Lakṣmaṇa for his part spoke as follows to his brother, Śrī Rāma : “At an inopportune moment indeed has this inordinate flurry appeared in you for fear of lapsing from the path of duty and with a view to disarming the grave suspicion in the mind of the people (that a prince who is disloyal to his father could not be expected to rule his subjects righteously). Indeed, how can a man like yourself speak as you are doing, unless he is agitated? I wonder how you regularly glorify in this way fate—which is indeed ineffectual, pitiable and impotent—powerful and foremost among the Kṣatriyas as you are? (4—7)

verses.text:
पापयोस्ते कथं नाम तयोः शङ्का न विद्यते।
सन्ति धर्मोपधासक्ता धर्मात्मन् किं न बुध्यसे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “It is a matter of surprise how there is no suspicion in your mind about that wicked couple (Daśaratha and Kaikeyī). Don’t you know, O pious Rāma, that there are men devoted to a semblance of piety? (8)

verses.text:
तयोः सुचरितं स्वार्थं शाठ्यात् परिजिहीर्षतोः।
यदि नैवं व्यवसितं स्याद्धि प्रागेव राघव।
तयोः प्रागेव दत्तश्च स्याद् वरःप्रकृतश्च सः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Had this not actually been at the very outset the intention, O scion of Raghu, of the couple, who seek through fraud for their own selfish end, to forsake you, the one who have such a noble conduct, the installation would not have been undertaken at all. Nay, if the story of the boon granted by the one and received by the other had been real, it would have been granted even before the preparations for the installation were taken in hand. (9)

verses.text:
लोकविद्विष्टमारब्धं त्वदन्यस्याभिषेचनम्।
नोत्सहे सहितुं वीर तत्र मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “What has now been commenced is disliked by the people. I cannot brook, O heroic Rāma, the installation of anyone other than you. Be pleased to forgive my intolerance in this matter. (10)

verses.text:
येनैवमागता द्वैधं तव बुद्धिर्महामते।
सोऽपि धर्मो मम द्वेष्यो यत्प्रसङ्गाद् विमुह्यसि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Repellent to me is that piety too by the thought of which your mind, which was once inclined to accept the office of Prince Regent, has thus been diverted from the purpose, O noble-minded brother, and through devotion to which you are falling a prey to infatuation. (11)

verses.text:
कथं त्वं कर्मणा शक्तः कैकेयीवशवर्तिनः।
करिष्यसि पितुर्वाक्यमधर्मिष्ठं विगर्हितम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Had it not been so how are you going to redeem the most unrighteous and reproachful pledge of your father who is under the thumb of Kaikeyī, even though you are able to set things right by recourse to action? (12)

verses.text:
यदयं किल्बिषाद् भेदः कृतोऽप्येवं न गृह्यते।
जायते तत्र मे दुःखं धर्मसङ्गश्च गर्हितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Since this interruption in your installation, though brought about through machination in the shape of connecting the story of a boon granted by the Emperor, is not being recognized by you as such, agony is caused to me on that account and partiality to such false piety is reprehensible in my view. (13)

verses.text:
तवायं धर्मसंयोगो लोकस्यास्य विगर्हितः।
मनसापि कथं कामं कुर्यात् त्वां कामवृत्तयोः।
तयोस्त्वहितयोर्नित्यं शत्र्वोः पित्रभिधानयोः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “This adherence of yours to piety is condemned in the eyes of the people of Ayodhyā. How can anyone other than you fulfil, even in thought, the desire of the aforesaid two enemies, bearing the name of parents, who follow their own pleasure and are ever hostile to you? (14)

verses.text:
यद्यपि प्रतिपत्तिस्ते दैवी चापि तयोर्मतम्।
तथाप्युपेक्षणीयं ते न मे तदपि रोचते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Although it is your belief that even the decision of your parents to stop your installation is inspired by fate, it nonetheless deserves to be ignored by yourself. Such a decree even of fate does not please me.(15)

verses.text:
विक्लवो वीर्यहीनो यः स दैवमनुवर्तते।
वीराः सम्भावितात्मानो न दैवं पर्युपासते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “He alone who is cowardly and powerless trusts in fate. The valiant, who are possessed of a strong mind, never seek shelter in fate. (16)

verses.text:
दैवं पुरुषकारेण यः समर्थः प्रबाधितुम्।
न दैवेन विपन्नार्थः पुरुषः सोऽवसीदति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “A man who is capable of setting aside the decree of fate through personal effort never feels disheartened on his purpose being thwarted by destiny. (17)

verses.text:
द्रक्ष्यन्ति त्वद्य दैवस्य पौरुषं पुरुषस्य च।
दैवमानुषयोरद्य व्यक्ता व्यक्तिर्भविष्यति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “People will see today the relative strength of fate and a human being. The distinction between fate and a human being will be manifest today. (18)

verses.text:
अद्य मे पौरुषहतं दैवं द्रक्ष्यन्ति वै जनाः।
यैर्दैवादाहतं तेऽद्य दृष्टं राज्याभिषेचनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “People by whom your installation on the throne of Ayodhyā has been seen interrupted through destiny today will find fate worsted this very day by my valour. (19)

verses.text:
अत्यङ्कुशमिवोद्दामं गजं मदजलोद्धतम्।
प्रधावितमहं दैवं पौरुषेण निवर्तये॥ २०॥
verses.m: “By sheer dint of bravery I shall repulse destiny rushing headlong like an uncontrollable and unrestrained elephant, haughty with fluid exuding from its temples. (20)

verses.text:
लोकपालाः समस्तास्ते नाद्य रामाभिषेचनम्।
न च कृत्स्नास्त्रयो लोका विहन्युः किं पुनः पिता॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Neither all the guardians of the spheres nor the denizens of all the three worlds, O Rāma, can interrupt your consecration today; how, then, can father do it? (21)

verses.text:
यैर्विवासस्तवारण्ये मिथो राजन् समर्थितः।
अरण्ये ते विवत्स्यन्ति चतुर्दश समास्तथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: “They alone by whom, O king, has your exile to the forest been unanimously supported will likewise live in exile for fourteen years. (22)

verses.text:
अहं तदाशां धक्ष्यामि पितुस्तस्याश्च या तव।
अभिषेकविघातेन पुत्रराज्याय वर्तते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I shall bring to naught that hope of father as well as of hers (Kaikeyī) which is directed towards securing sovereignty for her son through interruption of your consecration. (23)

verses.text:
मद्बलेन विरुद्धाय न स्याद् दैवबलं तथा।
प्रभविष्यति दुःखाय यथोग्रं पौरुषं मम॥ २४॥
verses.m: “For him who is antagonistic to my strength, the power of destiny will not prove helpful to the same extent as my fierce might will redound to his suffering. (24)

verses.text:
ऊर्ध्वं वर्षसहस्रान्ते प्रजापाल्यमनन्तरम्।
आर्यपुत्राः करिष्यन्ति वनवासं गते त्वयि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Later on when you have retired to take up your abode in the forest at the end of thousands of years, sons of your worthy self will rule over the people without interruption (leaving no room for others even then). (25)

verses.text:
पूर्वराजर्षिवृत्त्या हि वनवासोऽभिधीयते।
प्रजा निक्षिप्य पुत्रेषु पुत्रवत् परिपालने॥ २६॥
verses.m: “In conformity with the conduct of ancient royal sages, residence in the forest is recommended for kings only when they have committed the people to the care of their sons for being protected as sons. (26)

verses.text:
स चेद् राजन्यनेकाग्रे राज्यविभ्रमशङ्कया।
नैवमिच्छसि धर्मात्मन् राज्यं राम त्वमात्मनि॥ २७॥
verses.m: “If, constituted as you are, O pious-minded Rāma, you do not really seek sovereignty for yourself for fear of disaffection in the state, the king being irresolute in the matter of renouncing the kingship and retiring to the forest, you need not harbour any misgiving on that score. (27)

verses.text:
प्रतिजाने च ते वीर मा भूवं वीरलोकभाक्।
राज्यं च तव रक्षेयमहं वेलेव सागरम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Nay, I promise to you, O valiant brother, that I shall guard you as well as your kingdom even as the coastline guards the ocean and keeps it within bounds. Let me not earn the realms that fall to the share of heroes after death if I fail to do so. (28)

verses.text:
मङ्गलैरभिषिञ्चस्व तत्र त्वं व्यापृतो भव।
अहमेको महीपालानलं वारयितुं बलात्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Allow yourself to be consecrated by Vasiṣṭha and others with auspicious articles and be up and doing in that direction. I am enough to repel hostile monarchs forcibly single-handed. (29)

verses.text:
न शोभार्थाविमौ बाहू न धनुर्भूषणाय मे।
नासिराबन्धनार्थाय न शराः स्तम्भहेतवः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “These arms of mine are not intended to add to my charm nor is this bow meant to serve as an ornament for my body. Nor is my sword meant for being tied to my belt and hanging by my side as a badge of honour, nor are my arrows meant to serve as a support for some structure. (30)

verses.text:
अमित्रमथनार्थाय सर्वमेतच्चतुष्टयम्।
न चाहं कामयेऽत्यर्थं यः स्याच्छत्रुर्मतो मम॥ ३१॥
असिना तीक्ष्णधारेण विद्युच्चलितवर्चसा।
प्रगृहीतेन वै शत्रुं वज्रिणं वा न कल्पये॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “All these four exist only for crushing the enemy. Nor do I wish that I should not hew, with my uplifted keen-edged sword possessing an inconstant sheen like a flash of lightning, him who is considered to be my inveterate enemy, be he Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt. (31-32)

verses.text:
खड्गनिष्पेषनिष्पिष्टैर्गहना दुश्चरा च मे।
हस्त्यश्वरथिहस्तोरुशिरोभिर्भविता मही॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “The earth will be thickly set in no time with the trunks (or hands) of elephants, horses and warriors fighting in chariots, severed with the blows of my sword, and will become hard to tread. (33)

verses.text:
खड्गधाराहता मेऽद्य दीप्यमाना इवाग्नयः।
पतिष्यन्ति द्विषो भूमौ मेघा इव सविद्युतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Killed with the edge of my sword today and consequently bathed in blood, enemies will drop on the ground like so many blazing fires or clouds accompanied with flashes of lightning. (34)

verses.text:
बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणे प्रगृहीतशरासने।
कथं पुरुषमानी स्यात् पुरुषाणां मयि स्थिते॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “While I stand on the battlefield with finger-protectors (made of the skin of iguana) fastened glove-like round the left hand to prevent injury from a bow-string and with uplifted bow, how can anyone among men remain proud of his valour and dare stand before me? (35)

verses.text:
बहुभिश्चैकमत्यस्यन्नेकेन च बहूञ्जनान्।
विनियोक्ष्याम्यहं बाणान्नृवाजिगजमर्मसु॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Throwing down a single warrior with many shafts and many men with a single arrow, I shall dig arrows into the vitals of men, horses and elephants. (36)

verses.text:
अद्य मेऽस्त्रप्रभावस्य प्रभावः प्रभविष्यति।
राज्ञश्चाप्रभुतां कर्तुं प्रभुत्वं च तव प्रभो॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Today the effectiveness of the might of my weapons will manifest itself in order to prove the helplessness of the king, Daśaratha, and demonstrate your sovereignty, O lord ! (37)

verses.text:
अद्य चन्दनसारस्य केयूरामोक्षणस्य च।
वसूनां च विमोक्षस्य सुहृदां पालनस्य च॥ ३८॥
अनुरूपाविमौ बाहू राम कर्म करिष्यतः।
अभिषेचनविघ्नस्य कर्तॄणां ते निवारणे॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “These arms of mine, which are worthy of being daubed with sandal-paste and putting on a pair of armlets, as well as of giving away riches and protecting friends and relations, O Rāma, will exert themselves today to stop those who are interrupting your consecration. (38-39)

verses.text:
ब्रवीहि कोऽद्यैव मया वियुज्यतां
तवासुहृत् प्राणयशःसुहृज्जनैः।
यथा तवेयं वसुधा वशा भवेत्
तथैव मां शाधि तवास्मि किंकरः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Speak out, which enemy of yours may be deprived this very day of his life, fame of invincibility and relations. Pray, instruct me how to proceed so that the globe may be brought under your control. I am at your beck and call.” (40)

verses.text:
विमृज्य बाष्पं परिसान्त्व्य चासकृत्
स लक्ष्मणं राघववंशवर्धनः।
उवाच पित्रोर्वचने व्यवस्थितं
निबोध मामेष हि सौम्य सत्पथः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Wiping the tears of Lakṣmaṇa and comforting him more than once, Śrī Rāma, the promoter of Raghu’s race, replied, “Know me, gentle brother, to be firmly obedient to the command of my parents; for such is the path trodden by the righteous.” (41)

verses.text:
तं समीक्ष्य व्यवसितं पितुर्निर्देशपालने।
कौसल्या बाष्पसंरुद्धा वचो धर्मिष्ठमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving Śrī Rāma resolved on carrying out the command of his father, Kausalyā spoke as follows to her most pious son, her voice choked with tears : (1)

verses.text:
अदृष्टदुःखो धर्मात्मा सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः।
मयि जातो दशरथात् कथमुञ्छेन वर्तयेत्॥ २॥
