verses.m: “Ah! born of me through Daśaratha, how will the pious-minded boy, who has never known sorrow and who speaks kindly to all created beings, live on grains gleaned from a market-place (after the heaps collected there for sale have been disposed of)? (2)

verses.text:
यस्य भृत्याश्च दासाश्च मृष्टान्यन्नानि भुञ्जते।
कथं स भोक्ष्यते रामो वने मूलफलान्ययम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “How shall this boy, the same Rāma whose very dependants and servants partake of dainty dishes, eat roots and fruits in the forest? (3)

verses.text:
क एतच्छ्रद्दधेच्छ्रुत्वा कस्य वा न भवेद् भयम्।
गुणवान् दयितो राज्ञः काकुत्स्थो यद् विवास्यते॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Who will believe this story that Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, the pet child of the Emperor and rich in excellences, is being exiled? And who will not be alarmed to hear this? (4)

verses.text:
नूनं तु बलवाँल्लोके कृतान्तः सर्वमादिशन्।
लोके रामाभिरामस्त्वं वनं यत्र गमिष्यसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: Sure enough, in this world, O Rāma, where you, who are so charming, are going to retire to the forest, destiny alone is mighty and rules all. (5)

verses.text:
अयं तु मामात्मभवस्तवादर्शनमारुतः।
विलापदुःखसमिधो रुदिताश्रुहुताहुतिः॥ ६॥
चिन्ताबाष्पमहाधूमस्तवागमनचिन्तजः।
कर्शयित्वाधिकं पुत्र निःश्वासायाससम्भवः॥ ७॥
त्वया विहीनामिह मां शोकाग्निरतुलो महान्।
प्रधक्ष्यति यथा कक्ष्यं चित्रभानुर्हिमात्यये॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Emaciating me to a remarkable degree, my son, this huge and incomparable fire of grief—which has its source in the mind, is fanned by the wind of your impending absence and fed by the firewood of anguish caused by weeping and is nourished by oblations poured in the shape of tears welling up at the time of weeping, nay, which is crowned with voluminous smoke in the form of intensity of thought, which springs up from anxiety concerning your return from exile at the end of fourteen years and which grows in intensity through pumping in the form of respiration—will consume me, bereft of you, here in the same way as a forest fire burns away dry wood and grass etc., at the end of winter. (6—8)

verses.text:
कथं हि धेनुः स्वं वत्सं गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति।
अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि यत्र वत्स गमिष्यसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “It is well known how a milch cow follows its roaming calf. I too shall accordingly follow you whithersoever, my child, you will go.” (9)

verses.text:
यथा निगदितं मात्रा तद् वाक्यं पुरुषर्षभः।
श्रुत्वा रामोऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं मातरं भृशदुःखिताम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Duly hearing the aforesaid speech uttered by his mother, Śrī Rāma, a jewel among men, replied as follows to his mother, who was extremely distressed : (10)

verses.text:
कैकेय्या वञ्चितो राजा मयि चारण्यमाश्रिते।
भवत्या च परित्यक्तो न नूनं वर्तयिष्यति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Betrayed by Kaikeyī and particularly when I have retired to the forest, the king will surely not survive if he is further deserted by you. (11)

verses.text:
भर्तुः किल परित्यागो नृशंसः केवलं स्त्रियाः।
स भवत्या न कर्तव्यो मनसापि विगर्हितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Moreover, it is sheer cruelty on the part of a woman to desert her husband. That should not be done by you even with the mind; for it is highly deprecated. (12)

verses.text:
यावज्जीवति काकुत्स्थः पिता मे जगतीपतिः।
शुश्रूषा क्रियतां तावत् स हि धर्मः सनातनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “So long as my father, Emperor Daśaratha, a scion of Kakutstha, survives, let service be rendered to him by you; for such is the eternal moral code.” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु रामेण कौसल्या शुभदर्शना।
तथेत्युवाच सुप्रीता राममक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Feeling highly delighted when admonished as aforesaid by Śrī Rāma, Kausalyā of benign aspect, for her part, said “Amen !” to Śrī Rāma, who did things without undergoing any exertion. (14)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु वचनं रामो धर्मभृतां वरः।
भूयस्तामब्रवीद् वाक्यं मातरं भृशदुःखिताम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Addressed in the foregoing words, Śrī Rāma, the foremost among those upholding the cause of righteousness, however, further spoke as follows to his aforesaid mother, who was feeling deeply distressed : (15)

verses.text:
मया चैव भवत्या च कर्तव्यं वचनं पितुः।
राजा भर्ता गुरुः श्रेष्ठः सर्वेषामीश्वरः प्रभुः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Father’s command must be carried out by you as well as by me. He is the king, supporter, elder, superior, controller and master of us all. (16)

verses.text:
इमानि तु महारण्ये विहृत्य नव पञ्च च।
वर्षाणि परमप्रीत्या स्थास्यामि वचने तव॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Having sported in some great forest during the ensuing nine years and five with supreme delight, I shall then continue to be at your beck and call.” (17)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता प्रियं पुत्रं बाष्पपूर्णानना तदा।
उवाच परमार्ता तु कौसल्या सुतवत्सला॥ १८॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words, Kausalyā, for her part, who was full of affection for her son and was extremely miserable, then replied to her beloved son as follows, her face bathed in tears : (18)

verses.text:
आसां राम सपत्नीनां वस्तुं मध्ये न मे क्षमम्।
नय मामपि काकुत्स्थ वनं वन्यां मृगीमिव॥ १९॥
यदि ते गमने बुद्धिः कृता पितरपेक्षया।
तां तथा रुदतीं रामो रुदन् वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “It is not desirable for me, O Rāma, to live in the midst of these co-wives. If you have made up your mind to depart in deference to the wish of your father, pray, take me as well to the forest, O scion of Kakutstha, even as one would take a wild female deer.” Śrī Rāma, however, spoke to his mother, who was weeping as aforesaid : (19-20)

verses.text:
जीवन्त्या हि स्त्रिया भर्ता दैवतं प्रभुरेव च।
भवत्या मम चैवाद्य राजा प्रभवति प्रभुः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “For a married woman, so long as she is alive, her husband indeed is her deity as well as her lord. The king, our master, holds sway over you as well as over me today. (21)

verses.text:
न ह्यनाथा वयं राज्ञा लोकनाथेन धीमता।
भरतश्चापि धर्मात्मा सर्वभूतप्रियंवदः॥ २२॥
भवतीमनुवर्तेत स हि धर्मरतः सदा।
यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः॥ २३॥
श्रमं नावाप्नुयात् किंचिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु।
दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्॥ २४॥
राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।
व्रतोपवासनिरता या नारी परमोत्तमा॥ २५॥
भर्तारं नानुवर्तेत सा च पापगतिर्भवेत्।
भर्तुः शुश्रूषया नारी लभते स्वर्गमुत्तमम्॥ २६॥
अपि या निर्नमस्कारा निवृत्ता देवपूजनात्।
शुश्रूषामेव कुर्वीत भर्तुः प्रियहिते रता॥ २७॥
एष धर्मः स्त्रिया नित्यो वेदे लोके श्रुतः स्मृतः।
अग्निकार्येषु च सदा सुमनोभिश्च देवताः॥ २८॥
पूज्यास्ते मत्कृते देवि ब्राह्मणाश्चैव सत्कृताः।
एवं कालं प्रतीक्षस्व ममागमनकांक्षिणी॥ २९॥
नियता नियताहारा भर्तृशुश्रूषणे रता।
प्राप्स्यसे परमं कामं मयि पर्यागते सति॥ ३०॥
यदि धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो धारयिष्यति जीवितम्।
एवमुक्ता तु रामेण बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा॥ ३१॥
कौसल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।
गमने सुकृतां बुद्धिं न ते शक्नोमि पुत्रक॥ ३२॥
विनिवर्तयितुं वीर नूनं कालो दुरत्ययः।
गच्छ पुत्र त्वमेकाग्रो भद्रं तेऽस्तु सदा विभो॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “With the wise king continuing as the ruler of the world, surely we are not masterless. And Bharata too is pious-minded, speaks kindly to all created beings and is ever devoted to righteousness. He will undoubtedly serve you. Carefully act in such a way that when I have departed for the woods the king may not suffer agony in the least on account of grief caused by separation from his son, i.e., myself. And, remaining ever vigilant, constantly do good to the aged king, so that this poignant grief may not bring about his extinction. Nay, that woman who, though extremely noble and keenly devoted to sacred observances and fasts, does not serve her husband, is sure to attain the destiny of a sinner. Through service to one’s husband, on the other hand, even that woman who does not offer salutations to anyone other than her husband and is averse to the worship of gods, secures the highest heaven. Intent on doing that which is pleasing and good to her husband, a married woman should, therefore, do service to him alone: this is the lasting duty enjoined on a woman in the Vedas as well as in the Smṛti texts. Nay, while offering oblations to the fire, gods as well as celebrated Brāhmaṇas of noble vows should be worshipped with flowers and other articles for my sake, O godly lady ! Leading a regulated life and partaking of an austere fare, nay, devoted to the service of your husband, bide time as aforesaid, longing for my return from the forest. In this way you will attain the highest object of your desire when I have duly returned from the forest, provided, of course, the Emperor the foremost of those upholding the cause of righteousness retains his life.” Spoken to in these words by Śrī Rāma, however, Kausalyā, who was stricken with grief caused by the thought of the impending separation from her son, spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma, her eyes blinded with tears : “I cannot change your resolution to depart, which has been deliberately made, O dear and heroic son ! Surely destiny is hard to supersede. Therefore, depart you, my son, with an unwavering mind. Let good betide you at all times, O mighty son ! (22—33)

verses.text:
पुनस्त्वयि निवृत्ते तु भविष्यामि गतक्लमा।
प्रत्यागते महाभागे कृतार्थे चरितव्रते।
पितुरानृण्यतां प्राप्ते स्वपिष्ये परमं सुखम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “I shall be rid of affliction once more only when you have returned to Ayodhyā. I shall sleep most soundly only when you, my highly blessed son, return having accomplished your object and concluded your vow of leading a forest life for fourteen long years and thereby get square with i.e., cleared the debt of your father. (34)

verses.text:
कृतान्तस्य गतिः पुत्र दुर्विभाव्या सदा भुवि।
यस्त्वां संचोदयति मे वच आविध्य राघव॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “The course of destiny in this world is always hard to perceive, my son—the destiny which is urging you to depart setting aside my protest, O scion of Raghu ! (35)

verses.text:
गच्छेदानीं महाबाहो क्षेमेण पुनरागतः।
नन्दयिष्यसि मां पुत्र साम्ना श्लक्ष्णेन चारुणा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Depart now, O mighty-armed prince ! When you safely come back, you shall delight me, my son, with delightful and sweet words of consolation. (36)

verses.text:
अपीदानीं स कालः स्याद् वनात् प्रत्यागतं पुनः।
यत् त्वां पुत्रक पश्येयं जटावल्कलधारिणम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Would that be the time when I see you once more, my dear son, come back from the forest, wearing matted locks and the bark of trees, turned this very moment !” (37)

verses.text:
तथा हि रामं वनवासनिश्चितं
ददर्श देवी परमेण चेतसा।
उवाच रामं शुभलक्षणं वचो
बभूव च स्वस्त्ययनाभिकांक्षिणी॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Inasmuch as the pious lady, Kausalyā, perceived with her penetrating mind that Śrī Rāma was resolved to take up his abode in the forest, she spoke benedictory words to him and got inclined to perform rites of averting evil through recitation of sacred texts. (38)

verses.text:
सा विनीय तमायासमुपस्पृश्य जलं शुचि।
चकार माता रामस्य मङ्गलानि मनस्विनी॥ १॥
verses.m: Getting over through ratiocination the aforesaid agony caused by the thought of the impending separation from Śrī Rāma and sipping a little pure water in order to counteract the impurity occasioned by shedding tears, the high-minded mother Kausalyā performed rites conducive to the welfare of Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
न शक्यसे वारयितुं गच्छेदानीं रघूत्तम।
शीघ्रं च विनिवर्तस्व वर्तस्व च सतां क्रमे॥ २॥
verses.m: She said “Since your departure cannot be stopped, depart now, O jewel among the Raghus ! Nay, follow in the foot-steps of the righteous by redeeming your word of honour and return soon after serving the term of your exile. (2)

verses.text:
यं पालयसि धर्मं त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च।
स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥ ३॥
verses.m: “May that piety itself protect you on all sides—the piety which you scrupulously observe with love, O tiger among the scions of Raghu ! (3)

verses.text:
येभ्यः प्रणमसे पुत्र देवेष्वायतनेषु च।
ते च त्वामभिरक्षन्तु वने सह महर्षिभिः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “May those too to whom you humbly bow at cross-roads as well as in temples, my son, protect you on all sides alongwith eminent Ṛṣis. (4)

verses.text:
यानि दत्तानि तेऽस्त्राणि विश्वामित्रेण धीमता।
तानि त्वामभिरक्षन्तु गुणैः समुदितं सदा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “May those mystic missiles also that were imparted to you by the learned Viśwāmitra protect on all sides, you who are ever illumined by your excellences. (5)

verses.text:
पितृशुश्रूषया पुत्र मातृशुश्रूषया तथा।
सत्येन च महाबाहो चिरं जीवाभिरक्षितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Protected on all sides by the service you have rendered to your father and mothers as well as by your truthfulness, my mighty-armed son, may you live long ! (6)

verses.text:
समित्कुशपवित्राणि वेद्यश्चायतनानि च।
स्थण्डिलानि च विप्राणां शैला वृक्षाः क्षुपा ह्रदाः।
पतङ्गाः पन्नगाः सिंहास्त्वां रक्षन्तु नरोत्तम॥ ७॥
verses.m: “May the deities presiding over wooden sticks used for feeding the sacred fire, blades of the sacred Kuśa grass and rings of Kuśa grass worn on the fourth finger on sacrificial occasions, sacrificial altars, temples and sites selected by Brāhmaṇas for worship of gods, as well as mountains, trees, bushes, large and deep pools of water, birds, reptiles and lions protect you. O jewel among men !(7)

verses.text:
स्वस्ति साध्याश्च विश्वे च मरुतश्च महर्षिभिः।
स्वस्ति धाता विधाता च स्वस्ति पूषा भगोऽर्यमा॥ ८॥
लोकपालाश्च ते सर्वे वासवप्रमुखास्तथा।
ऋतवः षट् च ते सर्वे मासाः संवत्सराः क्षपाः॥ ९॥
दिनानि च मुहूर्ताश्च स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु ते सदा।
श्रुतिः स्मृतिश्च धर्मश्च पातु त्वां पुत्र सर्वतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Nay, may the Sādhyas and the Viśwedevas, two different classes of gods, and the wind-gods alongwith eminent Ṛṣis ensure your happiness; may the Cosmic Person and the creator bring happiness to you. May the gods Pūṣā, Bhaga and Aryamā (three of the twelve sons of Aditi) and the well-known guardians of the spheres with Indra at their head, as also the deities presiding over the six seasons, all the months, years, nights and days and hours always do good to you. Again, may Veda, the Smṛti texts taken as one body and piety incarnate protect you, my son, from all dangers. (8—10)

verses.text:
स्कन्दश्च भगवान् देवः सोमश्च सबृहस्पतिः।
सप्तर्षयो नारदश्च ते त्वां रक्षन्तु सर्वतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “May Lord Skanda, the younger son of Lord Śiva, and the moon-god alongwith the sage Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of gods, the well-known seven Ṛṣis as well as Sage Nārada guard you on all sides. (11)

verses.text:
ते चापि सर्वतः सिद्धा दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः।
स्तुता मया वने तस्मिन् पान्तु त्वां पुत्र नित्यशः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, glorified by me, may the celebrated Siddhas as well as the four quarters alongwith the guardians of the quarters protect you, my son, from day to day on all sides in that forest which you are going to inhabit.(12)

verses.text:
शैलाः सर्वे समुद्राश्च राजा वरुण एव च।
द्यौरन्तरिक्षं पृथिवी वायुश्च सचराचरः॥ १३॥
नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि ग्रहाश्च सह दैवतैः।
अहोरात्रे तथा संध्ये पान्तु त्वां वनमाश्रितम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “May all the seven principal mountains and oceans as well as the king of the oceans, Varuṇa (the god presiding over the waters), heaven, earth, the region intervening them, the atmosphere as well as the animate and inanimate creation, nay, all the lunar mansions as well as the sun and the planets alongwith the gods presiding over them, the deities presiding over day and night and the morning and evening twilights protect you while you remain in the forest. (13-14)

verses.text:
ऋतवश्चापि षट् चान्ये मासाः संवत्सरास्तथा।
कलाश्च काष्ठाश्च तथा तव शर्म दिशन्तु ते॥ १५॥
महावनेऽपि चरतो मुनिवेषस्य धीमतः।
तथा देवाश्च दैत्याश्च भवन्तु सुखदाः सदा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Again, may the deities presiding over the six seasons, the intercalary months and the years containing such months and even so measures of time known by the names of Kalā (equivalent to one minute) and Kāṣṭhā (1/30 of a Kalā or two seconds) grant you happiness. And may the gods and the Daityas (demons) too ever bestow happiness on you while you roam about in a large forest, clad as a hermit and full of wisdom. (15-16)

verses.text:
राक्षसानां पिशाचानां रौद्राणां क्रूरकर्मणाम्।
क्रव्यादानां च सर्वेषां मा भूत् पुत्रक ते भयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Let there be no fear to you, my dear son, from the fierce ogres, fiends of cruel deeds and all carnivorous animals. (17)

verses.text:
प्लवगा वृश्चिका दंशा मशकाश्चैव कानने।
सरीसृपाश्च कीटाश्च मा भूवन् गहने तव॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Let there be no monkeys, scorpions, gnats and mosquitoes, reptiles and insects in the impenetrable forest occupied by you. (18)

verses.text:
महाद्विपाश्च सिंहाश्च व्याघ्रा ऋक्षाश्च दंष्ट्रिणः।
महिषाः शृङ्गिणो रौद्रा न ते द्रुह्यन्तु पुत्रक॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Let not lordly elephants, lions, tigers, bears and other carnivorous animals and fierce buffaloes with prominent horns be hostile to you, my dear son ! (19)

verses.text:
नृमांसभोजना रौद्रा ये चान्ये सर्वजातयः।
मा च त्वां हिंसिषुः पुत्र मया सम्पूजितास्त्विह॥ २०॥
verses.m: “And let not other ferocious man-eaters, belonging to all species of living beings and propitiated by me here, kill you, my son ! (20)

verses.text:
आगमास्ते शिवाः सन्तु सिध्यन्तु च पराक्रमाः।
सर्वसम्पत्तयो राम स्वस्तिमान् गच्छ पुत्रक॥ २१॥
verses.m: “May your pathways be propitious and let your undertaking meet with success. May all kinds of wealth of the forest be at your disposal, O Rāma ! Depart you happily, my beloved son ! (21)

verses.text:
स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्वान्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यः पुनः पुनः।
सर्वेभ्यश्चैव देवेभ्यो ये च ते परिपन्थिनः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “May you enjoy security time and again against aerial beings and earthly creatures as well as against all the gods as also against those who are your adversaries. (22)

verses.text:
शुक्रः सोमश्च सूर्यश्च धनदोऽथ यमस्तथा।
पान्तु त्वामर्चिता राम दण्डकारण्यवासिनम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Worshipped by me, O Rāma, may the deities presiding over the planets Venus and the moon as also the sun and Kubera (the god of riches) and Yama (the god of retribution) protect you while you dwell in the forest of Daṇḍaka. (23)

verses.text:
अग्निर्वायुस्तथा धूमो मन्त्राश्चर्षिमुखच्युताः।
उपस्पर्शनकाले तु पान्तु त्वां रघुनन्दन॥ २४॥
verses.m: May the gods presiding over fire, the air and smoke as well as the sacred texts that have escaped from the lips of Ṛṣis and that will be uttered by you, actually protect you at the time of sipping water and bathing, O scion of Raghu ! (24)

verses.text:
सर्वलोकप्रभुर्ब्रह्मा भूतकर्तृ तथर्षयः।
ये च शेषाः सुरास्ते तु रक्षन्तु वनवासिनम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “May Brahmā, the suzerain lord of all the worlds, Brahma, the Infinite, responsible for the existence of all created beings, and the Ṛṣis as well as the gods that have not so far been mentioned by me, guard you while you reside in the forest.” (25)

verses.text:
इति माल्यैः सुरगणान् गन्धैश्चापि यशस्विनी।
स्तुतिभिश्चानुरूपाभिरानर्चायतलोचना ॥ २६॥
verses.m: Saying so, the illustrious Kausalyā, who had large eyes, worshipped the various gods with flowers and perfumes too as well as by means of hymns befitting them. (26)

verses.text:
ज्वलनं समुपादाय ब्राह्मणेन महात्मना।
हावयामास विधिना राममङ्गलकारणात्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Duly procuring fire, she caused oblations to be poured into it with due ceremony for the welfare of Śrī Rāma by a high-souled Brāhmaṇa. (27)

verses.text:
घृतं श्वेतानि माल्यानि समिधश्चैव सर्षपान्।
उपसम्पादयामास कौसल्या परमाङ्गना॥ २८॥
verses.m: Kausalyā, the lady par excellence, made available to the Brāhmaṇa ghee, white flowers, pieces of firewood for feeding the sacrificial fire and mustard seeds as well. (28)

verses.text:
उपाध्यायः स विधिना हुत्वा शान्तिमनामयम्।
हुतहव्यावशेषेण बाह्यं बलिमकल्पयत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having poured oblations into the sacred fire according to the scriptural ordinance for the sake of security and health of her son the priest offered oblations to Indra and the other nine guardians of the ten directions outside the area reserved for fire-worship with the remnants of materials used as offering to the fire. (29)

verses.text:
मधुदध्यक्षतघृतैः स्वस्तिवाच्यं द्विजांस्ततः।
वाचयामास रामस्य वने स्वस्त्ययनक्रियाम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: She then got Brāhmaṇas—who were supplied with honey, curds, unbroken grains of rice and ghee in order to enable them to invoke blessings on Śrī Rāma by the repetition of certain Mantras—to utter prayers for the welfare of Śrī Rāma in the forest. (30)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्मै द्विजेन्द्राय राममाता यशस्विनी।
दक्षिणां प्रददौ काम्यां राघवं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: The illustrious Kausalyā, Śrī Rāma’s mother, next bestowed on the aforesaid leader of Brāhmaṇas his fee as desired by him and spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma : (31)

verses.text:
यन्मङ्गलं सहस्राक्षे सर्वदेवनमस्कृते।
वृत्रनाशे समभवत् तत् ते भवतु मङ्गलम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “May the same victory woo you as wooed Indra (the thousand-eyed god), who is hailed by all the gods on the destruction of the demon Vṛtra. (32)

verses.text:
यन्मङ्गलं सुपर्णस्य विनताकल्पयत् पुरा।
अमृतं प्रार्थयानस्य तत् ते भवतु मङ्गलम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “May the same blessing descend on you as Vinatā (the mother of Garuḍa) invoked in the past on Garuḍa, who sought for nectar. (33)

verses.text:
अमृतोत्पादने दैत्यान् घ्नतो वज्रधरस्य यत्।
अदितिर्मङ्गलं प्रादात् तत् ते भवतु मङ्गलम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Let the same blessing come to you as Aditi, the mother of the gods, invoked on Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, while he was engaged in making short work of the Daityas at the time of extracting nectar out of the ocean of milk. (34)

verses.text:
त्रिविक्रमान् प्रक्रमतो विष्णोरतुलतेजसः।
यदासीन्मङ्गलं राम तत् ते भवतु मङ्गलम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Let the same good fortune come to you as attended Lord Viṣṇu, who is endowed with immense glory, while He took the three well-known strides in order to measure the three worlds, O Rāma ! (35)

verses.text:
ऋषयः सागरा द्वीपा वेदा लोका दिशश्च ते।
मङ्गलानि महाबाहो दिशन्तु शुभमङ्गलम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “May Ṛṣis, the seven oceans, the same number of Dwīpas (principal divisions of the globe girdled by them), the four Vedas, the three spheres and the well-known four quarters confer blessings, nay, the blessing of all blessings on you, O mighty-armed prince !” (36)

verses.text:
इति पुत्रस्य शेषाश्च कृत्वा शिरसि भामिनी।
गन्धैश्चापि समालभ्य राममायतलोचना॥ ३७॥
औषधीं च सुसिद्धार्थां विशल्यकरणीं शुभाम्।
चकार रक्षां कौसल्या मन्त्रैरभिजजाप च॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Saying so and fixing unbroken grains of rice on Śrī Rāma’s forehead as a form of benediction, and also daubing him with sandal-pastes of various kinds, the large-eyed Kausalyā, a proud woman, fastened about his wrist by way of an amulet a herb known by the name of Viśalyakaraṇī (so-called because it helps in painlessly extracting an arrow stuck into one’s body), whose efficacy had been amply proved, with the recitation of sacred texts and further muttered the Mantras in order to heighten its virtue. (37-38)

verses.text:
उवाचापि प्रहृष्टेव सा दुःखवशवर्तिनी।
वाङ्मात्रेण न भावेन वाचा संसज्जमानया॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Nay, she also spoke the Mantras aloud like one overjoyed, anxious as she was not to mar the joy and damp the enthusiasm of Śrī Rāma, although she was in the grip of sorrow and repeated the Mantras only mechanically in a faltering voice and not with her heart. (39)

verses.text:
आनम्य मूर्ध्नि चाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनी।
अवदत् पुत्रमिष्टार्थो गच्छ राम यथासुखम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Bending low and smelling the head of Śrī Rāma and embracing him, the illustrious lady, Kausalyā, said to Śrī Rāma, “Depart at ease, O Rāma, accomplished of purpose as you are. (40)

verses.text:
अरोगं सर्वसिद्धार्थमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्।
पश्यामि त्वां सुखं वत्स संधितं राजवर्त्मसु॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “I shall happily see you come back in sound health to Ayodhyā having all your objects accomplished and moving at peace with all on the main roads of Ayodhyā. (41)

verses.text:
प्रणष्टदुःखसंकल्पा हर्षविद्योतितानना।
द्रक्ष्यामि त्वां वनात् प्राप्तं पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “All my thoughts of sorrow completely vanished and my face illumined with joy I shall behold you returned from the forest like the full moon become visible on the horizon. (42)

verses.text:
भद्रासनगतं राम वनवासादिहागतम्।
द्रक्ष्यामि च पुनस्त्वां तु तीर्णवन्तं पितुर्वचः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “I shall undoubtedly see you returned here from your sojourn in the forest, having implemented the word of your father, and installed on the throne, O Rāma ! (43)

verses.text:
मङ्गलैरुपसम्पन्नो वनवासादिहागतः।
वध्वाश्च मम नित्यं त्वं कामान् संवर्ध याहि भोः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Having returned here from the forest and clad in festal robes and adorned with festal ornaments, ever fulfil the desires of my daughter-in-law. Depart now, O Rāma ! (44)

verses.text:
मयार्चिता देवगणाः शिवादयो
महर्षयो भूतगणाः सुरोरगाः।
अभिप्रयातस्य वनं चिराय ते
हितानि कांक्षन्तु दिशश्च राघव॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Worshipped by me, let the hosts of gods headed by Lord Śiva, the eminent Ṛṣis, the multitudes of spirits, the celestial serpents and the deities presiding over the four quarters wish well for a long time of you when you have set out for the forest, O scion of Raghu !” (45)

verses.text:
अतीव चाश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचना
समाप्य च स्वस्त्ययनं यथाविधि।
प्रदक्षिणं चापि चकार राघवं
पुनः पुनश्चापि निरीक्ष्य सस्वजे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Nay, having finished the sacred rite of invoking blessings on Śrī Rāma with due ceremony, Kausalyā whose eyes were overflowing with tears, further went clockwise round Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and, gazing on him again and again, embraced him. (46)

verses.text:
तया हि देव्या च कृतप्रदक्षिणो
निपीड्य मातुश्चरणौ पुनः पुनः।
जगाम सीतानिलयं महायशाः
स राघवः प्रज्वलितस्तया श्रिया॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Circumambulated clockwise by the said pious lady and pressing as a token of reverence his mother’s feet again and again, that highly illustrious scion of Raghu, irradiated as he was by the splendour occasioned by the mother’s benedictory rites, proceeded to Sītā’s apartments. (47)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य तु कौसल्यां रामः सम्प्रस्थितो वनम्।
कृतस्वस्त्ययनो मात्रा धर्मिष्ठे वर्त्मनि स्थितः॥ १॥
विराजयन् राजसुतो राजमार्गं नरैर्वृतम्।
हृदयान्याममन्थेव जनस्य गुणवत्तया॥ २॥
verses.m: Saluting Kausalyā while about to set out for the forest, Śrī Rāma, for his part, on whom blessings had been invoked by his mother and who stuck to the most righteous path, agitated as were the hearts of the people that had gathered there, through his richness in excellences of various kinds, illumining at the same time by his very proximity the king’s highway crowded with men anxious to have a look at the prince. (1-2)

verses.text:
वैदेही चापि तत् सर्वं न शुश्राव तपस्विनी।
तदेव हृदि तस्याश्च यौवराज्याभिषेचनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, in her turn, who had been observing austere vows, had not so far heard all that had happened in the meantime, causing interruption in the installation of Śrī Rāma and making for his exile into the forest, so that the aforesaid installation alone of Śrī Rāma in the office of Prince Regent stood foremost in her heart. (3)

verses.text:
देवकार्यं स्म सा कृत्वा कृतज्ञा हृष्टचेतना।
अभिज्ञा राजधर्माणां राजपुत्री प्रतीक्षति॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having offered worship to the gods, the celebrated princess, who knew her duty and was conversant with the moral code prescribed for kings, was waiting for her husband with a delighted mind. (4)

verses.text:
प्रविवेशाथ रामस्तु स्ववेश्म सुविभूषितम्।
प्रहृष्टजनसम्पूर्णं ह्रिया किंचिदवाङ्मुखः॥ ५॥
verses.m: In the meantime Śrī Rāma for his part entered his gynaeceum, which was most tastefully decorated and was crowded with overjoyed attendants, his head bent somewhat low through bashfulness. (5)

verses.text:
अथ सीता समुत्पत्य वेपमाना च तं पतिम्।
अपश्यच्छोकसंतप्तं चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Forthwith springing up from her seat, Sītā tremblingly saw her celebrated husband stricken with grief, his mind perplexed with anxiety. (6)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा स हि धर्मात्मा न शशाक मनोगतम्।
तं शोकं राघवः सोढुं ततो विवृततां गतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Seeing her the said Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, whose mind was given to righteousness, could not contain that grief existing in his mind; hence it became manifest. (7)

verses.text:
विवर्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा तं प्रस्विन्नममर्षणम्।
आह दुःखाभिसंतप्ता किमिदानीमिदं प्रभो॥ ८॥
verses.m: Seeing him pale of countenance, bathed in perspiration and unable to restrain his grief, Sītā, who felt sore stricken with grief, said, “What is this now, my lord? (8)

verses.text:
अद्य बार्हस्पतः श्रीमान् युक्तः पुष्येण राघव।
प्रोच्यते ब्राह्मणैः प्राज्ञैः केन त्वमसि दुर्मनाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The auspicious constellation Puṣya, which is presided over by the sage Bṛhaspati and which is propitious for installation is in the ascendant today. The ceremony is recommended by learned Brāhmaṇas when the moon is in conjunction with the said asterism, O scion of Raghu ! Wherefore then are you ill at ease? (9)

verses.text:
न ते शतशलाकेन जलफेननिभेन च।
आवृतं वदनं वल्गु च्छत्रेणाभिविराजते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Your lovely countenance does not shine splendidly as it should when canopied by an umbrella white as foam and provided with a hundred ribs. (10)

verses.text:
व्यजनाभ्यां च मुख्याभ्यां शतपत्रनिभेक्षणम्।
चन्द्रहंसप्रकाशाभ्यां वीज्यते न तवाननम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nor is your lotus-eyed face, I find, being fanned as it should with a pair of excellent chowries shining like the moon and a swan. (11)

verses.text:
वाग्मिनो वन्दिनश्चापि प्रहृष्टास्त्वां नरर्षभ।
स्तुवन्तो नाद्य दृश्यन्ते मङ्गलैः सूतमागधाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nor again are overjoyed minstrels and bards or even eloquent panegyrists seen extolling you in words full of benedictions today, O jewel among men! (12)

verses.text:
न ते क्षौद्रं च दधि च ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः।
मूर्ध्नि मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्य ददति स्म विधानतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Vedas have not poured with due ceremony honey and curds alongwith water from holy places on your head after you had taken a full bath drenching your head too. (13)

verses.text:
न त्वां प्रकृतयः सर्वाः श्रेणीमुख्याश्च भूषिताः।
अनुव्रजितुमिच्छन्ति पौरजानपदास्तथा॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Nor do all the king’s ministers and the foremost among the traders, decked with ornaments, nor again the citizens and people belonging to the countryside seek to follow you in state. (14)

verses.text:
चतुर्भिर्वेगसम्पन्नैर्हयैः काञ्चनभूषणैः।
मुख्यः पुष्परथो युक्तः किं न गच्छति तेऽग्रतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “How does an excellent chariot used for travelling or pleasure and driven by four swift horses, decked with gold ornaments, not go ahead of you? (15)

verses.text:
न हस्ती चाग्रतः श्रीमान् सर्वलक्षणपूजितः।
प्रयाणे लक्ष्यते वीर कृष्णमेघगिरिप्रभः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Nor is a glorious elephant, adorned with all noble characteristics and resembling a mountain crowned with a dark cloud, seen ahead of you in your drive back to the gynaeceum, O gallant prince? (16)

verses.text:
न च काञ्चनचित्रं ते पश्यामि प्रियदर्शन।
भद्रासनं पुरस्कृत्य यान्तं वीर पुरःसरम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nor again do I perceive marching before you a servant carrying in his hand an excellent seat (sitting mat) embroidered with a gold figure, O valiant prince of delightful appearance ! (17)

verses.text:
अभिषेको यदा सज्जः किमिदानीमिदं तव।
अपूर्वो मुखवर्णश्च न प्रहर्षश्च लक्ष्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “When the preparations for your consecration are complete, how is it that the colour of your face appears so changed and no great joy is perceived in you at this moment?” (18)

verses.text:
इतीव विलपन्तीं तां प्रोवाच रघुनन्दनः।
सीते तत्रभवांस्तातः प्रव्राजयति मां वनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, replied as follows to Sītā, who was wailing as aforesaid : “My adorable father, O Śītā, is sending me into exile to the forest. (19)

verses.text:
कुले महति सम्भूते धर्मज्ञे धर्मचारिणि।
शृणु जानकि येनेदं क्रमेणाद्यागतं मम॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Hear in order of sequence, O daughter of Janaka, descended, as you are, in a noble family, knowing as you do what is right and practising virtue, wherefore this exile has fallen to my lot today. (20)

verses.text:
राज्ञा सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन पित्रा दशरथेन वै।
कैकेय्यै मम मात्रे तु पुरा दत्तौ महावरौ॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a couple of momentous boons were actually granted in the days gone by in favour of mother, Kaikeyī, by my father, King Daśaratha, who is so true to his promise. (21)

verses.text:
तयाद्य मम सज्जेऽस्मिन्नभिषेके नृपोद्यते।
प्रचोदितः स समयो धर्मेण प्रतिनिर्जितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The preparations for my consecration, arranged through the Emperor’s endeavour, being complete today, the king was pressed hard by her to grant those boons and, having been bound with an oath, was completely brought under her thumb on grounds of morality. (22)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यं दण्डके मया।
पित्रा मे भरतश्चापि यौवराज्ये नियोजितः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I must take up my abode in the forest of Daṇḍaka for fourteen years and, furthermore, Bharata has been nominated by my father for the office of Prince Regent. (23)

verses.text:
सोऽहं त्वामागतो द्रष्टुं प्रस्थितो विजनं वनम्।
भरतस्य समीपे ते नाहं कथ्यः कदाचन॥ २४॥
verses.m: “As such I have come to see you while on my way to the lonely forest of Daṇḍaka. I should never be praised by you in the presence of Bharata whenever he calls on you in order to pay his respects to you, lest you should forfeit his goodwill. (24)

verses.text:
ऋद्धियुक्ता हि पुरुषा न सहन्ते परस्तवम्।
तस्मान्न ते गुणाः कथ्या भरतस्याग्रतो मम॥ २५॥
verses.m: “For, men endowed with power and fortune do not brook to hear the glorification of others. Therefore my virtues should never be extolled by you before Bharata. (25)

verses.text:
अहं ते नानुवक्तव्यो विशेषेण कदाचन।
अनुकूलतया शक्यं समीपे तस्य वर्तितुम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I should never be exalted to the skies by you even before your companions. You can stay with him only by behaving conformably to him. (26)

verses.text:
तस्मै दत्तं नृपतिना यौवराज्यं सनातनम्।
स प्रसाद्यस्त्वया सीते नृपतिश्च विशेषतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The office of Prince Regent has been conferred on him by the king once for all. He should, therefore, be pleased by you, O Sītā, more so because he is going to be the king as well. (27)

verses.text:
अहं चापि प्रतिज्ञां तां गुरोः समनुपालयन्।
वनमद्यैव यास्यामि स्थिरीभव मनस्विनि॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Duly implementing the aforesaid pledge of my father, I for my part shall proceed to the forest this very day. Please remain firm, O high-minded lady ! (28)

verses.text:
याते च मयि कल्याणि वनं मुनिनिषेवितम्।
व्रतोपवासपरया भवितव्यं त्वयानघे॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Nay, when I have left for the forest, inhabited by ascetics, O blessed lady, you should take to sacred observances and fasts, O sinless one ! (29)

verses.text:
कल्यमुत्थाय देवानां कृत्वा पूजां यथाविधि।
वन्दितव्यो दशरथः पिता मम जनेश्वरः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Rising at dawn and after performing worship of the gods according to the scriptural ordinance, King Daśaratha, my father, must be saluted by you. (30)

verses.text:
माता च मम कौसल्या वृद्धा संतापकर्शिता।
धर्ममेवाग्रतः कृत्वा त्वत्तः सम्मानमर्हति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “My mother, Kausalyā too, aged as she is and emaciated through agony, deserves to be duly respected by you since you must keep virtue foremost in your mind. (31)

verses.text:
वन्दितव्याश्च ते नित्यं याः शेषा मम मातरः।
स्नेहप्रणयसम्भोगैः समा हि मम मातरः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Those others too who are related to me as mothers deserve to be saluted by you everyday since all mothers are equal in my eyes, in point of affection and goodwill they cherish for me and the way in which they have looked after me when I was a child. (32)

verses.text:
भ्रातृपुत्रसमौ चापि द्रष्टव्यौ च विशेषतः।
त्वया भरतशत्रुघ्नौ प्राणैः प्रियतरौ मम॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “My brothers, Bharata and Śatrughna too, who are dearer to me than life, should be particularly regarded by you as your own brothers or sons. (33)

verses.text:
विप्रियं च न कर्तव्यं भरतस्य कदाचन।
स हि राजा च वैदेहि देशस्य च कुलस्य च॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “No offence should be given to Bharata at any time; for he is now, as it were, the ruler of our country as well as of our family, O princess of the Videha territory ! (34)

verses.text:
आराधिता हि शीलेन प्रयत्नैश्चोपसेविताः।
राजानः सम्प्रसीदन्ति प्रकुप्यन्ति विपर्यये॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Kings, really speaking, get highly pleased when propitiated through good conduct and served with continued endeavours and feel enraged otherwise. (35)

verses.text:
औरस्यानपि पुत्रान् हि त्यजन्त्यहितकारिणः।
समर्थान् सम्प्रगृह्णन्ति जनानपि नराधिपाः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Rulers of men forsake even sons sprung from their own loins if they are adverse, and duly accept as their own even strangers who are friendly to them. (36)

verses.text:
सा त्वं वसेह कल्याणि राज्ञः समनुवर्तिनी।
भरतस्य रता धर्मे सत्यव्रतपरायणा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Dwell you as such in Ayodhyā under the protection of the Emperor and conformably to the will of Bharata, remaining devoted to righteousness and following sacred observances of unfailing efficacy, O blessed lady ! (37)

verses.text:
अहं गमिष्यामि महावनं प्रिये
त्वया हि वस्तव्यमिहैव भामिनि।
यथा व्यलीकं कुरुषे न कस्यचित्
तथा त्वया कार्यमिदं वचो मम॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “I shall immediately proceed to the great forest of Daṇḍaka, my darling; while you should live here only, O high-minded lady ! You should conduct yourself in such a way as not to offend anyone: this is my advice to you.” (38)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही प्रियार्हा प्रियवादिनी।
प्रणयादेव संक्रुद्धा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Roused to indignation through sheer love when admonished as aforesaid, Sītā, the daughter of the king of the Videhas, for her part, who deserved kindness from her husband and always spoke kindly to him, replied to her husband as follows : (1)

verses.text:
किमिदं भाषसे राम वाक्यं लघुतया ध्रुवम्।
त्वया यदपहास्यं मे श्रुत्वा नरवरोत्तम॥ २॥
verses.m: “Wherefore do you tender me this advice, which makes me look indeed so small, O Rāma, and which I am amused to hear, O jewel among the foremost of men ! (2)

verses.text:
वीराणां राजपुत्राणां शस्त्रास्त्रविदुषां नृप।
अनर्हमयशस्यं च न श्रोतव्यं त्वयेरितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “What has been uttered by you is unworthy of valiant princes adept in the use of weapons and missiles, and disgraceful to them, O ruler of men, and is not worth listening to. (3)

verses.text:
आर्यपुत्र पिता माता भ्राता पुत्रस्तथा स्नुषा।
स्वानि पुण्यानि भुञ्जानाः स्वं स्वं भाग्यमुपासते॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Father, mother, brother, son and daughter-in-law, my darling, reap each his or her destiny, enjoying their own merits earned in previous lives. (4)

verses.text:
भर्तुर्भाग्यं तु नार्येका प्राप्नोति पुरुषर्षभ।
अतश्चैवाहमादिष्टा वने वस्तव्यमित्यपि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “A wife alone actually shares the fortune of her husband, O jewel among men ! For this very reason I too stand enjoined by my parents-in-law that I should as well take up my abode in the forest. (5)

verses.text:
न पिता नात्मजो वात्मा न माता न सखीजनः।
इह प्रेत्य च नारीणां पतिरेको गतिः सदा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In the case of women neither father nor son nor their own body nor mother nor their female companions serve as an asylum here or hereafter. The husband alone is their refuge at all times. (6)

verses.text:
यदि त्वं प्रस्थितो दुर्गं वनमद्यैव राघव।
अग्रतस्ते गमिष्यामि मृद्नन्ती कुशकण्टकान्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “If you depart this very day for the forest of Daṇḍaka which is difficult to penetrate, O scion of Raghu, I shall walk ahead of you crushing under my soles blades of the sacred Kuśa grass and thorns that lie on the way. (7)

verses.text:
ईर्ष्यां रोषं बहिष्कृत्य भुक्तशेषमिवोदकम्।
नय मां वीर विस्रब्धः पापं मयि न विद्यते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Casting away envy at my courage in voluntarily offering to accompany you to the forest and wrath at my insolence in flouting your command to stay in Ayodhyā, confidently take me with you as one would take water remaining in one’s pot after one has drunk it once, O valiant prince ! No sin that may deter you from taking me with you abides in me. (8)

verses.text:
प्रासादाग्रे विमानैर्वा वैहायसगतेन वा।
सर्वावस्थागता भर्तुः पादच्छाया विशिष्यते॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Protection under the feet of one’s husband under all circumstances is preferable for a woman to residence at the top of a palace, or living in aerial cars or coursing through the heavens by virtue of mystic powers acquired through proficiency in Yoga. (9)

verses.text:
अनुशिष्टास्मि मात्रा च पित्रा च विविधाश्रयम्।
नास्मि सम्प्रति वक्तव्या वर्तितव्यं यथा मया॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I have been taught in many ways by my mother and father how I should conduct myself in relation to you. As such I need not be instructed in this behalf at this juncture. (10)

verses.text:
अहं दुर्गं गमिष्यामि वनं पुरुषवर्जितम्।
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं शार्दूलगणसेवितम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Unattended by any male servant I shall proceed with you to the forest of Daṇḍaka, which is difficult to penetrate and teems with multitudes of beasts of various species and is infested with herds of tigers. (11)

verses.text:
सुखं वने निवत्स्यामि यथैव भवने पितुः।
अचिन्तयन्ती त्रीँल्लोकांश्चिन्तयन्ती पतिव्रतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, caring not for the sovereignty of the three worlds and concentrating my thought on the vow of serving my husband (yourself), I shall live happily in the forest as I would in my paternal home. (12)

verses.text:
शुश्रूषमाणा ते नित्यं नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी।
सह रंस्ये त्वया वीर वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Serving you everyday with self-restraint and practising sacred vows, I shall sport with you in woodlands fragrant with stores of honey, O valiant prince ! (13)

verses.text:
त्वं हि कर्तुं वने शक्तो राम सम्परिपालनम्।
अन्यस्यापि जनस्येह किं पुनर्मम मानद॥ १४॥
verses.m: “As for yourself, you are indeed capable of duly supporting in the forest even other men, who are not related to you, much more so myself, who am your wedded wife and entirely dependent on you, O Rāma, who bestow honour on others ! (14)

verses.text:
साहं त्वया गमिष्यामि वनमद्य न संशयः।
नाहं शक्या महाभाग निवर्तयितुमुद्यता॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Such as I am, I shall undoubtedly accompany you to the forest today. Bent as I am on going, I cannot be diverted from my purpose, O highly fortunate prince ! (15)

verses.text:
फलमूलाशना नित्यं भविष्यामि न संशयः।
न ते दुःखं करिष्यामि निवसन्ती त्वया सदा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I shall without doubt live on fruits and roots alone from day to day and shall not cause any annoyance to you while living with you. (16)

verses.text:
अग्रतस्ते गमिष्यामि भोक्ष्ये भुक्तवति त्वयि।
इच्छामि परतः शैलान् पल्वलानि सरांसि च॥ १७॥
द्रष्टुं सर्वत्र निर्भीता त्वया नाथेन धीमता।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाः पद्मिनीः साधुपुष्पिताः॥ १८॥
इच्छेयं सुखिनी द्रष्टुं त्वया वीरेण संगता।
अभिषेकं करिष्यामि तासु नित्यमनुव्रता॥ १९॥
सह त्वया विशालाक्ष रंस्ये परमनन्दिनी।
एवं वर्षसहस्राणि शतं वापि त्वया सह॥ २०॥
व्यतिक्रमं न वेत्स्यामि स्वर्गोऽपि हि न मे मतः।
स्वर्गेऽपि च विना वासो भविता यदि राघव।
त्वया विना नरव्याघ्र नाहं तदपि रोचये॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I shall walk ahead of you and shall take my food only when you have finished your meal. After that, I long to see mountains, ponds and lakes, remaining fearless everywhere with you as my wise protector. Accompanied by you, a heroic prince, I wish happily to see lotus-ponds teeming with swans and water-fowls and abounding in lotuses. Nay, remaining devoted to you I shall daily take my bath in them and, full of supreme joy, sport with you, in this way, O large-eyed lord ! Spending with you, say, thousands of years or even a hundred thousand years, I shall never experience any sorrow. Heaven too will not be acceptable to me otherwise. Even if an abode devoid of you is vouchsafed to me in heaven, O scion of Raghu, I shall never find pleasure in it without you, O tiger among men ! (17—21)

verses.text:
अहं गमिष्यामि वनं सुदुर्गमं
मृगायुतं वानरवारणैश्च।
वने निवत्स्यामि यथा पितुर्गृहे
तवैव पादावुपगृह्य सम्मता॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I shall proceed to the forest of Daṇḍaka which is most difficult to penetrate and is infested with game of various kinds as well as with monkeys and elephants. Nay, clinging to your feet alone and esteemed by you, I shall dwell in the forest as though in my father’s home. (22)

verses.text:
अनन्यभावामनुरक्तचेतसं
त्वया वियुक्तां मरणाय निश्चिताम्।
नयस्व मां साधु कुरुष्व याचनां
नातो मया ते गुरुता भविष्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Therefore, grant my prayer and take me with you to the forest—me, who am exclusively devoted to you, whose mind is fondly attached to you and who am determined to die if disunited from you. You shall not be burdened by my being taken alongwith you.” (23)

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवाणामपि धर्मवत्सलां
न च स्म सीतां नृवरो निनीषति।
उवाच चैनां बहु संनिवर्तने
वने निवासस्य च दुःखितां प्रति॥ २४॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the foremost among men, did not feel inclined in the least to take to the forest Sītā, who was so fond of righteousness and even though she spoke as aforesaid. Nay, in order to turn her away from her resolve, he spoke to her a lot about the miseries attendant upon forest life. (24)

verses.text:
स एवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां धर्मज्ञां धर्मवत्सलः।
न नेतुं कुरुते बुद्धिं वने दुःखानि चिन्तयन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Bearing in mind the hardships one will be called upon to bear in the forest, Śrī Rāma, who was fond of righteousness, did not favour the idea of taking alongwith him to the forest Sītā, who knew what is right, and spoke as aforesaid. (1)

verses.text:
सान्त्वयित्वा ततस्तां तु बाष्पदूषितलोचनाम्।
निवर्तनार्थे धर्मात्मा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ २॥
verses.m: Soothing with kind words Sītā, whose eyes were bedimmed with tears, Śrī Rāma, whose mind was given to piety, for his part, so the tradition goes, then spoke as follows with a view to turning her back from her resolve : (2)

verses.text:
सीते महाकुलीनासि धर्मे च निरता सदा।
इहाचरस्व धर्मं त्वं यथा मे मनसः सुखम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Sītā, you are born of a high pedigree and are ever devoted to righteousness. Practise you virtue here so that gratification may be caused to my mind. (3)

verses.text:
सीते यथा त्वां वक्ष्यामि तथा कार्यं त्वयाबले।
वने दोषा हि बहवो वसतस्तान् निबोध मे॥ ४॥
verses.m: “You should act as I am going to tell you, O frail Sītā ! A dweller in forest, really speaking, suffers from many a handicap: please know them from me. (4)

verses.text:
सीते विमुच्यतामेषा वनवासकृता मतिः।
बहुदोषं हि कान्तारं वनमित्यभिधीयते॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Let this idea of living in a forest be finally relinquished, O Sītā; for a dense forest is spoken of as fraught with manifold dangers. (5)

verses.text:
हितबुद्ध्या खलु वचो मयैतदभिधीयते।
सदा सुखं न जानामि दुःखमेव सदा वनम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “This advice is tendered by me with an eye to your welfare alone and not because you will prove a burden to me. Not only there is no joy in a forest at all times; I rather know it to be an abode of perpetual misery. (6)

verses.text:
गिरिनिर्झरसम्भूता गिरिनिर्दरिवासिनाम्।
सिंहानां निनदा दुःखाः श्रोतुं दुःखमतो वनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Intensified by the noise of hill-streams, the roars of lions dwelling in mountain caves are unpleasant to hear. Hence a forest is full of misery. (7)

verses.text:
क्रीडमानाश्च विस्रब्धा मत्ताः शून्ये तथा मृगाः।
दृष्ट्वा समभिवर्तन्ते सीते दुःखमतो वनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Again, on seeing a human being, wild beasts in rut, sporting fearlessly in a lonely retreat, attack him on all sides. Hence a forest is full of suffering. (8)

verses.text:
सग्राहाः सरितश्चैव पङ्कवत्यस्तु दुस्तराः।
मत्तैरपि गजैर्नित्यमतो दुःखतरं वनम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Rivers are full of alligators and marshy too and as such difficult to cross even for elephants in rut. Hence a forest is ever exceedingly unpleasant. (9)

verses.text:
लताकण्टकसंकीर्णाः कृकवाकूपनादिताः।
निरपाश्च सुदुःखाश्च मार्गा दुःखमतो वनम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The paths are waterless and extremely rugged, covered with creepers and thorns and rendered noisy by wild cocks. A forest is, therefore, full of misery. (10)

verses.text:
सुप्यते पर्णशय्यासु स्वयंभग्नासु भूतले।
रात्रिषु श्रमखिन्नेन तस्माद् दुःखमतो वनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Exhausted through toil entailed by search for food in the shape of fruits etc., one has to lie down during nights on beds of dry leaves fallen of themselves. Hence a forest is a source of great suffering. (11)

verses.text:
अहोरात्रं च संतोषः कर्तव्यो नियतात्मना।
फलैर्वृक्षावपतितैः सीते दुःखमतो वनम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “By day and by night hunger has to be appeased with one’s mind fully controlled by means of fruits fallen of themselves from trees, O Sītā ! Hence a forest is full of privations. (12)

verses.text:
उपवासश्च कर्तव्यो यथा प्राणेन मैथिलि।
जटाभारश्च कर्तव्यो वल्कलाम्बरधारणम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Fasting has to be observed according to one’s stamina, O princess of Mithilā ! Nay, a mass of matted hair has to be worn on the head and one has to remain clad in the bark of trees. (13)

verses.text:
देवतानां पितॄणां च कर्तव्यं विधिपूर्वकम्।
प्राप्तानामतिथीनां च नित्यशः प्रतिपूजनम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Worship must be offered everyday to the gods and the manes according to the scriptural ordinance and hospitality shown to unexpected guests arrived at his door. (14)

verses.text:
कार्यस्त्रिरभिषेकश्च काले काले च नित्यशः।
चरतां नियमेनैव तस्माद् दुःखतरं वनम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “By those living strictly in accordance with the scriptural ordinance ablutions must be performed thrice at the appointed time, viz., in the morning and evening as well as at midday, everyday. Hence a forest is full of great hardships. (15)

verses.text:
उपहारश्च कर्तव्यः कुसुमैः स्वयमाहृतैः।
आर्षेण विधिना वेद्यां सीते दुःखमतो वनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Worship must be offered according to the ordinance laid down by sages at the altar, prepared with one’s own hands by means of flowers gathered by oneself, O Sītā ! Hence a forest is a source of suffering. (16)

verses.text:
यथालब्धेन कर्तव्यः संतोषस्तेन मैथिलि।
यताहारैर्वनचरैः सीते दुःखमतो वनम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Eating sparingly, dwellers in forests have to appease their hunger with fruits etc. obtained according to season, O Sītā, princess of Mithilā ! Hence a forest is full of hardships. (17)

verses.text:
अतीव वातस्तिमिरं बुभुक्षा चाति नित्यशः।
भयानि च महान्त्यत्र ततो दुःखतरं वनम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The wind blows furiously everyday, thick darkness prevails and hunger too is rapacious. Besides there are great perils in the forest. Hence a forest is a source of great hardships. (18)

verses.text:
सरीसृपाश्च बहवो बहुरूपाश्च भामिनि।
चरन्ति पथि ते दर्पात् ततो दुःखतरं वनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Well-known serpents of various kinds proudly creep on the tracks in large numbers, O proud lady ! A forest, therefore, is a source of great miseries. (19)

verses.text:
नदीनिलयनाः सर्पा नदीकुटिलगामिनः।
तिष्ठन्त्यावृत्य पन्थानमतो दुःखतरं वनम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Serpents having their home in rivers and moving tortuously like rivers lie blocking the way. Hence a forest is full of great suffering. (20)

verses.text:
पतङ्गा वृश्चिकाः कीटा दंशाश्च मशकैः सह।
बाधन्ते नित्यमबले सर्वं दुःखमतो वनम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Moths, scorpions, worms and gnats alongwith mosquitoes harass everyone daily, O frail princess ! Hence a forest is full of suffering. (21)

verses.text:
द्रुमाः कण्टकिनश्चैव कुशाः काशाश्च भामिनि।
वने व्याकुलशाखाग्रास्तेन दुःखमतो वनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Thorny trees, blades of the sacred Kuśa grass and gnarled shrubs known by the name of Kāśas are seen with the ends of their limbs spreading on all sides in the forest, O proud lady ! Hence a forest is thickly beset with hardships. (22)

verses.text:
कायक्लेशाश्च बहवो भयानि विविधानि च।
अरण्यवासे वसतो दुःखमेव सदा वनम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Manifold bodily sufferings torment and perils of various kinds threaten a person taking up his abode in a forest dwelling. A forest is thus a perennial source of suffering. (23)

verses.text:
क्रोधलोभौ विमोक्तव्यौ कर्तव्या तपसे मतिः।
न भेतव्यं च भेतव्ये दुःखं नित्यमतो वनम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Anger and greed have to be completely abandoned, one’s heart has to be set on asceticism and one must not dread even that which deserves to be dreaded. Hence a forest is a perpetual source of suffering. (24)

verses.text:
तदलं ते वनं गत्वा क्षेमं नहि वनं तव।
विमृशन्निव पश्यामि बहुदोषकरं वनम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Therefore, have done with the idea of proceeding to the forest. A forest is not secure for you. Bestowing my thought on the subject I perceive the forest as fraught with many evils, as it were.” (25)

verses.text:
वनं तु नेतुं न कृता मतिर्यदा
बभूव रामेण तदा महात्मना।
न तस्य सीता वचनं चकार तं
ततोऽब्रवीद् राममिदं सुदुःखिता॥ २६॥
verses.m: When the high-souled Śrī Rāma did not agree to take Sītā to the forest, the latter for her part did not concur with his verdict. Sore afflicted, she then spoke as follows to the illustrious Śrī Rāma. (26)

verses.text:
एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रामस्य दुःखिता।
प्रसक्ताश्रुमुखी मन्दमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Distressed to hear this plea of Śrī Rāma, Sītā, for her part, who was deeply attached to the latter, gently spoke as follows, her face wet with tears : (1)

verses.text:
ये त्वया कीर्तिता दोषा वने वस्तव्यतां प्रति।
गुणानित्येव तान् विद्धि तव स्नेहपुरस्कृता॥ २॥
verses.m: “The disadvantages that have been enumerated by you as accruing from an abode in the forest, know them to be so many blessings in disguise in view of the fact that I am foremost in your affections. (2)

verses.text:
मृगाः सिंहा गजाश्चैव शार्दूलाः शरभास्तथा।
चमराः सृमराश्चैव ये चान्ये वनचारिणः॥ ३॥
अदृष्टपूर्वरूपत्वात् सर्वे ते तव राघव।
रूपं दृष्ट्वापसर्पेयुस्तव सर्वे हि बिभ्यति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Antelopes, lions and even so elephants, tigers and Śarabhas (a legendary animal with eight legs and said to be more powerful even than the lion), yaks as well as Gayals and many other beasts that roam about in the forest are all sure to run away on seeing your countenance since they have never seen your face before and because all are afraid of you. (3-4)

verses.text:
त्वया च सह गन्तव्यं मया गुरुजनाज्ञया।
त्वद्वियोगेन मे राम त्यक्तव्यमिह जीवितम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “In pursuance of the orders of your parents, I too must accompany you to the forest inasmuch as I am your counterpart* and cannot live apart from you. Nay, life in this world must be cast away by me in the event of separation from you, O Rāma ! (5)

verses.text:
नहि मां त्वत्समीपस्थामपि शक्रोऽपि राघव।
सुराणामीश्वरः शक्तः प्रधर्षयितुमोजसा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In fact, not even Indra, the ruler of gods, is capable of overpowering me by his might so long as I am by your side. (6)

verses.text:
पतिहीना तु या नारी न सा शक्ष्यति जीवितुम्।
काममेवंविधं राम त्वया मम निदर्शितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Such a thing has been amply brought home to me by you, O Rāma, that a devoted wife who stands disunited from her husband would not be able to survive. (7)

verses.text:
अथापि च महाप्राज्ञ ब्राह्मणानां मया श्रुतम्।
पुरा पितृगृहे सत्यं वस्तव्यं किल मे वने॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Moreover, in the days gone by while living at my father’s, O highly enlightened prince, the prophecy—which must come out true—was heard by me from the mouth of Brāhmaṇas well-versed in astrology that I must dwell in the forest. (8)

verses.text:
लक्षणिभ्यो द्विजातिभ्यः श्रुत्वाहं वचनं गृहे।
वनवासकृतोत्साहा नित्यमेव महाबल॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Having heard the prophecy at my parents’ home from Brāhmaṇas, able to interpret marks on the body, I have ever cherished a longing for forest life, O highly powerful prince ! (9)

verses.text:
आदेशो वनवासस्य प्राप्तव्यः स मया किल।
सा त्वया सह भर्त्राहं यास्यामि प्रिय नान्यथा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The truth of that prediction about forest life must be realized by me. I must accordingly accompany you, my Lord, O darling; it cannot be otherwise. (10)

verses.text:
कृतादेशा भविष्यामि गमिष्यामि त्वया सह।
कालश्चायं समुत्पन्नः सत्यवान् भवतु द्विजः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I am sure I shall be permitted by you to follow you and shall eventually accompany you. Nay, the time for the fulfilment of the prophecy has now arrived. Let the utterance of the Brāhmaṇas prove true. (11)

verses.text:
वनवासे हि जानामि दुःखानि बहुधा किल।
प्राप्यन्ते नियतं वीर पुरुषैरकृतात्मभिः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I certainly know there are sufferings of various kinds in the forest. They are, however, invariably experienced by men of unsubdued mind alone, O heroic prince ! (12)

verses.text:
कन्यया च पितुर्गेहे वनवासः श्रुतो मया।
भिक्षिण्याः शमवृत्ताया मम मातुरिहाग्रतः॥ १३॥
प्रसादितश्च वै पूर्वं त्वं मे बहुतिथं प्रभो।
गमनं वनवासस्य कांक्षितं हि सह त्वया॥ १४॥
verses.m: “While I was still unmarried, the prediction about my dwelling in the forest was heard by me in my father’s house from the mouth of a hermitess, spending her life in quietism, in the presence of my mother. Here too, my lord, you have been actually asked on many an occasion in the past the favour of taking me to the forest and spending some time there. Indeed a journey with a view to spending some time in the forest with you is longed for by me. (13-14)

verses.text:
कृतक्षणाहं भद्रं ते गमनं प्रति राघव।
वनवासस्य शूरस्य मम चर्या हि रोचते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I am feeling jubilant over the prospect of my departure for the forest. May all be well with you, O scion of Raghu ! Service to you,a heroic prince, dwelling in the forest is surely delightful to me. (15)

verses.text:
शुद्धात्मन् प्रेमभावाद्धि भविष्यामि विकल्मषा।
भर्तारमनुगच्छन्ती भर्ता हि परदैवतम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Following my husband to the forest with loving devotion I shall surely be absolved from all guilt, O pure-minded prince; for the husband is the supreme deity for a wife. (16)

verses.text:
प्रेत्यभावे हि कल्याणः संगमो मे सदा त्वया।
श्रुतिर्हि श्रूयते पुण्या ब्राह्मणानां यशस्विनाम्॥ १७॥
इहलोके च पितृभिर्या स्त्री यस्य महाबल।
अद्भिर्दत्ता स्वधर्मेण प्रेत्यभावेऽपि तस्य सा॥ १८॥
verses.m: “On my remaining united with you even in the forest, my union with you will continue forever and will be a source of blessedness to us both even hereafter. On this subject, O highly powerful prince, is heard from the lips of celebrated Brāhmaṇas the following holy Śruti text : ‘Even in the other world a woman continues to be the wife of that very man to whom she was given away in this world by her parents with water in their hands to solemnize the gift according to the moral code binding on them.’ (17-18)

verses.text:
एवमस्मात् स्वकां नारीं सुवृत्तां हि पतिव्रताम्।
नाभिरोचयसे नेतुं त्वं मां केनेह हेतुना॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Such being the case, for what reason on earth do you not agree to take me, your own wife, actually so devoted to her husband and of such good character, from this city? (19)

verses.text:
भक्तां पतिव्रतां दीनां मां समां सुखदुःखयोः।
नेतुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ समानसुखदुःखिनीम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “You ought, therefore, to take me, so devoted and faithful to my husband (yourself), miserable for fear of separation, alike to pleasure and pain and sharing your joys and sorrows, O scion of Kākutstha ! (20)

verses.text:
यदि मां दुःखितामेवं वनं नेतुं न चेच्छसि।
विषमग्निं जलं वाहमास्थास्ये मृत्युकारणात्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “If you do not feel inclined at all to take me, afflicted as I am as shown above, to the forest, I shall resort to poison, fire or water to hasten my end.” (21)

verses.text:
एवं बहुविधं तं सा याचते गमनं प्रति।
नानुमेने महाबाहुस्तां नेतुं विजनं वनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: In this way Sītā entreated him in many ways to let her accompany him. Nevertheless Śrī Rāma, the mighty-armed prince, did not consent to take her to the forest, which was destitute of friends. (22)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु सा चिन्तां मैथिली समुपागता।
स्नापयन्तीव गामुष्णैरश्रुभिर्नयनच्युतैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Discouraged thus, the celebrated Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, for her part, fell a prey to anxiety, moistening the earth as it were with burning tears dropped from her eyes. (23)

verses.text:
चिन्तयन्तीं तदा तां तु निवर्तयितुमात्मवान्।
क्रोधाविष्टां तु वैदेहीं काकुत्स्थो बह्वसान्त्वयत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: In order, however, to divert her from her resolve, the self-possessed Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, for his part then pacified in many ways the said princess of the Videha kingdom, who was overwhelmed with indignation roused by love and fell abrooding. (24)

verses.text:
सान्त्व्यमाना तु रामेण मैथिली जनकात्मजा।
वनवासनिमित्तार्थं भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Being consoled by Śrī Rāma, Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, the princess of Mithilā, for her part, replied thus to her husband in order to obtain his permission to live with him in the forest. (1)

verses.text:
सा तमुत्तमसंविग्ना सीता विपुलवक्षसम्।
प्रणयाच्चाभिमानाच्च परिचिक्षेप राघवम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Highly agitated at the thought of her separation from Śrī Rāma, the said Sītā taunted Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who was distinguished by a broad chest, from affection and pride in the following words: (2)

verses.text:
किं त्वामन्यत वैदेहः पिता मे मिथिलाधिपः।
राम जामातरं प्राप्य स्त्रियं पुरुषविग्रहम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Securing you as his son-in-law, O Rāma, did my father, Janaka (descended in the line of the Videhas), the king of Mithilā, recognise you to be a woman in the form of a man? (3)

verses.text:
अनृतं बत लोकोऽयमज्ञानाद् यदि वक्ष्यति।
तेजो नास्ति परं रामे तपतीव दिवाकरे॥ ४॥
verses.m: “It would be a matter for pity to me if in the event of your not taking me with you the people of Ayodhyā utter through ignorance the falsehood that ‘Supreme valour is lacking in Śrī Rāma, even though he blazes like the sun.’ (4)

verses.text:
किं हि कृत्वा विषण्णस्त्वं कुतो वा भयमस्ति ते।
यत् परित्यक्तुकामस्त्वं मामनन्यपरायणाम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “On what ground are you cast down or whence the fear in you for which you are inclined to desert me, exclusively devoted as I am to you? (5)

verses.text:
द्युमत्सेनसुतं वीरं सत्यवन्तमनुव्रताम्।
सावित्रीमिव मां विद्धि त्वमात्मवशवर्तिनीम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Know me you to be as obedient to your will as Sāvitrī (of historical fame) was devoted to the valiant Satyavān, son of King Dyumatsena. (6)

verses.text:
न त्वहं मनसा प्यन्यं द्रष्टास्मि त्वदृतेऽनघ।
त्वया राघव गच्छेयं यथान्या कुलपांसनी॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I will not cast my eyes even in thought on anyone else than you as any other woman bringing disgrace to her family would, O sinless one! I must accompany you, O scion of Raghu ! (7)

verses.text:
स्वयं तु भार्यां कौमारीं चिरमध्युषितां सतीम्।
शैलूष इव मां राम परेभ्यो दातुमिच्छसि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “How do you, like a man who lives by his wife, intend to deliver to others of your own will, me, your chaste wife, who was married to you before puberty and has lived with you for a long time, O Rāma? (8)

verses.text:
यस्य पथ्यंचरामात्थ यस्य चार्थेऽवरुध्यसे।
त्वं तस्य भव वश्यश्च विधेयश्च सदानघ॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Be you ever amenable to the control of and obedient to him whom you ask me to follow the wishes of Bharat, and for whose sake you are being pushed back. (9)

verses.text:
स मामनादाय वनं न त्वं प्रस्थितुमर्हसि।
तपो वा यदि वारण्यं स्वर्गो वा स्यात् त्वया सह॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Such as you are, you ought not to proceed to the forest without taking me with you. Be it a course of austerities, forest life or heavenly life, let it be with you. (10)

verses.text:
न च मे भविता तत्र कश्चित् पथि परिश्रमः।
पृष्ठतस्तव गच्छन्त्या विहारशयनेष्विव॥ ११॥
verses.m: “No more exertion will be caused to me in following at your heels on the paths in the forest than in strolling in a garden or in sleep. (11)

verses.text:
कुशकाशशरेषीका ये च कण्टकिनो द्रुमाः।
तूलाजिनसमस्पर्शा मार्गे मम सह त्वया॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Blades of the sacred Kuśa grass, shrubs known by the name of Kāśa, reeds and rushes and whatever prickly bushes fall in my way in your company will touch my soles like a heap of cotton or soft deerskin. (12)

verses.text:
महावातसमुद्भूतं यन्मामवकरिष्यति।
रजो रमण तन्मन्ये परार्घ्यमिव चन्दनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I shall reckon the dust raised by a storm that will cover my body as most exquisite sandal dust, my lord ! (13)

verses.text:
शाद्वलेषु यदा शिश्ये वनान्तर्वनगोचरा।
कुथास्तरणयुक्तेषु किं स्यात् सुखतरं ततः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “When, while living in the forest, I shall lie down on turfs in the heart of a forest with you, will lying in beds covered with soft carpets be more comfortable than that? (14)

verses.text:
पत्रं मूलं फलं यत्तु अल्पं वा यदि वा बहु।
दास्यसे स्वयमाहृत्य तन्मेऽमृतरसोपमम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Anything you will give me in the shape of leaves, roots or fruits, bringing it yourself in a small or large quantity will taste like nectar to me. (15)

verses.text:
न मातुर्न पितुस्तत्र स्मरिष्यामि न वेश्मनः।
आर्तवान्युपभुञ्जाना पुष्पाणि च फलानि च॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Enjoying there seasonal flowers and fruits too I shall neither remember my mother nor father nor home. (16)

verses.text:
न च तत्र ततः किंचिद् द्रष्टुमर्हसि विप्रियम्।
मत्कृते न च ते शोको न भविष्यामि दुर्भरा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “You ought not to foresee anything unwelcome following from my departure to the forest. Nor will any grief come to you on my account there, nor shall I prove hard to sustain. (17)

verses.text:
यस्त्वया सह स स्वर्गो निरयो यस्त्वया विना।
इति जानन् परां प्रीतिं गच्छ राम मया सह॥ १८॥
verses.m: “An abode which will be shared by me with you will be pleasing as heaven to me; while that which will be shorn of you will be repellent as hell. Knowing thus my supreme love for you, proceed to the forest with me, O Rāma ! (18)

verses.text:
अथ मामेवमव्यग्रां वनं नैव नयिष्यसे।
विषमद्यैव पास्यामि मा वशं द्विषतां गमम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “If you definitely do not take me to the forest, even though I am not the least afraid of going there as shown above, I shall drink poison this very day but would on no account submit to the will of enemies (Bharata and others). (19)

verses.text:
पश्चादपि हि दुःखेन मम नैवास्ति जीवितम्।
उज्झितायास्त्वया नाथ तदैव मरणं वरम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Surely as a result of agony caused by separation from you, I am not going to live even afterwards when abandoned by you, O lord ! It is, therefore, better that I should die in your very presence. (20)

verses.text:
इमं हि सहितुं शोकं मुहूर्तमपि नोत्सहे।
किं पुनर्दश वर्षाणि त्रीणि चैकं च दुःखिता॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I indeed cannot endure even for less than an hour the grief caused by separation from you. How, then, can I, an afflicted woman, bear it for ten years and four?”(21)

verses.text:
इति सा शोकसंतप्ता विलप्य करुणं बहु।
चुक्रोश पतिमायस्ता भृशमालिङ्ग्य सस्वरम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having wailed a lot in a piteous way as aforesaid, and closely embracing her husband, tormented as she was with grief, Sītā, who now felt exhausted, cried piteously shedding stream of tears. (22)

verses.text:
सा विद्धा बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्दिग्धैरिव गजाङ्गना।
चिरसंनियतं बाष्पं मुमोचाग्निमिवारणिः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Tortured with many homilies like a female elephant pierced with poisoned shafts, she shed tears that had long been restrained even as a piece of wood would emit fire through attrition with another. (23)

verses.text:
तस्याः स्फटिकसंकाशं वारि संतापसम्भवम्।
नेत्राभ्यां परिसुस्राव पङ्कजाभ्यामिवोदकम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Tear-drops sparkling as crystal and born of agony slipped from her eyes as water from a pair of lotuses. (24)

verses.text:
तत्सितामलचन्द्राभं मुखमायतलोचनम्।
पर्यशुष्यत बाष्पेण जलोद्धृतमिवाम्बुजम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Her countenance, that shone like the uneclipsed moon on a full moon night and was distinguished by big eyes, was blasted with hot tears as a lotus taken out of water is withered through heat. (25)

verses.text:
तां परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां विसंज्ञामिव दुःखिताम्।
उवाच वचनं रामः परिविश्वासयंस्तदा॥ २६॥
verses.m: Folding in his arms Sītā, who felt distressed and had fainted, as it were, Śrī Rāma then spoke to her as follows, fully reassuring her: (26)

verses.text:
न देवि बत दुःखेन स्वर्गमप्यभिरोचये।
नहि मेऽस्ति भयं किंचित् स्वयम्भोरिव सर्वतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Alas, I find no delight even in heaven obtained by causing agony to you, O pious lady ! Nor is there fear to me from any quarter any more than to Brahmā, the self-born. (27)

verses.text:
तव सर्वमभिप्रायमविज्ञाय शुभानने।
वासं न रोचयेऽरण्ये शक्तिमानपि रक्षणे॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Not knowing your full mind, O lady with a charming countenance, I did not approve of your sojourn in the forest, though capable of protecting you. (28)

verses.text:
यत् सृष्टासि मया सार्धं वनवासाय मैथिलि।
न विहातुं मया शक्या प्रीतिरात्मवता यथा॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Since you were obviously born to dwell with me in the forest, O princess of Mithilā, you are incapable of being abandoned by me even as tenderness cannot be given up by a man of self-knowledge. (29)

verses.text:
धर्मस्तु गजनासोरु सद्भिराचरितः पुरा।
तं चाहमनुवर्तिष्ये यथा सूर्यं सुवर्चला॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall abide by the moral law actually followed by the virtuous dwellers in the forest in the past, O lady with comely limbs ! Follow me now even as Suvarcalā (nicknamed Saṁjñā, wife of the sun-god) does the sun-god. (30)

verses.text:
न खल्वहं न गच्छेयं वनं जनकनन्दिनि।
वचनं तन्नयति मां पितुः सत्योपबृंहितम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Of course, it cannot be that I may not proceed to the forest, O daughter of Janaka; for that plighted word of my father is urging me to proceed to the forest. (31)

verses.text:
एष धर्मश्च सुश्रोणि पितुर्मातुश्च वश्यता।
आज्ञां चाहं व्यतिक्रम्य नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay, obedience to one’s father and mother—this is one’s sacred duty, O handsome lady ! And violating their command I dare not survive. (32)

verses.text:
अस्वाधीनं कथं दैवं प्रकारैरभिराध्यते।
स्वाधीनं समतिक्रम्य मातरं पितरं गुरुम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Disregarding one’s mother, father and teacher, whose command can be directly obtained, how can it be possible to propitiate one’s chosen deity, who is not so manifest, through traditional modes of worship? (33)

verses.text:
यत्र त्रयं त्रयो लोकाः पवित्रं तत्समं भुवि।
नान्यदस्ति शुभापाङ्गे तेनेदमभिराध्यते॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “No other worship is so sacred or capable of delivering the worshipper from the great fear of transmigration on earth as service to the aforesaid three, through which all the three worlds (heaven, earth and the space intervening them) can be propitiated and all the three objects of human pursuit viz., religious merit, earthly possessions and gratification of senses can be obtained, O lady with charming glances ! Hence the above-mentioned three are sought to be propitiated by me. (34)

verses.text:
न सत्यं दानमानौ वा यज्ञो वाप्याप्तदक्षिणाः।
तथा बलकराः सीते यथा सेवा पितुर्मता॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Neither truthfulness nor gifts and honour bestowed on the deserving, nor sacrificial performances in which sacrificial fees are handsomely paid are so potent in securing happiness in the other world as service to one’s father and mother is believed to be. (35)

verses.text:
स्वर्गो धनं वा धान्यं वा विद्या पुत्राः सुखानि च।
गुरुवृत्त्यनुरोधेन न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Heavenly bliss or earthly riches, foodgrains or learning, sons and amenities of life—nothing is hard to obtain through compliance with the wishes of one’s elders. (36)

verses.text:
देवगन्धर्वगोलोकान् ब्रह्मलोकांस्तथापरान्।
प्राप्नुवन्ति महात्मानो मातापितृपरायणाः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “High-souled men exclusively devoted to the service of their parents secure after their death the regions of the gods and the Gandharvas, the seventh heaven presided over by Brahmā, the creator, and other regions, nay, even Goloka (the highest heaven presided—over by Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa, so-called because it abounds in cows, the pets of Śrī Kṛṣṇa). (37)

verses.text:
स मां पिता यथा शास्ति सत्यधर्मपथे स्थितः।
तथा वर्तितुमिच्छामि स हि धर्मः सनातनः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “I wish to do precisely as my celebrated father, devoted to the path of truthfulness and virtue, enjoins me to do; for such is the eternal law of morality. (38)

verses.text:
मम सन्ना मतिः सीते नेतुं त्वां दण्डकावनम्।
वसिष्यामीति सा त्वं मामनुयातुं सुनिश्चिता॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Inasmuch as you are fully determined to follow me to the forest with a resolution to sojourn there, my former decision about not taking you to the forest of Daṇḍaka has become feeble, O Sītā ! (39)

verses.text:
सा हि दिष्टानवद्याङ्गि वनाय मदिरेक्षणे।
अनुगच्छस्व मां भीरु सहधर्मचरी भव॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Since you are now allowed by me to proceed to the forest with me, O timid lady with flawless limbs and bewitching eyes, follow me as such and be my partner in the practice of asceticism incumbent on the dwellers in a forest. (40)

verses.text:
सर्वथा सदृशं सीते मम स्वस्य कुलस्य च।
व्यवसायमनुक्रान्ता कान्ते त्वमतिशोभनम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Beloved Sītā, you have arrived at a most welcome decision worthy in everyway of my race as well as of yours. (41)

verses.text:
आरभस्व शुभश्रोणि वनवासक्षमाः क्रियाः।
नेदानीं त्वदृते सीते स्वर्गोऽपि मम रोचते॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Proceed with the duties preliminary to a sojourn in the woods, O lady with charming limbs! Without you even heaven does not catch my fancy at this moment. (42)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च रत्नानि भिक्षुकेभ्यश्च भोजनम्।
देहि चाशंसमानेभ्यः संत्वरस्व च मा चिरम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Nay, bestow valuable gifts on the Brāhmaṇas and also offer food to mendicants asking for it. Again, be very quick. Make no delay. (43)

verses.text:
भूषणानि महार्हाणि वरवस्त्राणि यानि च।
रमणीयाश्च ये केचित् क्रीडार्थाश्चाप्युपस्कराः॥ ४४॥
शयनीयानि यानानि मम चान्यानि यानि च।
देहि स्वभृत्यवर्गस्य ब्राह्मणानामनन्तरम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Give to the various grades of your dependants whatever costly ornaments, fine articles of wearing apparel and whatever lovely articles of household use and those meant for diversion, couches and conveyances, both mine as well as yours, and whatever articles are left after satisfying the Brāhmaṇas.” (44-45)

verses.text:
अनुकूलं तु सा भर्तुर्ज्ञात्वा गमनमात्मनः।
क्षिप्रं प्रमुदिता देवी दातुमेव प्रचक्रमे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Overjoyed to know her departure to the forest acceptable to her husband, the godly lady Sītā for her part quickly and definitely set about making gifts accordingly. (46)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहृष्टा प्रतिपूर्णमानसा
यशस्विनी भर्तुरवेक्ष्य भाषितम्।
धनानि रत्नानि च दातुमङ्गना
प्रचक्रमे धर्मभृतां मनस्विनी॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Feeling reassured in mind and overjoyed to ponder over the speech of her husband, the illustrious and strong-minded lady forthwith commenced gifting riches and jewels to virtuous souls. (47)

verses.text:
एवं श्रुत्वा स संवादं लक्ष्मणः पूर्वमागतः।
बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखः शोकं सोढुमशक्नुवन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the dialogue that passed between Śrī Rāma and Sītā as reproduced above, the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa, who had already reached there from Kausalyā’s apartments alongwith Śrī Rāma could not bear the grief born of his impending separation from Śrī Rāma, his face covered with tears. (1)

verses.text:
स भ्रातुश्चरणौ गाढं निपीड्य रघुनन्दनः।
सीतामुवाचातियशां राघवं च महाव्रतम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Tightly pressing the feet of his eldest brother, Lakṣmaṇa, the delight of the Raghus, spoke as follows to Sītā, who enjoyed great celebrity, as also to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who had undertaken a great vow : (2)

verses.text:
यदि गन्तुं कृता बुद्धिर्वनं मृगगजायुतम्।
अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि वनमग्रे धनुर्धरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “If your mind is set on proceeding to the forest, full of deer and elephants I shall accompany you to the woodland, walking ahead of you armed with a bow. (3)

verses.text:
मया समेतोऽरण्यानि रम्याणि विचरिष्यसि।
पक्षिभिर्मृगयूथैश्च संघुष्टानि समन्ततः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by me you will roam about in delightful woodlands rendered noisy all round by birds and swarms of deer. (4)

verses.text:
न देवलोकाक्रमणं नामरत्वमहं वृणे।
ऐश्वर्यं चापि लोकानां कामये न त्वया विना॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Without you I do not wish to ascend to heaven nor do I solicit godhood nor again do I crave for the rulership of the spheres.” (5)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणः सौमित्रिर्वनवासाय निश्चितः।
रामेण बहुभिः सान्त्वैर्निषिद्धः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, who was determined to dwell in the forest with his eldest brother and was discouraged by Śrī Rāma in so many soothing words, submitted once more as follows : (6)

verses.text:
अनुज्ञातस्तु भवता पूर्वमेव यदस्म्यहम्।
किमिदानीं पुनरपि क्रियते मे निवारणम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Even though I stand already permitted by you to accompany you to the forest, how am I being prohibited anew this moment? (7)

verses.text:
यदर्थं प्रतिषेधो मे क्रियते गन्तुमिच्छतः।
एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं संशयो हि ममानघ॥ ८॥
verses.m: “I wish to know definitely wherefore I am being disallowed though longing to proceed with you; for there is doubt in my mind, O sinless brother as to how permission was granted in the beginning and is being withheld now.” (8)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामो लक्ष्मणमग्रतः।
स्थितं प्राग्गामिनं धीरं याचमानं कृताञ्जलिम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with great splendour, then replied as follows to the strong-minded Lakṣmaṇa, who stood before him eager to precede Śrī Rāma to the forest and soliciting the latter’s permission with joined palms : (9)

verses.text:
स्निग्धो धर्मरतो धीरः सततं सत्पथे स्थितः।
प्रियः प्राणसमो वश्यो विजेयश्च सखा च मे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Full of affection for me, devoted to virtue, resolute, constantly firm on the right path as shown by the Vedas, dear to me as life, amenable to my control and obedient, you are my boon companion too and, therefore, worthy in every way of accompanying me. (10)

verses.text:
मयाद्य सह सौमित्रे त्वयि गच्छति तद्वनम्।
को भजिष्यति कौसल्यां सुमित्रां वा यशस्विनीम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Yet if you proceed with me to the forest for which I am leaving today, O son of Sumitrā, who will serve the illustrious Kausalyā and Sumitrā? (11)

verses.text:
अभिवर्षति कामैर्यः पर्जन्यः पृथिवीमिव।
स कामपाशपर्यस्तो महातेजा महीपतिः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “That highly glorious king, our father, who showered blessings on the people even as the god of rain sends down rain on the earth stands fettered by the cord of love. (12)

verses.text:
सा हि राज्यमिदं प्राप्य नृपस्याश्वपतेः सुता।
दुःखितानां सपत्नीनां न करिष्यति शोभनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Obtaining this kingdom, Kaikeyī, the daughter of King Aśwapati, will certainly not accord good treatment to her afflicted co-wives. (13)

verses.text:
न भरिष्यति कौसल्यां सुमित्रां च सुदुःखिताम्।
भरतो राज्यमासाद्य कैकेय्यां पर्यवस्थितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Having attained sovereignty Bharata too will not maintain the extremely miserable Kausalyā and Sumitrā, devoted as he will naturally be to Kaikeyī, his own mother. (14)

verses.text:
तामार्यां स्वयमेवेह राजानुग्रहणेन वा।
सौमित्रे भर कौसल्यामुक्तमर्थममुं चर॥ १५॥
verses.m: “By your own effort or by securing the goodwill of the king, O son of Sumitrā, please look after here the aforesaid Kausalyā, who is worthy of the utmost respect. Pray, accomplish this aforesaid purpose of mine. (15)

verses.text:
एवं मयि च ते भक्तिर्भविष्यति सुदर्शिता।
धर्मज्ञगुरुपूजायां धर्मश्चाप्यतुलो महान्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “On service being thus rendered to elders, O knower of what is right, devotion to me will have been fully demonstrated by you and incomparably great religious merit too will accrue to you. (16)

verses.text:
एवं कुरुष्व सौमित्रे मत्कृते रघुनन्दन।
अस्माभिर्विप्रहीणाया मातुर्नो न भवेत् सुखम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “For my sake, therefore, O son of Sumitrā, do as aforesaid; for there will be no happiness for my mother bereft of us, O scion of Raghu !” (17)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः श्लक्ष्णया गिरा।
प्रत्युवाच तदा रामं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Spoken to thus by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, for his part, who knew how to speak, then replied in sweet words as follows to his eldest brother, a master of expression himself : (18)

verses.text:
तवैव तेजसा वीर भरतः पूजयिष्यति।
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च प्रयतो नास्ति संशयः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Inspired by your moral lustre itself the devout Bharata will treat with respect Kausalyā and Sumitrā too: there is no doubt about it, O valiant prince ! (19)

verses.text:
यदि दुःस्थो न रक्षेत भरतो राज्यमुत्तमम्।
प्राप्य दुर्मनसा वीर गर्वेण च विशेषतः॥ २०॥
तमहं दुर्मतिं क्रूरं वधिष्यामि न संशयः।
तत्पक्षानपि तान् सर्वांस्त्रैलोक्यमपि किं तु सा॥ २१॥
कौसल्या बिभृयादार्या सहस्रं मद्विधानपि।
यस्याः सहस्रं ग्रामाणां सम्प्राप्तमुपजीविनाम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “If led astray in consequence of having obtained this first-rate kingdom, Bharata does not protect his mothers through perversity and particularly from pride, O heroic brother, I shall make short work not only of that evil-minded and cruel fellow but all his well-known adherents too, nay, all the three worlds if they side with him : there is no doubt about it. But the celebrated Kausalyā, who is worthy of the highest respect and even by whose dependants thousands of villages have been duly obtained as grants, can support thousands like me. (20—22)

verses.text:
तदात्मभरणे चैव मम मातुस्तथैव च।
पर्याप्ता मद्विधानां च भरणाय मनस्विनी॥ २३॥
verses.m: “As such the high-minded Kausalyā is capable of maintaining herself as well as myself and even so my mother, Sumitrā, and those like me. (23)

verses.text:
कुरुष्व मामनुचरं वैधर्म्यं नेह विद्यते।
कृतार्थोऽहं भविष्यामि तव चार्थः प्रकल्प्यते॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, kindly make me your attendant : there will be no unrighteousness in it. I shall thereby have accomplished my object and your purpose too will be adequately served. (24)

verses.text:
धनुरादाय सगुणं खनित्रपिटकाधरः।
अग्रतस्ते गमिष्यामि पन्थानं तव दर्शयन्॥ २५॥
