verses.m: “Taking my stringed bow and carrying a spade and a basket, I shall walk ahead of you showing you the way. (25)

verses.text:
आहरिष्यामि ते नित्यं मूलानि च फलानि च।
वन्यानि च तथान्यानि स्वाहार्हाणि तपस्विनाम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall procure for you from day to day wild roots and fruits and other products as well fit for being consigned as oblation into the sacred fire. (26)

verses.text:
भवांस्तु सह वैदेह्या गिरिसानुषु रंस्यसे।
अहं सर्वं करिष्यामि जाग्रतः स्वपतश्च ते॥ २७॥
verses.m: “You will sport at will with Sītā, a princess of the Videha clan, on mountain-tops. I shall do everything for you whether you are waking or sleeping.” (27)

verses.text:
रामस्त्वनेन वाक्येन सुप्रीतः प्रत्युवाच तम्।
व्रजापृच्छस्व सौमित्रे सर्वमेव सुहृज्जनम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Highly pleased at this submission Śrī Rāma for his part replied as follows to Lakṣmaṇa : “Go, take leave to proceed to the forest, O son of Sumitrā, of all your near and dear ones. (28)

verses.text:
ये च राज्ञो ददौ दिव्ये महात्मा वरुणः स्वयम्।
जनकस्य महायज्ञे धनुषी रौद्रदर्शने॥ २९॥
अभेद्ये कवचे दिव्ये तूणी चाक्षय्यसायकौ।
आदित्यविमलाभौ द्वौ खड्गौ हेमपरिष्कृतौ॥ ३०॥
सत्कृत्य निहितं सर्वमेतदाचार्यसद्मनि।
सर्वमायुधमादाय क्षिप्रमाव्रज लक्ष्मण॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Nay, the two heavenly bows, dreadful to look at, which the high-souled Varuṇa, the god of water, personally gave to King Janaka at a grand sacrifice performed by the latter, a pair of impenetrable pieces of armour, a couple of quivers containing an inexhaustible stock of arrows and a pair of swords shedding a spotless lustre like that of the sun and decked with gold—all these which had been presented to me by King Janaka as part of my dowry lie deposited after paying due reverence at the residence of our preceptor, Sage Vasiṣṭha. Taking all those arms return soon, O Lakṣmaṇa !” (29—31)

verses.text:
स सुहृज्जनमामन्त्र्य वनवासाय निश्चितः।
इक्ष्वाकुगुरुमागम्य जग्राहायुधमुत्तमम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Taking leave of his near and dear ones and approaching Vasiṣṭha, the preceptor of the Ikṣwākus, the prince, who was now assured of his sojourn in the forest, took all the excellent arms etc. (32)

verses.text:
तद् दिव्यं राजशार्दूलः सत्कृतं माल्यभूषितम्।
रामाय दर्शयामास सौमित्रिः सर्वमायुधम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, a tiger among princes, showed to Śrī Rāma all the aforesaid weapons, that were adored as divine and stood decorated with garlands. (33)

verses.text:
तमुवाचात्मवान् रामः प्रीत्या लक्ष्मणमागतम्।
काले त्वमागतः सौम्य कांक्षिते मम लक्ष्मण॥ ३४॥
verses.m: To Lakṣmaṇa, who had come back, Śrī Rāma, who had fully brought his mind under control, lovingly said, “You have returned within an hour as desired by me, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa ! (34)

verses.text:
अहं प्रदातुमिच्छामि यदिदं मामकं धनम्।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तपस्विभ्यस्त्वया सह परंतप॥ ३५॥
वसन्तीह दृढं भक्त्या गुरुषु द्विजसत्तमाः।
तेषामपि च मे भूयः सर्वेषां चोपजीविनाम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “With you, O chastiser of foes, I wish to give away whatever wealth of my own there is with me to Brāhmaṇas engaged in austerities as also to those jewels among Brāhmaṇas, who are firmly devoted to their preceptors and live here (in my palace) and again to all my dependants too. (35-36)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठपुत्रं तु सुयज्ञमार्यं
त्वमानयाशु प्रवरं द्विजानाम्।
अपि प्रयास्यामि वनं समस्ता-
नभ्यर्च्य शिष्टानपरान् द्विजातीन्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Meanwhile bring you speedily the most adorable Suyajña, son of Vasiṣṭha and the foremost among the Brāhmaṇas, as also other cultured Brāhmaṇas. Fully adoring them all, I shall forthwith proceed to the forest.” (37)

verses.text:
ततः शासनमाज्ञाय भ्रातुः प्रियकरं हितम्।
गत्वा स प्रविवेशाशु सुयज्ञस्य निवेशनम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Bowing to the delightful and salutary command of his eldest brother (the execution of which involved substantial service to deserving Brāhmaṇas) and departing, Lakṣmaṇa speedily entered the house of Suyajña. (1)

verses.text:
तं विप्रमग्न्यगारस्थं वन्दित्वा लक्ष्मणोऽब्रवीत्।
सखेऽभ्यागच्छ पश्य त्वं वेश्म दुष्करकारिणः॥ २॥
verses.m: Saluting the said Brāhmaṇa, who was present in the fire-sanctuary, he said, “O friend, visit you the palace of Śrī Rāma, who is going to do something hard to accomplish and witness his doing with your own eyes. (2)

verses.text:
ततः संध्यामुपास्थाय गत्वा सौमित्रिणा सह।
ऋद्धं स प्राविशल्लक्ष्म्या रम्यं रामनिवेशनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Concluding forthwith his periodical fire-worship for midday and proceeding with Lakṣmaṇa, he entered in no time the lovely palace of Śrī Rāma, overflowing with wealth of all kinds. (3)

verses.text:
तमागतं वेदविदं प्राञ्जलिः सीतया सह।
सुयज्ञमभिचक्राम राघवोऽग्निमिवार्चितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing him arrived, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, rose from his seat with joined palms alongwith Sītā to receive Suyajña, a knower of the Vedas, even as one would welcome a flame offered worship in the form of oblations. (4)

verses.text:
जातरूपमयैर्मुख्यैरङ्गदैः कुण्डलैः शुभैः।
सहेमसूत्रैर्मणिभिः केयूरैर्वलयैरपि॥ ५॥
अन्यैश्च रत्नैर्बहुभिः काकुत्स्थः प्रत्यपूजयत्।
सुयज्ञं स तदोवाच रामः सीताप्रचोदितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) gratified Suyajña with presents of excellent Aṅgadas (armlets) and beautiful earrings of gold, gems strung on gold threads as also with Keyūras (another ornament similar in shape to an Aṅgada but worn above it near the arm-pit) and bracelets as well as with many other super-excellent ornaments. Urged by Sītā, the said Rāma then spoke to Suyajña as follows : (5-6)

verses.text:
हारं च हेमसूत्रं च भार्यायै सौम्य हारय।
रशनां चाथ सा सीता दातुमिच्छति ते सखी॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The illustrious Sītā, your wife’s friend, wishes to bestow a pearl necklace as well as a string of gold and also a girdle on your wife, O gentle sage ! Please cause them to be conveyed to her. (7)

verses.text:
अङ्गदानि च चित्राणि केयूराणि शुभानि च।
प्रयच्छति सखी तुभ्यं भार्यायै गच्छती वनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Leaving for the forest this very day, Sītā, the friend of your wife, wishes to offer for her use Aṅgadas adorned with figures cut in it and beautiful Keyūras too. (8)

verses.text:
पर्यङ्कमग्र्यास्तरणं नानारत्नविभूषितम्।
तमपीच्छति वैदेही प्रतिष्ठापयितुं त्वयि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Sītā, a princess of the Videha clan, also intends to have sent to your house as a gift a well-known couch inlaid with various jewels and provided with a first-class coverlet. (9)

verses.text:
नागः शत्रुंजयो नाम मातुलोऽयं ददौ मम।
तं ते निष्कसहस्रेण ददामि द्विजपुङ्गव॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I gift to you alongwith a thousand gold coins, the elephant, Śatruñjaya by name, which my maternal uncle gave as a present to me, O jewel among the Brāhmaṇas !” (10)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः स तु रामेण सुयज्ञः प्रतिगृह्य तत्।
रामलक्ष्मणसीतानां प्रयुयोजाशिषः शिवाः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Accepting the gift, when requested as aforesaid by Śrī Rāma, the celebrated Suyajña for his part pronounced benign blessings on Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā. (11)

verses.text:
अथ भ्रातरमव्यग्रं प्रियं रामः प्रियंवदम्।
सौमित्रिं तमुवाचेदं ब्रह्मेव त्रिदशेश्वरम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: As Brahmā the creator would address Indra, the ruler of gods, Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to his celebrated and beloved brother, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), who was polite of speech and stood unperturbed by his side : (12)

verses.text:
अगस्त्यं कौशिकं चैव तावुभौ ब्राह्मणोत्तमौ।
अर्चयाहूय सौमित्रे रत्नैः सस्यमिवाम्बुभिः॥ १३॥
तर्पयस्व महाबाहो गोसहस्रेण राघव।
सुवर्णरजतैश्चैव मणिभिश्च महाधनैः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Calling Agastya (a son of the sage Agastya) and Kauśika (a son of Viśwāmitra), both of whom are foremost among the Brāhmaṇas, O son of Sumitrā, honour them by offering valuable gifts to them and then satiate them with presents of a thousand cows each as well as with gold and silver pieces and costly gems even as a cloud would drench the earth with showers, O scion of Raghu ! (13-14)

verses.text:
कौसल्यां च य आशीर्भिर्भक्तः पर्युपतिष्ठति।
आचार्यस्तैत्तिरीयाणामभिरूपश्च वेदवित्॥ १५॥
तस्य यानं च दासीश्च सौमित्रे सम्प्रदापय।
कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि यावत् तुष्यति स द्विजः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Further see that to the Brāhmaṇa who waits upon Kausalyā with benendictions every day, devoted as he is to her, nay, who is a teacher of those studying the Taittirīya recesion of the Yajurveda, is a knower of all the Vedas and as such worthy in every way, O son of Sumitrā, are duly gifted a conveyance and servant-maids and silken robes and as much wealth as that Brāhmaṇa may feel satisfied with. (15-16)

verses.text:
सूतश्चित्ररथश्चार्यः सचिवः सुचिरोषितः।
तोषयैनं महार्हैश्च रत्नैर्वस्त्रैर्धनैस्तथा॥ १७॥
पशुकाभिश्च सर्वाभिर्गवां दशशतेन च।
ये चेमे कठकालापा बहवो दण्डमाणवाः॥ १८॥
नित्यस्वाध्यायशीलत्वान्नान्यत् कुर्वन्ति किंचन।
अलसाः स्वादुकामाश्च महतां चापि सम्मताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “There is the venerable Citraratha, a charioteer cum minister of very long standing. Gratify him with presents of costly jewels, articles of wearing apparel and riches and even so with animals of all kinds such as female goats and buffaloes and a thousand cows. Besides, here are many religious students carrying staffs, as a distinguishing mark of celibacy, and studying the Kaṭha and Kalāpa recensions of the Vedas, who, being ever engaged in the study of the Vedas, do not practise any other austerities in the shape of fasting etc., but are nevertheless held in great esteem even by the great for their devotion to study, are inactive in the sense that they do not move out for begging alms and yet hanker for delicacies. (17—19)

verses.text:
तेषामशीतियानानि रत्नपूर्णानि दापय।
शालिवाहसहस्रं च द्वे शते भद्रकांस्तथा॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Cause them to be given eighty camels loaded with jewels, a thousand bullocks carrying loads of rice and, even so, two hundred bullocks useful for cultivation. (20)

verses.text:
व्यञ्जनार्थं च सौमित्रे गोसहस्रमुपाकुरु।
मेखलीनां महासङ्घः कौसल्यां समुपस्थितः।
तेषां सहस्रं सौमित्रे प्रत्येकं सम्प्रदापय॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Gift a thousand cows more to Brāhmaṇas maintaining the sacred fire for yielding milk products (curds and ghee etc., used for adding flavour to food), O Lakṣmaṇa! A large multitude of celibates, willing to marry on the impending expiry of their vow of celibacy, waits upon Kausalyā, my mother: see that they are given a thousand cows or gold coins each so as to enable them to pay the preceptor’s fee and defray the nuptial expenses, O son of Sumitrā ! (21)

verses.text:
अम्बा यथा नो नन्देच्च कौसल्या मम दक्षिणाम्।
तथा द्विजातींस्तान् सर्वाल्लँक्ष्मणार्चय सर्वशः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Nay, honour all the aforesaid Brāhmaṇas in everyway so liberally that our mother, Kausalyā, may rejoice to see my gift to the celibates depending on her, O Lakṣmaṇa !” (22)

verses.text:
ततः पुरुषशार्दूलस्तद् धनं लक्ष्मणः स्वयम्।
यथोक्तं ब्राह्मणेन्द्राणामददाद् धनदो यथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Like Kubera, the bestower of riches, Lakṣmaṇa, a veritable tiger among men, thereupon distributed that wealth of Śrī Rāma among the foremost of the Brāhmaṇas as instructed by him. (23)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद् बाष्पगलांस्तिष्ठतश्चोपजीविनः।
स प्रदाय बहुद्रव्यमेकैकस्योपजीवनम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Having bestowed abundant wealth, enough to sustain each one of them for the entire period of his impending exile into the forest, Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to his dependants standing with tears blocking their throat : (24)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्य च यद् वेश्म गृहं च यदिदं मम।
अशून्यं कार्यमेकैकं यावदागमनं मम॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Till my return from the forest the house which belongs to Lakṣmaṇa and also this house which is now occupied by me should always be guarded by each one of you by turn.” (25)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा दुःखितं सर्वं जनं तमुपजीविनम्।
उवाचेदं धनाध्यक्षं धनमानीयतां मम॥ २६॥
verses.m: Having instructed thus all his dependants, distressed as they were at the thought of his exile, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows to his treasurer, “Let my wealth be brought here.” (26)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्य धनमाजह्रुः सर्व एवोपजीविनः।
स राशिः सुमहांस्तत्र दर्शनीयो ह्यदृश्यत॥ २७॥
verses.m: All his dependants thereupon brought his wealth before him. That huge heap of wealth collected there really presented a splendid spectacle. (27)

verses.text:
ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तद् धनं सहलक्ष्मणः।
द्विजेभ्यो बालवृद्धेभ्यः कृपणेभ्यो ह्यदापयत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: With the help of Lakṣmaṇa that tiger among men then actually caused that wealth to be distributed among Brāhmaṇas, who were yet mere boys or aged, and to the afflicted. (28)

verses.text:
तत्रासीत् पिङ्गलो गार्ग्यस्त्रिजटो नाम वै द्विजः।
क्षतवृत्तिर्वने नित्यं फालकुद्दाललाङ्गली॥ २९॥
verses.m: “They say there lived in those days in the forest near about Ayodhyā, a Brāhmaṇa, Trijaṭa by name, born in the line of Garga, who looked pale due to privations and, all his means of subsistence having failed, always carried an axe, a spade and a ploughshare living as he did by digging the soil in order to get roots and bulbs etc. (29)

verses.text:
तं वृद्धं तरुणी भार्या बालानादाय दारकान्।
अब्रवीद् ब्राह्मणं वाक्यं स्त्रीणां भर्ता हि देवता॥ ३०॥
अपास्य फालं कुद्दालं कुरुष्व वचनं मम।
रामं दर्शय धर्मज्ञं यदि किंचिदवाप्स्यसि॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Taking her young children with her, his wife, who was still young, approached and spoke to the said Brāhmaṇa, who had grown old, as follows : “Although the husband is a veritable god to the weaker sex, does not deserve to be commanded by his wife, pray, follow my instructions, discarding the hatchet and the spade. Seek the presence of Śrī Rāma, who knows his duty by the Brāhmaṇas and you are sure to get something at least.” (30-31)

verses.text:
स भार्याया वचः श्रुत्वा शाटीमाच्छाद्य दुश्छदाम्।
स प्रातिष्ठत पन्थानं यत्र रामनिवेशनम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing the request of his wife and wrapping about his lower limbs a loin-cloth, that could hardly cover his body, tattered as it was, he set out on the track which led to Śrī Rāma’s palace. (32)

verses.text:
भृग्वङ्गिरःसमं दीप्त्या त्रिजटं जनसंसदि।
आपञ्चमायाः कक्ष्याया नैतं कश्चिदवारयत्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Up to the fifth gate none in the large concourse of men, collected at the gates of the palace, stopped this Trijaṭa, who vied with the sages Bhṛgu and Angirā in spiritual glow befitting a Brāhmaṇa. (33)

verses.text:
स राममासाद्य तदा त्रिजटो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
निर्धनो बहुपुत्रोऽस्मि राजपुत्र महाबल॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Approaching Śrī Rāma, the said Trijaṭa then spoke as follows : “I have many children, though destitute, O prince of extraordinary might ! (34)

verses.text:
क्षतवृत्तिर्वने नित्यं प्रत्यवेक्षस्व मामिति।
तमुवाच ततो रामः परिहाससमन्वितम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “All my means of subsistence having failed, I perpetually dwell in the forest. Pray, look to me.” Śrī Rāma thereupon replied jestingly to him as follows: (35)

verses.text:
गवां सहस्रमप्येकं न च विश्राणितं मया।
परिक्षिपसि दण्डेन यावत्तावदवाप्स्यसे॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Not even one thousand of my cows have been given away by me so far. You will get as many of them as you will cover by throwing your staff across them.” (36)

verses.text:
स शाटीं परितः कट्यां सम्भ्रान्तः परिवेष्ट्य ताम्।
आविध्य दण्डं चिक्षेप सर्वप्राणेन वेगतः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Tightening his aforesaid loin-cloth round his waist and twirling his staff he violently threw it with all his might, excited as he was. (37)

verses.text:
स तीर्त्वा सरयूपारं दण्डस्तस्य कराच्च्युतः।
गोव्रजे बहुसाहस्रे पपातोक्षणसंनिधौ॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Released from his hand and flying across the Sarayū, that staff fell close to a bull in the midst of the multitude of cows numbering many thousand, grazing there. (38)

verses.text:
तं परिष्वज्य धर्मात्मा आ तस्मात् सरयूतटात्।
आनयामास ता गावस्त्रिजटस्याश्रमं प्रति॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Embracing him, Śrī Rāma of devout mind, caused to be driven to Trijaṭa’s hermitage all the cows from the spot where the staff fell right up to that bank of the Sarayū beyond which the cows stood grazing. (39)

verses.text:
उवाच च तदा रामस्तं गार्ग्यमभिसान्त्वयन्।
मन्युर्न खलु कर्तव्यः परिहासो ह्ययं मम॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Nay, consoling the said scion of Garga in everyway, Śrī Rāma then said to him, “No offence should be taken by you, since this was only a jest indulged in by me. (40)

verses.text:
इदं हि तेजस्तव यद् दुरत्ययं
तदेव जिज्ञासितुमिच्छता मया।
इमं भवानर्थमभिप्रचोदितो
वृणीष्व किंचेदपरं व्यवस्यसि॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “You were requested by me to undergo this trial wishing, as I did, precisely to test this remarkable strength of yours, which is really hard to excel. If you desire anything else, please ask for it. (41)

verses.text:
ब्रवीमि सत्येन न ते स्म यन्त्रणां
धनं हि यद्यन्मम विप्रकारणात्।
भवत्सु सम्यक्प्रतिपादनेन
मयार्जितं चैव यशस्करं भवेत्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I tell you the truth: let there be no hesitation on your part; for whatever wealth belongs to me has been earned by me for the sake of Brāhmaṇas alone. Nay, through bestowal on you (Brāhmaṇas) according to the scriptural ordinance it will bring me renown.” (42)

verses.text:
ततः सभार्यस्त्रिजटो महामुनि-
र्गवामनीकं प्रतिगृह्य मोदितः।
यशोबलप्रीतिसुखोपबृंहिणी-
स्तदाशिषः प्रत्यवदन्महात्मनः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Taking the herd of cows bestowed upon him by Śrī Rāma the great ascetic, Trijaṭa, who felt rejoiced with his wife, thereupon pronounced on Śrī Rāma (the magnanimous prince) at that time blessings calculated to enhance his reputation, strength, delight and happiness. (43)

verses.text:
स चापि रामः प्रतिपूर्णपौरुषो
महाधनं धर्मबलैरुपार्जितम्।
नियोजयामास सुहृज्जने चिराद्
यथार्हसम्मानवचः प्रचोदितः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Encouraged by words expressive of highest regard befitting his rank, the illustrious Śrī Rāma too, who was endowed with perfect valour, portioned out to his near and dear ones in no time his enormous wealth earned through righteous might. (44)

verses.text:
द्विजः सुहृद् भृत्यजनोऽथवा तदा
दरिद्रभिक्षाचरणश्च यो भवेत्।
न तत्र कश्चिन्न बभूव तर्पितो
यथार्हसम्माननदानसम्भ्रमैः ॥ ४५॥
verses.m: At that time in Ayodhyā there was no Brāhmaṇa, relation, dependant or pauper who was living on alms, who was not gratified with honour, gifts and attentions conformable to his deserts. (45)

verses.text:
दत्त्वा तु सह वैदेह्या ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं बहु।
जग्मतुः पितरं द्रष्टुं सीतया सह राघवौ॥ १॥
verses.m: Having portioned out with Sītā (a princess of the Videha clan) abundant riches to the Brāhmaṇas, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, for their part proceeded with her to see their father, Emperor Daśaratha. (1)

verses.text:
ततो गृहीते प्रेष्याभ्यामशोभेतां तदायुधे।
मालादामभिरासक्ते सीतया समलंकृते॥ २॥
verses.m: Next to them shone the weapons of the two brothers, held by a couple of servants and nay, decorated with a number of wreaths and worshipped by Sītā herself with sandal paste etc. (2)

verses.text:
ततः प्रासादहर्म्याणि विमानशिखराणि च।
अभिरुह्य जनः श्रीमानुदासीनो व्यलोकयत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Ascending the roofs of temples and mansions and the tops of seven-storeyed buildings wealthy people gazed despondently on them. (3)

verses.text:
न हि रथ्याः सुशक्यन्ते गन्तुं बहुजनाकुलाः।
आरुह्य तस्मात् प्रासादाद् दीनाः पश्यन्ति राघवम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: The streets could not be easily passed through, crowded as they were with many men; mounting, therefore, to the top of seven-storeyed buildings, people looked sorrowfully on Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, from those mansions. (4)

verses.text:
पदातिं सानुजं दृष्ट्वा ससीतं च जनास्तदा।
ऊचुर्बहुजना वाचः शोकोपहतचेतसः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma walking with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, his younger brother, at that time, many men offered remarks as follows, their mind infatuated with grief : (5)

verses.text:
यं यान्तमनुयाति स्म चतुरङ्गबलं महत्।
तमेकं सीतया सार्धमनुयाति स्म लक्ष्मणः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Lo ! the same Śrī Rāma, who was at one time followed by a strong detachment consisting of all the four limbs (viz, infantry, cavalry, elephants and chariots), is walking, unattended by bodyguards, with Sītā, followed by Lakṣmaṇa alone. (6)

verses.text:
ऐश्वर्यस्य रसज्ञः सन् कामानां चाकरो महान्।
नेच्छत्येवानृतं कर्तुं वचनं धर्मगौरवात्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “He who, having tasted the delights of sovereignty, is a great repertory of objects of enjoyment, is anxious not to belie the plighted word of his father, prompted as he is by respect for virtue. (7)

verses.text:
या न शक्या पुरा द्रष्टुं भूतैराकाशगैरपि।
तामद्य सीतां पश्यन्ति राजमार्गगता जनाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Even people on the roads are able today to behold Sītā, who could not formerly be seen even by beings coursing in the air. (8)

verses.text:
अङ्गरागोचितां सीतां रक्तचन्दनसेविनीम्।
वर्षमुष्णं च शीतं च नेष्यत्याशु विवर्णताम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Rain, heat and cold will quickly reduce to pallor Sītā, who deserves to be daubed with pigments (such as musk-paste) and habitually paints her body with the paste of red sandal. (9)

verses.text:
अद्य नूनं दशरथः सत्त्वमाविश्य भाषते।
नहि राजा प्रियं पुत्रं विवासयितुमर्हति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Surely King Daśaratha has announced today his decision to banish Śrī Rāma, identifying himself with some evil spirit; for otherwise had he been his normal self he would not have sent his dearest son into exile. (10)

verses.text:
निर्गुणस्यापि पुत्रस्य कथं स्याद् विनिवासनम्।
किं पुनर्यस्य लोकोऽयं जितो वृत्तेन केवलम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “How could banishment be inflicted even on a son devoid of virtue, much less on him whose character alone has won the affection of the entire world? (11)

verses.text:
आनृशंस्यमनुक्रोशः श्रुतं शीलं दमः शमः।
राघवं शोभयन्त्येते षड्गुणाः पुरुषर्षभम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Harmlessness, compassion, learning, amiability of disposition, subjugation of the senses and tranquillity of mind—these six excellences adorn Śrī Rāma, the foremost of men. (12)

verses.text:
तस्मात् तस्योपघातेन प्रजाः परमपीडिताः।
औदकानीव सत्त्वानि ग्रीष्मे सलिलसंक्षयात्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “People, therefore, feel extremely pained by the injury which is being done to him by way of unmerited banishment, even as aquatic creatures are afflicted by depletion of water. (13)

verses.text:
पीडया पीडितं सर्वं जगदस्य जगत्पतेः।
मूलस्येवोपघातेन वृक्षः पुष्पफलोपगः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The whole world feels injured by the suffering inflicted on this protector of the world, even as a tree with its flowers and fruits is damaged by injury caused to its root. (14)

verses.text:
मूलं ह्येष मनुष्याणां धर्मसारो महाद्युतिः।
पुष्पं फलं च पत्रं च शाखाश्चास्येतरे जनाः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “For, Śrī Rāma, whose strength is virtue and who is possessed of extraordinary lustre, is the root of the tree of humanity; while other men are flowers and fruits, leaves and boughs. (15)

verses.text:
ते लक्ष्मण इव क्षिप्रं सपत्न्यः सहबान्धवाः।
गच्छन्तमनुगच्छामो येन गच्छति राघवः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “As such even as Lakṣmaṇa we will also with our wives and relations forthwith follow the departing Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, on the path the former is going to tread. (16)

verses.text:
उद्यानानि परित्यज्य क्षेत्राणि च गृहाणि च।
एकदुःखसुखा राममनुगच्छाम धार्मिकम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Relinquishing for good our gardens and fields and houses too, let us follow the pious Śrī Rāma, sharing his joys and sorrows. (17)

verses.text:
समुद्धृतनिधानानि परिध्वस्ताजिराणि च।
उपात्तधनधान्यानि हृतसाराणि सर्वशः॥ १८॥
रजसाभ्यवकीर्णानि परित्यक्तानि दैवतैः।
मूषकैः परिधावद्भिरुद्बिलैरावृतानि च॥ १९॥
अपेतोदकधूमानि हीनसम्मार्जनानि च।
प्रणष्टबलिकर्मेज्यामन्त्रहोमजपानि च॥ २०॥
दुष्कालेनेव भग्नानि भिन्नभाजनवन्ति च।
अस्मत्त्यक्तानि कैकेयी वेश्मानि प्रतिपद्यताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let Kaikeyī enjoy as her share the dwellings deserted by us and robbed of their substance in every way—their treasures unearthed, their courtyards neglected, their wealth and stocks of foodgrains removed—nay, covered by dust on all sides and as such deserted by the deities presiding over them, overrun by mice coming out of their holes and scurrying here and there, water and smoke having disappeared from them, unswept, dilapidated as though by adverse times and strewn with broken vessels, the rites of offering oblations to all creatures as well as to the sacred fire, worship of gods, the chanting of sacred texts and muttering of prayers having altogether ceased. (18—21)

verses.text:
वनं नगरमेवास्तु येन गच्छति राघवः।
अस्माभिश्च परित्यक्तं पुरं सम्पद्यतां वनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Let the forest itself, for which Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, is leaving, turn into a city and let the city of Ayodhyā, when deserted by us, be converted into a forest. (22)

verses.text:
बिलानि दंष्ट्रिणः सर्वे सानूनि मृगपक्षिणः।
त्यजन्त्वस्मद्भयाद्भीता गजाः सिंहा वनान्यपि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Scared by fear of us, all the snakes will forsake their holes; the deer and birds, their abode on the mountain-peaks and elephants and lions, the forests. (23)

verses.text:
अस्मत्त्यक्तं प्रपद्यन्तु सेव्यमानं त्यजन्तु च।
तृणमांसफलादानां देशं व्यालमृगद्विजम्॥ २४॥
प्रपद्यतां हि कैकेयी सपुत्रा सह बान्धवैः।
राघवेण वयं सर्वे वने वत्स्याम निर्वृताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Let them abandon the region going to be inhabited by us and flee for protection to the one forsaken by us. Let Kaikeyī with her son and relations actually obtain as her share the region where grass, meat and fruits can be had in abundance and which is inhabited by ferocious beasts and birds. We shall, on the other hand, live happily in the forest with Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu.” (24-25)

verses.text:
इत्येवं विविधा वाचो नानाजनसमीरिताः।
शुश्राव राघवः श्रुत्वा न विचक्रेऽस्य मानसम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, heard the aforesaid remarks of diverse kinds uttered by various men; hearing them, however, his mind was not in the least disturbed. (26)

verses.text:
स तु वेश्म पुनर्मातुः कैलासशिखरप्रभम्।
अभिचक्राम धर्मात्मा मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः॥ २७॥
verses.m: The prince, whose mind was given to piety, for his part walked once more with the strides of an elephant in rut to the palace of mother Kaikeyī, which shone as a peak of the Kailāsa mountain and in which his father was still lingering. (27)

verses.text:
विनीतवीरपुरुषं प्रविश्य तु नृपालयम्।
ददर्शावस्थितं दीनं सुमन्त्रमविदूरतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Entering the royal palace, however, which was being guarded by disciplined and valiant soldiers, he saw Sumantra standing disconsolate not very far from the palace. (28)

verses.text:
प्रतीक्षमाणोऽभिजनं तदार्त-
मनार्तरूपः प्रहसन्निवाथ।
जगाम रामः पितरं दिदृक्षुः
पितुर्निदेशं विधिवच्चिकीर्षुः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Appearing in no way afflicted, even though seeing the people of Ayodhyā, his native place, distressed at that time, Śrī Rāma as though smiling, forthwith approached his father, eager to see him and desirous of duly carrying out his behest. (29)

verses.text:
तत्पूर्वमैक्ष्वाकसुतो महात्मा
रामो गमिष्यन् नृपमार्तरूपम्।
व्यतिष्ठत प्रेक्ष्य तदा सुमन्त्रं
पितुर्महात्मा प्रतिहारणार्थम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Catching sight of Sumantra before that, while approaching the king, who wore a wretched appearance, the high-souled and high-minded Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, a scion of Ikṣwāku, waited awhile to announce his presence to his father. (30)

verses.text:
पितुर्निदेशेन तु धर्मवत्सलो
वनप्रवेशे कृतबुद्धिनिश्चयः।
स राघवः प्रेक्ष्य सुमन्त्रमब्रवी-
न्निवेदयस्वागमनं नृपाय मे॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Perceiving Sumantra, the illustrious Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was devoted to his duty and had for his part deliberately made up his mind to retire to the woods in obedience to the command of his father, said to him, “Pray, announce my arrival to His Majesty.” (31)

verses.text:
ततः कमलपत्राक्षः श्यामो निरुपमो महान्।
उवाच रामस्तं सूतं पितुराख्याहि मामिति॥ १॥
verses.m: Then the lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma, who was dark-brown of complexion and great beyond compare, spoke as follows to the said charioteer-minister: “Please announce me to father.” (1)

verses.text:
स रामप्रेषितः क्षिप्रं संतापकलुषेन्द्रियम्।
प्रविश्य नृपतिं सूतो निःश्वसन्तं ददर्श ह॥ २॥
verses.m: Promptly going inside, when despatched by Śrī Rāma, the charioteer found the king heaving sighs, his mind distracted with agony: so the tradition goes. (2)

verses.text:
उपरक्तमिवादित्यं भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम्।
तटाकमिव निस्तोयमपश्यज्जगतीपतिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: He regarded the Emperor as one would view the sun obscured by intervention of the earth between it and the eye (i.e., during solar eclipse) or a fire covered with ashes or a pond without water. (3)

verses.text:
आबोध्य च महाप्राज्ञः परमाकुलचेतनम्।
राममेवानुशोचन्तं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Accosting the king, whose mind was extremely agitated and who was grieving for Śrī Rāma alone, the highly enlightened charioteer, spoke with joined palms to him.(4)

verses.text:
तं वर्धयित्वा राजानं पूर्वं सूतो जयाशिषा।
भयविक्लवया वाचा मन्दया श्लक्ष्णयाब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Encouraging Daśaratha first with benedictions wishing him triumph, the charioteer addressed him in a low, soft and sweet tone faltering with fear: (5)

verses.text:
अयं स पुरुषव्याघ्रो द्वारि तिष्ठति ते सुतः।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा सर्वं चैवोपजीविनाम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Having given away all his wealth to the Brāhmaṇas as well as to his dependants, Śrī Rāma illustrious son of yours, a veritable tiger among men, stands at the door. (6)

verses.text:
स त्वां पश्यतु भद्रं ते रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
सर्वान् सुहृद आपृच्छ्य त्वां हीदानीं दिदृक्षते॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Let that Rāma of unfailing prowess see you: may good betide you; for, having taken leave of all his near and dear ones, he now desires to see Your Majesty. (7)

verses.text:
गमिष्यति महारण्यं तं पश्य जगतीपते।
वृतं राजगुणैः सर्वैरादित्यमिव रश्मिभिः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “He is about to proceed to the extensive forest. Pray, behold the prince, who is encompassed by kingly virtues even as the sun is encircled by rays.” (8)

verses.text:
स सत्यवाक्यो धर्मात्मा गाम्भीर्यात् सागरोपमः।
आकाश इव निष्पङ्को नरेन्द्रः प्रत्युवाच तम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: That pious monarch, who was truthful of speech and vied with the ocean in profundity, nay, who was stainless as the sky, replied to him as follows : (9)

verses.text:
सुमन्त्रानय मे दारान् ये केचिदिह मामकाः।
दारैः परिवृतः सर्वैर्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Sumantra, bring all my consorts who are here in the gynaeceum. I wish to see Rāma, a scion of Raghu, when I am accompanied by my wives.” (10)

verses.text:
सोऽन्तःपुरमतीत्यैव स्त्रियस्ता वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
आर्यो ह्वयति वो राजा गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Directly on entering the apartments of the other queens, Sumantra addressed those ladies as follows : “His Majesty the king summons you all; pray, let yourselves proceed there without delay.” (11)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः सुमन्त्रेण नृपाज्ञया।
प्रचक्रमुस्तद् भवनं भर्तुराज्ञाय शासनम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Coming to know the command of their husband, when addressed as above by Sumantra under orders of His Majesty, all the royal ladies proceeded to Kaikeyī’s apartments. (12)

verses.text:
अर्धसप्तशतास्तत्र प्रमदास्ताम्रलोचनाः।
कौसल्यां परिवार्याथ शनैर्जग्मुर्धृतव्रताः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Encircling Kausalyā, the seniormost queen, three hundred and fifty young ladies, steadfast in their vow of devotion to their husband, forthwith repaired to the king’s presence, their eyes reddened through grief over their impending separation from Śrī Rāma. (13)

verses.text:
आगतेषु च दारेषु समवेक्ष्य महीपतिः।
उवाच राजा तं सूतं सुमन्त्रानय मे सुतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Observing his consorts when they had come, the King-Emperor said to the celebrated charioteer, “Sumantra, now bring my son before me.” (14)

verses.text:
स सूतो राममादाय लक्ष्मणं मैथिलीं तथा।
जगामाभिमुखस्तूर्णं सकाशं जगतीपतेः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Taking Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, princess of Mithilā, the said charioteer speedily returned to the Emperor’s presence with his face turned towards the latter. (15)

verses.text:
स राजा पुत्रमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा चारात् कृताञ्जलिम्।
उत्पपातासनात् तूर्णमार्तः स्त्रीजनसंवृतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Beholding his son, Śrī Rāma, coming with folded hands from a distance, the illustrious king immediately rose from his seat alongwith the ladies, afflicted as he was. (16)

verses.text:
सोऽभिदुद्राव वेगेन रामं दृष्ट्वा विशाम्पतिः।
तमसम्प्राप्य दुःखार्तः पपात भुवि मूर्च्छितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma, the said king ran with impetuosity towards the latter. Before reaching him, however, he dropped senseless to the ground, stricken as he was with sorrow. (17)

verses.text:
तं रामोऽभ्यपतत् क्षिप्रं लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः।
विसंज्ञमिव दुःखेन सशोकं नृपतिं तथा॥ १८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa, an eminent chariot-warrior, rushed at once to the king, who lay quite unconscious as aforesaid, full of grief as he was through agony. (18)

verses.text:
स्त्रीसहस्रनिनादश्च संजज्ञे राजवेश्मनि।
हा हा रामेति सहसा भूषणध्वनिमिश्रितः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Nay, there burst forth all of a sudden in the palace a loud wail, mixed with the tinkling of ornaments, of thousands of women crying “Alas ! Alas !! O Rāma !!!” (19)

verses.text:
तं परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
पर्यङ्के सीतया सार्धं रुदन्तः समवेशयन्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Supporting him in their arms and crying, both the princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa alongwith Sītā laid him on the couch. (20)

verses.text:
अथ रामो मुहूर्तस्य लब्धसंज्ञं महीपतिम्।
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्बाष्पशोकार्णवपरिप्लुतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: With folded hands Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to the Emperor, who had soon regained his consciousness and was plunged in an ocean of grief, shedding tears : (21)

verses.text:
आपृच्छे त्वां महाराज सर्वेषामीश्वरोऽसि नः।
प्रस्थितं दण्डकारण्यं पश्य त्वं कुशलेन माम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I take leave of you, O Emperor, since you are the master of us all. Pray, regard me, who am about to leave for the Daṇḍaka forest, with favour. (22)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणं चानुजानीहि सीता चान्वेतु मां वनम्।
कारणैर्बहुभिस्तथ्यैर्वार्यमाणौ न चेच्छतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Grant leave to Lakṣmaṇa and let Sītā too accompany me to the forest. Though being forbidden by me on numerous valid grounds, they do not wish to stay behind. (23)

verses.text:
अनुजानीहि सर्वान् नः शोकमुत्सृज्य मानद।
लक्ष्मणं मां च सीतां च प्रजापतिरिवात्मजान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Giving up grief, O bestower of honour on all, grant leave to us all, viz., Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā and myself, even as Brahmā, the lord of created beings, did to his sons, Sanaka and his three brothers, who were intent on practising austerities in the forest.” (24)

verses.text:
प्रतीक्षमाणमव्यग्रमनुज्ञां जगतीपतेः।
उवाच राजा सम्प्रेक्ष्य वनवासाय राघवम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Fixing his gaze on Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was coolly awaiting His Majesty’s permission to dwell in the forest, the king said : (25)

verses.text:
अहं राघव कैकेय्या वरदानेन मोहितः।
अयोध्यायां त्वमेवाद्य भव राजा निगृह्य माम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I have been deprived of my senses by Kaikeyī through a boon granted by me in her favour, O scion of Raghu ! Taking me captive, therefore, be you the king of Ayodhyā.” (26)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो नृपतिना रामो धर्मभृतां वरः।
प्रत्युवाचाञ्जलिं कृत्वा पितरं वाक्यकोविदः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Joining his palms when told thus by the king, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of the champions of righteousness, who was a master of expression, replied as follows to his father : (27)

verses.text:
भवान् वर्षसहस्राय पृथिव्या नृपते पतिः।
अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि न मे राज्यस्य कांक्षिता॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Be you the ruler of the globe for another thousand years, O king ! I for my part shall live in the forest, since there is no ambition for sovereignty in me. (28)

verses.text:
नव पञ्च च वर्षाणि वनवासे विहृत्य ते।
पुनः पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि प्रतिज्ञान्ते नराधिप॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Having diverted myself in the course of my sojourn in the forest for nine years and five, I shall clasp your feet once more after redeeming my pledge, O ruler of men !” (29)

verses.text:
रुदन्नार्तः प्रियं पुत्रं सत्यपाशेन संयुतः।
कैकेय्या चोद्यमानस्तु मिथो राजा तमब्रवीत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Being urged in secret by Kaikeyī, the afflicted monarch, who was held fast in the fetters of truth, then said weeping to his aforesaid beloved son : (30)

verses.text:
श्रेयसे वृद्धये तात पुनरागमनाय च।
गच्छस्वारिष्टमव्यग्रः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Proceed, my darling, with an undisturbed mind on a happy and safe journey, which may bring you happiness hereafter and prosperity in this world and bring you back to Ayodhyā. (31)

verses.text:
न हि सत्यात्मनस्तात धर्माभिमनसस्तव।
संनिवर्तयितुं बुद्धिः शक्यते रघुनन्दन॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Your decision to dwell in the forest, O the delight of the Raghus, truthful as you are by nature and your mind being given to piety, O darling, cannot be reversed. (32)

verses.text:
अद्य त्विदानीं रजनीं पुत्र मा गच्छ सर्वथा।
एकाहं दर्शनेनापि साधु तावच्चराम्यहम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Pray, do not leave in any case today and stay at least for this night with me, so that I may live happily by your sight at least for a day. (33)

verses.text:
मातरं मां च सम्पश्यन् वसेमामद्य शर्वरीम्।
तर्पितः सर्वकामैस्त्वं श्वः काल्ये साधयिष्यसि॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Looking at your mother and myself, stay on the coming night today. Having been gratified by me with all desired objects you may leave the very next morning. (34)

verses.text:
दुष्करं क्रियते पुत्र सर्वथा राघव प्रिय।
त्वया हि मत्प्रियार्थं तु वनमेवमुपाश्रितम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Something which is in every respect hard to accomplish for others is being done by you, my beloved son, since it is for my sake that the forest is thus being resorted to by you, O scion of Raghu ! (35)

verses.text:
न चैतन्मे प्रियं पुत्र शपे सत्येन राघव।
छन्नया चलितस्त्वस्मि स्त्रिया भस्माग्निकल्पया॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “But I swear by my faith, my son : your exile is not agreeable to me, O Rāma ! On the other hand, I have been deflected from my course by Kaikeyī, who concealed her intentions and thus resembled a fire covered with ashes. (36)

verses.text:
वञ्चना या तु लब्धा मे तां त्वं निस्तर्तुमिच्छसि।
अनया वृत्तसादिन्या कैकेय्याभिप्रचोदितः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “How noble of you that egged on by Kaikeyī, who has cast to the winds the time-honoured family custom of a kingdom being inherited by the eldest son, you seek to redeem a pledge which was fraudulently extracted from me ! (37)

verses.text:
न चैतदाश्चर्यतमं यत् त्वं ज्येष्ठः सुतो मम।
अपानृतकथं पुत्र पितरं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “It is no great wonder, my child, that you, my seniormost son, both in point of age and virtue, should seek to make your father free from mendacity.” (38)

verses.text:
अथ रामस्तदा श्रुत्वा पितुरार्तस्य भाषितम्।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा दीनो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Distressed to hear on that occasion the request of his afflicted father, Śrī Rāma, alongwith his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, submitted as follows : (39)

verses.text:
प्राप्स्यामि यानद्य गुणान् को मे श्वस्तान् प्रदास्यति।
अपक्रमणमेवातः सर्वकामैरहं वृणे॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Tomorrow who will offer me the delicacies which I hope to get today? I should therefore only prefer to get away in lieu of all the enjoyments you can offer. (40)

verses.text:
इयं सराष्ट्रा सजना धनधान्यसमाकुला।
मया विसृष्टा वसुधा भरताय प्रदीयताम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Relinquished by me, this earth including the state of Kosala and its people and full of riches and foodgrains, may be made over to Bharata. (41)

verses.text:
वनवासकृता बुद्धिर्न च मेऽद्य चलिष्यति।
यस्तु युद्धे वरो दत्तः कैकेय्यै वरद त्वया॥ ४२॥
दीयतां निखिलेनैव सत्यस्त्वं भव पार्थिव।
अहं निदेशं भवतो यथोक्तमनुपालयन्॥ ४३॥
चतुर्दश समा वत्स्ये वने वनचरैः सह।
मा विमर्शो वसुमती भरताय प्रदीयताम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “My resolution to dwell in the forest shall in no case be shaken. The boon which was granted by you on the battlefield in favour of Kaikeyī, O bestower of boons, may, therefore, be implemented in toto at all events, and thus vindicate you your truthfulness, O ruler of the earth ! Carrying out your aforesaid command I shall dwell in the forest with ascetics for fourteen years. Let there be no demur on your part. The earth may be made over to Bharata. (42—44)

verses.text:
नहि मे कांक्षितं राज्यं सुखमात्मनि वा प्रियम्।
यथानिदेशं कर्तुं वै तवैव रघुनन्दन॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, neither sovereignty nor joy nor what is pleasing to the mind is coveted by me. On the other hand, to do as enjoined by you is solely desired by me, O the delight of the Raghus ! (45)

verses.text:
अपगच्छतु ते दुःखं मा भूर्बाष्पपरिप्लुतः।
नहि क्षुभ्यति दुर्धर्षः समुद्रः सरितां पतिः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Let your sorrow disappear and let you not be bathed in tears. The ocean, the lord of the rivers, which it is so difficult to assail, does not overstep its bounds. (46)

verses.text:
नैवाहं राज्यमिच्छामि न सुखं न च मेदिनीम्।
नैव सर्वानिमान् कामान् न स्वर्गं न च जीवितुम्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “I do not at all hanker for sovereignty or joy, nor again for the earth, nor in any case for all these delights of sense, nor for heaven nor even for life. (47)

verses.text:
त्वामहं सत्यमिच्छामि नानृतं पुरुषर्षभ।
प्रत्यक्षं तव सत्येन सुकृतेन च ते शपे॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “I swear by my veracity and virtue earned by me in my past lives as well as by you in your presence : I only wish you to prove true to your word and never to be false, O jewel among men ! (48)

verses.text:
न च शक्यं मया तात स्थातुं क्षणमपि प्रभो।
स शोकं धारयस्वेमं नहि मेऽस्ति विपर्ययः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Nor is it possible for me, dear father, to stay on at home even for an instant longer. Therefore, restrain this grief, my lord; for there is no going back upon my word now. (49)

verses.text:
अर्थितो ह्यस्मि कैकेय्या वनं गच्छेति राघव।
मया चोक्तं व्रजामीति तत्सत्यमनुपालये॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Since I have been commanded by mother Kaikeyī in the words ‘Proceed to the forest, O scion of Raghu’ and the reply given by me was ‘I am going’, I must redeem that pledge of mine. (50)

verses.text:
मा चोत्कण्ठां कृथा देव वने रंस्यामहे वयम्।
प्रशान्तहरिणाकीर्णे नानाशकुनिनादिते॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Nor should you feel anxious on our score, my lord ! We shall sport in the forest crowded with highly peaceful deer and rendered noisy by birds of various kinds. (51)

verses.text:
पिता हि दैवतं तात देवतानामपि स्मृतम्।
तस्माद् दैवतमित्येव करिष्यामि पितुर्वचः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a father has been declared to be a veritable deity even among gods. Hence I shall do the bidding of my father (yourself) as that of a god. (52)

verses.text:
चतुर्दशसु वर्षेषु गतेषु नृपसत्तम।
पुनर्द्रक्ष्यसि मां प्राप्तं संतापोऽयं विमुच्यताम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “When fourteen years have elapsed, you will find me come back, O jewel among kings ! Hence let this agony be given up. (53)

verses.text:
येन संस्तम्भनीयोऽयं सर्वो बाष्पकलो जनः।
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल किमर्थं विक्रियां गतः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Wherefore, O tiger among men, have you fallen a victim to grief—you, by whom all these other people, bathed in tears, ought to be consoled? (54)

verses.text:
पुरं च राष्ट्रं च मही च केवला
मया विसृष्टा भरताय दीयताम्।
अहं निदेशं भवतोऽनुपालयन्
वनं गमिष्यामि चिराय सेवितुम्॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “Renounced by me, the city of Ayodhyā and the state of Kosala and the rest of the globe too may be given to Bharata. Obeying your command, I for myself shall proceed to the forest in order to dwell in it for long. (55)

verses.text:
मया विसृष्टां भरतो महीमिमां
सशैलखण्डां सपुरोपकाननाम्।
शिवासु सीमास्वनुशास्तु केवलं
त्वया यदुक्तं नृपते तथास्तु तत्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Let Bharata rule over this globe, including the mountain ranges and cities with their gardens, relinquished by me. He should neither enjoy the sovereignty nor feel proud of it but keep within the bounds of righteousness salutary for a king. Let the pledge which has been given by you to Kaikeyī come to be true, O protector of men ! (56)

verses.text:
न मे तथा पार्थिव धीयते मनो
महत्सु कामेषु न चात्मनः प्रिये।
यथा निदेशे तव शिष्टसम्मते
व्यपैतु दुःखं तव मत्कृतेऽनघ॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “My heart is not given so much to the great delights of sense coveted by all, nor to that which is pleasing to the mind, as to the carrying out of your command, which is approved by the wise. Let your agony on my score, O sinless king, altogether disappear. (57)

verses.text:
तदद्य नैवानघ राज्यमव्ययं
न सर्वकामान् वसुधां न मैथिलीम्।
न चिन्तितं त्वामनृतेन योजयन्
वृणीय सत्यं व्रतमस्तु ते तथा॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Disfiguring you, who are full of anxiety on my score, with the stigma of mendacity, I do not on any account court eternal sovereignty nor all the delights of sense coveted by the world, nor the entire earth, nor even Sītā, princess of Mithilā, today, O sinless one ! Therefore, let your pledge given to Kaikeyī prove true. (58)

verses.text:
फलानि मूलानि च भक्षयन् वने
गिरींश्च पश्यन् सरितः सरांसि च।
वनं प्रविश्यैव विचित्रपादपं
सुखी भविष्यामि तवास्तु निर्वृतिः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Living in the forest on fruits and roots and viewing the mountains, rivers and lakes, I shall be happy the moment I enter the forest consisting of various trees. Let peace come to you on this account.” (59)

verses.text:
एवं स राजा व्यसनाभिपन्न-
स्तापेन दुःखेन च पीड्यमानः।
आलिङ्ग्य पुत्रं सुविनष्टसंज्ञो
भूमिं गतो नैव चिचेष्ट किंचित्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Embracing his son, Śrī Rāma, who had spoken as above, King Daśaratha, who had fallen on evil days and was being tormented with a burning sensation and agony, fell utterly unconscious to the ground and did not show any sign of life at all. (60)

verses.text:
देव्यः समस्ता रुरुदुः समेता-
स्तां वर्जयित्वा नरदेवपत्नीम्।
रुदन् सुमन्त्रोऽपि जगाम मूर्च्छां
हाहाकृतं तत्र बभूव सर्वम्॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Barring that favourite consort of Daśaratha, Kaikeyī, all the queens assembled there began to cry. Weeping aloud Sumantra too fell into a swoon and everyone there began to lament loudly. (61)

verses.text:
ततो निधूय सहसा शिरो निःश्वस्य चासकृत्।
पाणिं पाणौ विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान् कटकटाय्य च॥ १॥
लोचने कोपसंरक्ते वर्णं पूर्वोचितं जहत्।
कोपाभिभूतः सहसा संतापमशुभं गतः॥ २॥
मनः समीक्षमाणश्च सूतो दशरथस्य च।
कम्पयन्निव कैकेय्या हृदयं वाक्शरैः शितैः॥ ३॥
वाक्यवज्रैरनुपमैर्निर्भिन्दन्निव चाशुभैः।
कैकेय्याः सर्वमर्माणि सुमन्त्रः प्रत्यभाषत॥ ४॥
verses.m: Beating his head all of a sudden and sighing again and again, pressing his hand against the other and grinding his teeth, turning his eyes crimson with wrath, shedding his former (normal) colour, overwhelmed as he was with anger, and, suddenly falling a prey to bitter agony, nay, carefully reading the mind of Daśaratha, Sumantra spoke as follows, shaking Kaikeyī’s heart, as it were, with sharp arrows in the form of words and as though piercing all her vitals with his acrimonious words resembling so many peerless thunderbolts : (1—4)

verses.text:
यस्यास्तव पतिस्त्यक्तो राजा दशरथः स्वयम्।
भर्ता सर्वस्य जगतः स्थावरस्य चरस्य च॥ ५॥
नह्यकार्यतमं किंचित्तव देवीह विद्यते।
पतिघ्नीं त्वामहं मन्ये कुलघ्नीमपि चान्ततः॥ ६॥
यन्महेन्द्रमिवाजय्यं दुष्प्रकम्प्यमिवाचलम्।
महोदधिमिवाक्षोभ्यं संतापयसि कर्मभिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Surely there is nothing on earth most undesirable for you, by whom your husband, King Daśaratha himself, the supporter of the entire creation, both immobile and mobile, stands betrayed, O queen ! I consider you to be the murderess of your husband and ultimately the exterminator of your race too, in that you torment with your actions your husband, who is invincible as the great Indra, unshakable as a mountain and imperturbable as an ocean. (5—7).

verses.text:
मावमंस्था दशरथं भर्तारं वरदं पतिम्।
भर्तुरिच्छा हि नारीणां पुत्रकोट्या विशिष्यते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Do not despise Daśaratha, your husband and lord, the bestower of boons, as the will of a husband is superior to that of ten millions of sons. (8)

verses.text:
यथावयो हि राज्यानि प्राप्नुवन्ति नृपक्षये।
इक्ष्वाकुकुलनाथेऽस्मिंस्तं लोपयितुमिच्छसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Indeed, on the death of a king his sons inherit the sovereign rights according to seniority of age. You seek to violate this time-honoured practice even in the presence (life-time) of this ruler of the Ikṣwākus ! (9)

verses.text:
राजा भवतु ते पुत्रो भरतः शास्तु मेदिनीम्।
वयं तत्र गमिष्यामो यत्र रामो गमिष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Let your son, Bharata, be crowned king and rule over the earth. We, for our part, shall go wheresoever Rāma goes. (10)

verses.text:
न च ते विषये कश्चिद् ब्राह्मणो वस्तुमर्हति।
तादृशं त्वममर्यादमद्य कर्म करिष्यसि॥ ११॥
नूनं सर्वे गमिष्यामो मार्गं रामनिषेवितम्।
त्यक्ता या बान्धवैः सर्वैर्ब्राह्मणैः साधुभिः सदा॥ १२॥
का प्रीती राज्यलाभेन तव देवि भविष्यति।
तादृशं त्वममर्यादं कर्म कर्तुं चिकीर्षसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nor should any Brāhmaṇa dwell in your kingdom. If you perpetrate today such an act of impropriety (as you are intent on perpetrating), we shall all positively follow the path resorted to by Śrī Rāma. What joy, O royal lady, will be derived through attainment of sovereignty by you, who will thus be deserted for good by all your kith and kin, Brāhmaṇas and other pious souls? You seek to perpetrate such an act of impropriety. (11—13)

verses.text:
आश्चर्यमिव पश्यामि यस्यास्ते वृत्तमीदृशम्।
आचरन्त्या न विवृता सद्यो भवति मेदिनी॥ १४॥
महाब्रह्मर्षिसृष्टा वा ज्वलन्तो भीमदर्शनाः।
धिग्वाग्दण्डा न हिंसन्ति रामप्रव्राजने स्थिताम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I reckon it a wonder that the earth is not immediately rent asunder as a sequel to your resorting to such improper conduct. Nor do rods of punishment in the form of fiery and obviously fearful reproach uttered by great Brāhmaṇa sages (Vasiṣṭha and others) kill you, who are bent on exiling Śrī Rāma! (14-15)

verses.text:
आम्रं छित्त्वा कुठारेण निम्बं परिचरेत् तु कः।
यश्चैनं पयसा सिञ्चेन्नैवास्य मधुरो भवेत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Who on earth will nurture a Neem tree (with its proverbially bitter leaves and fruits etc.,) felling down a mango tree with an axe? And a Neem tree will not turn sweet for him who nourishes it with milk. (16)

verses.text:
आभिजात्यं हि ते मन्ये यथा मातुस्तथैव च।
न हि निम्बात् स्रवेत् क्षौद्रं लोके निगदितं वचः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Indeed, I account your innate disposition to be exactly similar to that of your mother. The proverb is often quoted in the world that surely honey does not flow from a Neem tree. (17)

verses.text:
तव मातुरसद्ग्राहं विद्म पूर्वं यथा श्रुतम्।
पितुस्ते वरदः कश्चिद् ददौ वरमनुत्तमम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “We know, as heard of in the past, the intentness of your mother on evil. Someone capable of granting boons bestowed a most excellent boon on your father. (18)

verses.text:
सर्वभूतरुतं तस्मात् संजज्ञे वसुधाधिपः।
तेन तिर्यग्गतानां च भूतानां विदितं वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “By virtue of it the king, your father, could understand the language of all created beings. The talk of those belonging to the sub-human species was thereby understood by him. (19)

verses.text:
ततो जृम्भस्य शयने विरुताद् भूरिवर्चसः।
पितुस्ते विदितो भावः स तत्र बहुधाहसत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “From the shrill cry of a bird heard by him while in his bed the meaning of it was accordingly deciphered by your exceedingly glorious father and he laughed over it repeatedly. (20)

verses.text:
तत्र ते जननी क्रुद्धा मृत्युपाशमभीप्सती।
हासं ते नृपते सौम्य जिज्ञासामीति चाब्रवीत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Your mother grew indignant at this and, seeking even to hang him in case he refused to disclose the reason of his laughter, spoke as follows : ‘I wish to know the meaning of your laughter, O gentle monarch ! (21)

verses.text:
नृपश्चोवाच तां देवीं हासं शंसामि ते यदि।
ततो मे मरणं सद्यो भविष्यति न संशयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The King too replied to that royal lady, ‘If I tell you the reason of my laughter, my death will speedily follow from it: there is no doubt about it.’ (22)

verses.text:
माता ते पितरं देवि पुनः केकयमब्रवीत्।
शंस मे जीव वा मा वा न मां त्वं प्रहसिष्यसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Your mother then said to your father, the ruler of the Kekayas, ‘Live or die as you will; in any case tell me the reason of your laughter. Then alone shall I be satisfied that you shall not laugh at me hereafter.’ (23)

verses.text:
प्रियया च तथोक्तः स केकयः पृथिवीपतिः।
तस्मै तं वरदायार्थं कथयामास तत्त्वतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Told thus by his beloved consort, the said king of the Kekayas for his part correctly reported the matter to the sage who had bestowed the boon on him. (24)

verses.text:
ततः स वरदः साधू राजानं प्रत्यभाषत।
म्रियतां ध्वंसतां वेयं मा शंसीस्त्वं महीपते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Thereupon the holy man who had bestowed the boon on him replied to the king, ‘Let her die or depart (from your house for her parents’ home); reveal you not the secret to her, O ruler of the earth !’ (25)

verses.text:
स तच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य प्रसन्नमनसो नृपः।
मातरं ते निरस्याशु विजहार कुबेरवत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid reply of the holy man, who was pleased at heart with him, and speedily repudiating your mother, the said king (your father) lived happily like Kubera (the god of riches). (26)

verses.text:
तथा त्वमपि राजानं दुर्जनाचरिते पथि।
असद्ग्राहमिमं मोहात् कुरुषे पापदर्शिनी॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Treading on the path trodden by wicked men and seeing evil everywhere, you too likewise are urging this Emperor through infatuation to adopt an evil course. (27)

verses.text:
सत्यश्चात्र प्रवादोऽयं लौकिकः प्रतिभाति मा।
पितॄन् समनुजायन्ते नरा मातरमङ्गनाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Nay, the popular saying on this subject that males take after their father and females after their mother appears to me as true. (28)

verses.text:
नैवं भव गृहाणेदं यदाह वसुधाधिपः।
भर्तुरिच्छामुपास्वेह जनस्यास्य गतिर्भव॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Do not follow the ways of your mother, and accept that which the Emperor enjoins on you. Following the will of your husband, be a protectress to these people here. (29)

verses.text:
मा त्वं प्रोत्साहिता पापैर्देवराजसमप्रभम्।
भर्तारं लोकभर्तारमसद्धर्ममुपादध॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Do not, as incited by the wicked, constrain your husband—who is, at the same time, the protector of the world and vies in splendour with Indra—to adopt an improper course of conduct. (30)

verses.text:
नहि मिथ्या प्रतिज्ञातं करिष्यति तवानघः।
श्रीमान् दशरथो राजा देवि राजीवलोचनः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The glorious and lotus-eyed King Daśaratha, who is free from sin, would not belie the promise made by him to you, O royal lady ! (31)

verses.text:
ज्येष्ठो वदान्यः कर्मण्यः स्वधर्मस्यापि रक्षिता।
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य बली रामोऽभिषिच्यताम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Let Rāma, the eldest of his sons—who is generous, strong and given to righteous acts and is capable not only of vindicating his own duty as a Kṣatriya but also of protecting the entire living creation, be installed on the throne of Ayodhyā. (32)

verses.text:
परिवादो हि ते देवि महाँल्लोके चरिष्यति।
यदि रामो वनं याति विहाय पितरं नृपम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “A great calumny will surely spread about you, O royal lady, if Rāma goes to the forest, leaving his royal father. (33)

verses.text:
स्वराज्यं राघवः पातु भव त्वं विगतज्वरा।
नहि ते राघवादन्यः क्षमः पुरवरे वसन्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Let Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, protect his own kingdom and be you free from anxiety. Ruling over Ayodhyā, the foremost of cities, no king other than Śrī Rāma will be favourably disposed to you. (34)

verses.text:
रामे हि यौवराज्यस्थे राजा दशरथो वनम्।
प्रवेक्ष्यति महेष्वासः पूर्ववृत्तमनुस्मरन्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Bearing in mind the conduct of his forbears, King Daśaratha, who wields a mighty bow, will surely retire to the forest in the event of Śrī Rāma being installed in the office of Prince Regent.” (35)

verses.text:
इति सान्त्वैश्च तीक्ष्णैश्च कैकेयीं राजसंसदि।
भूयः संक्षोभयामास सुमन्त्रस्तु कृताञ्जलिः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: In this way with folded hands Sumantra for his part violently shook Kaikeyī with pungent remarks as well as with kind words in the king’s court. (36)

verses.text:
नैव सा क्षुभ्यते देवी न च स्म परिदूयते।
न चास्या मुखवर्णस्य लक्ष्यते विक्रिया तदा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The said queen, however, was neither excited nor agonized nor was any change observed at that time in the colour of her face. (37)

verses.text:
ततः सुमन्त्रमैक्ष्वाकः पीडितोऽत्र प्रतिज्ञया।
सबाष्पमतिनिःश्वस्य जगादेदं पुनर्वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Sighing deeply with tears in his eyes, Daśaratha, a scion of Ikṣwāku, who was bound by the pledge given by him to Kaikeyī in the matter of sending Śrī Rāma into exile, then spoke to Sumantra again as follows : (1)

verses.text:
सूत रत्नसुसम्पूर्णा चतुर्विधबला चमूः।
राघवस्यानुयात्रार्थं क्षिप्रं प्रतिविधीयताम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Let a detachment consisting of all the four limbs of the army and richly provided with jewels be detailed at once to accompany Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O Sumantra ! (2)

verses.text:
रूपाजीवाश्च वादिन्यो वणिजश्च महाधनाः।
शोभयन्तु कुमारस्य वाहिनीः सुप्रसारिताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Nay, let courtesans adept in speaking, as well as merchants possessing enormous wealth and clever in efficiently spreading a network of shops dealing in provisions and other goods lend charm to the forces accompanying the prince. (3)

verses.text:
ये चैनमुपजीवन्ति रमते यैश्च वीर्यतः।
तेषां बहुविधं दत्त्वा तानप्यत्र नियोजय॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Further tell off in his service those wrestlers too who depend on him and in whom he takes delight by testing their comparative strength, bestowing various gifts on them. (4)

verses.text:
आयुधानि च मुख्यानि नागराः शकटानि च।
अनुगच्छन्तु काकुत्स्थं व्याधाश्चारण्यकोविदाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Let the principal weapons, courteous and well-bred men and bullock-carts too as well as hunters knowing the secrets of forests accompany Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha. (5)

verses.text:
निघ्नन् मृगान् कुञ्जरांश्च पिबंश्चारण्यकं मधु।
नदीश्च विविधाः पश्यन् न राज्यं संस्मरिष्यति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Killing the deer and elephants and drinking wild honey and seeing various rivers he would not miss his sovereignty. (6)

verses.text:
धान्यकोशश्च यः कश्चिद् धनकोशश्च मामकः।
तौ राममनुगच्छेतां वसन्तं निर्जने वने॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Let that which constitutes my granary and that which comprises my exchequer both accompany Rāma going to dwell in an uninhabited forest. (7)

verses.text:
यजन् पुण्येषु देशेषु विसृजंश्चाप्तदक्षिणाः।
ऋषिभिश्चापि संगम्य प्रवत्स्यति सुखं वने॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Performing sacrifices in holy regions and bestowing adequate gifts on the officiating priests and meeting sages too he will live away happily in the forest. (8)

verses.text:
भरतश्च महाबाहुरयोध्यां पालयिष्यति।
सर्वकामैः पुनः श्रीमान् रामः संसाध्यतामिति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “And the mighty-armed Bharata will rule over Ayodhyā. Let the glorious Rāma, therefore, be sent out with all objects of enjoyment.” (9)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कैकेय्या भयमागतम्।
मुखं चाप्यगमच्छोषं स्वरश्चापि व्यरुध्यत॥ १०॥
verses.m: While Daśaratha, a scion of Kakutstha, was speaking as aforesaid, fear seized Kaikeyī. Nay, her mouth too got parched and voice as well got choked. (10)

verses.text:
सा विषण्णा च संत्रस्ता मुखेन परिशुष्यता।
राजानमेवाभिमुखी कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Feeling dejected and dismayed, with her mouth getting parched, and her face turned exclusively towards the king, she replied as follows : (11)

verses.text:
राज्यं गतधनं साधो पीतमण्डां सुरामिव।
निरास्वाद्यतमं शून्यं भरतो नाभिपत्स्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Bharata will not accept a kingdom that has been stripped of its wealth and resembles wine divested of its spirituous part, and which is thus absolutely unenjoyable and unsubstantial, O pious soul !” (12)

verses.text:
कैकेय्यां मुक्तलज्जायां वदन्त्यामतिदारुणम्।
राजा दशरथो वाक्यमुवाचायतलोचनाम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: When Kaikeyī, who was thus shamelessly uttering most cruel words, King Daśaratha spoke as follows to that lady with large eyes : (13)

verses.text:
वहन्तं किं तुदसि मां नियुज्य धुरि माहिते।
अनार्ये कृत्यमारब्धं किं न पूर्वमुपारुधः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Having charged me with a burden (viz., that of sending Rāma into exile, which is so hard to bear), O hostile and vulgar woman, why do you lash me while I am carrying it? Why did you not check before (while asking the two boons, by laying down that Rāma should not be allowed to take anything with him) the proceedings now taken in hand of sending troops etc., with Rāma?” (14)

verses.text:
तस्यैतत् क्रोधसंयुक्तमुक्तं श्रुत्वा वराङ्गना।
कैकेयी द्विगुणं क्रुद्धा राजानमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Doubly incensed to hear the angry words of Daśaratha, Kaikeyī, the lovely women, replied to the king as follows : (15)

verses.text:
तवैव वंशे सगरो ज्येष्ठपुत्रमुपारुधत्।
असमञ्ज इति ख्यातं तथायं गन्तुमर्हति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “In your very dynasty Emperor Sagara cast away his eldest son known by the name of Asamañja. Rāma too should depart likewise without anything to depend upon.” (16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो धिगित्येव राजा दशरथोऽब्रवीत्।
व्रीडितश्च जनः सर्वः सा च तन्नावबुध्यत॥ १७॥
verses.m: Spoken to as above, King Daśaratha simply said, “Shame !” Everyone present there too felt ashamed. She, however, did not mind it. (17)

verses.text:
तत्र वृद्धो महामात्रः सिद्धार्थो नाम नामतः।
शुचिर्बहुमतो राज्ञः कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: On that occasion the aged and upright chief minister, Siddhārtha by name, who was highly esteemed by the king, spoke to Kaikeyī as follows: so the tradition goes : (18)

verses.text:
असमञ्जो गृहीत्वा तु क्रीडतः पथि दारकान्।
सरय्वां प्रक्षिपन्नप्सु रमते तेन दुर्मतिः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Catching hold of children playing in the street, Asamañja just used to throw them in the waters of the Sarayū and the evil-minded fellow took delight in it. (19)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा नागराः सर्वे क्रुद्धा राजानमब्रुवन्।
असमञ्जं वृणीष्वैकमस्मान् वा राष्ट्रवर्धन॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Enraged to see that murderous prank of the Crown prince, all the citizens submitted to the king, ‘Keep to yourself Asamañja alone allowing us to leave the city or preserve us, sending away the prince, O promoter of the State ! (20)

verses.text:
तानुवाच ततो राजा किंनिमित्तमिदं भयम्।
ताश्चापि राज्ञा सम्पृष्टा वाक्यं प्रकृतयोऽब्रुवन्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Thereupon the king said to them, ‘What is the occasion for this fear?’ Duly interrorgated by the king, those people too replied to the king. (21)

verses.text:
क्रीडतस्त्वेष नः पुत्रान् बालानुद्भ्रान्तचेतसः।
सरय्वां प्रक्षिपन्मौर्ख्यादतुलां प्रीतिमश्नुते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘He experiences incomparable joy while throwing through folly in the Sarayū our juvenile sons playing in an excited state of mind !’ (22)

verses.text:
स तासां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रकृतीनां नराधिपः।
तं तत्याजाहितं पुत्रं तासां प्रियचिकीर्षया॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Hearing the complaint of those people, the said king abandoned his son, malevolent to his subjects, with intent to oblige them. (23)

verses.text:
तं यानं शीघ्रमारोप्य सभार्यं सपरिच्छदम्।
यावज्जीवं विवास्योऽयमिति तानन्वशात् पिता॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Quickly placing him alongwith his wife and accessories (viz., a spade, basket and so on, necessary adjuncts to a forest life), he instructed those in authority in the following words: ‘He should be exiled for life.’ (24)

verses.text:
स फालपिटकं गृह्य गिरिदुर्गाण्यलोकयत्।
दिशः सर्वास्त्वनुचरन् स यथा पापकर्मकृत्॥ २५॥
इत्येनमत्यजद् राजा सगरो वै सुधार्मिकः।
रामः किमकरोत् पापं येनैवमुपरुध्यते॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Taking a basket and a spade and roaming about in all directions in search of roots and fruits etc., he ransacked mountain passes in quest of an abode. The highly pious King Sagara obviously abandoned Asamañja on the plea of his perpetrating sinful deeds as mentioned above. What sin has Śrī Rāma committed, for which he is being debarred from the throne in this way? (25-26)

verses.text:
नहि कंचन पश्यामो राघवस्यागुणं वयम्।
दुर्लभो ह्यस्य निरयः शशाङ्कस्येव कल्मषम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Surely we do not detect any fault in Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. It is as difficult to find a taint in him as in the new moon.(27)

verses.text:
अथवा देवि त्वं कंचिद् दोषं पश्यसि राघवे।
तमद्य ब्रूहि तत्त्वेन तदा रामो विवास्यते॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Or, if you perceive any fault in Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O queen, please point it out correctly today. Then Śrī Rāma will be sent into exile. (28)

verses.text:
अदुष्टस्य हि संत्यागः सत्पथे निरतस्य च।
निर्दहेदपि शक्रस्य द्युतिं धर्मविरोधवान्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Indeed, it is repugnant to all canons of righteousness to abandon one who is not only not guilty but also devoted to the straight path. It would destroy the splendour even of Indra, the ruler of gods. (29)

verses.text:
तदलं देवि रामस्य श्रिया विहतया त्वया।
लोकतोऽपि हि ते रक्ष्यः परिवादः शुभानने॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O queen, it is no use your withholding the royal fortune of Śrī Rāma. Censure coming from the public too should be guarded against by you, O lady with a charming countenance !” (30)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु सिद्धार्थवचो राजा श्रान्ततरस्वरः।
शोकोपहतया वाचा कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Hearing the remonstrance of Siddhārtha, the king, for his part, whose voice had grown very feeble, spoke as follows to Kaikeyī in a tone overwhelmed with grief: (31)

verses.text:
एतद्वचो नेच्छसि पापरूपे
हितं न जानासि ममात्मनोऽथवा।
आस्थाय मार्गं कृपणं कुचेष्टा
चेष्टा हि ते साधुपथादपेता॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Do you not like this advice, O embodiment of sin? Having taken to a path leading to woe, are you not alive to my interests or your own? Indeed, your gesture is remote from the path of the righteous and as such an undesirable one. (32)

verses.text:
अनुव्रजिष्याम्यहमद्य रामं
राज्यं परित्यज्य सुखं धनं च।
सर्वे च राज्ञा भरतेन च त्वं
यथासुखं भुङ् क्ष्व चिराय राज्यम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Abandoning the kingly state, bodily comfort and wealth, I shall follow Rāma to the forest today as also all the people of Ayodhyā. Rule you the kingdom happily for long with Bharata.” (33)

verses.text:
महामात्रवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथं तदा।
अभ्यभाषत वाक्यं तु विनयज्ञो विनीतवत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the remonstrance of the chief minister, Śrī Rāma, for his part, who was an adept in courtesy, politely addressed on that occasion the following words to Daśaratha : (1)

verses.text:
त्यक्तभोगस्य मे राजन् वने वन्येन जीवतः।
किं कार्यमनुयात्रेण त्यक्तसङ्गस्य सर्वतः॥ २॥
verses.m: “What purpose of mine, who have renounced all enjoyment and shaken off attachment for everything and am going to live on the products of the forest alone, will be served, O king, with an army following me? (2)

verses.text:
यो हि दत्त्वा द्विपश्रेष्ठं कक्ष्यायां कुरुते मनः।
रज्जुस्नेहेन किं तस्य त्यजतः कुञ्जरोत्तमम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “He who, having parted with an excellent elephant, seeks to retain the tether is indeed a fool. What is to be gained through attachment to a tether by him who has forgone an excellent elephant? (3)

verses.text:
तथा मम सतां श्रेष्ठ किं ध्वजिन्या जगत्पते।
सर्वाण्येवानुजानामि चीराण्येवानयन्तु मे॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Similarly, O jewel among the virtuous, what purpose of mine will be served with an army, O ruler of the world? I, therefore, allow all things to be used by Bharata. Let the servant-maids of mother Kaikeyī bring me robes fit for a dweller in forests alone.” (4)

verses.text:
खनित्रपिटके चोभे समानयत गच्छत।
चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वसतो मम॥ ५॥
verses.m: Addressing the maid-servants, he continues: “go and duly bring a spade and a basket both for me, who am going to take up my abode in a forest for fourteen years.”(5)

verses.text:
अथ चीराणि कैकेयी स्वयमाहृत्य राघवम्।
उवाच परिधत्स्वेति जनौघे निरपत्रपा॥ ६॥
verses.m: Personally bringing pieces of bark for being put on by Śrī Rāma and others, Kaikeyī, who was lost to all shame, forthwith said to Śrī Rāma in the midst of that concourse of men, “Put these on !” (6)

verses.text:
स चीरे पुरुषव्याघ्रः कैकेय्याः प्रतिगृह्य ते।
सूक्ष्मवस्त्रमवक्षिप्य मुनिवस्त्राण्यवस्त ह॥ ७॥
verses.m: Receiving from Kaikeyī two pieces of bark for being used as a loin-cloth and a cover respectively and discarding his raiment of fine yarn, that tiger among men put on the garb of ascetics: so the tradition goes. (7)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि तत्रैव विहाय वसने शुभे।
तापसाच्छादने चैव जग्राह पितुरग्रतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Nay, leaving his exquisite robes on that very spot, Lakṣmaṇa too put on in the presence of his father two pieces of bark fit for ascetics. (8)

verses.text:
अथात्मपरिधानार्थं सीता कौशेयवासिनी।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य चीरं संत्रस्ता पृषती वागुरामिव॥ ९॥
verses.m: Gazing with reverence on the piece of bark intended for being donned by her, Sītā, who was clad in silken robes, felt dismayed as a doe would on seeing a snare set for entrapping it. (9)

verses.text:
सा व्यपत्रपमाणेव प्रगृह्य च सुदुर्मनाः।
कैकेय्याः कुशचीरे ते जानकी शुभलक्षणा॥ १०॥
अश्रुसम्पूर्णनेत्रा च धर्मज्ञा धर्मदर्शिनी।
गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमं भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Feeling much abashed, as it were, while taking from the hand of Kaikeyī the two articles of wearing apparel made of Kuśa grass and greatly troubled in mind, Sītā (daughter of Janaka), who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks, knew what is right and served as an illustration of virtue, spoke as follows, her eyes overflowing with tears, to her husband, who vied with Citraratha, the ruler of the Gandharvas : (10-11)

verses.text:
कथं नु चीरं बध्नन्ति मुनयो वनवासिनः।
इति ह्यकुशला सीता सा मुमोह मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I wonder how ascetics dwelling in forests put on the bark of trees.” Saying so, the celebrated Sītā, who was in no way adept in wearing the bark of trees, erred again and again in her attempt to do so. (12)

verses.text:
कृत्वा कण्ठे स्म सा चीरमेकमादाय पाणिना।
तस्थौ ह्यकुशला तत्र व्रीडिता जनकात्मजा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Placing one piece about her neck and taking another in her hand, the said daughter of Janaka stood abashed, inapt as she was in wearing the bark. (13)

verses.text:
तस्यास्तत् क्षिप्रमागत्य रामो धर्मभृतां वरः।
चीरं बबन्ध सीतायाः कौशेयस्योपरि स्वयम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Quickly going near her, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those upholding the cause of virtue, then personally fastened the bark over her silken garment. (14)

verses.text:
रामं प्रेक्ष्य तु सीताया बध्नन्तं चीरमुत्तमम्।
अन्तःपुरचरा नार्यो मुमुचुर्वारि नेत्रजम्॥ १५॥
ऊचुश्च परमायत्ता रामं ज्वलिततेजसम्।
वत्स नैवं नियुक्तेयं वनवासे मनस्विनी॥ १६॥
verses.m: Perceiving Śrī Rāma fastening the excellent bark about Sītā, the female inmates of the gynaeceum began to shed tears and, sore distressed as they were, spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma of dazzling glory : “This high-minded princess has not been so commanded to reside in the forest (as you), dear child ! (15-16)

verses.text:
पितुर्वाक्यानुरोधेन गतस्य विजनं वनम्।
तावद् दर्शनमस्या नः सफलं भवतु प्रभो॥ १७॥
verses.m: “At least let her blessed sight continue to bring its reward to us during the interim period when you have departed to the lonely forest in obedience to your father’s command, O lord ! (17)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणेन सहायेन वनं गच्छस्व पुत्रक।
नेयमर्हति कल्याणि वस्तुं तापसवद् वने॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Proceed to the forest, dear son, with Lakṣmaṇa alone as your companion. This blessed princess does not deserve to dwell in the forest like an ascetic. (18)

verses.text:
कुरु नो याचनां पुत्र सीता तिष्ठतु भामिनी।
धर्मनित्यः स्वयं स्थातुं न हीदानीं त्वमिच्छसि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Grant our solicitation, O darling ! Let Sītā, the pretty young lady, continue to stay in Ayodhyā though surely you are not personally inclined to stay any longer, righteousness being your eternal companion.” (19)

verses.text:
तासामेवंविधा वाचः शृण्वन् दशरथात्मजः।
बबन्धैव तथा चीरं सीतया तुल्यशीलया॥ २०॥
verses.m: Even though hearing such loving remonstrances of those women, Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, persisted in fastening the bark over her silken garment as aforesaid (vide verse 14) as desired by Sītā, whose conduct came into line with his own. (20)

verses.text:
चीरे गृहीते तु तया सबाष्पो नृपतेर्गुरुः।
निवार्य सीतां कैकेयीं वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Stopping Sītā when the bark was taken by her (from the hands of Kaikeyī), Sage Vasiṣṭha, the king’s preceptor, for his part, spoke to Kaikeyī with tears in his eyes, as follows : (21)

verses.text:
अतिप्रवृत्ते दुर्मेधे कैकेयि कुलपांसनि।
वञ्चयित्वा तु राजानं न प्रमाणेऽवतिष्ठसि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having hoodwinked the king, O evil-minded Kaikeyī, who have exceeded your limits and brought disgrace to your family, you do not keep within bounds yet ! (22)

verses.text:
न गन्तव्यं वनं देव्या सीतया शीलवर्जिते।
अनुष्ठास्यति रामस्य सीता प्रकृतमासनम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “O woman, dead to all decorum, Princess Sītā shall not proceed to the forest. She will occupy the throne which was offered to Rāma. (23)

verses.text:
आत्मा हि दाराः सर्वेषां दारसंग्रहवर्तिनाम्।
आत्मेयमिति रामस्य पालयिष्यति मेदिनीम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “A wife is the very self to all householders. As the other self of Rāma, she will rule over the globe. (24)

verses.text:
अथ यास्यति वैदेही वनं रामेण संगता।
वयमत्रानुयास्यामः पुरं चेदं गमिष्यति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “If Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, retires to the forest alongwith Rāma, we, who are present here at this moment, shall follow suit and the people of this city too will go. (25)

verses.text:
अन्तपालाश्च यास्यन्ति सदारो यत्र राघवः।
सहोपजीव्यं राष्ट्रं च पुरं च सपरिच्छदम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “The soldiers guarding the gynaeceum too will go where Rāma, a scion of Raghu, stays with his wife. Nay, the entire state of Kosala including all its resources as well as the city of Ayodhyā with its goods and chattels will also go. (26)

verses.text:
भरतश्च सशत्रुघ्नश्चीरवासा वनेचरः।
वने वसन्तं काकुत्स्थमनुवत्स्यति पूर्वजम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Clad in the bark of trees and dwelling in a forest, Bharata too with Śatrughna will adopt the mode of life of his elder brother, Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, living in the forest. (27)

verses.text:
ततः शून्यां गतजनां वसुधां पादपैः सह।
त्वमेका शाधि दुर्वृत्ता प्रजानामहिते स्थिता॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Rule you alone after that the desolate earth, deserted by men, with its trees because it will be reduced to a mere forest, vile as you are and bent upon doing harm to the people. (28)

verses.text:
न हि तद् भविता राष्ट्रं यत्र रामो न भूपतिः।
तद् वनं भविता राष्ट्रं यत्र रामो निवत्स्यति॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The state in which Rāma is no longer the king will not survive; while the forest which Rāma is going to inhabit is sure to develop into a flourishing state. (29)

verses.text:
न ह्यदत्तां महीं पित्रा भरतः शास्तुमिच्छति।
त्वयि वा पुत्रवद् वस्तुं यदि जातो महीपतेः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Bharata surely would not rule over the earth which has not been voluntarily alienated by his father, nor would he live with you as a son, if he is sprung from the loins of the Emperor. (30)

verses.text:
यद्यपि त्वं क्षितितलाद् गगनं चोत्पतिष्यसि।
पितृवंशचरित्रज्ञः सोऽन्यथा न करिष्यति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Even if you soar into the heavens leaving the earth’s surface, he would not do anything contrary to the established usage, knowing as he does the practice of his forbears. (31)

verses.text:
तत् त्वया पुत्रगर्धिन्या पुत्रस्य कृतमप्रियम्।
लोके नहि स विद्येत यो न राममनुव्रतः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Therefore an unfriendly act alone has been done by you to your son, even though you covet his well-being; for there is none in the world who is not devoted to Rāma. (32)

verses.text:
द्रक्ष्यस्यद्यैव कैकेयि पशुव्यालमृगद्विजान्।
गच्छतः सह रामेण पादपांश्च तदुन्मुखान्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “O Kaikeyī, you will see this very day beasts, snakes, deer and birds going with Rāma to the forest and trees too eager to accompany him. (33)

verses.text:
अथोत्तमान्याभरणानि देवि
देहि स्नुषायै व्यपनीय चीरम्।
न चीरमस्याः प्रविधीयतेति
न्यवारयत् तद् वसनं वसिष्ठः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, laying aside the bark of trees, give your daughter-in-law excellent jewels, O queen ! The bark of trees is not meant for her.” Saying so, Vasiṣṭha forbade Sītā wearing it. (34)

verses.text:
एकस्य रामस्य वने निवास-
स्त्वया वृतः केकयराजपुत्रि।
विभूषितेयं प्रतिकर्मनित्या
वसत्वरण्ये सह राघवेण॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The sage continued, “The sojourn in the forest of Rāma alone has been asked for by you, O princess of the Kekaya territory ! Hence let Sītā, who deserves to be decorated daily, dwell in the forest with Rāma, a scion of Raghu, richly adorned. (35)

verses.text:
यानैश्च मुख्यैः परिचारकैश्च
सुसंवृता गच्छतु राजपुत्री।
वस्त्रैश्च सर्वैः सहितैर्विधानै-
र्नेयं वृता ते वरसम्प्रदाने॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Nay, let the princess proceed fully provided with excellent conveyances and attendants as well as with costumes of various kinds and all useful accessories; for, while asking for the boons her exile was not solicited by you.” (36)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तथा जल्पति विप्रमुख्ये
गुरौ नृपस्याप्रतिमप्रभावे।
नैव स्म सीता विनिवृत्तभावा
प्रियस्य भर्तुः प्रतिकारकामा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Even though the said preceptor of the king, the foremost among the Brāhmaṇas, who wielded an influence which had no parallel, spoke as above, Sītā, who wished to follow the ways of her husband, did not desist from her purpose in the least. (37)

verses.text:
तस्यां चीरं वसानायां नाथवत्यामनाथवत्।
प्रचुक्रोश जनः सर्वो धिक् त्वां दशरथं त्विति॥ १॥
verses.m: On Sītā wearing the bark of trees like a helpless woman though protected by her husband, all the people present there loudly exclaimed, “Fie upon you, (the powerless) Daśaratha, who does not stop this flagrant injustice !” (1)

verses.text:
तेन तत्र प्रणादेन दुःखितः स महीपतिः।
चिच्छेद जीविते श्रद्धां धर्मे यशसि चात्मनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Pained to hear that loud cry, the said Emperor lost all his interest in life, religious merit and renown. (2)

verses.text:
स निःश्वस्योष्णमैक्ष्वाकस्तां भार्यामिदमब्रवीत्।
कैकेयि कुशचीरेण न सीता गन्तुमर्हति॥ ३॥
verses.m: Heaving a sigh of grief, that scion of Ikṣwāku spoke to his wife, Kaikeyī, as follows: “Sītā surely does not deserve to depart in a robe made of Kuśa grass, O Kaikeyī! (3)

verses.text:
सुकुमारी च बाला च सततं च सुखोचिता।
नेयं वनस्य योग्येति सत्यमाह गुरुर्मम॥ ४॥
verses.m: “My preceptor, Vasiṣṭha, truly says that delicate of body, young and ever used to amenities of life, as she is, she is not fit for residence in a forest. (4)

verses.text:
इयं हि कस्यापि करोति किंचित्
तपस्विनी राजवरस्य पुत्री।
या चीरमासाद्य जनस्य मध्ये
स्थिता विसंज्ञा श्रमणीव काचित्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Has this innocent daughter of Janaka, a jewel among kings, really done any injury to anyone whosoever, that having received a robe of bark she stands dumbfounded like an ordinary hermitess in the midst of men? (5)

verses.text:
चीराण्यपास्याज्जनकस्य कन्या
नेयं प्रतिज्ञा मम दत्तपूर्वा।
यथासुखं गच्छतु राजपुत्री
वनं समग्रा सह सर्वरत्नैः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, shed her robes of bark. No such pledge that she would accompany her husband in robes of bark was given by me in the past. Let the princess, therefore, proceed at pleasure to the forest fully equipped with clothes and ornaments and provided with all valuable possessions. (6)

verses.text:
अजीवनार्हेण मया नृशंसा
कृता प्रतिज्ञा नियमेन तावत्।
त्वया हि बाल्यात् प्रतिपन्नमेतत्
तन्मा दहेद् वेणुमिवात्मपुष्पम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “In the first place a cruel promise was made on oath by me, who no longer deserve to survive; on top of it, this unjust act of providing the robes of a hermitess to Sītā has been initiated by you through sheer childishness. That is sure to consume me even as the blossoming of a bamboo brings about its own destruction. (7)

verses.text:
रामेण यदि ते पापे किंचित्कृतमशोभनम्।
अपकारः क इह ते वैदेह्या दर्शितोऽधमे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Even supposing some offence was given to you by Rāma, what wrong on earth was done to you by Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, O vile woman? (8)

verses.text:
मृगीवोत्फुल्लनयना मृदुशीला मनस्विनी।
अपकारं कमिव ते करोति जनकात्मजा॥ ९॥
verses.m: “What injury on earth could the lofty-minded Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, do to you—Sītā, who is distinguished by a pair of blooming eyes like a female gazelle and is possessed of a mild disposition? (9)

verses.text:
ननु पर्याप्तमेवं ते पापे रामविवासनम्।
किमेभिः कृपणैर्भूयः पातकैरपि ते कृतैः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, sending Rāma into exile in the robes of a hermit, as you are doing, O sinful woman, is enough for you. What more do you seek to gain through these further sins in the shape of exiling Sītā and that too in the robes of a hermitess which are going to be perpetrated by you and which are calculated to land you in untold suffering? (10)

verses.text:
प्रतिज्ञातं मया तावत् त्वयोक्तं देवि शृण्वता।
रामं यदभिषेकाय त्वमिहागतमब्रवीः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Hearing your command,* which you gave to Rāma, who called here (the other day) in connection with his installation as Prince Regent, O queen, that much was silently acquiesced in by me. (11)

verses.text:
तत्त्वेतत् समतिक्रम्य निरयं गन्तुमिच्छसि।
मैथिलीमपि या हि त्वमीक्षसे चीरवासिनीम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Distinctly going beyond that, however, as you are doing now, you seek to go to hell in that you would have Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, too, clad in the bark of trees.”(12)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवन्तं पितरं रामः सम्प्रस्थितो वनम्।
अवाक्शिरसमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: To his father, who sat with his head bent low, while speaking as aforesaid, Śrī Rāma, who was now actually on his way to the forest, submitted as follows : (13)

verses.text:
इयं धार्मिक कौसल्या मम माता यशस्विनी।
वृद्धा चाक्षुद्रशीला च न च त्वां देव गर्हते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “This illustrious mother of mine, Kausalyā, has not only grown old, but is of a generous disposition too and never speaks ill of you, O pious monarch ! (14)

verses.text:
मया विहीनां वरद प्रपन्नां शोकसागरम्।
अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसनां भूयः सम्मन्तुमर्हसि॥ १५॥
पुत्रशोकं यथा नर्च्छेत् त्वया पूज्येन पूजिता।
मां हि संचिन्तयन्ती सा त्वयि जीवेत् तपस्विनी॥ १६॥
