verses.m: “When she is bereft of me and consequently drowned in a sea of grief, although she has known no suffering before, O bestower of boons, you ought to show greater regard to her, so that the poor lady may not fall a prey to grief caused by separation from me (her son) and treated with respect by you, who are worthy of adoration to her, and contemplating on me, may survive under your care. (15-16)

verses.text:
इमां महेन्द्रोपम जातगर्धिनीं
तथा विधातुं जननीं ममार्हसि।
यथा वनस्थे मयि शोककर्शिता
न जीवितं न्यस्य यमक्षयं व्रजेत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Kindly handle my mother, who is sure to pine for me (her son), in such a way, O compeer of the mighty Indra, the lord of paradise, as to ensure that, stricken with grief, when I am sojourning in the forest, she may not depart to the abode of Yama, the god of death, giving up the ghost.” (17)

verses.text:
रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा मुनिवेषधरं च तम्।
समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगतचेतनः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the intercession of Śrī Rāma and perceiving him clad in the garb of a hermit, the king for his part with his consorts fell unconscious. (1)

verses.text:
नैनं दुःखेन संतप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत राघवम्।
न चैनमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रत्यभाषत दुर्मनाः॥ २॥
verses.m: Sore stricken with agony he could neither regale his eyes on Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) nor could he accost him even on casting a look at him awhile, disconsolate as he was. (2)

verses.text:
स मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञो दुःखितश्च महीपतिः।
विललाप महाबाहू राममेवानुचिन्तयन्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Remaining senseless, as it were, for an hour or so and feeling distressed, the mighty-armed monarch repented in various ways, thinking all the time of Śrī Rāma alone: (3)

verses.text:
मन्ये खलु मया पूर्वं विवत्सा बहवः कृताः।
प्राणिनो हिंसिता वापि तन्मामिदमुपस्थितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I think in my past life many a cow indeed was robbed of its calf or in any case many living beings were destroyed by me. Hence this calamity has befallen me. (4)

verses.text:
न त्वेवानागते काले देहाच्च्यवति जीवितम्।
कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानस्य मृत्युर्मम न विद्यते॥ ५॥
योऽहं पावकसंकाशं पश्यामि पुरतः स्थितम्।
विहाय वसने सूक्ष्मे तापसाच्छादमात्मजम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Surely life does not depart from the body until the appointed hour has arrived. It is, therefore, that death does not claim me even though I am being tormented by Kaikeyī and even though I behold my son, effulgent as fire, standing before me clad in the robes of an ascetic, having shed garments of fine fabric. (5-6)

verses.text:
एकस्याः खलु कैकेय्याः कृतेऽयं खिद्यते जनः।
स्वार्थे प्रयतमानायाः संश्रित्य निकृतिं त्विमाम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Indeed all these people have to suffer on account of Kaikeyī alone, who, having resorted to this roguery, is striving hard to gain her object.” (7)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं बाष्पेण विहतेन्द्रियः।
रामेति सकृदेवोक्त्वा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक सः॥ ८॥
संज्ञां तु प्रतिलभ्यैव मुहूर्तात् स महीपतिः।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having uttered these words and saying “O Rāma !” only once, the Emperor, however, whose vocal organs had been choked by tears, could not speak any more. Just regaining his consciousness after an hour or so, the said Emperor for his part spoke to Sumantra with his eyes flooded with tears as follows : (8-9)

verses.text:
औपवाह्यं रथं युक्त्वा त्वमायाहि हयोत्तमैः।
प्रापयैनं महाभागमितो जनपदात् परम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Fitting with the best of horses a chariot used for pleasure-drives, return you soon and take this highly blessed prince beyond this territory. (10)

verses.text:
एवं मन्ये गुणवतां गुणानां फलमुच्यते।
पित्रा मात्रा च यत्साधुर्वीरो निर्वास्यते वनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Since a pious and valiant son is being exiled to the forest by his very father and mother, such I believe is declared (by the scriptures) to be the reward of virtues of the virtuous.” (11)

verses.text:
राज्ञो वचनमाज्ञाय सुमन्त्रः शीघ्रविक्रमः।
योजयित्वा ययौ तत्र रथमश्वैरलंकृतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Bowing to the king’s command and fitting with horses a chariot decked with ornaments, Sumantra, who was swift of pace, returned quickly to that very spot where Śrī Rāma stood ready with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa to depart for the forest. (12)

verses.text:
तं रथं राजपुत्राय सूतः कनकभूषितम्।
आचचक्षेऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Joining his palms as a token of submission, the charioteer announced to the Crown prince, Śrī Rāma, the arrival of the chariot, decked with gold and fitted with excellent horses. (13)

verses.text:
राजा सत्वरमाहूय व्यापृतं वित्तसंचये।
उवाच देशकालज्ञो निश्चितं सर्वतः शुचिः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Promptly summoning to his presence the officer placed in charge of the treasury, the king, who knew what should be done at a particular place and time and was free from all impurities in the shape of duplicity etc., spoke in a decisive tone as follows : (14)

verses.text:
वासांसि च वरार्हाणि भूषणानि महान्ति च।
वर्षाण्येतानि संख्याय वैदेह्याः क्षिप्रमानय॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Taking into consideration all the years that Sītā has to spend in exile, pray, speedily bring for Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, costly robes and valuable ornaments.” (15)

verses.text:
नरेन्द्रेणैवमुक्तस्तु गत्वा कोशगृहं ततः।
प्रायच्छत् सर्वमाहृत्य सीतायै क्षिप्रमेव तत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Proceeding to the treasury when commanded thus by the king, and bringing everything that he was instructed to fetch, the officer for his part immediately delivered the whole lot to Sītā. (16)

verses.text:
सा सुजाता सुजातानि वैदेही प्रस्थिता वनम्।
भूषयामास गात्राणि तैर्विचित्रैर्विभूषणैः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Bound as she was for the forest, Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, of noble (uncommon) birth (in that she was not born of a womb), adorned her limbs, which were endowed with propitious marks, with those marvellous jewels. (17)

verses.text:
व्यराजयत वैदेही वेश्म तत् सुविभूषिता।
उद्यतोंऽशुमतः काले खं प्रभेव विवस्वतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Splendidly and profusely decked with ornaments, Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, illumined that palace (where she stood) in the same way as the radiance of the rising sun with its bright rays illumines the sky in the morning, particularly when there is no mist or cloud. (18)

verses.text:
तां भुजाभ्यां परिष्वज्य श्वश्रूर्वचनमब्रवीत्।
अनाचरन्तीं कृपणं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय मैथिलीम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Folding in her arms that princess of Mithilā, who never behaved in an unseemly way, and smelling her head as a token of affection, her mother-in-law, Kausalyā, spoke in the following words : (19)

verses.text:
असत्यः सर्वलोकेऽस्मिन् सततं सत्कृताः प्रियैः।
भर्तारं नानुमन्यन्ते विनिपातगतं स्त्रियः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Women who, though constantly adored by their beloved consorts, cease to esteem their husband, who has fallen on evil days, are dubbed as wicked throughout this world. (20)

verses.text:
एष स्वभावो नारीणामनुभूय पुरा सुखम्।
अल्पामप्यापदं प्राप्य दुष्यन्ति प्रजहत्यपि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Having enjoyed happiness in the past they malign and even desert their husband on meeting with the least misfortune : such is the nature of wicked women. (21)

verses.text:
असत्यशीला विकृता दुर्गा अहृदयाः सदा।
असत्यः पापसंकल्पाः क्षणमात्रविरागिणः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Wicked are those women who are ever untruthful by nature and swayed by passion, are difficult to comprehend, heartless and of sinful resolve and who get estranged in a moment. (22)

verses.text:
न कुलं न कृतं विद्या न दत्तं नापि संग्रहः।
स्त्रीणां गृह्णाति हृदयमनित्यहृदया हि ताः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Neither noble birth nor good turn, nor learning, nor gift nor even marriage ties capture the heart of such women, fickle of heart as they are. (23)

verses.text:
साध्वीनां तु स्थितानां तु शीले सत्ये श्रुते स्थिते।
स्त्रीणां पवित्रं परमं पतिरेको विशिष्यते॥ २४॥
verses.m: “In the case, however, of virtuous women, who are, in fact, devoted to good conduct, truthfulness and the precepts of their elders and keep within the bounds of decorum laid down for their family, their husband is the most sacred object and he alone excels all. (24)

verses.text:
स त्वया नावमन्तव्यः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो वनम्।
तव देवसमस्त्वेष निर्धनः सधनोऽपि वा॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Though being sent into exile to the forest, my son, Śrī Rāma, should not be despised by you. Endowed with means or resourceless, he is surely as good as a deity to you.” (25)

verses.text:
विज्ञाय वचनं सीता तस्या धर्मार्थसंहितम्।
कृत्वाञ्जलिमुवाचेदं श्वश्रूमभिमुखे स्थिता॥ २६॥
verses.m: Perceiving her advice to be in consonance with righteousness, which constituted her aim in life, and joining her palms, Sītā replied to her mother-in-law as follows, standing in front of her : (26)

verses.text:
करिष्ये सर्वमेवाहमार्या यदनुशास्ति माम्।
अभिज्ञास्मि यथा भर्तुर्वर्तितव्यं श्रुतं च मे॥ २७॥
verses.m: “I shall surely do all that your worthy self instructs me to do. I know how I should behave towards my husband and I have also heard about it from my elders. (27)

verses.text:
न मामसज्जनेनार्या समानयितुमर्हति।
धर्माद् विचलितुं नाहमलं चन्द्रादिव प्रभा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Your noble self ought not to equate me with wicked women. I am unable to deviate from virtue even as moonlight is incapable of parting from the moon. (28)

verses.text:
नातन्त्री वाद्यते वीणा नाचक्रो विद्यते रथः।
नापतिः सुखमेधेत या स्यादपि शतात्मजा॥ २९॥
verses.m: “A ‘Vina’ is of no use without chords and a chariot is of no use without wheels. Nor can a wife, who is bereft of her husband, prosper in a happy state even though she may have a hundred sons. (29)

verses.text:
मितं ददाति हि पिता मितं भ्राता मितं सुतः।
अमितस्य तु दातारं भर्तारं का न पूजयेत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a father bestows limited joy, a brother too bestows limited joy and a son as well bestows limited happiness. What woman, then, would not adore her husband, the bestower of unlimited joy? (30)

verses.text:
साहमेवंगता श्रेष्ठा श्रुतधर्मपरावरा।
आर्ये किमवमन्येयं स्त्रिया भर्ता हि दैवतम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having heard about the special and ordinary duties of a wife from my superiors and thus convinced that the husband is a veritable deity to a married woman, how can I, such as I am, despise my husband, O venerable lady?” (31)

verses.text:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा कौसल्या हृदयङ्गमम्।
शुद्धसत्त्वा मुमोचाश्रु सहसा दुःखहर्षजम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing Sītā’s reply, which touched the chords of her heart, Kausalyā of pure mind suddenly began to shed tears born of agony at the thought of the impending separation from her sons and daughter-in-law and delight over the pious sentiments expressed by Sītā. (32)

verses.text:
तां प्राञ्जलिरभिप्रेक्ष्य मातृमध्येऽतिसत्कृताम्।
रामः परमधर्मात्मा मातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Gazing at Kausalyā, his own mother, who was highly respected among his mothers, Śrī Rāma, who had a supremely pious mind, spoke to her with folded hands as follows : (33)”

verses.text:
अम्ब मा दुःखिता भूत्वा पश्येस्त्वं पितरं मम।
क्षयोऽपि वनवासस्य क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Pray, don’t you regard my father with a doleful countenance. The end of exile too will come rather soon. (34)

verses.text:
सुप्तायास्ते गमिष्यन्ति नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च।
समग्रमिह सम्प्राप्तं मां द्रक्ष्यसि सुहृद्वृतम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Nine years and five will slip past you even while you are asleep. One fine morning you will find me duly arrived back here in Ayodhyā in my entire being alongwith Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, surrounded by my friends and relations.” (35)

verses.text:
एतावदभिनीतार्थमुक्त्वा स जननीं वचः।
त्रयः शतशतार्धा हि ददर्शावेक्ष्य मातरः॥ ३६॥
ताश्चापि स तथैवार्ता मातॄर्दशरथात्मजः।
धर्मयुक्तमिदं वाक्यं निजगाद कृताञ्जलिः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Having made the aforesaid comprehensive submission to his mother, and gazing on his three hundred and fifty stepmothers, he actually found those mothers too distressed in the same way as his own mother was. Nay, folding his hands the said son of Daśaratha once more made the following submission, which was in consonance with the spirit of righteousness : (36-37)

verses.text:
संवासात् परुषं किंचिदज्ञानादपि यत् कृतम्।
तन्मे समुपजानीत सर्वाश्चामन्त्रयामि वः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Pray, forgive whatever unkind word or even act may have been uttered or done by me through ignorance because we lived together. Now I take leave of you all.” (38)

verses.text:
वचनं राघवस्यैतद् धर्मयुक्तं समाहितम्।
शुश्रुवुस्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः शोकोपहतचेतसः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: All those royal ladies whose mind was agitated through grief, heard the aforesaid cool submission of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, which conformed to the principles of righteousness. (39)

verses.text:
जज्ञेऽथ तासां संनादः क्रौञ्चीनामिव निःस्वनः।
मानवेन्द्रस्य भार्याणामेवं वदति राघवे॥ ४०॥
verses.m: While Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, was speaking thus, an outcry resembling the wail of female cranes rose from the mouth of those consorts of Daśaratha (a ruler of men). (40)

verses.text:
मुरजपणवमेघघोषवद्
दशरथवेश्म बभूव यत् पुरा।
विलपितपरिदेवनाकुलं
व्यसनगतं तदभूत् सुदुःखितम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: The same palace of Daśaratha, which was formerly marked with the sound of tomtoms, large drums and Meghas (a musical instrument the sound of which resembled the rumbling of clouds), was now filled with extreme agony, agitated as it was through wails and cries and fallen on evil days. (41)

verses.text:
अथ रामश्च सीता च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः।
उपसंगृह्य राजानं चक्रुर्दीनाः प्रदक्षिणम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Clasping the feet of and bowing to the king, Śrī Rāma and Sītā as well as Lakṣmaṇa, who felt miserable (because of their inability to be of any service to their aged parents) forthwith went round him clockwise with folded hands. (1)

verses.text:
तं चापि समनुज्ञाप्य धर्मज्ञः सह सीतया।
राघवः शोकसम्मूढो जननीमभ्यवादयत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Duly obtaining leave of him and accompanied by Sītā, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who knew what is right and stood through desolate grief of his mother, bowed to Kausalyā. (2)

verses.text:
अन्वक्षं लक्ष्मणो भ्रातुः कौसल्यामभ्यवादयत्।
अपि मातुः सुमित्राया जग्राह चरणौ पुनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Following at the heels of his brother, Lakṣmaṇa too greeted Kausalyā; then he clasped the feet of his own mother, Sumitrā. (3)

verses.text:
तं वन्दमानं रुदती माता सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।
हितकामा महाबाहुं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय लक्ष्मणम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Smelling as a token of affection the head of the mighty-armed Lakṣmaṇa, who was saluting her, the mother, who wished well of him, spoke weeping to that son of hers as follows : (4)

verses.text:
सृष्टस्त्वं वनवासाय स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज्जने।
रामे प्रमादं मा कार्षीः पुत्र भ्रातरि गच्छति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Excessively fond as you are of your kinsman, Rāma, you have been permitted by me to dwell in the forest with your eldest brother. But do not neglect, my son, the service of your brother, Rāma, who is going with you. (5)

verses.text:
व्यसनी वा समृद्धो वा गतिरेष तवानघ।
एष लोके सतां धर्मो यज्ज्येष्ठवशगो भवेत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “He alone is your refuge, whether in adversity or in affluent circumstances, O sinless one ! Such is the rule of conduct followed by the virtuous in the world that a younger brother should be subject to the control of his elder brother. (6)

verses.text:
इदं हि वृत्तमुचितं कुलस्यास्य सनातनम्।
दानं दीक्षा च यज्ञेषु तनुत्यागो मृधेषु हि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “To practise charity, to consecrate oneself for sacrificial performances and to drop one’s body on the field of battle alone—these indeed constitute the conduct appropriate to this race of the Raghus for all time.” (7)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वासौ संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्।
सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Having exhorted Lakṣmaṇa as aforesaid, the said Sumitrā repeatedly said to the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was loved by all and was bent on leaving for the forest, “Fare forth ! Fare forth !! May all be well with you.” (8)

verses.text:
रामं दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्।
अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: She said to Lakṣmaṇa again, “Know Rāma to be Daśaratha as your father, look upon Sītā (the daughter of Janaka) as myself (your mother) and esteem the forest as Ayodhyā (your home) and depart, dear son, happily.” (9)

verses.text:
ततः सुमन्त्रः काकुत्स्थं प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
विनीतो विनयज्ञश्च मातलिर्वासवं यथा॥ १०॥
verses.m: Then Sumantra, who was meek and knew how to behave politely, submitted with folded hands as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) even as Mātali (the charioteer of Indra) would to Indra (the ruler of gods) : (10)

verses.text:
रथमारोह भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः।
क्षिप्रं त्वां प्रापयिष्यामि यत्र मां राम वक्ष्यसे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Mount the chariot, O highly illustrious prince; may all be well with you. I shall speedily take you to whatever place you will direct me to go. (11)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानि वने त्वया।
तान्युपक्रमितव्यानि यानि देव्या प्रचोदितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Indeed those fourteen years that have to be spent by you in the forest as directed by the queen (Kaikeyī) are to be considered as having commenced this very day.” (12)

verses.text:
तं रथं सूर्यसंकाशं सीता हृष्टेन चेतसा।
आरुरोह वरारोहा कृत्वालंकारमात्मनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having decked herself with the articles of wearing apparel and ornaments bestowed on her by her father-in-law, Sītā, who had comely limbs, mounted with a delighted mind that chariot, which was resplendent like the sun. (13)

verses.text:
वनवासं हि संख्याय वासांस्याभरणानि च।
भर्तारमनुगच्छन्त्यै सीतायै श्वशुरो ददौ॥ १४॥
तथैवायुधजातानि भ्रातृभ्यां कवचानि च।
रथोपस्थे प्रविन्यस्य सचर्म कठिनं च यत्॥ १५॥
अथो ज्वलनसंकाशं चामीकरविभूषितम्।
तमारुरुहतुस्तूर्णं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having carefully arranged in the hinder part of the chariot the raiments and jewels which her father-in-law, duly taking into account the period of her exile in the forest, had bestowed on Sītā, while she was ready to accompany her husband to the forest, and even so the sets of weapons and the pieces of armour he had given to the two brothers, as well as the basket, covered with leather, and the spade, the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, then quickly mounted the aforesaid chariot, which was decked in gold and shone like fire. (14—16)

verses.text:
सीतातृतीयानारूढान् दृष्ट्वा रथमचोदयत्।
सुमन्त्रः सम्मतानश्वान् वायुवेगसमाञ्जवे॥ १७॥
verses.m: Seeing the three exiles, of whom Sītā constituted the third, mounted on the chariot, Sumantra drove the horses, which were thought highly of and wied in speed with the velocity of the wind. (17)

verses.text:
प्रयाते तु महारण्यं चिररात्राय राघवे।
बभूव नगरे मूर्च्छा बलमूर्च्छा जनस्य च॥ १८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, having departed for the great forest of Daṇḍaka for a long term, unconsciousness, however, prevailed among the people in the city; there was unconsciousness in the army including even horses and elephants as well as among the people visiting Ayodhyā from the districts. (18)

verses.text:
तत् समाकुलसम्भ्रान्तं मत्तसंकुपितद्विपम्।
हयसिञ्जितनिर्घोषं पुरमासीन्महास्वनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Confounded and flurried with its elephants in rut highly excited, and resonant with the tinkling of the ornaments of its horses, the aforesaid city of Ayodhyā was filled with great noise. (19)

verses.text:
ततः सबालवृद्धा सा पुरी परमपीडिता।
राममेवाभिदुद्राव घर्मार्तः सलिलं यथा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Sore stricken with agony, that city including the youngsters as well as the old people rushed towards Śrī Rāma in the same way as one oppressed with the sun would rush towards water. (20)

verses.text:
पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चापि लम्बमानास्तदुन्मुखाः।
बाष्पपूर्णमुखाः सर्वे तमूचुर्भृशनिःस्वनाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Clinging to the sides and back of the chariot with their faces turned towards him and bathed with tears, all submitted to Sumantra in a loud voice: (21)

verses.text:
संयच्छ वाजिनां रश्मीन् सूत याहि शनैः शनैः।
मुखं द्रक्ष्याम रामस्य दुर्दर्शं नो भविष्यति॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Hold in the reins of the horses, O charioteer, and drive slowly and slowly. We would behold the countenance of Śrī Rāma, which would henceforth be difficult to behold. (22)

verses.text:
आयसं हृदयं नूनं राममातुरसंशयम्।
यद् देवगर्भप्रतिमे वनं याति न भिद्यते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The heart of Kausalyā (Śrī Rāma’s mother) is surely and undoubtedly made of steel in that it does not get riven even when her son, who resembles an offspring of gods, is departing for the forest ! (23)

verses.text:
कृतकृत्या हि वैदेही छायेवानुगता पतिम्।
न जहाति रता धर्मे मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, has done what ought to be done inasmuch as she follows her husband like a shadow and, devoted to her duty, does not leave him any more than the light of the sun forsakes Mount Meru. (24)

verses.text:
अहो लक्ष्मण सिद्धार्थः सततं प्रियवादिनम्।
भ्रातरं देवसंकाशं यस्त्वं परिचरिष्यसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “O Lakṣmaṇa, you are accomplished of purpose in that you are going to serve your godlike brother, who is ever disposed to speak kind words to all. (25)

verses.text:
महत्येषा हि ते बुद्धिरेष चाभ्युदयो महान्।
एष स्वर्गस्य मार्गश्च यदेनमनुगच्छसि॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Indeed this constitutes your great wisdom; nay, this is your great good fortune and this is the way to heaven for you that you are following Śrī Rāma !” (26)

verses.text:
एवं वदन्तस्ते सोढुं न शेकुर्बाष्पमागतम्।
नरास्तमनुगच्छन्ति प्रियमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Saying so, those men could not restrain their tears, that had already welled up in their eyes, and followed their beloved Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣwākus. (27)

verses.text:
अथ राजा वृतः स्त्रीभिर्दीनाभिर्दीनचेतनः।
निर्जगाम प्रियं पुत्रं द्रक्ष्यामीति ब्रुवन् गृहात्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Meanwhile, surrounded by his consorts—who were all feeling miserable—and distressed in mind, the king sallied forth from his palace, saying “I shall see my beloved son.” (28)

verses.text:
शुश्रुवे चाग्रतः स्त्रीणां रुदतीनां महास्वनः।
यथा नादः करेणूनां बद्धे महति कुञ्जरे॥ २९॥
verses.m: In front of him was heard the great noise of crying women, resembling the trumpeting of she-elephants on a lordly elephant, the leader of their herd, having been bound with chains. (29)

verses.text:
पिता हि राजा काकुत्स्थः श्रीमान् सन्नस्तदा बभौ।
परिपूर्णः शशी काले ग्रहेणोपप्लुतो यथा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: At that time, the father of Śrī Rāma, the glorious King Daśaratha, a scion of Kakutstha, looked lustreless indeed like the full moon overshadowed by Rāhu during a lunar eclipse. (30)

verses.text:
स च श्रीमानचिन्त्यात्मा रामो दशरथात्मजः।
सूतं संचोदयामास त्वरितं वाह्यतामिति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: The illustrious son of Daśaratha, Śrī Rāma, on the other hand, of inconceivable firmness, commanded the charioteer in the words “Let the chariot be driven fast.” (31)

verses.text:
रामो याहीति तं सूतं तिष्ठेति च जनस्तथा।
उभयं नाशकत् सूतः कर्तुमध्वनि चोदितः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma commanded the celebrated charioteer in the words “Move on !” And the people following the chariot likewise said to him, “Stop !” Urged both ways on the road, the charioteer, however, could do neither. (32)

verses.text:
निर्गच्छति महाबाहौ रामे पौरजनाश्रुभिः।
पतितैरभ्यवहितं प्रणनाश महीरजः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: The dust raised on the road even as the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma drove out of the city for the forest settled down due to the tears that fell from the eyes of the citizens following at his heels. (33)

verses.text:
रुदिताश्रुपरिद्यूनं हाहाकृतमचेतनम्।
प्रयाणे राघवस्यासीत् पुरं परमपीडितम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Full of lamentation and tears and, therefore, doleful in appearance at the departure of Śrī Rāma, the citizens of Ayodhyā, who were stricken with deep agony and commenced wailing loudly, became unconscious. (34)

verses.text:
सुस्राव नयनैः स्त्रीणामस्रमायाससम्भवम्।
मीनसंक्षोभचलितैः सलिलं पङ्कजैरिव॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Tears born of agony, caused by separation from Śrī Rāma, flowed from the eyes of women like drops of water from lotuses shaken by the commotion of fish. (35)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तु नृपतिः श्रीमानेकचित्तगतं पुरम्।
निपपातैव दुःखेन कृत्तमूल इव द्रुमः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Seeing the city reduced to singleness of mind, the glorious king for his part fell down precipitately like a tree cut at the root. (36)

verses.text:
ततो हलहलाशब्दो जज्ञे रामस्य पृष्ठतः।
नराणां प्रेक्ष्य राजानं सीदन्तं भृशदुःखितम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Perceiving the king sore distressed and suffering agony, an outcry thereupon rose from the mouths of men in the rear of Śrī Rāma. (37)

verses.text:
हा रामेति जनाः केचिद् राममातेति चापरे।
अन्तःपुरसमृद्धं च क्रोशन्तं पर्यदेवयन्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Seeing him wailing with the inmates of his gynaeceum some people cried out, “Oh Rāma”, while others exclaimed, “Oh Rāma’s mother !” (38)

verses.text:
अन्वीक्षमाणो रामस्तु विषण्णं भ्रान्तचेतसम्।
राजानं मातरं चैव ददर्शानुगतौ पथि॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Looking back, Śrī Rāma forthwith beheld the king, dejected and perplexed in mind, as well as his own mother, Kausalyā, following him on the road. (39)

verses.text:
स बद्ध इव पाशेन किशोरो मातरं यथा।
धर्मपाशेन संयुक्तः प्रकाशं नाभ्युदैक्षत॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Bound by the cord of duty, he did not openly gaze on them any more than a foal, caught in a snare would look at its dam. (40)

verses.text:
पदातिनौ च यानार्हावदुःखार्हौ सुखोचितौ।
दृष्ट्वा संचोदयामास शीघ्रं याहीति सारथिम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Seeing them walking, though worthy of a chariot, unworthy of suffering and deserving of comfort, he commanded the charioteer in the words “Drive fast !” (41)

verses.text:
नहि तत् पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुःखजं दर्शनं पितुः।
मातुश्च सहितुं शक्तस्तोत्त्रैर्नुन्न इव द्विपः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Even as an elephant urged on with goads is unable to look behind, Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, too was unable to bear the distressing sight of his father and mother (following him on foot). (42)

verses.text:
प्रत्यगारमिवायान्ती सवत्सा वत्सकारणात्।
बद्धवत्सा यथा धेनू राममाताभ्यधावत॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Kausalyā, Śrī Rāma’s mother, rushed forth after Śrī Rāma as a cow that has given birth to a calf and whose calf stands tied at the stall, would run to meet it while returning to its stall from the pasture. (43)

verses.text:
तथा रुदन्तीं कौसल्यां रथं तमनुधावतीम्।
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च॥ ४४॥
रामलक्ष्मणसीतार्थं स्रवन्तीं वारि नेत्रजम्।
असकृत् प्रैक्षत स तां नृत्यन्तीमिव मातरम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma repeatedly gazed on his aforesaid mother, Kausalyā, who was weeping as above and following that chariot as though dancing, crying “Rāma, O Rāma, O Sītā, O Lakṣmaṇa !” and shedding tears for the sake of Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā. (44-45)

verses.text:
तिष्ठेति राजा चुक्रोश याहि याहीति राघवः।
सुमन्त्रस्य बभूवात्मा चक्रयोरिव चान्तरा॥ ४६॥
verses.m: The king, on the one hand, exclaimed saying “Stop !”, while Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, called out “Go on ! Proceed !!” In this way Sumantra’s mind was placed in a dilemma as one would feel while standing between two revolving wheels. (46)

verses.text:
नाश्रौषमिति राजानमुपालब्धोऽपि वक्ष्यसि।
चिरं दुःखस्य पापिष्ठमिति रामस्तमब्रवीत्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma said to him, “Even when twitted by the king on going back to Ayodhyā, for not carrying out his orders, you will say, ‘I did not hear your call.’ Prolongation of this agony caused by witnessing the sad plight of my aged and feeble parents would prove most calamitous.” (47)

verses.text:
स रामस्य वचः कुर्वन्ननुज्ञाप्य च तं जनम्।
व्रजतोऽपि हयान् शीघ्रं चोदयामास सारथिः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Carrying out the behest of Śrī Rāma and taking leave of that crowd which was following at his heels, the aforesaid charioteer urged on the horses, that were already moving ahead, to go fast. (48)

verses.text:
न्यवर्तत जनो राज्ञो रामं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्।
मनसाप्याशुवेगेन न न्यवर्तत मानुषम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Mentally going round Śrī Rāma clockwise, the king’s men returned to the king’s presence with their body, which could not keep pace with the chariot, though they accompanied Śrī Rāma with their mind to the forest; the commonalty, however, did not return even with their body as they did not return with their mind, which was possessed of a quick speed. (49)

verses.text:
यमिच्छेत् पुनरायातं नैनं दूरमनुव्रजेत्।
इत्यमात्या महाराजमूचुर्दशरथं वचः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: On returning to the king’s presence, the ministers submitted to Emperor Daśaratha as follows : “One should not follow to a long distance him whom one wishes to see come back.” (50)

verses.text:
तेषां वचः सर्वगुणोपपन्नः
प्रस्विन्नगात्रः प्रविषण्णरूपः।
निशम्य राजा कृपणः सभार्यो
व्यवस्थितस्तं सुतमीक्षमाणः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Hearing their submission, the king, who was endowed with all virtues and felt miserable, stopped short, gazing with his consorts, on his celebrated son, Śrī Rāma, nay, perspiring all over his body and wearing a most dejected appearance. (51)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रे निष्क्रामति कृताञ्जलौ।
आर्तशब्दो हि संजज्ञे स्त्रीणामन्तःपुरे महान्॥ १॥
verses.m: Even as Śrī Rāma, that tiger among men, was driving out of Ayodhyā with folded hands, a loud plaintive cry actually burst forth from the mouths of the ladies in the gynaeceum. (1)

verses.text:
अनाथस्य जनस्यास्य दुर्बलस्य तपस्विनः।
यो गतिः शरणं चासीत् स नाथः क्व नु गच्छति॥ २॥
verses.m: They exclaimed : “Oh, where goes that lord, who was the refuge and protector of us, helpless, weak and forlorn people? (2)

verses.text:
न क्रुध्यत्यभिशस्तोऽपि क्रोधनीयानि वर्जयन्।
क्रुद्धान् प्रसादयन् सर्वान् समदुःखः क्व गच्छति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Oh, where goes the prince to whom joy and sorrow made no difference, nay who did not lose temper even when slandered, avoided provoking words and pacified all who were angry? (3)

verses.text:
कौसल्यायां महातेजा यथा मातरि वर्तते।
तथा यो वर्ततेऽस्मासु महात्मा क्व नु गच्छति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Where goes the high-souled Śrī Rāma, who is endowed with exceptional glory and who behaved with us in the same way as he did with his own mother, Kausalyā? (4)

verses.text:
कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानेन राज्ञा संचोदितो वनम्।
परित्राता जनस्यास्य जगतः क्व नु गच्छति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Oh, where goes Śrī Rāma, the protector not only of us all but even of the world, enjoined to proceed to the forest by the king, who was being tormented by Kaikeyī? (5)

verses.text:
अहो निश्चेतनो राजा जीवलोकस्य संक्षयम्।
धर्म्यं सत्यव्रतं रामं वनवासे प्रवत्स्यति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “How insensible is the king, who has sent into exile to the forest the virtuous Prince Rāma, who is the support of the entire living creation and is vowed to truthfulness !” (6)

verses.text:
इति सर्वा महिष्यस्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः।
रुरुदुश्चैव दुःखार्ताः सस्वरं च विचुक्रुशुः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Stricken with agony all the aforesaid queens lamented in this way and cried at the top of their voice like so many cows bereft of their calf. (7)

verses.text:
स तमन्तःपुरे घोरमार्तशब्दं महीपतिः।
पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः श्रुत्वा चासीत् सुदुःखितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing that frightful plaintive cry in the gynaeceum, King Daśaratha, who was already tormented with grief caused by separation from his son, felt sore distressed. (8)

verses.text:
नाग्निहोत्राण्यहूयन्त नापचन् गृहमेधिनः।
अकुर्वन् न प्रजाः कार्यं सूर्यश्चान्तरधीयत॥ ९॥
verses.m: No oblations were poured into the sacred fire by those maintaining the sacred fire; no householders cooked food; people did not carry on their business and the sun went out of sight even before sunset due to untimely clouds. (9)

verses.text:
व्यसृजन् कवलान् नागा गावो वत्सान् न पाययन्।
पुत्रं प्रथमजं लब्ध्वा जननी नाभ्यनन्दत॥ १०॥
verses.m: Elephants dropped grass etc., from their mouths; cows refused to give suck to their calves; mothers did not rejoice to meet their first-born son. (10)

verses.text:
त्रिशङ्कुर्लोहिताङ्गश्च बृहस्पतिबुधावपि।
दारुणाः सोममभ्येत्य ग्रहाः सर्वे व्यवस्थिताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Getting conjoined through a retrogade movement with the moon, Triśaṅku and Mars, even Jupiter and Mercury and all other luminaries assumed a stern aspect. (11)

verses.text:
नक्षत्राणि गतार्चींषि ग्रहाश्च गततेजसः।
विशाखाश्च सधूमाश्च नभसि प्रचकाशिरे॥ १२॥
verses.m: The lunar mansions lost their brilliance and the planets their splendour. Proceeding on a wrong course they cast a hazy lustre in the heavens. (12)

verses.text:
कालिकानिलवेगेन महोदधिरिवोत्थितः।
रामे वनं प्रव्रजिते नगरं प्रचचाल तत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Driven by a blast of wind, a mass of clouds rose in the sky like a turbulent ocean. Nay, Śrī Rāma having departed for the forest, the city of Ayodhyā rocked to and fro. (13)

verses.text:
दिशः पर्याकुलाः सर्वास्तिमिरेणेव संवृताः।
न ग्रहो नापि नक्षत्रं प्रचकाशे न किंचन॥ १४॥
verses.m: All the four quarters became obscure as though enveloped in darkness. No planet nor any lunar mansion emitted the faintest light. (14)

verses.text:
अकस्मान्नागरः सर्वो जनो दैन्यमुपागमत्।
आहारे वा विहारे वा न कश्चिदकरोन्मनः॥ १५॥
verses.m: All of a sudden all the people of Ayodhyā were reduced to a wretched plight. None could give his or her mind to food or recreation. (15)

verses.text:
शोकपर्यायसंतप्तः सततं दीर्घमुच्छ्वसन्।
अयोध्यायां जनः सर्वश्चुक्रोश जगतीपतिम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Tormented with recurrence of grief and sighing heavily all the time, all the people of Ayodhyā cursed the Emperor. (16)

verses.text:
बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखो राजमार्गगतो जनः।
न हृष्टो लभ्यते कश्चित् सर्वः शोकपरायणः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Men walking on the public road had their face soiled with tears. None was found merry, all were plunged in grief. (17)

verses.text:
न वाति पवनः शीतो न शशी सौम्यदर्शनः।
न सूर्यस्तपते लोकं सर्वं पर्याकुलं जगत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: No cool breeze blew nor did the moon present a placid appearance, nor again did the sun warm the people with its rays. The whole world was disturbed in mind. (18)

verses.text:
अनर्थिनः सुताः स्त्रीणां भर्तारो भ्रातरस्तथा।
सर्वे सर्वं परित्यज्य राममेवान्वचिन्तयन्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Sons were indifferent to their mothers, husbands were of no use to their wives and brothers had no use for their brothers. Abandoning everything else, all focussed their thought on Śrī Rāma alone. (19)

verses.text:
ये तु रामस्य सुहृदः सर्वे ते मूढचेतसः।
शोकभारेण चाक्रान्ताः शयनं नैव भेजिरे॥ २०॥
verses.m: All those, however, who were friends of Śrī Rāma were perplexed in mind and had no sleep, overwhelmed as they were with excess of grief. (20)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वयोध्या रहिता महात्मना
पुरन्दरेणेव मही सपर्वता।
चचाल घोरं भयशोकदीपिता
सनागयोधाश्वगणा ननाद च॥ २१॥
verses.m: Agitated through fear and grief, the city of Ayodhyā, bereft of Śrī Rāma, the high-souled prince, was thereupon violently disturbed—even as the earth alongwith its mountains rocks to and fro when bereft of Indra (the destroyer of strongholds)—and cried with its elephants, warriors and horses. (21)

verses.text:
यावत् तु निर्यतस्तस्य रजोरूपमदृश्यत।
नैवेक्ष्वाकुवरस्तावत् संजहारात्मचक्षुषी॥ १॥
verses.m: So long, however, as the clouds of the dust that followed Śrī Rāma even as he was going out to the forest could be seen, Daśaratha, the foremost of the Ikṣwākus, did not turn his eyes away from them. (1)

verses.text:
यावद् राजा प्रियं पुत्रं पश्यत्यत्यन्तधार्मिकम्।
तावद् व्यवर्धतेवास्य धरण्यां पुत्रदर्शने॥ २॥
verses.m: So long as the king saw his beloved and most virtuous son (in the form of the dust raised by his chariot) his body stood on the ground growing in size as it were to be able to catch a glimpse of his gradually receding son. (2)

verses.text:
न पश्यति रजोऽप्यस्य यदा रामस्य भूमिपः।
तदाऽऽतश्च निषण्णश्च पपात धरणीतले॥ ३॥
verses.m: The moment, however, the king ceased to behold even the dust of the chariot of the said Śrī Rāma, he dropped to the ground afflicted and dejected. (3)

verses.text:
तस्य दक्षिणमन्वागात् कौसल्या बाहुमङ्गना।
परं चास्यान्वगात् पार्श्वं कैकेयी सा सुमध्यमा॥ ४॥
verses.m: His seniormost wife, Kausalyā, approached his right arm in order to lift him up by that arm, while the notorious Kaikeyī of charming limbs went up to his other (left) side. (4)

verses.text:
तां नयेन च सम्पन्नो धर्मेण विनयेन च।
उवाच राजा कैकेयीं समीक्ष्य व्यथितेन्द्रियः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Distressed in mind to behold Kaikeyī, the king, who was richly endowed with prudence, as well as with piety and culture, spoke to her as follows : (5)

verses.text:
कैकेयि मामकाङ्गानि मा स्प्राक्षीः पापनिश्चये।
नहि त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छामि न भार्या न च बान्धवी॥ ६॥
verses.m: “O Kaikeyī of sinful resolve, pray, do not touch my limbs, really I do not wish to see you; you are neither my wedded wife nor my relation. (6)

verses.text:
ये च त्वामनुजीवन्ति नाहं तेषां न ते मम।
केवलार्थपरां हि त्वां त्यक्तधर्मां त्यजाम्यहम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Nay, I am no longer the master of those who depend for their subsistence on you nor are they my servants any more. I disown you, who are solely devoted to your selfish ends and have forsaken virtue. (7)

verses.text:
अगृह्णां यच्च ते पाणिमग्निं पर्यणयं च यत्।
अनुजानामि तत् सर्वमस्मिंल्लोके परत्र च॥ ८॥
verses.m: “I hereby disclaim all the benefits that will accrue to me hereafter in this world and the next from the fact that I clasped your hand in marriage and took you round the fire with me. (8)

verses.text:
भरतश्चेत् प्रतीतः स्याद् राज्यं प्राप्यैतदव्ययम्।
यन्मे स दद्यात् पित्रर्थं मा मां तद्दत्तमागमत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “If Bharata gets delighted to receive this sovereignty free from hindrance, let not that which he offers to me after my death by way of obsequial oblations intended for his departed ancestors reach me in the other world.” (9)

verses.text:
अथ रेणुसमुद्ध्वस्तं समुत्थाप्य नराधिपम्।
न्यवर्तत तदा देवी कौसल्या शोककर्शिता॥ १०॥
verses.m: Forthwith lifting up the king, who was soiled with dust due to his having toppled down, Queen Kausalyā, who had been emaciated through grief, then returned to the palace with the king. (10)

verses.text:
हत्वेव ब्राह्मणं कामात् स्पृष्ट्वाग्निमिव पाणिना।
अन्वतप्यत धर्मात्मा पुत्रं संचिन्त्य राघवम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thinking deeply of his son, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Daśaratha (of pious mind) gave way to repentance for having sent him into exile under pressure from Kaikeyī, even as one is stung with remorse on having voluntarily killed a Brāhmaṇa or on touching a blazing fire with one’s own hand. (11)

verses.text:
निवृत्यैव निवृत्यैव सीदतो रथवर्त्मसु।
राज्ञो नातिबभौ रूपं ग्रस्तस्यांशुमतो यथा॥ १२॥
verses.m: The appearance of the king, who, turning back again and again, exerted himself to gaze on the path which the chariot of Śrī Rāma had taken, did not look charming any more than the orb of the sun in eclipse. (12)

verses.text:
विललाप स दुःखार्तः प्रियं पुत्रमनुस्मरन्।
नगरान्तमनुप्राप्तं बुद्ध्वा पुत्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Thinking all the time of his beloved son, Śrī Rāma, he lamented, stricken with agony as he was. Coming to know of his son having reached the outskirts of the city, he then spoke as follows: (13)

verses.text:
वाहनानां च मुख्यानां वहतां तं ममात्मजम्।
पदानि पथि दृश्यन्ते स महात्मा न दृश्यते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The marks of the hoofs of the excellent horses drawing the chariot of my celebrated son are no doubt seen on the road, but that high-souled prince is no longer seen. (14)

verses.text:
यः सुखेनोपधानेषु शेते चन्दनरूषितः।
वीज्यमानो महार्हाभिः स्त्रीभिर्मम सुतोत्तमः॥ १५॥
स नूनं क्वचिदेवाद्य वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः।
काष्ठं वा यदि वाश्मानमुपधाय शयिष्यते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “That jewel among my sons, who, having been smeared all over with sandal-paste, used to repose comfortably on cushions and pillows, while being fanned by women possessed of great comeliness and adorned with costly jewels, will surely lie down today at some unknown place at the foot of a tree resting his head on a block of wood or stone ! (15-16)

verses.text:
उत्थास्यति च मेदिन्याः कृपणः पांसुगुण्ठितः।
विनिःश्वसन् प्रस्रवणात् करेणूनामिवर्षभः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nay, at the close of night he will rise from the bare ground in a wretched condition, enveloped in dust and exhaling audibly like a leader of elephants rising from beside a spring. (17)

verses.text:
द्रक्ष्यन्ति नूनं पुरुषा दीर्घबाहुं वनेचराः।
राममुत्थाय गच्छन्तं लोकनाथमनाथवत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Undoubtedly people living in the forest will behold Rāma, the protector of the world, who is possessed of long arms, rising from sleep in the forest and going forth like one forlorn. (18)

verses.text:
सा नूनं जनकस्येष्टा सुता सुखसदोचिता।
कण्टकाक्रमणक्लान्ता वनमद्य गमिष्यति॥ १९॥
verses.m: “That beloved daughter of Janaka, who is ever worthy of all kinds of amenities, will surely walk today to the forest barefooted and, therefore, injured by treading on thorns. (19)

verses.text:
अनभिज्ञा वनानां सा नूनं भयमुपैष्यति।
श्वपदानर्दितं श्रुत्वा गम्भीरं रोमहर्षणम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Unacquainted as she is with the woods, she will doubtless be struck with fear to hear the deep and thrilling roar of beasts of prey. (20)

verses.text:
सकामा भव कैकेयि विधवा राज्यमावस।
नहि तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं विना जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Having your wishes fulfilled, O Kaikeyī, enjoy the kingdom as a widow. I am unable to live without that tiger among men.” (21)

verses.text:
इत्येवं विलपन् राजा जनौघेनाभिसंवृतः।
अपस्नात इवारिष्टं प्रविवेश गृहोत्तमम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Lamenting as aforesaid, and surrounded on all sides by a multitude of men, the king entered his excellent abode, which was full of sorrow, like one who has bathed on the death of a relation. (22)

verses.text:
शून्यचत्वरवेश्मान्तां संवृतापणवेदिकाम्।
क्लान्तदुर्बलदुःखार्तां नात्याकीर्णमहापथाम्॥ २३॥
तामवेक्ष्य पुरीं सर्वां राममेवानुचिन्तयन्।
विलपन् प्राविशद् राजा गृहं सूर्य इवाम्बुदम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Perceiving the entire city of Ayodhyā with its cross roads and portals deserted and the sheds in front of shops, where merchandise was spread, closed, its people depressed in spirits, feeble and afflicted and its highways not very crowded, the king entered his palace wailing and thinking all the time of Śrī Rāma alone, even as the sun enters a cloud. (23-24)

verses.text:
महाह्रदमिवाक्षोभ्यं सुपर्णेन हृतोरगम्।
रामेण रहितं वेश्म वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च॥ २५॥
verses.m: Bereft of Śrī Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, the palace looked like a big pool rendered imperturbable due to its snakes having been carried away by Garuḍa. (25)

verses.text:
अथ गद्गदशब्दस्तु विलपन् वसुधाधिपः।
उवाच मृदु मन्दार्थं वचनं दीनमस्वरम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: The lamenting Emperor then spoke to the porters in faltering, soft, pitiful and indistinct words, which were also not clearly intelligible as follows : (26)

verses.text:
कौसल्याया गृहं शीघ्रं राममातुर्नयन्तु माम्।
नह्यन्यत्र ममाश्वासो हृदयस्य भविष्यति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Take me speedily to the apartments of Kausalyā, the mother of Rāma; for nowhere else will my heart find solace.” (27)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवन्तं राजानमनयन् द्वारदर्शिनः।
कौसल्याया गृहं तत्र न्यवेश्यत विनीतवत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: The porters took the king, who was speaking as aforesaid, to the apartments of Kausalyā and there he was gently laid by them on a couch. (28)

verses.text:
ततस्तत्र प्रविष्टस्य कौसल्याया निवेशनम्।
अधिरुह्यापि शयनं बभूव लुलितं मनः॥ २९॥
verses.m: The mind of the king, even though he had entered Kausalyā’s apartments and had been laid on a couch, continued to be restless. (29)

verses.text:
पुत्रद्वयविहीनं च स्नुषया च विवर्जितम्।
अपश्यद् भवनं राजा नष्टचन्द्रमिवाम्बरम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: The king found the palace, which was bereft of his two sons and destitute of his daughter-in-law, devoid of charm as the sky without the moon and the stars. (30)

verses.text:
तच्च दृष्ट्वा महाराजो भुजमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्।
उच्चैःस्वरेण प्राक्रोशद्धा राम विजहासि नौ॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Looking at the palace and lifting up his arm, the powerful Emperor cried in a loud voice: “Oh Rāma, are you really deserting us both, your mother as well as myself? (31)

verses.text:
सुखिता बत तं कालं जीविष्यन्ति नरोत्तमाः।
परिष्वजन्तो ये रामं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Alas, those jewels among men alone who will survive the term of Rāma’s exile and are eventually able to see him come back, clasping him to their bosom, will be really happy !” (32)

verses.text:
अथ रात्र्यां प्रपन्नायां कालरात्र्यामिवात्मनः।
अर्धरात्रे दशरथः कौसल्यामिदमब्रवीत्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Now when the night arrived—the night which was, as it were, the night of Dissolution for him—King Daśaratha spoke at midnight to Kausalyā as follows: (33)

verses.text:
न त्वां पश्यामि कौसल्ये साधु मां पाणिना स्पृश।
रामं मेऽनुगता दृष्टिरद्यापि न निवर्तते॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Kausalyā, I am unable to see you. Please touch me with your hand well. Having followed Rāma, my sight has not yet returned.” (34)

verses.text:
तं राममेवानुविचिन्तयन्तं
समीक्ष्य देवी शयने नरेन्द्रम्।
उपोपविश्याधिकमार्तरूपा
विनिश्वसन्तं विललाप कृच्छ्रम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Perceiving the aforesaid monarch on the couch—who was thinking deeply all the time of Śrī Rāma alone and breathing hard with difficulty—and sitting by his side, the queen (Kausalyā), who wore a distressed look about her, began to wail. (35)

verses.text:
ततः समीक्ष्य शयने सन्नं शोकेन पार्थिवम्।
कौसल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता तमुवाच महीपतिम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving the king lying on the couch stricken with grief, Kausalyā, who was feeling distressed due to grief on account of separation from her son, Śrī Rāma, spoke to the said king as follows : (1)

verses.text:
राघवे नरशार्दूले विषं मुक्त्वाहिजिह्मगा।
विचरिष्यति कैकेयी निर्मुक्तेव हि पन्नगी॥ २॥
verses.m: “Having discharged her poison on Rāma (a scion of Raghu), a tiger among men, indeed, Kaikeyī of crooked ways will surely wander about freely like a female serpent that has cast off its slough. (2)

verses.text:
विवास्य रामं सुभगा लब्धकामा समाहिता।
त्रासयिष्यति मां भूयो दुष्टाहिरिव वेश्मनि॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Having exiled Rāma and thereby achieving her desired end, Kaikeyī, whose stars are propitious and whose mind is at rest now, will further cause fear to me, undisturbed like a wicked serpent dwelling in one’s own house. (3)

verses.text:
अथास्मिन् नगरे रामश्चरन् भैक्षं गृहे वसेत्।
कामकारो वरं दातुमपि दासं ममात्मजम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Even if Rāma were allowed to remain at his home in Ayodhyā living on alms, it would be preferable to me in comparison to his exile. Nay, it would be better even to consign my son to her as a slave. (4)

verses.text:
पातयित्वा तु कैकेय्या रामं स्थानाद् यथेष्टतः।
प्रविद्धो रक्षसां भागः पर्वणीवाहिताग्निना॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Having wantonly thrown Rāma out of his position, Kaikeyī has acted in the same way as an oblation intended for the gods may be consigned to ogres on a new or full moon by one who tends the sacred fire. (5)

verses.text:
नागराजगतिर्वीरो महाबाहुर्धनुर्धरः।
वनमाविशते नूनं सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by his wife and Lakṣmaṇa and walking like a king of elephants, bow in hand, the mighty-armed hero will have surely entered the forest by now. (6)

verses.text:
वने त्वदृष्टदुःखानां कैकेय्यनुमते त्वया।
त्यक्तानां वनवासाय कान्यावस्था भविष्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “In a forest what other fate than the hardships of forest life can befall the youths, who had never known suffering before and who have been consigned by you to a forest life following the wishes of Kaikeyī? (7)

verses.text:
ते रत्नहीनास्तरुणाः फलकाले विवासिताः।
कथं वत्स्यन्ति कृपणाः फलमूलैः कृताशनाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Exiled at a time when they should have in the ordinary circumstances enjoyed the fruits (amenities) of life, how shall the poor youths, who have been deprived of all precious things, drag their existence living on fruits and roots? (8)

verses.text:
अपीदानीं स कालः स्यान्मम शोकक्षयः शिवः।
सहभार्यं सह भ्रात्रा पश्येयमिह राघवम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Will that happy time, marked with the end of my grief, ever come, when I shall be able to see Rāma (a scion of Raghu) accompanied by his wife and younger brother back in Ayodhyā? (9)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वैवोपस्थितौ वीरौ कदायोध्या भविष्यति।
यशस्विनी हृष्टजना सूच्छ्रितध्वजमालिनी॥ १०॥
verses.m: “When will Ayodhyā regain her pristine glory, throb with joyous crowds and be adorned once more with rows of towering banners the moment it hears of the two heroic princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, being present? (10)

verses.text:
कदा प्रेक्ष्य नरव्याघ्रावरण्यात् पुनरागतौ।
भविष्यति पुरी हृष्टा समुद्र इव पर्वणि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “When will the city wax jubilant again like an ocean on a full moon night to perceive the two princes, who are really tigers among men, come back from the forest? (11)

verses.text:
कदायोध्यां महाबाहुः पुरीं वीरः प्रवेक्ष्यति।
पुरस्कृत्य रथे सीतां वृषभो गोवधूमिव॥ १२॥
verses.m: “When will the mighty-armed hero, Śrī Rāma, enter again the city of Ayodhyā placing Sītā at his head in the chariot, even as a bull would follow a cow? (12)

verses.text:
कदा प्राणिसहस्राणि राजमार्गे ममात्मजौ।
लाजैरवकरिष्यन्ति प्रविशन्तावरिंदमौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “When will thousands of men cover with parched grains of paddy on the public road my two sons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the subduers of their enemy, entering the city? (13)

verses.text:
प्रविशन्तौ कदायोध्यां द्रक्ष्यामि शुभकुण्डलौ।
उदग्रायुधनिस्तिं्रशौ सशृङ्गाविव पर्वतौ॥ १४॥
verses.m: “When shall I be able to see the two princes, adorned with splendid earrings and armed with excellent bows and swords, entering Ayodhyā like a pair of mountains crowned with peaks? (14)

verses.text:
कदा सुमनसःकन्या द्विजातीनां फलानि च।
प्रदिशन्त्यः पुरीं हृष्टाः करिष्यन्ति प्रदक्षिणम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “When will the three darlings merrily go round the city clockwise, receiving on the way flowers from the hands of virgins and fruits from those of Brāhmaṇas? (15)

verses.text:
कदा परिणतो बुद्ध्या वयसा चामरप्रभाः।
अभ्युपैष्यति धर्मात्मा सुवर्ष इव लालयन्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “When will the pious Rāma, grown ripe in intellect and shining like a god in point of age (eternal youth), return, fostering the world like a good (timely) shower? (16)

verses.text:
निःसंशयं मया मन्ये पुरा वीर कदर्यया।
पातुकामेषु वत्सेषु मातॄणां शातिताः स्तनाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Undoubtedly in some past life, I believe, O valiant king, the teats of cows were cut off by me, mean-minded as I was, while their calves stood waiting to suck them. (17)

verses.text:
साहं गौरिव सिंहेन विवत्सा वत्सला कृता।
कैकेय्या पुरुषव्याघ्र बालवत्सेव गौर्बलात्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Fond of my child like a cow, O tiger among men, I have for this very reason been forcibly deprived of my child by Kaikeyī in the same way as a cow, having a calf of tender age, may be deprived of her calf by a lion. (18)

verses.text:
नहि तावद्गुणैर्जुष्टं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्।
एकपुत्रा विना पुत्रमहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Having only one son, I am surely unable to survive without that son, who is endowed with all virtues and is well-versed in all the scriptures. (19)

verses.text:
न हि मे जीविते किंचित् सामर्थ्यमिह कल्प्यते।
अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियं पुत्रं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “There is not the least capacity in me to sustain my life here so long as I fail to perceive my beloved son, Rāma, and the valorous Lakṣmaṇa. (20)

verses.text:
अयं हि मां दीपयतेऽद्य वह्नि-
स्तनूजशोकप्रभवो महाहितः।
महीमिमां रश्मिभिरुत्तमप्रभो
यथा निदाघे भगवान् दिवाकरः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “This fire, born of grief occasioned by separation from my son, which is exceedingly harmful to me sure enough, is torturing me today in the same way as the glorious sun, possessed of greatest splendour, scorches this earth with its rays in summer.” (21)

verses.text:
विलपन्तीं तथा तां तु कौसल्यां प्रमदोत्तमाम्।
इदं धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यं सुमित्रा वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Sumitrā, who was devoted to righteousness, addressed for her part the following words, which were in consonance with the spirit of righteousness, to the celebrated Kausalyā, the foremost of women, who had been wailing as aforesaid : (1)

verses.text:
तवार्ये सद्गुणैर्युक्तः स पुत्रः पुरुषोत्तमः।
किं ते विलपितेनैवं कृपणं रुदितेन वा॥ २॥
verses.m: “That son of yours, O noble lady, is adorned with excellent virtues and is the foremost among men. What purpose will be served by your wailing in this way or by weeping piteously? (2)

verses.text:
यस्तवार्ये गतः पुत्रस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं महाबलः।
साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानं पितरं सत्यवादिनम्॥ ३॥
शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्शश्वत् प्रेत्य फलोदये।
रामो धर्मे स्थितः श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Your noblest son, Rāma, who is possessed of great strength, O noble lady, and who, having renounced the throne, has proceeded to the forest, thereby proving his high-souled father to be perfectly truthful, is devoted to the path of virtue, which has been eternally and duly followed by the cultured and which brings its reward in the other world. As such he never deserves to be pitied. (3-4)

verses.text:
वर्तते चोत्तमां वृत्तिं लक्ष्मणोऽस्मिन् सदानघः।
दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु लाभस्तस्य महात्मनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The sinless Lakṣmaṇa, who is full of compassion to all created beings, always renders the best form of service to Rāma. Thus there is gain alone to that high-souled prince. (5)

verses.text:
अरण्यवासे यद् दुःखं जानन्त्येव सुखोचिता।
अनुगच्छति वैदेही धर्मात्मानं तवात्मजम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The daughter of the ruler of the Videhas too, who is worthy of all comfort, is following your pious-minded son, even though aware of the suffering attendant upon forest life. (6)

verses.text:
कीर्तिभूतां पताकां यो लोके भ्रमयति प्रभुः।
धर्मः सत्यव्रतपरः किं न प्राप्तस्तवात्मजः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “What blessing has not been secured by your powerful son, who is all virtue and is pledged to the vow of truthfulness, and the banner of whose fame flutters throughout the world? (7)

verses.text:
व्यक्तं रामस्य विज्ञाय शौचं माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्।
न गात्रमंशुभिः सूर्यः संतापयितुमर्हति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Fully aware of the purity, which is so well-known, as well as of the great magnanimity of Rāma, the sun ought not to scorch his person by its rays. (8)

verses.text:
शिवः सर्वेषु कालेषु काननेभ्यो विनिःसृतः।
राघवं युक्तशीतोष्णः सेविष्यति सुखोऽनिलः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “A favourable and delightful breeze of moderate heat and cold, blowing from the woods at all times, will render service to Rāma. (9)

verses.text:
शयानमनघं रात्रौ पितेवाभिपरिष्वजन्।
घर्मघ्नः संस्पृशन् शीतश्चन्द्रमा ह्लादयिष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Gently stroking him with its rays when he is reposing at night, and hugging him like a father, and driving away the heat of the day, the cool moon will exhilarate the sinless Rāma. (10)

verses.text:
ददौ चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि यस्मै ब्रह्मा महौजसे।
दानवेन्द्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा तिमिध्वजसुतं रणे॥ ११॥
स शूरः पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः।
असंत्रस्तो ह्यरण्येऽसौ वेश्मनीव निवत्स्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Relying solely on the might of his arms, that heroic prince, a veritable tiger among men—on whom, endowed with great strength, Sage Viśwāmitra, a Brāhmaṇa who vied with Brahmā in creating a world of his own, bestowed celestial missiles on seeing the demon Subāhu, son of Śambara, whose banner bore the device of a large fish, the chief of demons, killed on the battlefield by Rāma—will surely dwell undaunted in the forest as in his own palace. (11-12)

verses.text:
यस्येषुपथमासाद्य विनाशं यान्ति शत्रवः।
कथं न पृथिवी तस्य शासने स्थातुमर्हति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “How can the earth fail to obey the command of Rāma, to whose shafts the enemies fall an easy prey? (13)

verses.text:
या श्रीः शौर्यं च रामस्य या च कल्याणसत्त्वता।
निवृत्तारण्यवासः स्वं क्षिप्रं राज्यमवाप्स्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The splendour that invests Śrī Rāma, the valour that is natural to him and the beneficent strength that resides in him, lead one to believe that when the term of his exile in the forest has concluded, he will speedily regain his throne. (14)

verses.text:
सूर्यस्यापि भवेत् सूर्यो ह्यग्नेरग्निः प्रभोः प्रभुः।
श्रियाः श्रीश्च भवेदग्र्या कीर्त्याः कीर्तिः क्षमाक्षमा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Indeed he is the illuminator of the sun, which illumines the whole universe, the fire, revealer of fire, the ruler of rules, the foremost splendour of splendour, the glory, essence of glory and the forbearance, the sustaining power of forbearance. (15)

verses.text:
दैवतं देवतानां च भूतानां भूतसत्तमः।
तस्य के ह्यगुणा देवि वने वाप्यथवा पुरे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Nay, he is the god, adored of gods, the foremost being of all beings. Indeed what handicaps can there be for him in the forest or in Ayodhyā, O queen? (16)

verses.text:
पृथिव्या सह वैदेह्या श्रिया च पुरुषर्षभः।
क्षिप्रं तिसृभिरेताभिः सह रामोऽभिषेक्ष्यते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Assuredly the aforesaid Rāma, a jewel among men, will soon be installed on the throne alongwith the following three, viz, Mother Earth (a Consort of Lord Viṣṇu), Sītā (a princess of the Videha kingdom) and Śrī (the Goddess of Fortune, another Consort of Lord Viṣṇu, whom Rāma represents). (17)

verses.text:
दुःखजं विसृजत्यश्रु निष्क्रामन्तमुदीक्ष्य यम्।
अयोध्यायां जनः सर्वः शोकवेगसमाहतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Perceiving him departing (from Ayodhyā), all the people in Ayodhyā shed tears of agony, smitten as they were with an upsurge of grief. (18)

verses.text:
कुशचीरधरं वीरं गच्छन्तमपराजितम्।
सीतेवानुगता लक्ष्मीस्तस्य किं नाम दुर्लभम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Nay, Sītā, who is a compeer of Lakṣmī, followed the invincible hero even as he departed for the forest clad in a garment of the sacred Kuśa grass. Indeed what can be difficult to obtain for him? (19)

verses.text:
धनुर्ग्रहवरो यस्य बाणखड्गास्त्रभृत् स्वयम्।
लक्ष्मणो व्रजति ह्यग्रे तस्य किं नाम दुर्लभम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “In fact, what can be hard to obtain for him ahead of home indeed walks Lakṣmaṇa himself, the foremost of bowmen, wielding a sword, arrows and other missiles? (20)

verses.text:
निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्।
जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “O queen, I tell you the truth: you will be able to see Rāma come back (to Ayodhyā) on having concluded the term of his exile in the forest. Pray, abandon grief and infatuation. (21)

verses.text:
शिरसा चरणावेतौ वन्दमानमनिन्दिते।
पुनर्द्रक्ष्यसि कल्याणि पुत्रं चन्द्रमिवोदितम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “You will again see your son—as one sees the rising moon, saluting these feet of yours with his head bent low, O blessed and irreproachable lady ! (22)

verses.text:
पुनः प्रविष्टं दृष्ट्वा तमभिषिक्तं महाश्रियम्।
समुत्स्रक्ष्यसि नेत्राभ्यां शीघ्रमानन्दजं जलम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Seeing him returned to the palace and installed on the throne and invested with extraordinary splendour, you will soon begin to shed tears of joy in profusion. (23)

verses.text:
मा शोको देवि दुःखं वा न रामे दृष्यतेऽशिवम्।
क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि पुत्रं त्वं ससीतं सहलक्ष्मणम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Let there be no grief or sorrow with regard to Rāma, O queen; for no ill-luck is seen in Rāma. Nay, you will soon behold your son accompanied by Sītā and by Lakṣmaṇa. (24)

verses.text:
त्वयाऽशेषो जनश्चायं समाश्वास्यो यतोऽनघे।
किमिदानीमिदं देवि करोषि हृदि विक्लवम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Since all these people stricken with agony caused by separation from Rāma too deserve to be comforted by you, O sinless one, why do you harbour such grief in your heart at this moment, O godly lady? (25)

verses.text:
नार्हा त्वं शोचितुं देवि यस्यास्ते राघवः सुतः।
नहि रामात् परो लोके विद्यते सत्पथे स्थितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “You, O queen, whose son is Rāma, a scion of Raghu, ought not to grieve; for none is more devoted to the right path in the world than Rāma. (26)

verses.text:
अभिवादयमानं तं दृष्ट्वा ससुहृदं सुतम्।
मुदाश्रु मोक्ष्यसे क्षिप्रं मेघरेखेव वार्षिकी॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Seeing your aforesaid son greeting you with his friends, you will at once begin to shed tears through joy in the same way as a mass of monsoon clouds would pour rain. (27)

verses.text:
पुत्रस्ते वरदः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां पुनरागतः।
कराभ्यां मृदुपीनाभ्यां चरणौ पीडयिष्यति॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Returned soon to Ayodhyā, your son, who is capable of bestowing boons, will press your feet with his tender and fleshy hands. (28)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य नमस्यन्तं शूरं ससुहृदं सुतम्।
मुदास्रैः प्रोक्षसे पुत्रं मेघराजिरिवाचलम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Seeing your valiant son saluting you with his friends after accosting you with reverence, you will bathe him in tears shed through joy even as a mass of clouds would drench a mountain.” (29)

verses.text:
आश्वासयन्ती विविधैश्च वाक्यै-
र्वाक्योपचारे कुशलानवद्या।
रामस्य तां मातरमेवमुक्त्वा
देवी सुमित्रा विरराम रामा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having spoken to Śrī Rāma’s celebrated mother as aforesaid, the charming and faultless Queen Sumitrā, who was a pastmaster in eloquence and was busy consoling her through various modes of expression, became silent. (30)

verses.text:
निशम्य तल्लक्ष्मणमातृवाक्यं
रामस्य मातुर्नरदेवपत्न्याः।
सद्यः शरीरे विननाश शोकः
शरद्गतो मेघ इवाल्पतोयः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: On hearing that speech of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa’s mother, the grief that had emaciated the body of Queen Kausalyā, the mother of Śrī Rāma, quickly disappeared like an autumnal cloud containing meagre water. (31)

verses.text:
अनुरक्ता महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।
अनुजग्मुः प्रयान्तं तं वनवासाय मानवाः॥ १॥
verses.m: People devoted to the high-souled Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess followed him on his way to the forest for exile. (1)

verses.text:
निवर्तितेऽतीव बलात् सुहृद्धर्मेण राजनि।
नैव ते संन्यवर्तन्त रामस्यानुगता रथम्॥ २॥
अयोध्यानिलयानां हि पुरुषाणां महायशाः।
बभूव गुणसम्पन्नः पूर्णचन्द्र इव प्रियः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Even when the king was made to return much against his will, governed as he was by the code of conduct prescribed for friends and relations (accompanying a departing friend to some distance only), they would not return on any account and continued to follow the chariot; for Śrī Rāma, who enjoyed great celebrity and was richly endowed with excellences, had become the favourite like the full moon of the people residing in Ayodhyā. (2-3)

verses.text:
स याच्यमानः काकुत्स्थस्ताभिः प्रकृतिभिस्तदा।
कुर्वाणः पितरं सत्यं वनमेवान्वपद्यत॥ ४॥
verses.m: Even though being implored by those devoted people to return, the said Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, pressed on to the forest only, thereby proving his father to be true to his word. (4)

verses.text:
अवेक्षमाणः सस्नेहं चक्षुषा प्रपिबन्निव।
उवाच रामः सस्नेहं ताः प्रजाः स्वाः प्रजा इव॥ ५॥
verses.m: Fondly gazing on those people as though drinking them with his eyes, Śrī Rāma lovingly spoke to them as follows as though they were his own children : (5)

verses.text:
या प्रीतिर्बहुमानश्च मय्ययोध्यानिवासिनाम्।
मत्प्रियार्थं विशेषेण भरते सा विधीयताम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The love and high esteem that has been bestowed upon me by you (the inhabitants of Ayodhyā) may, for my pleasure, be bestowed in a special measure on Bharata. (6)

verses.text:
स हि कल्याणचारित्रः कैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनः।
करिष्यति यथावद् वः प्रियाणि च हितानि च॥ ७॥
verses.m: “For, Bharata, who enhances the delight of Kaikeyī and who is possessed of an excellent conduct, will properly do things which are not only pleasing but conducive to your best interests, too. (7)

verses.text:
ज्ञानवृद्धो वयोबालो मृदुर्वीर्यगुणान्वितः।
अनुरूपः स वो भर्ता भविष्यति भयापहः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Elderly in wisdom, though juvenile in age, tender though adorned with heroic qualities, he will prove to be a worthy master and will dispel your fears. (8)

verses.text:
स हि राजगुणैर्युक्तो युवराजः समीक्षितः।
अपि चापि मया शिष्टैः कार्यं वो भर्तृशासनम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Endowed as he is with kingly virtues, he has been thought fit to be the Prince Regent. For this reason too the behest of your master must be carried out by you and also because you are enjoined by me. (9)

verses.text:
न संतप्येद् यथा चासौ वनवासं गते मयि।
महाराजस्तथा कार्यो मम प्रियचिकीर्षया॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Moreover, with intent to oblige me, the said Emperor should be treated by you in such a way that he may not suffer agony when I have gone in exile to the forest.” (10)

verses.text:
यथा यथा दाशरथिर्धर्ममेवाश्रितो भवेत्।
तथा तथा प्रकृतयो रामं पतिमकामयन्॥ ११॥
verses.m: The more did Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) hold fast to righteousness in the form of obedience to his father’s wishes, the more did the people desire him to be their ruler. (11)

verses.text:
बाष्पेण पिहितं दीनं रामः सौमित्रिणा सह।
चकर्षेव गुणैर्बद्धं जनं पुरनिवासिनम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) drew, as it were, by their virtues the residents of Ayodhyā—who were afflicted and covered with tears—as though bound with cords. (12)

verses.text:
ते द्विजास्त्रिविधं वृद्धा ज्ञानेन वयसौजसा।
वयःप्रकम्पशिरसो दूरादूचुरिदं वचः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Of them such Brāhmaṇas as were senior in three ways, viz., in point of wisdom, age and power acquired through asceticism, and whose heads were shaking under the weight of senility, spoke from a distance as follows, unable as they were to keep pace with the chariot of Śrī Rāma: (13)

verses.text:
वहन्तो जवना रामं भो भो जात्यास्तुरंगमाः।
निवर्तध्वं न गन्तव्यं हिता भवत भर्तरि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Return, O swift steeds of excellent breed drawing the chariot conveying Śrī Rāma, and be friendly to your master, since by taking Śrī Rāma against our wishes you will be doing a disservice to him; you ought not to proceed further. (14)

verses.text:
कर्णवन्ति हि भूतानि विशेषेण तुरङ्गमाः।
यूयं तस्मान्निवर्तध्वं याचनां प्रतिवेदिताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Indeed all created beings which are endowed with ears, more so horses, stand apprised of our entreaty. Therefore, please return. (15)

verses.text:
धर्मतः स विशुद्धात्मा वीरः शुभदृढव्रतः।
उपवाह्यस्तु वो भर्ता नापवाह्यः पुराद् वनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The said master of yours is exceedingly pure-minded, heroic and a man of virtuous and firm resolve. As such he justly deserves to be conveyed by you nearer the city and not to be carried away from the city to the forest.” (16)

verses.text:
एवमार्तप्रलापांस्तान् वृद्धान् प्रलपतो द्विजान्।
अवेक्ष्य सहसा रामो रथादवततार ह॥ १७॥
verses.m: Perceiving those aged Brāhmaṇas uttering such plaintive words, Śrī Rāma precipitately got down from the chariot: so the tradition goes. (17)

verses.text:
पद्भ्यामेव जगामाथ ससीतः सहलक्ष्मणः।
संनिकृष्टपदन्यासो रामो वनपरायणः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Taking close strides in order to enable the aged Brāhmaṇas to overtake him, Śrī Rāma now proceeded on foot with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa in the direction of the forest, which constituted his final destination (without stopping or receding to meet and console the Brāhmaṇas since that would amount to a breach of the vow undertaken by him to depart for the forest). (18)

verses.text:
द्विजातीन् हि पदातींस्तान् रामश्चारित्रवत्सलः।
न शशाक घृणाचक्षुः परिमोक्तुं रथेन सः॥ १९॥
verses.m: For, the said Śrī Rāma, who was affectionate by disposition and had compassion in his eyes, could not send back those Brāhmaṇas walking on foot while continuing to be in the chariot himself. (19)

verses.text:
गच्छन्तमेव तं दृष्ट्वा रामं सम्भ्रान्तमानसाः।
ऊचुः परमसंतप्ता रामं वाक्यमिदं द्विजाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Perplexed in mind, nay, sore distressed to see the celebrated Śrī Rāma still pressing on, the Brāhmaṇas spoke to him as follows : (20)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मण्यं कृत्स्नमेतत् त्वां ब्रह्मण्यमनुगच्छति।
द्विजस्कन्धाधिरूढास्त्वामग्नयोऽप्यनुयान्त्वमी ॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The whole of this Brāhmaṇa community is following you, devoted as you are to the Brahmaṇas. Nay, borne on the shoulders of the Brāhmaṇs through the medium of the two pieces of wood used for kindling the fire by attrition and the vessel intended for holding it, these sacred fires too are following them. (21)

verses.text:
वाजपेयसमुत्थानि च्छत्राण्येतानि पश्य नः।
पृष्ठतोऽनुप्रयातानि मेघानिव जलात्यये॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Pray, look at these canopies* obtained by us during the performance of a Vājapeya sacrifice and following at your heels like white clouds appearing in autumn, marking the end of the monsoon. (22)

verses.text:
अनवाप्तातपत्रस्य रश्मिसंतापितस्य ते।
एभिश्छायां करिष्यामः स्वैश्छत्रैर्वाजपेयकैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “With these canopies of ours, obtained during a Vājapeya sacrifice, we shall give shade to you, who have got no canopy and as such are being scorched with rays of the sun. (23)

verses.text:
या हि नः सततं बुद्धिर्वेदमन्त्रानुसारिणी।
त्वत्कृते सा कृता वत्स वनवासानुसारिणी॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Indeed that mind of ours, which was heretofore engaged in pursuing the study of Vedic texts, has now been made to follow the course of exile to the forest for your sake, O darling ! (24)

verses.text:
हृदयेष्ववतिष्ठन्ते वेदा ये नः परं धनम्।
वत्स्यन्त्यपि गृहेष्वेव दाराश्चारित्ररक्षिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The Vedas, which constitute our supreme riches, stand preserved in our hearts (memory); and protected by their character, our consorts too will continue to stay in our homes alone. We need not, therefore, be deterred by any anxiety on their score. (25)

verses.text:
पुनर्न निश्चयः कार्यस्त्वद्गतौ सुकृता मतिः।
त्वयि धर्मव्यपेक्षे तु किं स्याद् धर्मपथे स्थितम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “No decision need be taken by us on the matter afresh, since our mind is fully determined to follow you to the forest. Yet we should like to tell you that in the event of your turning indifferent to piety (in the form of listening to the advice of Brāhmaṇas), what being will remain devoted to the path of virtue? (26)

verses.text:
याचितो नो निवर्तस्व हंसशुक्लशिरोरुहैः।
शिरोभिर्निभृताचार महीपतनपांसुलैः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Solicited by us with our heads bent low, heads which are covered with hair white as the down of swans and are soiled with dust as a result of their falling on the ground (in the course of our prostration to you, whom we know to be none other than Lord Viṣṇu)—pray, turn back, O prince resolute of conduct ! (27)

verses.text:
बहूनां वितता यज्ञा द्विजानां य इहागताः।
तेषां समाप्तिरायत्ता तव वत्स निवर्तने॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Sacrifices have been started by many of those Brāhmaṇas that have come here, to follow you. Their conclusion, O darling, depends on your return. (28)

verses.text:
भक्तिमन्तीह भूतानि जङ्गमाजङ्गमानि च।
याचमानेषु तेषु त्वं भक्तिं भक्तेषु दर्शय॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Nay, all created beings—both inanimate and animate—here are full of devotion to you. Pray, show your affection to such devotees, who are imploring you to return by acceding to their request. (29)

verses.text:
अनुगन्तुमशक्तास्त्वां मूलैरुद्धतवेगिनः।
उन्नता वायुवेगेन विक्रोशन्तीव पादपाः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Tall trees, whose power of locomotion stands completely hampered by their roots penetrating deep into the earth and which are, therefore, unable to follow you, are crying, as it were, through the creaking sound produced by the force of wind, and thus asking you to return. (30)

verses.text:
निश्चेष्टाहारसंचारा वृक्षैकस्थाननिश्चिताः।
पक्षिणोऽपि प्रयाचन्ते सर्वभूतानुकम्पिनम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Birds too, which sit motionless and are unable to go out in search of food and which remain fixed to one spot on the boughs of trees, solicit you to return, compassionate as you are to all created beings.” (31)

verses.text:
एवं विक्रोशतां तेषां द्विजातीनां निवर्तने।
ददृशे तमसा तत्र वारयन्तीव राघवम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: While the aforesaid Brāhmaṇas were crying thus with a view to persuading Śrī Rāma to return, the river Tamasā came to view as though retarding the progress of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (32)

verses.text:
ततः सुमन्त्रोऽपि रथाद् विमुच्य
श्रान्तान् हयान् सम्परिवर्त्य शीघ्रम्।
पीतोदकांस्तोयपरिप्लुताङ्गा-
नचारयद् वै तमसाविदूरे॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Releasing the horses, fatigued as they were, from the chariot and quickly making them roll afterwards, Sumantra too allowed them to graze not very far from the bank of the Tamasā once they had drunk water and had their body washed in the river. (33)

verses.text:
ततस्तु तमसातीरं रम्यमाश्रित्य राघवः।
सीतामुद्वीक्ष्य सौमित्रिमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Then, taking his stand on the delightful bank of the Tamasā and gazing on Sītā, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, as follows : (1)

verses.text:
इयमद्य निशा पूर्वा सौमित्रे प्रहिता वनम्।
वनवासस्य भद्रं ते न चोत्कण्ठितुमर्हसि॥ २॥
verses.m: “Today, O Lakṣmaṇa, is the very first night of our exile in the forest. And since it is to the forest that we have been sent away, you ought not to feel anxious for those that have been left behind; may all be well with you ! (2)

verses.text:
पश्य शून्यान्यरण्यानि रुदन्तीव समन्ततः।
यथानिलयमायद्भिर्निलीनानि मृगद्विजैः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Look here: sought for shelter by beasts and birds retiring to their respective abode, the desolate woods are crying, as it were, on all sides. (3)

verses.text:
अद्यायोध्या तु नगरी राजधानी पितुर्मम।
सस्त्रीपुंसा गतानस्मान् शोचिष्यति न संशयः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The city of Ayodhyā, the capital of my father, King Daśaratha, with its men and women will for its part lament today for us three, that have departed for the forest: there is no doubt about it. (4)

verses.text:
अनुरक्ता हि मनुजा राजानं बहुभिर्गुणैः।
त्वां च मां च नरव्याघ्र शत्रुघ्नभरतौ तथा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “For, the people of Ayodhyā are devoted to the king no less than to you and myself, as also to Bharata and Śatrughna, for our manifold virtues, O tiger among men ! (5)

verses.text:
पितरं चानुशोचामि मातरं च यशस्विनीम्।
अपि नान्धौ भवेतां नौ रुदन्तौ तावभीक्ष्णशः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I bewail the lot of my father as well as my illustrious mother, Kausalyā. I fear lest those parents of ours, who must be incessantly weeping, should be deprived of their eyesight. (6)

verses.text:
भरतः खलु धर्मात्मा पितरं मातरं च मे।
धर्मार्थकामसहितैर्वाक्यैराश्वासयिष्यति ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I am sure that the pious-minded Bharata will console my father and mother by means of words assuring them of religious merit, material welfare and sense-gratification. (7)

verses.text:
भरतस्यानृशंसत्वं संचिन्त्याहं पुनः पुनः।
नानुशोचामि पितरं मातरं च महाभुज॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Reflecting again and again on the tender-heartedness of Bharata, O mighty-armed prince, I do not lament for my father and mother. (8)

verses.text:
त्वया कार्यं नरव्याघ्र मामनुव्रजता कृतम्।
अन्वेष्टव्या हि वैदेह्या रक्षणार्थं सहायता॥ ९॥
verses.m: “By following me to the forest, O tiger among men, a great purpose of mine has been served by you; for, otherwise aid would have to be sought for by me for looking after Sītā (a princess of the Videha kingdom). (9)

verses.text:
अद्भिरेव हि सौमित्रे वत्स्याम्यद्य निशामिमाम्।
एतद्धि रोचते मह्यं वन्येऽपि विविधे सति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I shall certainly live on water alone tonight, O son of Sumitrā ! Although there are various kinds of wild fruits and roots, this alone pleases me.” (10)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सौमित्रिं सुमन्त्रमपि राघवः।
अप्रमत्तस्त्वमश्वेषु भव सौम्येत्युवाच ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having told Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) as above, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, so the tradition goes, spoke to Sumantra too as follows : “Attend you to the horses now, O good sir !” (11)

verses.text:
सोऽश्वान् सुमन्त्रः संयम्य सूर्येऽस्तं समुपागते।
प्रभूतयवसान् कृत्वा बभूव प्रत्यनन्तरः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Fastening the horses tightly, the sun having completely set, and supplying them with abundant grass, the said Sumantra returned to the presence of Śrī Rāma. (12)

verses.text:
उपास्य तु शिवां संध्यां दृष्ट्वा रात्रिमुपागताम्।
रामस्य शयनं चक्रे सूतः सौमित्रिणा सह॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having worshipped the goddess presiding over the benign evening twilight (according to his grade in society) and seeing the night fallen, the charioteer alongwith Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, prepared a ground suitable for Śrī Rāma to sleep on (by brushing aside gravel and particles of dust etc.) as well as a bed of leaves. (13)

verses.text:
तां शय्यां तमसातीरे वीक्ष्य वृक्षदलैर्वृताम्।
रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सभार्यः संविवेश ह॥ १४॥
verses.m: Perceiving the aforesaid bed overspread by Sumantra with fresh leaves of trees on the bank of the Tamasā with the help of Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), Śrī Rāma with his consort lay down on it: so they say. (14)

verses.text:
सभार्यं सम्प्रसुप्तं तु श्रान्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः।
कथयामास सूताय रामस्य विविधान् गुणान्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Observing Śrī Rāma buried in deep sleep with his spouse, fatigued as he was, Lakṣmaṇa for his part began to recount the various virtues of Śrī Rāma before the charioteer. (15)

verses.text:
जाग्रतोरेव तां रात्रिं सौमित्रेरुदितो रविः।
सूतस्य तमसातीरे रामस्य ब्रुवतो गुणान्॥ १६॥
verses.m: The sun rose past Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) even as he was recounting to the charioteer on the bank of the Tamasā the excellences of Śrī Rāma, both Lakṣmaṇa and Sumantra keeping awake the whole of that night. (16)

verses.text:
गोकुलाकुलतीरायास्तमसाया विदूरतः।
अवसत् तत्र तां रात्रिं रामः प्रकृतिभिः सह॥ १७॥
verses.m: At a respectable distance from the Tamasā, whose bank was crowded with herds of cows, Śrī Rāma spent that night with the citizens on the aforesaid stretch of land. (17)

verses.text:
उत्थाय च महातेजाः प्रकृतीस्ता निशाम्य च।
अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं पुण्यलक्षणम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Getting up from the bed and seeing those people lying at some distance, Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of extraordinary splendour, spoke as follows to his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks : (18)

verses.text:
अस्मद्व्यपेक्षान् सौमित्रे निर्व्यपेक्षान् गृहेष्वपि।
वृक्षमूलेषु संसक्तान् पश्य लक्ष्मण साम्प्रतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa, the citizens, full of great longing for us and absolutely unmindful of their homes as also of their near and dear ones, lying close to the roots of trees till this late hour, O son of Sumitrā ! (19)

verses.text:
यथैते नियमं पौराः कुर्वन्त्यस्मन्निवर्तने।
अपि प्राणान् न्यसिष्यन्ति न तु त्यक्ष्यन्ति निश्चयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “From the way in which these citizens are taking pains to take us back to Ayodhyā, it seems they will even lay down their lives but would in no case give up their resolve. (20)

verses.text:
यावदेव तु संसुप्तास्तावदेव वयं लघु।
रथमारुह्य गच्छामः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्॥ २१॥
अतो भूयोऽपि नेदानीमिक्ष्वाकुपुरवासिनः।
स्वपेयुरनुरक्ता मा वृक्षमूलेषु संश्रिताः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, while they are fast asleep let us in the meantime quickly mount the chariot and take a route which has no fear of molestation from any quarter, so that the citizens of Ayodhyā, the ancient capital of Ikṣwāku, who are so keenly devoted to me, may not henceforth have to repose leaning against the roots of trees as now. (21-22)

verses.text:
पौरा ह्यात्मकृताद् दुःखाद् विप्रमोच्या नृपात्मजैः।
न तु खल्वात्मना योज्या दुःखेन पुरवासिनः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The residents of a city ruled over by a king should indeed be completely and finally rid by the sons of their rulers of suffering brought about by the citizens themselves. The citizens should on no account be burdened with affliction caused by the princes themselves, as in our case.” (23)

verses.text:
अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणो रामं साक्षाद् धर्ममिव स्थितम्।
रोचते मे तथा प्राज्ञ क्षिप्रमारुह्यतामिति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Lakṣmaṇa replied as follows to Śrī Rāma, who was firm as virtue incarnate : “What you say appeals to me, O wise brother; pray, ascend the chariot quickly.” (24)

verses.text:
अथ रामोऽब्रवीत् सूतं शीघ्रं संयुज्यतां रथः।
गमिष्यामि ततोऽरण्यं गच्छ शीघ्रमितः प्रभो॥ २५॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma then said to the charioteer, “Please get the chariot ready soon. On it I shall proceed to the forest. Depart from this place at once, my Revered !” (25)

verses.text:
सूतस्ततः संत्वरितः स्यन्दनं तैर्हयोत्तमैः।
योजयित्वा तु रामस्य प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्यवेदयत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Having got the chariot ready with those excellent horses yoked to it with great expedition, the charioteer for his part thereupon submitted as follows with folded hands to Śrī Rāma : (26)

verses.text:
अयं युक्तो महाबाहो रथस्ते रथिनां वर।
त्वरयाऽऽरोह भद्रं ते ससीतः सहलक्ष्मणः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Here is your chariot ready, O mighty-armed prince ! Pray, ascend it quickly with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, O jewel among chariot-warriors; may prosperity attend you !” (27)

verses.text:
तं स्यन्दनमधिष्ठाय राघवः सपरिच्छदः।
शीघ्रगामाकुलावर्तां तमसामतरन्नदीम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Mounting the aforesaid chariot with all necessaries for travelling (viz., his bow, armour, quiver, spade, basket and so on), Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, speedily crossed thereby the swift-flowing Tamasā, thickly set with eddies. (28)

verses.text:
स संतीर्य महाबाहुः श्रीमान् शिवमकण्टकम्।
प्रापद्यत महामार्गमभयं भयदर्शिनाम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having duly crossed the stream, the glorious Śrī Rāma (who was possessed of mighty arms) reached a smooth road, free from obstacles and safe even for those who are apprehensive of danger. (29)

verses.text:
मोहनार्थं तु पौराणां सूतं रामोऽब्रवीद् वचः।
उदङ्मुखः प्रयाहि त्वं रथमारुह्य सारथे॥ ३०॥
मुहूर्तं त्वरितं गत्वा निवर्तय रथं पुनः।
यथा न विद्युः पौरा मां तथा कुरु समाहितः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: With a view to putting the citizens off the scent, Śrī Rāma for his part spoke to the charioteer as follows : “Mounting the chariot alone, O charioteer, proceed you northward and, going apace awhile, bring the chariot back again. Remaining careful, drive the chariot in such a way that the citizens may not be able to locate me.” (30-31)

verses.text:
रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे च सारथिः।
प्रत्यागम्य च रामस्य स्यन्दनं प्रत्यवेदयत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, the said charioteer for his part did as he was told and, returning by a different route reported to Śrī Rāma the arrival of the chariot. (32)

verses.text:
तौ सम्प्रयुक्तं तु रथं समास्थितौ
तदा ससीतौ रघुवंशवर्धनौ।
प्रचोदयामास ततस्तुरंगमान्
