स सारथिर्येन पथा तपोवनम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Then Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa (the promoters of the race of Raghu) for their part alongwith Sītā comfortably took their seats in the chariot, which was duly kept ready by the charioteer for their use. The said charioteer thereupon urged the horses along the route by which they could reach a forest suited to the practice of austerities. (33)

verses.text:
ततः समास्थाय रथं महारथः
ससारथिर्दाशरथिर्वनं ययौ।
उदङ्मुखं तं तु रथं चकार
प्रयाणमाङ्गल्यनिमित्तदर्शनात् ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: At the outset, however, the charioteer placed the chariot facing the north; for he saw omens auspicious for journey in that quarter. Having duly occupied the chariot, Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who was a great car-warrior, thereupon proceeded to the forest alongwith the charioteer. (34)

verses.text:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पौरास्ते राघवं विना।
शोकोपहतनिश्चेष्टा बभूवुर्हतचेतसः॥ १॥
verses.m: The night having ended in dawn, the aforesaid citizens, who were stunned with grief, became unconscious, as it were. (1)

verses.text:
शोकजाश्रुपरिद्यूना वीक्षमाणास्ततस्ततः।
आलोकमपि रामस्य न पश्यन्ति स्म दुःखिताः॥ २॥
verses.m: Made miserable by tears born of grief and full of agony, they could not catch even a glimpse of Śrī Rāma, though casting their eyes all round. (2)

verses.text:
ते विषादार्तवदना रहितास्तेन धीमता।
कृपणाः करुणा वाचो वदन्ति स्म मनीषिणः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Their faces withered through despondency, deprived as they were of Śrī Rāma who was full of wisdom, and, therefore, non-plussed, the citizens, even though they were wise, uttered plaintive words as follows : (3)

verses.text:
धिगस्तु खलु निद्रां तां ययापहतचेतसः।
नाद्य पश्यामहे रामं पृथूरस्कं महाभुजम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Woe indeed be to that slumber, rendered unconscious by which we could not perceive today Śrī Rāma, who is distinguished by a broad chest and mighty arms ! (4)

verses.text:
कथं रामो महाबाहुः स तथावितथक्रियः।
भक्तं जनमभित्यज्य प्रवासं तापसो गतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “How did that mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, whose actions, as is well known, are never ineffectual, leave for other lands in the garb of an ascetic, abandoning us, his devoted subjects? (5)

verses.text:
यो नः सदा पालयति पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्।
कथं रघूणां स श्रेष्ठस्त्यक्त्वा नो विपिनं गतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “How did that jewel among the Raghus, who ever protected us as a father does his own children, proceed to the forest abandoning us? (6)

verses.text:
इहैव निधनं याम महाप्रस्थानमेव वा।
रामेण रहितानां नो किमर्थं जीवितं हितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Let us meet our end at this very place by fasting or definitely set out on the grand journey to the north with a resolve to die. For what purpose can life be good for us, deprived as we are of Śrī Rāma? (7)

verses.text:
सन्ति शुष्काणि काष्ठानि प्रभूतानि महान्ति च।
तैः प्रज्वाल्य चितां सर्वे प्रविशामोऽथवा वयम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Or, there are any number of big logs of dry wood here. Lighting a funeral pile, let us all enter the fire together. (8)

verses.text:
किं वक्ष्यामो महाबाहुरनसूयः प्रियंवदः।
नीतः स राघवोऽस्माभिरिति वक्तुं कथं क्षमम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Shall we break the news when asked by those left behind in Ayodhyā that Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) of mighty arms, who is free from jealousy and speaks kindly to all, has been conveyed to the forest by us? How can such words be uttered by us? (9)

verses.text:
सा नूनं नगरी दीना दृष्ट्वास्मान् राघवं विना।
भविष्यति निरानन्दा सस्त्रीबालवयोऽधिका॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Seeing us back without Śrī Rāma, that city of Ayodhyā will surely assume a wretched and cheerless aspect with its womenfolk, children and elderly people. (10)

verses.text:
निर्यातास्तेन वीरेण सह नित्यं महात्मना।
विहीनास्तेन च पुनः कथं द्रक्ष्याम तां पुरीम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “How shall we, who went out with that high-souled hero for good, can behold that city again without him?” (11)

verses.text:
इतीव बहुधा वाचो बाहुमुद्यम्य ते जनाः।
विलपन्ति स्म दुःखार्ता हृतवत्सा इवाग्र्यगाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Holding up their arms, the above-mentioned men, who were stricken with agony like cows of excellent breed, bereft of their calf, lamented in various ways as above. (12)

verses.text:
ततो मार्गानुसारेण गत्वा किंचित् ततः क्षणम्।
मार्गनाशाद् विषादेन महता समभिप्लुताः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Then proceeding to some distance along the tracks, left by Śrī Rāma’s chariot for some moments, they were overwhelmed with great despondency, the tracks having disappeared immediately afterwards due to the chariot having returned by another route. (13)

verses.text:
रथमार्गानुसारेण न्यवर्तन्त मनस्विनः।
किमिदं किं करिष्यामो दैवेनोपहता इति॥ १४॥
verses.m: The high-minded citizens eventually returned to Ayodhyā along the tracks left by the chariot while leaving Ayodhyā, saying “How is it that the tracks have disappeared so soon? What shall we do? We are doomed by Providence.” (14)

verses.text:
तदा यथागतेनैव मार्गेण क्लान्तचेतसः।
अयोध्यामगमन् सर्वे पुरीं व्यथितसज्जनाम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Depressed in spirits, they all then returned by the same route along which they had come, to the city of Ayodhyā, where all good people were feeling distressed. (15)

verses.text:
आलोक्य नगरीं तां च क्षयव्याकुलमानसाः।
आवर्तयन्त तेऽश्रूणि नयनैः शोकपीडितैः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Nay, seeing the city which presented a sorry spectacle, they shed tears in profusion through their eyes tormented with grief, their mind distracted through cheerlessness. (16)

verses.text:
एषा रामेण नगरी रहिता नातिशोभते।
आपगा गरुडेनेव ह्रदादुद्धृतपन्नगा॥ १७॥
verses.m: Bereft of Śrī Rāma, the aforesaid city of Ayodhyā did not look any more charming than a river whose snakes have been uprooted from its deep pool by Garuḍa. (17)

verses.text:
चन्द्रहीनमिवाकाशं तोयहीनमिवार्णवम्।
अपश्यन् निहतानन्दं नगरं ते विचेतसः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Those bewildered men beheld the city joyless like the firmament bereft of the moon and an ocean without water. (18)

verses.text:
ते तानि वेश्मानि महाधनानि
दुःखेन दुःखोपहता विशन्तः।
नैव प्रजग्मुः स्वजनं परं वा
निरीक्ष्यमाणाः प्रविनष्टहर्षाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Entering their dwellings full of abundant riches with difficulty, the citizens could not distinguish between their own people and others, though casting their eyes all round, stricken as they were with sorrow, their joy having altogether disappeared for good. (19)

verses.text:
तेषामेवं विषण्णानां पीडितानामतीव च।
बाष्पविप्लुतनेत्राणां सशोकानां मुमूर्षया॥ १॥
अभिगम्य निवृत्तानां रामं नगरवासिनाम्।
उद्गतानीव सत्त्वानि बभूवुरमनस्विनाम्॥ २॥
verses.m: The life of those citizens who had returned dejected and dispirited in this way even after meeting Śrī Rāma, and felt sore afflicted—full of grief as they were and seized with a longing to give up the ghost, their eyes overflowing with tears—became extinct, as it were. (1-2)

verses.text:
स्वं स्वं निलयमागम्य पुत्रदारैः समावृताः।
अश्रूणि मुमुचुः सर्वे बाष्पेण पिहिताननाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Reaching each his own abode and surrounded by their sons and wife, all shed tears, their face being covered with them. (3)

verses.text:
न चाहृष्यन् न चामोदन् वणिजो न प्रसारयन्।
न चाशोभन्त पण्यानि नापचन् गृहमेधिनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: People neither made merry nor did they rejoice. Merchants did not spread their merchandise, nor did the saleable goods (spread by them) look charming. Nor, again, did the householders cook their food at their home. (4)

verses.text:
नष्टं दृष्ट्वा नाभ्यनन्दन् विपुलं वा धनागमम्।
पुत्रं प्रथमजं लब्ध्वा जननी नाप्यनन्दत॥ ५॥
verses.m: The people of Ayodhyā did not rejoice to recover their lost property or to receive a large (additional) fortune. Nor did a mother rejoice to meet her first-born male issue. (5)

verses.text:
गृहे गृहे रुदत्यश्च भर्तारं गृहमागतम्।
व्यगर्हयन्त दुःखार्ता वाग्भिस्तोत्त्रैरिव द्विपान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Stricken with sorrow not to find Śrī Rāma back in Ayodhyā and shedding tears, women in every house sharply reproached (in the following words) their husband returned home without Śrī Rāma even as the drivers of elephants would prick them with goads : (6)

verses.text:
किं नु तेषां गृहैः कार्यं किं दारैः किं धनेन वा।
पुत्रैर्वापि सुखैर्वापि ये न पश्यन्ति राघवम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “What purpose of theirs who do not behold Śrī Rāma will be served by their dwellings, wife or even riches or even sons or even pleasures? (7)

verses.text:
एकः सत्पुरुषो लोके लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया।
योऽनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थं रामं परिचरन् वने॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The only virtuous man in this world is Lakṣmaṇa, who with Sītā has followed Śrī Rāma, rendering service to him in the forest. (8)

verses.text:
आपगाः कृतपुण्यास्ताः पद्मिन्यश्च सरांसि च।
येषु यास्यति काकुत्स्थो विगाह्य सलिलं शुचि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Fortunate too are those rivers, lotus-ponds and lakes, bathing in whose sacred waters Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, will proceed further ! (9)

verses.text:
शोभयिष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमटव्यो रम्यकाननाः।
आपगाश्च महानूपाः सानुमन्तश्च पर्वताः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Forests with delightful rows of trees, as well as rivers, tracts of land abounding in water and mountains with beautiful peaks will adorn the presence of Śrī Rāma. (10)

verses.text:
काननं वापि शैलं वा यं रामोऽनुगमिष्यति।
प्रियातिथिमिव प्राप्तं नैनं शक्ष्यन्त्यनर्चितुम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The forest or mountain which Śrī Rāma will visit will not fail to honour him like a beloved guest arrived near. (11)

verses.text:
विचित्रकुसुमापीडा बहुमञ्जरिधारिणः।
राघवं दर्शयिष्यन्ति नगा भ्रमरशालिनः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Trees crowned with flowers of various kinds and bearing numerous bunches of flowers and adorned with black bees will appear before Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). (12)

verses.text:
अकाले चापि मुख्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च।
दर्शयिष्यन्त्यनुक्रोशाद् गिरयो राममागतम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Out of regard mountains will display before Śrī Rāma as he visits them excellent blossoms and fruits, too, even out of season. (13)

verses.text:
प्रस्रविष्यन्ति तोयानि विमलानि महीधराः।
विदर्शयन्तो विविधान् भूयश्चित्रांश्च निर्झरान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Bringing to light picturesque cascades of various kinds, mountains will further release crystal clear waters. (14)

verses.text:
पादपाः पर्वताग्रेषु रमयिष्यन्ति राघवम्।
यत्र रामो भयं नात्र नास्ति तत्र पराभवः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Trees standing on mountain-tops will afford delight to Śrī Rāma. And there is no cause for fear where Śrī Rāma is, nor is there any occasion for humiliation. (15)

verses.text:
स हि शूरो महाबाहुः पुत्रो दशरथस्य च।
पुरा भवति नोऽदूरादनुगच्छाम राघवम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “That heroic and mighty-armed son of Daśaratha will surely come to our view not far from this place. Let us once more follow Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (16)

verses.text:
पादच्छाया सुखं भर्तुस्तादृशस्य महात्मनः।
स हि नाथो जनस्यास्य स गतिः स परायणम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The shelter of the feet of such a high-souled master, as Śrī Rāma is, is our only joy; in fact he is the protector of us all; he is our goal, he is our supreme asylum. (17)

verses.text:
वयं परिचरिष्यामः सीतां यूयं च राघवम्।
इति पौरस्त्रियोभर्तॄन् दुःखार्तास्तत्तदब्रुवन्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “We shall attend on Sītā, while you shall serve Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu).” In so many words did the citizens’ wives, stricken with agony, address their husbands. (18)

verses.text:
युष्माकं राघवोऽरण्ये योगक्षेमं विधास्यति।
सीता नारीजनस्यास्य योगक्षेमं करिष्यति॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu),” (they continued,) will satisfy your needs and safeguard your interests in the forest, while Sītā will do the same thing with regard to us, the womenfolk. (19)

verses.text:
को न्वनेनाप्रतीतेन सोत्कण्ठितजनेन च।
सम्प्रीयेतामनोज्ञेन वासेन हृतचेतसा॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Who can possibly remain highly pleased with residence in this city, which is not commendable in any way—much less agreeable to the mind, the people here being full of longing for the return of Śrī Rāma—and by which the mind gets unsettled? (20)

verses.text:
कैकेय्या यदि चेद् राज्यं स्यादधर्म्यमनाथवत्।
न हि नो जीवितेनार्थः कुतः पुत्रैः कुतो धनैः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “If there comes to be the rule of Kaikeyī, which will not be in consonance with righteousness and which will be as good as without a protector, surely no use will be left for our life, much less for our sons and riches. (21)

verses.text:
यया पुत्रश्च भर्ता च त्यक्तावैश्वर्यकारणात्।
कं सा परिहरेदन्यं कैकेयी कुलपांसनी॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Whom else would that Kaikeyī—who has brought disgrace to her family and by whom her (step-) son and husband too have been forsaken for the sake of power—not abandon? (22)

verses.text:
कैकेय्या न वयं राज्ये भृतका हि वसेमहि।
जीवन्त्या जातु जीवन्त्यः पुत्रैरपि शपामहे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “We swear by our sons that so long as we breathe we can under no circumstances live in the kingdom of Kaikeyī, till she is alive, even though we may be supported by her. (23)

verses.text:
या पुत्रं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य प्रवासयति निर्घृणा।
कस्तां प्राप्य सुखं जीवेदधर्म्यां दुष्टचारिणीम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Who can live happily on having obtained as one’s sovereign that impious woman of wicked conduct who has sent into exile Prince Rāma (son of Daśaratha, a ruler of rulers), merciless as she is? (24)

verses.text:
उपद्रुतमिदं सर्वमनालम्भमनायकम्।
कैकेय्यास्तु कृते सर्वं विनाशमुपयास्यति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The whole of this kingdom is soon going to be deprived of its ruler; it will no longer have any sacrificial performances and will be visited by calamities. Nay, thanks to Kaikeyī, everything will meet with ruination. (25)

verses.text:
नहि प्रव्रजिते रामे जीविष्यति महीपतिः।
मृते दशरथे व्यक्तं विलोपस्तदनन्तरम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “For, Śrī Rāma having gone into exile, the Emperor will not survive and when Daśaratha is dead, destruction will be the fate of the distinguished kingdom which has run an uninterrupted course ever since the time of Ikṣwāku. (26)

verses.text:
ते विषं पिबतालोड्य क्षीणपुण्याः सुदुःखिताः।
राघवं वानुगच्छध्वमश्रुतिं वापि गच्छत॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Therefore drink poison mixing it with water, sore distressed as you are, the stock of your merit having been exhausted; or follow Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) to the forest or leave for some land where even the name of Kaikeyī may not reach your ears. (27)

verses.text:
मिथ्याप्रव्राजितो रामः सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः।
भरते संनिबद्धाः स्मः सौनिके पशवो यथा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, alongwith his consort, Sītā, and with Lakṣmaṇa, his younger brother, has been deceitfully sent into exile and we have been tied firm to the apron-strings of Bharata in the same way as animals are bound tightly together (for being slaughtered) in a shambles. (28)

verses.text:
पूर्णचन्द्राननः श्यामो गूढजत्रुररिंदमः।
आजानुबाहुः पद्माक्षो रामो लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः॥ २९॥
पूर्वाभिभाषी मधुरः सत्यवादी महाबलः।
सौम्यश्च सर्वलोकस्य चन्द्रवत् प्रियदर्शनः॥ ३०॥
नूनं पुरुषशार्दूलो मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः।
शोभयिष्यत्यरण्यानि विचरन् स महारथः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: That lotus-eyed great chariot-warrior, Śrī Rāma, elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa—a tiger among men and a subduer of foes—who is dark-brown of complexion and has a countenance resembling the full moon, nay whose collar-bone is invisible (because of its being covered with flesh), whose arms extend up to the knees, who takes the initiative in speaking, is sweet of expression, truthful of speech and possessed of extraordinary might, is easy of address to all people and is delightful of aspect as the moon, and whose gait resembles that of an elephant in rut, will surely adorn the woods while roaming through them.” (29—31)

verses.text:
तास्तथा विलपन्त्यस्तु नगरे नागरस्त्रियः।
चुक्रुशुर्दुःखसंतप्ता मृत्योरिव भयागमे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Lamenting thus in the city of Ayodhyā, the aforesaid wives of citizens, for their part, cried as one would do at the approach of some danger foreboding death, tormented as they were with agony. (32)

verses.text:
इत्येवं विलपन्तीनां स्त्रीणां वेश्मसु राघवम्।
जगामास्तं दिनकरो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत॥ ३३॥
verses.m: The sun sank below the horizon past these women,who had been mourning as aforesaid in their homes for Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), and the night fell. (33)

verses.text:
नष्टज्वलनसंतापा प्रशान्ताध्यायसत्कथा।
तिमिरेणानुलिप्तेव तदा सा नगरी बभौ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: The city of Ayodhyā in which the kindling of fires even for the purposes of Agnihotra had ceased and the chanting of the Vedas and the narration of sacred stories relating to the Purāṇas died out, looked as though coated with darkness at that time. (34)

verses.text:
उपशान्तवणिक्पण्या नष्टहर्षा निराश्रया।
अयोध्या नगरी चासीन्नष्टतारमिवाम्बरम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The city of Ayodhyā—in which the business of the trading class had been brought to a standstill and whose joy had gone, nay, which had now become supportless, looked dark as the sky in which the stars had disappeared. (35)

verses.text:
तदा स्त्रियो रामनिमित्तमातुरा
यथा सुते भ्रातरि वा विवासिते।
विलप्य दीना रुरुदुर्विचेतसः
सुतैर्हि तासामधिकोऽपि सोऽभवत्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Giving expression to their grief in various ways on that occasion, the women of Ayodhyā, who were sick of mind on account of Śrī Rāma, as one would feel on one’s own son or brother having been sent into exile, cried miserably and fell unconscious; for Śrī Rāma was dearer to them than their very sons. (36)

verses.text:
प्रशान्तगीतोत्सवनृत्यवादना
विभ्रष्टहर्षा पिहितापणोदया।
तदा ह्ययोध्या नगरी बभूव सा
महार्णवः संक्षपितोदको यथा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The celebrated city of Ayodhyā—in which all singing, rejoicing, dancing and instrumental music had been completely set at rest, whose delight had fled forever and the steady rise of whose trade had been hampered—looked at that time like an ocean whose waters had dried up. (37)

verses.text:
रामोऽपि रात्रिशेषेण तेनैव महदन्तरम्।
जगाम पुरुषव्याघ्रः पितुराज्ञामनुस्मरन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Revolving in his mind the command of his father, Śrī Rāma too, a tiger among men, covered a long distance in the course of the remaining hours of the night itself. (1)

verses.text:
तथैव गच्छतस्तस्य व्यपायाद् रजनी शिवा।
उपास्य तु शिवां संध्यां विषयानत्यगाहत॥ २॥
verses.m: Even as he drove along with the same alacrity, the delightful night passed. Having worshipped the blissful morning twilight, he passed beyond a number of territories. (2)

verses.text:
ग्रामान् विकृष्टसीमान्तान् पुष्पितानि वनानि च।
पश्यन्नतिययौ शीघ्रं शनैरिव हयोत्तमैः॥ ३॥
शृण्वन् वाचो मनुष्याणां ग्रामसंवासवासिनाम्।
राजानं धिग् दशरथं कामस्य वशमास्थितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing villages whose outskirts had been carefully tilled, and woodlands laden with blossoms, and led by excellent horses, he proceeded apace as though slowly, engrossed as he was in enjoying the sights, hearing (as under) the words of those residing in villages and hamlets close by : “Woe unto King Daśaratha, who has fallen into the clutches of concupiscence. (3-4)

verses.text:
हा नृशंसाद्य कैकेयी पापा पापानुबन्धिनी।
तीक्ष्णा सम्भिन्नमर्यादा तीक्ष्णकर्मणि वर्तते॥ ५॥
या पुत्रमीदृशं राज्ञः प्रवासयति धार्मिकम्।
वनवासे महाप्राज्ञं सानुक्रोशं जितेन्द्रियम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Ah, the cruel and sinful Kaikeyī, who is hot-tempered and of sinful designs and has transgressed the bounds of propriety, is herself engaged at present in a cruel game in that she has been instrumental in sending into exile in the forest such a pious, highly enlightened, compassionate and self-controlled son of the Emperor. (5-6)

verses.text:
कथं नाम महाभागा सीता जनकनन्दिनी।
सदा सुखेष्वभिरता दुःखान्यनुभविष्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “How will the highly blessed Sītā, daughter of King Janaka, who is ever given to comforts, actually suffer hardships? (7)

verses.text:
अहो दशरथो राजा निःस्नेहः स्वसुतं प्रति।
प्रजानामनघं रामं परित्यक्तुमिहेच्छति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “What a pity that King Daśaratha has grown so devoid of affection on this occasion that he seeks to abandon Śrī Rāma, who is sinless towards the people !” (8)

verses.text:
एता वाचो मनुष्याणां ग्रामसंवासवासिनाम्।
शृण्वन्नतिययौ वीरः कोसलान् कोसलेश्वरः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing these remarks of men residing in the adjoining villages and hamlets, the heroic prince of Kosala, Śrī Rāma, passed beyond the limits of Kosala. (9)

verses.text:
ततो वेदश्रुतिं नाम शिववारिवहां नदीम्।
उत्तीर्याभिमुखः प्रायादगस्त्याध्युषितां दिशम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Having crossed the river named Vedaśruti, which carries auspicious waters, he then pressed forward facing the south, the quarter occupied by Sage Agastya. (10)

verses.text:
गत्वा तु सुचिरं कालं ततः शीतवहां नदीम्।
गोमतीं गोयुतानूपामतरत् सागरङ्गमाम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Journeying for his part in that direction for a pretty long time, he next crossed the river Gomatī, which carried cool waters and heads towards the sea through the medium of the holy Gaṅgā and whose banks are adorned with cows. (11)

verses.text:
गोमतीं चाप्यतिक्रम्य राघवः शीघ्रगैर्हयैः।
मयूरहंसाभिरुतां ततार स्यन्दिकां नदीम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Having reached the other bank of the Gomatī too, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, crossed with the help of swift-going horses the river Syandikā as well, made resonant by peacocks and swans. (12)

verses.text:
स महीं मनुना राज्ञा दत्तामिक्ष्वाकवे पुरा।
स्फीतां राष्ट्रवृतां रामो वैदेहीमन्वदर्शयत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: The said Śrī Rāma now showed to Sītā (a princess of the Videha kingdom) the prosperous land of Kosala, the southern boundary of which was defined by the Syandikā, which was given of yore by Manu, the king of kings, to his eldest son, Ikṣwāku, and which was bounded on all sides by other adjoining territories. (13)

verses.text:
सूत इत्येव चाभाष्य सारथिं तमभीक्ष्णशः।
हंसमत्तस्वरः श्रीमानुवाच पुरुषोत्तमः॥ १४॥
कदाहं पुनरागम्य सरय्वाः पुष्पिते वने।
मृगयां पर्यटिष्यामि मात्रा पित्रा च संगतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Repeatedly addressing the aforesaid charioteer in the words “O charioteer,” the glorious Rāma, the foremost of men, whose voice resembled the cackling of a swan in rut, said, “When, returning back to Ayodhyā and united once more with my parents, shall I roam hunting in the woodland bordering on the Sarayū and laden with blossoms? (14-15)

verses.text:
नात्यर्थमभिकांक्षामि मृगयां सरयूवने।
रतिर्ह्येषातुला लोके राजर्षिगणसम्मता॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I do not hanker much after sport in the woodland bordering on the Sarayū. In fact it is a unique enjoyment made much of in the world by hosts of royal sages. (16)

verses.text:
राजर्षीणां हि लोकेऽस्मिन् रत्यर्थं मृगया वने।
काले कृतां तां मनुजैर्धन्विनामभिकांक्षिताम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Truly speaking, hunting in a forest was resorted to in this world for the gratification of royal sages. Even though it was adopted at times by the sons of Manu and was sought after by other bowmen, I do not long for it excessively.” (17)

verses.text:
स तमध्वानमैक्ष्वाकः सूतं मधुरया गिरा।
तं तमर्थमभिप्रेत्य ययौ वाक्यमुदीरयन्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Conversing thus with the charioteer on various topics in sweet words, the said Śrī Rāma, a scion of Ikṣwāku, advanced along that route. (18)

verses.text:
विशालान् कोसलान् रम्यान् यात्वा लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।
अयोध्यामुन्मुखो धीमान् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having travelled across the extensive and beautiful territory of Kosala and standing with his face turned towards Ayodhyā, the wise Śrī Rāma, elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, with folded hands addressed the following words to Ayodhyā : (1)

verses.text:
आपृच्छे त्वां पुरिश्रेष्ठे काकुत्स्थपरिपालिते।
दैवतानि च यानि त्वां पालयन्त्यावसन्ति च॥ २॥
verses.m: “I take leave of you, O pre-eminent city, carefully protected by King Daśaratha, a scion of Kakutstha, as well as of the deities that protect you and dwell in you. (2)

verses.text:
निवृत्तवनवासस्त्वामनृणो जगतीपतेः।
पुनर्द्रक्ष्यामि मात्रा च पित्रा च सह संगतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “When the period of my exile in the forest has expired and I have got square with the Emperor (by executing his command and implementing the promise made by him to Kaikeyī), I shall see you again, united once more with my mother and father.” (3)

verses.text:
ततो रुचिरताम्राक्षो भुजमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम्।
अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनोऽब्रवीज्जानपदं जनम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Lifting up His right arm and wearing a wretched look, his face covered with tears, Śrī Rāma (who was possessed of lovely reddish eyes) then spoke to the people hailing from the countryside as follows : (4)

verses.text:
अनुक्रोशो दया चैव यथार्हं मयि वः कृतः।
चिरं दुःखस्य पापीयो गम्यतामर्थसिद्धये॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Respect and compassion according to my worth in your eyes have been shown to me by you all. Prolongation of the agony which is being experienced by you due to your presence by my side is most undesirable. Therefore, pray, let you be gone for accomplishing your desired chores (viz., attending to your household work) !” (5)

verses.text:
तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्।
विलपन्तो नरा घोरं व्यतिष्ठंश्च क्वचित् क्वचित्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Greeting the high-souled prince and going round him clockwise as a mark of respect, those men stood rooted here and there, not minding where they stood, wailing frightfully. (6)

verses.text:
तथा विलपतां तेषामतृप्तानां च राघवः।
अचक्षुर्विषयं प्रायाद् यथार्कः क्षणदामुखे॥ ७॥
verses.m: Even while they were lamenting as aforesaid, unsated as they were with the sight of Śrī Rāma, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, passed beyond their sight just as the sun goes out of sight at the commencement of night. (7)

verses.text:
ततो धान्यधनोपेतान् दानशीलजनान् शिवान्।
अकुतश्चिद्भयान् रम्यांश्चैत्ययूपसमावृतान्॥ ८ ॥
उद्यानाम्रवणोपेतान् सम्पन्नसलिलाशयान्।
तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णान् गोकुलाकुलसेवितान्॥ ९ ॥
रक्षणीयान् नरेन्द्राणां ब्रह्मघोषाभिनादितान्।
रथेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः कोसलानत्यवर्तत॥ १०॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, then crossed in His chariot the blessed and lovely territory of Kosala, which was full of foodgrains and other riches and was peopled by men given to charity, which had no fear from any quarter and was covered all over with temples and sacrificial posts, which was rich in gardens and mango groves and strewn with ponds full of water, which was thickly populated with contented and well-fed people and abounded in herds of cows, nay, each village of which deserved to be protected by kings and which was made resonant with the chanting of the Vedas. (8—10)

verses.text:
मध्येन मुदितं स्फीतं रम्योद्यानसमाकुलम्।
राज्यं भोज्यं नरेन्द्राणां ययौ धृतिमतां वरः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Thence Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those possessed of firmness drove at a moderate speed to a happy and prosperous territory ruled over by a number of feudatory chiefs and abounding in lovely gardens. (11)

verses.text:
तत्र त्रिपथगां दिव्यां शीततोयामशैवलाम्।
ददर्श राघवो गङ्गां रम्यामृषिनिषेविताम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: There in the confines of that kingdom Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, saw the celestial and lovely river Gaṅgā, which takes a threefold course flowing as it does through heaven, earth and the subterranean regions, carries cool waters, is free from duck-weed sand and is frequented by Ṛṣis. (12)

verses.text:
आश्रमैरविदूरस्थैः श्रीमद्भिः समलंकृताम्।
कालेऽप्सरोभिर्हृष्टाभिः सेविताम्भोह्रदां शिवाम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: The blessed river was adorned with splendid hermitages standing not very far from one another; and its pools, overflowing with water, were resorted to at suitable hours by merry celestial nymphs. (13)

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैः किंनरैरुपशोभिताम्।
नागगन्धर्वपत्नीभिः सेवितां सततं शिवाम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Nay, the blessed river was graced with the presence of gods and demons, Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and Kinnaras and was constantly* visited by the consorts of Nāgas and Gandharvas. (14)

verses.text:
देवाक्रीडशताकीर्णां देवोद्यानयुतां नदीम्।
देवार्थमाकाशगतां विख्यातां देवपद्मिनीम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: The well-known river was hemmed in by hundreds of pleasure-hills forming part of the Himalayan range and adorned with celestial gardens; it coursed through the heavens for the benefit of gods and contained celestial lotuses. (15)

verses.text:
जलाघाताट्टहासोग्रां फेननिर्मलहासिनीम्।
क्वचिद् वेणीकृतजलां क्वचिदावर्तशोभिताम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: It assumed a severe aspect while indulging in a horse-laugh in the form of a noise produced by the striking of its waters against rocks, and seemed to shed a bright smile when covered with white foam. At some places its water was reduced to the shape of plaited locks because of its flowing in a curved line, while at other places it was adorned with eddies. (16)

verses.text:
क्वचित् स्तिमितगम्भीरां क्वचिद् वेगसमाकुलाम्।
क्वचिद् गम्भीरनिर्घोषां क्वचिद् भैरवनिःस्वनाम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Somewhere its waters were still and deep, and at other places they were disturbed with violent agitation. Here it made a deep roaring sound and there it produced a terrific noise. (17)

verses.text:
देवसंघाप्लुतजलां निर्मलोत्पलसंकुलाम्।
क्वचिदाभोगपुलिनां क्वचिन्निर्मलवालुकाम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hosts of gods took a dip into its water, covered all over with white lotuses. Here it was hemmed in with spacious banks and there it was lined with white sands. (18)

verses.text:
हंससारससंघुष्टां चक्रवाकोपशोभिताम्।
सदामत्तैश्च विहगैरभिपन्नामनिन्दिताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: The river, which is free from reproach in everyway was rendered noisy by swans and cranes, was graced with Cakrawākas (a species of bird which gets disunited with its mate by night); and other birds which are in rut all the year round, kept hovering on its waters. (19)

verses.text:
क्वचित् तीररुहैर्वृक्षैर्मालाभिरिव शोभिताम्।
क्वचित् फुल्लोत्पलच्छन्नां क्वचित् पद्मवनाकुलाम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Here it was decked with trees growing on its banks, which encircled it like garlands. Here it was covered with full-blown lotuses, while there it was carpeted with a bed of lotuses. (20)

verses.text:
क्वचित् कुमुदखण्डैश्च कुड्मलैरुपशोभिताम्।
नानापुष्परजोध्वस्तां समदामिव च क्वचित्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Here it was graced with beds of water-lilies in the form of buds, while there it was reddened with the pollen of numerous flowers and looked like a woman excited with passion. (21)

verses.text:
व्यपेतमलसंघातां मणिनिर्मलदर्शनाम्।
दिशागजैर्वनगजैर्मत्तैश्च वरवारणैः॥ २२॥
देवराजोपवाह्यैश्च संनादितवनान्तराम्।
प्रमदामिव यत्नेन भूषितां भूषणोत्तमैः॥ २३॥
फलपुष्पैः किसलयैर्वृतां गुल्मैर्द्विजैस्तथा।
विष्णुपादच्युतां दिव्यामपापां पापनाशिनीम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Stocks of sins of those bathing in it or drinking of its waters are washed away by it and it presents an appearance spotless as the effulgence of a gem. The interior of the forests encircling its banks is rendered noisy by the elephants guarding the quarters, wild elephants and other tame elephants of excellent breed, belonging to the Airāvata species, used for riding by Indra, the ruler of gods. Surrounded by trees laden with fruits and flowers and tender leaves, shrubs and birds of various species, it looked like a young woman artistically decked with the best of jewels. Not only devoid of sins, the celestial river dispels all sins, flowing as it does from the holy feet of Lord Viṣṇu. (22—24)

verses.text:
शिंशुमारैश्च नक्रैश्च भुजंगैश्च समन्विताम्।
शंकरस्य जटाजूटाद् भ्रष्टां सागरतेजसा॥ २५॥
verses.m: In deep waters the river was infested with sharks and crocodiles as well as with snakes and had fallen from the mass of matted hair on the head of Lord Śaṅkara, thanks to the Yoga power acquired through religious austerities by Emperor Bhagīratha. (25)

verses.text:
समुद्रमहिषीं गङ्गां सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम्।
आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गवेरपुरं प्रति॥ २६॥
verses.m: In the vicinity of Śṛṅgaverapura (the modern Singraur) Śrī Rāma, the mighty-armed prince, reached the bank of the Gaṅgā, the principal consort of Ocean, which was rendered noisy by cranes and herons. (26)

verses.text:
तामूर्मिकलिलावर्तामन्ववेक्ष्य महारथः।
सुमन्त्रमब्रवीत् सूतमिहैवाद्य वसामहे॥ २७॥
verses.m: Perceiving the river, which was full of eddies interspersed with its waves, the great car-warrior said to the charioteer, Sumantra, “Let us halt at this very spot today. (27)

verses.text:
अविदूरादयं नद्या बहुपुष्पप्रवालवान्।
सुमहानिङ्गुदीवृक्षो वसामोऽत्रैव सारथे॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Not very far from the river stands this very large Iṅgudī tree containing abundant flowers and fresh leaves. Let us halt under this very tree, O charioteer ! (28)

verses.text:
प्रेक्षामि सरितां श्रेष्ठां सम्मान्यसलिलां शिवाम्।
देवमानवगन्धर्वमृगपन्नगपक्षिणाम् ॥ २९॥
verses.m: “I shall clearly behold from that place the benign Gaṅgā, the foremost of rivers, whose waters deserve to be respected by gods, human beings, Gandharvas, beasts, reptiles and birds alike.” (29)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणश्च सुमन्त्रश्च बाढमित्येव राघवम्।
उक्त्वा तमिङ्गुदीवृक्षं तदोपययतुर्हयैः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Saying “Very well!” and nothing more to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Lakṣmaṇa and Sumantra too then drove up to the Iṅgudī tree in the chariot drawn by horses. (30)

verses.text:
रामोऽभियाय तं रम्यं वृक्षमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।
रथादवतरत् तस्मात् सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Approaching that lovely tree, Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣwākus, alighted from that chariot alongwith his consort and with Lakṣmaṇa. (31)

verses.text:
सुमन्त्रोऽप्यवतीर्याथ मोचयित्वा हयोत्तमान्।
वृक्षमूलगतं राममुपतस्थे कृताञ्जलिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Getting down and unyoking the excellent horses, Sumantra too with joined palms stood by the side of Śrī Rāma, seated at the foot of the tree. (32)

verses.text:
तत्र राजा गुहो नाम रामस्यात्मसमः सखा।
निषादजात्यो बलवान् स्थपतिश्चेति विश्रुतः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: The king of that territory, Guha by name, was a friend of Śrī Rāma, dear to him as his own life. He was a Niṣāda by birth, possessed of bodily as well as military strength, owning as he did a large army consisting of all the four limbs, viz., elephants, chariots, horsemen and foot soldiers, and well-known as a ruler of the Niṣādas. (33)

verses.text:
स श्रुत्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं रामं विषयमागतम्।
वृद्धैः परिवृतोऽमात्यैर्ज्ञातिभिश्चाप्युपागतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Hearing of Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, having arrived in his territory, and accompanied by his elderly ministers and relations too, he sought the prince. (34)

verses.text:
ततो निषादाधिपतिं दृष्ट्वा दूरादुपस्थितम्।
सह सौमित्रिणा रामः समागच्छद् गुहेन सः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Seeing from a distance the ruler of the Niṣādas waiting, the said Śrī Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) thereupon went forth to meet Guha. (35)

verses.text:
तमार्तः सम्परिष्वज्य गुहो राघवमब्रवीत्।
यथायोध्या तथेदं ते राम किं करवाणि ते॥ ३६॥
ईदृशं हि महाबाहो कः प्राप्स्यत्यतिथिं प्रियम्।
ततो गुणवदन्नाद्यमुपादाय पृथग्विधम्॥ ३७॥
अर्घ्यं चोपानयच्छीघ्रं वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह।
स्वागतं ते महाबाहो तवेयमखिला मही॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Closely embracing Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Guha, who felt distressed to see him clad in the robes of a hermit, said to him, “This principality of Śṛṅgaverapura is as much yours as Ayodhyā, O Rāma ! What shall I do for you? In fact, who will get such a beloved guest as you, O mighty-armed prince?” Having brought cooked rice of excellent quality and other dishes of various kinds, he then quickly offered him water to wash his hands with and other articles of worship and spoke as follows: so the tradition goes : “Welcome is your advent to this place, O mighty-armed prince ! This entire land (of mine) is yours. (36—38)

verses.text:
वयं प्रेष्या भवान् भर्ता साधु राज्यं प्रशाधि नः।
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च पेयं च लेह्यं चैतदुपस्थितम्।
शयनानि च मुख्यानि वाजिनां खादनं च ते॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “We are your servants, you are our master; pray, rule over our kingdom in the proper way from now. Nay, here are at your service dishes requiring mastication (such as rice) and those which can be eaten without mastication (such as milk boiled with rice and sugar), those which can be drunk, those which are fit to be licked up and those which can be sucked. Moreover, there are excellent beds for you to sleep on as well as fodder for your horses.” (39)

verses.text:
गुहमेवं ब्रुवाणं तु राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह।
अर्चिताश्चैव हृष्टाश्च भवता सर्वदा वयम्॥ ४०॥
पद्भ्यामभिगमाच्चैव स्नेहसंदर्शनेन च।
भुजाभ्यां साधुवृत्ताभ्यां पीडयन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: To Guha, who was speaking as aforesaid, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), for his part, they say, replied as follows : “We stand honoured by you by your very coming all the way on foot to meet us as well as by your exhibition of affection, and are always pleased with you.” Pressing Guha tightly once more with his rounded arms, Śrī Rāma added the following : (40-41)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या त्वां गुह पश्यामि ह्यरोगं सह बान्धवैः।
अपि ते कुशलं राष्ट्रे मित्रेषु च वनेषु च॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I am glad, O Guha, I see you quite in good health with your relations. Is all well with your state, allies and forests? (42)

verses.text:
यत् त्विदं भवता किंचित् प्रीत्या समुपकल्पितम्।
सर्वं तदनुजानामि नहि वर्ते प्रतिग्रहे॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “I for my part accept and allow you to take back all this, that has been lovingly offered by you, since I do not make use of gifts for my own purpose. (43)

verses.text:
कुशचीराजिनधरं फलमूलाशनं च माम्।
विद्धि प्रणिहितं धर्मे तापसं वनगोचरम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Know me as under a vow to wear (a zone of) Kuśa grass, the bark of trees and deerskin and to subsist on fruits and roots alone, to practise austerities and dwell in the forest, remaining devoted to piety. (44)

verses.text:
अश्वानां खादनेनाहमर्थी नान्येन केनचित्।
एतावतात्र भवता भविष्यामि सुपूजितः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “I am interested only in having food for the horses and in nothing else. By being provided with this much at the present moment I shall be duly entertained by you. (45)

verses.text:
एते हि दयिता राज्ञः पितुर्दशरथस्य मे।
एतैः सुविहितैरश्वैर्भविष्याम्यहमर्चितः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Since these horses are beloved of my father, King Daśaratha, I shall feel honoured by these horses being duly fed.” (46)

verses.text:
अश्वानां प्रतिपानं च खादनं चैव सोऽन्वशात्।
गुहस्तत्रैव पुरुषांस्त्वरितं दीयतामिति॥ ४७॥
verses.m: On that very spot the said Guha commanded his men in the following words : “Let milk etc., (which horses of excellent breed are given to drink after being fed with grass etc.) and barley flour mixed with ghee, sugar and so on, which they are given to eat in addition to grass etc., be promptly supplied to the horses.” (47)

verses.text:
ततश्चीरोत्तरासङ्गः संध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्।
जलमेवाददे भोज्यं लक्ष्मणेनाहृतं स्वयम्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Having worshipped the evening twilight, appearing in the west, with an upper garment made of the bark of trees on his person, Śrī Rāma then took for food only water brought by Lakṣmaṇa himself thus observing a fast in honour of the sacred river which he visited. (48)

verses.text:
तस्य भूमौ शयानस्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य लक्ष्मणः।
सभार्यस्य ततोऽभ्येत्य तस्थौ वृक्षमुपाश्रितः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Having cleanly washed the feet of Śrī Rāma, and his consort lying on the ground to repose for the night, and receding from that place, Lakṣmaṇa took his position at the foot of another tree close by. (49)

verses.text:
गुहोऽपि सह सूतेन सौमित्रिमनुभाषयन्।
अन्वजाग्रत् ततो राममप्रमत्तो धनुर्धरः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Following in the footsteps of Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) and encouraging him to speak on the virtues of Śrī Rāma, and wielding his bow, Guha too thereupon kept vigil with the charioteer, remaining alert all the time in the interest of Śrī Rāma. (50)

verses.text:
तथा शयानस्य ततो यशस्विनो
मनस्विनो दाशरथेर्महात्मनः।
अदृष्टदुःखस्य सुखोचितस्य सा
तदा व्यतीता सुचिरेण शर्वरी॥ ५१॥
verses.m: While the illustrious, lofty-minded and high-souled Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha), who had never undergone suffering and who was used to all comforts, remained lying after that on the ground as aforesaid, that night eventually lingered away. (51)

verses.text:
तं जाग्रतमदम्भेन भ्रातुरर्थाय लक्ष्मणम्।
गुहः संतापसंतप्तो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Distressed with agony to see the princely couple lying on the ground, Guha spoke as follows to the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa (a scion of Raghu), who was keeping awake, through sincere love, for the protection of his elder brother, Śrī Rāma : (1)

verses.text:
इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता।
प्रत्याश्वसिहि साध्वस्यां राजपुत्र यथासुखम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Here is a cosy bed nicely prepared for you, dear brother; pray, repose comfortably on it, O prince ! (2)

verses.text:
उचितोऽयं जनः सर्वः क्लेशानां त्वं सुखोचितः।
गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामः काकुत्स्थस्य वयं निशाम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “We are all inured to hardships, while you are deserving of comforts. We shall keep vigil for the night for the protection of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha. (3)

verses.text:
नहि रामात् प्रियतमो ममास्ते भुवि कश्चन।
ब्रवीम्येव च ते सत्यं सत्येनैव च ते शपे॥ ४॥
verses.m: “For, none on earth is more beloved of me than Śrī Rāma: I tell you the bare truth and swear to you by truth. (4)

verses.text:
अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेऽस्मिन् सुमहद् यशः।
धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थकामौ च पुष्कलौ॥ ५॥
verses.m: “By his grace alone I hope to earn very great renown in this world as also to acquire religious merit as well as abundant riches and sense-enjoyment. (5)

verses.text:
सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया।
रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणिः सर्वथा ज्ञातिभिः सह॥ ६॥
verses.m: “As such, I shall with my kindred guard in everyway, bow in hand, my beloved friend, Śrī Rāma, reposing with Sītā. (6)

verses.text:
न मेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिद् वनेऽस्मिंश्चरतः सदा।
चतुरङ्गं ह्यतिबलं सुमहत् संतरेमहि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Nothing in this woodland is unknown to me, wandering as I do all the time in it. We can also undoubtedly get the better of a surpassingly huge and exceptionally mighty army consisting of the four limbs viz., elephants, chariots, horsemen and foot soldiers.” (7)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्तु तदोवाच रक्ष्यमाणास्त्वयानघ।
नात्र भीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता॥ ८॥
verses.m: Thereupon Lakṣmaṇa for his part replied as follows : “Being protected by you, who keep your duty alone in view, O sinless Guha, we all are not the least afraid of any in this land. (8)

verses.text:
कथं दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया।
शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितं वा सुखानि वा॥ ९॥
verses.m: “But so long as Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, remains lying down on the ground with Sītā, how can sleep be had by me, much less nourishment intended to keep the body and soul together or amenities of life? (9)

verses.text:
यो न देवासुरैः सर्वैः शक्यः प्रसहितुं युधि।
तं पश्य सुखसंसुप्तं तृणेषु सह सीतया॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Behold him, who cannot be withstood in battle by all the gods and demons put together, fast asleep with comfort on a bed of straw with Sītā ! (10)

verses.text:
यो मन्त्रतपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च पराक्रमैः।
एको दशरथस्यैष पुत्रः सदृशलक्षणः॥ ११॥
अस्मिन् प्रव्रजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति।
विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: “When Śrī Rāma—who was secured as a foremost (eldest both in age and virtues) son, endowed with characteristics similar to his own, by Daśaratha by virtue of his chanting of sacred texts and austerities as well as through various undertakings in the form of sacrificial performances etc.—has gone into exile, the king (Daśaratha) will not live long and the earth will surely be widowed forthwith (by the demise of Daśaratha). (11-12)

verses.text:
विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः।
निर्घोषोपरतं तात मन्ये राजनिवेशनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Having uttered forth a shrill cry, the women in the city must have ceased weeping through exhaustion by this time. I believe the royal palace too has by now become silent after a loud wail. (13)

verses.text:
कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम।
नाशंसे यदि जीवन्ति सर्वे ते शर्वरीमिमाम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I do not expect that the great queen Kausalyā (Śrī Rāma’s mother) and the king and even so my mother (Sumitrā)—all these will outlive this night. (14)

verses.text:
जीवेदपि हि मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया।
तद् दुःखं यदि कौसल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “My mother might even survive due to her expecting to meet Śatrughna. But it will be painful if Kausalyā, who has given birth to a heroic son, dies. (15)

verses.text:
अनुरक्तजनाकीर्णा सुखालोकप्रियावहा।
राजव्यसनसंसृष्टा सा पुरी विनशिष्यति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “That city of Ayodhyā, which has till now been crowded with men and women full of love for Śrī Rāma, nay, which has been a source of joy to all and brought pleasure to the world, will perish when seized with agony over the king’s death. (16)

verses.text:
कथं पुत्रं महात्मानं ज्येष्ठपुत्रमपश्यतः।
शरीरं धारयिष्यन्ति प्राणा राज्ञो महात्मनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “How will the life-breath of the high-souled king retain its hold on his body when he is no longer able to behold the high-souled Śrī Rāma, his eldest son? (17)

verses.text:
विनष्टे नृपतौ पश्चात् कौसल्या विनशिष्यति।
अनन्तरं च मातापि मम नाशमुपैष्यति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “When the king is dead, Kausalyā will die in his wake and my mother (Sumitrā) too will meet her end immediately after. (18)

verses.text:
अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्।
राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Not attaining his desired end and without installing Śrī Rāma on the throne of Ayodhyā, my father will breathe his last with the words ‘Lost ! Lost !!’ on his lips. (19)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन् काले ह्युपस्थिते।
प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति राघवम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Fortunate men alone will consecrate our deceased father, Daśaratha (a scion of Raghu) in the course of all funeral rites when that unlucky moment has actually arrived. (20)

verses.text:
रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां संविभक्तमहापथाम्।
हर्म्यप्रासादसम्पन्नां गणिकावरशोभिताम्॥ २१॥
रथाश्वगजसम्बाधां तूर्यनादनिनादिताम्।
सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्॥ २२॥
आरामोद्यानसम्पन्नां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्।
सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम॥ २३॥
verses.m: “If, on the other hand, Daśaratha survives, people will move about happily in the capital of my father, provided with cross roads, allocated at lovely sites, and well-aligned roads, nay, rich in mansions of well-to-do men, temples of gods and royal palaces, adorned with the foremost of courtesans, crowded with chariots, horses and elephants, made resonant with the sound of musical instruments, full of all blessings and crowded with merry and well-fed men, well-provided with gardens and royal parks and bright with festivities carried on under the auspices of associations. (21—23)

verses.text:
अपि जीवेद् दशरथो वनवासात् पुनर्वयम्।
प्रत्यागम्य महात्मानमपि पश्याम सुव्रतम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “In case Daśaratha, our father, survives, we might on returning from our exile in the forest see that high-souled king of noble vows once more. (24)

verses.text:
अपि सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयम्।
निवृत्ते वनवासेऽस्मिन्नयोध्यां प्रविशेमहि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Let us hope when this period of exile in the forest has expired, we may safely return to Ayodhyā alongwith Śrī Rāma, who is true to his promise.” (25)

verses.text:
परिदेवयमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः।
तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी सात्यवर्तत॥ २६॥
verses.m: While the high-souled prince, Lakṣmaṇa, sat lamenting as above, afflicted with agony as he was, that night slipped away. (26)

verses.text:
तथा हि सत्यं ब्रुवति प्रजाहिते
नरेन्द्रसूनौ गुरुसौहृदाद् गुहः।
मुमोच बाष्पं व्यसनाभिपीडितो
ज्वरातुरो नाग इव व्यथातुरः॥ २७॥
verses.m: While Lakṣmaṇa, son of Daśaratha, a friend of the people, was speaking the truth as above out of affection for his elder brother, Śrī Rāma, Guha, who was sore pinched with adversity and oppressed with agony, shed tears like an elephant tormented with fever. (27)

verses.text:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पृथुवक्षा महायशाः।
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्॥ १॥
verses.m: The night having ended in dawn, the highly illustrious Śrī Rāma, who was distinguished by a broad chest, spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks : (1)

verses.text:
भास्करोदयकालोऽसौ गता भगवती निशा।
असौ सुकृष्णो विहगः कोकिलस्तात कूजति॥ २॥
verses.m: “The hour of sunrise is at hand and the glorious night has passed. Over there the very dark bird, the cuckoo, is uttering its notes, O dear brother ! (2)

verses.text:
बर्हिणानां च निर्घोषः श्रूयते नदतां वने।
तराम जाह्नवीं सौम्य शीघ्रगां सागरङ्गमाम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The shrill note of peacocks crying in the woodland is also heard. Let us, therefore, O good brother, cross the swift-flowing Gaṅgā (the daughter of Jahnu*), which runs towards the sea.” (3)

verses.text:
विज्ञाय रामस्य वचः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः।
गुहमामन्त्र्य सूतं च सोऽतिष्ठद् भ्रातुरग्रतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Grasping the intention of Śrī Rāma’s words and informing Guha as well as the charioteer accordingly, the said Lakṣmaṇa, the delight of his friends, stood facing his elder brother, Śrī Rāma. (4)

verses.text:
स तु रामस्य वचनं निशम्य प्रतिगृह्य च।
स्थपतिस्तूर्णमाहूय सचिवानिदमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma and bowing to it, nay, speedily summoning his ministers, Guha, the ruler of the Niṣādas, for his part spoke to one of them as follows : (5)

verses.text:
अस्यवाहनसंयुक्तां कर्णग्राहवतीं शुभाम्।
सुप्रतारां दृढां तीर्थे शीघ्रं नावमुपाहर॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Quickly bring to the landing-place a beautiful and stout boat, duly equipped with oars and a helmsman, by which Śrī Rāma and his party could easily ferry across.” (6)

verses.text:
तं निशम्य गुहादेशं गुहामात्यो गतो महान्।
उपोह्य रुचिरां नावं गुहाय प्रत्यवेदयत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid command of Guha, the great minister of Guha departed and, bringing a charming boat to the nearest landing-place, reported the compliance to Guha. (7)

verses.text:
ततः स प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा गुहो राघवमब्रवीत्।
उपस्थितेयं नौर्देव भूयः किं करवाणि ते॥ ८॥
verses.m: Folding his hands, the said Guha then said to Śrī Rāma, “Here is the boat ready, my lord! What more shall I do for you? (8)

verses.text:
तवामरसुतप्रख्य तर्तुं सागरगामिनीम्।
नौरियं पुरुषव्याघ्र शीघ्रमारोह सुव्रत॥ ९॥
अथोवाच महातेजा रामो गुहमिदं वचः।
कृतकामोऽस्मि भवता शीघ्रमारोप्यतामिति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Here is a boat brought for you, O tiger among men, to cross the Gaṅgā (flowing towards the sea), O prince, effulgent as the son of a divinity ! Pray, get into it promptly, O observer of noble vows !” The exceptionally glorious Śrī Rāma thereupon spoke to Guha as follows : “My desire has been accomplished by you. Please have everything placed in the boat quickly.”(9-10)

verses.text:
ततः कलापान् संनह्य खड्गौ बध्वा च धन्विनौ।
जग्मतुर्येन तां गङ्गां सीतया सह राघवौ॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having equipped themselves with an armour each and fastened their quivers and swords to their person, the two archers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, scions of Raghu, with Sītā then sought the said Gaṅgā through the same landing-place as was resorted to by others. (11)

verses.text:
राममेवं तु धर्मज्ञमुपागत्य विनीतवत्।
किमहं करवाणीति सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Humbly approaching Śrī Rāma, who knew what is right and stood ready to leave, the charioteer humbly spoke with folded hands as follows : “What shall I do?” (12)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीद् दाशरथिः सुमन्त्रं
स्पृशन् करेणोत्तमदक्षिणेन।
सुमन्त्र शीघ्रं पुनरेव याहि
राज्ञः सकाशे भव चाप्रमत्तः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Touching Sumantra with his auspicious right hand, Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) thereupon replied to him, “Return speedily to the king’s presence, O Sumantra, and do not lose your presence of mind.” (13)

verses.text:
निवर्तस्वेत्युवाचैनमेतावद्धि कृतं मम।
रथं विहाय पद्भ्यां तु गमिष्यामो महावनम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Please return,” said he to Sumantra and added, “this much is enough service to me. Leaving the chariot, we shall henceforth proceed to the great forest of Daṇḍaka on foot.” (14)

verses.text:
आत्मानं त्वभ्यनुज्ञातमवेक्ष्यार्तः स सारथिः।
सुमन्त्रः पुरुषव्याघ्रमैक्ष्वाकमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Distressed to find himself dismissed, the said charioteer, Sumantra, for his part submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Ikṣwāku, a tiger among men : (15)

verses.text:
नातिक्रान्तमिदं लोके पुरुषेणेह केनचित्।
तव सभ्रातृभार्यस्य वासः प्राकृतवद् वने॥ १६॥
verses.m: “That destiny, by which has been brought about your exile in the forest with your consort and younger brother like that of a common man, has never been set aside by any man in this world. (16)

verses.text:
न मन्ये ब्रह्मचर्ये वा स्वधीते वा फलोदयः।
मार्दवार्जवयोर्वापि त्वां चेद् व्यसनमागतम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I believe there is no gain in leading the austere life of a religious student in the house of one’s teacher, in studying the Vedas as an integral part of such a life or even in cultivating tenderness and guilelessness, when adversity has come even to you in the shape of exile. (17)

verses.text:
सह राघव वैदेह्या भ्रात्रा चैव वने वसन्।
त्वं गतिं प्राप्स्यसे वीर त्रींल्लोकांस्तु जयन्निव॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Living as an exile in the forest with Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, and younger brother, O scion of Raghu, you will surely attain the same exalted position as one who has conquered all the worlds. (18)

verses.text:
वयं खलु हता राम ये त्वया ह्युपवञ्चिताः।
कैकेय्या वशमेष्यामः पापाया दुःखभागिनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “We are actually ruined, O Rāma, in that, forsaken by you, we shall surely fall under the sway of the sinful Kaikeyī and reap suffering.” (19)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवन्नात्मसमं सुमन्त्रः सारथिस्तदा।
दृष्ट्वा दूरगतं रामं दुःखार्तो रुरुदे चिरम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Speaking thus in a strain worthy of himself, Sumantra, the charioteer, then wept long, stricken with sorrow as he was to see with his mental eyes Śrī Rāma gone to some distance. (20)

verses.text:
ततस्तु विगते बाष्पे सूतं स्पृष्ट्वोदकं शुचिम्।
रामस्तु मधुरं वाक्यं पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: When his tears got dried up and the charioteer had sipped some water and got purified (the tears having brought defilement in him), Śrī Rāma for his part repeatedly spoke to him in a sweet tone as follows : (21)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकूणां त्वया तुल्यं सुहृदं नोपलक्षये।
यथा दशरथो राजा मां न शोचेत् तथा कुरु॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I do not perceive anyone who is as great a friend of the Ikṣwākus as you are. Pray, act in such wise that King Daśaratha may not grieve for me. (22)

verses.text:
शोकोपहतचेताश्च वृद्धश्च जगतीपतिः।
कामभारावसन्नश्च तस्मादेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The Emperor is not only confused in mind through grief, he is aged too and has his host of desires (to see me installed as Prince Regent and so on) thwarted. Hence I tell you this : (23)

verses.text:
यद् यथा ज्ञापयेत् किंचित् स महात्मा महीपतिः।
कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं कार्यं तदविकांक्षया॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Whatever and howsoever that high-souled Emperor may enjoin you to do with intent to oblige mother Kaikeyī should be unhesitatingly done by you. (24)

verses.text:
एतदर्थं हि राज्यानि प्रशासति नराधिपाः।
यदेषां सर्वकृत्येषु मनो न प्रतिहन्यते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Kings rule their states only with this end in view that their will may not be crossed in any undertaking. (25)

verses.text:
यद् यथा स महाराजो नालीकमधिगच्छति।
न च ताम्यति शोकेन सुमन्त्र कुरु तत् तथा॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Handle everything in such a way, O Sumantra, that the said Emperor neither gets displeased nor does he feel distressed through grief. (26)

verses.text:
अदृष्टदुःखं राजानं वृद्धमार्यं जितेन्द्रियम्।
ब्रूयास्त्वमभिवाद्यैव मम हेतोरिदं वचः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Only after greeting the old and venerable king, who has never known suffering and has subdued his senses, make you this submission to him on my behalf :(27)

verses.text:
न चाहमनुशोचामि लक्ष्मणो न च शोचति।
अयोध्यायाश्च्युताश्चेति वने वत्स्यामहेति वा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Neither do I grieve nor does Lakṣmaṇa nor Sītā feel sorry that we have been uprooted from Ayodhyā or that we are going to dwell in the forest. (28)

verses.text:
चतुर्दशसु वर्षेषु निवृत्तेषु पुनः पुनः।
लक्ष्मणं मां च सीतां च द्रक्ष्यसे शीघ्रमागतान्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘When fourteen years have elapsed, you will once more see Lakṣmaṇa, myself and Sītā too returned apace (from the forest).’ (29)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं मातरं च सुमन्त्र मे।
अन्याश्च देवीः सहिताः कैकेयीं च पुनः पुनः॥ ३०॥
आरोग्यं ब्रूहि कौसल्यामथ पादाभिवन्दनम्।
सीताया मम चार्यस्य वचनाल्लक्ष्मणस्य च॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having repeated as aforesaid to the king and my mother (Kausalyā), O Sumantra, as well as to the other queens alongwith Sumitrā, as also to Kaikeyī, tell Kausalyā that I am keeping good health. Then convey salutations at her feet on behalf of Sītā as well as myself, the elder brother, and of Lakṣmaṇa. (30-31)

verses.text:
ब्रूयाश्चापि महाराजं भरतं क्षिप्रमानय।
आगतश्चापि भरतः स्थाप्यो नृपमते पदे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Also submit to the Emperor, my father, ‘Pray, get Bharata soon. And when returned from his maternal uncle’s, Bharata should be installed in the office intended for him by Your Majesty. (32)

verses.text:
भरतं च परिष्वज्य यौवराज्येऽभिषिच्य च।
अस्मत्संतापजं दुःखं न त्वामभिभविष्यति॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “ ‘When you have met and embraced Bharata and installed him in the office of Prince Regent, the agony caused by the remorse felt by you on our account will no longer be able to overpower you.’ (33)

verses.text:
भरतश्चापि वक्तव्यो यथा राजनि वर्तसे।
तथा मातृषु वर्तेथाः सर्वास्वेवाविशेषतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Bharata too should be exhorted in the following words : ‘You should behave towards all your mothers without distinction in the same way as you do towards the king (your father). (34)

verses.text:
यथा च तव कैकेयी सुमित्रा चाविशेषतः।
तथैव देवी कौसल्या मम माता विशेषतः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Even as Kaikeyī and Sumitrā too are equally worthy of respect to you, more so is my mother, Queen Kausalyā, who is senior to all. (35)

verses.text:
तातस्य प्रियकामेन यौवराज्यमवेक्षता।
लोकयोरुभयोः शक्यं नित्यदा सुखमेधितुम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “ ‘If you accept the office of Prince Regent with intent to please our father, it will be possible for you to thrive happily in both the worlds (this world and the next).’ ”(36)

verses.text:
निवर्त्यमानो रामेण सुमन्त्रः प्रतिबोधितः।
तत्सर्वं वचनं श्रुत्वा स्नेहात् काकुत्स्थमब्रवीत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Hearing the whole of the aforesaid discourse when instructed (as above) by Śrī Rāma with a view to his being sent back to Ayodhyā, Sumantra lovingly replied to him as follows : (37)

verses.text:
यदहं नोपचारेण ब्रूयां स्नेहादविक्लवम्।
भक्तिमानिति तत् तावद् वाक्यं त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “If I speak to you in an unfaltering tone due to affection and do not speak with reverence (which is due to you as my master), you ought in fact to forgive my mode of speech, considering me as full of devotion to you. (38)

verses.text:
कथं हि त्वद्विहीनोऽहं प्रतियास्यामि तां पुरीम्।
तव तात वियोगेन पुत्रशोकातुरामिव॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Bereft of you, how shall I actually return to that city of Ayodhyā, which through separation from you has been reduced to the state of a mother stricken with grief due to separation from her son, O dear child? (39)

verses.text:
सराममपि तावन्मे रथं दृष्ट्वा तदा जनः।
विना रामं रथं दृष्ट्वा विदीर्येतापि सा पुरी॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “The people of Ayodhyā were really torn with grief even to see this chariot with Śrī Rāma (yourself) at the time of your departure from Ayodhyā. On seeing it without Śrī Rāma this time that city itself may be riven in two. (40)

verses.text:
दैन्यं हि नगरी गच्छेद् दृष्ट्वा शून्यमिमं रथम्।
सूतावशेषं स्वं सैन्यं हतवीरमिवाहवे॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “The city will be reduced to a sad plight on seeing this chariot without you, even as the army of a hero on seeing his chariot with the charioteer alone surviving, the warrior having been killed in battle. (41)

verses.text:
दूरेऽपि निवसन्तं त्वां मानसेनाग्रतः स्थितम्।
चिन्तयन्तोऽद्य नूनं त्वां निराहाराः कृताः प्रजाः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Thinking of you, who though dwelling afar, are ever mentally present before them, the people of Ayodhyā must have gone without their food and drink today. (42)

verses.text:
दृष्टं तद् वै त्वया राम यादृशं त्वत्प्रवासने।
प्रजानां संकुलं वृत्तं त्वच्छोकक्लान्तचेतसाम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “The great confusion that ensued, on (the occasion of) your exile, among the people of Ayodhyā, whose mind was depressed through grief on your account, was witnessed by you with your own eyes, O Rāma ! (43)

verses.text:
आर्तनादो हि यः पौरैरुन्मुक्तस्त्वत्प्रवासने।
सरथं मां निशाम्यैव कुर्युः शतगुणं ततः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Nay, perceiving me alone with the chariot, the people of Ayodhyā will raise a cry of distress a hundred times louder than that which was actually raised by them at the time of your banishment. (44)

verses.text:
अहं किं चापि वक्ष्यामि देवीं तव सुतो मया।
नीतोऽसौ मातुलकुलं संतापं मा कृथा इति॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Again, shall I falsely submit to the queen, Kausalyā, as follows : ‘Your son, Rāma, has been conveyed to his maternal uncle’s; pray, do not give way to agony’. (45)

verses.text:
असत्यमपि नैवाहं ब्रूयां वचनमीदृशम्।
कथमप्रियमेवाहं ब्रूयां सत्यमिदं वचः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “I dare not make such a false report, even though it is pleasing to the ear, and save her from agony for sometime. On the other hand, how can I make a correct yet unpalatable report that Rāma has proceeded to the forest? (46)

verses.text:
मम तावन्नियोगस्थास्त्वद्बन्धुजनवाहिनः।
कथं रथं त्वया हीनं प्रवाह्यन्ति हयोत्तमाः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Even if you insist on my returning to Ayodhyā at all events, how will the excellent horses drawing the chariot, which are subject to my control, and transport only your kindred and yourself, draw the chariot without you? (47)

verses.text:
तन्न शक्ष्याम्यहं गन्तुमयोध्यां त्वदृतेऽनघ।
वनवासानुयानाय मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O sinless prince, I shall not be able to return to Ayodhyā even if I try to do so without you. You ought under such circumstances to allow me to follow you to share your exile in the forest. (48)

verses.text:
यदि मे याचमानस्य त्यागमेव करिष्यसि।
सरथोऽग्निं प्रवेक्ष्यामि त्यक्तमात्र इह त्वया॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “If you still insist on leaving me, even though I solicit you to take me with you, I shall enter a fire, chariot and all, on this spot the moment I am forsaken by you. (49)

verses.text:
भविष्यन्ति वने यानि तपोविघ्नकराणि ते।
रथेन प्रतिबाधिष्ये तानि सर्वाणि राघव॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “With the help of the chariot, O scion of Raghu, I shall repel all those creatures that cause interruption in your austerities in the forest. (50)

verses.text:
त्वत्कृतेन मया प्राप्तं रथचर्याकृतं सुखम्।
आशंसे त्वत्कृतेनाहं वनवासकृतं सुखम्॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “By your kind offices the pleasure of driving your chariot was secured by me. By your grace alone I hope this time to enjoy the pleasure of dwelling with you in the forest. (51)

verses.text:
प्रसीदेच्छामि तेऽरण्ये भवितुं प्रत्यनन्तरः।
प्रीत्याभिहितमिच्छामि भव मे प्रत्यनन्तरः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Be gracious to me by allowing me to follow you to the forest. I long to be your close associate in the forest. I wish to hear your loving assent in the words ‘Be my close associate !’ (52)

verses.text:
इमेऽपि च हया वीर यदि ते वनवासिनः।
परिचर्यां करिष्यन्ति प्राप्स्यन्ति परमां गतिम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “These horses too, O heroic prince, if they get an opportunity to serve you while you dwell in the forest, will attain the highest destiny by serving their beloved master. (53)

verses.text:
तव शुश्रूषणं मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन्।
अयोध्यां देवलोकं वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्यहम्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Dwelling in the forest with you I shall render service to you with my head bent low, and in order to be allowed this privilege I quit for good in everyway Ayodhyā and even heaven, the realm of gods. (54)

verses.text:
नहि शक्या प्रवेष्टुं सा मयायोध्या त्वया विना।
राजधानी महेन्द्रस्य यथा दुष्कृतकर्मणा॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “Bereft of you, Ayodhyā is incapable of being entered by me much in the same way as Amarāvatī, the capital of the mighty Indra, is inaccessible to a man of sinful deeds. (55)

verses.text:
वनवासे क्षयं प्राप्ते ममैष हि मनोरथः।
यदनेन रथेनैव त्वां वहेयं पुरीं पुनः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Indeed this is my ambition that when your exile in the forest has come to an end, I may convey you back to Ayodhyā in this very chariot. (56)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि सहितस्य त्वया वने।
क्षणभूतानि यास्यन्ति शतसंख्यानि चान्यथा॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “So long as I remain with you in the forest, fourteen years will undoubtedly slip away past me as though reduced to as many moments; whereas if I stay away from you they will multiply a hundredfold. (57)

verses.text:
भृत्यवत्सल तिष्ठन्तं भर्तृपुत्रगते पथि।
भक्तं भृत्यं स्थितं स्थित्या न मा त्वं हातुमर्हसि॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “O prince, who are so fond of your dependants, you ought not to desert me, your devoted servant, standing resolved to tread on the path chosen by the son of his master and ever keeping within bounds.” (58)

verses.text:
एवं बहुविधं दीनं याचमानं पुनः पुनः।
रामो भृत्यानुकम्पी तु सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, for his part, compassionate as he was towards his dependants, replied as follows to Sumantra, who was piteously supplicating again and again in many ways as aforesaid : (59)

verses.text:
जानामि परमां भक्तिमहं ते भर्तृवत्सल।
शृणु चापि यदर्थं त्वां प्रेषयामि पुरीमितः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “I know your supreme devotion to me, O charioteer, so fond of your master ! Nevertheless, pray, hear wherefore I send you back to Ayodhyā from here. (60)

verses.text:
नगरीं त्वां गतं दृष्ट्वा जननी मे यवीयसी।
कैकेयी प्रत्ययं गच्छेदिति रामो वनं गतः॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “Seeing you returned to the capital, my youngest mother, Kaikeyī, should feel convinced that I, Rāma, have left for the forest. (61)

verses.text:
विपरीते तुष्टिहीना वनवासं गते मयि।
राजानं नातिशङ्केत मिथ्यावादीति धार्मिकम्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Otherwise in the event of your remaining with me, let not Kaikeyī—who is not going to derive satisfaction otherwise even on my having gone into exile in the forest—suspect the pious king to be a liar. (62)

verses.text:
एष मे प्रथमः कल्पो यदम्बा मे यवीयसी।
भरतारक्षितं स्फीतं पुत्रराज्यमवाप्स्यते॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “This is my foremost intention in sending you back to Ayodhyā that my youngest mother, Kaikeyī, should secure the kingdom of Ayodhyā, protected by Bharata and thus ruled by her own son, in good condition and this will be possible only on your returning to Ayodhyā; for till then the possibility of my returning to Ayodhyā will not be completely ruled out and till then Bharata too will not be called back to Ayodhyā and everyone will remain in a state of suspense. (63)

verses.text:
मम प्रियार्थं राज्ञश्च सुमन्त्र त्वं पुरीं व्रज।
संदिष्टश्चापि यानर्थांस्तांस्तान् ब्रूयास्तथा तथा॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “For my pleasure and for the pleasure of the Emperor, therefore, O Sumantra, return you to the capital and deliver all the messages that you have been asked to deliver, each in the way you have been asked to do.” (64)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं सूतं सान्त्वयित्वा पुनः पुनः।
गुहं वचनमक्लीबो रामो हेतुमदब्रवीत्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: Having offered explanation to the charioteer as aforesaid and consoling him again and again, Śrī Rāma, who was not feeling the least timorous, gave the following reasoned instructions to Guha : (65)

verses.text:
नेदानीं गुह योग्योऽयं वासो मे सजने वने।
अवश्यमाश्रमे वासः कर्तव्यस्तद्गतो विधिः॥ ६६॥
verses.m: “It is not proper for me on this occasion to dwell, as I am doing, in a forest in which my own men are present. Therefore, an abode must be taken up by me in a hermitage in an uninhabited region and the procedure to be followed in this behalf must be observed by me. (66)

verses.text:
सोऽहं गृहीत्वा नियमं तपस्विजनभूषणम्।
हितकामः पितुर्भूयः सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च॥ ६७॥
जटाः कृत्वा गमिष्यामि न्यग्रोधक्षीरमानय।
तत्क्षीरं राजपुत्राय गुहः क्षिप्रमुपाहरत्॥ ६८॥
verses.m: “Adopting with the concurrence of Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa a discipline in the shape of eating wild fruits, roots and bulbs etc., and reposing on the ground and so on, which serves as an embellishment for ascetics, seeking as I do the spiritual welfare of my father, and wearing matted hair, I should like to proceed further. Therefore, please bring the milk-like exudation of a banyan tree.” Guha fetched such exudation at once for the prince. (67-68)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्यात्मनश्चैव रामस्तेनाकरोज्जटाः।
दीर्घबाहुर्नरव्याघ्रो जटिलत्वमधारयत्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: With that exudation Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, who was possessed of long arms, formed his own locks as well as those of Lakṣmaṇa (who had also taken a vow of ascetic life) into a mass of clotted hair and thus wore the distinguishing mark of an ascetic in the shape of matted hair. (69)

verses.text:
तौ तदा चीरसम्पन्नौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ।
अशोभेतामृषिसमौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Clad in the bark of trees and wearing a rounded mass of matted locks on their head those two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, looked charming at that time like two Ṛṣis (ascetic sages). (70)

verses.text:
ततो वैखानसं मार्गमास्थितः सहलक्ष्मणः।
व्रतमादिष्टवान् रामः सहायं गुहमब्रवीत्॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Having temporarily adopted the ways of a hermit alongwith Lakṣmaṇa and accepted the vow of an ascetic life, Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to his helpmate, Guha : (71)

verses.text:
अप्रमत्तो बले कोशे दुर्गे जनपदे तथा।
भवेथा गुह राज्यं हि दुरारक्षतमं मतम्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “Remain vigilant in the matter of your army, exchequer, fortress and the people, O Guha; for a state is recognized as most difficult to protect.” (72)

verses.text:
ततस्तं समनुज्ञाप्य गुहमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।
जगाम तूर्णमव्यग्रः सभार्यः सहलक्ष्मणः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Having duly taken leave of the celebrated Guha, and remaining undisturbed all the time, Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣwākus, then quickly departed alongwith his consort, Sītā, and with Lakṣmaṇa. (73)

verses.text:
स तु दृष्ट्वा नदीतीरे नावमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः।
तितीर्षुः शीघ्रगां गङ्गामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: Beholding a boat on the bank of the river and keen to cross the swift-flowing Gaṅgā, Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Ikṣwākus, for his part spoke to Lakṣmaṇa as follows : (74)

verses.text:
आरोह त्वं नरव्याघ्र स्थितां नावमिमां शनैः।
सीतां चारोपयान्वक्षं परिगृह्य मनस्विनीम्॥ ७५॥
verses.m: “Holding the boat standing there and thereby steadying it, help the timid Sītā to get into it slowly and step you into it forthwith, O lion among men !” (75)

verses.text:
स भ्रातुः शासनं श्रुत्वा सर्वमप्रतिकूलयन्।
आरोप्य मैथिलीं पूर्वमारुरोहात्मवांस्ततः॥ ७६॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of his elder brother and helping Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, to get into the boat first, the self-possessed Lakṣmaṇa stepped into the boat afterwards, thus acting in full conformity with his brother’s command. (76)

verses.text:
अथारुरोह तेजस्वी स्वयं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।
ततो निषादाधिपतिर्गुहो ज्ञातीनचोदयत्॥ ७७॥
verses.m: The glorious Rāma (elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa) himself got into the boat last; and after that Guha, the ruler of the Niṣādas, commanded his kinsmen to row the boat across the stream. (77)

verses.text:
राघवोऽपि महातेजा नावमारुह्य तां ततः।
ब्रह्मवत्क्षत्रवच्चैव जजाप हितमात्मनः॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Having got into the aforesaid boat, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part, who was possessed of unique splendour, then recited a sacred text (दैवी नावम् etc.,) fit for the Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas alike and conducive to his own good. (78)

verses.text:
आचम्य च यथाशास्त्रं नदीं तां सह सीतया।
प्रणमत्प्रीतिसंतुष्टो लक्ष्मणश्च महारथः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: Nay, sipping the water of the Gaṅgā according to the scriptural ordinance and feeling highly gratified, Śrī Rāma with Sītā bowed low to that river and Lakṣmaṇa, the great car-warrior, followed suit. (79)

verses.text:
अनुज्ञाय सुमन्त्रं च सबलं चैव तं गुहम्।
आस्थाय नावं रामस्तु चोदयामास नाविकान्॥ ८०॥
verses.m: Further, bidding farewell to Sumantra as well as to the celebrated Guha and his army and, occupying his seat in the boat, Śrī Rāma for his part urged the boatmen to row the boat. (80)

verses.text:
ततस्तैश्चालिता नौका कर्णधारसमाहिता।
शुभस्फ्यवेगाभिहता शीघ्रं सलिलमत्यगात्॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Rowed by the boatmen and directed by the helmsman, the boat, propelled by the swift movement of the beautiful oars, moved swiftly across the water. (81)

verses.text:
मध्यं तु समनुप्राप्य भागीरथ्यास्त्वनिन्दिता।
वैदेही प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तां नदीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Having duly reached the middle of the Gaṅgā, Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, for her part, who was irreproachable in everyway, spoke as follows with joined palms to the said river : (82)

verses.text:
पुत्रो दशरथस्यायं महाराजस्य धीमतः।
निदेशं पालयत्वेनं गङ्गे त्वदभिरक्षितः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: “Protected on all sides by you, O mother Gaṅgā, may this son of the wise Emperor Daśaratha execute this decree of the Emperor to remain in exile for fourteen years. (83)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि समग्राण्युष्य कानने।
भ्रात्रा सह मया चैव पुनः प्रत्यागमिष्यति॥ ८४॥
ततस्त्वां देवि सुभगे क्षेमेण पुनरागता।
यक्ष्ये प्रमुदिता गङ्गे सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी॥ ८५॥
verses.m: “When, having sojourned in the forest for full fourteen years, he arrives at your bank once more with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, and myself, then, returned in safety, O blessed goddess, with all my desires fulfilled, O Gaṅgā, I shall worship you with great delight. (84-85)

verses.text:
त्वं हि त्रिपथगे देवि ब्रह्मलोकं समक्षसे।
भार्या चोदधिराजस्य लोकेऽस्मिन् सम्प्रदृश्यसे॥ ८६॥
सा त्वां देवि नमस्यामि प्रशंसामि च शोभने।
प्राप्तराज्ये नरव्याघ्रे शिवेन पुनरागते॥ ८७॥
गवां शतसहस्रं च वस्त्राण्यन्नं च पेशलम्।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदास्यामि तव प्रियचिकीर्षया॥ ८८॥
verses.m: “Since you, O goddess, flowing through heaven, earth and the subterranean regions, include in your basin the realm of Brahmā (the outermost of the six spheres enveloping the earth) and are vividly seen on this terrestrial plane as a consort of the Ocean-king, the deity presiding over the oceans, I, Sītā, greet and extol you, O charming goddess ! When Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, has safely returned and regained his throne, I shall give away a lakh of cows as well as articles of wearing apparel and food-stuffs of excellent quality to the Brahmans with intent to please you. (86—88)

verses.text:
सुराघटसहस्रेण मांसभूतौदनेन च।
यक्ष्ये त्वां प्रीयतां देवि पुरीं पुनरुपागता॥ ८९॥
verses.m: “Having returned to Ayodhyā, I shall worship you with thousand and one articles not available even to gods as well as with lands free from revenue, raiment and cooked rice*. Be pleased with me, O goddess ! (89)

verses.text:
यानि त्वत्तीरवासीनि दैवतानि च सन्ति हि।
तानि सर्वाणि यक्ष्यामि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च॥ ९०॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall without doubt offer worship to all the deities that have their abode on your banks as well as to all sacred spots and sites on your banks. (90)

verses.text:
पुनरेव महाबाहुर्मया भ्रात्रा च संगतः।
अयोध्यां वनवासात् तु प्रविशत्वनघोऽनघे॥ ९१॥
verses.m: “May the sinless Rāma, who is possessed of mighty arms for his part re-enter Ayodhyā from the forest alongwith Lakṣmaṇa and myself, O sinless goddess !” (91)

verses.text:
तथा सम्भाषमाणा सा सीता गङ्गामनिन्दिता।
दक्षिणा दक्षिणं तीरं क्षिप्रमेवाभ्युपागमत्॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Praying to Gaṅgā as aforesaid, the celebrated Sītā, who was irreproachable in everyway and devoted to her husband, speedily reached the southern bank. (92)

verses.text:
तीरं तु समनुप्राप्य नावं हित्वा नरर्षभः।
प्रातिष्ठत सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या च परंतपः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Having safely reached the aforesaid bank and leaving the boat, Śrī Rāma, a jewel among men, the chastiser of his foes, for his part, proceeded further with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom. (93)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महाबाहुः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनम्।
भव संरक्षणार्थाय सजने विजनेऽपि वा॥ ९४॥
verses.m: The mighty-armed prince now said to Lakṣmaṇa (who heightened the joy of Sumitrā). “Be prepared for the protection of Sītā in the inhabited as well as in the uninhabited areas. (94)

verses.text:
अवश्यं रक्षणं कार्यं मद्विधैर्विजने वने।
अग्रतो गच्छ सौमित्रे सीता त्वामनुगच्छतु॥ ९५॥
verses.m: “Protection needs must be afforded in an uninhabited forest to the weaker sex by men like me, who maintain the moral order. Therefore, lead the way, O son of Sumitrā, and let Sītā follow you. (95)

verses.text:
पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि सीतां त्वां चानुपालयन्।
अन्योन्यस्य हि नो रक्षा कर्तव्या पुरुषर्षभ॥ ९६॥
verses.m: “I, for my part, shall follow in the rear, protecting Sītā as well as yourself from behind; for protection must be vouchsafed by us to one another, O jewel among men! (96)

verses.text:
न हि तावदतिक्रान्तासुकरा काचन क्रिया।
अद्य दुःखं तु वैदेही वनवासस्य वेत्स्यति॥ ९७॥
verses.m: “In fact, no severe trial has gone out of possibility as yet. On the other hand, Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, will experience only today, the suffering entailed by a sojourn in the forest. (97)

verses.text:
प्रणष्टजनसम्बाधं क्षेत्रारामविवर्जितम्।
विषमं च प्रपातं च वनमद्य प्रवेक्ष्यति॥ ९८॥
verses.m: “She will enter today a forest in which traces of blades of grass etc., having been crushed under the feet of men are no longer visible, there being no traffic of men, which is utterly devoid of fields and gardens, has a rugged surface and is full of yawning chasms etc.” (98)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं प्रतस्थे लक्ष्मणोऽग्रतः।
अनन्तरं च सीताया राघवो रघुनन्दनः॥ ९९॥
verses.m: Hearing the advice of Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa led the way, Sītā following him, and immediately after Sītā followed Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the delight of the Raghus. (99)

verses.text:
गतं तु गङ्गापरपारमाशु
रामं सुमन्त्रः सततं निरीक्ष्य।
अध्वप्रकर्षाद् विनिवृत्तदृष्टि-
र्मुमोच बाष्पं व्यथितस्तपस्वी॥ १००॥
verses.m: Constantly gazing on Śrī Rāma, who had soon reached the other bank of the Gaṅgā, and his vision having failed due to the long distance covered by the exiles in the meantime, Sumantra, who was full of remorse and afflicted too, shed tears of grief over his separation from Śrī Rāma. (100)

verses.text:
स लोकपालप्रतिमप्रभाव-
स्तीर्त्वा महात्मा वरदो महानदीम्।
ततः समृद्धान् शुभसस्यमालिनः
क्रमेण वत्सान् मुदितानुपागमत्॥ १०१॥
verses.m: Having crossed the great river Gaṅgā, the high-souled Śrī Rāma, who vied in glory with the guardians of the spheres and was capable of bestowing boons, thence reached step by step the prosperous and happy land of Vatsa, the land comprised between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā rivers, which contained rows of beautiful crops. (101)

verses.text:
तौ तत्र हत्वा चतुरो महामृगान्
वराहमृश्यं पृषतं महारुरुम्।
आदाय मेध्यं त्वरितं बुभुक्षितौ
वासाय काले ययतुर्वनस्पतिम्॥ १०२॥
verses.m: Having hunted for love of sport four large deer, viz., a Varāha, Ṛśya, Pṛṣata and Mahāruru (the four principal species of deer), and taking with them articles of food consisting of fruits etc. fit for being consigned as an oblation into the sacred fire, now that they felt hungry (after sport), the two brothers quickly sought the foot of a tree where they had evidently stationed Sītā within their sight for the time they were engaged in sport, for taking rest after supper during the night. (102)

verses.text:
स तं वृक्षं समासाद्य संध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्।
रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठ इति होवाच लक्ष्मणम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having reached the foot of the aforesaid tree and worshipped the evening twilight, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those affording delight to others., spoke to Lakṣmaṇa as follows: so the tradition goes : (1)

verses.text:
अद्येयं प्रथमा रात्रिर्याता जनपदाद् बहिः।
या सुमन्त्रेण रहिता तां नोत्कण्ठितुमर्हसि॥ २॥
verses.m: “This night, which has overtaken us today outside the territory inhabited by our own people, is the first night which will pass without Sumantra. You ought not to sorrow over it. (2)

verses.text:
जागर्तव्यमतन्द्रिभ्यामद्यप्रभृति रात्रिषु।
योगक्षेमौ हि सीताया वर्तेते लक्ष्मणावयोः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Remaining free from lassitude, we must both keep awake during the coming nights; for the procuration of what is needed by Sītā and the protection of her person and honour etc., are our care, O Lakṣmaṇa! (3)

verses.text:
रात्रिं कथंचिदेवेमां सौमित्रे वर्तयामहे।
अपवर्तामहे भूमावास्तीर्य स्वयमर्जितैः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Let us pass this night anyhow, O son of Sumitrā! Let us lie down on the ground, covering it with straw, leaves and so on procured with our own hands.” (4)

verses.text:
स तु संविश्य मेदिन्यां महार्हशयनोचितः।
इमाः सौमित्रये रामो व्याजहार कथाः शुभाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Sitting on the bare ground, the said Śrī Rāma, for his part, who was accustomed to costly beds, addressed the following suitable remarks to Lakṣmaṇa : (5)

verses.text:
ध्रुवमद्य महाराजो दुःखं स्वपिति लक्ष्मण।
कृतकामा तु कैकेयी तुष्टा भवितुमर्हति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Surely the Emperor must be sleeping uncomfortably tonight, O Lakṣmaṇa ! Kaikeyī, on the other hand, who has her desired object accomplished, ought to feel gratified. (6)

verses.text:
सा हि देवी महाराजं कैकेयी राज्यकारणात्।
अपि न च्यावयेत् प्राणान् दृष्ट्वा भरतमागतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Seeing Bharata returned from his maternal grandfather’s, Queen Kaikeyī, I am afraid, may not actually rob the Emperor of his very life for the sake of sovereignty. (7)

verses.text:
अनाथश्च हि वृद्धश्च मया चैव विना कृतः।
किं करिष्यति कामात्मा कैकेय्या वशमागतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “What will the king—whose desire to see me installed as Prince Regent lingers even now in his mind and who has fallen into the clutches of Kaikeyī, nay, who is aged and, therefore, helpless and has further been disunited from me—do to foil her designs upon his life? (8)

verses.text:
इदं व्यसनमालोक्य राज्ञश्च मतिविभ्रमम्।
काम एवार्थधर्माभ्यां गरीयानिति मे मतिः॥ ९॥
