verses.m: “Viewing this evil plight of mine and the perversion of the king’s mind, I am led to think that gratification of the senses is of greater moment than earthly gain and religious merit. (9)

verses.text:
को ह्यविद्वानपि पुमान् प्रमदायाः कृते त्यजेत्।
छन्दानुवर्तिनं पुत्रं तातो मामिव लक्ष्मण॥ १०॥
verses.m: “What man, even though ignorant, would actually abandon for the sake of a woman, a son following his will, even as father has abandoned me, O Lakṣmaṇa? (10)

verses.text:
सुखी बत सुभार्यश्च भरतः केकयीसुतः।
मुदितान् कोसलानेको यो भोक्ष्यत्यधिराजवत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Ah, Kaikeyī’s son, Bharata alone is happy and the spouse of a lucky woman in that he is going to rule over the prosperous kingdom of Kosala like an overlord, his claim being disputed by none! (11)

verses.text:
स हि राज्यस्य सर्वस्य सुखमेकं भविष्यति।
ताते तु वयसातीते मयि चारण्यमाश्रिते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “For, he will enjoy the undivided blessings of the entire kingdom, now that father is superannuated and I have retired to the forest. (12)

verses.text:
अर्थधर्मौ परित्यज्य यः काममनुवर्तते।
एवमापद्यते क्षिप्रं राजा दशरथो यथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “He who pursues sensuous pleasure, neglecting wealth and virtue, soon comes to grief in the same way as King Daśaratha has. (13)

verses.text:
मन्ये दशरथान्ताय मम प्रव्राजनाय च।
कैकेयी सौम्य सम्प्राप्ता राज्याय भरतस्य च॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I believe, O good brother, that Kaikeyī came to this house to bring about the end of Daśaratha, to send me into exile and to secure kingship for Bharata. (14)

verses.text:
अपीदानीं तु कैकेयी सौभाग्यमदमोहिता।
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च सा प्रबाधेत मत्कृते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Blinded by pride of good fortune, I am afraid, the aforesaid Kaikeyī may even now persecute Kausalyā and Sumitrā too because of their relation with me and you. (15)

verses.text:
मातास्मत्कारणाद् देवी सुमित्रा दुःखमावसेत्।
अयोध्यामित एव त्वं काले प्रविश लक्ष्मण॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Your mother, Queen Sumitrā, is likely to suffer hardship because of her affinity to us. From this very place, therefore, O Lakṣmaṇa, proceed you to Ayodhyā next morning. (16)

verses.text:
अहमेको गमिष्यामि सीतया सह दण्डकान्।
अनाथाया हि नाथस्त्वं कौसल्याया भविष्यसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I shall proceed to the Daṇḍaka forest alone with Sītā, while you will be a protector to Kausalyā, who will be left without a protector after the death of King Daśaratha. (17)

verses.text:
क्षुद्रकर्मा हि कैकेयी द्वेषादन्यायमाचरेत्।
परिदद्याद्धि धर्मज्ञ गरं ते मम मातरम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Kaikeyī of vile deeds may undoubtedly resort to unfair means due to malice and even administer poison to your mother and mine, O knower of what is right ! (18)

verses.text:
नूनं जात्यन्तरे तात स्त्रियः पुत्रैर्वियोजिताः।
जनन्या मम सौमित्रे तदद्यैतदुपस्थितम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “In some other past birth, O dear brother, women must have been deprived of their sons by my mother, Kausalyā. That act of hers alone, O Lakṣmaṇa, has recoiled on her in the form of this visitation. (19)

verses.text:
मया हि चिरपुष्टेन दुःखसंवर्धितेन च।
विप्रयुज्यत कौसल्या फलकाले धिगस्तु माम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “At a time when Kausalyā, my mother, should have found her labours repaid by me, she has been deprived of my company by me, who was nurtured by her for long years and brought up with great pains. Woe to me ! (20)

verses.text:
मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज्जनयेत् पुत्रमीदृशम्।
सौमित्रे योऽहमम्बाया दद्मि शोकमनन्तकम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let no matron give birth to such a son as myself, who, O Lakṣmaṇa, have inflicted endless sorrow on my mother ! (21)

verses.text:
मन्ये प्रीतिविशिष्टा सा मत्तो लक्ष्मण सारिका।
यत्तस्याः श्रूयते वाक्यं शुक पादमरेर्दश॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I believe that myna, which is kept as a pet by mother Kausalyā, O Lakṣmaṇa, is more affectionate towards my mother than I, since from her are heard the words ‘Bite, O parrot, the foot of the enemy of our master and thereby render him incapable of marching against our master.’ (22)

verses.text:
शोचन्त्याश्चाल्पभाग्याया न किंचिदुपकुर्वता।
पुत्रेण किमपुत्राया मया कार्यमरिंदम॥ २३॥
verses.m: “What purpose of my grieving mother of poor luck, who is as good as issueless, can be served by me, her son, who does no good to her, O chastiser of foes? (23)

verses.text:
अल्पभाग्या हि मे माता कौसल्या रहिता मया।
शेते परमदुःखार्ता पतिता शोकसागरे॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Of poor luck indeed is my mother, Kausalyā, who, bereft as she is of me, is stricken with great agony and lies plunged in a sea of grief. (24)

verses.text:
एको ह्यहमयोध्यां च पृथिवीं चापि लक्ष्मण।
तरेयमिषुभिः क्रुद्धो ननु वीर्यमकारणम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “When enraged I can surely subdue with my arrows single-handed not only the kingdom of Ayodhyā but the earth as well, O Lakṣmaṇa ! But show of valour is not always conducive to good in the other world. (25)

verses.text:
अधर्मभयभीतश्च परलोकस्य चानघ।
तेन लक्ष्मण नाद्याहमात्मानमभिषेचये॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I am afraid of sin that will be incurred by me if I fail to help my father in implementing the boons conferred by him on Kaikeyī as well as of ruining my prospects in the other world, O sinless Lakṣmaṇa ! Hence I do not install myself in the office of Prince Regent (by force) today.” (26)

verses.text:
एतदन्यच्च करुणं विलप्य विजने बहु।
अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनो निशि तूष्णीमुपाविशत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Having wailed piteously as aforesaid and in many other ways in that lonely forest, Śrī Rāma sat quiet during the night, afflicted as he was, his face bathed in tears. (27)

verses.text:
विलापोपरतं रामं गतार्चिषमिवानलम्।
समुद्रमिव निर्वेगमाश्वासयत लक्ष्मणः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa comforted Śrī Rāma as follows when the latter had ceased lamenting and looked like a fire whose flames had gone out and a sea that had lost its vehemence : (28)

verses.text:
ध्रुवमद्य पुरी राम अयोध्याऽऽयुधिनां वर।
निष्प्रभा त्वयि निष्क्रान्ते गतचन्द्रेव शर्वरी॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The city of Ayodhyā, O Rāma, now that you have come away from it, has undoubtedly been divested of its splendour and resembles a night without the moon, O jewel among armed warriors ! (29)

verses.text:
नैतदौपयिकं राम यदिदं परितप्यसे।
विषादयसि सीतां च मां चैव पुरुषर्षभ॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “It is not desirable, O Rāma, that you should grieve in this way. You make Sītā and myself too sad thereby, O jewel among men! (30)

verses.text:
न च सीता त्वया हीना न चाहमपि राघव।
मुहूर्तमपि जीवावो जलान्मत्स्याविवोद्धृतौ॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Bereft of you, O scion of Raghu, neither Sītā nor I myself can survive even for a shortwhile any more than fish taken out of water. (31)

verses.text:
नहि तातं न शत्रुघ्नं न सुमित्रां परंतप।
द्रष्टुमिच्छेयमद्याहं स्वर्गं चापि त्वया विना॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Today I wish to see neither father nor Śatrughna (my younger brother) nor Sumitrā (my own mother) nor even heaven without you, O tormentor of foes !” (32)

verses.text:
ततस्तत्र समासीनौ नातिदूरे निरीक्ष्य ताम्।
न्यग्रोधे सुकृतां शय्यां भेजाते धर्मवत्सलौ॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Perceiving a bed decently prepared by Lakṣmaṇa at the foot of the banyan tree not very far from the place occupied by them, while they were comfortably seated there, Śrī Rāma and Sītā, who were tenderly alive to their duty, then sought the bed. (33)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणस्योत्तमपुष्कलं वचो
निशम्य चैवं वनवासमादरात्।
समाः समस्ता विदधे परंतपः
प्रपद्य धर्मं सुचिराय राघवः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Hearing attentively the excellently-worded and comprehensive submission of Lakṣmaṇa, reproduced above, and embracing for a fairly lengthy period the course of conduct prescribed for hermits, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the tormentor of foes, resolved to spend all the years of his exile with Lakṣmaṇa. (34)

verses.text:
ततस्तु तस्मिन् विजने महाबलौ
महावने राघववंशवर्धनौ।
न तौ भयं सम्भ्रममभ्युपेयतु-
र्यथैव सिंहौ गिरिसानुगोचरौ॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Thenceforward the two exceptionally mighty princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the promoters of the race of Raghu, never experienced fear or agitation while dwelling in that great lonely forest any more than a couple of lions living on a mountain-peak. (35)

verses.text:
ते तु तस्मिन् महावृक्षे उषित्वा रजनीं शुभाम्।
विमलेऽभ्युदिते सूर्ये तस्माद् देशात् प्रतस्थिरे॥ १॥
verses.m: Having spent the beautiful night under that big tree, the party for their part set out from that place when the sun had clearly risen. (1)

verses.text:
यत्र भागीरथीं गङ्गां यमुनाभिप्रवर्तते।
जग्मुस्तं देशमुद्दिश्य विगाह्य सुमहद् वनम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Travelling across a fairly extensive forest they proceeded in the direction of that region where the Yamunā rushes to meet the Gaṅgā (associated with the name of Emperor Bhagīratha, who had the credit of bringing down the stream to the terrestrial plane by dint of his devotion and austerities in order to purify the ashes of his departed great granduncles). (2)

verses.text:
तेभूमिभागान् विविधान् देशांश्चापि मनोहरान्।
अदृष्टपूर्वान् पश्यन्तस्तत्र तत्र यशस्विनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Beholding here and there various tracts of land and soul-captivating regions never seen before, the illustrious travellers moved on. (3)

verses.text:
यथा क्षेमेण सम्पश्यन् पुष्पितान् विविधान् द्रुमान्।
निर्वृत्तमात्रे दिवसे रामः सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
प्रयागमभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूममुत्तमम्।
अग्नेर्भगवतः केतुं मन्ये संनिहितो मुनिः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Gazing on the various trees laden with blossoms while travelling at ease, Śrī Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) when the day had just ended : “Behold, O son of Sumitrā, agreeable fragrant smoke, the emblem of the glorious god of fire near Prayāga (the confluence of the holy Gaṅgā and Yamunā rivers). From this I conclude the sage Bharadwāja is near about. (4-5)

verses.text:
नूनं प्राप्ताः स्म सम्भेदं गङ्गायमुनयोर्वयम्।
तथाहि श्रूयते शब्दो वारिणोर्वारिघर्षजः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “We have surely reached the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā rivers; for the noise produced by the clashing of the waters of the two streams is heard.(6)

verses.text:
दारूणि परिभिन्नानि वनजैरुपजीविभिः।
छिन्नाश्चाप्याश्रमे चैते दृश्यन्ते विविधा द्रुमाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Logs of wood, hewn by men living by the produce of the forest, as also the trees of various kinds thus dismembered are seen in the hermitage here.” (7)

verses.text:
धन्विनौ तौ सुखं गत्वा लम्बमाने दिवाकरे।
गङ्गायमुनयोः संधौ प्रापतुर्निलयं मुनेः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Walking at ease the aforesaid two archers reached the outskirts of the sage’s dwelling in the space intervening the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, while the sun was going down. (8)

verses.text:
रामस्त्वाश्रममासाद्य त्रासयन् मृगपक्षिणः।
गत्वा मुहूर्तमध्वानं भरद्वाजमुपागमत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having reached the precincts of the hermitage and scaring the beasts and birds of the locality by his very appearance as a bowman and covering the intervening distance, which could be covered in a short while, Śrī Rāma for his part approached the hermitage of Bharadwāja. (9)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वाश्रममासाद्य मुनेर्दर्शनकांक्षिणौ।
सीतयानुगतौ वीरौ दूरादेवावतस्थतुः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Arriving at the hermitage, the two valiant princes, for their part, who longed for a sight of the sage and were accompanied by Sītā, then halted at some distance awaiting his permission to see him. (10)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्य महात्मानमृषिं शिष्यगणैर्वृतम्।
संशितव्रतमेकाग्रं तपसा लब्धचक्षुषम्॥ ११॥
हुताग्निहोत्रं दृष्ट्वैव महाभागः कृताञ्जलिः।
रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सीतया चाभ्यवादयत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Eventually entering the hut occupied by the sage after obtaining his permission through some pupil, and beholding the high-souled sage of rigid vows,who had acquired omniscience through askesis and sat absorbed in meditation in the midst of hosts of his pupils, having poured oblations into the sacred fire, the celebrated and highly blessed Śrī Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) and Sītā, greeted him with folded hands. (11-12)

verses.text:
न्यवेदयत चात्मानं तस्मै लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।
पुत्रौ दशरथस्यावां भगवन् रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १३॥
भार्या ममेयं कल्याणी वैदेही जनकात्मजा।
मां चानुयाता विजनं तपोवनमनिन्दिता॥ १४॥
verses.m: Nay, Śrī Rāma, the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa, introduced himself to the sage in the following words : “We are Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, sons of Emperor Daśaratha, O venerable sage! Here is my blessed and irreproachable wife, a princess of the Videha kingdom and daughter of King Janaka, who has followed me to the lonely forest suited for religious austerities. (13-14)

verses.text:
पित्रा प्रव्राज्यमानं मां सौमित्रिरनुजः प्रियः।
अयमन्वगमद् भ्राता वनमेव धृतव्रतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “While I was being exiled by my father, this my beloved younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), of firm vows has also followed me to the forest. (15)

verses.text:
पित्रा नियुक्ता भगवन् प्रवेक्ष्यामस्तपोवनम्।
धर्ममेवाचरिष्यामस्तत्र मूलफलाशनाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Ordered by our father, O venerable sage, we shall retire to a forest suited for austerities and shall practise virtue alone there, living on roots and fruits only.” (16)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः।
उपानयत धर्मात्मा गामर्घ्यमुदकं ततः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid submission of the sagacious prince, Śrī Rāma, Sage Bharadwāja, whose mind is given to piety, thereupon offered to him by way of a present due to an honoured guest a bull as well as water to wash his hands with as a preliminary to the hospitality that was to follow. (17)

verses.text:
नानाविधानन्नरसान् वन्यमूलफलाश्रयान्।
तेभ्यो ददौ तप्ततपा वासं चैवाभ्यकल्पयत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: The sage, who had practised austerities, offered them delicacies of all descriptions prepared from wild roots and fruits, and also arranged accommodation for them. (18)

verses.text:
मृगपक्षिभिरासीनो मुनिभिश्च समन्ततः।
राममागतमभ्यर्च्य स्वागतेनागतं मुनिः॥ १९॥
प्रतिगृह्य तु तामर्चामुपविष्टं स राघवम्।
भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं धर्मयुक्तमिदं तदा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Honouring with words of welcome Śrī Rāma, who had approached him by slow stages pausing a little at intervals and then advancing meticulously out of respect, the said Sage Bharadwāja, seated in the company of beasts and birds as well as of hermits all round, now addressed the following words, consistent with righteousness, to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who had since taken his seat after accepting the aforesaid hospitality offered by the sage : (19-20)

verses.text:
चिरस्य खलु काकुत्स्थ पश्याम्यहमुपागतम्।
श्रुतं तव मया चैव विवासनमकारणम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “In fact, I have since long been expecting your arrival, O scion of Kakutstha ! And your gratuitous exile has also been heard of by me. (21)

verses.text:
अवकाशो विविक्तोऽयं महानद्योः समागमे।
पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च वसत्विह भवान् सुखम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “This open stretch of land at the confluence of the two great rivers is not only secluded but sacred and lovely too. Dwell you here comfortably.” (22)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु वचनं भरद्वाजेन राघवः।
प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं रामः सर्वहिते रतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Addressed in these words by Bharadwāja, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part, who was devoted to the good of all, replied in the following agreeable words : (23)

verses.text:
भगवन्नित आसन्नः पौरजानपदो जनः।
सुदर्शमिह मां प्रेक्ष्य मन्येऽहमिममाश्रमम्॥ २४॥
आगमिष्यति वैदेहीं मां चापि प्रेक्षको जनः।
अनेन कारणेनाहमिह वासं न रोचये॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The people of the city as well as of the state of Ayodhyā, O venerable sir, are proximate to this place. Finding me easy to behold at this place, people keen to gaze on Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, as well as on myself, I presume, will frequent this hermitage. For this reason I do not relish my sojourn here. (24-25)

verses.text:
एकान्ते पश्य भगवन्नाश्रमस्थानमुत्तमम्।
रमते यत्र वैदेही सुखार्हा जनकात्मजा॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Pray, therefore, look for some excellent site for a hermitage in some lonely place, O venerable sir, where Sītā (a princess of the Videha dynasty), daughter of King Janaka, who deserves every comfort, may find delight.” (26)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः।
राघवस्य तु तद् वाक्यमर्थग्राहकमब्रवीत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Hearing this pious submission of Śrī Rāma, the great sage Bharadwāja for his part made the following answer pointing out the place sought by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu : (27)

verses.text:
दशक्रोश इतस्तात गिरिर्यस्मिन् निवत्स्यसि।
महर्षिसेवितः पुण्यः पर्वतः शुभदर्शनः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Sixty* miles from this place, O dear son, lies a sacred mountain, on which you take up your abode, which is inhabited by great Ṛṣis and is charming to look at, and has a number of offshoots. (28)

verses.text:
गोलाङ्गूलानुचरितो वानरर्क्षनिषेवितः।
चित्रकूट इति ख्यातो गन्धमादनसंनिभः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “It is infested by the black species of monkeys with a long tail (of the size of a cow-tail), is haunted by apes and bears, is known by the name of Citrakūta and closely resembles the Gandhamādana mountain in beauty. (29)

verses.text:
यावता चित्रकूटस्य नरः शृङ्गाण्यवेक्षते।
कल्याणानि समाधत्ते न पापे कुरुते मनः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “So long as a man beholds the peaks of the Citrakūṭa hill, he devotes himself entirely to virtuous acts and never sets his mind on sin. (30)

verses.text:
ऋषयस्तत्र बहवो विहृत्य शरदां शतम्।
तपसा दिवमारूढाः कपालशिरसा सह॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having spent a hundred winters in austerities as though in sport on that mountain, many a seer with a head hoary through age as a bare skull ascended to heaven. (31)

verses.text:
प्रविविक्तमहं मन्ये तं वासं भवतः सुखम्।
इह वा वनवासाय वस राम मया सह॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “I consider that mountain to be a very lonely and comfortable place for you to live in. Else dwell with me here at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā for the period of exile.” (32)

verses.text:
स रामं सर्वकामैस्तं भरद्वाजः प्रियातिथिम्।
सभार्यं सह च भ्रात्रा प्रतिजग्राह हर्षयन्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: The celebrated Sage Bharadwāja entertained his aforesaid beloved guest, Śrī Rāma, with his consort, Sītā, and with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, delighting them with all desired objects. (33)

verses.text:
तस्य प्रयागे रामस्य तं महर्षिमुपेयुषः।
प्रपन्ना रजनी पुण्या चित्राः कथयतः कथाः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: While Śrī Rāma, having approached that great seer at Prayāga (the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā), was talking with him on various topics, the delightful night arrived. (34)

verses.text:
सीतातृतीयः काकुत्स्थः परिश्रान्तः सुखोचितः।
भरद्वाजाश्रमे रम्ये तां रात्रिमवसत् सुखम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Greatly fatigued, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who was accompanied by Sītā as the third (Lakṣmaṇa being the second) and deserved all comforts, happily spent that night at the lovely hermitage of Bharadwāja. (35)

verses.text:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां भरद्वाजमुपागमत्।
उवाच नरशार्दूलो मुनिं ज्वलिततेजसम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: The night having ended in dawn, Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, approached and spoke as follows to Sage Bharadwāja of resplendent glory : (36)

verses.text:
शर्वरीं भगवन्नद्य सत्यशील तवाश्रमे।
उषिताः स्मोऽह वसतिमनुजानातु नो भवान्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “We have lodged tonight at your hermitage, O venerable sir ! Pray, allow us to proceed to the place fixed for our abode now, O sage given to truthfulness !” (37)

verses.text:
रात्र्यां तु तस्यां व्युष्टायां भरद्वाजोऽब्रवीदिदम्।
मधुमूलफलोपेतं चित्रकूटं व्रजेति ह॥ ३८॥
verses.m: That night having come to an end, Bharadwāja, when requested as above, replied for his part, they say, as follows : “Proceed gladly to Citrakūṭa, rich in honey, roots and fruits. (38)

verses.text:
वासमौपयिकं मन्ये तव राम महाबल।
नानानगगणोपेतः किन्नरोरगसेवितः॥ ३९॥
मयूरनादाभिरतो गजराजनिषेवितः।
गम्यतां भवता शैलश्चित्रकूटः स विश्रुतः॥ ४०॥
पुण्यश्च रमणीयश्च बहुमूलफलायुतः।
तत्र कुञ्जरयूथानि मृगयूथानि चैव हि॥ ४१॥
विचरन्ति वनान्तेषु तानि द्रक्ष्यसि राघव।
सरित्प्रस्रवणप्रस्थान् दरीकन्दरनिर्झरान्।
चरतः सीतया सार्धं नन्दिष्यति मनस्तव॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I deem it a fit place for your abode, O Rāma, possessed of great strength ! Repair you to that well-known sacred and lovely mountain, Citrakūṭa, which is adorned with clusters of trees of every description and frequented by Kinnaras and Nāgas, is rendered charming by the cries of peacocks and infested with lordly elephants and abounds in roots and fruits. Since herds of elephants as well as troops of deer roam about in the sylvan regions there, you will behold them, O scion of Raghu, as well as rivers, cascades, peaks of mountains, fissures in rocks, caves and rivulets, which will delight your mind as you roam about in the woods with Sītā. (39—42)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टकोयष्टिभकोकिलस्वनै-
र्विनोदयन्तं च सुखं परं शिवम्।
मृगैश्च मत्तैर्बहुभिश्च कुञ्जरैः
सुरम्यमासाद्य समावसाश्रयम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Reaching the agreeable and highly blessed mountain, which entertains the visitors with the notes of the overjoyed §Tiṭṭibha bird and cuckoo, is most delightful because of its many deer and elephants in rut and is fit for habitation, take up your abode on it. (43)

verses.text:
उषित्वा रजनीं तत्र राजपुत्रावरिंदमौ।
महर्षिमभिवाद्याथ जग्मतुस्तं गिरिं प्रति॥ १॥
verses.m: Having spent the night at the hermitage of Sage Bharadwāja and greeting the great seer, the two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the subduers of their foes, forthwith proceeded in the direction of the said mountain. (1)

verses.text:
तेषां स्वस्त्ययनं चैव महर्षिः स चकार ह।
प्रस्थितान् प्रेक्ष्य तांश्चैव पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Nay, perceiving the three travellers about to start on their journey, that great seer too, so the tradition goes, performed a religious rite ensuring their safe journey (scattering boiled rice on the ground and invoking blessings through the repetition of certain sacred texts) in the same way as a father would bless his own sons (and daughter-in-law). (2)

verses.text:
ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुं वचनं स महामुनिः।
भरद्वाजो महातेजा रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Then that eminent sage, Bharadwāja, who was invested with great spiritual glory, proceeded to instruct Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of unfailing valour, as follows : (3)

verses.text:
गङ्गायमुनयोः संधिमासाद्य मनुजर्षभौ।
कालिन्दीमनुगच्छेतां नदीं पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Reaching the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, the two jewels among men, should follow the river Yamunā, which has taken a westerly course (for some distance due to the great rush of the waters of the Gaṅgā). (4)

verses.text:
अथासाद्य तु कालिन्दीं प्रतिस्रोतःसमागताम्।
तस्यास्तीर्थं प्रचरितं प्रकामं प्रेक्ष्य राघव।
तत्र यूयं प्लवं कृत्वा तरतांशुमतीं नदीम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Then, approaching the Yamunā turned in an opposite direction, and carefully perceiving in it a passage (across the river) too much frequented, O scion of Raghu, cross you the river Yamunā (the deity presiding over which is the daughter of the sun-god) after preparing a raft. (5)

verses.text:
ततो न्यग्रोधमासाद्य महान्तं हरितच्छदम्।
परीतं बहुभिर्वृक्षैः श्यामं सिद्धोपसेवितम्॥ ६॥
तस्मिन् सीताञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रयुञ्जीताशिषां क्रियाम्।
समासाद्य च तं वृक्षं वसेद् वातिक्रमेत वा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Then, approaching an extensive banyan tree, full of dark green leaves and, therefore, going by the name of Śyāma (dark-green), nay, surrounded by many other trees and visited by Siddhas, Sītā should, joining her palms, offer prayers to the deity presiding over the tree for your safe return to Ayodhyā. Again, duly reaching the foot of the aforesaid tree, she should halt there awhile in the event of her feeling fatigued, or else pass beyond it. (6-7)

verses.text:
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा नीलं प्रेक्ष्य च काननम्।
सल्लकीबदरीमिश्रं रम्यं वंशैश्च यामुनैः॥ ८॥
स पन्थाश्चित्रकूटस्य गतस्य बहुशो मया।
रम्यो मार्दवयुक्तश्च दावैश्चैव विवर्जितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “After walking a distance of only two miles from that tree and beholding the Nīlavana, interspersed with Sallakī and jujube trees and charming with bamboos standing on the bank of the Yamunā, will be found that delightful way to Citrakūṭa—which has frequently been visited by me—marked with smoothness and devoid of forest fires.”(8-9)

verses.text:
इति पन्थानमादिश्य महर्षिः संन्यवर्तत।
अभिवाद्य तथेत्युक्त्वा रामेण विनिवर्तितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Having thus pointed out the way to Citrakūṭa and being urged by Śrī Rāma to return, after he had greeted the sage and said “I shall follow your instructions”, the great seer, Bharadwāja, duly returned. (10)

verses.text:
उपावृत्ते मुनौ तस्मिन् रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
कृतपुण्याः स्म भद्रं ते मुनिर्यन्नोऽनुकम्पते॥ ११॥
verses.m: The aforesaid sage having returned, Śrī Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa, “May prosperity attend on you! We must have done meritorious deeds in the past in that the sage has been compassionate to us.” (11)

verses.text:
इति तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्रयित्वा मनस्विनौ।
सीतामेवाग्रतः कृत्वा कालिन्दीं जग्मतुर्नदीम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Talking as aforesaid, and placing Sītā definitely ahead, the two high-minded tigers among men headed towards the river Yamunā. (12)

verses.text:
अथासाद्य तु कालिन्दीं शीघ्रस्रोतस्विनीं नदीम्।
चिन्तामापेदिरे सद्यो नदीजलतितीर्षवः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Reaching the bank of the river Yamunā, which flowed in a swift current, the princely travellers for their part fell apondering, keen as they were to cross speedily the waters of the river. (13)

verses.text:
तौ काष्ठसंघाटमथो चक्रतुः सुमहाप्लवम्।
शुष्कैर्वंशैः समाकीर्णमुशीरैश्च समावृतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: The two brothers then prepared a fairly big raft consisting of a number of wooden logs placed side by side, overspread with dry bamboos and covered all over with the fragrant roots of the Uśīra plant (Andropogon muricatus). (14)

verses.text:
ततो वैतसशाखाश्च जम्बुशाखाश्च वीर्यवान्।
चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्त्वा सीतायाः सुखमासनम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Then, cutting shoots of canes and twigs of the rose-apple tree, the powerful Lakṣmaṇa made a comfortable seat for Sītā. (15)

verses.text:
तत्र श्रियमिवाचिन्त्यां रामो दाशरथिः प्रियाम्।
ईषत्स लज्जमानां तामध्यारोपयत प्लवम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then the celebrated Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, helped Sītā, his beloved consort—who vied with Śrī (the goddess of fortune) of unimaginable beauty and was feeling a bit abashed—ascend the raft. (16)

verses.text:
पार्श्वे तत्र च वैदेह्या वसने भूषणानि च।
प्लवे कठिनकाजं च रामश्चक्रे समाहितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma also carefully placed on the aforesaid raft the pair of her garments as well as her jewels as also the shovel and basket beside her. (17)

verses.text:
आरोप्य सीतां प्रथमं संघाटं परिगृह्य तौ।
ततः प्रतेरतुर्यत्तौ प्रीतौ दशरथात्मजौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having first enabled Sītā to ascend the raft, holding the structure themselves, the two sons of Daśaratha, full of delight, now cautiously began to row the raft. (18)

verses.text:
कालिन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत।
स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वां पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Arrived in mid stream, Sītā for her part saluted the deity presiding over the stream and prayed to her as follows : “May I safely cross your waters (with my husband and brother-in-law), O glorious lady; and let my husband fulfil his vow of spending fourteen years in exile in the forest. (19)

verses.text:
यक्ष्ये त्वां गोसहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च।
स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरीमिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “When Śrī Rāma safely returns to the city of Ayodhyā, ruled over by the Ikṣwākus, I shall propitiate you by offering a thousand cows and a hundred and one articles of worship which cannot be procured even by gods.” (20)

verses.text:
कालिन्दीमथ सीता तु याचमाना कृताञ्जलिः।
तीरमेवाभिसम्प्राप्ता दक्षिणं वरवर्णिनी॥ २१॥
verses.m: Even while praying to the river Kālindī in the aforesaid words with folded hands, Sītā, for her part, who was possessed of a most excellent complexion, forthwith approached the southern bank of the Yamunā itself. (21)

verses.text:
ततः प्लवेनांशुमतीं शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम्।
तीरजैर्बहुभिर्वृक्षैः संतेरुर्यमुनां नदीम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Thus they duly crossed by means of a raft the rippling and swift-going Yamunā river, daughter of the sun-god, fringed with numerous trees sprung on its banks. (22)

verses.text:
ते तीर्णाः प्लवमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थाय यमुनावनात्।
श्यामं न्यग्रोधमासेदुः शीतलं हरितच्छदम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Leaving the raft in the midst of those trees and departing from the forest on the bank of the Yamunā, they reached the cool banyan tree, covered with green leaves and accordingly bearing the name of Śyāma. (23)

verses.text:
न्यग्रोधं समुपागम्य वैदेही चाभ्यवन्दत।
नमस्तेऽस्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्॥ २४॥
कौसल्यां चैव पश्येम सुमित्रां च यशस्विनीम्।
इति सीताञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगच्छन्मनस्विनी॥ २५॥
verses.m: Nay, going very near the banyan tree, Sītā (a princess of the Videha dynasty) bowed low to it and said, “Hail to you, O gigantic tree! Let my husband fulfil his vow of forest life and let us see once more mother Kausalyā as well as the illustrious Sumitrā.” So saying and joining her palms, the high-minded Sītā went round the banyan tree clockwise. (24-25)

verses.text:
अवलोक्य ततः सीतामायाचन्तीमनिन्दिताम्।
दयितां च विधेयां च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्॥ २६॥
सीतामादाय गच्छ त्वमग्रतो भरतानुज।
पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि सायुधो द्विपदां वर॥ २७॥
verses.m: Seeing his beloved and agreeable consort, Sītā, of unimpeachable conduct, offering prayers to the deity presiding over the banyan tree, Śrī Rāma now said to Lakṣmaṇa, “Taking Sītā with you, walk you in the van, O Lakṣmaṇa, younger brother of Bharata ! Equipped with arms, I shall follow in the rear, O jewel among men ! (26-27)

verses.text:
यद् यत् फलं प्रार्थयते पुष्पं वा जनकात्मजा।
तत् तत् प्रयच्छ वैदेह्या यत्रास्या रमते मनः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Offer to Sītā, a princess of the Videha clan, whatever fruit or flower the daughter of Janaka asks for and in which her mind finds delight.” (28)

verses.text:
एकैकं पादपं गुल्मं लतां वा पुष्पशालिनीम्।
अदृष्टरूपां पश्यन्ती रामं पप्रच्छ साऽबला॥ २९॥
verses.m: Beholding every single tree, shrub or creeper, charming with blossoms, that she had never seen before, that lady questioned Śrī Rāma about it. (29)

verses.text:
रमणीयान् बहुविधान् पादपान् कुसुमोत्करान्।
सीतावचनसंरब्ध आनयामास लक्ष्मणः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Seized with a flurry on hearing Sītā’s command, Lakṣmaṇa fetched lovely twigs of various trees, bearing bunches of flowers. (30)

verses.text:
विचित्रवालुकजलां हंससारसनादिताम्।
रेमे जनकराजस्य सुता प्रेक्ष्य तदा नदीम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: The daughter of King Janaka rejoiced to gaze at that time on the river distinguished with charming sands and waters and rendered noisy by swans and cranes. (31)

verses.text:
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
बहून् मेध्यान् मृगान् हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having walked only a couple of miles from that place and killing many a consecrated deer, the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, roamed about in the forest on the bank of the Yamunā. (32)

verses.text:
विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते
शुभे वने वारणवानरायुते।
समं नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सत्वरं
निवासमाजग्मुरदीनदर्शनाः ॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Having diverted themselves in the charming forest, made noisy by flocks of peacocks and infested with monkeys and elephants, and reaching a level ground on the bank of the river, the princely travellers, who wore an undepressed look, quickly sought a tree fit for abode. (33)

verses.text:
अथ रात्र्यां व्यातीतायामवसुप्तमनन्तरम्।
प्रबोधयामास शनैर्लक्ष्मणं रघुपुङ्गवः॥ १॥
verses.m: The night having slipped past, Śrī Rāma, a jewel among the Raghus, now gently roused (in the following words) Lakṣmaṇa, who lay asleep for a second time after waking from sleep : (1)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे शृणु वन्यानां वल्गु व्याहरतां स्वनम्।
सम्प्रतिष्ठामहे कालः प्रस्थानस्य परंतप॥ २॥
verses.m: “Hear, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the notes of sweetly warbling wild birds, the parrot, the cuckoo, myna and so on. Let us duly resume our journey as the hour for departure has commenced, O tormentor of enemies ! (2)

verses.text:
प्रसुप्तस्तु ततो भ्रात्रा समये प्रतिबोधितः।
जहौ निद्रां च तन्द्रां च प्रसक्तं च परिश्रमम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Awakened in time by his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, who was fast asleep, for his part, immediately shook off his slumber, drowsiness and fatigue consequent on the previous day’s journey. (3)

verses.text:
तत उत्थाय ते सर्वे स्पृष्ट्वा नद्याः शिवं जलम्।
पन्थानमृषिभिर्जुष्टं चित्रकूटस्य तं ययुः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Getting up and bathing in the cool waters of the Yamunā, they all then proceeded on the aforesaid path to Citrakūṭa, trodden by the seers. (4)

verses.text:
ततः सम्प्रस्थितः काले रामः सौमित्रिणा सह।
सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having duly set out with Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) at that time, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows to the lotus-eyed Sītā : (5)

verses.text:
आदीप्तानिव वैदेहि सर्वतः पुष्पितान् नगान्।
स्वैः पुष्पैः किंशुकान् पश्य मालिनः शिशिरात्यये॥ ६॥
verses.m: “See, O Sītā, a princess of the Videha clan, the Kiṁśuka (Butea frondosa) trees laden with blossoms on all sides and appearing as though illumined and adorned with garlands, as it were, due to the rows of their flowers in this vernal season synchronizing with the close of winter. (6)

verses.text:
पश्य भल्लातकान् बिल्वान् नरैरनुपसेवितान्।
फलपुष्पैरवनतान् नूनं शक्ष्याम जीवितुम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Look at the markingnut and Bel trees, not made use of by men (being out of their reach) and bent low under the weight of their fruit and blossoms. We shall surely be able to live through. (7)

verses.text:
पश्य द्रोणप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि लक्ष्मण।
मधूनि मधुकारीभिः सम्भृतानि नगे नगे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Behold hanging from every tree honeycombs equal in weight to a Droṇa (fifteen kg.) and constructed and stocked with honey by bees, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (8)

verses.text:
एष क्रोशति नत्यूहस्तं शिखी प्रतिकूजति।
रमणीये वनोद्देशे पुष्पसंस्तरसंकटे॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Here is a Cātaka bird crying and a peacock responding to it in a charming part of the forest thick with a scattered mass of flowers. (9)

verses.text:
मातङ्गयूथानुसृतं पक्षिसंघानुनादितम्।
चित्रकूटमिमं पश्य प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Look at this Citrakūṭa hill with elevated peaks, a hill infested with herds of elephants and rendered noisy by flocks of birds. (10)

verses.text:
समभूमितले रम्ये द्रुमैर्बहुभिरावृते।
पुण्ये रंस्यामहे तात चित्रकूटस्य कानने॥ ११॥
verses.m: “We shall sport, dear brother, in the lovely and holy forest of Citrakūṭa consisting of level grounds and covered by many trees.” (11)

verses.text:
ततस्तौ पादचारेण गच्छन्तौ सह सीतया।
रम्यमासेदतुः शैलं चित्रकूटं मनोरमम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Going on foot with Sītā, the two brothers then reached the delightful and soul-captivating Citrakūṭa hill. (12)

verses.text:
तं तु पर्वतमासाद्य नानापक्षिगणायुतम्।
बहुमूलफलं रम्यं सम्पन्नसरसोदकम्॥ १३॥
मनोज्ञोऽयं गिरिः सौम्य नानाद्रुमलतायुतः।
बहुमूलफलो रम्यः स्वाजीवः प्रतिभाति मे॥ १४॥
verses.m: Reaching that lovely mountain, abounding in flocks of birds of many kinds and having a rich stock of roots and fruits and having sweet water in abundance, Śrī Rāma for his part said to Lakṣmaṇa, “Soul-captivating is this delightful mountain adorned with many trees and creepers and abounds in roots and fruits. To me it appears to be a place where sustenance could be found with ease, O gentle brother ! (13-14)

verses.text:
मुनयश्च महात्मानो वसन्त्यस्मिन् शिलोच्चये।
अयं वासो भवेत् तात वयमत्र वसेमहि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “High-souled ascetics too dwell on this mountain. It may prove habitable, O dear brother ! Let us take up our abode here.” (15)

verses.text:
इति सीता च रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः।
अभिगम्याश्रमं सर्वे वाल्मीकिमभिवादयन्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Saying so and entering the hermitage of Vālmīki, Sītā and Śrī Rāma, and with folded hands, Lakṣmaṇa, too, greeted sage Vālmīki. (16)

verses.text:
तान् महर्षिः प्रमुदितः पूजयामास धर्मवित्।
आस्यतामिति चोवाच स्वागतं तं निवेद्य च॥ १७॥
verses.m: Greatly delighted and offering welcome to Śrī Rāma (the principal guest), the eminent sage, Vālmīki, who knew what is right, received them with honour and said, “Be seated !” (17)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
संनिवेद्य यथान्यायमात्मानमृषये प्रभुः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Duly presenting himself to the seer according to the rules of propriety (obtaining in those days), the powerful Śrī Rāma of mighty arms, the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa, then spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa : (18)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणानय दारूणि दृढानि च वराणि च।
कुरुष्वावसथं सौम्य वासे मेऽभिरतं मनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Fetch, O Lakṣmaṇa, strong and excellent logs of wood and erect a hut, O gentle brother ! My mind is intent on dwelling here.” (19)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिर्विविधान् द्रुमान्।
आजहार ततश्चक्रे पर्णशालामरिंदमः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Hearing his aforesaid command, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) brought boughs of various trees and with them the prince, a subduer of his foes, erected a hut of leaves. (20)

verses.text:
तां निष्ठितां बद्धकटां दृष्ट्वा रामः सुदर्शनाम्।
शुश्रूषमाणमेकाग्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Seeing the hut consolidated with a wall of strong wooden stakes and thatched and charming to look at, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood listening with rapt attention : (21)

verses.text:
ऐणेयं मांसमाहृत्य शालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्।
कर्तव्यं वास्तुशमनं सौमित्रे चिरजीविभिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Fetching the pulp1 of the bulb known by the name of Gajakanda we shall propitiate the deity presiding over the hut (roasting the pulp and offering it as an oblation to the deity). The rite of appeasing the evil spirit haunting a newly-erected structure must be gone through by those wishing to live long. (22)

verses.text:
मृगं हत्वाऽऽनय क्षिप्रं लक्ष्मणेह शुभेक्षण।
कर्तव्यः शास्त्रदृष्टो हि विधिर्धर्ममनुस्मर॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Digging out the bulb2 known by the name of Gajakanda, bring it here at once, O fair-eyed Lakṣmaṇa; for the procedure laid down in the scriptures must be observed. Always mind your sacred obligations.” (23)

verses.text:
भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
चकार च यथोक्तं हि तं रामः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ २४॥
ऐणेयं श्रपयस्वैतच्छालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्।
त्वर सौम्यमुहूर्तोऽयं ध्रुवश्च दिवसो ह्ययम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Clearly perceiving the command of his eldest brother, the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of hostile warriors, actually did as he was told and Śrī Rāma said to him again, “Dress this bulb, we shall propitiate the deities (the fire-god, Parjanya and so on, numbering fifty) presiding over the hut by offering the dressed bulb to them. Look sharp! The current is a propitious hour and this day too bears the name of ‘Dhruva’1 (undying).” (24-25)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणः कृष्णमृगं हत्वा मेध्यं प्रतापवान्।
अथ चिक्षेप सौमित्रिः समिद्धे जातवेदसि॥ २६॥
verses.m: Unearthing the bulb, which has a black peel and is fit for being offered as an oblation to gods, the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, full of glory as he was, forthwith cast it into the blazing fire. (26)

verses.text:
तत् तु पक्वं समाज्ञाय निष्टप्तं छिन्नशोणितम्।
लक्ष्मणः पुरुषव्याघ्रमथ राघवमब्रवीत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Having definitely come to know that its pulp had been fully roasted and dressed and divested of its ruddy colour, Lakṣmaṇa now submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men : (27)

verses.text:
अयं सर्वः समस्ताङ्गः शृतः कृष्णमृगो मया।
देवता देवसंकाश यजस्व कुशलो ह्यसि॥ २८॥
verses.m: “This bulb, known by the name of Gajakanda and endowed with a black peel, and by which all disordered limbs are put right, has been fully dressed by me. Pray, propitiate the gods presiding over the hut by offering it as an oblation to them, inasmuch as you are well-versed in the rite, O brother, vying with gods in glory !” (28)

verses.text:
रामः स्नात्वा तु नियतो गुणवाञ्जपकोविदः।
संग्रहेणाकरोत् सर्वान् मन्त्रान् सत्रावसानिकान्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having finished his bath and fully disciplined as he was, Śrī Rāma, for his part, who was full of virtues and well-versed in the sacred texts to be muttered on the occasion, went through, in brief, the ceremony of Vāstu-Śānti, reciting the sacred texts bearing on the conclusion of a sacrificial performance. (29)

verses.text:
इष्ट्वा देवगणान् सर्वान् विवेशावसथं शुचिः।
बभूव च मनोह्लादो रामस्यामिततेजसः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having propitiated all the hosts of gods presiding over the newly-erected hut and thus purified, Śrī Rāma entered the hut. Nay, great satisfaction of mind was caused thereby to Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of immense glory. (30)

verses.text:
वैश्वदेवबलिं कृत्वा रौद्रं वैष्णवमेव च।
वास्तुसंशमनीयानि मङ्गलानि प्रवर्तयन्॥ ३१॥
जपं च न्यायतः कृत्वा स्नात्वा नद्यां यथाविधि।
पापसंशमनं रामश्चकार बलिमुत्तमम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having bathed in the river Mandākinī according to the procedure laid down in the scriptures and muttering sacred texts such as the Gāyatrī in the right way, and intending as he did to perform solemn rites calculated to ward off the evils attendant on a new construction, Śrī Rāma offered excellent oblations to Lord Rudra and Lord Viṣṇu too after performing the Vaiśwadeva (a religious ceremony which ought to be performed every morning and evening and especially before the midday meal and consists in homage paid to the Viśwedevas, followed by Baliharaṇa or offering of small portions of cooked food to the gods who give the food and especially to the god of fire, who cooks the food for us and bears the offering to heaven). (31-32)

verses.text:
वेदिस्थलविधानानि चैत्यान्यायतनानि च।
आश्रमस्यानुरूपाणि स्थापयामास राघवः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, erected and consecrated altars of a size proportionate to the hut for offering oblations to the eight guardians of the quarters and the intermediate points and Caityas (places of worship for Gaṇeśa and other gods) and Āyatanas, places for worship of Lord Viṣṇu and others. (33)

verses.text:
तां वृक्षपर्णच्छदनां मनोज्ञां
यथाप्रदेशं सुकृतां निवाताम्।
वासाय सर्वे विविशुः समेताः
सभां यथा देवगणाः सुधर्माम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Even as multitudes of gods entered their assembly hall, named Sudharmā in heaven, all the three princely exiles entered together for habitation the aforesaid soul-captivating hut, thatched with the leaves of trees, erected well on a suitable site and sheltered from winds. (34)

verses.text:
सुरम्यमासाद्य तु चित्रकूटं
नदीं च तां माल्यवतीं सुतीर्थाम्।
ननन्द हृष्टो मृगपक्षिजुष्टां
जहौ च दुःखं पुरविप्रवासात्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to reach the exceedingly delightful Citrakūṭa and the celebrated river, Mālyavatī (Mandākinī), which was provided with good descents and was sought by beasts and birds, Śrī Rāma for his part rejoiced and shed the agony caused by his exile from the city of Ayodhyā. (35)

verses.text:
कथयित्वा तु दुःखार्तः सुमन्त्रेण चिरं सह।
रामे दक्षिणकूलस्थे जगाम स्वगृहं गुहः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having talked long with Sumantra on the virtues of Śrī Rāma, Guha for his part, stricken as he was with agony due to separation from Śrī Rāma, left for his home when Śrī Rāma set his foot on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā. (1)

verses.text:
भरद्वाजाभिगमनं प्रयागे च सभाजनम्।
आ गिरेर्गमनं तेषां तत्रस्थैरभिलक्षितम्॥ २॥
verses.m: The meeting of Śrī Rāma and others with Bharadwāja at Prayāga and their reception by the latter as well as their journey up to the Citrakūta hill was witnessed by the spies of Guha, resident of Śṛṅgaverapura and reported to Guha, who apprised Sumantra of it. (2)

verses.text:
अनुज्ञातः सुमन्त्रोऽथ योजयित्वा हयोत्तमान्।
अयोध्यामेव नगरीं प्रययौ गाढदुर्मनाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Therefore, yoking the excellent horses to his chariot, taking leave of Guha, Sumantra drove straight to Ayodhyā, deeply disconsolate at heart. (3)

verses.text:
स वनानि सुगन्धीनि सरितश्च सरांसि च।
पश्यन् यत्तो ययौ शीघ्रं ग्रामाणि नगराणि च॥ ४॥
verses.m: Viewing woodlands diffusing sweet odours, rivers and lakes, villages and cities, the charioteer carefully drove along at a quick speed. (4)

verses.text:
ततः सायाह्नसमये द्वितीयेऽहनि सारथिः।
अयोध्यां समनुप्राप्य निरानन्दां ददर्श ह॥ ५॥
verses.m: Duly reaching Ayodhyā at dusk on the second day (since his departure from Śṛṅgaverapura), the charioteer found it cheerless : so it is said. (5)

verses.text:
स शून्यामिव निःशब्दां दृष्ट्वा परमदुर्मनाः।
सुमन्त्रश्चिन्तयामास शोकवेगसमाहतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Greatly troubled in mind to see Ayodhyā noiseless as though desolate, and overpowered with the vehemence of grief, Sumantra reflected : (6)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न सगजा साश्वा सजना सजनाधिपा।
रामसंतापदुःखेन दग्धा शोकाग्निना पुरी॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I hope the city of Ayodhyā with its elephants, horses, people and sovereign has not been consumed by the fire of grief caused by the agony of separation from Śrī Rāma.”(7)

verses.text:
इति चिन्तापरः सूतो वाजिभिः शीघ्रयायिभिः।
नगरद्वारमासाद्य त्वरितः प्रविवेश ह॥ ८॥
verses.m: Reaching the city gate by the chariot driven by swift-going horses, while pondering thus, the charioteer, they say, hastily entered the city. (8)

verses.text:
सुमन्त्रमभिधावन्तः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
क्व राम इति पृच्छन्तः सूतमभ्यद्रवन् नराः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Inquiring where Śrī Rāma was, people forthwith rushed in their hundreds and thousands towards Sumantra, who was driving in the direction of the palace. (9)

verses.text:
तेषां शशंस गङ्गायामहमापृच्छ्य राघवम्।
अनुज्ञातो निवृत्तोऽस्मि धार्मिकेण महात्मना॥ १०॥
verses.m: He replied to them, “Taking leave of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), when sent back by that pious and lofty-minded prince, on the bank of the Gaṅgā at Śṛṅgaverapura, I have returned from that place.” (10)

verses.text:
ते तीर्णा इति विज्ञाय बाष्पपूर्णमुखा नराः।
अहो धिगिति निःश्वस्य हा रामेति विचुक्रुशुः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Coming to know for certain that the exiles had crossed the Gaṅgā, and sighing with the words “Oh, fie upon us !” people with their faces bathed in tears cried aloud, “Ah Rāma !” (11)

verses.text:
शुश्राव च वचस्तेषां वृन्दं वृन्दं च तिष्ठताम्।
हताः स्म खलु ये नेह पश्याम इति राघवम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Nay, he heard the lament of the people, who stood in batches saying, “Doomed indeed are we, who do not perceive Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) in this chariot ! (12)

verses.text:
दानयज्ञविवाहेषु समाजेषु महत्सु च।
न द्रक्ष्यामः पुनर्जातु धार्मिकं राममन्तरा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Alas, we shall never see the pious Śrī Rāma in our midst again on the occasions of bestowing gifts, sacrificial performances and weddings nor in large gatherings. (13)

verses.text:
किं समर्थं जनस्यास्य किं प्रियं किं सुखावहम्।
इति रामेण नगरं पित्रेव परिपालितम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The citizens of Ayodhyā were looked after by Śrī Rāma as by a father with due regard to what was conducive to one’s good, what was agreeable to an individual and what brought happiness to one.” (14)

verses.text:
वातायनगतानां च स्त्रीणामन्वन्तरापणम्।
राममेवाभितप्तानां शुश्राव परिदेवनाम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Driving through the bazars, Sumantra heard the wailing of women standing at the windows of their houses and feeling distressed on account of Śrī Rāma’s exile. (15)

verses.text:
स राजमार्गमध्येन सुमन्त्रः पिहिताननः।
यत्र राजा दशरथस्तदेवोपययौ गृहम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: His face covered with cloth, the said Sumantra headed through the middle of the king’s highway towards the palace where King Daśaratha was. (16)

verses.text:
सोऽवतीर्य रथाच्छीघ्रं राजवेश्म प्रविश्य च।
कक्ष्याः सप्ताभिचक्राम महाजनसमाकुलाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Quickly alighting from the chariot and entering the royal palace, he crossed the seven portals thronged with large crowds of men. (17)

verses.text:
हर्म्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्याथ समागतम्।
हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामादर्शनकर्शिताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Finding from their mansions, seven-storied buildings and palaces that Sumantra had duly returned from the forest without Śrī Rāma, ladies, who had been emaciated because of their not being able to see Śrī Rāma all these days, burst into a loud wail. (18)

verses.text:
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः।
अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Deeply distressed, the ladies gazed on one another vacantly with their big eyes flooded with an upsurge of tears and, therefore, rid of their collyrium. (19)

verses.text:
ततो दशरथस्त्रीणां प्रासादेभ्यस्ततस्ततः।
रामशोकाभितप्तानां मन्दं शुश्राव जल्पितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then he heard the talk in low tones of the consorts of Emperor Daśaratha—who were stricken with grief caused by separation from Śrī Rāma—from their palaces here and there. (20)

verses.text:
सह रामेण निर्यातो विना राममिहागतः।
सूतः किं नाम कौसल्यां क्रोशन्तीं प्रतिवक्ष्यति॥ २१॥
verses.m: “They said to one another : “What reply will the charioteer (Sumantra), who departed from Ayodhyā with Rāma and has returned to the capital without Rāma, give to the screaming Kausalyā when questioned by her? (21)

verses.text:
यथा च मन्ये दुर्जीवमेवं न सुकरं ध्रुवम्।
आच्छिद्य पुत्रे निर्याते कौसल्या यत्र जीवति॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Since Kausalyā continues to survive even though her son Rāma has left Ayodhyā relinquishing the throne, I am led to believe that surely it is not so easy to end one’s life, as it is hard to preserve life against odds.” (22)

verses.text:
सत्यरूपं तु तद् वाक्यं राजस्त्रीणां निशामयन्।
प्रदीप्त इव शोकेन विवेश सहसा गृहम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid truthful assertion of the King’s consorts, Sumantra for his part entered the palace all at once as though he were set ablaze with grief. (23)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्याष्टमीं कक्ष्यां राजानं दीनमातुरम्।
पुत्रशोकपरिद्यूनमपश्यत् पाण्डुरे गृहे॥ २४॥
verses.m: Entering the eighth gateway, he beheld in the white chamber the afflicted and over-anxious monarch withered through grief for his son. (24)

verses.text:
अभिगम्य तमासीनं राजानमभिवाद्य च।
सुमन्त्रो रामवचनं यथोक्तं प्रत्यवेदयत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Approaching the aforesaid king, who was seated, and greeting him, Sumantra delivered to him the message of Śrī Rāma, as instructed by the latter. (25)

verses.text:
स तूष्णीमेव तच्छ्रुत्वा राजा विद्रुतमानसः।
मूर्च्छितो न्यपतद् भूमौ रामशोकाभिपीडितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Hearing that message in perfect silence, the aforesaid monarch felt perplexed in mind and dropped unconscious to the ground, tormented as he was with grief caused by separation from Śrī Rāma. (26)

verses.text:
ततोऽन्तःपुरमाविद्धं मूर्च्छिते पृथिवीपतौ।
उच्छ्रित्य बाहू चुक्रोश नृपतौ पतिते क्षितौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: The Emperor having fainted, the entire gynaeceum now felt sore distressed. And when the king fell to the ground, the inmates of the gynaeceum burst into a wail raising their arms. (27)

verses.text:
सुमित्रया तु सहिता कौसल्या पतितं पतिम्।
उत्थापयामास तदा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Assisted by Sumitrā, Kausalyā for her part lifted up her fallen husband on that occasion and submitted as follows : (28)

verses.text:
इमं तस्य महाभाग दूतं दुष्करकारिणः।
वनवासादनुप्राप्तं कस्मान्न प्रतिभाषसे॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Wherefore, O highly blessed king, do you not make answer to the messenger of Rāma—who has accomplished a difficult task—returned from his recent trip to the forest? (29)

verses.text:
अद्येममनयं कृत्वा व्यपत्रपसि राघव।
उत्तिष्ठ सुकृतं तेऽस्तु शोके न स्यात् सहायता॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Having perpetrated this unseemly act in the shape of banishing your eldest and worthiest son, do you feel abashed today, O scion of Raghu? Kindly get up ! Let your virtue resulting from your devotion to truth abide. In the event of your giving way to grief, your associates too may cease to be. (30)

verses.text:
देव यस्या भयाद् रामं नानुपृच्छसि सारथिम्।
नेह तिष्ठति कैकेयी विश्रब्धं प्रतिभाष्यताम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Kaikeyī, for fear of whom you do not address inquiries concerning Rāma to the charioteer (Sumantra), O lord, is not present here. Therefore, reply may be given to Sumantra with confidence.” (31)

verses.text:
सा तथोक्त्वा महाराजं कौसल्या शोकलालसा।
धरण्यां निपपाताशु बाष्पविप्लुतभाषिणी॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having submitted to the Emperor as aforesaid, the celebrated Kausalyā, who was wholly given up to grief, and was faltering through tears, forthwith dropped to the ground. (32)

verses.text:
विलपन्तीं तथा दृष्ट्वा कौसल्यां पतितां भुवि।
पतिं चावेक्ष्य ताः सर्वाः समन्ताद् रुरुदुः स्त्रियः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Seeing Kausalyā fallen to the ground, wailing as aforesaid, and gazing on their husband lying senseless, all those ladies around her wept. (33)

verses.text:
ततस्तमन्तःपुरनादमुत्थितं
समीक्ष्य वृद्धास्तरुणाश्च मानवाः।
स्त्रियश्च सर्वा रुरुदुः समन्ततः
पुरं तदासीत् पुनरेव संकुलम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Perceiving that plaintive cry raised in the gynaeceum, men, both aged and young, and all women flocked around weeping and the city of Ayodhyā was agitated once more. (34)

verses.text:
प्रत्याश्वस्तो यदा राजा मोहात् प्रत्यागतस्मृतिः।
तदाजुहाव तं सूतं रामवृत्तान्तकारणात्॥ १॥
verses.m: When the king woke from his swoon, consciousness having returned to him, he confidently summoned to his presence the charioteer, Sumantra, in order to hear the news about Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
तदा सूतो महाराजं कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः।
राममेवानुशोचन्तं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम्॥ २॥
वृद्धं परमसंतप्तं नवग्रहमिव द्विपम्।
विनिःश्वसन्तं ध्यायन्तमस्वस्थमिव कुञ्जरम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: With joined palms the charioteer then sought the presence of the aged Emperor, who was dolefully sighing, seized as he was with agony and grief and, feeling sore distressed and ill at ease, was mourning for Śrī Rāma alone and thus resembled a newly-captured elephant, hissing and remembering the leader of its herd. (2-3)

verses.text:
राजा तु रजसा सूतं ध्वस्ताङ्गं समुपस्थितम्।
अश्रुपूर्णमुखं दीनमुवाच परमार्तवत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Like one sore afflicted, the king for his part said to the charioteer, who stood respectfully, wearing a wretched look, his limbs stained with dust and his face bathed in tears : (4)

verses.text:
क्व नु वत्स्यति धर्मात्मा वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः।
सोऽत्यन्तसुखितः सूत किमशिष्यति राघवः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Where will Rāma, a scion of Raghu, whose mind is given to piety, live, taking shelter under a tree? What, O charioteer, will he eat, having lived most comfortably all along (right from his birth)? (5)

verses.text:
दुःखस्यानुचितो दुःखं सुमन्त्र शयनोचितः।
भूमिपालात्मजो भूमौ शेते कथमनाथवत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “How, O Sumantra, does the prince, who is undeserving of suffering and is worthy of reposing on a costly bed, lie down miserably on the ground like one forlorn? (6)

verses.text:
यं यान्तमनुयान्ति स्म पदातिरथकुञ्जराः।
स वत्स्यति कथं रामो विजनं वनमाश्रितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “How will Rāma, whom foot-soldiers, chariots and elephants used to follow whenever he went out of his palace, live confined to a lonely forest? (7)

verses.text:
व्यालैर्मृगैराचरितं कृष्णसर्पनिषेवितम्।
कथं कुमारौ वैदेह्या सार्धं वनमुपाश्रितौ॥ ८॥
verses.m: “How have the two princes taken up their abode with Sītā (a princess of the Videha clan) in a forest frequented by carnivorous animals and deer and infested with cobras? (8)

verses.text:
सुकुमार्या तपस्विन्या सुमन्त्र सह सीतया।
राजपुत्रौ कथं पादैरवरुह्य रथाद् गतौ॥ ९॥
verses.m: “How did the two princes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, with Sītā of delicate frame and engaged in austerities, proceed on foot, getting down from the chariot, O Sumantra? (9)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्थः खलु सूत त्वं येन दृष्टौ ममात्मजौ।
वनान्तं प्रविशन्तौ तावश्विनाविव मन्दरम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Accomplished of purpose indeed are you, O charioteer, by whom my aforesaid two sons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have been seen entering deep into the forest region as the Aświns, the twin-born physicians of gods, enter the precincts of Mount Mandara (a mountain frequented by gods). (10)

verses.text:
किमुवाच वचो रामः किमुवाच च लक्ष्मणः।
सुमन्त्र वनमासाद्य किमुवाच च मैथिली॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having reached the forest, O Sumantra, what words did Rāma utter and what did Lakṣmaṇa say? And what did Sītā, daughter of the king of Mithilā, say? (11)

verses.text:
आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय।
जीविष्याम्ययमेतेन ययातिरिव साधुषु॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Pray, speak to me about the mode of Rāma’s sitting, lying down to sleep and eating, O charioteer ! I shall survive on the strength of this information even as King Yayāti, when hurled down from heaven on his stock of merits having been exhausted through self-praise, lived happily in the midst of pious souls.”* (12)

verses.text:
इति सूतो नरेन्द्रेण चोदितः सज्जमानया।
उवाच वाचा राजानं स बाष्पपरिबद्धया॥ १३॥
verses.m: * We read in the Mahābhārata, Ādiparva, how when doomed to fall from heaven, King Yayāti Urged thus by the Emperor, the said charioteer replied to the king in a faltering voice choked with tears as follows : (13)

verses.text:
अब्रवीन्मे महाराज धर्ममेवानुपालयन्।
अञ्जलिं राघवः कृत्वा शिरसाभिप्रणम्य च॥ १४॥
सूत मद्वचनात् तस्य तातस्य विदितात्मनः।
शिरसा वन्दनीयस्य वन्द्यौ पादौ महात्मनः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Folding his hands and offering respectful greetings with bent head and thus strictly following the prescribed course of conduct, O great king, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, said to me, ‘The feet of that high-souled father of mine, who has realized the Self and deserves to be greeted with bent head, should be saluted in my name, O charioteer ! (14-15)

verses.text:
सर्वमन्तःपुरं वाच्यं सूत मद्वचनात् त्वया।
आरोग्यमविशेषेण यथार्हमभिवादनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘The whole gynaeceum, O charioteer, should be asked without distinction on my behalf of their welfare by you and should be offered greetings in the order of their rank (seniority). (16)

verses.text:
माता च मम कौसल्या कुशलं चाभिवादनम्।
अप्रमादं च वक्तव्या ब्रूयाश्चैनामिदं वचः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘And my mother, Kausalyā, should be told of my welfare and offered greetings on my behalf and assured of my punctiliousness with regard to my sacred obligations. Again the following message should be delivered to her : (17)

verses.text:
धर्मनित्या यथाकालमग्न्यगारपरा भव।
देवि देवस्य पादौ च देववत् परिपालय॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Remain constantly devoted to righteousness and attend the fire-sanctuary at the proper time (the time of fire-worship). And tend, O godly lady, the feet of your spouse as those of a deity. (18)

verses.text:
अभिमानं च मानं च त्यक्त्वा वर्तस्व मातृषु।
अनुराजानमार्यां च कैकेयीमम्ब कारय॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Shaking off pride of descent and self-esteem born of seniority, treat my other mothers on an equal footing. And, O mother, treat Kaikeyī, to whom the king is so devoted, as superior to you. (19)

verses.text:
कुमारे भरते वृत्तिर्वर्तितव्या च राजवत्।
अप्यज्येष्ठा हि राजानो राजधर्ममनुस्मर॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Treatment should be accorded to Prince Bharata as to His Majesty. Even though junior in age, kings deserve to be honoured. Pray, bear in mind your duty towards a king. (20)

verses.text:
भरतः कुशलं वाच्यो वाच्यो मद्वचनेन च।
सर्वास्वेव यथान्यायं वृत्तिं वर्तस्व मातृषु॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘Bharata too should be told of my welfare and admonished in the following words on my behalf : Pray, behave justly towards all your mothers. (21)

verses.text:
वक्तव्यश्च महाबाहुरिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः।
पितरं यौवराज्यस्थो राज्यस्थमनुपालय॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘The mighty-armed Bharata, the delight of Ikṣwāku’s race, should be further exhorted as follows : Even when installed in the office of Prince Regent, please serve your father, who still occupies the throne of Ayodhyā. (22)

verses.text:
अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मा स्मैनं व्यपरोरुधः।
कुमारराज्ये जीवस्व तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘The king has gone beyond the age of rulership: do not dethrone him on this score. Therefore, by keeping up his authority above all else, maintain yourself by the office of Prince Regent.’ (23)

verses.text:
अब्रवीच्चापि मां भूयो भृशमश्रूणि वर्तयन्।
मातेव मम माता ते द्रष्टव्या पुत्रगर्धिनी॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Nay, shedding tears again and again, Śrī Rāma further asked me to tell Bharata : My mother (Kausalyā), who is excessively fond of myself (her son), should be looked upon as your own mother.’ (24)

verses.text:
इत्येवं मां महाबाहुर्ब्रुवन्नेव महायशाः।
रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो भृशमश्रूण्यवर्तयत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Even while instructing me as aforesaid, the mighty-armed and highly illustrious Śrī Rāma, who has eyes resembling the petals of a lotus, shed tears again and again. (25)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
केनायमपराधेन राजपुत्रो विवासितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Highly enraged, Lakṣmaṇa for his part spoke hissing as follows : ‘For what offence has this prince, Śrī Rāma, been exiled? (26)

verses.text:
राज्ञा तु खलु कैकेय्या लघु चाश्रुत्य शासनम्।
कृतं कार्यमकार्यं वा वयं येनाभिपीडिताः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having quickly promised to carry out the command of Kaikeyī, the king executed it, not minding whether it was worth doing or not, as a result of which we have been subjected to excessive suffering. (27)

verses.text:
यदि प्रव्राजितो रामो लोभकारणकारितम्।
वरदाननिमित्तं वा सर्वथा दुष्कृतं कृतम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “ ‘If the event of Śrī Rāma having been exiled was brought about through greed for power or because a boon had been granted to that effect by the Emperor, a wholly undesirable act has been done. (28)

verses.text:
इदं तावद् यथाकाममीश्वरस्य कृते कृतम्।
रामस्य तु परित्यागे न हेतुमुपलक्षये॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Whether this was done according to the king’s pleasure or through the will of Providence, I do not find any justification whatsoever for Śrī Rāma’s exile. (29)

verses.text:
असमीक्ष्य समारब्धं विरुद्धं बुद्धिलाघवात्।
जनयिष्यति संक्रोशं राघवस्य विवासनम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “ ‘The exile of Śrī Rāma, which has been brought about contrary to usage without proper consideration, due to shortsight, will lead to remorse. (30)

verses.text:
अहं तावन्महाराजे पितृत्वं नोपलक्षये।
भ्राता भर्ता च बन्धुश्च पिता च मम राघवः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “ ‘I, at any rate, perceive no parenthood in the Emperor; Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) is my elder brother, master, kinsman and father too. (31)

verses.text:
सर्वलोकप्रियं त्यक्त्वा सर्वलोकहिते रतम्।
सर्वलोकोऽनुरज्येत कथं चानेन कर्मणा॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘How can the entire populace be pleased through this act with the king, who is devoted to the good of all people, having forsaken Śrī Rāma, the beloved of all people? (32)

verses.text:
सर्वप्रजाभिरामं हि रामं प्रव्रज्य धार्मिकम्।
सर्वलोकविरोधेन कथं राजा भविष्यति॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having actually exiled the pious Śrī Rāma, the delighter of all the people, in opposition to the will of all people, how can father continue to be the king?’ (33)

verses.text:
जानकी तु महाराज निःश्वसन्ती तपस्विनी।
भूतोपहतचित्तेव विष्ठिता विस्मृता स्थिता॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Sītā (daughter of Janaka), for her part, who is engaged in austerities, stood sighing and motionless, oblivious of everything as though her mind was possessed by a spirit, O Emperor ! (34)

verses.text:
अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसना राजपुत्री यशस्विनी।
तेन दुःखेन रुदती नैव मां किंचिदब्रवीत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Having never seen adversity before, the illustrious princess did not speak anything at all to me, weeping, as she did, due to the distress of her husband. (35)

verses.text:
उद्वीक्षमाणा भर्तारं मुखेन परिशुष्यता।
मुमोच सहसा बाष्पं प्रयान्तमुपवीक्ष्य सा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Seeing me about to depart for Ayodhyā, she suddenly broke into tears as she stood looking at her husband with a withering face. (36)

verses.text:
तथैव रामोऽश्रुमुखः कृताञ्जलिः
स्थितोऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणबाहुपालितः।
तथैव सीता रुदती तपस्विनी
निरीक्षते राजरथं तथैव माम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Precisely, as aforesaid, spoke Śrī Rāma, protected by the arms of Lakṣmaṇa, and standing with joined palms, his face covered with tears. And so did Sītā, engaged in austerities, gazed weeping on the royal chariot driven by me, as well as on me.” (37)

verses.text:
मम त्वश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि।
उष्णमश्रु विमुञ्चन्तो रामे सम्प्रस्थिते वनम्॥ १॥
उभाभ्यां राजपुत्राभ्यामथ कृत्वाहमञ्जलिम्।
प्रस्थितो रथमास्थाय तद्दुःखमपि धारयन्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Offering salutation with folded hands to both the princes on Śrī Rāma having duly departed for the forest, and mounting the chariot, I too forthwith made ready to depart for Ayodhyā, restraining that unbearable agony of separation from Śrī Rāma. My horses, however, even as I turned my back on Śrī Rāma, did not proceed on their journey to Ayodhyā and stood shedding tears of grief. (1-2)

verses.text:
गुहेन सार्धं तत्रैव स्थितोऽस्मि दिवसान् बहून्।
आशया यदि मां रामः पुनः शब्दापयेदिति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I remained with Guha, the chieftain of Śṛṅgaverapura, at his own place for many (three) days in the hope that Śrī Rāma might probably call me again through foresters. (3)

verses.text:
विषये ते महाराज महाव्यसनकर्शिताः।
अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानाः सपुष्पाङ्कुरकोरकाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Withered through intense suffering, O great monarch, even trees in your kingdom with their flowers, shoots and buds have been blasted. (4)

verses.text:
उपतप्तोदका नद्यः पल्वलानि सरांसि च।
परिशुष्कपलाशानि वनान्युपवनानि च॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The water of the rivers as well as of ponds and lakes has got dried up. Nay, the leaves in the wood and groves have got withered. (5)

verses.text:
न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्याला न प्रचरन्ति च।
रामशोकाभिभूतं तन्निष्कूजमभवद् वनम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Living beings in the forest do not move about, nor do reptiles crawl even in search of food, the entire living creation being overwhelmed with grief born of separation from Śrī Rāma. Nay, the forest on the way is noiseless too, as it were, though full of birds. (6)

verses.text:
लीनपुष्करपत्राश्च नद्यश्च कलुषोदकाः।
संतप्तपद्माः पद्मिन्यो लीनमीनविहंगमाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The water of the rivers, again, has become turbid and the leaves of the lotuses in them have fallen down. The lotuses in the ponds have got dried up and the fishes and water-fowls in them have perished. (7)

verses.text:
जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च।
नातिभान्त्यल्पगन्धीनि फलानि च यथापुरम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nay, giving forth very little fragrance, aquatic flowers and those growing on land do not look very charming and fruits too are not so luscious as before. (8)

verses.text:
अत्रोद्यानानि शून्यानि प्रलीनविहगानि च।
न चाभिरामानारामान् पश्यामि मनुजर्षभ॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Desolate are the gardens in the city and the birds in them have disappeared. Nor do I find the parks so pleasing, O jewel among men ! (9)

verses.text:
प्रविशन्तमयोध्यायां न कश्चिदभिनन्दति।
नरा राममपश्यन्तो निःश्वसन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “None greeted me as I entered Ayodhyā. Not perceiving Śrī Rāma, men sighed again and again. (10)

verses.text:
देव राजरथं दृष्ट्वा विना राममिहागतम्।
दूरादश्रुमुखः सर्वो राजमार्गे गतो जनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Seeing from a distance the royal chariot arrived in Ayodhyā without Śrī Rāma, O lord, all the people present on the main road had their faces drenched with tears. (11)

verses.text:
हर्म्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्य रथमागतम्।
हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामादर्शनकर्शिताः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Perceiving from their mansions, seven-storeyed buildings and palaces the chariot returned from the forest, the ladies, who were feeling distressed due to their not being able to see Śrī Rāma, broke into lamentation. (12)

verses.text:
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः।
अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “The ladies, who were sore afflicted due to the exile of Śrī Rāma, mutely gazed on one another with their large eyes flooded with an upsurge of tears, their collyrium washed thereby. (13)

verses.text:
नामित्राणां न मित्राणामुदासीनजनस्य च।
अहमार्ततया कंचिद् विशेषं नोपलक्षये॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I do not perceive any difference in point of affliction between his enemies, friends and neutrals. (14)

verses.text:
अप्रहृष्टमनुष्या च दीननागतुरंगमा।
आर्तस्वरपरिम्लाना विनिःश्वसितनिःस्वना॥ १५॥
निरानन्दा महाराज रामप्रव्राजनातुरा।
कौसल्या पुत्रहीनेव अयोध्या प्रतिभाति मे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “With its cheerless men and women and wretched elephants and horses, nay, looking blasted through plaintive cries and full of noise in the shape of sighs, O great monarch, Ayodhyā appears to me joyless and distressed through the banishment of Śrī Rāma, like Empress Kausalyā, bereft of her son.” (15-16)

verses.text:
सूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा वाचा परमदीनया।
बाष्पोपहतया सूतमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of Sumantra, Daśaratha made the following reply to the charioteer in a most piteous tone, faltering through tears: (17)

verses.text:
कैकेय्या विनियुक्तेन पापाभिजनभावया।
मया न मन्त्रकुशलैर्वृद्धैः सह समर्थितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “No deliberation was made by me on the point of sending Rāma into exile with the elders, clever in giving counsel, dictated as I was by Kaikeyī of sinful birth and intention. (18)

verses.text:
न सुहृद्भिर्न चामात्यैर्मन्त्रयित्वा सनैगमैः।
मयायमर्थः सम्मोहात् स्त्रीहेतोः सहसा कृतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Without taking counsel with my well-wishers and ministers, including those well-versed in the Vedas, was this step precipitately taken by me through excessive infatuation in order to please my wife. (19)

verses.text:
भवितव्यतया नूनमिदं वा व्यसनं महत्।
कुलस्यास्य विनाशाय प्राप्तं सूत यदृच्छया॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Or, this great calamity has surely taken us by surprise by the will of Providence for the destruction of this race, O charioteer ! (20)

verses.text:
सूत यद्यस्ति ते किंचिन्मयापि सुकृतं कृतम्।
त्वं प्रापयाशु मां रामं प्राणाः संत्वरयन्ति माम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “If at all, O charioteer, any good turn has been done to you by me, take you me at once to Rāma; for my senses are importunately hastening me to catch a last glimpse of Rāma. (21)

verses.text:
यद्यद्यापि ममैवाज्ञा निवर्तयतु राघवम्।
न शक्ष्यामि विना रामं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “If my authority alone prevails even today, let anyone fetch Rāma back to Ayodhyā; for I shall not be able to survive without Rāma even for an hour or so. (22)

verses.text:
अथवापि महाबाहुर्गतो दूरं भविष्यति।
मामेव रथमारोप्य शीघ्रं रामाय दर्शय॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Or, may be the mighty-armed prince might have gone afar by now. In that case helping me on to a chariot, promptly show me to Rāma. (23)

verses.text:
वृत्तदंष्ट्रो महेष्वासः क्वासौ लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।
यदि जीवामि साध्वेनं पश्येयं सीतया सह॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Where is that Rāma (the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa) who has pearl-like teeth and is possessed of a mighty bow? I can survive only if I am properly able to see him with Sītā. (24)

verses.text:
लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुमामुक्तमणिकुण्डलम्।
रामं यदि न पश्येयं गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “If I am not able to see the mighty-armed Rāma with reddish eyes and adorned with earrings made of gems, I shall surely reach the abode of Yama, the god of death. (25)

verses.text:
अतो नु किं दुःखतरं योऽहमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्।
इमामवस्थामापन्नो नेह पश्यामि राघवम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “What can possibly be more painful to me than the fact that I do not behold Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the delight of the Ikṣwākus, at this juncture, when I am reduced to this wretched plight? (26)

verses.text:
हा राम रामानुज हा हा वैदेहि तपस्विनि।
न मां जानीत दुःखेन म्रियमाणमनाथवत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Ah Rāma, Ah Lakṣmaṇa (younger brother of Rāma), Ah Sītā (a princess of the Videha clan), who are engaged in austerities, you do not know that I am dying through agony like a forlorn creature.” (27)

verses.text:
स तेन राजा दुःखेन भृशमर्पितचेतनः।
अवगाढः सुदुष्पारं शोकसागरमब्रवीत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: His mind being overwhelmed with that unbearable agony, and plunged as he was in that ocean of grief, which was most difficult to cross, the aforesaid king spoke of his grief in terms of an ocean in the following words : (28)

verses.text:
रामशोकमहावेगः सीताविरहपारगः।
श्वसितोर्मिमहावर्तो बाष्पवेगजलाविलः॥ २९॥
बाहुविक्षेपमीनोऽसौ विक्रन्दितमहास्वनः।
प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः कैकेयीवडवामुखः॥ ३०॥
ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः।
वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः॥ ३१॥
यस्मिन् बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना।
दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयायं शोकसागरः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “This ocean of grief, in which, alas! I am plunged, O Kausalyā, bereft as I am of Rāma, is difficult for me to cross while I am living, O godly lady ! Consciousness of Rāma’s grief caused by his separation from his parents, relations and friends etc., is its tremendous force. Severance from Sītā is the other shore to which it extends. Outgoing and ingoing breaths are the waves and whirlpools. It is rendered turbid by the water of rivers flowing into it in the shape of the upsurge of tears of Kausalyā and others. The throwing about of arms in agony represents the leaping of fishes. The loud wailings represent its roaring. Dishevelled hair are the sea-weeds. Kaikeyī represents the submarine fire. It is the source of showers in the form of the welling up of my tears. The words of Mantharā are so many mighty alligators infesting its waters. The couple of boons granted by me in favour of Kaikeyī represent its coastline and the term of Rāma’s exile marks its extent. (29—32)

verses.text:
अशोभनं योऽहमिहाद्य राघवं
दिदृक्षमाणो न लभे सलक्ष्मणम्।
इतीव राजा विलपन् महायशाः
पपात तूर्णं शयने स मूर्च्छितः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “It is most unfortunate that I am unable to clasp on Rāma, a scion of Raghu, alongwith Lakṣmaṇa on this spot today, even though I long to see them.” Lamenting thus, that highly illustrious monarch immediately dropped senseless, as it were, on the couch. (33)

verses.text:
इति विलपति पार्थिवे प्रणष्टे
करुणतरं द्विगुणं च रामहेतोः।
वचनमनुनिशम्य तस्य देवी
भयमगमत् पुनरेव राममाता॥ ३४॥
verses.m: When the Emperor fainted while lamenting most piteously for Rāma as aforesaid, Queen Kausalyā, Śrī Rāma’s mother, once more fell a prey to twofold fear on hearing his wail. (34)

verses.text:
ततो भूतोपसृष्टेव वेपमाना पुनः पुनः।
धरण्यां गतसत्त्वेव कौसल्या सूतमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Trembling again and again as though possessed by a spirit, and lying on the floor as though life had departed from her, Kausalyā thereupon spoke to Sumantra as follows : (1)

verses.text:
नय मां यत्र काकुत्स्थः सीता यत्र च लक्ष्मणः।
तान् विना क्षणमप्यद्य जीवितुं नोत्सहे ह्यहम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Take me to the place where Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa happen to be; for without them I cannot bear to live even for a moment longer today. (2)

verses.text:
निवर्तय रथं शीघ्रं दण्डकान् नय मामपि।
अथ तान् नानुगच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Quickly take the chariot back and convey me too to the Daṇḍaka forest. In case I do not follow them, I will proceed to the abode of Death.” (3)

verses.text:
बाष्पवेगोपहतया स वाचा सज्जमानया।
इदमाश्वासयन् देवीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeking to comfort the queen, the aforesaid charioteer submitted to her with folded hands as follows in a faltering voice choked with an upsurge of tears : (4)

verses.text:
त्यज शोकं च मोहं च सम्भ्रमं दुःखजं तथा।
व्यवधूय च संतापं वने वत्स्यति राघवः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Abandon grief and infatuation as well as agitation born of sorrow; for, shaking off agony, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) will take up his abode in the forest. (5)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामस्य पादौ परिचरन् वने।
आराधयति धर्मज्ञः परलोकं जितेन्द्रियः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Serving the feet of Śrī Rāma in the forest, Lakṣmaṇa too, who knows what is right and has subdued his senses, is straightening his path to the other world thereby. (6)

verses.text:
विजनेऽपि वने सीता वासं प्राप्य गृहेष्विव।
विस्रम्भं लभतेऽभीता रामे विन्यस्तमानसा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Getting her abode even in a lonely forest, Sītā, whose mind stands focussed on Śrī Rāma, remains undaunted and enjoys composure as if she were in her own house. (7)

verses.text:
नास्या दैन्यं कृतं किंचित् सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्ष्यते।
उचितेव प्रवासानां वैदेही प्रतिभाति मे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Not the faintest dejection of any kind caused by her exile is traceable in her. The daughter of Janaka, the ruler of the Videha kingdom, appears to me as though accustomed to staying away from home now and then. (8)

verses.text:
नगरोपवनं गत्वा यथा स्म रमते पुरा।
तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्वपि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Sītā finds as much delight in lonely forests as she used to do in the past whenever she visited the groves in the precincts of the city. (9)

verses.text:
बालेव रमते सीताबालचन्द्रनिभानना।
रामा रामे ह्यदीनात्मा विजनेऽपि वने सती॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The charming and virtuous Sītā, whose countenance shone like the full moon and who was ever undepressed in spirits, surely found delight as a girl even in the lonely forest in the presence of Śrī Rāma. (10)

verses.text:
तद्गतं हृदयं यस्यास्तदधीनं च जीवितम्।
अयोध्या हि भवेदस्या रामहीना तथा वनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Devoid of Śrī Rāma, however, Ayodhyā too would be no better than a forest to Sītā, whose heart is intent on him and whose life is dependent on him. (11)

verses.text:
परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च।
गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान् विविधानपि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Seeing villages and cities too as well as the flow of rivers as also trees of every description, Sītā, a princess of the Videha clan, makes inquiries concerning them of Rāma or Lakṣmaṇa, whoever is by her side. (12)

verses.text:
रामं वा लक्ष्मणं वापि दृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी।
अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव साश्रिता॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Finding Śrī Rāma or Lakṣmaṇa beside her, the daughter of Janaka feels that she is, as it were, on a visit to a pleasure-garden only a couple of miles away from Ayodhyā. (13)

verses.text:
इदमेव स्मराम्यस्याः सहसैवोपजल्पितम्।
कैकेयीसंश्रितं जल्पं नेदानीं प्रतिभाति माम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I remember only this much pertaining to Sītā. The remark uttered by her only in an unguarded moment concerning Kaikeyī does not strike me just at present.” (14)

verses.text:
ध्वंसयित्वा तु तद् वाक्यं प्रमादात् पर्युपस्थितम्।
ह्लादनं वचनं सूतो देव्या मधुरमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Skipping over that reference that had escaped from his lips through inadvertence, the charioteer spoke the following agreeable words that brought delight to the queen : (15)

verses.text:
अध्वना वातवेगेन सम्भ्रमेणातपेन च।
न विगच्छति वैदेह्याश्चन्द्रांशुसदृशी प्रभा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The splendour of Sītā (a princess of the Videha clan), which resembles the moonlight, does not fade through fatigue of the journey, high velocity of the winds, agitation caused by the sight of fearful beasts etc., and the heat of the sun. (16)

verses.text:
सदृशं शतपत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम्।
वदनं तद् वदान्याया वैदेह्या न विकम्पते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The well-known face of sweet-speaking Sītā, a princess of the Videha Kingdom, which resembles a lotus and whose effulgence vies with that of the full moon, never fades. (17)

verses.text:
अलक्तरसरक्ताभावलक्तरसवर्जितौ।
अद्यापि चरणौ तस्याः पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Her soles, which, though no longer painted with Alakta (the red juice obtained from the resin of certain trees), still look red as Alakta and cast an effulgence akin to that of a lotus bud. (18)

verses.text:
नूपुरोत्कृष्टलीलेव खेलं गच्छति भामिनी।
इदानीमपि वैदेही तद्रागान्यस्तभूषणा॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The high-minded Sītā (a princess of the Videha clan), who has not renounced her jewels out of love for Śrī Rāma, who is pleased to see her adorned, walks in a charming gait, as though outvying the cackling of swans by the music of her anklets. (19)

verses.text:
गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिंहं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता।
नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Though living in the forest, she does not give way to fear on seeing an elephant or a lion or a tiger, fully relying as she does on the arms of Śrī Rāma. (20)

verses.text:
न शोच्यास्ते न चात्मा ते शोच्यो नापि जनाधिपः।
इदं हि चरितं लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Neither they, nor your own self, nor the king deserves to be pitied. This story of Śrī Rāma will abide in the world forever. (21)

verses.text:
विधूय शोकं परिहृष्टमानसा
महर्षियाते पथि सुव्यवस्थिताः।
वने रता वन्यफलाशनाः पितुः
शुभां प्रतिज्ञां प्रतिपालयन्ति ते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having shaken off grief, the three exiles, who are firmly established with a highly delighted mind on the path trodden by eminent sages and are enamoured of the forest, are fully implementing the sacred vow of their father, living on wild fruits etc., alone.” (22)

verses.text:
तथापि सूतेन सुयुक्तवादिना
निवार्यमाणा सुतशोककर्शिता।
न चैव देवी विरराम कूजितात्
प्रियेति पुत्रेति च राघवेति च॥ २३॥
verses.m: Even though being forbidden in the aforesaid manner by the charioteer, who spoke highly reasonable words, queen Kausalyā, who was torn with grief caused by separation from her son, did not cease in the least from crying out: “O my darling ! O my son !! O scion of Raghu !!!” (23)

verses.text:
वनं गते धर्मरते रामे रमयतां वरे।
कौसल्या रुदती चार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, who was devoted to righteousness and was the foremost among those who bring delight to the people, having departed for the forest, Kausalyā, who was feeling distressed due to separation from her son spoke weeping to her husband as follows : (1)

verses.text:
यद्यपि त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितं ते महद् यशः।
सानुक्रोशो वदान्यश्च प्रियवादी च राघवः॥ २॥
कथं नरवरश्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया।
दुःखितौ सुखसंवृद्धौ वने दुःखं सहिष्यतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Although your great glory is extended through all the three worlds, and it is well-known that you, a scion of Raghu, are full of compassion and generous and speak kindly to all, you never paused to think how your aforesaid two sons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, with Sītā, who have been brought up in ease, will endure suffering in the forest when faced with hardships, O jewel among the foremost of men ! (2-3)

verses.text:
सा नूनं तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुखोचिता।
कथमुष्णं च शीतं च मैथिली विसहिष्यते॥ ४॥
