यथा दृष्टिः शरीरस्य नित्यमेव प्रवर्तते।
तथा नरेन्द्रो राष्ट्रस्य प्रभवः सत्यधर्मयोः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Just as the eye ever strives for the good of the body by serving as a guide to it and showing it the right path, so does the king, who is the fountain of truth and righteousness, ever strive for the good of the state. (33)

verses.text:
राजा सत्यं च धर्मश्च राजा कुलवतां कुलम्।
राजा माता पिता चैव राजा हितकरो नृणाम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “The king is truthfulness and virtue incarnate; the king constitutes the nobility of birth in men of a high pedigree. The king is the mother as well as the father; the king is the benefactor of men. (34)

verses.text:
यमो वैश्रवणः शक्रो वरुणश्च महाबलः।
विशिष्यन्ते नरेन्द्रेण वृत्तेन महता ततः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Even Yama, the god of retribution, Kubera (son of Viśravā, the god of riches), Indra (the ruler of gods) and the very mighty Varuṇa (the deity presiding over water) are outstripped by a king of excellent conduct by virtue of such conduct inasmuch as he combines in himself the virtues of all the above-named deities. (35)

verses.text:
अहो तम इवेदं स्यान्न प्रज्ञायेत किंचन।
राजा चेन्न भवेल्लोके विभजन् साध्वसाधुनी॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “If there is no king demarcating good and evil in the world, oh, this world will be reduced to utter darkness, as it were, and nothing can be clearly perceived. (36)

verses.text:
जीवत्यपि महाराजे तवैव वचनं वयम्।
नातिक्रमामहे सर्वे बेलां प्राप्येव सागरः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Even while the Emperor was alive, we all never violated, O sage Vasiṣṭha, your command, any more than the oceans overstep the coastline on reaching it. (37)

verses.text:
स नः समीक्ष्य द्विजवर्य वृत्तं
नृपं विना राष्ट्रमरण्यभूतम्।
कुमारमिक्ष्वाकुसुतं तथान्यं
त्वमेव राजानमिहाभिषेचय॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, fully considering our past conduct, which has ever been loyal to the king and devoted to the best interests of the state and looking on the state, which has been converted into a veritable jungle for want of a king, crown you alone as king on this throne any prince who is a scion of Ikṣwāku, or anyone else, O jewel among the Brāhmaṇas !” (38)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह।
मित्रामात्यजनान् सर्वान् ब्राह्मणांस्तानिदं वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid speech of the counsellors, Mārkaṇḍeya and others, Vasiṣṭha, they say, addressed the following words to the king’s friends, the ministers as well as to all the Brāhmaṇas assembled there on that occasion : (1)

verses.text:
यदसौ मातुलकुले दत्तराज्यः परं सुखी।
भरतो वसति भ्रात्रा शत्रुघ्नेन मुदान्वितः॥ २॥
तच्छीघ्रं जवना दूता गच्छन्तु त्वरितं हयैः।
आनेतुं भ्रातरौ वीरौ किं समीक्षामहे वयम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Since the celebrated Bharata, on whom kingship has been bestowed by the Emperor, as urged by Kaikeyī, is leading a most happy and joyous life at his maternal uncle’s with his younger brother Śatrughna; therefore, let swift messengers proceed quickly on horses to bring the two gallant brothers. What else can we thoughtfully consider?” (2-3)

verses.text:
गच्छन्त्विति ततः सर्वे वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रुवन्।
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Then all submitted to Vasiṣṭha as follows : “Let the messengers depart.” Hearing that reply of the counsellors, Vasiṣṭha again spoke as follows : (4)

verses.text:
एहि सिद्धार्थ विजय जयन्ताशोकनन्दन।
श्रूयतामितिकर्तव्यं सर्वानेव ब्रवीमि वः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Come along, O Siddhārtha, Vijaya, Jayanta, Aśoka and Nandana ! Please hear what has got to be done by you : I speak to you all. (5)

verses.text:
पुरं राजगृहं गत्वा शीघ्रं शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः।
त्यक्तशोकैरिदं वाच्यः शासनाद् भरतो मम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Reaching the city of Rājagṛha quickly on (the back of) horses galloping at a swift speed, and shaking off grief, you should speak to Bharata under my orders as follows : (6)

verses.text:
पुरोहितस्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः।
त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘The family-priest as well as all the counsellors have told you that all is well. Pray, depart hence hastily; there is some most urgent business awaiting you.’ (7)

verses.text:
मा चास्मै प्रोषितं रामं मा चास्मै पितरं मृतम्।
भवन्तः शंसिषुर्गत्वा राघवाणामितः क्षयम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Going there, pray, do not inform him of Rāma having gone into exile or of his father having demised or of the threatened destruction of the scions of Raghu as a result of these incidents. (8)

verses.text:
कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि भूषणानि वराणि च।
क्षिप्रमादाय राज्ञश्च भरतस्य च गच्छत॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Taking with you silken robes as well as excellent ornaments for the king, Bharata’s maternal grandfather, and for Bharata as a present from the king of Ayodhyā, depart at once.” (9)

verses.text:
दत्तपथ्यशना दूता जग्मुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्।
केकयांस्ते गमिष्यन्तो हयानारुह्य सम्मतान्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Having been furnished with the wherewithals to purchase provisions for the journey and while about to leave for the Kekaya kingdom mounting horses thought highly of for their swiftness, the messengers proceeded each to his own house to take leave of his own people. (10)

verses.text:
ततः प्रास्थानिकं कृत्वा कार्यशेषमनन्तरम्।
वसिष्ठेनाभ्यनुज्ञाता दूताः संत्वरितं ययुः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having immediately finished all preparations that remained to be made for the journey, and duly permitted by Vasiṣṭha, the messengers proceeded post haste to their destination. (11)

verses.text:
न्यन्तेनापरतालस्य प्रलम्बस्योत्तरं प्रति।
निषेवमाणास्ते जग्मुर्नदीं मध्येन मालिनीम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: They moved on touching Mālinī river flowing between the extreme southern end of Aparatāla mountain and the northern end of Pralamba mountain. (12)

verses.text:
ते हास्तिनपुरे गङ्गां तीर्त्वा प्रत्यङ्मुखा ययुः।
पाञ्चालदेशमासाद्य मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्॥ १३॥
सरांसि च सुफुल्लानि नदीश्च विमलोदकाः।
निरीक्षमाणा जग्मुस्ते दूताः कार्यवशाद्द्रुतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Crossing the Gaṅgā at Hastināpura they proceeded westward and, reaching the territory of Pañcāla through Kurujāṅgala and keenly perceiving lakes with full-blown flowers and rivers containing limpid waters, the aforesaid messengers swiftly moved on because of the pressing nature of their errand. (13-14)

verses.text:
ते प्रसन्नोदकां दिव्यां नानाविहगसेविताम्।
उपातिजग्मुर्वेगेन शरदण्डां जलाकुलाम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Reaching the bank of the charming river Śaradaṇḍā, which not only contained translucent waters but was also full of water and was frequented by birds of various kinds, they speedily crossed it. (15)

verses.text:
निकूलवृक्षमासाद्य दिव्यं सत्योपयाचनम्।
अभिगम्याभिवाद्यं तं कुलिङ्गां प्राविशन् पुरीम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Reaching a holy tree (inhabited by some divinity) standing on the western bank of the Śaradaṇḍā, and named Satyopayācana (so-called because prayers addressed to it invariably proved efficacious), which was worthy of salutation, and going round it clockwise as a token of respect, the messengers entered the city of Kuliṅgā. (16)

verses.text:
अभिकालं ततः प्राप्य तेजोऽभिभवनाच्च्युताः।
पितृपैतामहीं पुण्यां तेरुरिक्षुमतीं नदीम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Emerged from the village of Tejobhibhavana and reaching thence the village of Abhikāla, the messengers crossed the holy river Ikṣumatī, associated with the father and grandfather of the deceased Emperor. (17)

verses.text:
अवेक्ष्याञ्जलिपानांश्च ब्राह्मणान् वेदपारगान्।
ययुर्मध्येन बाह्लीकान् सुदामानं च पर्वतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Nay, perceiving Brāhmaṇas, who had mastered the Vedas and lived on as much water as could be contained in the hollow of their palms, they reached the Sudāmā mountain in the interior of the Bāhlīka kingdom, now known by the name of Balkh. (18)

verses.text:
विष्णोः पदं प्रेक्ष्यमाणा विपाशां चापि शाल्मलीम्।
नदीर्वापीतटाकानि पल्वलानि सरांसि च॥ १९॥
पश्यन्तो विविधांश्चापि सिंहान् व्याघ्रान् मृगान् द्विपान्।
ययुः पथातिमहता शासनं भर्तुरीप्सवः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Beholding the spot on the top of Sudāmā mountain containing the footprints of Lord Viṣṇu, as well as the rivers Vipāśā (now known by the name of Beas) and Śālmalī and other rivers, big wells provided with stairs to reach the water and ponds, pools and lakes, and looking on lions, tigers, deer and elephants of various kinds, they proceeded along an exceptionally broad highway, keen as they were to execute the command of their master. (19-20)

verses.text:
ते श्रान्तवाहना दूता विकृष्टेन सता पथा।
गिरिव्रजं पुरवरं शीघ्रमासेदुरञ्जसा॥ २१॥
verses.m: Even though their horses felt exhausted, the messengers shortly and directly reached the foremost town of Girivraja, the capital of the Kekaya kingdom, by a long yet peaceful route. (21)

verses.text:
भर्तुः प्रियार्थं कुलरक्षणार्थं
भर्तुश्च वंशस्य परिग्रहार्थम्।
अहेडमानास्त्वरया स्म दूता
रात्र्यां तु ते तत्पुरमेव याताः॥ २२॥
verses.m: For the pleasure of their master, Sage Vasiṣṭha, as well as for the protection of the people and for vindicating the honour of their king’s race, the messengers for their part respectfully and speedily entered that town during the night itself. (22)

verses.text:
यामेव रात्रिं ते दूताः प्रविशन्ति स्म तां पुरीम्।
भरतेनापि तां रात्रिं स्वप्नो दृष्टोऽयमप्रियः॥ १॥
verses.m: The very night the aforesaid messengers entered that city of Girivraja an unpleasant dream, which is being described as follows, was seen by Bharata. (1)

verses.text:
व्युष्टामेव तु तां रात्रिं दृष्ट्वा तं स्वप्नमप्रियम्।
पुत्रो राजाधिराजस्य सुभृशं पर्यतप्यत॥ २॥
verses.m: Seeing that unpleasant dream at an hour* when the night had well-nigh ended, Bharata, the emperor’s son, felt extremely perturbed. (2)

verses.text:
तप्यमानं तमाज्ञाय वयस्याः प्रियवादिनः।
आयासं विनयिष्यन्तः सभायां चक्रिरे कथाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Finding him disconsolate, his friends, who ever spoke kindly to him, commenced chatting in a coterie, seeking, as they did, to relieve his agony. (3)

verses.text:
वादयन्ति तदा शान्तिं लासयन्त्यपि चापरे।
नाटकान्यपरे स्माहुर्हास्यानि विविधानि च॥ ४॥
verses.m: Some friends played upon musical instruments at that time, while others indulged in gentle dance accompanied with vocal and instrumental music, with a view to relieving his anxiety; while still others read out to him dramas of various kinds having mirth for their dominant sentiment. (4)

verses.text:
स तैर्महात्मा भरतः सखिभिः प्रियवादिभिः।
गोष्ठीहास्यानि कुर्वद्भिर्न प्राहृष्यत राघवः॥ ५॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Bharata, a scion of Raghu and an exalted soul as he was, did not, however, feel much delighted in the company of those friends, who spoke kindly to him and indulged in jokes worthy of an assembly. (5)

verses.text:
तमब्रवीत् प्रियसखो भरतं सखिभिर्वृतम्।
सुहृद्भिः पर्युपासीनः किं सखे नानुमोदसे॥ ६॥
verses.m: A beloved friend of Bharata spoke as follows to the said Bharata, who was surrounded by many friends : “Why, O friend, do you not join us in rejoicing, sitting as you are in the midst of friends?” (6)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं सुहृदं भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह।
शृणु त्वं यन्निमित्तं मे दैन्यमेतदुपागतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: To the friend speaking as aforesaid, Bharata replied as follows : “Hear you the circumstances due to which this depression has overtaken me. (7)

verses.text:
स्वप्ने पितरमद्राक्षं मलिनं मुक्तमूर्धजम्।
पतन्तमद्रिशिखरात् कलुषे गोमये ह्रदे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “In a dream I saw father dejected and falling from a mountain-peak, his hair dishevelled, into a dirty pool full of cow-dung. (8)

verses.text:
प्लवमानश्च मे दृष्टः स तस्मिन् गोमये ह्रदे।
पिबन्नञ्जलिना तैलं हसन्निव मुहुर्मुहुः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “He was further seen by me swimming in that pool of cow-dung, drinking oil from the hollow of his palms and laughing as it were, again and again. (9)

verses.text:
ततस्तिलोदनं भुक्त्वा पुनः पुनरधःशिराः।
तैलेनाभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्गस्तैलमेवान्वगाहत ॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Then, partaking of rice cooked with sesame seeds and himself smeared all over with sesame oil, he took a dip again and again, head foremost in the oil. (10)

verses.text:
स्वप्नेऽपि सागरं शुष्कं चन्द्रं च पतितं भुवि।
उपरुद्धां च जगतीं तमसेव समावृताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Also in the dream I saw the ocean dry and the moon fallen on the earth and the entire globe molested by Rākṣasas and others and enveloped, as it were, in darkness. (11)

verses.text:
औपवाह्यस्य नागस्य विषाणं शकलीकृतम्।
सहसा चापि संशान्ता ज्वलिता जातवेदसः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I further beheld a tusk of the king’s elephant broken to pieces and blazing fires suddenly extinguished. (12)

verses.text:
अवदीर्णां च पृथिवीं शुष्कांश्च विविधान् द्रुमान्।
अहं पश्यामि विध्वस्तान् सधूमांश्चैव पर्वतान्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I also saw the earth riven and trees of various kinds withered up and mountains too emitting smoke and razed to the ground. (13)

verses.text:
पीठे कार्ष्णायसे चैव निषष्ण्णं कृष्णवाससम्।
प्रहरन्ति स्म राजानं प्रमदाः कृष्णपिङ्गलाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Young women, dark and reddish brown of complexion, assailed the king, seated on an iron seat, attired in black. (14)

verses.text:
त्वरमाणश्च धर्मात्मा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः।
रथेन खरयुक्तेन प्रयातो दक्षिणामुखः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Nay, adorned with a garland of crimson flowers and smeared with red sandal-paste, the pious-minded king hastily departed southward in a chariot drawn by donkeys.(15)

verses.text:
प्रहसन्तीव राजानं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी।
प्रकर्षन्ती मया दृष्टा राक्षसी विकृतानना॥ १६॥
verses.m: “A young ogress with an ugly face and clad in crimson was seen by me mocking the king, as it were, and dragging him. (16)

verses.text:
एवमेतन्मया दृष्टमिमां रात्रिं भयावहाम्।
अहं रामोऽथवा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “During the last night, fearful as it was, this was the vision seen by me as aforesaid. This prognosticates that either myself or Śrī Rāma or the king or Lakṣmaṇa is going to die. (17)

verses.text:
नरो यानेन यः स्वप्ने खरयुक्तेन याति हि।
अचिरात्तस्य धूम्राग्रं चितायां सम्प्रदृश्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “A column of smoke is surely and vividly perceived before long on the funeral pile of a man who drives in a dream in a chariot drawn by donkeys. (18)

verses.text:
एतन्निमित्तं दीनोऽहं न वचः प्रतिपूजये।
शुष्यतीव च मे कण्ठो न स्वस्थमिव मे मनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “This is why I feel depressed and do not make much of your words. My throat is getting parched, as it were, and my mind is not quite at ease. (19)

verses.text:
न पश्यामि भयस्थानं भयं चैवोपधारये।
भ्रष्टश्च स्वरयोगो मे छाया चापगता मम।
जुगुप्सु इव चात्मानं न च पश्यामि कारणम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I do not perceive any tangible ground for fear, yet I experience fear. Nay, my voice has become hoarse and my lustre has departed. Moreover, I have begun to hate myself, yet I do not see any cause for it. (20)

verses.text:
इमां च दुःस्वप्नगतिं निशम्य हि
त्वनेकरूपामवितर्कितां पुरा।
भयं महत् तुद् हृदयान्न याति मे
विचिन्त्य राजानमचिन्त्यदर्शनम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Even as I reflect on the course of my evil dreams, which were seen in many forms—a course which was never imagined by me before—and even as I think deeply of the king, whose sight is something which can no longer be anticipated, the great fear that has been roused in me does not depart from my heart.” (21)

verses.text:
भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नं दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः।
प्रविश्यासह्यपरिखं रम्यं राजगृहं पुरम्॥ १॥
समागम्य च राज्ञा ते राजपुत्रेण चार्चिताः।
राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा च तमूचुर्भरतं वचः॥ २॥
verses.m: Entering the lovely city of Rājagṛha—the moat enclosing which was unassailable by the enemies—at a time when Bharata was narrating the dream to his friends, their horses being exhausted, nay, meeting the king of Kekaya as well as the Crown prince and treated with honour by them, and touching as a mark of respect the feet of Bharata, their prospective king, the aforesaid messengers spoke to the celebrated Bharata as follows : (1-2)

verses.text:
पुरोहितस्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः।
त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Sage Vasiṣṭha (the family-priest) as well as all the counsellors tell you that all is well. Yet please depart expeditiously. There is business with you, which cannot brook delay. (3)

verses.text:
इमानि च महार्हाणि वस्त्राण्याभरणानि च।
प्रतिगृह्य विशालाक्ष मातुलस्य च दापय॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Nay, accepting from us these valuable robes and jewels, O large-eyed prince, have them presented to your maternal grandfather and maternal uncle too. (4)

verses.text:
अत्र विंशतिकोट्यस्तु नृपतेर्मातुलस्य ते।
दशकोट्यस्तु सम्पूर्णास्तथैव च नृपात्मज॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Of these, articles worth twenty crores, of course, are meant for the king; while full ten crores worth of articles are likewise meant for your maternal uncle, O prince !” (5)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तत् सर्वं स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज्जने।
दूतानुवाच भरतः कामैः सम्प्रतिपूज्य तान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Accepting for his part all those presents brought by the messengers from Ayodhyā, Bharata, who was very fond of his near and dear ones, had them presented on behalf of his royal father to his maternal grandfather and maternal uncle and, having entertained the messengers with articles of food and drink coveted by them, spoke to them as follows : (6)

verses.text:
कच्चित् स कुशली राजा पिता दशरथो मम।
कच्चिदारोग्यता रामे लक्ष्मणे च महात्मनि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Is my father, the celebrated Daśaratha, doing well? Does good health abide in Śrī Rāma and the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa? (7)

verses.text:
आर्या च धर्मनिरता धर्मज्ञा धर्मवादिनी।
अरोगा चापि कौसल्या माता रामस्य धीमतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “And is the mother of the wise Śrī Rāma, the noble Kausalyā, who is devoted to virtue, knows what is right and talks virtue, enjoying good health? (8)

verses.text:
कच्चित् सुमित्रा धर्मज्ञा जननी लक्ष्मणस्य या।
शत्रुघ्नस्य च वीरस्य अरोगा चापि मध्यमा॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Is my intermediate mother, Sumitrā—who knows what is right and is the mother of Lakṣmaṇa and the valiant Śatrughna—also free from ailment? (9)

verses.text:
आत्मकामा सदा चण्डी क्रोधना प्राज्ञमानिनी।
अरोगा चापि मे माता कैकेयी किमुवाच ह॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Is my own mother, Kaikeyī, who always seeks to gain her own ends, is violent and given to wrath and accounts herself wise—also healthy and what message has she sent for me?” (10)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते दूता भरतेन महात्मना।
ऊचुः सम्प्रश्रितं वाक्यमिदं तं भरतं तदा॥ ११॥
verses.m: Questioned thus by the high-souled Bharata on that occasion, the aforesaid messengers for their part addressed the following most polite words to the said Bharata : (11)

verses.text:
कुशलास्ते नरव्याघ्र येषां कुशलमिच्छसि।
श्रीश्च त्वां वृणुते पद्मा युज्यतां चापि ते रथः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “They are all well, whose welfare you seek, O tiger among men ! Nay, holding a lotus in her hand, Śrī, the goddess of fortune, looks on you with favour. Therefore let your chariot be equipped for journey.” (12)

verses.text:
भरतश्चापि तान् दूतानेवमुक्तोऽभ्यभाषत।
आपृच्छेऽहं महाराजं दूताः संत्वरयन्ति माम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Told thus, Bharata too replied to the messengers, “I shall presently seek the permission of the monarch, my maternal grandfather, saying that you, the messengers, are urging me to make haste to depart for Ayodhyā”. (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तान् दूतान् भरतः पार्थिवात्मजः।
दूतैः संचोदितो वाक्यं मातामहमुवाच ह॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having told the messengers thus, Prince Bharata for his part made the following submission to his maternal grandfather, as entreated by the messengers : so the tradition goes : (14)

verses.text:
राजन् पितुर्गमिष्यामि सकाशं दूतचोदितः।
पुनरप्यहमेष्यामि यदा मे त्वं स्मरिष्यसि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Urged by the messengers, I shall, Your Majesty, return to the presence of my father. I shall come again whenever you remember me.” (15)

verses.text:
भरतेनैवमुक्तस्तु नृपो मातामहस्तदा।
तमुवाच शुभं वाक्यं शिरस्याघ्राय राघवम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Smelling (as a token of affection) the head of Bharata (a scion of Raghu), when requested as aforesaid by the latter on that occasion, the king, his maternal grandfather, addressed to him the following agreeable words : (16)

verses.text:
गच्छ तातानुजाने त्वां कैकेयी सुप्रजास्त्वया।
मातरं कुशलं ब्रूयाः पितरं च परंतप॥ १७॥
पुरोहितं च कुशलं ये चान्ये द्विजसत्तमाः।
तौ च तात महेष्वासौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Depart, dear child ! I grant you leave to return to Ayodhyā. Kaikeyī is blessed with a noble son in you. Communicate, O tormentor of enemies, our welfare to your mother as well as to your father on my behalf, also to Sage Vasiṣṭha (the family-priest) and to other jewels among Brāhmaṇas, whoever are present on the occasion and lastly to the two celebrated brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the wielders of mighty bows.” (17-18)

verses.text:
तस्मै हस्त्युत्तमांश्चित्रान् कम्बलानजिनानि च।
सत्कृत्य केकयो राजा भरताय ददौ धनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Treating him with honour, the king of Kekaya bestowed on the aforesaid Bharata foremost of elephants, multi-coloured blankets, deerskins and riches consisting of gold vessels etc. (19)

verses.text:
अन्तःपुरेऽतिसंवृद्धान् व्याघ्रवीर्यबलोपमान्।
दंष्ट्रायुक्तान् महाकायान् शुनश्चोपायनं ददौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: He also gave as a present dogs of enormous size, possessed of large teeth, brought up with care in the gynaeceum itself and vying in prowess and strength of body with a tiger. (20)

verses.text:
रुक्मनिष्कसहस्रे द्वे षोडशाश्वशतानि च।
सत्कृत्य केकयीपुत्रं केकयो धनमादिशत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Receiving him kindly, the king of the Kekayas further bestowed on Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, wealth consisting of two thousand gold mohurs and sixteen hundred horses. (21)

verses.text:
तदामात्यानभिप्रेतान् विश्वास्यांश्च गुणान्वितान्।
ददावश्वपतिः शीघ्रं भरतायानुयायिनः॥ २२॥
verses.m: On that occasion King Aśwapati also quickly sent as escorts for Bharata esteemed and trustworthy ministers endowed with good qualities. (22)

verses.text:
ऐरावतानैन्द्रशिरान् नागान् वै प्रियदर्शनान्।
खरान् शीघ्रान् सुसंयुक्तान् मातुलोऽस्मै धनं ददौ॥ २३॥
verses.m: Bharata’s maternal uncle, Yudhājit, too bestowed on him wealth consisting of elephants of the Airāvata breed and those born in the territory of Indraśira and agreeable to the sight, as well as swift-going and well-trained mules. (23)

verses.text:
स दत्तं केकयेन्द्रेण धनं तन्नाभ्यनन्दत।
भरतः केकयीपुत्रो गमनत्वरया तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Because of his hurry to depart for Ayodhyā, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, did not at that moment welcome the aforesaid wealth gifted by the king of the Kekayas. (24)

verses.text:
बभूव ह्यस्य हृदये चिन्ता सुमहती तदा।
त्वरया चापि दूतानां स्वप्नस्यापि च दर्शनात्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Nay, due to the hastening of the messengers and also because of his having seen the ominous dream indeed a (very) great anxiety appeared in his heart at that time. (25)

verses.text:
स स्ववेश्माभ्यतिक्रम्य नरनागाश्वसंकुलम्।
प्रपेदे सुमहच्छ्रीमान् राजमार्गमनुत्तमम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Returning to his own residence and then leaving it, Bharata, who now owned a very large fortune, reached the main road, which was crowded with men, elephants and horses and unexcelled by other roads. (26)

verses.text:
अभ्यतीत्य ततोऽपश्यदन्तःपुरमनुत्तमम्।
ततस्तद् भरतः श्रीमानाविवेशानिवारितः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Passing thence he saw the gynaeceum, which was unsurpassed by other mansions. The glorious Bharata thereupon entered it unchallenged. (27)

verses.text:
स मातामहमापृच्छ्य मातुलं च युधाजितम्।
रथमारुह्य भरतः शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ॥ २८॥
verses.m: Taking leave of his maternal grandfather and grandmother as well as of his maternal uncle, Yudhājit, and aunt and mounting his chariot with Śatrughna, the said Bharata left for Ayodhyā. (28)

verses.text:
रथान् मण्डलचक्रांश्च योजयित्वा परः शतम्।
उष्ट्रगोऽश्वखरैर्भृत्या भरतं यान्तमन्वयुः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Fitting a hundred other chariots having circular wheels with camels, bullocks, horses and mules, servants of King Aśwapati followed Bharata as he departed. (29)

verses.text:
बलेन गुप्तो भरतो महात्मा
सहार्यकस्यात्मसमैरमात्यैः।
आदाय शत्रुघ्नमपेतशत्रु-
र्गृहाद् ययौ सिऽद्ध इवेन्द्रलोकात्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Guarded by a detachment sent by his maternal grandfather and taking Śatrughna with him, Bharata, who was possessed of great fortitude and had no enemies, departed with ministers, who were equalled by none but themselves, from his residence even as a Siddha (a member of a class of demigods credited with supernatural powers by virtue of their very birth) would from the realm of Indra, the lord of paradise. (30)

verses.text:
स प्राङ्मुखो राजगृहादभिनिर्याय वीर्यवान्।
ततः सुदामां द्युतिमान् संतीर्यावेक्ष्य तां नदीम्॥ १॥
ह्रादिनीं दूरपारां च प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम्।
शतद्रुमतरच्छ्रीमान् नदीमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Proceeding from Rājagṛha in an easterly direction and then surveying and crossing the well-known river Sudāmā* as well as the broad river Hrādinī, the powerful and dignified Bharata, a glorious scion of Ikṣwāku, crossed the river Śatadru (the modern Sutlej), whose stream takes a westward course. (1-2)

verses.text:
ऐलधाने नदीं तीर्त्वा प्राप्य चापरपर्वतान्।
शिलामाकुर्वतीं तीर्त्वा आग्नेयं शल्यकर्षणम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Crossing another stream at Ailadhāna, a village of that name, and reaching the territory of Aparaparvata and crossing a river which petrified everything thrown into it, he reached the tract lying to the south-east and known by the name of Śalyakarṣaṇa (so-called because it abounded in a herb possessing the virtue of extracting a thorn etc.,). (3)

verses.text:
सत्यसंधः शुचिर्भूत्वा प्रेक्षमाणः शिलावहाम्।
अभ्यगात् स महाशैलान् वनं चैत्ररथं प्रति॥ ४॥
verses.m: Gazing on the river Śilāvahā (so-called because it carried away even rocks along its swift stream) and getting purified (through bathing in it), Bharata, who was true to his promise, crossed the Mahāśaila hills heading towards the forest of Caitraratha. (4)

verses.text:
सरस्वतीं च गङ्गां च युग्मेन प्रतिपद्य च।
उत्तरान् वीरमत्स्यानां भारुण्डं प्राविशद् वनम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Reaching the river Saraswatī, flowing towards the west and a branch of the holy Gaṅgā at their confluence, he passed through the northern part of the Vīramatsya territory and entered the forest of Bhāruṇḍa. (5)

verses.text:
वेगिनीं च कुलिङ्गाख्यां ह्रादिनीं पर्वतावृताम्।
यमुनां प्राप्य संतीर्णो बलमाश्वासयत् तदा॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having duly crossed the swift and thundering river named Kuliṅgā, hemmed in by mountains, and reaching the Yamunā, he allowed the detachment accompanying him to rest for the time being. (6)

verses.text:
शीतीकृत्य तु गात्राणि क्लान्तानाश्वास्य वाजिनः।
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च प्रायादादाय चोदकम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Refreshing the limbs of the horses by bathing them and giving the fatigued animals food and rest in the shade of trees, nay, himself bathing and quenching his thirst, and taking water for the journey ahead, Bharata proceeded further. (7)

verses.text:
राजपुत्रो महारण्यमनभीक्ष्णोपसेवितम्।
भद्रो भद्रेण यानेन मारुतः खमिवात्यगात्॥ ८॥
verses.m: The prince, who had undergone propitious rites before embarking on the long journey, crossed speedily by his excellent chariot the great forest lying on the way, which was not frequented, even as the wind sweeps through the atmosphere. (8)

verses.text:
भागीरथीं दुष्प्रतरां सोंऽशुधाने महानदीम्।
उपायाद् राघवस्तूर्णं प्राग्वटे विश्रुते पुरे॥ ९॥
verses.m: Finding the great river Gaṅgā associated with the name of Emperor Bhagīratha, who was instrumental in bringing the stream to the terrestrial region difficult to cross at the village of Aṁśudhāna, Bharata, a scion of Raghu, hastily approached it with a view to crossing it at the well-known town of Prāgvaṭa, where it could be easily crossed. (9)

verses.text:
स गङ्गां प्राग्वटे तीर्त्वा समायात् कुटिकोष्टिकाम्।
सबलस्तां स तीर्त्वाथ समगाद् धर्मवर्धनम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Crossing the holy Gaṅgā at Prāgvaṭa, he reached the river Kuṭikoṣṭikā. Again crossing the latter alongwith the detachment accompanying him, he duly arrived at the village of Dharmavardhana. (10)

verses.text:
तोरणं दक्षिणार्धेन जम्बूप्रस्थं समागमत्।
वरूथं च ययौ रम्यं ग्रामं दशरथात्मजः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Bharata, son of Daśaratha, duly reached the village of Jambūprastha through the southern portion of the village of Toraṇa and then arrived at the lovely village of Varūtha. (11)

verses.text:
तत्र रम्ये वने वासं कृत्वासौ प्राङ्मुखो ययौ।
उद्यानमुज्जिहानायाः प्रियका यत्र पादपाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Having halted for the night in a delightful grove adjoining that village, he drove in an easterly direction to the garden of Ujjihānā, a city, in which existed a cluster of Kadamba trees. (12)

verses.text:
स तांस्तु प्रियकान् प्राप्य शीघ्रानास्थाय वाजिनः।
अनुज्ञाप्याथ भरतो वाहिनीं त्वरितो ययौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having reached those Kadamba trees and getting swifter horses yoked to his chariot and allowing the army to come slowly since he had reached his own territory, Bharata for his part hastily proceeded further. (13)

verses.text:
वासं कृत्वा सर्वतीर्थे तीर्त्वा चोत्तानिकां नदीम्।
अन्या नदीश्च विविधैः पार्वतीयैस्तुरङ्गमैः॥ १४॥
हस्तिपृष्ठकमासाद्य कुटिकामप्यवर्तत।
ततार च नरव्याघ्रो लोहित्ये च कपीवतीम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having halted that night in the village of Sarvatīrtha and forded next morning the river Uttānikā and other streams on the back of various mountain ponies and reaching the village of Hastipṛṣṭhaka, Bharata, a tiger among men, crossed the river Kuṭikā and at Lohitya (another village) crossed the river Kapīvatī, too. (14-15)

verses.text:
एकसाले स्थाणुमतीं विनते गोमतीं नदीम्।
कलिङ्गनगरे चापि प्राप्य सालवनं तदा॥ १६॥
भरतः क्षिप्रमागच्छत् सुपरिश्रान्तवाहनः।
वनं च समतीत्याशु शर्वर्यामरुणोदये॥ १७॥
अयोध्यां मनुना राज्ञा निर्मितां स ददर्श ह।
तां पुरीं पुरुषव्याघ्रः सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि॥ १८॥
verses.m: He crossed the Sthāṇumatī at the village of Ekasāla and, reaching the river Gomatī, he crossed it near the village of Vinata. And then Bharata quickly reached a grove of sal trees at Kaliṅganagara. Nay, hurriedly driving through the grove during the night, his horses having been completely exhausted, the tiger among men beheld the celebrated city of Ayodhyā, founded by King Vaivaswata Manu, at dawn, having spent seven nights, on the way: so the tradition goes. (16—18)

verses.text:
अयोध्यामग्रतो दृष्ट्वा सारथिं चेदमब्रवीत्।
एषा नातिप्रतीता मे पुण्योद्याना यशस्विनी॥ १९॥
verses.m: Nay, seeing Ayodhyā in front of him, Bharata spoke as follows to the charioteer : “This well-famed city, consisting of sacred gardens, does not look very cheerful to me. (19)

verses.text:
अयोध्या दृश्यते दूरात् सारथे पाण्डुमृत्तिका।
यज्विभिर्गुणसम्पन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः ॥ २०॥
भूयिष्ठमृद्धैराकीर्णा राजर्षिवरपालिता।
अयोध्यायां पुरा शब्दः श्रूयते तुमुलो महान्॥ २१॥
समन्तान्नरनारीणां तमद्य न शृणोम्यहम्।
उद्यानानि हि सायाह्ने क्रीडित्वोपरतैर्नरैः॥ २२॥
समन्ताद् विप्रधावद्भिः प्रकाशन्ते ममान्यथा।
तान्यद्यानुरुदन्तीव परित्यक्तानि कामिभिः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Ayodhyā, O charioteer, which was thickly crowded with Brāhmaṇas given to sacrificial performances, endowed with good qualities and well-versed in the Vedas, as well as with wealthy men and was protected by the foremost of royal sages, looks from a distance to be a heap of white clay. Formerly in Ayodhyā was heard on all sides a great, confused noise of men and women; I do not hear it today. Indeed, gardens, which looked bright with men running helter-skelter on all sides, having ceased sporting in the morning after entering them at dusk and sporting the whole night, appear to me quite different. Deserted by gallants, they are weeping, as it were, today. (20—23)

verses.text:
अरण्यभूतेव पुरी सारथे प्रतिभाति माम्।
नह्यत्र यानैर्दृश्यन्ते न गजैर्न च वाजिभिः।
निर्यान्तो वाभियान्तो वा नरमुख्या यथा पुरा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The city, O charioteer, appears to me as converted into a woodland; for high-class men are not seen going out or coming here in conveyances or on the back of elephants or horses as before. (24)

verses.text:
उद्यानानि पुरा भान्ति मत्तप्रमुदितानि च।
जनानां रतिसंयोगेष्वत्यन्तगुणवन्ति च॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The gardens in this city formerly looked excited with joy and enraptured and were extremely favourable for lovecontacts of men. (25)

verses.text:
तान्येतान्यद्य पश्यामि निरानन्दानि सर्वशः।
स्रस्तपर्णैरनुपथं विक्रोशद्भिरिव द्रुमैः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Today I find those very gardens bereft of joy in everyway with their trees shedding tears in the form of leaves on the alleys and piteously wailing, as it were. (26)

verses.text:
नाद्यापि श्रूयते शब्दो मत्तानां मृगपक्षिणाम्।
सरक्तां मधुरां वाणीं कलं व्याहरतां बहु॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Not even at this hour of sunrise is heard the cry of deer and birds in rut profusely and inarticulately giving forth their sweet and impassioned utterances. (27)

verses.text:
चन्दनागुरुसम्पृक्तो धूपसम्मूर्च्छितोऽमलः।
प्रवाति पवनः श्रीमान् किं नु नाद्य यथा पुरा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “I wonder how a pure and delightful breeze laden with the fragrance of sandalwood and aloe and scented with the fume of burnt incense does not blow today as before. (28)

verses.text:
भेरीमृदङ्गवीणानां कोणसंघट्टितः पुनः।
किमद्य शब्दो विरतः सदादीनगतिः पुरा॥ २९॥
verses.m: “It is not known how has the sound, which ever proceeded unstintedly in the past, of kettledrums, clay tomtoms and Vīṇās, played upon with a drum-stick, palms or fingers, has ceased today? (29)

verses.text:
अनिष्टानि च पापानि पश्यामि विविधानि च।
निमित्तान्यमनोज्ञानि तेन सीदति मे मनः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “I also perceive unwelcome, portentous and unpleasant omens of every description. My mind is feeling dejected on that score. (30)

verses.text:
सर्वथा कुशलं सूत दुर्लभं मम बन्धुषु।
तथा ह्यसति सम्मोहे हृदयं सीदतीव मे॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The all-round welfare of my near and dear ones is difficult to find, O charioteer ! For, even when there is no ostensible cause for infatuation, my heart is sinking, as it were.” (31)

verses.text:
विषण्णः श्रान्तहृदयस्त्रस्तः संलुलितेन्द्रियः।
भरतः प्रविवेशाशु पुरीमिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Dejected and alarmed, his heart weary and senses extremely perturbed, Bharata speedily entered the city protected by the scions of Ikṣwāku. (32)

verses.text:
द्वारेण वैजयन्तेन प्राविशच्छ्रान्तवाहनः।
द्वाःस्थैरुत्थाय विजयमुक्तस्तैः सहितो ययौ॥ ३३॥
verses.m: His horses being fatigued, he effected his entry by the western gate known by the name of Vaijayanta. Greeted with shouts of triumph by the porters, who rose to usher him in, he moved on accompanied by them. (33)

verses.text:
स त्वनेकाग्रहृदयो द्वाःस्थं प्रत्यर्च्य तं जनम्।
सूतमश्वपतेः क्लान्तमब्रवीत् तत्र राघवः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Sending the porters back with honour, the said Bharata (a scion of Raghu) for his part, troubled as he was at heart, spoke on the spot to the wearied charioteer of King Aśwapati as follows : (34)

verses.text:
किमहं त्वरयाऽऽनीतः कारणेन विनानघ।
अशुभाशङ्कि हृदयं शीलं च पततीव मे॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Why have I been brought to Ayodhyā in a hurry without mentioning any cause, O sinless one? My heart is, therefore, apprehensive of some misfortune and my composure is vanishing, as it were. (35)

verses.text:
श्रुता नु यादृशाः पूर्वं नृपतीनां विनाशने।
आकारांस्तानहं सर्वानिह पश्यामि सारथे॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “I observe at this moment, O charioteer, all those indications that have been heard of by me in the past as pointing to the demise of kings. (36)

verses.text:
सम्मार्जनविहीनानि परुषाण्युपलक्षये।
असंयतकवाटानि श्रीविहीनानि सर्वशः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “I behold the dwellings of householders unswept, dirty-coloured, shorn of splendour in everyway and with open doors. (37)

verses.text:
बलिकर्मविहीनानि धूपसम्मोदनेन च।
अनाशितकुटुम्बानि प्रभाहीनजनानि च॥ ३८॥
अलक्ष्मीकानि पश्यामि कुटुम्बिभवनान्यहम्।
अपेतमाल्यशोभानि असम्मृष्टाजिराणि च॥ ३९॥
देवागाराणि शून्यानि न भान्तीह यथा पुरा।
देवतार्चाः प्रविद्धाश्च यज्ञगोष्ठास्तथैव च॥ ४०॥
माल्यापणेषु राजन्ते नाद्य पण्यानि वा तथा।
दृश्यन्ते वणिजोऽप्यद्य न यथापूर्वमत्र वै॥ ४१॥
ध्यानसंविग्नहृदया नष्टव्यापारयन्त्रिताः।
देवायतनचैत्येषु दीनाः पक्षिमृगास्तथा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I find that no oblations have been offered in them to the various creatures, that they are devoid of odour coming from the burning of incense and bereft of fortune, that members of the household have not been fed in them for many days past and their inmates look pale. Temples which are no longer adorned with garlands hanging on the gates, whose courtyards have not been swept for the last so many days and which are devoid of men, do not look charming now as before. Images of gods as well as sacrificial halls have been deserted; saleable goods such as flowers and garlands do not figure prominently as before in flower marts today. Merchants too in this city, whose hearts are seized with fear due to anxiety and who feel dispirited because of their business having been brought to a standstill, do not appear as happy as they looked before. Nay, birds and beasts in temples and other places of worship are distressed. (38—42)

verses.text:
मलिनं चाश्रुपूर्णाक्षं दीनं ध्यानपरं कृशम्।
सस्त्रीपुंसं च पश्यामि जनमुत्कण्ठितं पुरे॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Again, I behold the people in the city, including men and women, in soiled attire, miserable, worried, emaciated and sorrowful, with eyes full of tears.” (43)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतः सूतं तं दीनमानसः।
तान्यनिष्टान्ययोध्यायां प्रेक्ष्य राजगृहं ययौ॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Perceiving those unwelcome indications in Ayodhyā and having spoken to the said charioteer as above, Bharata drove to the royal palace afflicted in mind. (44)

verses.text:
तां शून्यशृङ्गाटकवेश्मरथ्यां
रजोरुणद्वारकवाटयन्त्राम्।
दृष्ट्वा पुरीमिन्द्रपुरीप्रकाशां
दुःखेन सम्पूर्णतरो बभूव॥ ४५॥
verses.m: He was filled to the brim with sorrow to see that city, which had shone at one time like Amarāvatī, the capital of Indra in paradise, with its crossroads, houses and streets desolate and its doors and bolts soiled with dust. (45)

verses.text:
बभूव पश्यन् मनसोऽप्रियाणि
यान्यन्यदा नास्य पुरे बभूवुः।
अवाक्शिरा दीनमना न हृष्टः
पितुर्महात्मा प्रविवेश वेश्म॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Beholding things distasteful to the mind, things which had never come to pass in his city before, the high-souled Bharata became cheerless and entered his father’s apartments distressed in mind, his head hung down. (46)

verses.text:
अपश्यंस्तु ततस्तत्र पितरं पितुरालये।
जगाम भरतो द्रष्टुं मातरं मातुरालये॥ १॥
verses.m: Not finding his father in the latter’s apartments in the palace, Bharata for his part then proceeded to see his mother in her apartments. (1)

verses.text:
अनुप्राप्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा कैकेयी प्रोषितं सुतम्।
उत्पपात तदा हृष्टा त्यक्त्वा सौवर्णमासनम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to see her aforesaid son, who had long been absent from home, returned, Kaikeyī for her part sprang on her feet at once, quitting her seat of gold. (2)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्यैव धर्मात्मा स्वगृहं श्रीविवर्जितम्।
भरतः प्रेक्ष्य जग्राह जनन्याश्चरणौ शुभौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: Immediately on entering his mother’s apartments and observing them completely shorn of splendour, the celebrated Bharata, whose mind was given to piety, clasped his mother’s lovable feet. (3)

verses.text:
तं मूर्ध्नि समुपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनम्।
अङ्के भरतमारोप्य प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ ४॥
verses.m: Duly smelling his head as a token of motherly affection and embracing the illustrious Bharata and seating him on her lap, she coolly proceeded to question him as follows : (4)

verses.text:
अद्य ते कतिचिद् रात्र्यश्च्युतस्यार्यकवेश्मनः।
अपि नाध्वश्रमः शीघ्रं रथेनापततस्तव॥ ५॥
verses.m: “How many nights have elapsed today since you departed from your maternal grandfather’s abode and was not fatigue experienced by you in the course of the long and tedious journey while you rode fast in your chariot? (5)

verses.text:
आर्यकस्ते सुकुशली युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव।
प्रवासाच्च सुखं पुत्र सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हसि॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Is your maternal grandfather as well as your maternal uncle, Yudhājit, enjoying perfect health? And has everything been well with you ever since you left home, my son? You should tell me everything.” (6)

verses.text:
एवं पृष्टस्तु कैकेय्या प्रियं पार्थिवनन्दनः।
आचष्ट भरतः सर्वं मात्रे राजीवलोचनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Questioned thus in endearing terms by Kaikeyī, the lotus-eyed Prince Bharata, for his part, related to his mother everything concerning himself. (7)

verses.text:
अद्य मे सप्तमी रात्रिश्च्युतस्यार्यकवेश्मनः।
अम्बायाः कुशली तातो युधाजिन्मातुलश्च मे॥ ८॥
verses.m: He said “Today has elapsed the seventh night since I departed from the abode of my maternal grandfather. My maternal grandfather as well as my maternal uncle, Yudhājit, are enjoying good health. (8)

verses.text:
यन्मे धनं च रत्नं च ददौ राजा परंतपः।
परिश्रान्तं पथ्यभवत् ततोऽहं पूर्वमागतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The animals carrying the wealth (gold) and jewels that King Aśwapati (a tormentor of his enemies) gave to me, got fatigued on the way; hence I came away first. (9)

verses.text:
राजवाक्यहरैर्दूतैस्त्वर्यमाणोऽहमागतः।
यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि तदम्बा वक्तुमर्हति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Being urged by the messengers, carrying the royal message, to hurry up, I came away in advance. Be pleased, O mother, to tell me now what I intend to ask. (10)

verses.text:
शून्योऽयं शयनीयस्ते पर्यङ्को हेमभूषितः।
न चायमिक्ष्वाकुजनः प्रहृष्टः प्रतिभाति मे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “This couch of yours, fit for reposing on and plated with gold as it is, is unoccupied by the king, who used to grace it every now and then. These attendants of Daśaratha (a scion of Ikṣwāku) do not appear much delighted to me either. (11)

verses.text:
राजा भवति भूयिष्ठमिहाम्बाया निवेशने।
तमहं नाद्य पश्यामि द्रष्टुमिच्छन्निहागतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The king used mostly to be present here in your apartments. Though I have come here longing to see him, I do not see him today. (12)

verses.text:
पितुर्ग्रहीष्ये पादौ च तं ममाख्याहि पृच्छतः।
आहोस्विदम्बाज्येष्ठायाः कौसल्याया निवेशने॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall clasp the feet of my father: pray, tell me, even as I ask you, where he may be. Is he in the apartments of Kausalyā, the seniormost of my mothers?” (13)

verses.text:
तं प्रत्युवाच कैकेयी प्रियवद् घोरमप्रियम्।
अजानन्तं प्रजानन्ती राज्यलोभेन मोहिता॥ १४॥
verses.m: Infatuated by greed of sovereignty, Kaikeyī, who knew everything in detail, related to Bharata, who knew nothing about it, the whole event, which was so terrible and unpleasant, as though it were agreeable to hear : (14)

verses.text:
या गतिः सर्वभूतानां तां गतिं ते पिता गतः।
राजा महात्मा तेजस्वी यायजूकः सतां गतिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The high-souled and glorious king, your father, who was given to the performance of sacrifices and was the haven of the virtuous, has met the same fate as is the destined end of all created beings.” (15)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं धर्माभिजनवाञ्छुचिः।
पपात सहसा भूमौ पितृशोकबलार्दितः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid reply from the lips of Kaikeyī, the guileless Bharata, who came of a pious family, fell to the ground all at once, hard smitten with grief caused by the death of his father. (16)

verses.text:
हा हतोऽस्मीति कृपणां दीनां वाचमुदीरयन्।
निपपात महाबाहुर्बाहू विक्षिप्य वीर्यवान्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Uttering in piteous tones the plaintive words “Alas, I am ruined !” and striking his arms against the floor, the heroic Bharata, who possessed long arms, fell prostrate. (17)

verses.text:
ततः शोकेन संवीतः पितुर्मरणदुःखितः।
विललाप महातेजा भ्रान्ताकुलितचेतनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Overwhelmed with grief and distressed over the death of his father, Bharata, who was endowed with great glory, then lamented in the following words, his mind being confused and agitated through grief : (18)

verses.text:
एतत् सुरुचिरं भाति पितुर्मे शयनं पुरा।
शशिनेवामलं रात्रौ गगनं तोयदात्यये॥ १९॥
verses.m: “This couch of my father looked most charming before like a clear sky adorned with the moon on an autumnal night. (19)

verses.text:
तदिदं न विभात्यद्य विहीनं तेन धीमता।
व्योमेव शशिना हीनमप्शुष्क इव सागरः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Devoid of that sagacious king, however, the same couch does not shine brightly today any more than a moonless sky or a sea whose water has been dried up by the fire of universal dissolution.” (20)

verses.text:
बाष्पमुत्सृज्य कण्ठेन स्वात्मना परिपीडितः।
प्रच्छाद्य वदनं श्रीमद् वस्त्रेण जयतां वरः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Shedding tears with a sound expressive of anguish from his throat, and covering his charming face with a cloth, Bharata, the foremost of victorious men, who felt greatly troubled in his own mind, continued to wail. (21)

verses.text:
तमार्तं देवसंकाशं समीक्ष्य पतितं भुवि।
निकृत्तमिव सालस्य स्कन्धं परशुना वने॥ २२॥
माता मातङ्गसंकाशं चन्द्रार्कसदृशं सुतम्।
उत्थापयित्वा शोकार्तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Perceiving her aforesaid son, shining brightly like a god—who closely resembled the young of an elephant and vied with the moon and the sun in splendour and felt stricken with grief, fallen in a wretched plight on the ground like a bough of a sal severed with an axe in a forest—and lifting him, the mother Kaikeyī spoke to him as follows : (22-23)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे राजन्नत्र महायशः।
त्वद्विधा नहि शोचन्ति सन्तः सदसि सम्मताः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Get up, O king ! Rise, O highly illustrious one ! Wherefore are you lying down here on the ground? Virtuous souls like you, honoured in an assembly of men, do not grieve. (24)

verses.text:
दानयज्ञाधिकारा हि शीलश्रुतितपोनुगा।
बुद्धिस्ते बुद्धिसम्पन्न प्रभेवार्कस्य मन्दिरे॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Your mind, O prince richly endowed with intelligence—which is ever devoted to charity and sacrificial performances and which pursues right conduct—follows the injunctions of the Vedas, and is prone to austerities—is steady as the radiance of the sun is fixed in the orb of the sun.” (25)

verses.text:
स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं भूमौ परिविवृत्य च।
जननीं प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Weeping for a long time and rolling on the floor, Bharata, who was filled with many-sided grief, replied to his mother as follows : (26)

verses.text:
अभिषेक्ष्यति रामं तु राजा यज्ञं नु यक्ष्यते।
इत्यहं कृतसंकल्पो हृष्टो यात्रामयासिषम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Having arrived at the conclusion that the king will most probably install Śrī Rāma as Prince Regent or perform a sacrifice, I gladly undertook the journey to Ayodhyā. (27)

verses.text:
तदिदं ह्यन्यथाभूतं व्यवदीर्णं मनो मम।
पितरं यो न पश्यामि नित्यं प्रियहिते रतम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Indeed that calculation of mine has come to be incorrect, and my mind is torn with anguish in that I do not behold my father, who was ever intent on doing kind acts to me and devoted to my good. (28)

verses.text:
अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते।
धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Of what disease did the king die before I arrived, O mother? How fortunate are Śrī Rāma and all others, by whom father was cremated with their own hands ! (29)

verses.text:
न नूनं मां महाराजः प्राप्तं जानाति कीर्तिमान्।
उपजिघ्रेत् तु मां मूर्ध्नि तातः संनाम्य सत्वरम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Surely the illustrious Emperor does not know me to have come home. Otherwise, pressing me down, father would have quickly smelt my head as a token of affection. (30)

verses.text:
क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Where is that hand, agreeable to the touch, of my father—who did great things without much exertion—that would wipe me again and again when he found me soiled with dust. (31)

verses.text:
यो मे भ्राता पिता बन्धुर्यस्य दासोऽस्मि सम्मतः।
तस्य मां शीघ्रमाख्याहि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Pray, announce me soon to Śrī Rāma, who is unwearied in action, nay, who is my elder brother, father in the absence of the Emperor and friend, all in one, and whose beloved servant I am. (32)

verses.text:
पिता हि भवति ज्येष्ठो धर्ममार्यस्य जानतः।
तस्य पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि स हीदानीं गतिर्मम॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “To a worthy man knowing what is right, an elder brother is a virtual father. I shall, clasp his feet as a mark of respect since he is my support now. (33)

verses.text:
धर्मविद् धर्मशीलश्च महाभागो दृढव्रतः।
आर्ये किमब्रवीद् राजा पिता मे सत्यविक्रमः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “What did the king, my father, of firm resolve and unfailing prowess—who knew what is right, had a virtuous disposition and was highly fortunate—say to my elder brother at the last moment? (34)

verses.text:
पश्चिमं साधुसंदेशमिच्छामि श्रोतुमात्मनः।
इति पृष्टा यथातत्त्वं कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “I wish to hear his last kind message for me.” Questioned thus, Kaikeyī replied as follows, strictly in consonance with facts : (35)

verses.text:
रामेति राजा विलपन् हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च।
स महात्मा परं लोकं गतो मतिमतां वरः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “That high-souled monarch, the foremost among the wise, departed for the other world crying ‘O Rāma, O Sītā, O Lakṣmaṇa !’ (36)

verses.text:
इतीमां पश्चिमां वाचं व्याजहार पिता तव।
कालधर्मं परिक्षिप्तः पाशैरिव महागजः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Bound by the laws of Time (according to which a living being meets his end at the appointed time), like a huge elephant bound with ropes, your father uttered the following parting words : (37)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्थास्तु नरा राममागतं सह सीतया।
लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: ‘Only those men who are able to behold Rāma returned with Sītā, as also the mighty-armed Lakṣmaṇa come back to Ayodhyā, will have their object accomplished.’ (38)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विषसादैव द्वितीयाप्रियशंसनात्।
विषण्णवदनो भूत्वा भूयः पप्रच्छ मातरम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid report, the prince grew melancholy at that other unpleasant tidings and, assuming a dejected look, further questioned his mother as follows : (39)

verses.text:
क्व चेदानीं स धर्मात्मा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया च समागतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Where is Śrī Rāma, whose mind is given to virtue and who enhances the joy of Kausalyā, now, conjoined with brother Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā?” (40)

verses.text:
तथा पृष्टा यथान्यायमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे।
मातास्य युगपद्वाक्यं विप्रियं प्रियशंसया॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Questioned as aforesaid, his mother began duly to relate as follows the unpleasant event, simultaneously with the news of his father’s demise in the tone of breaking a welcome news : (41)

verses.text:
स हि राजसुतः पुत्र चीरवासा महावनम्।
दण्डकान् सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणानुचरो गतः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Actually, clad in the bark of trees, my son, and followed by Lakṣmaṇa, the aforesaid prince proceeded to the great forest of Daṇḍaka with Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory.” (42)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्त्रस्तो भ्रातुश्चारित्रशङ्कया।
स्वस्य वंशस्य माहात्म्यात् प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Filled with apprehension to hear the tidings because of his misgivings about the character of his elder brother, Śrī Rāma, and remembering as he did the greatness of his royal house, Bharata commenced interrogating her as follows : (43)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न ब्राह्मणधनं हृतं रामेण कस्यचित्।
कच्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “I hope no property of a Brāhmaṇa was wantonly seized by Śrī Rāma. I am sure, no sinless man, whether wealthy or destitute, was killed by him. (44)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न परदारान् वा राजपुत्रोऽभिमन्यते।
कस्मात् स दण्डकारण्ये भ्राता रामो विवासितः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Nor did the prince long for another’s wife, I am sure. If not, wherefore was my celebrated brother sent into exile to the Daṇḍaka forest?” (45)

verses.text:
अथास्य चपला माता तत् स्वकर्म यथातथम्।
तेनैव स्त्रीस्वभावेन व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Prompted by her feminine (frivolous) nature, which was too well-known, Bharata’s capricious mother forthwith began to recount her notorious doing precisely as matters stood. (46)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी भरतेन महात्मना।
उवाच वचनं हृष्टा वृथापण्डितमानिनी॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Questioned as aforesaid by the high-souled Bharata, Kaikeyī, for her part, who vainly accounted her wise, merrily replied as follows : (47)

verses.text:
न ब्राह्मणधनं किंचिद्धृतं रामेण कस्यचित्।
कश्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः।
न रामः परदारान् स चक्षुर्भ्यामपि पश्यति॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “No property whatsoever of a Brāhmaṇa or anyone else was wantonly seized by Rāma, nor was any innocent man, wealthy or destitute, killed by him. Nor did the celebrated Rāma look on another’s wife even with sinless eyes. (48)

verses.text:
मया तु पुत्र श्रुत्वैव रामस्येहाभिषेचनम्।
याचितस्ते पिता राज्यं रामस्य च विवासनम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “The moment I heard of Rāma’s installation as Prince Regent on the throne of Ayodhyā, my son, your father was in fact asked by me for the sovereignty of Ayodhyā in your favour and the banishment of Rāma. (49)

verses.text:
स स्ववृत्तिं समास्थाय पिता ते तत् तथाकरोत्।
रामस्तु सहसौमित्रिः प्रेषितः सह सीतया॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Following his own truthful nature, your father thereupon did as he was asked by me. Accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma was accordingly sent into exile alongwith Sītā. (50)

verses.text:
तमपश्यन् प्रियं पुत्रं महीपालो महायशाः।
पुत्रशोकपरिद्यूनः पञ्चत्वमुपपेदिवान्॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Missing his beloved son, Rāma, and stricken with grief over his separation from that son, the highly illustrious Emperor met his end. (51)

verses.text:
त्वया त्विदानीं धर्मज्ञ राजत्वमवलम्ब्यताम्।
त्वत्कृते हि मया सर्वमिदमेवंविधं कृतम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Let the throne of Ayodhyā be accepted by you now, O knower of what is right ! Indeed, all this has been manipulated by me in this wise for your sake. (52)

verses.text:
मा शोकं मा च संतापं धैर्यमाश्रय पुत्रक।
त्वदधीना हि नगरी राज्यं चैतदनामयम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Do not yield to grief nor to remorse, my dear son, but have recourse to firmness. Indeed, the existence of the city of Ayodhyā as well as this kingdom, which is free from trouble, is dependent on you. (53)

verses.text:
तत् पुत्र शीघ्रं विधिना विधिज्ञै-
र्वसिष्ठमुख्यैः सहितो द्विजेन्द्रैः।
संकाल्य राजानमदीनसत्त्व-
मात्मानमुर्व्यामभिषेचयस्व ॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, speedily performing with due ceremony the funeral rites with respect to the king (your deceased father) with the help of the foremost of Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the scriptural ordinance, get yourself installed, my son, as the ruler of the entire globe, undepressed in spirits.” (54)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा च स पितुर्वृत्तं भ्रातरौ च विवासितौ।
भरतो दुःखसंतप्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Sore stricken with sorrow to hear the unwelcome news about his father, as well as of his brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, having been sent into exile, Bharata replied as follows : (1)

verses.text:
किं नु कार्यं हतस्येह मम राज्येन शोचतः।
विहीनस्याथ पित्रा च भ्रात्रा पितृसमेन च॥ २॥
verses.m: “What object on earth will possibly be gained through sovereignty by me, a wretched being, deprived of his father and elder brother—who was as good as a father—and, therefore, grieving? (2)

verses.text:
दुःखे मे दुःखमकरोर्व्रणे क्षारमिवाददाः।
राजानं प्रेतभावस्थं कृत्वा रामं च तापसम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Reducing the king to the state of a departed soul and turning Śrī Rāma an ascetic on top of it, you have brought calamity after calamity to me—rubbed salt, as it were, into my wound. (3)

verses.text:
कुलस्य त्वमभावाय कालरात्रिरिवागता।
अङ्गारमुपगूह्य स्म पिता मे नावबुद्धवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Like the night of universal dissolution (or Goddess Kālarātri, one of the nine Durgās or manifestations of the Divine Energy associated with the dissolution of the universe), you made your appearance in my father’s house for the extermination of my race ! Even on clasping a live coal to his bosom, my father did not recognize it as such. (4)

verses.text:
मृत्युमापादितो राजा त्वया मे पापदर्शिनि।
सुखं परिहृतं मोहात् कुलेऽस्मिन् कुलपांसनि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The king, my father, has been consigned to death by you, O woman, who perceive evil even where there is none and have brought disgrace to your family ! Through infatuation the joy of this family has been taken away by you. (5)

verses.text:
त्वां प्राप्य हि पिता मेऽद्य सत्यसंधो महायशाः।
तीव्रदुःखाभिसंतप्तो वृत्तो दशरथो नृपः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Indeed, having got you for his wife, my highly illustrious father, King Daśaratha, who was true to his promise and was sore stricken with acute agony, born of separation from his eldest son, has passed away. (6)

verses.text:
विनाशितो महाराजः पिता मे धर्मवत्सलः।
कस्मात् प्रव्राजितो रामः कस्मादेव वनं गतः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Wherefore was the Emperor, my father, who was so lovingly devoted to duty, deprived of his life by you? For what precise reason was Śrī Rāma sent into exile and he proceeded to the forest? (7)

verses.text:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिते।
दुष्करं यदि जीवेतां प्राप्य त्वां जननीं मम॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Having got you, my mother for their co-wife, Kausalyā and Sumitrā too have been tormented with grief caused by separation from their own son. They would indeed accomplish something hard if they survive any longer. (8)

verses.text:
नन्वार्योऽपि च धर्मात्मा त्वयि वृत्तिमनुत्तमाम्।
वर्तते गुरुवृत्तिज्ञो यथा मातरि वर्तते॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Surely, my elder brother, Śrī Rāma, too, whose mind is given to piety and who knows full well how to serve his elders, rendered the best services to you as he did to his own mother ! (9)

verses.text:
तथा ज्येष्ठा हि मे माता कौसल्या दीर्घदर्शिनी।
त्वयि धर्मं समास्थाय भगिन्यामिव वर्तते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Even so, my seniormost mother, Kausalyā, who takes a long-range view of things, behaved towards you as towards her own sister, following, as she does, the principles of right conduct. (10)

verses.text:
तस्याः पुत्रं महात्मानं चीरवल्कलवाससम्।
प्रस्थाप्य वनवासाय कथं पापे न शोचसे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having sent her high-souled son, clad in tatters and the bark of trees, into exile in a forest, wherefore do you not grieve, O sinful woman? (11)

verses.text:
अपापदर्शिनं शूरं कृतात्मानं यशस्विनम्।
प्रव्राज्य चीरवसनं किं नु पश्यसि कारणम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Having sent into exile, clad in the bark of trees, the illustrious hero, who never detected others’ sin and had mastered his self, what gain on earth do you expect? (12)

verses.text:
लुब्धाया विदितो मन्ये न तेऽहं राघवं यथा।
तथा ह्यनर्थो राज्यार्थं त्वयाऽऽनीतो महानयम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “To you, who are full of greed for power and pelf, I am not known, I believe, in my reality as to how devoted I am to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). That is why this great tragedy has been enacted by you for the sake of sovereignty. (13)

verses.text:
अहं हि पुरुषव्याघ्रावपश्यन् रामलक्ष्मणौ।
केन शक्तिप्रभावेण राज्यं रक्षितुमुत्सहे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Failing to perceive the two tigers among men, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, by virtue of what strength can I venture to protect the kingdom of Ayodhyā? (14)

verses.text:
तं हि नित्यं महाराजो बलवन्तं महौजसम्।
उपाश्रितोऽभूद् धर्मात्मा मेरुर्मेरुवनं यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Even the Emperor, whose mind was given to piety, ever depended on the might of the powerful Śrī Rāma—who is possessed of extraordinary strength—just as Mount Meru depends for its protection against inroads on the forest grown on it. (15)

verses.text:
सोऽहं कथमिमं भारं महाधुर्यसमुद्यतम्।
दम्यो धुरमिवासाद्य सहेयं केन चौजसा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How and with what stamina shall I, whose only strength is Śrī Rāma, sustain this burden of kingship any more than a calf would stand the strain on getting a load, borne with ease by a giant bull? (16)

verses.text:
अथवा मे भवेच्छक्तिर्योगैर्बुद्धिबलेन वा।
सकामां न करिष्यामि त्वामहं पुत्रगर्द्धिनीम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Or, even if such capacity could be brought out in me through contrivances or through intellectual calibre, I shall never allow you to attain your desired end—you, who covet sovereignty for your son, i.e., myself. (17)

verses.text:
न मे विकांक्षा जायेत त्यक्तुं त्वां पापनिश्चयाम्।
यदि रामस्य नावेक्षा त्वयि स्यान्मातृवत् सदा॥ १८॥
verses.m: “No disinclination would be felt by me even in deserting you, a woman of sinful resolve, if Śrī Rāma did not regard you as a mother at all times. (18)

verses.text:
उत्पन्ना तु कथं बुद्धिस्तवेयं पापदर्शिनी।
साधुचारित्रविभ्रष्टे पूर्वेषां नो विगर्हिता॥ १९॥
verses.m: “How did this idea of securing the kingdom for a younger brother in supersession of the eldest—an idea which contemplates evil in relation to others and which has been severely condemned by our forbears—enter your mind at all, O woman fallen from virtuous conduct? (19)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् कुले हि सर्वेषां ज्येष्ठो राज्येऽभिषिच्यते।
अपरे भ्रातरस्तस्मिन् प्रवर्तन्ते समाहिताः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Indeed in our house the eldest* of all brothers is installed on the throne. The other brothers devoutly obey him. (20)

verses.text:
न हि मन्ये नृशंसे त्वं राजधर्ममवेक्षसे।
गतिं वा न विजानासि राजवृत्तस्य शाश्वतीम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I believe you do not at all respect the moral code prescribed for kings, nor do you know the eternal way of life of kings, O cruel woman ! (21)

verses.text:
सततं राजपुत्रेषु ज्येष्ठो राजाभिषिच्यते।
राज्ञामेतत् समं तत् स्यादिक्ष्वाकूणां विशेषतः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Among the sons of a king the eldest alone is invariably crowned king. This is a common practice among all kings, and it is particularly true of the Ikṣwākus. (22)

verses.text:
तेषां धर्मैकरक्षाणां कुलचारित्रशोभिनाम्।
अद्य चारित्रशौटीर्यं त्वां प्राप्य विनिवर्तितम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The self-esteem, born of loftiness of character, cherished by the aforesaid kings—who were protected by their righteousness alone and who shone by virtue of a mode of life befitting their race—has disappeared today on coming to be associated with you. (23)

verses.text:
तवापि सुमहाभागे जनेन्द्रकुलपूर्वके।
बुद्धिमोहः कथमयं सम्भूतस्त्वयि गर्हितः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “How has this perversity of reason, contemptible for you, appeared in you too, O exceptionally blessed lady, born of a royal lineage ! (24)

verses.text:
न तु कामं करिष्यामि तवाहं पापनिश्चये।
यया व्यसनमारब्धं जीवितान्तकरं मम॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I will not in any case accomplish your desired object, O woman of sinful resolve, since a calamity which may eventually prove fatal to me, has been set on foot by you. (25)

verses.text:
एष त्विदानीमेवाहमप्रियार्थं तवानघम्।
निवर्तयिष्यामि वनाद् भ्रातरं स्वजनप्रियम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “In order to give offence to you, I shall, however, forthwith cause to return from the forest my sinless elder brother, Śrī Rāma, the beloved of his people. (26)

verses.text:
निवर्तयित्वा रामं च तस्याहं दीप्ततेजसः।
दासभूतो भविष्यामि सुस्थितेनान्तरात्मना॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Nay, having caused Śrī Rāma to return from the forest, I shall settle down in life with a composed mind, turning a servant of the aforesaid prince of effulgent glory.” (27)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतो महात्मा
प्रियेतरैर्वाक्यगणैस्तुदंस्ताम्।
शोकार्दितश्चापि ननाद भूयः
सिंहो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid to his mother, pricking her once more with volleys of piercing words, the high-souled Bharata, even though tormented with grief, roared like a lion ensconced in a cave of Mount Mandara. (28)

verses.text:
तां तथा गर्हयित्वा तु मातरं भरतस्तदा।
रोषेण महताविष्टः पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having reproached his mother, Kaikeyī, as aforesaid, on that occasion, Bharata, for his part, who was filled with violent anger, spoke once more as follows : (1)

verses.text:
राज्याद् भ्रंशस्व कैकेयि नृशंसे दुष्टचारिणि।
परित्यक्तासि धर्मेण मा मृतं रुदती भव॥ २॥
verses.m: “Be deprived of sovereignty, O cruel Kaikeyī of vicious conduct! Since you have been forsaken by virtue, keep wailing for life, taking me to be dead (since the course you have adopted is bound to prove fatal to me). (2)

verses.text:
किं नु तेऽदूषयद् रामो राजा वा भृशधार्मिकः।
ययोर्मृत्युर्विवासश्च त्वत्कृते तुल्यमागतौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: “What interest of yours, I wonder, did Śrī Rāma or the exceedingly pious king mar, whose banishment and death (severally) came about at one and the same time because of you? (3)

verses.text:
भ्रूणहत्यामसि प्राप्ता कुलस्यास्य विनाशनात्।
कैकेयि नरकं गच्छ मा च तातसलोकताम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “By having brought destruction to this family you have incurred the sin of having killed a Brāhmaṇa studying the Veda. Proceed you, therefore, to hell after death, O Kaikeyī, and not to heaven in common with my father (your husband, the virtuous King Daśaratha). (4)

verses.text:
यत्त्वया हीदृशं पापं कृतं घोरेण कर्मणा।
सर्वलोकप्रियं हित्वा ममाप्यापादितं भयम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Since such a gross sin has been incurred by you through a terrible act in the form of taking the life of a pious husband and sending into exile a loving and virtuous son, peril of being disowned by my loving brother has been brought by you to me as well by banishing a prince, who is the beloved of all people. (5)

verses.text:
त्वत्कृते मे पिता वृत्तो रामश्चारण्यमाश्रितः।
अयशो जीवलोके च त्वयाहं प्रतिपादितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Because of you my father has joined the majority, while Śrī Rāma has taken up his abode in the forest, and I too have been subjected to ignominy in the world of mortals by you. (6)

verses.text:
मातृरूपे ममामित्रे नृशंसे राज्यकामुके।
न तेऽहमभिभाष्योऽस्मि दुर्वृत्ते पतिघातिनि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I ought not to be spoken to by you, O cruel woman of evil conduct and covetous of sovereignty, who have killed your own husband and are my enemy in the guise of a mother ! (7)

verses.text:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या मम मातरः।
दुःखेन महताविष्टास्त्वां प्राप्य कुलदूषिणीम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Having got you, the disgrace of your family, for a co-wife, Kausalyā and Sumitrā and my other mothers too have been filled with great agony. (8)

verses.text:
न त्वमश्वपतेः कन्या धर्मराजस्य धीमतः।
राक्षसी तत्र जातासि कुलप्रध्वंसिनी पितुः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Surely you are not the daughter of the virtuous and wise King Aśwapati, but an ogress sprung from his loins, who has brought complete ruin to my father’s race. (9)

verses.text:
यत् त्वया धार्मिको रामो नित्यं सत्यपरायणः।
वनं प्रस्थापितो वीरः पितापि त्रिदिवं गतः॥ १०॥
यत् प्रधानासि तत् पापं मयि पित्रा विना कृते।
भ्रातृभ्यां च परित्यक्ते सर्वलोकस्य चाप्रिये॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Since the virtuous hero, Śrī Rāma, who is ever devoted to truth, has been sent into exile to the forest by you and my father too has departed for heaven because of you, the sin that has been chiefly incurred by you thereby has been visited on me, who have consequently been deprived of my father, nay, abandoned by my brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and have become unpopular with the whole world. (10-11)

verses.text:
कौसल्यां धर्मसंयुक्तां वियुक्तां पापनिश्चये।
कृत्वा कं प्राप्स्यसे ह्यद्य लोकं निरयगामिनि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Indeed, having rendered Kausalyā, who is wedded to piety, desolate (by depriving her of her husband and only son), O woman of sinful resolve and doomed to perdition, what realm other than the infernal regions will you attain now after death? (12)

verses.text:
किं नावबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतं बन्धुसंश्रयम्।
ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं रामं कौसल्यायात्मसम्भवम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Did you not cognize Śrī Rāma, born of Kausalyā’s own womb, to be my eldest brother and, therefore, as good as my father, self-controlled and the asylum of his kinsfolk, O cruel woman? (13)

verses.text:
अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गजः पुत्रो हृदयाच्चाभिजायते।
तस्मात् प्रियतरो मातुः प्रिया एव तु बान्धवाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “A son takes his shape from the essence of the various primary and secondary limbs of his father (in the form of his generative fluid) and the heart of his mother (which is the fount of her ovum). Hence he is dearer than all others to his mother, whereas her other relations are simply dear to her. (14)

verses.text:
अन्यदा किल धर्मज्ञा सुरभिः सुरसम्मता।
वहमानौ ददर्शोर्व्यां पुत्रौ विगतचेतसौ॥ १५॥
verses.m: “On one occasion in the hoary past, so the tradition goes, Surabhi, the cow of plenty, who knows what is right and is adored by gods, saw a pair of bullocks (her own sons) fallen unconscious on the ground while drawing the plough. (15)

verses.text:
तावर्धदिवसं श्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रौ महीतले।
रुरोद पुत्रशोकेन बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Seeing her two sons lying on the ground exhausted due to their having toiled hard for half the day, Surabhi wept with grief born of anxiety for her sons, her eyes blinded with tears. (16)

verses.text:
अधस्ताद् व्रजतस्तस्याः सुरराज्ञो महात्मनः।
बिन्दवः पतिता गात्रे सूक्ष्माः सुरभिगन्धिनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Her sweet-scented tear-drops fell on the person of the high-souled Indra, the ruler of gods, who happened to pass below. (17)

verses.text:
निरीक्षमाणस्तां शक्रो ददर्श सुरभिं स्थिताम्।
आकाशे विष्ठितां दीनां रुदतीं भृशदुःखिताम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Looking upwards Indra beheld the said Surabhi standing, weeping in the heavens in a miserable plight, sore afflicted. (18)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा शोकसंतप्तां वज्रपाणिर्यशस्विनीम्।
इन्द्रः प्राञ्जलिरुद्विग्नः सुरराजोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Perturbed to find the illustrious cow agonized through grief, Indra, the ruler of gods, who carried a thunderbolt in one of his hands, spoke with folded hands as follows: (19)

verses.text:
भयं कच्चिन्न चास्मासु कुतश्चिद् विद्यते महत्।
कुतोनिमित्तः शोकस्ते ब्रूहि सर्वहितैषिणि॥ २०॥
verses.m: ‘I hope there is no grave danger to us (heavenly beings) from any quarter whatsoever. Now tell me, O well-wisher of all, what is the occasion for your grief?’ (20)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु सुरभिः सुरराजेन धीमता।
प्रत्युवाच ततो धीरा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदा॥ २१॥
verses.m: Addressed in the aforesaid words by the wise Indra, the ruler of gods, the intelligent Surabhi for her part, who was adept in speaking, forthwith replied in the following words : (21)

verses.text:
शान्तं पापं न वः किंचित् कुतश्चिदमराधिप।
अहं तु मग्नौ शोचामि स्व पुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ॥ २२॥
एतौ दृष्ट्वा कृशौ दीनौ सूर्यरश्मिप्रतापितौ।
वध्यमानौ बलीवर्दौ कर्षकेण दुरात्मना॥ २३॥
verses.m: ‘Heaven forbid ! There is no danger whatsoever to you from any quarter, O ruler of immortals ! I, however, grieve to see plunged in adversity a pair of bullocks, my own progeny, emaciated and miserable, scorched by the sun’s rays and, on top of it, being beaten by an evil-minded farmer. (22-23)

verses.text:
मम कायात् प्रसूतौ हि दुःखितौ भारपीडितौ।
यौ दृष्ट्वा परितप्येऽहं नास्ति पुत्रसमः प्रियः॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘I feel sore distressed to find the two bullocks, who are sprung from my own womb, afflicted and oppressed with a heavy load; for there is none so dear to a mother as a son.’ (24)

verses.text:
यस्याः पुत्रसहस्रैस्तु कृत्स्नं व्याप्तमिदं जगत्।
तां दृष्ट्वा रुदतीं शक्रो न सुतान् मन्यते परम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Seeing Surabhi—by whose countless offsprings (in the shape of the bovine race) the whole creation is filled—weeping, Indra reckoned none as dearer to a mother than a son. (25)

verses.text:
इन्द्रो ह्यश्रुनिपातं तं स्वगात्रे पुण्यगन्धिनम्।
सुरभिं मन्यते दृष्ट्वा भूयसीं तामिहेश्वरः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Perceiving that dropping of tears, which emitted a sweet odour, from the eyes of Surabhi on his own person, the powerful Indra recognized the said Surabhi to be the greatest of all in this world. (26)

verses.text:
समाप्रतिमवृत्ताया लोकधारणकाम्यया।
श्रीमत्या गुणमुख्यायाः स्वभावपरिचेष्टया॥ २७॥
यस्याः पुत्रसहस्राणि सापि शोचति कामधुक्।
किं पुनर्या विना रामं कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति॥ २८॥
verses.m: “When even the celebrated cow of plenty—whose conduct in the world is uniformly beneficent to all and is without parallel in this respect, actuated as she is by the desire to sustain the world, nay, who is rich in the power to grant the desire of all, whosoever approaches her, and is foremost in her virtue of truthfulness etc., and who is blessed with numberless offsprings—grieves for them as an outward expression of her natural love for her progeny, how much more will Kausalyā, who will have to drag her existence without Śrī Rāma, her only son? (27-28)

verses.text:
एकपुत्रा च साध्वी च विवत्सेयं त्वया कृता।
तस्मात् त्वं सततं दुःखं प्रेत्य चेह च लप्स्यसे॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Kausalyā, who is blessed with one son only and is a virtuous lady to boot, has been deprived of her son by you. Hence you will incessantly undergo suffering here as well as after death. (29)

verses.text:
अहं त्वपचितिं भ्रातुः पितुश्च सकलामिमाम्।
वर्धनं यशसश्चापि करिष्यामि न संशयः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “I for my part shall offer worship as follows in the form of bringing him back from the forest and restoring his patrimony to him, my elder brother, Śrī Rāma, and entire worship in the form of all obsequial rites to my father and also enhance their reputation : there is no doubt about it. (30)

verses.text:
आनाय्य च महाबाहुं कोसलेन्द्रं महाबलम्।
स्वयमेव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनं मुनिनिषेवितम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having caused Śrī Rāma (the ruler of the kingdom of Kosala)—who is distinguished by long arms and is possessed of great might—to return to Ayodhyā, I shall myself retire in his place to the forest frequented by hermits and thus save him from the sin of having violated his vow. (31)

verses.text:
नह्यहं पापसंकल्पे पापे पापं त्वया कृतम्।
शक्तो धारयितुं पौरैरश्रुकण्ठैर्निरीक्षितः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Looked on by the citizens with their throat full of tears, I shall surely not be able to brook the sin perpetrated by you in the shape of sending the eldest brother into exile and securing the kingdom in favour of a younger one, O wicked woman of sinful resolve ! (32)

verses.text:
सा त्वमग्निं प्रविश वा स्वयं वा विश दण्डकान्।
रज्जुं बद्ध्वाथवा कण्ठे नहि तेऽन्यत् परायणम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Having deliberately committed this sin, enter you the fire or retire yourself to the Daṇḍaka forest or again end your life by tying a cord round your neck and throttling yourself : there is no other course left for you. (33)

verses.text:
अहमप्यवनीं प्राप्ते रामे सत्यपराक्रमे।
कृतकृत्यो भविष्यामि विप्रवासितकल्मषः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “I too shall have washed my stain and accomplished my purpose only when Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess has returned to his native land.” (34)

verses.text:
इति नाग इवारण्ये तोमराङ्कुशतोदितः।
पपात भुवि संक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus and hissing, highly enraged, like a serpent, Bharata dropped unconscious to the ground like an elephant pricked with a javelin and a goad in a forest. (35)

verses.text:
संरक्तनेत्रः शिथिलाम्बरस्तथा
विधूतसर्वाभरणः परंतपः।
बभूव भूमौ पतितो नृपात्मजः
शचीपतेः केतुरिवोत्सवक्षये॥ ३६॥
verses.m: With deep red eyes, his garment loosened and all his jewels tossed about, the prince, Bharata, the tormentor of his foes, fell to the ground like a banner raised in honour of Indra and pulled down at the end of the festival. (36)

verses.text:
दीर्घकालात् समुत्थाय संज्ञां लब्ध्वा स वीर्यवान्।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां दीनामुद्वीक्ष्य मातरम्॥ १॥
सोऽमात्यमध्ये भरतो जननीमभ्यकुत्सयत्।
राज्यं न कामये जातु मन्त्रये नापि मातरम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Regaining his consciousness after a long time the said Bharata, who was full of valour, got up and, casting a glance at his mother, who looked miserable at the unexpected turn of events, with her eyes full of tears, reproached her right and left in the midst of the ministers (who had evidently collected there on coming to know of Bharata’s arrival) and said, “I never coveted the throne, nor did I ever hold any consultation with my mother. (1-2)

verses.text:
अभिषेकं न जानामि योऽभूद् राज्ञा समीक्षितः।
विप्रकृष्टे ह्यहं देशे शत्रुघ्नसहितोऽभवम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Nor did I know anything about the installation of Śrī Rāma as Prince Regent which was contemplated by the king; for, I happened to be at that time in a distant land with Śatrughna, my brother. (3)

verses.text:
वनवासं न जानामि रामस्याहं महात्मनः।
विवासनं च सौमित्रेः सीतायाश्च यथाभवत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Nor again was I aware of the residence in the forest of the high-souled Śrī Rāma, nor how the exile of Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) and Sītā came about.” (4)

verses.text:
तथैव क्रोशतस्तस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः।
कौसल्या शब्दमाज्ञाय सुमित्रां चेदमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Recognizing the voice of the celebrated Bharata of noble mind, who was lamenting as aforesaid, Kausalyā spoke to Sumitrā as follows : (5)

verses.text:
आगतः क्रूरकार्यायाः कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः।
तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भरतं दीर्घदर्शिनम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I think Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī of cruel deeds, has returned from his maternal grandfather’s. I long to see the aforesaid Bharata, who takes a long-range view of things.” (6)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा सुमित्रां तां विवर्णवदना कृशा।
प्रतस्थे भरतो यत्र वेपमाना विचेतना॥ ७॥
verses.m: Speaking as aforesaid to the said Sumitrā, the pale-faced and emaciated lady, who looked absent-minded, advanced trembling to the place where Bharata was. (7)

verses.text:
स तु राजात्मजश्चापि शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा।
प्रतस्थे भरतो येन कौसल्याया निवेशनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Nay, accompanied by Śatrughna, the said prince, Bharata, too, on the other side, proceeded that very moment along the route by which Kausalyā’s apartments could be reached. (8)

verses.text:
ततः शत्रुघ्नभरतौ कौसल्यां प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितौ।
पर्यष्वजेतां दुःखार्तां पतितां नष्टचेतनाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Perceiving Kausalyā, who was stricken with sorrow, and had fallen unconscious on the way, the two afflicted brothers, Śatrughna and Bharata, hugged her. (9)

verses.text:
रुदन्तौ रुदती दुःखात् समेत्यार्या मनस्विनी।
भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं कौसल्या भृशदुःखिता॥ १०॥
verses.m: Embracing in return the two brothers, who were weeping through agony, the noble and high-minded Kausalyā, who was sore distressed, addressed Bharata as follows : (10)

verses.text:
इदं ते राज्यकामस्य राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्।
सम्प्राप्तं बत कैकेय्या शीघ्रं क्रूरेण कर्मणा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Enjoy this kingdom, devoid of enemies, obtained by you, who coveted it. Alas, it has been promptly secured for you by Kaikeyī through a cruel deed in the shape of banishing Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. (11)

verses.text:
प्रस्थाप्य चीरवसनं पुत्रं मे वनवासिनम्।
कैकेयी कं गुणं तत्र पश्यति क्रूरदर्शिनी॥ १२॥
verses.m: “What good did the cruel-eyed Kaikeyī expect by sending into exile, as she did, my son, Rāma, as an ascetic clad in the bark of trees? (12)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं मामपि कैकेयी प्रस्थापयितुमर्हति।
हिरण्यनाभो यत्रास्ते सुतो मे सुमहायशाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Kaikeyī ought to send away soon me as well to the place where my exceptionally illustrious son with a golden navel (a distinguishing mark of Lord Viṣṇu) is sojourning. (13)

verses.text:
अथवा स्वयमेवाहं सुमित्रानुचरा सुखम्।
अग्निहोत्रं पुरस्कृत्य प्रस्थास्ये यत्र राघवः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Or, placing the sacrificial fire* (carried by a Brāhmaṇa) ahead and followed by Sumitrā, I shall myself depart happily along the route by which Rāma has proceeded to the forest. (14)

verses.text:
कामं वा स्वयमेवाद्य तत्र मां नेतुमर्हसि।
यत्रासौ पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तप्यते मे सुतस्तपः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Or, you ought personally to take me now freely to the place where my aforesaid son, a veritable tiger among men, is practising austerities. (15)

verses.text:
इदं हि तव विस्तीर्णं धनधान्यसमाचितम्।
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पूर्णं राज्यं निर्यातितं तया॥ १६॥
verses.m: “This extensive kingdom overflowing with riches and foodgrains and fully equipped with elephants, horses and chariots has actually been conferred on you by her, your mother.” (16)

verses.text:
इत्यादिबहुभिर्वाक्यैः क्रूरैः सम्भर्त्सितोऽनघः।
विव्यथे भरतोऽतीव व्रणे तुद्येव सूचिना॥ १७॥
verses.m: Bitterly reproached in many such cruel words, the sinless Bharata felt extremely pained as he would when pricked with a needle in the wound. (17)

verses.text:
पपात चरणौ तस्यास्तदा सम्भ्रान्तचेतनः।
विलप्य बहुधासंज्ञो लब्धसंज्ञस्तदाभवत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having lost his consciousness, his mind being utterly confused to hear the taunting words of Kausalyā, Bharata presently regained his senses and, wailing in many ways, then fell at her feet. (18)

verses.text:
एवं विलपमानां तां प्राञ्जलिर्भरतस्तदा।
कौसल्यां प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: To Kausalyā, overwhelmed with griefs of many kinds and lamenting as aforesaid, Bharata then replied with folded hands as follows : (19)

verses.text:
आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्।
विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Wherefore do you reproach me, O noble lady, guileless as I am and did not know anything about Śrī Rāma’s exile before I returned to Ayodhyā? Nay, you know my great love borne towards Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (20)

verses.text:
कृतशास्त्रानुगा बुद्धिर्मा भूत् तस्य कदाचन।
सत्यसंधः सतां श्रेष्ठो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let his judgment never follow (the teachings of) the scriptures as taught by his preceptor, with whose concurrence my elder brother, who is true to his promise and is the foremost of the virtuous, has gone into exile. (21)

verses.text:
प्रैष्यं पापीयसां यातु सूर्यं च प्रति मेहतु।
हन्तु पादेन गाः सुप्ता यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile suffer the lot of a servant of men belonging to the lowest stratum of society, incur the sin of answering the calls of nature facing the sun and reap the consequences of kicking cows lying asleep. (22)

verses.text:
कारयित्वा महत् कर्म भर्ता भृत्यमनर्थकम्।
अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile incur the sin that attaches to a master who robs his servant of his resources after getting him accomplish a great deed for him. (23)

verses.text:
परिपालयमानस्य राज्ञो भूतानि पुत्रवत्।
