ततस्तु द्रुह्यतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Let the sin attaching to those bearing enmity to a king protecting his subjects as his own offspring, be incurred by him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile. (24)

verses.text:
बलिषड्भागमुद्धृत्य नृपस्यारक्षितुः प्रजाः।
अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Let the sin that attaches to a king who fails to protect the people even after collecting the land revenue in the form of one-sixth of the produce be incurred by him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile. (25)

verses.text:
संश्रुत्य च तपस्विभ्यः सत्रे वै यज्ञदक्षिणाम्।
तां चापलपतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Let the sin attaching to those withholding payment of the sacrificial fee even after promising it to the priests practising austerities and officiating at a sacrifice be incurred by him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile. (26)

verses.text:
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधे युद्धे शस्त्रसमाकुले।
मा स्म कार्षीत् सतां धर्मं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Let the sin attaching to the man who fails to observe the code of warfare followed by the virtuous on a field of battle crowded with elephants, horses and chariots and thick with weapons of all kinds be incurred by him with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile. (27)

verses.text:
उपदिष्टं सुसूक्ष्मार्थं शास्त्रं यत्नेन धीमता।
स नाशयतु दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Let that wicked soul with whose concurrence my elder brother has gone into exile forget the sacred lore expounding the most esoteric truths, taught with great pains by an enlightened preceptor. (28)

verses.text:
मा च तं व्यूढबाह्वंसं चन्द्रभास्करतेजसम्।
द्राक्षीद् राज्यस्थमासीनं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the forest not live to see Śrī Rāma of muscular arms and shoulders, and possessing the splendour of the moon and the sun installed on the throne. (29)

verses.text:
पायसं कृसरं छागं वृथा सोऽश्नातु निर्घृणः।
गुरूंश्चाप्यवजानातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Let that merciless fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods incur the sin of partaking of milk boiled with rice and sugar, seasoned rice boiled with sesame seeds and Moong (a kind of kidney bean), and goat-milk in vain (without offering them in the first instance to the almighty Lord, gods and manes etc.,) and of showing disrespect to his elders by failing to rise on their arrival and greet them. (30)

verses.text:
गाश्च स्पृशतु पादेन गुरून् परिवदेत च।
मित्रे द्रुह्येत सोऽत्यर्थं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the forest incur the sin of touching the body of cows with his feet, reviling his elders and bearing deep-rooted malice to a friend. (31)

verses.text:
विश्वासात् कथितं किंचित् परिवादं मिथः क्वचित्।
विवृणोतु स दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Let that evil-minded fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the forest incur the sin of revealing to someone else a fault of another confessed in private out of reliance (that he will not divulge the secret before anyone). (32)

verses.text:
अकर्ता चाकृतज्ञश्च त्यक्तात्मा निरपत्रपः।
लोके भवतु विद्विष्टो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods never be in a position to return a service; nay, let him prove ungrateful and shameless, let him be shunned by good men and hated by all. (33)

verses.text:
पुत्रैर्दासैश्च भृत्यैश्च स्वगृहे परिवारितः।
स एको मृष्टमश्नातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods incur the sin of partaking of a savoury dish alone, at his own home, though surrounded by a number of sons, servants and dependants. (34)

verses.text:
अप्राप्य सदृशान् दाराननपत्यः प्रमीयताम्।
अनवाप्य क्रियां धर्म्यां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods die issueless, failing to secure a wife becoming of him, in point of pedigree, disposition and so on and in this way not enjoying the privilege of performing sacred duties like Agnihotra etc., which can be performed only by a married couple. (35)

verses.text:
माऽऽत्मनः संततिं द्राक्षीत् स्वेषु दारेषु दुःखितः।
आयुःसमग्रमप्राप्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods not behold the face of a male child through his wedded wife and die full of agony without attaining the full age of a hundred years. (36)

verses.text:
राजस्त्रीबालवृद्धानां वधे यत् पापमुच्यते।
भृत्यत्यागे च यत् पापं तत् पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Let him incur the same sin which is declared as attaching to the act of killing a ruler, woman, infant or aged man and forsaking a dependant. (37)

verses.text:
लाक्षया मधुमांसेन लोहेन च विषेण च।
सदैव बिभृयाद् भृत्यान् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed (for the woods) always support his dependants through sale of lacquer, honey and flesh, iron and poison, which is prohibited in the Śāstras*. (38)

verses.text:
संग्रामे समुपोढे च शत्रुपक्षभयंकरे।
पलायमानो वध्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods be killed while fleeing at a time when a battle inspiring terror into the adversaries has commenced. (39)

verses.text:
कपालपाणिः पृथिवीमटतां चीरसंवृतः।
भिक्षमाणो यथोन्मत्तो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods roam about like a madman, clad in tatters and begging alms, bowl in hand. (40)

verses.text:
मद्यप्रसक्तो भवतु स्त्रीष्वक्षेषु च नित्यशः।
कामक्रोधाभिभूतश्च यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods be given over from day to day to wine as well as to women and dice and overpowered by lust and anger. (41)

verses.text:
मास्य धर्मे मनो भूयादधर्मं स निषेवताम्।
अपात्रवर्षी भवतु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Let the man with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods indulge in unrighteousness and shower his wealth on the undeserving and let his mind never take delight in piety. (42)

verses.text:
संचितान्यस्य वित्तानि विविधानि सहस्रशः।
दस्युभिर्विप्रलुप्यन्तां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Let the possessions of every description, accumulated in thousands, of the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods be looted by robbers. (43)

verses.text:
उभे संध्ये शयानस्य यत् पापं परिकल्प्यते।
तच्च पापं भवेत् तस्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Let that very sin which attaches to a man who sleeps during both the twilights be incurred by him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods. (44)

verses.text:
यदग्निदायके पापं यत् पापं गुरुतल्पगे।
मित्रद्रोहे च यत् पापं तत् पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Let him incur that very sin which attaches to the man who practises arson, to him who violates the bed of his teacher and to the fellow who plays a friend foul. (45)

verses.text:
देवतानां पितॄणां च मातापित्रोस्तथैव च।
मा स्म कार्षीत् स शुश्रूषां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods not have an opportunity to do service to gods in the form of Agnihotra etc., and to the manes in the form of periodical Śrāddha and likewise to his living parents. (46)

verses.text:
सतां लोकात् सतां कीर्त्याः सज्जुष्टात् कर्मणस्तथा।
भ्रश्यतु क्षिप्रमद्यैव यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Let the man with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods forfeit this very day, nay, at once his claim to the region inhabited by the virtuous after their death, forfeit his claim to the reputation enjoyed by good men and fall from the course of conduct followed by the righteous. (47)

verses.text:
अपास्य मातृशुश्रूषामनर्थे सोऽवतिष्ठताम्।
दीर्घबाहुर्महावक्षा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother, distinguished by long arms and a broad chest, has departed for the woods be devoted to the evil path, giving up service to his mother. (48)

verses.text:
बहुभृत्यो दरिद्रश्च ज्वररोगसमन्वितः।
समायात् सततं क्लेशं यस्यार्योनुमते गतः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods be a pauper though having many dependants to support; let him be seized with ailment in the form of fever and suffer hardship continually. (49)

verses.text:
आशामाशंसमानानां दीनानामूर्ध्वचक्षुषाम्।
अर्थिनां वितथां कुर्याद् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Let the man with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods falsify the hopes of destitute suppliants uttering his praises and looking upwards in his face in expectancy. (50)

verses.text:
मायया रमतां नित्यं पुरुषः पिशुनोऽशुचिः।
राज्ञो भीतस्त्वधर्मात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods ever delight in deception, remaining a backbiter and impure and afraid of the king all his life, his mind being given to unrighteousness. (51)

verses.text:
ऋतुस्नातां सतीं भार्यामृतुकालानुरोधिनीम्।
अतिवर्तेत दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Let the evil-minded fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods ignore his chaste wife who has attained purity after menstruation (and is thus fit to conceive) and approaches him for union, the period being favourable for procreation. (52)

verses.text:
विप्रलुप्तप्रजातस्य दुष्कृतं ब्राह्मणस्य यत्।
तदेतत् प्रतिपद्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods incur that very sin which attaches to a Brāhmaṇa whose offsprings have perished for lack of nourishment. (53)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणायोद्यतां पूजां विहन्तु कलुषेन्द्रियः।
बालवत्सां च गां दोग्धु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Let that man of sinful mind with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods interrupt the worship going to be offered to a Brāhmaṇa by another and milk a cow which calved less than ten days ago. (54)

verses.text:
धर्मदारान् परित्यज्य परदारान् निषेवताम्।
त्यक्तधर्मरतिर्मूढो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “Let the fool with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods enjoy another’s wife, forsaking his lawful wife and having given up his love for piety. (55)

verses.text:
पानीयदूषके पापं तथैव विषदायके।
यत्तदेकः स लभतां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Let the fellow with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods incur all at once the sin that attaches to him who defiles the water of a well or tank as well as that which attaches to one who administers poison. (56)

verses.text:
तृषार्तं सति पानीये विप्रलम्भेन योजयन्।
यत् पापं लभते तत् स्याद् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “Let the sin, which a man disappointing a person oppressed with thirst by recourse to deception in the form of giving a false report denying the presence of water, even though there is water with him, attach to him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods. (57)

verses.text:
भक्त्या विवदमानेषु मार्गमाश्रित्य पश्यतः।
तेन पापेन युज्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Let him with whose concurrence my elder brother has departed for the woods be held guilty of the same sin which attaches to a man standing on the road and witnessing a dispute with partiality for one of the disputing parties.” (58)

verses.text:
एवमाश्वासयन्नेव दुःखार्तोऽनुपपात ह।
विहीनां पतिपुत्राभ्यां कौसल्यां पार्थिवात्मजः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Even while reassuring as aforesaid Kausalyā, who was bereft both of her husband and son, the prince, Bharata, they say, fell to the ground, stricken as he was with agony. (59)

verses.text:
तदा तं शपथैः कष्टैः शपमानमचेतनम्।
भरतं शोकसंतप्तं कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Thereupon Kausalyā spoke as follows to Bharata, who was solemnly pleading his innocence by means of oaths that were hard to take and had become unconscious, sore stricken as he was with grief : (60)

verses.text:
मम दुःखमिदं पुत्र भूयः समुपजायते।
शपथैः शपमानो हि प्राणानुपरुणत्सि मे॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “The present agony of mine, my son, is aggravated all the more inasmuch as you are choking my breath while solemnly pleading your innocence by means of oaths. (61)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या न चलितो धर्मादात्मा ते सहलक्षणः।
वत्स सत्यप्रतिज्ञो हि सतां लोकानवाप्स्यसि॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Luckily enough your mind, endowed as it is with excellences, has not deviated from righteousness. Since you are true to your promise, you will attain to the realms of the virtuous, my child !” (62)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा चाङ्कमानीय भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्।
परिष्वज्य महाबाहुं रुरोद भृशदुःखिता॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Saying so and placing the mighty-armed Bharata, who was so fond of his brother, on her lap, and embracing him, Kausalyā, who felt sore distressed, wept aloud. (63)

verses.text:
एवं विलपमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः।
मोहाच्च शोकसंरम्भाद् बभूव लुलितं मनः॥ ६४॥
verses.m: The mind of the high-souled Bharata, who was wailing as aforesaid, stricken as he was with sorrow, got agitated through infatuation and excess of grief. (64)

verses.text:
लालप्यमानस्य विचेतनस्य
प्रणष्टबुद्धेः पतितस्य भूमौ।
मुहुर्मुहुर्निःश्वसतश्च दीर्घं
सा तस्य शोकेन जगाम रात्रिः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: While Bharata was lamenting thus and lay fallen unconscious on the ground, sighing again and again through grief, his power of judgment having been lost, the aforesaid night passed. (65)

verses.text:
तमेवं शोकसंतप्तं भरतं कैकयीसुतम्।
उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठवागृषिः॥ १॥
verses.m: To Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, who was sore stricken with grief, as aforesaid, Sage Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of speakers, spoke as follows in a most polite language : (1)

verses.text:
अलं शोकेन भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः।
प्राप्तकालं नरपतेः कुरु संयानमुत्तमम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Have done with grief, O highly illustrious prince ! May good betide you ! Perform now in an excellent way the funeral of the deceased king, which is now overdue.” (2)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भरतो धरणीं गतः।
प्रेतकृत्यानि सर्वाणि कारयामास धर्मवित्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing the admonition of Vasiṣṭha, Bharata, who knew what is right, fell prostrate and ordered all obsequies concerning his father to be taken in hand. (3)

verses.text:
उद्धृत्य तैलसंसेकात् स तु भूमौ निवेशितम्।
आपीतवर्णवदनं प्रसुप्तमिव भूमिपम्॥ ४॥
संवेश्य शयने चाग्र्ये नानारत्नपरिष्कृते।
ततो दशरथं पुत्रो विललाप सुदुःखितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Taking the dead body of the king out of the vessel in which it lay immersed in oil, and placing Daśaratha—who was first laid on the ground and, though pale-faced, looked as though he were fast asleep—on an exquisite bier decked with various jewels, his son, Bharata, lamented as follows, sore distressed as he was : (4-5)

verses.text:
किं ते व्यवसितं राजन् प्रोषिते मय्यनागते।
विवास्य रामं धर्मज्ञं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Having sent into exile Śrī Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa, possessed of great strength, at a time when I was away from home and had not yet returned, what did you intend to do, O king, knowing as you did what is right? (6)

verses.text:
क्व यास्यसि महाराज हित्वेमं दुःखितं जनम्।
हीनं पुरुषसिंहेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Where will you go abandoning this distressed servant of yours, already bereft of Śrī Rāma, a veritable lion among men, who does great deeds without the least exertion, O great king? (7)

verses.text:
योगक्षेमं तु तेऽव्यग्रं कोऽस्मिन् कल्पयिता पुरे।
त्वयि प्रयाते स्वस्तात रामे च वनमाश्रिते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Now that you have departed for heaven, O dear father, and Śrī Rāma has retired to the woods, I wonder who will quietly meet the needs of the people and ensure the safety of their person and property in this capital of yours? (8)

verses.text:
विधवा पृथिवी राजंस्त्वया हीना न राजते।
हीनचन्द्रेव रजनी नगरी प्रतिभाति माम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Bereft of you and thus deprived of its lord, the earth does not look charming any more; nay, the city too appears to me cheerless as a night bereft of the moon.”(9)

verses.text:
एवं विलपमानं तं भरतं दीनमानसम्।
अब्रवीद् वचनं भूयो वसिष्ठस्तु महामुनिः॥ १०॥
verses.m: To Bharata, who was lamenting as aforesaid, afflicted in mind as he was, the eminent sage Vasiṣṭha for his part spoke again in the following words : (10)

verses.text:
प्रेतकार्याणि यान्यस्य कर्तव्यानि विशाम्पतेः।
तान्यव्यग्रं महाबाहो क्रियतामविचारितम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Whatever funeral rites in relation to the deceased monarch ought to be done should be coolly and unhesitatingly gone through, O mighty-armed prince !” (11)

verses.text:
तथेति भरतो वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्याभिपूज्य तत्।
ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यांस्त्वरयामास सर्वशः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Bowing to the aforesaid command of Vasiṣṭha in the words “Let it be so !” Bharata urged everyone, viz., the priests engaged for sacrificial purposes, family priests and the Ācāryas to make haste. (12)

verses.text:
ये त्वग्नयो नरेन्द्रस्य अग्न्यगाराद् बहिष्कृताः।
ऋत्विग्भिर्याजकैश्चैव ते हूयन्ते यथाविधि॥ १३॥
verses.m: The sacred fires maintained by the king, that had been taken out of the fire-sanctuary on the latter’s death, were being worshipped by the priests engaged for sacrificial purposes and superintending priests according to the scriptural ordinance. (13)

verses.text:
शिबिकायामथारोप्य राजानं गतचेतनम्।
बाष्पकण्ठा विमनसस्तमूहुः परिचारकाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having placed the king, whose consciousness had departed days ago, on a bier, the servants, who were feeling disconsolate, now bore him on their shoulders to the cremation ground, their throats choked with tears. (14)

verses.text:
हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च वासांसि विविधानि च।
प्रकिरन्तो जना मार्गे नृपतेरग्रतो ययुः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Scattering flowers of silver and gold and pieces of cloth of every description on the road, people walked ahead of the king. (15)

verses.text:
चन्दनागुरुनिर्यासान् सरलं पद्मकं तथा।
देवदारूणि चाहृत्य क्षेपयन्ति तथापरे॥ १६॥
verses.m: While others fetching sandalwood, aloe, bdellium, the wood of Sarala (a species of pine) and Cerasus puddum and logs of deodar (the Himalayan cedar), made pile. (16)

verses.text:
गन्धानुच्चावचांश्चान्यांस्तत्र गत्वाथ भूमिपम्।
तत्र संवेशयामासुश्चितामध्ये तमृत्विजः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Nay, throwing other fragrant substances of various kinds into the funeral pile, the priests officiating at the obsequies laid the deceased emperor in the middle of the pyre at the cremation ground. (17)

verses.text:
तदा हुताशनं हुत्वा जेपुस्तस्य तदृत्विजः।
जगुश्च ते यथाशास्त्रं तत्र सामानि सामगाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Pouring oblations into the fire, the aforesaid priests engaged for the benefit of the emperor then recited sacred texts relevant to the funeral rites; while those among the officiating priests who could recite the hymns of Sāmaveda, chanted them according to the rules. (18)

verses.text:
शिबिकाभिश्च यानैश्च यथार्हं तस्य योषितः।
नगरान्निर्ययुस्तत्र वृद्धैः परिवृतास्तथा॥ १९॥
verses.m: Attended by elderly guards the king’s consorts likewise went out of the city to the cremation ground in palanquins and chariots according to their rank. (19)

verses.text:
प्रसव्यं चापि तं चक्रुर्ऋत्विजोऽग्निचितं नृपम्।
स्त्रियश्च शोकसंतप्ताः कौसल्याप्रमुखास्तदा॥ २०॥
verses.m: Then the priests officiating at the obsequies too as well as the ladies led by Kausalyā who were sore stricken with grief, went clockwise round the said monarch, who had performed sacrifices culminating in Aśwamedha. (20)

verses.text:
क्रौञ्चीनामिव नारीणां निनादस्तत्र शुश्रुवे।
आर्तानां करुणं काले क्रोशन्तीनां सहस्रशः॥ २१॥
verses.m: There was heard on that occasion the noise of afflicted women wailing piteously in thousands like so many female cranes. (21)

verses.text:
ततो रुदन्त्यो विवशा विलप्य च पुनः पुनः।
यानेभ्यः सरयूतीरमवतेरुर्नृपाङ्गनाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having lamented again and again and crying helplessly, the king’s consorts got down from their chariots at the bank of the Sarayū. (22)

verses.text:
कृत्वोदकं ते भरतेन सार्धं
नृपाङ्गना मन्त्रिपुरोहिताश्च।
पुरं प्रविश्याश्रुपरीतनेत्रा
भूमौ दशाहं व्यनयन्त दुःखम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having offered water to the spirit of the deceased alongwith Bharata and entering the city once more, the king’s consorts as well as the counsellors and family priests spent the following ten days of their impurity caused by the emperor’s death in agony, reposing on the ground, their eyes filled with tears. (23)

verses.text:
ततो दशाहेऽतिगते कृतशौचो नृपात्मजः।
द्वादशेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते श्राद्धकर्माण्यकारयत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having attained purity by performing the obsequial rites pertaining to the eleventh day of his father’s death when ten days had elapsed the prince (Bharata) next performed the obsequial rites pertaining to the twelfth day when that day duly arrived. (1)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं रत्नं ददावन्नं च पुष्कलम्।
वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च।
वास्तिकं बहु शुक्लं च गाश्चापि बहुशस्तदा॥ २॥
verses.m: On that occasion he gifted to the Brāhmaṇas abundant gold, jewellery, foodgrains, precious garments, various types of gems, a large herd of white goats, silver and good many cows, too. (2)

verses.text:
दासीर्दासांश्च यानानि वेश्मानि सुमहान्ति च।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुत्रो राज्ञस्तस्यौर्ध्वदेहिकम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: The prince further gave away to the Brāhmaṇas, for the good of the king in the life beyond, female as well as male servants, chariots and very big houses. (3)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसे च त्रयोदशे।
विललाप महाबाहुर्भरतः शोकमूर्च्छितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Then on the thirteenth day at the time of daybreak the mighty-armed Bharata, overwhelmed as he was with grief, broke into a lament. (4)

verses.text:
शब्दापिहितकण्ठश्च शोधनार्थमुपागतः।
चितामूले पितुर्वाक्यमिदमाह सुदुःखितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Nay, having reached the foot of his father’s funeral pile in order to collect the bones for their immersion in the holy Sarayū river, the prince, who was sore distressed, addressed the following words to his deceased father, his throat being choked through crying : (5)

verses.text:
तात यस्मिन् निसृष्टोऽहं त्वया भ्रातरि राघवे।
तस्मिन् वनं प्रव्रजिते शून्ये त्यक्तोऽस्म्यहं त्वया॥ ६॥
verses.m: “My celebrated elder brother, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), to whose care I was committed by you, having retired to the forest, O dear father, I have been virtually abandoned by you in a desolate place. (6)

verses.text:
यस्या गतिरनाथायाः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो वनम्।
तामम्बां तात कौसल्यां त्यक्त्वा त्वं क्व गतो नृप॥ ७॥
verses.m: “O dear father, O protector of men, where have you gone, leaving Kausalyā, that mother of mine, whose son, the support of that forlorn lady, has been exiled to the forest?” (7)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा भस्मारुणं तच्च दग्धास्थि स्थानमण्डलम्।
पितुः शरीरनिर्वाणं निष्टनन् विषसाद ह॥ ८॥
verses.m: Seeing that circular spot, the place where his father’s remains had been consigned to fire, nay, which was now covered with ashes and red because of its having been burnt with a blazing fire and was further strewn with burnt bones, Bharata, they say, grew melancholy and began to cry. (8)

verses.text:
स तु दृष्ट्वा रुदन् दीनः पपात धरणीतले।
उत्थाप्यमानः शक्रस्य यन्त्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Nay, afflicted to behold the spot, Bharata fell weeping on the ground as a tall banner would while being raised in honour of Indra with the help of a mechanical device. (9)

verses.text:
अभिपेतुस्ततः सर्वे तस्यामात्याः शुचिव्रतम्।
अन्तकाले निपतितं ययातिमृषयो यथा॥ १०॥
verses.m: Thereupon all his ministers rushed to Bharata of holy resolve as royal sages Aṣṭaka and others hastily approached King Yayāti fallen down from heaven when the stock of his merits that sustained him in heaven had been exhausted. (10)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नश्चापि भरतं दृष्ट्वा शोकपरिप्लुतम्।
विसंज्ञो न्यपतद् भूमौ भूमिपालमनुस्मरन्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Nay, perceiving Bharata overwhelmed with grief, Śatrughna too, who had all along been thinking of the emperor his father, dropped senseless on the ground. (11)

verses.text:
उन्मत्त इव निश्चित्तो विललाप सुदुःखितः।
स्मृत्वा पितुर्गुणाङ्गानि तानि तानि तदा तदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: Sore distressed to remember the various gestures of his father born of his loving qualities and made by him from time to time, Śatrughna lamented as follows like a madman, bewildered as he was : (12)

verses.text:
मन्थराप्रभवस्तीव्र कैकेयीग्राहसंकुलः।
वरदानमयोऽक्षोभ्योऽमज्जयच्छोकसागरः ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “The violent and formidable sea of grief, released by Mantharā, which has appeared in the form of the boons granted by my father in favour of Kaikeyī and has been rendered fearful by alligators in the form of Kaikeyīs words, has engulfed us all. (13)

verses.text:
सुकुमारं च बालं च सततं लालितं त्वया।
क्व तात भरतं हित्वा विलपन्तं गतो भवान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Where have you gone, dear father, leaving Bharata—who is yet a mere stripling, tender of body, and was constantly fondled by you—weeping? (14)

verses.text:
ननु भोज्येषु पानेषु वस्त्रेष्वाभरणेषु च।
प्रवारयति सर्वान् नस्तन्नः कोऽद्य करिष्यति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, you made us all, the four brothers, have our best choice out of a large variety of eatables, drinks, articles of wearing apparel and ornaments placed before us. Since you have disappeared from our midst, who will discharge this function now? (15)

verses.text:
अवदारणकाले तु पृथिवी नावदीर्यते।
विहीना या त्वया राज्ञा धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How strange that this earth, even though it has been deprived of you, its high-souled ruler, who knew what is right, is not riven even at a time when it should have been riven ! (16)

verses.text:
पितरि स्वर्गमापन्ने रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते।
किं मे जीवितसामर्थ्यं प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “My father having reached heaven and Śrī Rāma having retired to the forest, what energy has been left in me to survive? I shall acordingly enter the fire. (17)

verses.text:
हीनो भ्रात्रा च पित्रा च शून्यामिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।
अयोध्यां न प्रवेक्ष्यामि प्रवेक्ष्यामि तपोवनम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Bereft of my brother and father, too, I would not return to Ayodhyā—which, though ruled so long by scions of Ikṣwāku, has now become desolate—but shall withdraw to a forest suitable for austerities.” (18)

verses.text:
तयोर्विलपितं श्रुत्वा व्यसनं चाप्यवेक्ष्य तत्।
भृशमार्ततरा भूयः सर्व एवानुगामिनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing the lament of the two brothers and perceiving their extreme agony aforesaid, all their attendants felt sore distressed even more. (19)

verses.text:
ततो विषण्णौ श्रान्तौ च शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ।
धरायां स्म व्यचेष्टेतां भग्नशृङ्गाविवर्षभौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: Dejected and distressed, Śatrughna and Bharata both now began to roll on the ground like a pair of bulls whose horns have been broken. (20)

verses.text:
ततः प्रकृतिमान् वैद्यः पितुरेषां पुरोहितः।
वसिष्ठो भरतं वाक्यमुत्थाप्य तमुवाच ह॥ २१॥
verses.m: Raising Bharata up, the omniscient Vasiṣṭha, the family priest of their father as well as of them all, endowed as he was with an amiable disposition, spoke to him as follows, so the tradition goes : (21)

verses.text:
त्रयोदशोऽयं दिवसः पितुर्वृत्तस्य ते विभो।
सावशेषास्थिनिचये किमिह त्वं विलम्बसे॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Today is the thirteenth day since your father was cremated, my lord ! Why then do you lag behind now in winding up the remaining part of the ceremony of collecting the bones, viz., cleaning and washing the ground on which the king’s body had been cremated and consigning the ashes to the river? (22)

verses.text:
त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः।
तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Three pairs of opposites (life and death, joy and sorrow, gain and loss) prevail alike in all living beings. And they being unavoidable, you ought not to behave like this.” (23)

verses.text:
सुमन्त्रश्चापि शत्रुघ्नमुत्थाप्याभिप्रसाद्य च।
श्रावयामास तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतभवाभवौ॥ २४॥
verses.m: Raising up and pacifying Śatrughna, Sumantra too, a knower of the Truth, told him how birth and death were inevitable for all created beings. (24)

verses.text:
उत्थितौ तौ नरव्याघ्रौ प्रकाशेते यशस्विनौ।
वर्षातपपरिग्लानौ पृथगिन्द्रध्वजाविव॥ २५॥
verses.m: The two illustrious princes, who were veritable tigers among men and had now got up, shone like two banners, severally raised in honour of Indra, the god of rain, and soiled through rain and the sun. (25)

verses.text:
अश्रूणि परिमृद्नन्तौ रक्ताक्षौ दीनभाषिणौ।
अमात्यास्त्वरयन्ति स्म तनयौ चापराः क्रियाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: The ministers now urged the two princes—who were wiping their tears and speaking in a piteous tone, their eyes reddened through excessive grief—to expedite the other rites pertaining to the thirteenth day, viz., lifting the ashes and immersing them into the river and so on.(26)

verses.text:
अथ यात्रां समीहन्तं शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः।
भरतं शोकसंतप्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: To Bharata, who was sore stricken with grief and was contemplating to undertake a journey to meet Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa—spoke as follows : (1)

verses.text:
गतिर्यः सर्वभूतानां दुःखे किं पुनरात्मनः।
स रामः सत्त्वसम्पन्नः स्त्रिया प्रव्राजितो वनम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “How strange that the same Śrī Rāma who is possessed of extraordinary might and is the support of all created beings in distress, much more of himself and his own, was exiled into the forest by a woman ! (2)

verses.text:
बलवान् वीर्यसम्पन्नो लक्ष्मणो नाम योऽप्यसौ।
किं न मोचयते रामं कृत्वापि पितृनिग्रहम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “What a pity that even Lakṣmaṇa, who is full of might and rich in prowess, did not deliver Śrī Rāma from distress, going the length, even if necessary, of restraining his father ! (3)

verses.text:
पूर्वमेव तु विग्राह्यः समवेक्ष्य नयानयौ।
उत्पथं यः समारूढो नार्या राजा वशं गतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “In fact, fully considering what is just and what is unjust, the king, who had adopted a wrong course, having fallen into the clutches of a woman, ought to have been restrained even before matters came to a head.” (4)

verses.text:
इति सम्भाषमाणे तु शत्रुघ्ने लक्ष्मणानुजे।
प्राग्द्वारेऽभूत् तदा कुब्जा सर्वाभरणभूषिता॥ ५॥
verses.m: Even while Śatrughna, the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, was speaking as aforesaid, Mantharā, the hunchbacked maidservant of Kaikeyī, appeared at that very moment decked with all sorts of ornaments at the eastern door. (5)

verses.text:
लिप्ता चन्दनसारेण राजवस्त्राणि बिभ्रती।
विविधं विविधैस्तैस्तैर्भूषणैश्च विभूषिता॥ ६॥
verses.m: Smeared all over with excellent sandal-paste and wearing royal costumes she was adorned in various ways with ornaments of every description pertaining to all limbs. (6)

verses.text:
मेखलादामभिश्चित्रैरन्यैश्च वरभूषणैः।
बभासे बहुभिर्बद्धा रज्जुबद्धेव वानरी॥ ७॥
verses.m: Adorned with lovely girdles and other excellent ornaments worn round the waist, she looked like a female monkey bound with a number of strings. (7)

verses.text:
तां समीक्ष्य तदा द्वाःस्थो भृशं पापस्य कारिणीम्।
गृहीत्वाकरुणं कुब्जां शत्रुघ्नाय न्यवेदयत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Gazing on that humpback, who was responsible for the sinful deed in the form of banishment of Śrī Rāma and others, which had proved a terrible curse for the entire population of Ayodhyā and seizing her most heartlessly, the porter on duty delivered her to Śatrughna with the following words : (8)

verses.text:
यस्याः कृते वने रामो न्यस्तदेहश्च वः पिता।
सेयं पापा नृशंसा च तस्याः कुरु यथामति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Here is that cruel wretch because of whom Śrī Rāma is living in the forest and your father has cast off his body ! Deal with her as you please.” (9)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नश्च तदाज्ञाय वचनं भृशदुःखितः।
अन्तःपुरचरान् सर्वानित्युवाच धृतव्रतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Pondering the aforesaid submission of the porter and having determined his course of action, Śatrughna, who was feeling sore distressed, spoke to all the inmates of the gynaeceum as follows : (10)

verses.text:
तीव्रमुत्पादितं दुःखं भ्रातॄणां मे तथा पितुः।
यथा सेयं नृशंसस्य कर्मणः फलमश्नुताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Let this wench reap the fruit of her cruel deed as acute agony has been caused by her to my brothers as well as to my father.” (11)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा च तेनाशु सखीजनसमावृता।
गृहीता बलवत् कुब्जा सा तद् गृहमनादयत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: With these words the humpback, who was surrounded by her female companions, was violently seized by him at once; and she in her turn made that chamber, where he stood, resound with her shrieks. (12)

verses.text:
ततः सुभृशसंतप्तस्तस्याः सर्वः सखीजनः।
क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय शत्रुघ्नं व्यपलायत सर्वशः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Extremely agonized to perceive Śatrughna enraged, all her female companions forthwith ran away helter-skelter in all directions. (13)

verses.text:
अमन्त्रयत कृत्स्नश्च तस्याः सर्वः सखीजनः।
यथायं समुपक्रान्तो निःशेषं नः करिष्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: All her female companions as well as the entire menial staff said to one another, “From the way in which he has started dealing with us, it can easily be concluded that he will put an end to us all. (14)

verses.text:
सानुक्रोशां वदान्यां च धर्मज्ञां च यशस्विनीम्।
कौसल्यां शरणं यामः सा हि नोऽस्ति ध्रुवा गतिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “We shall fly for protection to Kausalyā, who is merciful, polite of speech and glorious and knows what is right; for she is our unfailing asylum.” (15)

verses.text:
स च रोषेण संवीतः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुशासनः।
विचकर्ष तदा कुब्जां क्रोशन्तीं पृथिवीतले॥ १६॥
verses.m: Nay, overwhelmed with anger, the said Śatrughna, the chastiser of his enemies, then violently dragged the crying humpback along the floor. (16)

verses.text:
तस्यां ह्याकृष्यमाणायां मन्थरायां ततस्ततः।
चित्रं बहुविधं भाण्डं पृथिव्यां तद्व्यशीर्यत॥ १७॥
verses.m: While the notorious Mantharā was being dragged to and fro on the ground, her excellent ornaments of various kinds, mentioned above, were actually dashed to pieces. (17)

verses.text:
तेन भाण्डेन विस्तीर्णं श्रीमद् राजनिवेशनम्।
अशोभत तदा भूयः शारदं गगनं यथा॥ १८॥
verses.m: Strewn with those broken ornaments, the splendid royal palace shone all the more at that moment like the clear actual sky spangled with stars. (18)

verses.text:
स बली बलवत् क्रोधाद् गृहीत्वा पुरुषर्षभः।
कैकेयीमभिनिर्भर्त्स्य बभाषे परुषं वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Continuing to hold Mantharā in violent rage and sharply rebuking Kaikeyī (who had come to protect her maidservant), that mighty prince, a veritable jewel among men, spoke harsh words to her. (19)

verses.text:
तैर्वाक्यैः परुषैर्दुःखैः कैकेयी भृशदुःखिता।
शत्रुघ्नभयसंत्रस्ता पुत्रं शरणमागता॥ २०॥
verses.m: Greatly pained by those harsh and unpleasant words and overwhelmed with fear of Śatrughna, Kaikeyī fled for protection to her own son. (20)

verses.text:
तं प्रेक्ष्य भरतः क्रुद्धं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।
अवध्याः सर्वभूतानां प्रमदाः क्षम्यतामिति॥ २१॥
verses.m: Perceiving Śatrughna enraged, Bharata spoke to him as follows : “Women are undeserving of death at the hands of all men. Let her be forgiven as such. (21)

verses.text:
हन्यामहमिमां पापां कैकेयीं दुष्टचारिणीम्।
यदि मां धार्मिको रामो नासूयेन्मातृघातकम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I myself would have slain this sinful Kaikeyī of vicious conduct had it not been for the fact that the pious Śrī Rāma is sure to get angry with me for my having killed my own mother. (22)

verses.text:
इमामपि हतां कुब्जां यदि जानाति राघवः।
त्वां च मां चैव धर्मात्मा नाभिभाषिष्यते ध्रुवम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Nay, Śrī Rāma, whose mind is given to piety, will surely never speak not only with you but also with me if he ultimately comes to know even of this humpback having been killed by us.” (23)

verses.text:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः।
न्यवर्तत ततो दोषात् तां मुमोच च मूर्च्छिताम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing the admonition of Bharata, Śatrughna, the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, desisted from the aforesaid crime and left her almost unconscious. (24)

verses.text:
सा पादमूले कैकेय्या मन्थरा निपपात ह।
निःश्वसन्ती सुदुःखार्ता कृपणं विललाप ह॥ २५॥
verses.m: The notorious Mantharā, it is said, fell at the soles of Kaikeyī’s feet. (Nay) drawing a deep audible breath expressive of sadness, sore stricken as she was with sorrow, she piteously wailed: so the tradition goes. (25)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नविक्षेपविमूढसंज्ञां
समीक्ष्य कुब्जां भरतस्य माता।
शनैः समाश्वासयदार्तरूपां
क्रौञ्चीं विलग्नामिव वीक्षमाणाम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Perceiving the humpback stunned because of her having been dragged to and fro by Śatrughna, and wearing a wretched look and looking on her boss like a female crane released from captivity, Bharata’s mother slowly calmed her. (26)

verses.text:
ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ चतुर्दशे।
समेत्य राजकर्तारो भरतं वाक्यमब्रुवन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Coming together on the fourteenth day at daybreak, the king’s counsellors forthwith spoke to Bharata as follows : (1)

verses.text:
गतो दशरथः स्वर्गं यो नो गुरुतरो गुरुः।
रामं प्रव्राज्य वै ज्येष्ठं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Alas, having sent into exile his eldest son, Śrī Rāma, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, who is possessed of extraordinary might, Daśaratha, who was our most venerable sovereign, has ascended to heaven. (2)

verses.text:
त्वमद्य भव नो राजा राजपुत्रो महायशः।
संगत्या नापराध्नोति राज्यमेतदनायकम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “This kingdom being without a ruler, be you our ruler now, O highly illustrious prince ! There being justification for your assuming the reins of government because your elder brother has been exiled under the command of your father and you have been nominated by him as his successor, you are not to blame for superseding the claims of your brother. (3)

verses.text:
आभिषेचनिकं सर्वमिदमादाय राघव।
प्रतीक्षते त्वां स्वजनः श्रेणयश्च नृपात्मज॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Taking all these requisites for your consecration, O scion of Raghu, your own people, the counsellors and ministers, as well as the citizens are awaiting your pleasure, O prince ! (4)

verses.text:
राज्यं गृहाण भरत पितृपैतामहं ध्रुवम्।
अभिषेचय चात्मानं पाहि चास्मान् नरर्षभ॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Accept the throne of Ayodhyā, which has surely been inherited by you from your father and grandfather, O Bharata, and have yourself consecrated and thereby protect us, O jewel among men !” (5)

verses.text:
आभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं कृत्वा सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम्।
भरतस्तं जनं सर्वं प्रत्युवाच धृतव्रतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Going clockwise as a mark of respect round all the requisites for consecration, Bharata, who had taken the vow of propitiating Śrī Rāma, replied to all those counsellors as follows : (6)

verses.text:
ज्येष्ठस्य राजता नित्यमुचिता हि कुलस्य नः।
नैवं भवन्तो मां वक्तुमर्हन्ति कुशला जनाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Since the practice of conferring the kingship on the eldest brother has ever been regarded as commendable in our race; you, who are all clever people, ought not to make such a request to me. (7)

verses.text:
रामः पूर्वो हि नो भ्राता भविष्यति महीपतिः।
अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि वर्षाणि नव पञ्च च॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma will be the ruler of the earth, since he is our eldest brother. I, for my part, shall reside in the forest for nine years and five on his behalf. (8)

verses.text:
युज्यतां महती सेना चतुरङ्गमहाबला।
आनयिष्याम्यहं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरं राघवं वनात्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Let a large and exceptionally powerful army consisting of all the four limbs be got ready to accompany me to the forest. I shall bring back in state my elder brother, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, from the forest. (9)

verses.text:
आभिषेचनिकं चैव सर्वमेतदुपस्कृतम्।
पुरस्कृत्य गमिष्यामि रामहेतोर्वनं प्रति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Placing in the van all these requisites got together for the consecration ceremony, I shall proceed in the direction of the forest in order to meet Śrī Rāma. (10)

verses.text:
तत्रैव तं नरव्याघ्रमभिषिच्य पुरस्कृतम्।
आनयिष्यामि वै रामं हव्यवाहमिवाध्वरात्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having consecrated that tiger among men in the forest itself, I shall surely bring Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā with honour even as one would bring a sacred fire from a big fire-sanctuary to one’s own house. (11)

verses.text:
न सकामां करिष्यामि स्वामिमां मातृगन्धिनीम्।
वने वत्स्याम्यहं दुर्गे रामो राजा भविष्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I shall not allow this so-called mother of mine to realize her ambition of seeing her son crowned king. I shall, on the contrary, reside in a forest difficult to cross, while Śrī Rāma will be crowned king. (12)

verses.text:
क्रियतां शिल्पिभिः पन्थाः समानि विषमाणि च।
रक्षिणश्चानुसंयान्तु पथि दुर्गविचारकाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Let a passage be carved by masons where there is none, let uneven roads be levelled, and let guards knowing the difficult and narrow passages duly follow us.” (13)

verses.text:
एवं सम्भाषमाणं तं रामहेतोर्नृपात्मजम्।
प्रत्युवाच जनः सर्वः श्रीमद् वाक्यमनुत्तमम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: To the above mentioned prince, Bharata, who was talking as aforesaid in the interest of Śrī Rāma, all the counsellors made the following agreeable and excellent reply : (14)

verses.text:
एवं ते भाषमाणस्य पद्मा श्रीरुपतिष्ठताम्।
यस्त्वं ज्येष्ठे नृपसुते पृथिवीं दातुमिच्छसि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Let the Goddess of Fortune, known by the name of Padmā (so-called because She has Her abode in a bed of lotuses), ever be with you, who are speaking in this strain and seek to restore the sovereignty of the globe to the eldest prince, Śrī Rāma !” (15)

verses.text:
अनुत्तमं तद्वचनं नृपात्मजः
प्रभाषितं संश्रवणे निशम्य च।
प्रहर्षजास्तं प्रति बाष्पबिन्दवो
निपेतुरार्यानननेत्रसम्भवाः ॥ १६॥
verses.m: The prince, Bharata, rejoiced to hear the excellent benediction poured by the counsellors into his ears. Nay, teardrops born of excessive delight and gratitude towards them flowed from the eyes of Bharata, whose countenance too was lit up with joy. (16)

verses.text:
ऊचुस्ते वचनमिदं निशम्य हृष्टाः
सामात्याः सपरिषदो वियातशोकाः।
पन्थानं नरवरभक्तिमान् जनश्च
व्यादिष्टस्तव वचनाच्च शिल्पिवर्गः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to hear the aforesaid proposal of Bharata to proceed to the forest to bring back Śrī Rāma to Ayodhyā after consecrating him as king in the forest itself, the counsellors including the ministers as well as those invited to take part in the assembly, found their grief altogether vanished and said, “In obedience to your command, O jewel among men, engineers as well as guards, who are full of devotion to you as well as to Śrī Rāma, have been told off to prepare the way.” (17)

verses.text:
अथ भूमिप्रदेशज्ञाः सूत्रकर्मविशारदाः।
स्वकर्माभिरताः शूराः खनका यन्त्रकास्तथा॥ १॥
कर्मान्तिकाः स्थपतयः पुरुषा यन्त्रकोविदाः।
तथा वर्धकयश्चैव मार्गिणो वृक्षतक्षकाः॥ २॥
सूपकाराः सुधाकारा वंशचर्मकृतस्तथा।
समर्था ये च द्रष्टारः पुरतश्च प्रतस्थिरे॥ ३॥
verses.m: Now men expert in divining the presence of subterranean water in a given plot of land, those adept in designing buildings, pavilions etc., gallant men vigilant in their duty (of guarding the roadways), workmen expert in sinking wells and digging tunnels etc., mechanics contriving devices for crossing streams etc., or obstructing the flow of water, paid labourers, architects, men expert in making catapults etc., even so carpenters, those entrusted with the duty of clearing or guarding the way, hewers of trees and cooks, men expert in plastering and whitewashing etc., those preparing mats and winnowing fans etc., from bamboos and making articles of leather such as saddles, and capable guides set forth in advance. (1—3)

verses.text:
स तु हर्षात् तमुद्देशं जनौघो विपुलः प्रयान्।
अशोभत महावेगः सागरस्येव पर्वणि॥ ४॥
verses.m: Marching with joy to the region where Śrī Rāma was sojourning, that huge multitude of men really shone like a great upsurge of the ocean on a full moon. (4)

verses.text:
ते स्ववारं समास्थाय वर्त्मकर्मणि कोविदाः।
करणैर्विविधोपेतैः पुरस्तात् सम्प्रतस्थिरे॥ ५॥
verses.m: Seeking the company of their own confreres, men skilled in constructing roads etc., marched ahead with implements of various kinds. (5)

verses.text:
लता वल्लीश्च गुल्मांश्च स्थाणूनश्मन एव च।
जनास्ते चक्रिरे मार्गं छिन्दन्तो विविधान् द्रुमान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Removing boughs of trees as well as creepers and shrubs, stumps and rocks too and cutting down trees of every description that obstructed the way, those men hewed out a path. (6)

verses.text:
अवृक्षेषु च देशेषु केचिद् वृक्षानरोपयन्।
केचित् कुठारैष्टङ्कैश्च दात्रैश्छिन्दन् क्वचित् क्वचित्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Nay, some men raised trees in treeless areas for providing shade; while others hewed the existing ones here and there by means of axes, hatchets and sickles. (7)

verses.text:
अपरे वीरणस्तम्बान् बलिनो बलवत्तराः।
विधमन्ति स्म दुर्गाणि स्थलानि च ततस्ततः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Still others, who were stronger than the rest, tore by the roots with their own hands tufts of Vīraṇa grass (a fragrant grass), that had got firmly rooted, and levelled uneven stretches of land at different places. (8)

verses.text:
अपरेऽपूरयन् कूपान् पांसुभिः श्वभ्रमायतम्।
निम्नभागांस्तथैवाशु समांश्चक्रुः समन्ततः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Others filled waterless wells covered with grass etc., that fell on the way, as well as extensive pits with earth. Similarly, they levelled low-lying lands all round in no time. (9)

verses.text:
बबन्धुर्बन्धनीयांश्च क्षोद्यान् संचुक्षुदुस्तथा।
बिभिदुर्भेदनीयांश्च तांस्तान् देशान् नरास्तदा॥ १०॥
verses.m: On that occasion the workmen bridged the streams that could be bridged, and likewise crushed the pebbles etc., that could be crushed and smashed the impediments that obstructed the passage of water and were worth smashing. (10)

verses.text:
अचिरेण तु कालेन परिवाहान् बहूदकान्।
चक्रुर्बहुविधाकारान् सागरप्रतिमान् बहून्॥ ११॥
verses.m: By constructing dams they actually turned in a short time rivulets into many ponds of various sizes and shapes, containing plentiful water and resembling seas. (11)

verses.text:
निर्जलेषु च देशेषु खानयामासुरुत्तमान्।
उदपानान् बहुविधान् वेदिकापरिमण्डितान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Nay, in waterless tracts they caused to be sunk excellent wells of every description embellished with platforms for people to sit on. (12)

verses.text:
ससुधाकुट्टिमतलः प्रपुष्पितमहीरुहः।
मत्तोद्घुष्टद्विजगणः पताकाभिरलंकृतः॥ १३॥
चन्दनोदकसंसिक्तो नानाकुसुमभूषितः।
बह्वशोभत सेनायाः पन्थाः सुरपथोपमः॥ १४॥
verses.m: The highway carved out for the army to pass along was paved with concrete mixed with lime and lined with trees laden with blossoms. Flocks of birds excited with sexual passion and giving out shrill cries were seen on those trees and the road was also decorated with buntings. The road, which was sprinkled with water mixed with sandal-paste, and adorned with flowers of various kinds, looked most charming like a pathway of gods. (13-14)

verses.text:
आज्ञाप्याथ यथाज्ञप्ति युक्तास्तेऽधिकृता नराः।
रमणीयेषु देशेषु बहुस्वादुफलेषु च॥ १५॥
यो निवेशस्त्वभिप्रेतो भरतस्य महात्मनः।
भूयस्तं शोभयामासुर्भूषाभिर्भूषणोपमम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Nay, having given orders to the workers to fix tents etc., as enjoined by Bharata, the aforesaid officers entrusted with the work of fixing tents etc., who were all alert, got tents pitched forthwith in delightful areas abounding in luscious fruits. They further adorned with decorations the tent which was liked by the high-souled Bharata and in itself resembled an ornament. (15-16)

verses.text:
नक्षत्रेषु प्रशस्तेषु मुहूर्तेषु च तद्विदः।
निवेशान् स्थापयामासुर्भरतस्य महात्मनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: The knowers of the science of architecture consecrated the camps erected for the high-souled Bharata at auspicious hours on days when the stars were propitious. (17)

verses.text:
बहुपांसुचयाश्चापि परिखाः परिवारिताः।
तत्रेन्द्रनीलप्रतिमाः प्रतोलीवरशोभिताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Many heaps of earth were raised and moats too excavated round these camps. Enclosed by those moats stood tents containing images of sapphire and adorned with excellent lanes. (18)

verses.text:
प्रासादमालासंयुक्ताः सौधप्राकारसंवृताः।
पताकाशोभिताः सर्वे सुनिर्मितमहापथाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Accompanied by rows of temples, the camps were bounded by enclosures whitewashed with lime. They were all decorated with buntings and divided by well-designed roads. (19)

verses.text:
विसर्पद्भिरिवाकाशे विटङ्काग्रविमानकैः।
समुच्छ्रितैर्निवेशास्ते बभुः शक्रपुरोपमाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Standing side by side with seven storeyed mansions, the tops of which were provided with dove-cots and which flew about, as it were, in the air, the said camps shone like so many capitals of Indra. (20)

verses.text:
जाह्नवीं तु समासाद्य विविधद्रुमकाननाम्।
शीतलामलपानीयां महामीनसमाकुलाम्॥ २१॥
सचन्द्रतारागणमण्डितं यथा
नभः क्षपायाममलं विराजते।
नरेन्द्रमार्गः स तदा व्यराजत
क्रमेण रम्यः शुभशिल्पिनिर्मितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Extending up to the bank of the holy Gaṅgā (foster-daughter of King Jahnu)—which was hemmed in with forests consisting of trees of every description, was full of cool and limpid waters and infested with large fishes—that delightful road, constructed in gradual stages by capable engineers, looked very charming at that time even as a cloudless sky adorned with a host of stars accompanied by the moon during the night. (21-22)

verses.text:
ततो नान्दीमुखीं रात्रिं भरतं सूतमागधाः।
तुष्टुवुः सविशेषज्ञाः स्तवैर्मङ्गलसंस्तवैः॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing the night preceding the Nāndīmukha* and other festal ceremonies (proposed to be performed by Vasiṣṭha preliminary to Bharata’s coronation the following morning) approaching its end, the bards and panegyrists well-versed in eulogizing kings and princes on special occasions extolled Bharata by means of benedictory encomia. (1)

verses.text:
सुवर्णकोणाभिहतः प्राणदद्यामदुन्दुभिः।
दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च शतशो वाद्यांश्चोच्चावचस्वरान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Struck with a gold stick, the drum which was beaten at regular hours to notify the end of every quarter of the day sounded loudly. Nay, the servants blew conches and sounded hundreds of musical instruments of various pitches. (2)

verses.text:
स तूर्यघोषः सुमहान् दिवमापूरयन्निव।
भरतं शोकसंतप्तं भूयः शोकैररन्धयत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Filling the space on all sides, as it were, that very loud sound of musical instruments further oppressed with grief Bharata, who was already tormented with grief. (3)

verses.text:
ततः प्रबुद्धो भरतस्तं घोषं संनिवर्त्य च।
नाहं राजेति चोक्त्वा तं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Causing that music to be completely stopped the moment he was roused as a result of it, and saying that he was not the ruler, spoke to the celebrated Śatrughna as follows : (4)

verses.text:
पश्य शत्रुघ्न कैकेय्या लोकस्यापकृतं महत्।
विसृज्य मयि दुःखानि राजा दशरथो गतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “See, O Śatrughna, the great wrong that has been done to the world by Kaikeyī. And leaving a legacy of sufferings to my share, King Daśaratha too has departed from this world. (5)

verses.text:
तस्यैषा धर्मराजस्य धर्ममूला महात्मनः।
परिभ्रमति राजश्रीर्नौरिवाकर्णिका जले॥ ६॥
verses.m: “This royal fortune, rooted in righteousness, of that high-souled monarch, who was an embodiment of piety, is drifting like a boat without a pilot in water. (6)

verses.text:
यो हि नः सुमहान् नाथः सोऽपि प्रव्राजितो वने।
अनया धर्ममुत्सृज्य मात्रा मे राघवः स्वयम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Even the celebrated Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who was undoubtedly our very great protector and lord, has been sent in exile to the forest by this very mother of mine casting righteousness to the winds.” (7)

verses.text:
इत्येवं भरतं वीक्ष्य विलपन्तमचेतनम्।
कृपणा रुरुदुः सर्वाः सुस्वरं योषितस्तदा॥ ८॥
verses.m: Perceiving Bharata lamenting as aforesaid in a distracted state of mind at that critical moment, all the women present in the gynaeceum piteously wailed at the top of their voice. (8)

verses.text:
तथा तस्मिन् विलपति वसिष्ठो राजधर्मवित्।
सभामिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य प्रविवेश महायशाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: While Bharata was wailing as mentioned above, the highly illustrious Sage Vasiṣṭha, who was well-versed in the code of conduct prescribed for kings, entered the court of King Daśaratha (the ruler of the Ikṣwākus). (9)

verses.text:
शातकुम्भमयीं रम्यां मणिहेमसमाकुलाम्।
सुधर्मामिव धर्मात्मा सगणः प्रत्यपद्यत॥ १०॥
verses.m: Accompanied by his host of pupils, the sage, whose mind was given to piety, got into the delightful council-chamber, which was mostly built of gold and studded all over with pearls and precious stones of various kinds and looked like Sudharmā (the court of Indra, the lord of paradise). (10)

verses.text:
स काञ्चनमयं पीठं स्वस्त्यास्तरणसंवृतम्।
अध्यास्त सर्ववेदज्ञो दूताननुशशास च॥ ११॥
verses.m: The sage, who had mastered all the Vedas, occupied a seat of gold covered by a cloth bearing the design of swāstika (denoting good luck), and commanded the messengers as follows: so the tradition goes : (11)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् योधानमात्यान् गणवल्लभान्।
क्षिप्रमानयताव्यग्राः कृत्यमात्ययिकं हि नः॥ १२॥
सराजपुत्रं शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्।
युधाजितं सुमन्त्रं च ये च तत्र हिता जनाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Since there is some urgent business to be disposed of by us, please bring here promptly and quietly Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, warriors, ministers, troop commanders, Śatrughna and the illustrious Bharata with other princes, Yudhājit (one of the chief counsellors, nicknamed Vijaya) and Sumantra as well as all other people who are friendly to Bharata.” (12-13)

verses.text:
ततो हलहलाशब्दो महान् समुदपद्यत।
रथैरश्वैर्गजैश्चापि जनानामुपगच्छताम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: A great noise then burst forth from men approaching in chariots as well as on horseback and on elephants. (14)

verses.text:
ततो भरतमायान्तं शतक्रतुमिवामराः।
प्रत्यनन्दन् प्रकृतयो यथा दशरथं तथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: The ministers and counsellors as well as the people cheered Bharata coming to the council-chamber as they used to greet Daśaratha and even as gods would greet Indra (who is believed to have performed a hundred Aśwamedha sacrifices as a condition precedent for his assuming the position of Indra). (15)

verses.text:
ह्रद इव तिमिनागसंवृतः
स्तिमितजलो मणिशङ्खशर्करः।
दशरथसुतशोभिता सभा
सदशरथेव बभूव सा पुरा॥ १६॥
verses.m: Resembling a pool* (in the sea), having still waters and infested with Timis (a kind of fish credited with a length and breadth of many leagues) and sea-elephants and full of gems, conches and dust of gold, the aforesaid court graced with the august presence of Bharata, son of Daśaratha, looked as it did when adorned with the presence of Daśaratha in the past. (16)

verses.text:
तामार्यगणसम्पूर्णां भरतः प्रग्रहां सभाम्।
ददर्श बुद्धिसम्पन्नः पूर्णचन्द्रां निशामिव॥ १॥
verses.m: Bharata, who was rich in intelligence, beheld the aforesaid assembly, full of hosts of worthy men and attended by great souls like Vasiṣṭha and as such resembling a night illumined by a full moon and adorned with other major planets. (1)

verses.text:
आसनानि यथान्यायमार्याणां विशतां तदा।
वस्त्राङ्गरागप्रभया द्योतिता सा सभोत्तमा॥ २॥
verses.m: That eminent gathering was lit up with the splendour of the raiment worn and the pigment painted on the person of the worthies occupying their seats according to their deserts on that occasion. (2)

verses.text:
सा विद्वज्जनसम्पूर्णा सभा सुरुचिरा तथा।
अदृश्यत घनापाये पूर्णचन्द्रेव शर्वरी॥ ३॥
verses.m: That most brilliant conclave looked as charming as a night illumined by a full moon during the autumn marked by the absence of clouds. (3)

verses.text:
राज्ञस्तु प्रकृतीः सर्वाः स सम्प्रेक्ष्य च धर्मवित्।
इदं पुरोहितो वाक्यं भरतं मृदु चाब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Looking intently on and reading the mind of all the king’s ministers and the people present there, the said Vasiṣṭha (the family-priest of the rulers of Ayodhyā), for his part, who knew what was right, spoke as follows and gently too to Bharata : (4)

verses.text:
तात राजा दशरथः स्वर्गतो धर्ममाचरन्।
धनधान्यवतीं स्फीतां प्रदाय पृथिवीं तव॥ ५॥
verses.m: “King Daśaratha, my child, has ascended to heaven practising virtue (in the form of redeeming his plighted word) and bequeathing the sovereignty of the prosperous earth, full of gold and foodgrains, to you. (5)

verses.text:
रामस्तथा सत्यवृत्तिः सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्।
नाजहात् पितुरादेशं शशी ज्योत्स्नामिवोदितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Bearing in mind the duty of virtuous souls, viz., obeying the command of their parents, Śrī Rāma, who is truthful of conduct like his father, did not disregard the command of his father any more than the risen moon quits the moonlight. (6)

verses.text:
पित्रा भ्रात्रा च ते दत्तं राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्।
तद् भुङ् क्ष्व मुदितामात्यः क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचय॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Sovereignty with all its thorns completely removed has been conferred on you by your father and elder brother. Assisted by ministers, who are all pleased with you, enjoy it and quickly get yourself consecrated for the coronation. (7)

verses.text:
उदीच्याश्च प्रतीच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च केवलाः।
कोट्यापरान्ताः सामुद्रा रत्नान्युपहरन्तु ते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Let the rulers of the north and the west as well as of the south and the east and the kings of the western borders near the Sahya mountains, who are without a throne and, therefore, not enjoying sovereign rights, as well as seafaring traders bring countless jewels as offerings to you.” (8)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं शोकेनाभिपरिप्लुतः।
जगाम मनसा रामं धर्मज्ञो धर्मकांक्षया॥ ९॥
verses.m: Overwhelmed with grief to hear the aforesaid advice of his family-priest, Bharata, who knew the right course, viz., to restore the kingdom to his elder brother, mentally betook himself to Śrī Rāma with intent to get inspiration from him to do the right thing in the shape of waiting as a servant on his elder brother rather than superseding his claim to the throne. (9)

verses.text:
सबाष्पकलया वाचा कलहंसस्वरो युवा।
विललाप सभामध्ये जगर्हे च पुरोहितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: In a voice choked with tears, the prince, who was in the prime of his youth and therefore incapable of renunciation, lamented as follows in the open assembly in tones resembling the cackling of a swan and reproached his family-priest for his unjust advice and offering the kingship to a cruel and unrighteous fellow like himself : (10)

verses.text:
चरितब्रह्मचर्यस्य विद्यास्नातस्य धीमतः।
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य को राज्यं मद्विधो हरेत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “What sensible and knowing man like me can usurp the kingdom of a sagacious prince, like Śrī Rāma, who has duly studied the Vedas with a vow of celibacy in the house of a teacher and gone through the ceremony of lustration after completing his studies and is applying himself to the practice of virtue in the shape of redeeming the plighted word of his father? (11)

verses.text:
कथं दशरथाज्जातो भवेद् राज्यापहारकः।
राज्यं चाहं च रामस्य धर्मं वक्तुमिहार्हसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “How can I, sprung from the loins of Daśaratha, who renounced his very life on being told that Śrī Rāma had not returned to Ayodhyā and had left for the forest, become a usurper of the throne of my elder brother, when not only the throne, but I too belong to Śrī Rāma? Therefore, in this conclave you ought to speak what is right. (12)

verses.text:
ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठश्च धर्मात्मा दिलीपनहुषोपमः।
लब्धुमर्हति काकुत्स्थो राज्यं दशरथो यथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, who is not only the eldest of us all, but the worthiest too, whose mind is intent on piety and who vies in eminence with Dilīpa and Nahuṣa, two most ancient and illustrious representatives of the solar and the lunar dynasty respectively deserves to inherit the kingdom as did Daśaratha in the past. (13)

verses.text:
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यं कुर्यां पापमहं यदि।
इक्ष्वाकूणामहं लोके भवेयं कुलपांसनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “If I perpetrate this sin of superseding the claims of my elder brother, which is resorted to only by unworthy men and does not lead to heaven, I shall bring disgrace to the line of Ikṣwāku in the world. (14)

verses.text:
यद्धि मात्रा कृतं पापं नाहं तदपि रोचये।
इहस्थो वनदुर्गस्थं नमस्यामि कृताञ्जलिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I do not even approve of, much less be a party to, the sinful act in the shape of disinheriting and banishing Śrī Rāma that has actually been committed by my mother. That is why even though present here, I salute with folded hands Śrī Rāma sojourning in a forest region difficult of access. (15)

verses.text:
राममेवानुगच्छामि स राजा द्विपदां वरः।
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां राघवो राज्यमर्हति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I shall, therefore, follow Śrī Rāma alone. Being the foremost of men, he alone is the ruler of this kingdom. Nay, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, deserves the sovereignty even of all the three worlds (viz., earth, heaven and the intermediate region).” (16)

verses.text:
तद्वाक्यं धर्मसंयुक्तं श्रुत्वा सर्वे सभासदः।
हर्षान्मुमुचुरश्रूणि रामे निहितचेतसः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid reply, which was in full accord with righteousness, all those who sat in the assembly shed tears through joy, their mind being absorbed in Śrī Rāma. (17)

verses.text:
यदि त्वार्यं न शक्ष्यामि विनिवर्तयितुं वनात्।
वने तत्रैव वत्स्यामि यथार्यो लक्ष्मणस्तथा॥ १८॥
verses.m: “If, however, Bharata continued, I do not succeed in bringing my elder brother back from the forest, I shall continue in that forest itself in the same way as the noble Lakṣmaṇa is doing. (18)

verses.text:
सर्वोपायं तु वर्तिष्ये विनिवर्तयितुं बलात्।
समक्षमार्यमिश्राणां साधूनां गुणवर्तिनाम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “In the presence of the honourable members of this assembly, who are all impartial and practise good virtues, I for my part shall try every means to bring him back forcibly. (19)

verses.text:
विष्टिकर्मान्तिकाः सर्वे मार्गशोधकदक्षकाः।
प्रस्थापिता मया पूर्वं यात्रा च मम रोचते॥ २०॥
verses.m: “All expert road-workers working on or without wages, have already been despatched by me. Hence journeying to the forest alone finds favour with me.” (20)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः।
समीपस्थमुवाचेदं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रकोविदम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus, the pious-minded Bharata for his part who was so fond of his elder brother, spoke as follows to Sumantra, who sat near him and was accomplished in giving counsel : (21)

verses.text:
तूर्णमुत्थाय गच्छ त्वं सुमन्त्र मम शासनात्।
यात्रामाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं बलं चैव समानय॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Getting up at once, O Sumantra, depart you under my command and issue orders to all to proceed on a journey to the place where Śrī Rāma may be and quickly send out the army too.” (22)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः सुमन्त्रस्तु भरतेन महात्मना।
प्रहृष्टः सोऽदिशत् सर्वं यथासंदिष्टमिष्टवत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Sumantra for his part felt highly rejoiced when commanded in the foregoing words by the high-souled Bharata. He communicated to all everything as instructed by Bharata as something welcome. (23)

verses.text:
ताः प्रहृष्टाः प्रकृतयो बलाध्यक्षा बलस्य च।
श्रुत्वा यात्रां समाज्ञप्तां राघवस्य निवर्तने॥ २४॥
verses.m: The citizens present in the assembly as well as the generals were immensely delighted to hear of the departure to the forest of the army duly ordered by Bharata with the object of bringing Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā. (24)

verses.text:
ततो योधाङ्गनाः सर्वा भर्तॄन् सर्वान् गृहे गृहे।
यात्रागमनमाज्ञाय त्वरयन्ति स्म हर्षिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Delighted to know of the expedition of the army on a pilgrimage to the forest to bring back Śrī Rāma, all the wives of soldiers thereupon urged, in their eagerness to see Śrī Rāma and others back in Ayodhyā, all the husbands in their own homes to make haste to depart. (25)

verses.text:
ते हयैर्गोरथैः शीघ्रं स्यन्दनैश्च मनोजवैः।
सह योषिद्बलाध्यक्षा बलं सर्वमचोदयन्॥ २६॥
verses.m: The aforesaid generals urged the entire army to march quickly with the womenfolk, on horseback, in bullockcarts as well as in chariots quick as thought. (26)

verses.text:
सज्जं तु तद् बलं दृष्ट्वा भरतो गुरुसंनिधौ।
रथं मे त्वरयस्वेति सुमन्त्रं पार्श्वतोऽब्रवीत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Seeing that army ready to depart, Bharata for his part said to Sumantra, standing by his side, in the presence of his preceptor Sage Vasiṣṭha, “Get my chariot ready soon.” (27)

verses.text:
भरतस्य तु तस्याज्ञां परिगृह्य प्रहर्षितः।
रथं गृहीत्वोपययौ युक्तं परमवाजिभिः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Bowing to the command of the celebrated Bharata and taking a chariot driven by excellent horses, Sumantra for his part approached him, highly delighted at the prospect of meeting Śrī Rāma and others as well as of their returning to Ayodhyā. (28)

verses.text:
स राघवः सत्यधृतिः प्रतापवान्
ब्रुवन् सुयुक्तं दृढसत्यविक्रमः।
गुरुं महारण्यगतं यशस्विनं
प्रसादयिष्यन् भरतोऽब्रवीत् तदा॥ २९॥
verses.m: Intending to undertake a journey to persuade his illustrious elder brother Śrī Rāma, staying in a dreary forest viz., the Daṇḍaka, to return to Ayodhyā by arguing with him in a well-reasoned way, that glorious scion of Raghu, Bharata of unfailing firmness and unflinching veracity and prowess, spoke on that occasion as follows : (29)

verses.text:
तूर्णं त्वमुत्थाय सुमन्त्र गच्छ
बलस्य योगाय बलप्रधानान्।
आनेतुमिच्छामि हि तं वनस्थं
प्रसाद्य रामं जगतो हिताय॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Getting up promptly, O Sumantra, approach you the generals of the army in order to get them equip the forces for the journey; for, propitiating Śrī Rāma residing in the forest, I intend to bring him back to Ayodhyā for the good of the world.” (30)

verses.text:
स सूतपुत्रो भरतेन सम्य-
गाज्ञापितः सम्परिपूर्णकामः।
शशास सर्वान् प्रकृतिप्रधानान्
बलस्य मुख्यांश्च सुहृज्जनं च॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Commanded as above by Bharata and accounting thereby his ambition of seeing Śrī Rāma fully realized, Sumantra duly issued orders accordingly to all the leading citizens and army chiefs as well as to the friends and relations of Bharata. (31)

verses.text:
ततः समुत्थाय कुले कुले ते
राजन्यवैश्या वृषलाश्च विप्राः।
अयूयुजन्नुष्ट्ररथान् खरांश्च
नागान् हयांश्चैव कुलप्रसूतान्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Springing on their feet in great eagerness, people from every house—Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas, Śūdras and Brāhmaṇas—thereupon got ready for the journey camels and chariots, donkeys and elephants, as well as horses of excellent breed. (32)

verses.text:
ततः समुत्थितः कल्यमास्थाय स्यन्दनोत्तमम्।
प्रययौ भरतः शीघ्रं रामदर्शनकाम्यया॥ १॥
verses.m: Having got up from sleep at daybreak, and mounting an excellent chariot, Bharata forthwith departed with expedition with a longing to see Śrī Rāma. (1)

verses.text:
अग्रतः प्रययुस्तस्य सर्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहिताः।
अधिरुह्य हयैर्युक्तान् रथान् सूर्यरथोपमान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Mounting chariots drawn by horses and vying with the chariot of the sun-god, all the counsellors and family-priests drove ahead of him. (2)

verses.text:
नवनागसहस्राणि कल्पितानि यथाविधि।
अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Nine thousand elephants duly caparisoned followed Bharata, the delight of Ikṣwākus race, even as he moved on. (3)

verses.text:
षष्ठी रथसहस्राणि धन्विनो विविधायुधाः।
अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तं राजपुत्रं यशस्विनम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Sixty thousand chariots with archers armed with varied weapons seated in them followed the illustrious Prince Bharata (next) as he advanced. (4)

verses.text:
शतं सहस्राण्यश्वानां समारूढानि राघवम्।
अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तं राजपुत्रं यशस्विनम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: A hundred thousand horses mounted by cavaliers followed Prince Bharata, an illustrious scion of Raghu, as he proceeded along. (5)

verses.text:
कैकेयी च सुमित्रा च कौसल्या च यशस्विनी।
रामानयनसंतुष्टा ययुर्यानेन भास्वता॥ ६॥
verses.m: Kaikeyī and Sumitrā and the illustrious Kausalyā too, who were highly gratified by the thought of bringing Śrī Rāma back from the forest drove in a splendid chariot each. (6)

verses.text:
प्रयाताश्चार्यसंघाता रामं द्रष्टुं सलक्ष्मणम्।
तस्यैव च कथाश्चित्राः कुर्वाणा हृष्टमानसाः॥ ७॥
मेघश्यामं महाबाहुं स्थिरसत्त्वं दृढव्रतम्।
कदा द्रक्ष्यामहे रामं जगतः शोकनाशनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hosts of members of the twice-born classes also set out with a delighted mind in order to be able to see Śrī Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā and saying various things about him alone in the following strain : “When shall we be able to behold the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, dark-brown as a cloud, stable of mind and firm of resolve, the dispeller of the grief of the world? (7-8)

verses.text:
दृष्ट एव हि नः शोकमपनेष्यति राघवः।
तमः सर्वस्य लोकस्य समुद्यन्निव भास्करः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “As the sun disperses the darkness of the whole world even while fully appearing in the horizon, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, will surely dispel our grief the moment he is seen by us.” (9)

verses.text:
इत्येवं कथयन्तस्ते सम्प्रहृष्टाः कथाः शुभाः।
परिष्वजानाश्चान्योन्यं ययुर्नागरिकास्तदा॥ १०॥
verses.m: Saying many good things as mentioned above on that occasion and hugging one another, highly rejoiced as they were over the prospect of being able to see Śrī Rāma, the citizens went forth to meet Śrī Rāma. (10)

verses.text:
ये च तत्रापरे सर्वे सम्मता ये च नैगमाः।
रामं प्रतिययुर्हृष्टाः सर्वाः प्रकृतयः शुभाः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Those merchants who were held in great esteem in Ayodhyā and all others who were not so honoured and, even so, all other good citizens joyously proceeded to meet Śrī Rāma. (11)

verses.text:
मणिकाराश्च ये केचित् कुम्भकाराश्च शोभनाः।
सूत्रकर्मविशेषज्ञा ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः॥ १२॥
मायूरकाः क्राकचिका वेधका रोचकास्तथा।
दन्तकाराः सुधाकारा ये च गन्धोपजीविनः॥ १३॥
सुवर्णकाराः प्रख्यातास्तथा कम्बलकारकाः।
स्नापकोष्णोदका वैद्या धूपकाः शौण्डिकास्तथा॥ १४॥
रजकास्तुन्नवायाश्च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः।
शैलूषाश्च सह स्त्रीभिर्यान्ति कैवर्तकास्तथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: Whatever lapidaries there were in the city and skilled potters, those adept in weaving and those who lived by manufacture of arms, those who made fans etc., of peacock-feathers, those who lived by the saw, those who pierced gems and pearls etc., as well as polishers of gems, ornaments and utensils etc., those who made articles of ivory, those who prepared lime by burning limestone etc., and those who lived by perfumery, highly reputed goldsmiths and weavers of blankets and other woollen goods, those who provided baths for others, masseurs, physicians, fumigators and distillers and vintners, washermen and tailors, chiefs of villages and hamlets and dancers with their womenfolk as well as boatmen joined the expedition. (12—15)

verses.text:
समाहिता वेदविदो ब्राह्मणा वृत्तसम्मताः।
गोरथैर्भरतं यान्तमनुजग्मुः सहस्रशः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Brāhmaṇas remaining absorbed in meditation, well-versed in the Vedas and highly respected for their conduct followed the departing Bharata in thousands on bullockcarts, etc. (16)

verses.text:
सुवेषाः शुद्धवसनास्ताम्रमृष्टानुलेपिनः।
सर्वे ते विविधैर्यानैः शनैर्भरतमन्वयुः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Decently dressed, clad in pure raiment and having smeared their body with sandal-paste mixed with red substances like saffron, they all followed slowly in the wake of Bharata on various kinds of vehicles. (17)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टमुदिता सेना सान्वयात् कैकयीसुतम्।
भ्रातुरानयने यातं भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Thrilled with joy and delighted in mind, the aforesaid army too followed Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, who was so fond of his elder brother and set out on the mission of bringing his said brother back from the forest. (18)

verses.text:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं रथयानाश्वकुञ्जरैः।
समासेदुस्ततो गङ्गां शृङ्गवेरपुरं प्रति॥ १९॥
यत्र रामसखा वीरो गुहो ज्ञातिगणैर्वृतः।
निवसत्यप्रमादेन देशं तं परिपालयन्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Having covered a long distance from Ayodhyā in chariots, on palanquins and on the back of horses and elephants, they reached the bank of the holy Gaṅgā in the precincts of Śṛṅgaverapura, where dwelt the valiant Guha, a friend of Śrī Rāma, surrounded by hosts of his kinsmen and ruling that area with vigilance. (19-20)

verses.text:
उपेत्य तीरं गङ्गायाश्चक्रवाकैरलंकृतम्।
व्यवतिष्ठत सा सेना भरतस्यानुयायिनी॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having arrived at the bank of the Gaṅgā, adorned by Cakrawāka birds, that army following in the wake of Bharata halted. (21)

verses.text:
निरीक्ष्यानुत्थितां सेनां तां च गङ्गां शिवोदकाम्।
भरतः सचिवान् सर्वानब्रवीद् वाक्यकोविदः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Seeing the aforesaid army inactive and beholding the Gaṅgā with its holy waters, Bharata, who was a master of expression, spoke to all his ministers as follows : (22)

verses.text:
निवेशयत मे सैन्यमभिप्रायेण सर्वतः।
विश्रान्ताः प्रतरिष्यामः श्व इमां सागरङ्गमाम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Let my army encamp at will on all sides. Having taken rest today we shall cross this sea-bound river tomorrow. (23)

verses.text:
दातुं च तावदिच्छामि स्वर्गतस्य महीपतेः।
और्ध्वदेहनिमित्तार्थमवतीर्योदकं नदीम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “In the meantime, descending into the river, I wish to offer libations of water to the spirit of the emperor, my father, who has ascended to heaven, for happiness in his life after death.” (24)

verses.text:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतोऽमात्यास्तथेत्युक्त्वा समाहिताः।
न्यवेशयंस्तांश्छन्देन स्वेन स्वेन पृथक् पृथक्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Saying “Amen” to Bharata, who was speaking as above, the ministers, who were all attention, encamped the troops separately, each unit according to its liking. (25)

verses.text:
निवेश्य गङ्गामनु तां महानदीं
चमूं विधानैः परिबर्हशोभिनीम्।
उवास रामस्य तदा महात्मनो
विचिन्तमानो भरतो निवर्तनम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Having caused that army, which looked charming with its equipage in the shape of tents etc., to encamp methodically along the bank of the great river Gaṅgā, Bharata too halted then, reflecting all the time how to bring the high-souled Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā. (26)

verses.text:
ततो निविष्टां ध्वजिनीं गङ्गामन्वाश्रितां नदीम्।
निषादराजो दृष्ट्वैव ज्ञातीन् स परितोऽब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: The moment Guha, the chief of the Niṣādas, saw the army of Bharata encamped along the bank of the river Gaṅgā, he now spoke as follows to his kinsmen sitting around him : (1)

verses.text:
महतीयमितः सेना सागराभा प्रदृश्यते।
नास्यान्तमवगच्छामि मनसापि विचिन्तयन्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Even from this place this huge army appears like a sea. Though pondering deeply, I do not perceive its end even with the mind. (2)

verses.text:
यदा नु खलु दुर्बुद्धिर्भरतः स्वयमागतः।
स एष हि महाकायः कोविदारध्वजो रथे॥ ३॥
बन्धयिष्यति वा पाशैरथ वास्मान् वधिष्यति।
अनु दाशरथिं रामं पित्रा राज्याद् विवासितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “If Bharata—who has surely come in person because here is seen that towering banner bearing the device of a Kovidāra tree on the chariot—has evil intent, he will either cause us to be bound with chains or kill us, who are devoted to Śrī Rāma, the eldest son of Daśaratha, exiled from his kingdom by his father. (3-4)

verses.text:
सम्पन्नां श्रियमन्विच्छंस्तस्य राज्ञः सुदुर्लभाम्।
भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो हन्तुं समधिगच्छति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Seeking to possess the entire fortune of that monarch, Śrī Rāma, which is otherwise most difficult to get, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, has taken it into his head to kill him. (5)

verses.text:
भर्ता चैव सखा चैव रामो दाशरथिर्मम।
तस्यार्थकामाः संनद्धा गङ्गानूपेऽत्र तिष्ठत॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is my lord and friend, too. Therefore, seeking to advance his interests, remain stationed on this bank of the Gaṅgā, clothed with mail. (6)

verses.text:
तिष्ठन्तु सर्वदाशाश्च गङ्गामन्वाश्रिता नदीम्।
बलयुक्ता नदीरक्षा मांसमूलफलाशनाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Let all my ferrymen, accompanied by troops, remain rooted to the bank of the river Gaṅgā, guarding access to the river and living on meat, roots and fruits stored in the boats. (7)

verses.text:
नावां शतानां पञ्चानां कैवर्तानां शतं शतम्।
संनद्धानां तथा यूनां तिष्ठन्त्वित्यभ्यचोदयत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “And let one hundred each youthful fishermen, clothed with mail occupy all of the five hundred boats,” so did Guha issue his commands. (8)

verses.text:
यदि तुष्टस्तु भरतो रामस्येह भविष्यति।
इयं स्वस्तिमती सेना गङ्गामद्य तरिष्यति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “If, however, Bharata proves to be favourably disposed towards Śrī Rāma at this moment, this army will be allowed to cross safely the Gaṅgā today.” (9)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वोपायनं गृह्य मत्स्यमांसमधूनि च।
अभिचक्राम भरतं निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Saying so and taking sugar-candy, the pulp of fruits and honey as an offering, Guha, the chief of the Niṣādas, proceeded to meet Bharata. (10)

verses.text:
तमायान्तं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
भरतायाचचक्षेऽथ समयज्ञो विनीतवत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Vividly perceiving him coming, the glorious Sumantra (the son of a charioteer) for his part, who knew what is called for at a particular time, forthwith spoke to Bharata as follows like a humble servant : (11)

verses.text:
एष ज्ञातिसहस्रेण स्थपतिः परिवारितः।
कुशलो दण्डकारण्ये वृद्धो भ्रातुश्च ते सखा॥ १२॥
तस्मात् पश्यतु काकुत्स्थं त्वां निषादाधिपो गुहः।
असंशयं विजानीते यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Attended by a thousand of his kinsmen, here comes Guha, the sovereign lord of the Niṣādas, who is a senior friend of your elder brother, Śrī Rāma, and is closely acquainted with the Daṇḍaka forest. Therefore, allow him to see you, O scion of Kakutstha ! Doubtless he knows well where the celebrated Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa may be.” (12-13)

verses.text:
एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुमन्त्राद् भरतः शुभम्।
उवाच वचनं शीघ्रं गुहः पश्यतु मामिति॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing this pleasing report from the lips of Sumantra, Bharata for his part made the following reply : “Let Guha see me at once.” (14)

verses.text:
लब्ध्वानुज्ञां सम्प्रहृष्टो ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः।
आगम्य भरतं प्रह्वो गुहो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Immensely rejoiced to receive permission to see the prince and approaching Bharata, Guha, who was surrounded by his kinsmen, meekly submitted as follows : (15)

verses.text:
निष्कुटश्चैव देशोऽयं वञ्चिताश्चापि ते वयम्।
निवेदयाम ते सर्वं स्वके दाशगृहे वस॥ १६॥
verses.m: “This territory is but a pleasure-grove attached to your palace and we have been taken in by our unwariness in failing to know of your visit beforehand (and thus being deprived of an opportunity to receive you in advance). We hereby offer you all that we have; pray, dwell in the house of a ferryman, which is your own. (16)

verses.text:
अस्ति मूलफलं चैतन्निषादैः स्वयमर्जितम्।
आर्द्रं शुष्कं तथा मांसं वन्यं चोच्चावचं तथा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Here are roots and fruits, both green and dried, procured by the Niṣādas (a tribe of fishermen, Guha’s own clansmen) themselves as well as the pulp of fruits and wild cereals of various kinds. (17)

verses.text:
आशंसे स्वाशिता सेना वत्स्यत्येनां विभावरीम्।
अर्चितो विविधैः कामैः श्वः ससैन्यो गमिष्यसि॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I hope the army, being well fed by us, will stay here tonight. Entertained with various objects of enjoyment, you too, I hope, will leave with your army only tomorrow.” (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्।
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंहितम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Spoken to as above, Bharata, for his part, who was exceedingly wise, gave to Guha, the ruler of the Niṣādas, the following reply, which was consonant with reason and purposeful : (1)

verses.text:
ऊर्जितः खलु ते कामः कृतो मम गुरोः सखे।
यो मे त्वमीदृशीं सेनामभ्यर्चयितुमिच्छसि॥ २॥
verses.m: “Indeed your great object of according a right royal reception to me has been accomplished in that you seek to entertain my army of such magnitude, O friend of my elder brother!” (2)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा स महातेजा गुहं वचनमुत्तमम्।
अब्रवीद् भरतः श्रीमान् पन्थानं दर्शयन् पुनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having spoken as above, the said illustrious Bharata, who was possessed of great splendour, once more addressed the following excellently-worded question to Guha, about the way ahead : (3)

verses.text:
कतरेण गमिष्यामि भरद्वाजाश्रमं यथा।
गहनोऽयं भृशं देशो गङ्गानूपो दुरत्ययः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “By which of the two routes appearing before me shall I proceed to the hermitage of Ṛṣi Bharadwāja? This tract of land drained by the Gaṅgā is most thickly set with trees etc., and as such difficult to cross.” (4)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः।
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा गुहो गहनगोचरः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid question of that intelligent prince, Bharata, Guha, who used to roam about in the woods, replied with folded hands as follows : (5)

verses.text:
दाशास्त्वनुगमिष्यन्ति देशज्ञाः सुसमाहिताः।
अहं चानुगमिष्यामि राजपुत्र महाबल॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Ferrymen who are familiar with the region and very attentive will undoubtedly accompany you. I too shall follow you in person, O exceptionally mighty prince ! (6)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न दुष्टो व्रजसि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
इयं ते महती सेना शङ्कां जनयतीव मे॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I hope you are not going with evil intent towards Śrī Rāma, who does great deeds without any exertion? This huge army of yours gives rise to apprehension in my mind, as it were.” (7)

verses.text:
तमेवमभिभाषन्तमाकाश इव निर्मलः।
भरतः श्लक्ष्णया वाचा गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: To the aforesaid Guha, who was talking as above, Bharata, whose heart was absolutely taintless as the sky, replied in sweet words as follows : (8)

verses.text:
मा भूत् स कालो यत् कष्टं न मां शङ्कितुमर्हसि।
राघवः स हि मे भ्राता ज्येष्ठः पितृसमो मतः॥ ९॥
