verses.m: “May that time never come when such wickedness appears in me. You ought not to entertain any misgiving about me; for that scion of Raghu is my elder brother and is esteemed by me as equal to my father. (9)

verses.text:
तं निवर्तयितुं यामि काकुत्स्थं वनवासिनम्।
बुद्धिरन्या न मे कार्या गुह सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I go to bring back Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who is dwelling in the woods. I tell you the bare truth, O Guha ! No other motive should be imputed to me.” (10)

verses.text:
स तु संहृष्टवदनः श्रुत्वा भरतभाषितम्।
पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वाक्यं भरतं प्रति हर्षितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: With his face rendered extremely bright with joy on hearing Bharata’s reply, Guha for his part joyfully spoke once more to Bharata as follows : (11)

verses.text:
धन्यस्त्वं न त्वया तुल्यं पश्यामि जगतीतले।
अयत्नादागतं राज्यं यस्त्वं त्यक्तुमिहेच्छसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Blessed are you. I find none on the surface of this globe equal to you who seek to relinquish a kingdom come to you without any effort on your part ! (12)

verses.text:
शाश्वती खलु ते र्कीतिर्लोकाननु चरिष्यति।
यस्त्वं कृच्छ्रगतं रामं प्रत्यानयितुमिच्छसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Surely your lasting fame will extend to the spheres inasmuch as you wish to bring back to Ayodhyā Śrī Rāma, who has fallen in adversity.” (13)

verses.text:
एवं सम्भाषमाणस्य गुहस्य भरतं तदा।
बभौ नष्टप्रभः सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत॥ १४॥
verses.m: While Guha was conversing thus with Bharata, the sun lost its splendour and night fell. (14)

verses.text:
संनिवेश्य स तां सेनां गुहेन परितोषितः।
शत्रुघ्नेन समं श्रीमाञ्छयनं पुनरागमत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Lodging the said army in camps, and soothed by Guha, the glorious Bharata then went to bed with Śatrughna. (15)

verses.text:
रामचिन्तामयः शोको भरतस्य महात्मनः।
उपस्थितो ह्यनर्हस्य धर्मप्रेक्षस्य तादृशः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Grief born of anxiety for Śrī Rāma and unique of its kind now overtook the high-souled Bharata, whose eyes were fixed on righteousness and who surely did not deserve this mental torture. (16)

verses.text:
अन्तर्दाहेन दहनः संतापयति राघवम्।
वनदाहाग्निसंतप्तं गूढोऽग्निरिव पादपम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Even as a fire hidden in the hollow of a tree burns a tree already scorched by a forest-consuming fire, so did the fire of anxiety for Śrī Rāma inwardly begin to consume Bharata (a scion of Raghu), who was already scorched by the fire of grief caused by his father’s death. (17)

verses.text:
प्रसृतः सर्वगात्रेभ्यः स्वेदं शोकाग्निसम्भवम्।
यथा सूर्यांशुसंतप्तो हिमवान् प्रसृतो हिमम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Bharata began to exude sweat, born of the fire of grief, from all his limbs in the same way as the Himālaya mountain heated by the sun’s rays allows its snow to melt and flow. (18)

verses.text:
ध्याननिर्दरशैलेन विनिःश्वसितधातुना।
दैन्यपादपसंघेन शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा॥ १९॥
प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन संतापौषधिवेणुना।
आक्रान्तो दुःखशैलेन महता कैकयीसुतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, was weighed down by a huge mountain of agony, consisting of a compact mass of rocks in the shape of loving contemplation on Śrī Rāma, which contained minerals in the shape of sighs, was clothed with a cluster of trees in the shape of recoiling of the senses from their objects and was crowned with a tall peak in the shape of languor caused by grief, infested by numberless beasts in the shape of swoons and covered by herbs and bamboos in the shape of burning of the internal and external organs of sense. (19-20)

verses.text:
विनिःश्वसन् वै भृशदुर्मनास्ततः
प्रमूढसंज्ञः परमापदं गतः।
शमं न लेभे हृदयज्वरार्दितो
नरर्षभो यूथहतो यथर्षभः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Like a bull strayed from its herd, Bharata, a jewel among men—who, having really fallen in extreme adversity, felt miserably disconsolate, his mind being utterly confused in consequence, and was heaving sighs, afflicted as he was with anguish of heart—found no peace in his bed. (21)

verses.text:
गुहेन सार्धं भरतः समागतो
महानुभावः सजनः समाहितः।
सुदुर्मनास्तं भरतं तदा पुन-
र्गुहः समाश्वासयदग्रजं प्रति॥ २२॥
verses.m: When the noble-minded Bharata, who, though composed, felt very disconsolate, got united alongwith his men with Guha again, the latter reassured him once more with reference to his elder brother. (22)

verses.text:
आचचक्षेऽथ सद्भावं लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः।
भरतायाप्रमेयाय गुहो गहनगोचरः॥ १॥
verses.m: Guha, who used to roam about in the woods, now reported to Bharata, who was immeasurably great, the praiseworthy attitude of the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa towards his eldest brother : (1)

verses.text:
तं जाग्रतं गुणैर्युक्तं वरचापेषुधारिणम्।
भ्रातृगुप्त्यर्थमत्यन्तमहं लक्ष्मणमब्रुवम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “I spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with excellences of various kinds such as devotion and obedience to his eldest brother, and was keeping vigil for the safety of his eldest brother and his beloved consort, wielding an excellent bow and arrows : (2)

verses.text:
इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता।
प्रत्याश्वसिहि शेष्वास्यां सुखं राघवनन्दन॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Here is a cosy bed prepared for you, O dear brother! Be reassured about the safety of Śrī Rāma and Sītā and repose on it with ease, O delight of Raghu’s race ! (3)

verses.text:
उचितोऽयं जनः सर्वो दुःखानां त्वं सुखोचितः।
धर्मात्मंस्तस्य गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामहे वयम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “All of us, your servants, are used to hardships, while you are deserving of ease. As for Śrī Rāma, we shall keep awake for his safety, O pious-minded prince ! (4)

verses.text:
नहि रामात् प्रियतरो ममास्ति भुवि कश्चन।
मोत्सुको भूर्ब्रवीम्येतदथ सत्यं तवाग्रतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Surely none on earth is dearer to me than Śrī Rāma. No longer be anxious about the safety of your eldest brother and sister-in-law: I tell you this truth in your presence. (5)

verses.text:
अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेऽस्मिन् सुमहद्यशः।
धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थकामौ च केवलौ॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Through his grace I hope to acquire very great renown in this world and to earn religious merit in abundance as well as wealth and enjoyment free from blemish. (6)

verses.text:
सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया।
रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणिः सर्वैः स्वैर्ज्ञातिभिः सह॥ ७॥
verses.m: “As such I shall guard, bow in hand, with all my kinsmen, my beloved friend, Śrī Rāma, reposing with Sītā. (7)

verses.text:
नहि मेऽविदितं किंचिद् वनेऽस्मिंश्चरतः सदा।
चतुरङ्गं ह्यपि बलं प्रसहेम वयं युधि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Surely there is nothing unknown in this forest to me, who constantly roam about in it. In fact, we can withstand here even an army consisting of all the four limbs on the field of battle. (8)

verses.text:
एवमस्माभिरुक्तेन लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना।
अनुनीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Spoken to by us as aforesaid, the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, who kept righteousness alone in view, politely replied to us all in the following words : (9)

verses.text:
कथं दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया।
शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितानि सुखानि वा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “ ‘How can sleep be had, or even life or comforts be enjoyed by me when Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is reposing on the ground with Sītā? (10)

verses.text:
यो न देवासुरैः सर्वैः शक्यः प्रसहितुं युधि।
तं पश्य गुह संविष्टं तृणेषु सह सीतया॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘Behold, O Guha, stretched on blades of grass with Sītā, he who cannot be withstood on the field of battle by all the gods and demons gathered together ! (11)

verses.text:
महता तपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च परिश्रमैः।
एको दशरथस्यैष पुत्रः सदृशलक्षणः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘This peerless son of Daśaratha, possessing characteristics like unto his own, was secured by virtue of great austerities and through exertions in the shape of sacrificial undertakings of various kinds. (12)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् प्रव्राजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति।
विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘He having been exiled, the king will not survive long and Mother Earth will surely be widowed soon enough. (13)

verses.text:
विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः।
निर्घोषो विरतो नूनमद्य राजनिवेशने॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Nay, having uttered a very loud cry consequent on the emperor’s death, which must already have occurred, the women must have ceased crying because of exertion; and the great noise in the palace must have surely died out by this time. (14)

verses.text:
कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम।
नाशंसे यदि ते सर्वे जीवेयुः शर्वरीमिमाम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘I do not expect that mother Kausalyā and the king and, even so, my own mother, Sumitrā—all these will survive till this night. (15)

verses.text:
जीवेदपि च मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया।
दुःखिता या हि कौसल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Even if my mother survives in expectation of the return of Śatrughna, the afflicted Kausalyā, who has given birth to a hero like Śrī Rāma, will surely die. (16)

verses.text:
अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्।
राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Failing to install Śrī Rāma on the throne of Ayodhyā and thus without realizing his long cherished ambition, my father will expire exclaiming “Everything is past and gone !’’ (17)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन् काले ह्युपस्थिते।
प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति भूमिपम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Accomplished of purpose indeed are they who will, when the time comes for it, consecrate my father, the deceased emperor, in the course of all the funeral rites. (18)

verses.text:
रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्।
हर्म्यप्रासादसम्पन्नां सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम्॥ १९॥
गजाश्वरथसम्बाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्।
सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्॥ २०॥
आरामोद्यानसम्पूर्णां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्।
सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘And happy are they who will, in the event of my father’s survival, move about in the capital of my father, the cross-roads of which are located in beautiful spots, whose main roads are clearly defined, which is richly endowed with mansions as well as with temples and palaces and adorned with all sorts of precious things, which is crowded with elephants, horses and chariots and made resonant by the sound of clarionets, which is full of all blessings and peopled by joyous and well-fed men and women, and which is rich in gardens and pleasances and looks charming with a series of festivals. (19—21)

verses.text:
अपि सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयम्।
निवृत्ते समये ह्यस्मिन् सुखिताः प्रविशेमहि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘When this term of exile is actually over, shall we Sītā and myself happily return to Ayodhyā alongwith Śrī Rāma, who shall have safely redeemed his word?’ (22)

verses.text:
परिदेवयमानस्य तस्यैवं हि महात्मनः।
तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी सात्यवर्तत॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Even while that high-souled prince, Lakṣmaṇa, who remained sitting all the while, was lamenting as aforesaid, that night actually slipped away. (23)

verses.text:
प्रभाते विमले सूर्ये कारयित्वा जटा उभौ।
अस्मिन् भागीरथीतीरे सुखं संतारितौ मया॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Next morning, when a cloudless sun appeared in the sky, both the brothers alongwith Sītā were safely ferried by me across the stream after helping them in entangling their locks into a mass of hair as ascetics do, on this very bank of the Gaṅgā. (24)

verses.text:
जटाधरौ तौ द्रुमचीरवाससौ
महाबलौ कुञ्जरयूथपोपमौ।
वरेषुधीचापधरौ परंतपौ
व्यपेक्षमाणौ सह सीतया गतौ॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Wearing matted locks and attired in the bark of trees, nay, wielding an excellent quiver and bow each and looking all round to scan the beauty of the landscape, the two princes, who were possessed of extraordinary strength and looked like a pair of lordly elephants, and were capable of tormenting their enemy, departed with Sītā.” (25)

verses.text:
गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतो भृशमप्रियम्।
ध्यानं जगाम तत्रैव यत्र तच्छ्रुतमप्रियम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the report of Guha about Śrī Rāma’s matted locks of hair, which was most disagreeable to hear, Bharata began to think deeply of Śrī Rāma alone, of whom that unpleasant news was heard by him as it made him apprehensive that Śrī Rāma might not return to Ayodhyā now that he had entangled his hair into a mass. (1)

verses.text:
सुकुमारो महासत्त्वः सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः।
पुण्डरीकविशालाक्षस्तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः॥ २॥
प्रत्याश्वस्य मुहूर्तं तु कालं परमदुर्मनाः।
ससाद सहसा तोत्रैर्हृदि विद्ध इव द्विपः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having remained composed awhile, the mightly-armed prince, Bharata, for his part—who, though tender of body, was possessed of extraordinary strength, whose shoulders resembled a lion’s and who had eyes big as a lotus, and who was both young and pleasing of appearance—suddenly sank to the ground extremely sad at heart, like an elephant pierced with goads. (2-3)

verses.text:
भरतं मूर्च्छितं दृष्ट्वा विवर्णवदनो गुहः।
बभूव व्यथितस्तत्र भूमिकम्पे यथा द्रुमः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing Bharata unconscious, Guha felt shaken at that time like a tree during an earthquake, and his face grew pale. (4)

verses.text:
तदवस्थं तु भरतं शत्रुघ्नोऽनन्तरस्थितः।
परिष्वज्य रुरोदोच्चैर्विसंज्ञः शोककर्शितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Embracing Bharata, lying in that unconscious state, Śatrughna, for his part, who stood nearby, got non-plussed, stricken as he was with grief, and loudly cried. (5)

verses.text:
ततः सर्वाः समापेतुर्मातरो भरतस्य ताः।
उपवासकृशा दीना भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Then rushed together all the mothers of Bharata. They were emaciated through fasting, looked miserable and felt afflicted due to separation from their husband. (6)

verses.text:
ताश्च तं पतितं भूमौ रुदत्यः पर्यवारयन्।
कौसल्या त्वनुसृत्यैनं दुर्मनाः परिषस्वजे॥ ७॥
verses.m: Nay, shedding tears they surrounded Bharata fallen on the ground. Approaching him sad at heart, Kausalyā for her part hugged him. (7)

verses.text:
वत्सला स्वं यथा वत्समुपगुह्य तपस्विनी।
परिपप्रच्छ भरतं रुदती शोकलालसा॥ ८॥
verses.m: Pressing him to her bosom as a cow does its own calf, that exceedingly thoughtful lady, who was totally given up to grief, questioned Bharata in the following words, shedding tears all the time : (8)

verses.text:
पुत्र व्याधिर्न ते कच्चिच्छरीरं प्रति बाधते।
अस्य राजकुलस्याद्य त्वदधीनं हि जीवितम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I hope no ailment of any kind afflicts your body. In fact, the life of this entire royal household hinges on you. (9)

verses.text:
त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुत्र जीवामि रामे सभ्रातृके गते।
वृत्ते दशरथे राज्ञि नाथ एकस्त्वमद्य नः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Looking on you alone, my son, do I survive. Rāma with his brother, Lakṣmaṇa, having left for the forest and King Daśaratha, your father, having expired, you alone are our protector today. (10)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न लक्ष्मणे पुत्र श्रुतं ते किंचिदप्रियम्।
पुत्रे वा ह्येकपुत्रायाः सहभार्ये वनं गते॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I hope nothing unwelcome has been heard by you regarding Lakṣmaṇa or my own son, Rāma—I having only one son, who has proceeded to the forest with his consort.” (11)

verses.text:
स मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य रुदन्नेव महायशाः।
कौसल्यां परिसान्त्व्येदं गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Returning to his normal self after an hour or so, and consoling Kausalyā with the assurance that nothing unwelcome had been heard with reference to Lakṣmaṇa or Śrī Rāma, Bharata, the highly illustrious prince, spoke weeping all the same to Guha as follows : (12)

verses.text:
भ्राता मे क्वावसद् रात्रौ क्व सीता क्व च लक्ष्मणः।
अस्वपच्छयने कस्मिन् किं भुक्त्वा गुह शंस मे॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Where did my elder brother, Śrī Rāma, stay during the night? Where did Sītā spend the night and where Lakṣmaṇa? On what kind of bed and eating what did he repose? Tell me this, O Guha !’’ (13)

verses.text:
सोऽब्रवीद् भरतं हृष्टो निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः।
यद्विधं प्रतिपेदे च रामे प्रियहितेऽतिथौ॥ १४॥
verses.m: Questioned thus, Guha, the ruler of the Niṣādas, thereupon joyfully told Bharata in the following words what kind of arrangement he had made for feeding and reposing his beloved and kind guest : (14)

verses.text:
अन्नमुच्चावचं भक्ष्याः फलानि विविधानि च।
रामायाभ्यवहारार्थं बहुशोऽपहृतं मया॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Boiled rice of various kinds, other foods requiring mastication and fruits of every description were brought by me in abundance to the presence of Śrī Rama for his repast. (15)

verses.text:
तत् सर्वं प्रत्यनुज्ञासीद् रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
न हि तत् प्रत्यगृह्णात् स क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess accepted all that for my pleasure and returned it to me. Bearing in mind the duty of a Kṣatriya (who is not permitted by the Śāstras to accept a gift, much less on the bank of a holy river), however, he did not partake of it. (16)

verses.text:
नह्यस्माभिः प्रतिग्राह्यं सखे देयं तु सर्वदा।
इति तेन वयं सर्वे अनुनीता महात्मना॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘No gift in any case is to be accepted by us (Kṣatriyas), my friend: a gift can only be made by us.’ In these words were we all pacified by that high-souled prince. (17)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणेन यदानीतं पीतं वारि महात्मना।
औपवास्यं तदाकार्षीद् राघवः सह सीतया॥ १८॥
verses.m: “That water alone which was brought by Lakṣmaṇa was drunk by the high-souled prince. Along with Sītā, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, then observed a fast for the day. (18)

verses.text:
ततस्तु जलशेषेण लक्ष्मणोऽप्यकरोत् तदा।
वाग्यतास्ते त्रयः संध्यां समुपासन्त संहिताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Then Lakṣmaṇa too forthwith slaked his thirst by means of the water that was left over. All the three, viz., Śrī Rāma, Lakśmaṇa and Sumantra, duly worshipped the deity presiding over the evening twilight silently together. (19)

verses.text:
सौमित्रिस्तु ततः पश्चादकरोत् स्वास्तरं शुभम्।
स्वयमानीय बर्हींषि क्षिप्रं राघवकारणात्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “After that, fetching blades of Kuśa grass himself, Lakṣmaṇa for his part promptly prepared a sacred bed for Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (20)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् समाविशद् रामः स्वास्तरे सह सीतया।
प्रक्षाल्य च तयोः पादौ व्यपाक्रामत् स लक्ष्मणः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Srī Rāma sat down on the bed with Sītā and, washing the feet of Śrī Rāma and Sītā (Śrī Rāma’s with his own hands and Sītā’s by giving water to her), the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa moved to a distance. (21)

verses.text:
एतत् तदिङ्गुदीमूलमिदमेव च तत् तृणम्।
यस्मिन् रामश्च सीता च रात्रिं तां शयितावुभौ॥ २२॥
verses.m: “This is the foot of the same Iṅgudī tree and these are the same blades of Kuśa grass where and on which Śrī Rāma and Sītā both reposed that night. (22)

verses.text:
नियम्य पृष्ठे तु तलाङ्गुलित्रवान्
शरैः सुपूर्णाविषुधी परंतपः।
महद्धनुः सज्जमुपोह्य लक्ष्मणो
निशामतिष्ठत् परितोऽस्य केवलम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Fastening at his back, one on each side, a pair of quivers fully packed with arrows and donning gloves about his hands and wielding a large stringed bow, Laksmana, a tormentor of his foes, for his part remained walking round Śrī Rāma during the night singly. (23)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वहं चोत्तमबाणचापभृत्
स्थितोऽभवं तत्र स यत्र लक्ष्मणः।
अतन्द्रितैर्ज्ञातिभिरात्तकार्मुकै-
र्महेन्द्रकल्पं परिपालयंस्तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Wielding excellent arrows and bow, I too remained posted where the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa kept moving, carefully guarding Śrī Rāma (who vied with Indra) with my vigilant kinsmen carrying bows in their hands.” (24)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरतः सह मन्त्रिभिः।
इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवैक्षत॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing all that attentively and reaching the foot of the Iṅgudi tree with the king’s counsellors, Bharata saw Śrī Rāma’s bed. (1)

verses.text:
अब्रवीज्जननीः सर्वा इह तस्य महात्मनः।
शर्वरी शयिता भूमाविदमस्य विमर्दितम्॥ २॥
verses.m: He said to all his mothers, “Here was the night spent by that high-souled prince lying on the ground. These are the blades of Kuśa grass crushed by his body while reposing on them. (2)

verses.text:
महाराजकुलीनेन महाभागेन धीमता।
जातो दशरथेनोर्व्यां न रामः स्वप्तुमर्हति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, who was procreated by the wise and highly blessed Daśaratha, born in the line of great kings, does not deserve to sleep on the ground without any shade or couch. (3)

verses.text:
अजिनोत्तरसंस्तीर्णे वरास्तरणसंचये।
शयित्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रः कथं शेते महीतले॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Having reposed all along on a bed consisting of a pile of excellent rugs and covered with an outermost covering of superb deerskin fit for kings, how does Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, sleep on the ground? (4)

verses.text:
प्रासादाग्रविमानेषु वलभीषु च सर्वदा।
हैमराजतभौमेषु वरास्तरणशालिषु॥ ५॥
पुष्पसंचयचित्रेषु चन्दनागुरुगन्धिषु।
पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेषु शुकसंघरुतेषु च॥ ६॥
प्रासादवरवर्येषु शीतवत्सु सुगन्धिषु।
उषित्वा मेरुकल्पेषु कृतकाञ्चनभित्तिषु॥ ७॥
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषैर्वराभरणनिःस्वनैः।
मृदङ्गवरशब्दैश्च सततं प्रतिबोधितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Sleeping always on the topmost storey of palaces built after the style of aerial cars and in turrets and in the foremost apartments of excellent seven-storeyed buildings—which were provided with floors paved with gold and silver and furnished with excellent carpets, which looked picturesque with heaps of flowers and were fragrant with the odour of sandalwood and aloe, which shone like white clouds and were noisy with the chatter of flocks of parrots, where natural coolness prevailed and which emitted a sweet fragrance of camphor etc., nay which vied with Mount Meru in height and whose walls were inlaid with gold—he was awakened everyday by the strains of vocal and instrumental music, the tinkling of excellent jewels and the excellent sound of clay tomtoms. (5—8)

verses.text:
बन्दिभिर्वन्दितः काले बहुभिः सूतमागधैः।
गाथाभिरनुरूपाभिः स्तुतिभिश्च परंतपः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Again Śrī Rāma, the tormentor of his enemy, was glorified at the time of waking by a number of panegyrists, bards and minstrels through appropriate verses and songs of praise. (9)

verses.text:
अश्रद्धेयमिदं लोके न सत्यं प्रतिभाति मा।
मुह्यते खलु मे भावः स्वप्नोऽयमिति मे मतिः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This is incredible in the world and does not appear true to me. My mind is really confused. My conclusion, therefore, is that this is a dream. (10)

verses.text:
न नूनं दैवतं किंचित् कालेन बलवत्तरम्।
यत्र दाशरथी रामो भूमावेवमशेत सः॥ ११॥
यस्मिन् विदेहराजस्य सुता च प्रियदर्शना।
दयिता शयिता भूमौ स्नुषा दशरथस्य च॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Surely there is no deity more powerful than Time (the will of God), impelled by which the aforesaid Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, reposes on the ground in this way and by force of which the daughter of Janaka (the king of the Videha territory), who is so pleasing to the sight and the beloved daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, has to lie down on the ground. (11-12)

verses.text:
इयं शय्या मम भ्रातुरिदमावर्तितं शुभम्।
स्थण्डिले कठिने सर्वं गात्रैर्विमृदितं तृणम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “This is the bed of my elder brother and here are the blessed marks of his changing sides in the form of all the blades of Kuśa grass crushed by his limbs against the hard ground. (13)

verses.text:
मन्ये साभरणा सुप्ता सीतास्मिन्शयने शुभा।
तत्र तत्र हि दृश्यन्ते सक्ताः कनकबिन्दवः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “It appears the blessed Sītā lay down decked with ornaments on this bed; for here and there are seen stuck to the grass particles of gold. (14)

verses.text:
उत्तरीयमिहासक्तं सुव्यक्तं सीतया तदा।
तथा ह्येते प्रकाशन्ते सक्ताः कौशेयतन्तवः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Sītā quite evidently had her upper garment entangled with these blades of grass at that time. That is why these silk threads appear stuck to them. (15)

verses.text:
मन्ये भर्तुः सुखा शय्या येन बाला तपस्विनी।
सुकुमारी सती दुःखं न विजानाति मैथिली॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I conclude the husband’s bed, be it soft or hard, is comfortable at all events to a devoted wife, as is evident from the fact that Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, though youthful and tender, experiences no smart even while reposing on such a hard and rough bed, virtuous as she is and devoted to austerities. (16)

verses.text:
हा हतोऽस्मि नृशंसोऽस्मि यत् सभार्यः कृते मम।
ईदृशीं राघवः शय्यामधिशेते ह्यनाथवत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Alas, I am ruined. Cruel am I, in that on my account Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) with his wife has to lie down on such a hard bed like a forlorn creature ! (17)

verses.text:
सार्वभौमकुले जातः सर्वलोकसुखावहः।
सर्वप्रियकरस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं प्रियमनुत्तमम्॥ १८॥
कथमिन्दीवरश्यामो रक्ताक्षः प्रियदर्शनः।
सुखभागी न दुःखार्हः शयितो भुवि राघवः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Relinquishing his beloved rulership, which is unsurpassed, how did Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), born in a line of universal monarchs, who brings happiness to the whole world and does good to all, who is blue as a lotus, has reddish eyes and is pleasing of appearance and who is deserving of happiness and unworthy of suffering, lie down on the ground? (18-19)

verses.text:
धन्यः खलु महाभागो लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः।
भ्रातरं विषमे काले यो राममनुवर्तते॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Blessed and highly fortunate indeed is Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with auspicious bodily marks, who is following his eldest brother in a critical period of his life ! (20)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्था खलु वैदेही पतिं यानुगता वनम्।
वयं संशयिताः सर्वे हीनास्तेन महात्मना॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Truly accomplished of purpose is Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, who followed her husband to the forest ! We are, however, all plunged in doubt as to our getting a chance to serve him, bereft as we are of that high-souled prince. (21)

verses.text:
अकर्णधारा पृथिवी शून्येव प्रतिभाति मे।
गते दशरथे स्वर्गं रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Emperor Daśaratha having ascended to heaven and Śrī Rāma having taken up his abode in the forest, the earth appears desolate to me like a boat without a pilot. (22)

verses.text:
न च प्रार्थयते कश्चिन्मनसापि वसुंधराम्।
वने निवसतस्तस्य बाहुवीर्याभिरक्षिताम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Nor does anyone lay claim even with his mind to the sovereignty of the globe, which stands protected on all sides by the very might of arms of Śrī Rāma dwelling in the forest. (23)

verses.text:
शून्यसंवरणारक्षामयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम्।
अनावृतपुरद्वारां राजधानीमरक्षिताम्॥ २४॥
अप्रहृष्टबलां शून्यां विषमस्थामनावृताम्।
शत्रवो नाभिमन्यन्ते भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The enemies do not claim as their own, any more than one would like to have articles made of poisoned food, the capital, Ayodhyā, whose protective wall is lying undefended, the horses and elephants in which roam about uncontrolled, whose entrances are never closed and the troops stationed in which are cheerless, and as such which is altogether unprotected, unguarded, desolate and reduced to a wretched condition. (24-25)

verses.text:
अद्यप्रभृति भूमौ तु शयिष्येऽहं तृणेषु वा।
फलमूलाशनो नित्यं जटाचीराणि धारयन्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “From this day onward I shall lie down on the bare ground or on blades of grass, living on fruits and roots alone from day to day and wearing matted hair on my head and the bark of trees on my person. (26)

verses.text:
तस्याहमुत्तरं कालं निवत्स्यामि सुखं वने।
तत् प्रतिश्रुतमार्यस्य नैव मिथ्या भविष्यति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “I shall comfortably dwell in the forest for the rest of the period of Śrī Rāma’s exile as his representative. In that way, the well-known vow of my elder brother will not be belied. (27)

verses.text:
वसन्तं भ्रातुरर्थाय शत्रुघ्नो मानुवत्स्यति।
लक्ष्मणेन सहायोध्यामार्यो मे पालयिष्यति॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Śatrughna will dwel with me when I live in the forest on behalf of my elder brother; while the latter with Lakṣmaṇa will protect Ayodhyā. (28)

verses.text:
अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमयोध्यायां द्विजातयः।
अपि मे देवताः कुर्युरिमं सत्यं मनोरथम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The Brāhmaṇas will install Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) on the throne of Ayodhyā. May the gods fulfil this desire of mine. (29)

verses.text:
प्रसाद्यमानः शिरसा मया स्वयं
बहुप्रकारं यदि न प्रपत्स्यते।
ततोऽनुवत्स्यामि चिराय राघवं
वनेचरं नार्हति मामुपेक्षितुम्॥ ३०
verses.m: “If he does not agree to return to Ayodhyā even when being solicited by me personally in many ways with my head bent low, in that case I shall dwell with Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) for any length of time so long as he roams about in the forest. He ought not to disregard me, I think. (30)

verses.text:
व्युष्य रात्रिं तु तत्रैव गङ्गाकूले स राघवः।
काल्यमुत्थाय शत्रुघ्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having spent the night at that very spot where Śrī Rāma had rested not long ago on the bank of the Gaṅgā and rising at daybreak, the said Bharata for his part spoke to Śatrughna as follows : (1)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्।
शीघ्रमानय भद्रं ते तारयिष्यति वाहिनीम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “How do you continue to sleep till now? Get up, O Śatrughna, and fetch Guha, the ruler of the Niṣādas, quickly; so that he will convey the army to the other bank. May all be well with you.’’ (2)

verses.text:
जागर्मि नाहं स्वपिमि तथैवार्यं विचिन्तयन्।
इत्येवमब्रवीद् भ्राता शत्रुघ्नो विप्रचोदितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Contemplating on Śrī Rāma, my eldest brother, even as you are, I am keeping awake, not sleeping.’’ In these very words did Śatrughna, Bharata’s younger brother, reply when admonished as above by Bharata. (3)

verses.text:
इति संवदतोरेवमन्योन्यं नरसिंहयोः।
आगम्य प्राञ्जलिः काले गुहो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Arriving at an opportune moment while Bharata and Śatrughna, the two lions among men were conversing with each other as aforesaid, Guha submitted to Bharata with folded hands as follows : (4)

verses.text:
कच्चित् सुखं नदीतीरेऽवात्सीः काकुत्स्थ शर्वरीम्।
कच्चिच्च सहसैन्यस्य तव नित्यमनामयम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I hope you spent the night comfortably on the river bank, O scion of Kakutstha. And I hope you are entirely free from distemper alongwith your army.’’ (5)

verses.text:
गुहस्य तत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा स्नेहादुदीरितम्।
रामस्यानुवशो वाक्यं भरतोऽपीदमब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid question asked with affection by Guha, Bharata too, for his part, who had subordinated his will to Śrī Rāma, made the following reply : (6)

verses.text:
सुखा नः शर्वरी धीमन् पूजिताश्चापि ते वयम्।
गङ्गां तु नौभिर्बह्वीभिर्दाशाः संतारयन्तु नः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “It was a happy night for us, O sagacious friend, and we have been properly entertained by you. Let your fishermen now duly ferry us across the Gaṅgā on a number of boats.’’ (7)

verses.text:
ततो गुहः संत्वरितः श्रुत्वा भरतशासनम्।
प्रतिप्रविश्य नगरं तं ज्ञातिजनमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing Bharata’s command and returning to the city with great expedition, Guha forthwith spoke as follows to his said kinsmen : (8)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठत प्रबुध्यध्वं भद्रमस्तु हि वः सदा।
नावः समुपकर्षध्वं तारयिष्यामि वाहिनीम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Wake up and rise : may prosperity ever actually attend you. Duly haul the boats to the bank, I shall have the army ferried across the Gaṅgā.’’ (9)

verses.text:
ते तथोक्ताः समुत्थाय त्वरिता राजशासनात्।
पञ्च नावां शतान्येव समानिन्युः समन्ततः॥ १०॥
अन्याः स्वस्तिकविज्ञेया महाघण्टाधरावराः।
शोभमानाः पताकिन्यो युक्तवाहाः सुसंहताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Springing up on their feet when addressed thus by Guha, the boatmen hurriedly brought together from all sides in obedience to their chiefs command five hundred boats and other excellent boats too, known by the name of Swāstika (because of their bearing the mark of Swāstika), which looked charming, were distinguished by flags and equipped with rowers, nay, which were strongly built and had large bells tied to their sails. (10-11)

verses.text:
ततः स्वस्तिकविज्ञेयां पाण्डुकम्बलसंवृताम्।
सनन्दिघोषां कल्याणीं गुहो नावमुपाहरत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Then Guha himself brought a lovely boat, also known by the name of Swāstika, the floor of which was covered with white rugs (fit for kings) and which was distinguished by the sound of festal music. (12)

verses.text:
तामारुरोह भरतः शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः।
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या राजयोषितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Bharata and Śatrughna, who was possessed of great might, as well as Kausalyā, Sumitrā and whatever other royal ladies there were, ascended it. (13)

verses.text:
पुरोहितश्च तत् पूर्वं गुरवो ब्राह्मणाश्च ये।
अनन्तरं राजदारास्तथैव शकटापणाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Sage Vasiṣṭha, the family priest, and whatever elderly Brāhmaṇas were present there took their seats even before Bharata and the royal ladies and immediately after these followed the other ladies of the royal family as well as the bullock-carts and the provisions, which were loaded on other boats. (14)

verses.text:
आवासमादीपयतां तीर्थं चाप्यवगाहताम्।
भाण्डानि चाददानानां घोषस्तु दिवमस्पृशत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: The din of men setting fire* to the huts erected for them as well as resorting to the descent in order to be able to ascend the boats and collecting the utensils in order to load them, actually rose to the skies. (15)

verses.text:
पताकिन्यस्तु ता नावः स्वयं दाशैरधिष्ठिताः।
वहन्त्यो जनमारूढं तदा सम्पेतुराशुगाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Ferrying the men seated in them, those swift-going boats, which were adorned with flags and controlled by the fishermen, then sailed automatically, as it were. (16)

verses.text:
नारीणामभिपूर्णास्तु काश्चित् काश्चित् तु वाजिनाम्।
काश्चित् तत्र वहन्ति स्म यानयुग्यं महाधनम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Some boats were full of women, while others were loaded with horses; while some more of them ferried costly chariots and animals of draught. (17)

verses.text:
तास्तु गत्वा परं तीरमवरोप्य च तं जनम्।
निवृत्ताः काण्डचित्राणि क्रियन्ते दाशबन्धुभिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having reached the opposite bank and enabled those men etc., to land, the boats for their part returned and were plied as so many toy-boats on water by the rowers, who were all kinsmen of Guha. (18)

verses.text:
सवैजयन्तास्तु गजा गजारोहैः प्रचोदिताः।
तरन्तः स्म प्रकाशन्ते सपक्षा इव पर्वताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Swimming across the Gaṅgā as urged by their mahouts, the elephants with flags on their back actually shone like winged mountains. (19)

verses.text:
नावश्चारुरुहुस्त्वन्ये प्लवैस्तेरुस्तथापरे।
अन्ये कुम्भघटैस्तेरुरन्ये तेरुश्च बाहुभिः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Nay, other men took their seats on boats while others crossed the river by means of rafts; still others swam across with the help of big and small earthen vessels and the rest swam with their arms alone. (20)

verses.text:
सा पुण्या ध्वजिनी गङ्गां दाशैः संतारिता स्वयम्।
मैत्रे मुहूर्ते प्रययौ प्रयागवनमुत्तमम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Ferried across the Gaṅgā by the fishermen themselves, that holy army which was hallowed through contact with holy men like Prince Bharata and Sage Vasiṣṭha as well as through a bath in the Gaṅgā and other sacred streams and was proceeding on the holy mission of bringing Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā, marched towards the excellent forest encircling Prayāga during the hour known by the name of Maitra* (because of its being sacred to Mitra, the sun-god). (21)

verses.text:
आश्वासयित्वा च चमूं महात्मा
निवेशयित्वा च यथोपजोषम्।
द्रष्टुं भरद्वाजमृषिप्रवर्य-
मृत्विक्सदस्यैर्भरतः प्रतस्थे॥ २२॥
verses.m: Nay, cheering up the troops and comfortably encamping them in the forest encircling Prayāga, the hight souled Bharata alongwith the priests and the (king’s) councillors set out to meet Bharadwāja, the foremost of Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras). (22)

verses.text:
स ब्राह्मणस्याश्रममभ्युपेत्य
महात्मनो देवपुरोहितस्य।
ददर्श रम्योटजवृक्षदेशं
महद्वनं विप्रवरस्य रम्यम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Reaching the hermitage of the high-souled Bharadwāja (the family priest of gods), who was not only a knower of Brahma but also the foremost of Vedic scholars,* Bharata saw the extensive and delightful grove surrounding the hermitage, consisting of clusters of trees interspersed with lovely huts of leafy twigs. (23)

verses.text:
भरद्वाजाश्रमं गत्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः।
जनं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः॥ १॥
पद्भ्यामेव तु धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः।
वसानो वाससी क्षौमे पुरोधाय पुरोहितम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Having reached the precincts of the hermitage of Bharadwāja and leaving all his people only a couple of miles away on this side of the hermitage so as not to cause disturbance to the hermits living peacefully there, Bharata, a jewel among men, for his part, who knew what is right, proceeded further with his counsellors on foot, placing Sage Vasiṣṭha (his family-priest) ahead and putting on only a pair of silk garments (viz., a loin-cloth and an outer covering), laying aside his weapons and ornaments etc. (1-2)

verses.text:
ततः संदर्शने तस्य भरद्वाजस्य राघवः।
मन्त्रिणस्तानवस्थाप्य जगामानुपुरोहितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Bidding the aforesaid counsellors stay behind, the moment the celebrated Bharadwāja was clearly in sight, Bharata (a scion of Raghu) then proceeded at the heels of Vasiṣṭha, his family-priest. (3)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठमथ दृष्ट्वैव भरद्वाजो महातपाः।
संचचालासनात् तूर्णं शिष्यानर्घ्यमिति ब्रुवन्॥ ४॥
verses.m: At the very sight of Vasiṣṭha, Bharadwāja, who practised great austerities, at once hurriedly rose from his seat, asking his pupils to fetch water to wash the hands of the distinguished guest with. (4)

verses.text:
समागम्य वसिष्ठेन भरतेनाभिवादितः।
अबुध्यत महातेजाः सुतं दशरथस्य तम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Uniting in embrace with Vasiṣṭha and greeted by Bharata, the highly glorious sage inferred him to be a son of Daśaratha. (5)

verses.text:
ताभ्यामर्घ्यं च पाद्यं च दत्त्वा पश्चात् फलानि च।
आनुपूर्व्याच्च धर्मज्ञः पप्रच्छ कुशलं कुले॥ ६॥
अयोध्यायां बले कोशे मित्रेष्वपि च मन्त्रिषु।
जानन् दशरथं वृत्तं न राजानमुदाहरत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Offering to the two guests in order of seniority (one after another) water to wash their hands and feet with and also fruits afterwards, Bharadwāja, who knows what is right, made inquiries concerning the welfare of the family of each and also whether all was well with the city of Ayodhyā, the army, the exchequer, the king’s allies and ministers. Knowing, as he did, Daśaratha to be dead, he made no inquiries concerning the king. (6-7)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठो भरतश्चैनं पप्रच्छतुरनामयम्।
शरीरेऽग्निषु शिष्येषु वृक्षेषु मृगपक्षिषु॥ ८॥
verses.m: Vasiṣṭha and Bharata in return inquired whether all was well with his body, sacred fires, pupils, trees, deer and birds. (8)

verses.text:
तथेति तु प्रतिज्ञाय भरद्वाजो महायशाः।
भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं राघवस्नेहबन्धनात्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Having admitted that it was so, the highly illustrious Bharadwāja for his part replied to Bharata as follows, impelled as he was by the ties of affection that he bore to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu : (9)

verses.text:
किमिहागमने कार्यं तव राज्यं प्रशासतः।
एतदाचक्ष्व सर्वं मे न हि मे शुध्यते मनः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “What motive could you have in coming all the way to this place, busy as you must have been ruling the kingdom of Ayodhyā? Please tell me all this; for my mind is not getting cleared of doubts (about your intentions towards Śrī Rāma). (10)

verses.text:
सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्याऽऽनन्दवर्धनम्।
भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्॥ ११॥
नियुक्तः स्त्रीनिमित्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः।
वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश॥ १२॥
कच्चिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि।
अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Seeking to enjoy the kingdom rightfully belonging to Śrī Rāma without any thorn in your side, I hope, you do not intend to do any bodily harm in this forest to Lakṣmaṇa, his younger brother, and the highly illustrious prince, Śrī Rāma Himself, the destroyer of enemies and the promoter of joy in this world, whom Kausalyā gave birth to, and who, having been urged, they say, by his father through the instrumentality of the latter’s wife, Kaikeyī, in the following words : Dwell in the forest for fourteen years, was exiled to the forest with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, and wife, Sītā, to the forest for a long term.” (11—13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो भरद्वाजं भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह।
पर्यश्रुनयनो दुःखाद् वाचा संसज्जमानया॥ १४॥
verses.m: Spoken to as aforesaid, Bharata, they say, replied as follows in a faltering tone with tears flowing from his eyes through agony : (14)

verses.text:
हतोऽस्मि यदि मामेवं भगवानपि मन्यते।
मत्तो न दोषमाशङ्के मैवं मामनुशाधि हि॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I am ruined if Your Holiness too who is omniscient, reckons me as such. I cannot even think of any harm having proceeded from me to Śrī Rāma. Therefore, please do not say much harsh words to me. (15)

verses.text:
न चैतदिष्टं माता मे यदवोचन्मदन्तरे।
नाहमेतेन तुष्टश्च न तद्वचनमाददे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Neither is that which my mother said during my absence (at my maternal grandfather’s) agreeable to me nor am I pleased with that which she has done, nor again have I even now accepted her word, asking me to enjoy the sovereignty of Ayodhyā. (16)

verses.text:
अहं तु तं नरव्याघ्रमुपयातः प्रसादकः।
प्रतिनेतुमयोध्यायां पादौ चास्याभिवन्दितुम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I have, on the other hand, come to take that tiger among men back to Ayodhyā after having propitiated him, and also to bow down at his feet. (17)

verses.text:
तं मामेवंगतं मत्वा प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।
शंस मे भगवन् रामः क्व सम्प्रति महीपतिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Believing me as such to have come with the aforesaid intention, you be gracious to me. Also kindly tell me, venerable Sir, where Emperor Rāma may at present be.” (18)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठादिभिर्ऋत्विग्भिर्याचितो भगवांस्ततः।
उवाच तं भरद्वाजः प्रसादाद् भरतं वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Solicited by the priests (who had obviously joined the party in the meantime) headed by Vasiṣṭha, the venerable Bharadwāja thereupon graciously spoke to the celebrated Bharata as follows: (19)

verses.text:
त्वय्येतत् पुरुषव्याघ्र युक्तं राघववंशजे।
गुरुवृत्तिर्दमश्चैव साधूनां चानुयायिता॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Service to your elders as also self-control and walking in the footsteps of the virtuous—this is worthy of you, descended, as you are, in the line of Raghu, O tiger among men ! (20)

verses.text:
जाने चैतन्मनःस्थं ते दृढीकरणमस्त्विति।
अपृच्छं त्वां तवात्यर्थं कीर्तिं समभिवर्धयन्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I already knew (by my yogic power) what existed in your mind. All the same I questioned you as though I knew nothing in order that your resolution may be strengthened and in order further to enchance your renown beyond measure. (21)

verses.text:
जाने च रामं धर्मज्ञं ससीतं सहलक्ष्मणम्।
अयं वसति ते भ्राता चित्रकूटे महागिरौ॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I know where Śrī Rāma, who knows what is right, is staying accompanied by Sītā and followed by Lakṣmaṇa. Your brother is dwelling at present on the great Citrakūṭa mountain. (22)

verses.text:
श्वस्तु गन्तासि तं देशं वसाद्य सह मन्त्रिभिः।
एतं मे कुरु सुप्राज्ञ कामं कामार्थकोविद॥ २३॥
verses.m: “You will certainly proceed to that area tomorrow. Halt here with your counsellors today. Grant this desire of mine, O highly sagacious prince, knowing how to fulfil the desired object of your friends and well-wishers ! (23)

verses.text:
ततस्तथेत्येवमुदारदर्शनः
प्रतीतरूपो भरतोऽब्रवीद् वचः।
चकार बुद्धिं च तदाश्रमे तदा
निशानिवासाय नराधिपात्मजः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Thereupon Bharata, who had a broad outlook and whose reality as a devotee of Śrī Rāma had now come to be known, replied as follows : “So be it.” Nay, the prince forthwith made up his mind to stay in that hermitage during the night. (24)

verses.text:
कृतबुद्धिं निवासाय तत्रैव स मुनिस्तदा।
भरतं केकयीपुत्रमातिथ्येन न्यमन्त्रयत्॥ १॥
verses.m: The celebrated sage then invited to a hospitable reception Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, who had made up his mind (as shown before) to stay in that very hermitage for the night. (1)

verses.text:
अब्रवीद् भरतस्त्वेनं नन्विदं भवता कृतम्।
पाद्यमर्घ्यमथातिथ्यं वने यदुपपद्यते॥ २॥
verses.m: Bharata for his part said to Bharadwāja, “Sure enough the kind of hospitality which could possibly be arranged in a forest has already been shown by you to us just now in the form of water to wash our feet and hands with and fruit and roots.” (2)

verses.text:
अथोवाच भरद्वाजो भरतं प्रहसन्निव।
जाने त्वां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं तुष्येस्त्वं येन केनचित्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Bharadwāja forthwith replied to Bharata as follows, laughing heartily as it were: “I know you to be full of affection to me. As such you are likely to be pleased with anything and everything that is offered to you. (3)

verses.text:
सेनायास्तु तवैवास्याः कर्तुमिच्छामि भोजनम्।
मम प्रीतिर्यथारूपा त्वमर्हो मनुजर्षभ॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I, however, only wish to feed this army of yours. And you ought to do that in which my pleasure lies, O jewel among men ! (4)

verses.text:
किमर्थं चापि निक्षिप्य दूरे बलमिहागतः।
कस्मान्नेहोपयातोऽसि सबलः पुरुषर्षभ॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Moreover, wherefore did you come here encamping the army at a distance from my hermitage? Why did you not turn up here, army and all, O jewel among men?’’ (5)

verses.text:
भरतः प्रत्युवाचेदं प्राञ्जलिस्तं तपोधनम्।
न सैन्येनोपयातोऽस्मि भगवन् भगवद्भयात्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Bharata with folded hands replied as follows to the sage, whose only wealth was his asceticism : “I did not turn up with the army for fear of displeasing you; O venerable sage ! (6)

verses.text:
राज्ञा हि भगवन् नित्यं राजपुत्रेण वा तथा।
यत्नतः परिहर्तव्या विषयेषु तपस्विनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “In fact, distance should always be maintained from ascetics (lest they be disturbed) in their own lands by a King or a King’s son under similar circumstances, Your Holiness ! (7)

verses.text:
वाजिमुख्या मनुष्याश्च मत्ताश्च वरवारणाः।
प्रच्छाद्य भगवन् भूमिं महतीमनुयान्ति माम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Best specimens of horses as well as men and excellent elephants in rut are following in my wake occupying a large area. (8)

verses.text:
ते वृक्षानुदकं भूमिमाश्रमेषूटजांस्तथा।
न हिंस्युरिति तेनाहमेक एवागतस्ततः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I came away from that place where the troops have been encamped all alone, accompanied by Sage Vasiṣṭha, lest they should destroy the trees, foul the waters and land as well as the huts in the hermitage.” (9)

verses.text:
आनीयतामितः सेनेत्याज्ञप्तः परमर्षिणा।
तथानुचक्रे भरतः सेनायाः समुपागमम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Commanded by the eminent sage in the following words : “Let the army be brought hither !’’ Bharata forthwith caused the army to be duly brought all the way to the hermitage accordingly. (10)

verses.text:
अग्निशालां प्रविश्याथ पीत्वापः परिमृज्य च।
आतिथ्यस्य क्रियाहेतोर्विश्वकर्माणमाह्वयत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Entering the fire-sanctuary, sipping water (thrice according to the Śruti text त्रिराचामेत् with the recitation of the Divine Names for self-purification) and wiping the lips twice according to the Vedic injunction द्विः परिमृज्य, the sage next invoked in the following words Viśwakarmā (the architect of gods) for providing hospitality to the army of Prince Bharata: (11)

verses.text:
आह्वये विश्वकर्माणमहं त्वष्टारमेव च।
आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संविधीयताम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I invoke god Viśwakarmā, who is also the divine carpenter (Twaṣṭā). I wish to provide hospitality (to the army of Prince Bharata). Let everything be got ready in that connection for me. (12)

verses.text:
आह्वये लोकपालांस्त्रीन् देवान् शक्रपुरोगमान्।
आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संविधीयताम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I further invoke the presence of the three gods viz., Yama, Varuṇa and Kubera, who are the guardians of the spheres, headed by Indra, the ruler of gods. I wish to provide hospitality to the army of Prince Bharata. Let everything be got ready for me towards that end. (13)

verses.text:
प्राक्स्रोतसश्च या नद्यस्तिर्यक्स्रोतस एव च।
पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च समायान्त्वद्य सर्वशः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Let all the rivers that flow in an easterly direction as well as those flowing in a westerly direction on the surface of the earth as also in the aerial region meet today in this tract of land. (14)

verses.text:
अन्याः स्रवन्तु मैरेयं सुरामन्याः सुनिष्ठिताम्।
अपराश्चोदकं शीतमिक्षुकाण्डरसोपमम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Let some of those rivers bear along Maireya (a kind of wine made from date palms etc.,) others highly refined Surā (another species of wine made from jaggery, honey and flour), and still others cool water, delicious like the juice of sugarcane. (15)

verses.text:
आह्वये देवगन्धर्वान् विश्वावसुहहाहुहून्।
तथैवाप्सरसो देवगन्धर्वैश्चापि सर्वशः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I also invoke the presence of the celestial Gandharvas Viśwāvasu, Hāhā and Hūhū and even so all the celestial nymphs alongwith the other celestial Gandharvas. (16)

verses.text:
घृताचीमथ विश्वाचीं मिश्रकेशीमलम्बुषाम्।
नागदत्तां च हेमां च सोमामद्रिकृतस्थलीम्॥ १७॥
शक्रं याश्चोपतिष्ठन्ति ब्रह्माणं याश्च भामिनीः।
सर्वास्तुम्बुरुणा सार्धमाह्वये सपरिच्छदाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I invoke the Apsarā named Ghṛtācī and Viśwācī, Miśrakeśī, Alambuṣā, Nāgadattā and Hemā as also Somā, who has taken up her abode on a mountain called Mahendra as well as all the nymphs that wait upon Indra, the ruler of paradise, as also the dancing girls that wait upon Brahmā in Brahmaloka alongwith their teacher, Tumburu and all external appendage such as musical instruments. (17-18)

verses.text:
वनं कुरुषु यद् दिव्यं वासोभूषणपत्रवत्।
दिव्यनारीफलं शश्वत् तत्कौबेरमिहैव तु॥ १९॥
verses.m: “In the same way let that celestial grove known by the name of Caitraratha presided over by Kubera, the guardian of the northern quarter, which is located in the land of the Uttara Kurus (in the north of India) and the trees of which are clothed with leaves in the form of heavenly raiment and jewels and perpetually bear fruits in the form of heavenly damsels, actually apppear at this very spot. (19)

verses.text:
इह मे भगवान् सोमो विधत्तामन्नमुत्तमम्।
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च चोष्यं च लेह्यं च विविधं बहु॥ २०॥
विचित्राणि च माल्यानि पादपप्रच्युतानि च।
सुरादीनि च पेयानि मांसानि विविधानि च॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let the glorious moon-god, the diety presiding over the annual plants, place at my disposal abundant excellent food of every variety, consisting of dishes requiring mastication as well as those that can be gulped without mastication, nay those that can be sucked and those that require to be licked, and also lovely garlands dropped straight from trees, also drinks such as wine and meats of various kinds.’’ (20-21)

verses.text:
एवं समाधिना युक्तस्तेजसाप्रतिमेन च।
शिक्षास्वरसमायुक्तं सुव्रतश्चाब्रवीन्मुनिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: So did the sage of noble vows, who is rich in concentration of mind and endowed with matchless glory too, utter words of invocation pronounced according to the rules of phonetics and accented according to the rules of grammar. (22)

verses.text:
मनसा ध्यायतस्तस्य प्राङ्मुखस्य कृताञ्जलेः।
आजग्मुस्तानि सर्वाणि दैवतानि पृथक् पृथक्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Even as the sage invoked the aforesaid gods with his mind, sitting with his face turned towards the east, his palms joined together in supplication, all those deities that had been invoked by the sage came one by one before him. (23)

verses.text:
मलयं दर्दुरं चैव ततः स्वेदनुदोऽनिलः।
उपस्पृश्य ववौ युक्त्या सुप्रियात्मा सुखं शिवः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Thereupon a cool breeze, which was most delightful to the touch and which wiped one’s sweat through mere contact blew gently touching the Malaya and Dardura mountains, clothed with forests of sandalwood trees. (24)

verses.text:
ततोऽभ्यवर्षन्त घना दिव्याः कुसुमवृष्टयः।
देवदुन्दुभिघोषश्च दिक्षु सर्वासु शुश्रुवे॥ २५॥
verses.m: Then fell down thick showers of heavenly flowers and the sound of celestial kettledrums was heard in all the quarters. (25)

verses.text:
प्रववुश्चोत्तमा वाता ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः।
प्रजगुर्देवगन्धर्वा वीणाः प्रमुमुचुः स्वरान्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Nay, excellent breezes began incessantly to blow and bevies of celestial nymphs began to dance. Heavenly Gandharvas beautifully sang and Vinas gave forth melodies. (26)

verses.text:
स शब्दो द्यां च भूमिं च प्राणिनां श्रवणानि च।
विवेशोच्चावचः श्लक्ष्णः समो लयगुणान्वितः॥ २७॥
verses.m: That sound of vocal and instrumental music—which rose and fell at intervals, was soft and of a moderate pitch and endowed with the virtue of a uniform measure of time—penetrated into heaven, earth and the ears of living beings. (27)

verses.text:
तस्मिन्नेवंगते शब्दे दिव्ये श्रोत्रसुखे नृणाम्।
ददर्श भारतं सैन्यं विधानं विश्वकर्मणः॥ २८॥
verses.m: While that heavenly melody, agreeable to the ears of men, came in that way, the army of Bharata beheld the handiwork of Viśwakarmā. (28)

verses.text:
बभूव हि समा भूमिः समन्तात् पञ्चयोजनम्।
शाद्वलैर्बहुभिश्छन्ना नीलवैदूर्यसंनिभैः॥ २९॥
verses.m: The entire stretch of land within a radius of forty miles not only turned even but was also carpeted with many patches of fresh grass resembling blue cat’s-eye gems in hue. (29)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् बिल्वाः कपित्थाश्च पनसा बीजपूरकाः।
आमलक्यो बभूवुश्च चूताश्च फलभूषिताः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: In that land sprang up Bel, Kapittha (lit., on which monkeys dwell), Panasa (the bread-fruit), Bījapūraka (citron), Āmalakī (emblic myrobalan) and mango trees adorned with fruits. (30)

verses.text:
उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश्च वनं दिव्योपभोगवत्।
आजगाम नदी सौम्या तीरजैर्बहुभिर्वृता॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Nay, from the territory of the Uttara Kuru’s came the grove (presided over by Kubera, the god of riches, and known by the name of Caitraratha) rich in products worthy of being enjoyed by heavenly beings, as well as a delightful stream hemmed in with a number of trees growing on its banks. (31)

verses.text:
चतुःशालानि शुभ्राणि शालाश्च गजवाजिनाम्।
हर्म्यप्रासादसंयुक्ततोरणानि शुभानि च॥ ३२॥
verses.m: There stood up white mansions each consisting of four rooms, as well as stables for elephants and horses and charming citygates with mansions and palaces. (32)

verses.text:
सितमेघनिभं चापि राजवेश्म सुतोरणम्।
शुक्लमाल्यकृताकारं दिव्यगन्धसमुक्षितम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: There also stood a royal palace, looking like a white cloud and provided with a lovely arched doorway, nay, decorated with white garlands and sprinkled with exquisite scents. (33)

verses.text:
चतुरस्रमसम्बाधं शयनासनयानवत्।
दिव्यैः सर्वरसैर्युक्तं दिव्यभोजनवस्त्रवत्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: It was quadrilateral in shape, commodious, furnished with couches, seats and palanquins, supplied with all delicious drinks and provided with excellent food and clothing. (34)

verses.text:
उपकल्पितसर्वान्नं धौतनिर्मलभाजनम्।
क्लृप्तसर्वासनं श्रीमत्स्वास्तीर्णशयनोत्तमम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Victuals of every description had been kept ready there as well as cleaned vessels free from dirt. All kinds of seats had been arranged at proper places and the palace looked charming with superb couches duly covered with counterpanes. (35)

verses.text:
प्रविवेश महाबाहुरनुज्ञातो महर्षिणा।
वेश्म तद् रत्नसम्पूर्णं भरतः कैकयीसुतः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Permitted by the eminent sage, Bharadwāja, Prince Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, who was distinguished by unusually long arms, duly entered that palace richly stocked with precious stones. (36)

verses.text:
अनुजग्मुश्च ते सर्वे मन्त्रिणः सपुरोहिताः।
बभूवुश्च मुदा युक्तास्तं दृष्ट्वा वेश्मसंविधिम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: All the aforesaid counsellors accompanied by family-priests also followed suit and were filled with delight to see that excellent get-up of houses. (37)

verses.text:
तत्र राजासनं दिव्यं व्यजनं छत्रमेव च।
भरतो मन्त्रिभिः सार्धमभ्यवर्तत राजवत्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Alongwith the counsellors Bharata went clockwise round the excellent royal throne as well as round the whisk made from the tail of a yak and the royal umbrella kept there, as if round a sovereign. (38)

verses.text:
आसनं पूजयामास रामायाभिप्रणम्य च।
वालव्यजनमादाय न्यषीदत् सचिवासने॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Bowing down low to Śrī Rāma as though the latter were seated on it, he paid homage to the throne itself and, taking the whisk, sat down on the seat meant for the chief minister. (39)

verses.text:
आनुपूर्व्यान्निषेदुश्च सर्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहिताः।
ततः सेनापतिः पश्चात् प्रशास्ता च न्यषीदत॥ ४०॥
verses.m: All the counsellors and family-priests too sat down in order of precedence. Then sat down the generalissimo and afterwards the officer-in-charge of the encampment. (40)

verses.text:
ततस्तत्र मुहूर्तेन नद्यः पायसकर्दमाः।
उपातिष्ठन्त भरतं भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Then after a short while streams having milk thickened with rice, in place of mud, flowed past Bharata on that site at the command of Bharadwāja. (41)

verses.text:
आसामुभयतःकूलं पाण्डुमृत्तिकलेपनाः।
रम्याश्चावसथा दिव्या ब्राह्मणस्य प्रसादजाः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: On both the banks of these streams rose excellent and lovely houses plastered with lime and brought into being by the grace of the Brāhmaṇa sage, Bharadwāja. (42)

verses.text:
तेनैव च मुहूर्तेन दिव्याभरणभूषिताः।
आगुर्विंशतिसाहस्राः ब्रह्मणा प्रहिताः स्त्रियः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Nay, during that very hour arrived there twenty thousand women adorned with excellent jewels and sent by Brahmā, the creator. (43)

verses.text:
सुवर्णमणिमुक्तेन प्रवालेन च शोभिताः।
आगुर्विंशतिसाहस्राः कुबेरप्रहिताः स्त्रियः॥ ४४॥
याभिर्गृहीतः पुरुषः सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते।
आगुर्विंशतिसाहस्रा नन्दनादप्सरोगणाः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: There also came twenty thousand women decked with ornaments of gold, gems and pearls and coral sent by Kubera. There also arrived from the Nandana grove in paradise twenty thousand celestial nymphs, embraced by whom a man looked as though seized with a fit of insanity.* (44-45)

verses.text:
नारदस्तुम्बुरुर्गोपः प्रभया सूर्यवर्चसः।
एते गन्धर्वराजानो भरतस्याग्रतो जगुः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: The following chiefs of Gandharvas—Nārada, Tumburu and Gopa—who shone like the sun because of their splendour, began to sing before Bharata. (46)

verses.text:
अलम्बुषा मिश्रकेशी पुण्डरीकाथ वामना।
उपानृत्यन्त भरतं भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Alambuṣā, Miśrakeśī, Puṇḍarīkā and Vāmanā started dancing in the presence of Bharata under orders of Bharadwāja. (47)

verses.text:
यानि माल्यानि देवेषु यानि चैत्ररथे वने।
प्रयागे तान्यदृश्यन्त भरद्वाजस्य तेजसा॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Those celestial flowers which are found solely among gods and those which exist in the grove named Caitraratha, belonging to Kubera, the god of riches, were seen at Prayāga, thanks to the spiritual might of Bharadwāja. (48)

verses.text:
बिल्वा मार्दङ्गिका आसन् शम्याग्राहा बिभीतकाः।
अश्वत्था नर्तकाश्चासन् भरद्वाजस्य तेजसा॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Bel trees assumed the role of playing on clay tomtoms, Vibhītaka trees picked up a pair of cymbals known by the name of Śāmyā in order to strike them so as to keep time and Peepul trees played the role of dancers thanks to the spiritual might of Bharadwāja. (49)

verses.text:
ततः सरलतालाश्च तिलकाः सतमालकाः।
प्रहृष्टास्तत्र सम्पेतुः कुब्जा भूत्वाथ वामनाः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Then deodars, palmyra and Tilaka trees alongwith Tamāla trees arrived there highly rejoiced, assuming the forms of hunchbacks and dwarfs to render services to Bharata. (50)

verses.text:
शिंशपाऽऽमलकी जम्बूर्याश्चान्याः कानने लताः।
मालती मल्लिका जातिर्याश्चान्याः कानने लताः।
प्रमदाविग्रहं कृत्वा भरद्वाजाश्रमेऽवसन्॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Siṁśapās (Aśoka trees), Amalakīs (emblic myrobalan), Jambūs (rose-apple trees); Mālatī, Mallikā and Jāti and whatever other trees bearing female names and creepers there were in the forest took up their abode in the hermitage of Bharadwāja assuming the form of young women in order to be able to serve Bharata. (51)

verses.text:
सुरां सुरापाः पिबत पायसं च बुभुक्षिताः।
मांसानि च सुमेध्यानि भक्ष्यन्तां यो यदिच्छति॥ ५२॥
verses.m: They said to the troops: “Drink wine, O soldiers addicted to drinking, and drink milk thickened with rice, O troops stricken with hunger ! Let meats also, eminently fit for sacrifice, be eaten, as you will. One will get whatever one seeks.” (52)

verses.text:
उच्छोद्य स्नापयन्ति स्म नदीतीरेषु वल्गुषु।
अप्येकमेकं पुरुषं प्रमदाः सप्त चाष्ट च॥ ५३॥
verses.m: A batch of seven or eight young women bathed every single man on the charming river-banks after first daubing his body with a fragrant paste of oil-seeds and then rubbing off the dirt. (53)

verses.text:
संवाहन्त्यः समापेतुर्नार्यो विपुललोचनाः।
परिमृज्य तदान्योन्यं पाययन्ति वराङ्गनाः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: There also appeared on the scene women with big eyes, kneading the feet of men; nay, wiping off the moisture on their body, the lovely women gave them delicious beverages to drink in seclusion. (54)

verses.text:
हयान् गजान् खरानुष्ट्रांस्तथैव सुरभेः सुतान्।
अभोजयन् वाहनपास्तेषां भोज्यं यथाविधि॥ ५५॥
verses.m: The keepers (created and detailed by Bharadwāja) of the animals carrying Bharata’s men on their backs duly fed the horses, elephants, donkeys, camels as well as the bullocks with articles fit for their consumption. (55)

verses.text:
इक्षूंश्च मधुलाजांश्च भोजयन्ति स्म वाहनान्।
इक्ष्वाकुवरयोधानां चोदयन्तो महाबलाः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: Coaxing the animals carrying the gallant warriors of Ikṣwāku’s race on their back, the aforesaid very mighty keepers fed them with pieces of sugarcane as well as with fried grains of paddy soaked in honey. (56)

verses.text:
नाश्वबन्धोऽश्वमाजानान्न गजं कुञ्जरग्रहः।
मत्तप्रमत्तमुदिता सा चमूस्तत्र सम्बभौ॥ ५७॥
verses.m: The groom did not recognize the horse in his charge nor did the elephant-keeper recognize his charge (since the animals were fed and groomed so well that they got changed beyond recognition). The aforesaid army appeared intoxicated, maddened and enraptured on that spot. (57)

verses.text:
तर्पिताः सर्वकामैश्च रक्तचन्दनरूषिताः।
अप्सरोगणसंयुक्ताः सैन्या वाचमुदीरयन्॥ ५८॥
verses.m: Sated with all desired enjoyments and smeared with red sandal-paste, the troops, attended by hosts of celestial nymphs, uttered the following words : (58)

verses.text:
नैवायोध्यां गमिष्यामो न गमिष्याम दण्डकान्।
कुशलं भरतस्यास्तु रामस्यास्तु तथा सुखम्॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “We shall neither return to Ayodhyā nor go to the Daṇḍaka forest. Let all be well with Bharata because of whom we are enjoying heavenly delights here on earth and let lasting happiness be the lot of Śrī Rāma as a foretaste of whose blessed sight we have secured these heavenly enjoyments !’’ (59)

verses.text:
इति पादातयोधाश्च हस्त्यश्वारोहबन्धकाः।
अनाथास्तं विधिं लब्ध्वा वाचमेतामुदीरयन्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: So did the foot soldiers as well as those mounted on horses and elephants and their keepers too, who in their inebriety considered themselves independent (lit., without a master) on receiving such attentions from the sage, utter the aforesaid words. (60)

verses.text:
सम्प्रहृष्टा विनेदुस्ते नरास्तत्र सहस्रशः।
भरतस्यानुयातारः स्वर्गोऽयमिति चाब्रुवन्॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Extremely rejoiced to see the untold affluence and power of the sage, those men on that spot, who had followed Bharata in his journey to Citrakūṭa, to bring Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā, in their thousands thundered and said, “This is heaven indeed.’’ (61)

verses.text:
नृत्यन्तश्च हसन्तश्च गायन्तश्चैव सैनिकाः।
समन्तात् परिधावन्तो माल्योपेताः सहस्रशः॥ ६२॥
verses.m: Adorned with garlands the troops in their thousands ran in every direction dancing and laughing and singing. (62)

verses.text:
ततो भुक्तवतां तेषां तदन्नममृतोपमम्।
दिव्यानुद्वीक्ष्य भक्ष्यांस्तानभवद् भक्षणे मतिः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: In spite of their having partaken of that ambrosia-like food, their mind felt inclined to eat again the moment they saw those excellent dishes. (63)

verses.text:
प्रेष्याश्चेट्यश्च वध्वश्च बलस्थाश्चापि सर्वशः।
बभूवुस्ते भृशं प्रीताः सर्वे चाहतवाससः॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Servants and maid-servants as also the wives of the troops as well as the troops themselves—they all felt highly delighted, nay, all were supplied with a new set of clothes. (64)

verses.text:
कुञ्जराश्च खरोष्ट्राश्च गोऽश्वाश्च मृगपक्षिणः।
बभूवुः सुभृतास्तत्र नातो ह्यन्यमकल्पयत्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: Elephants and donkeys and camels too as well as bullocks and horses, nay, even deer and birds in that region were fully nourished; hence they coveted nothing else. (65)

verses.text:
नाशुक्लवासास्तत्रासीत् क्षुधितो मलिनोऽपि वा।
रजसा ध्वस्तकेशो वा नरः कश्चिददृश्यत॥ ६६॥
verses.m: No one in that area was clad in soiled attire, hungry or even untidy. Nor was any man seen with his hair soiled with dust. (66)

verses.text:
आजैश्चापि च वाराहैर्निष्ठानवरसंचयैः।
फलनिर्यूहसंसिद्धैः सूपैर्गन्धरसान्वितैः॥ ६७॥
पुष्पध्वजवतीः पूर्णाः शुक्लस्यान्नस्य चाभितः।
ददृशुर्विस्मितास्तत्र नरा लौहीः सहस्रशः॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Struck with wonder people beheld there placed all round, in thousands, gold vessels decorated with floral flags and filled with excellent seasoned articles of food prepared from bulbs known by the name of Vārahī, flavoured with Ptychotis ajowan, and well boiled in the decoction of fruits; as well as with flavoursome boiled pulses and spotless white boiled rice. (67-68)

verses.text:
बभूवुर्वनपार्श्वेषु कूपाः पायसकर्दमाः।
ताश्च कामदुघा गावो द्रुमाश्चासन् मधुच्युतः॥ ६९॥
verses.m: The wells in the precincts of the forest around the hermitage of Bharadwāja had their mud transformed into milk thickened with rice and sugar; the cows in that region were transformed into cows of plenty and the trees dripped honey. (69)

verses.text:
वाप्यो मैरेयपूर्णाश्च मृष्टमांसचयैर्वृताः।
प्रतप्तपिठरैश्चापि मार्गमायूरकौक्कुटैः॥ ७०॥
verses.m: The bigger wells with flights of stairs got filled with Maireya (a kind of intoxicating drink) and were banked with heaps of dainty meat of deer, peacocks and fowls dressed in intensely heated earthen vessels (perhaps for the use of Niṣādas and other low-caste people in the army of Bharata). (70)

verses.text:
पात्रीणां च सहस्राणि स्थालीनां नियुतानि च।
न्यर्बुदानि च पात्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Thousands of gold vessels containing boiled rice, lakhs of gold cauldrons holding seasoned articles of food and millions of plates, also made of gold were to be seen there. (71)

verses.text:
स्थाल्यः कुम्भ्यः करम्भ्यश्च दधिपूर्णाः सुसंस्कृताः।
यौवनस्थस्य गौरस्य कपित्थस्य सुगन्धिनः॥ ७२॥
ह्रदाः पूर्णा रसालस्य दध्नः श्वेतस्य चापरे।
बभूवुः पायसस्यान्ये शर्कराणां च संचयाः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: There appeared clay pans, smaller earthen vessels and big broad-mouthed clay vessels full of curds duly spiced with dry ginger etc., and tanks full of fragrant buttermilk tinged yellow with saffron and prepared a few hours back, as well as of buttermilk flavoured with cumin seeds, others full of white curds and still others of milk, as also heaps of sugar. (72-73)

verses.text:
कल्कांश्चूर्णकषायांश्च स्नानानि विविधानि च।
ददृशुर्भाजनस्थानि तीर्थेषु सरितां नराः॥ ७४॥
verses.m: On the stairs for descent to the rivers people saw kept in large pans crushed emblic myrobalans and powdered fragrant substances and varied articles such as oils, hot water etc., useful for a bath. (74)

verses.text:
शुक्लानंशुमतश्चापि दन्तधावनसंचयान्।
शुक्लांश्चन्दनकल्कांश्च समुद्रेष्ववतिष्ठतः॥ ७५॥
दर्पणान् परिमृष्टांश्च वाससां चापि संचयान्।
पादुकोपानहं चैव युग्मान्यत्र सहस्रशः॥ ७६॥
आञ्जनीः कङ्कतान् कूर्चांश्छत्राणि च धनूंषि च।
मर्मत्राणानि चित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च॥ ७७॥
प्रतिपानह्रदान् पूर्णान् खरोष्ट्रगजवाजिनाम्।
अवगाह्यसुतीर्थांश्च ह्रदान् सोत्पलपुष्करान्।
आकाशवर्णप्रतिमान् स्वच्छतोयान् सुखाप्लवान्॥ ७८॥
नीलवैदूर्यवर्णांश्च मृदून् यवससंचयान्।
निर्वापार्थं पशूनां ते ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वशः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: They further beheld at every place in that area bundles of fresh white twigs with their one end crushed for being used as a tooth-brush, as well as the paste of white sandalwood for being used as a shampoo, kept in round covered wooden cases, perfectly cleaned mirrors as well as piles of textiles, as also thousands of pairs of wooden sandals and leather shoes, small caskets containing collyrium, combs, brushes for combing moustaches and beards, nay, umbrellas, and bows, armour and different kinds of beds and seats, tanks full of water worth drinking, feed for donkeys, camels, elephants and horses, as well as tanks, provided with excellent descents, where one could easily take a plunge, full of lilies and lotuses, resembling the sky in hue, containing limpid water and pleasing to bathe in and heaps of tender grass resembling the blue cat’s-eyes gem in hue for the consumption of animals. (75—79)

verses.text:
व्यस्मयन्त मनुष्यास्ते स्वप्नकल्पं तदद्भुतम्।
दृष्ट्वाऽऽतिथ्यं कृतं तादृग् भरतस्य महर्षिणा॥ ८०॥
verses.m: The aforesaid men were amazed to see that entertainment, wonderful like a dream, provided so long for Bharata by the eminent sage Bharadwāja. (80)

verses.text:
इत्येवं रममाणानां देवानामिव नन्दने।
भरद्वाजाश्रमे रम्ये सा रात्रिर्व्यत्यवर्तत॥ ८१॥
verses.m: While the people that had followed Bharata in his journey to Citrakūṭa were still busy enjoying, as aforesaid, in that lovely hermitage of Bharadwāja the delights provided by the sage like so many gods in the Nandana grove in paradise, that night passed away. (81)

verses.text:
प्रतिजग्मुश्च ता नद्यो गन्धर्वाश्च यथागतम्।
भरद्वाजमनुज्ञाप्य ताश्च सर्वा वराङ्गनाः॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Taking leave of Bharadwāja, those rivers as well as the Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and all the lovely women, viz., the celestial nymphs, returned even as they had come. (82)

verses.text:
तथैव मत्ता मदिरोत्कटा नरा-
स्तथैव दिव्यागुरुचन्दनोक्षिताः।
तथैव दिव्या विविधाः स्रगुत्तमाः
पृथग्विकीर्णा मनुजैः प्रमर्दिताः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: The people, however, remained flushed and drunk with wine much in the same way even at dawn; they stood smeared with the exquisite paste of aloe wood and sandalwood even as before; and the excellent celestial garlands of various kinds lay strewn here and there separately as fresh as at the beginning, crushed as they were by men through constant use for the whole night. (83)

verses.text:
ततस्तां रजनीं व्युष्य भरतः सपरिच्छदः।
कृतातिथ्यो भरद्वाजं कामादभिजगाम ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Having spent the previous night with his family at the hermitage of Bharadwāja, Bharata, to whom hospitality had been extended by the sage, approached Bharadwāja to take leave of him to proceed to Citrakūṭa: so the tradition goes. (1)

verses.text:
तमृषिः पुरुषव्याघ्रं प्रेक्ष्य प्राञ्जलिमागतम्।
हुताग्निहोत्रो भरतं भरद्वाजोऽभ्यभाषत॥ २॥
verses.m: Perceiving that tiger among men arrived with folded hands and having poured oblations into the sacred fire, Sage Bharadwāja spoke to Bharata as follows : (2)

verses.text:
कच्चिदत्र सुखा रात्रिस्तवास्मद्विषये गता।
समग्रस्ते जनः कच्चिदातिथ्ये शंस मेऽनघ॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Tell me, O sinless one, was your night happily spent here in this hermitage of ours? Were all your men fully gratified with the hospitality shown to them?’’ (3)

verses.text:
तमुवाचाञ्जलिं कृत्वा भरतोऽभिप्रणम्य च।
आश्रमादुपनिष्क्रान्तमृषिमुत्तमतेजसम् ॥ ४॥
verses.m: Folding his hands, and bowing down low before him, Bharata replied as follows to the sage, who was invested with the highest glory, and had come out of the hermitage to meet him : (4)

verses.text:
सुखोषितोऽस्मि भगवन् समग्रबलवाहनः।
बलवत्तर्पितश्चाहं बलवान् भगवंस्त्वया॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I spent the night comfortably with my entire army and all my animals. And I with my army was fully sated by you, O venerable Sir. (5)

verses.text:
अपेतक्लमसंतापाः सुभिक्षाः सुप्रतिश्रयाः।
अपि प्रेष्यानुपादाय सर्वे स्म सुसुखोषिताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Including even servants we have all spent our time most happily, relieved of our fatigue and discomfort, richly supplied with food and drink and lodge in excellent houses. (6)

verses.text:
आमन्त्रयेऽहं भगवन् कामं त्वामृषिसत्तम।
समीपं प्रस्थितं भ्रातुर्मैत्रेणेक्षस्व चक्षुषा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I fervently entreat you, O venerable Sir: pray, regard me, set out towards the presence of my elder brother, with a benign look, O jewel among sages ! (7)

verses.text:
आश्रमं तस्य धर्मज्ञ धार्मिकस्य महात्मनः।
आचक्ष्व कतमो मार्गः कियानिति च शंस मे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Tell me the location of the hermitage of that pious and high-souled prince, O knower of what is right, and also let me know which route leads to it and how long it is.” (8)

verses.text:
इति पृष्टस्तु भरतं भ्रातुर्दर्शनलालसम्।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा भरद्वाजो महातपाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Questioned thus, Bharadwāja, for his part, who is endowed with exceptional glory and noted for his great asceticism, replied as follows to Bharata, who was eager to secure the blessed sight of his elder brother : (9)

verses.text:
भरतार्धतृतीयेषु योजनेष्वजने वने।
चित्रकूटगिरिस्तत्र रम्यनिर्झरकाननः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “At a distance of two and a half Yojanas* or twenty miles from here in the midst of a forest uninhabited by men other than ascetics, there stands a well-known mountain named Citrakūṭa, abounding in lovely caves and groves. (10)

verses.text:
उत्तरं पार्श्वमासाद्य तस्य मन्दाकिनी नदी।
पुष्पितद्रुमसंछन्ना रम्यपुष्पितकानना॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Touching its northern side flows the river Mandākinī, shaded by trees in blossom and hemmed with lovely groves laden with flowers. (11)

verses.text:
अनन्तरं तत्सरितश्चित्रकूटं च पर्वतम्।
तयोः पर्णकुटीं तात तत्र तौ वसतो ध्रुवम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Not far from that river and adjacent to the Citrakūṭa hill, you will find the hut of the two brothers, made of leafy twigs; the two brothers undoubtedly dwell in that hut. (12)

verses.text:
दक्षिणेन च मार्गेण सव्यदक्षिणमेव च।
गजवाजिसमाकीर्णां वाहिनीं वाहिनीपते॥ १३॥
वाहयस्व महाभाग ततो द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्।
प्रयाणमिति च श्रुत्वा राजराजस्य योषितः॥ १४॥
हित्वा यानानि यानार्हा ब्राह्मणं पर्यवारयन्।
वेपमाना कृशा दीना सह देव्या सुमित्रया॥ १५॥
कौसल्या तत्र जग्राह कराभ्यां चरणौ मुनेः।
असमृद्धेन कामेन सर्वलोकस्य गर्हिता॥ १६॥
कैकेयी तत्र जग्राह चरणौ सव्यपत्रपा।
तं प्रदक्षिणमागम्य भगवन्तं महामुनिम्॥ १७॥
अदूराद् भरतस्यैव तस्थौ दीनमनास्तदा।
तत्र पप्रच्छ भरतं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Leaving by the southern route (proceeding along the southern bank of the Yamunā) take the army full of elephants and horses along the bye-path turning to the left and proceeding southward, O lord of the army ! Proceeding along that route you will be able to behold Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O highly fortunate prince !” Nay, hearing the talk going on about the journey to Citrakūṭa, the consorts of the deceased emperor, Kausalyā and others, stood encircling the Brāhmaṇa (Bharadwāja), leaving their chariots, even though they deserved to remain in their vehicles because of their sex, old age and high rank. Of them Kausalyā—who was quaking through old age and emotion, was emaciated through grief caused by the loss of her husband and afflicted because of her separation from Śrī Rāma—while Queen Sumitrā clasped the sage’s feet with both her hands. Kaikeyī too—who was condemned by the whole world because of her ambition to see her son appointed as Prince Regent of Ayodhyā having not been fulfilled, clasped the sage’s feet with bashfulness because of her having brought about the banishment of Śrī Rāma. Having gone round that venerable and eminent sage clockwise, she stood close to Bharata himself, sad at heart because of her designs having been frustrated on that occasion and the ignoming she had suffered. At that time the eminent sage Bharadwāja spoke to Bharata as follows : (13—18)

verses.text:
विशेषं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि मातॄणां तव राघव।
एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो भरद्वाजेन धार्मिकः॥ १९॥
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यं वचनकोविदः।
यामिमां भगवन् दीनां शोकानशनकर्शिताम्॥ २०॥
पितुर्हि महिषीं देवीं देवतामिव पश्यसि।
एषां तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्॥ २१॥
कौसल्या सुषुवे रामं धातारमदितिर्यथा।
अस्या वामभुजं श्लिष्टा या सा तिष्ठति दुर्मनाः॥ २२॥
इयं सुमित्रा दुःखार्ता देवी राज्ञश्च मध्यमा।
कर्णिकारस्य शाखेव शीर्णपुष्पा वनान्तरे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I seek to know the particulars concerning your mothers, O scion of Raghu!” Addressed thus by Bharadwāja, the pious Bharata, for his part, who was a master of expression, made the following answer with folded hands : “This godlike Queen Kausalyā, the seniormost consort of my father, whom indeed you see here afflicted and emaciated through fasting on account of grief, O venerable Sir, brought forth that tiger among men, Śrī Rāma—who takes gallant strides like a lion—even as Aditi (the mother of gods) gave birth to Upendra (Lord Vāmana, so-called because he was a younger brother to Indra). Here is the celebrated Sumitrā, the middle queen of the king, stricken with agony, who stands disconsolate at heart clinging to the left arm of Kausalyā and looking like a branch of Karṇikāra tree with withered flowers standing in the interior of a grove. (19—23)

verses.text:
एतस्यास्तौ सुतौ देव्याः कुमारौ देववर्णिनौ।
उभौ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ वीरौ सत्यपराक्रमौ॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Both Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, those two heroic princes of godlike appearance and unfailing prowess, are the sons of this godly lady. (24)

verses.text:
यस्याः कृते नरव्याघ्रौ जीवनाशमितो गतौ।
राजा पुत्रविहीनश्च स्वर्गं दशरथो गतः॥ २५॥
क्रोधनामकृतप्रज्ञां दृप्तां सुभगमानिनीम्।
ऐश्वर्यकामां कैकेयीमनार्यामार्यरूपिणीम्॥ २६॥
ममैतां मातरं विद्धि नृशंसां पापनिश्चयाम्।
यतोमूलं हि पश्यामि व्यसनं महदात्मनः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Know this irate, vain, vulgar, though noble to all appearance, and cruel Kaikeyī, my mother of uncultured mind and sinful resolve, who esteems herself good-looking and is covetous of power, nay, thanks to whose designs, Srī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two tigers among men, have reached here, the end of their life in the form of exile in the forest, which is fraught with dangers at every step, while King Daśaratha, having been deprived of his two sons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, has ascended to heaven and whom I consider to be the root cause of the great adversity that has befallen me.” (25—27)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा नरशार्दूलो बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा।
विनिःश्वस्य स ताम्राक्षः क्रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Having uttered these words in a voice choked with tears and his eyes reddened through anger mixed with grief, that tiger among men began to draw a deep audible breath like a cobra hissing in wrath. (28)

verses.text:
भरद्वाजो महर्षिस्तं ब्रुवन्तं भरतं तदा।
प्रत्युवाच महाबुद्धिरिदं वचनमर्थवित्॥ २९॥
verses.m: To the said Bharata, who was speaking thus, Bharadwāja, the eminent sage, who was gifted with great intelligence and who knew everything, made the following answer : (29)

verses.text:
न दोषेणावगन्तव्या कैकेयी भरत त्वया।
रामप्रव्राजनं ह्येतत् सुखोदर्कं भविष्यति॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Kaikeyī, O Bharata, should not be regarded by you as guilty, for this banishment of Śrī Rāma will result in happiness to all. (30)

verses.text:
देवानां दानवानां च ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्।
हितमेव भविष्यद्धि रामप्रव्राजनादिह॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “In fact, good alone in this universe will result from the exile of Śrī Rāma to gods, demons and Ṛṣis, who contemplate on the Supreme Self.” (31)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य तु संसिद्धः कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम्।
आमन्त्र्य भरतः सैन्यं युज्यतामिति चाब्रवीत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Greeting the sage and going round him clockwise, and taking leave of him, Bharata, for his part, who had achieved his object by coming to know the whereabouts of Śrī Rāma and receiving the benedictions of the sage, commanded the army in the following words : “Let preparations be made for the journey.” (32)

verses.text:
ततो वाजिरथान् युक्त्वा दिव्यान् हेमविभूषितान्।
अध्यारोहत् प्रयाणार्थं बहून् बहुविधो जनः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Then, having joined the horses to their many excellent chariots embellished with gold, the different kinds of people ascended them for the march. (33)

verses.text:
गजकन्या गजाश्चैव हेमकक्ष्याः पताकिनः।
जीमूता इव घर्मान्ते सघोषाः सम्प्रतस्थिरे॥ ३४॥
verses.m: She-elephants and male elephants provided with girths of gold and flags marched in body, distinguished by the sound of bells, like thundering clouds at the close of summer. (34)

verses.text:
विविधान्यपि यानानि महान्ति च लघूनि च।
प्रययुः सुमहार्हाणि पादैरपि पदातयः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: People drove in various highly precious conveyances, big as well as small; while those travelling on foot proceeded on foot. (35)

verses.text:
अथ यानप्रवेकैस्तु कौसल्याप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः।
रामदर्शनकांक्षिण्यः प्रययुर्मुदितास्तदा॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Then departed full of joy in excellent vehicles ladies headed by Kausalyā, desirous as they were of seeing Śrī Rāma at that moment. (36)

verses.text:
चन्द्रार्कतरुणाभासां नियुक्तां शिबिकां शुभाम्।
आस्थाय प्रययौ श्रीमान् भरतः सपरिच्छदः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Ascending a lovely palanquin possessing the splendour of the midday sun and the full moon and borne by four men, proceeded the glorious Bharata with the outfit for travelling. (37)

verses.text:
सा प्रयाता महासेना गजवाजिसमाकुला।
दक्षिणां दिशमावृत्य महामेघ इवोत्थितः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Full of elephants and horses, that huge army on its march looked like a vast cloud burst upon the view, enveloping the southern quarter. (38)

verses.text:
वनानि च व्यतिक्रम्य जुष्टानि मृगपक्षिभिः।
गङ्गायाः परवेलायां गिरिष्वथ नदीष्वपि॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Traversing woodlands inhabited by deer and birds and hemming mountains as well as rivers beyond the western bank of the Gaṅgā flowing in a southerly direction, the army moved along. (39)

verses.text:
सा सम्प्रहृष्टद्विपवाजियूथा
वित्रासयन्ती मृगपक्षिसंघान्।
महद्वनं तत् प्रविगाहमाना
रराज सेना भरतस्य तत्र॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Striking the hosts of deer and birds inhabiting that region with terror, while penetrating through that extensive forest in the precincts of Citrakūṭa, the said army of Bharata, consisting as it did of overjoyed elephants and horses,looked charming on that spot. (40)

verses.text:
तया महत्या यायिन्या ध्वजिन्या वनवासिनः।
अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ताः सयूथाः सम्प्रदुद्रुवुः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hard pressed by that huge moving army, the leaders of herds of wild elephants and so on in rut ran away helter-skelter alongwith their herds. (1)

verses.text:
ऋक्षाः पृषतमुख्याश्च रुरवश्च समन्ततः।
दृश्यन्ते वनवाटेषु गिरिष्वपि नदीषु च॥ २॥
verses.m: Bears, the leaders of spotted deer as well as the deer without spots known by the name of Rurus, were seen running everywhere on the tracks of the forest, on mountains as well as along river banks. (2)

verses.text:
स सम्प्रतस्थे धर्मात्मा प्रीतो दशरथात्मजः।
वृतो महत्या नादिन्या सेनया चतुरङ्गया॥ ३॥
