verses.m: Followed by a huge army consisting of four limbs, viz., chariots, horsemen, elephants and foot soldiers and full of noise (caused by the rattling of chariot wheels, the neighing of horses and the trumpeting of elephants) Bharata (son of Daśaratha), whose mind was given to piety, delightfully proceeded alongwith others in the hope of meeting Śrī Rāma. (3)

verses.text:
सागरौघनिभा सेना भरतस्य महात्मनः।
महीं संछादयामास प्रावृषि द्यामिवाम्बुदः॥ ४॥
verses.m: The army of the high-souled Bharata, which resembled the high-tide of an ocean, overran the land even as a cloud over-spreads the sky during the monsoon. (4)

verses.text:
तुरंगौघैरवतता वारणैश्च महाबलैः।
अनालक्ष्या चिरं कालं तस्मिन् काले बभूव सा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Covered all over by hosts of horses and very mighty elephants, the ground at that time became invisible for a long period. (5)

verses.text:
स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं सम्परिश्रान्तवाहनः।
उवाच वचनं श्रीमान् वसिष्ठं मन्त्रिणां वरम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having covered a long distance, the glorious Bharata, whose animals were now fully exhausted, submitted as follows to Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of his counsellors : (6)

verses.text:
यादृशं लक्ष्यते रूपं यथा चैव मया श्रुतम्।
व्यक्तं प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “From the topography of this region as it is observed by us as well as from what has been heard by me about it, it is clear that we have reached that area of which Sage Bharadwāja spoke to us. (7)

verses.text:
अयं गिरिश्चित्रकूटस्तथा मन्दाकिनी नदी।
एतत् प्रकाशते दूरान्नीलमेघनिभं वनम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Here is the Citrakūṭa hill and there is the river Mandākinī. And here comes into view the forest looking like a blue cloud from a distance. (8)

verses.text:
गिरेः सानूनि रम्याणि चित्रकूटस्य सम्प्रति।
वारणैरवमृद्यन्ते मामकैः पर्वतोपमैः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The lovely peaks of the Citrakūṭa mountain are being trampled at present by my elephants resembling so many hills. (9)

verses.text:
मुञ्चन्ति कुसुमान्येते नगाः पर्वतसानुषु।
नीला इवातपापाये तोयं तोयधरा घनाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Shaken by the elephants, the yonder trees shed flowers on the hill-tops even as dark rain-bearing clouds pour water at the end of summer.” (10)

verses.text:
किंनराचरितं देशं पश्य शत्रुघ्न पर्वते।
हयैः समन्तादाकीर्णं मकरैरिव सागरम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Turning to Śatrughna, Bharata continued : “Behold, O Śatrughna, the region on the upper part of the mountain, frequented till now by Kinnaras, now overrun on all sides by horses even as a sea is infested by alligators. (11)

verses.text:
एते मृगगणा भान्ति शीघ्रवेगाः प्रचोदिताः।
वायुप्रविद्धाः शरदि मेघजाला इवाम्बरे॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Running with quick speed as urged forward by the troops, these herds of deer look charming like masses of clouds sailing in the sky when driven by the wind in autumn. (12)

verses.text:
कुर्वन्ति कुसुमापीडान् शिरःसु सुरभीनमी।
मेघप्रकाशैः फलकैर्दाक्षिणात्या नरा यथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Like men of the south, these troops distinguished by shields resembling clouds in hue wear fragrant floral ornaments on their heads. (13)

verses.text:
निष्कूजमिव भूत्वेदं वनं घोरप्रदर्शनम्।
अयोध्येव जनाकीर्णा सम्प्रति प्रतिभाति मे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Getting crowded with men, this forest, which was noiseless and wore a terrifying look till now, now appears to me like Ayodhyā. (14)

verses.text:
खुरैरुदीरितो रेणुर्दिवं प्रच्छाद्य तिष्ठति।
तं वहत्यनिलः शीघ्रं कुर्वन्निव मम प्रियम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The dust raised by the hoofs of the horses and other animals hangs over the sky. The wind blows it away quickly as though doing a kindly act to me by making the landscape visible to me. (15)

verses.text:
स्यन्दनांस्तुरगोपेतान् सूतमुख्यैरधिष्ठितान्।
एतान् सम्पततः शीघ्रं पश्य शत्रुघ्न कानने॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Behold these chariots, drawn by horses and controlled by the best of charioteers, advancing rapidly through the forest eager as their occupants are to see Śrī Rāma, O Śatrughna ! (16)

verses.text:
एतान् वित्रासितान् पश्य बर्हिणः प्रियदर्शनान्।
एवमापततः शैलमधिवासं पतत्त्रिणः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Behold these peacocks—which are so delightful to look at and are greatly frightened by the sight of the army—hastening thus towards the mountain, the abode of birds. (17)

verses.text:
अतिमात्रमयं देशो मनोज्ञः प्रतिभाति मे।
तापसानां निवासोऽयं व्यक्तं स्वर्गपथोऽनघ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “This region appears most enchanting to me. This home of ascetics is clearly a road to heaven, O sinless one ! (18)

verses.text:
मृगा मृगीभिः सहिता बहवः पृषता वने।
मनोज्ञरूपा लक्ष्यन्ते कुसुमैरिव चित्रिताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Many spotted deer accompanied by their hinds and endowed with enchanting forms appear as though decorated with flowers. (19)

verses.text:
साधु सैन्याः प्रतिष्ठन्तां विचिन्वन्तु च काननम्।
यथा तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ दृश्येते रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Let troops go forward in an unobtrusive manner and examine the forest, so that those two tigers among men, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, may be found out.” (20)

verses.text:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा पुरुषाः शस्त्रपाणयः।
विविशुस्तद्वनं शूरा धूमाग्रं ददृशुस्ततः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Hearing Bharata’s command, gallant troops with arms in their hands entered that forest and presently saw a column of smoke rising at some distance. (21)

verses.text:
ते समालोक्य धूमाग्रमूचुर्भरतमागताः।
नामनुष्ये भवत्यग्निर्व्यक्तमत्रैव राघवौ॥ २२॥
verses.m: Clearly perceiving a column of smoke they approached Bharata and submitted, “There can be no fire in a place uninhabited by human beings. Evidently Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, dwell on this very spot. (22)

verses.text:
अथ नात्र नरव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ परंतपौ।
अन्ये रामोपमाः सन्ति व्यक्तमत्र तपस्विनः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “If the two princes, who are veritable tigers among men and the scorchers of their enemy, are not here, obviously there are other ascetics like Śrī Rāma on this spot.” (23)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्तेषां वचनं साधुसम्मतम्।
सैन्यानुवाच सर्वांस्तानमित्रबलमर्दनः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid submission of the soldiers, which was esteemed even by pious men, Bharata, who was capable of crushing a hostile army, spoke to all those troops as follows : (24)

verses.text:
यत्ता भवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तु नेतो गन्तव्यमग्रतः।
अहमेव गमिष्यामि सुमन्त्रो धृतिरेव च॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Let you remain vigilant where you are; you should not proceed farther than this place. I shall go myself to meet Śrī Rāma, as also Sumantra and Dhṛti, two trusted ministers of King Daśaratha.” (25)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्ततः सैन्यास्तत्र तस्थुः समन्ततः।
भरतो यत्र धूमाग्रं तत्र दृष्टिं समादधत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Commanded thus by Bharata, the troops thereupon remained stationed all round on that very spot; while Bharata fixed his gaze on the spot where a column of smoke was visible. (26)

verses.text:
व्यवस्थिता या भरतेन सा चमू-
र्निरीक्षमाणापि च भूमिमग्रतः।
बभूव हृष्टा नचिरेण जानती
प्रियस्य रामस्य समागमं तदा॥ २७॥
verses.m: Even though perceiving the place (where Śrī Rāma was supposed to be) ahead, the aforesaid army, which was held up on that spot by Bharata, felt rejoiced even then anticipating (as they did) their meeting with their beloved Rāma at no distant hour. (27)

verses.text:
दीर्घकालोषितस्तस्मिन् गिरौ गिरिवरप्रियः।
वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकांक्षन् स्वं च चित्तं विलोभयन्॥ १॥
अथ दाशरथिश्चित्रं चित्रकूटमदर्शयत्।
भार्याममरसंकाशः शचीमिव पुरंदरः॥ २॥
verses.m: Seeking to please Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, and diverting his own mind, Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who was fond of excellent mountains and had now lived on that mountain, Citrakūṭa, for a long time covering a period of about three months, nay, who shone brightly as a god, showed to his spouse the beauties of the wonderful Citrakūṭa, deservedly so-called, consisting as it did of many wonders, and Indra, the destroyer of strongholds, would show the beauties of the Nandana grove to Śacī, his consort : (1-2)

verses.text:
न राज्यभ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः।
मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “On seeing this delightful hill neither loss of sovereignty nor separation from my near and dear ones vexes my mind, O good lady ! (3)

verses.text:
पश्येममचलं भद्रे नानाद्विजगणायुतम्।
शिखरैः खमिवोद्विद्धैर्धातुमद्भिर्विभूषितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Behold this mountain, inhabited by flocks of birds of every description, and adorned with peaks rich in minerals, that stand piercing the skies, as it were, O blessed one ! (4)

verses.text:
केचिद् रजतसंकाशाः केचित् क्षतजसंनिभाः।
पीतमाञ्जिष्ठवर्णाश्च केचिन्मणिवरप्रभाः॥ ५॥
पुष्पार्ककेतकाभाश्च केचिज्ज्योतीरसप्रभाः।
विराजन्तेऽचलेन्द्रस्य देशा धातुविभूषिताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Adorned with minerals, parts of this king of mountains shine brightly, some glittering like silver, some blood-red, some yellowish, some red as madder, some sparkling like the foremost of gems, some possessing the lustre of topaz and crystal and the hue of the Ketaka flower and others shinning like stars and mercury. (5-6)

verses.text:
नानामृगगणैर्द्वीपितरक्ष्वृक्षगणैर्वृतः।
अदुष्टैर्भात्ययं शैलो बहुपक्षिसमाकुलः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Teeming with herds of deer of every description and hosts of harmless tigers, leopards and bears, and crowded with numerous birds, this mountain looks charming. (7)

verses.text:
आम्रजम्ब्वसनैर्लोध्रैः प्रियालैः पनसैर्धवैः।
अङ्कोलैर्भव्यतिनिशैर्बिल्वतिन्दुकवेणुभिः ॥ ८॥
काश्मर्यारिष्टवरणैर्मधूकैस्तिलकैरपि।
बदर्यामलकैर्नीपैर्वेत्रधन्वनबीजकैः ॥ ९॥
पुष्पवद्भिः फलोपेतैश्छायावद्भिर्मनोरमैः।
एवमादिभिराकीर्णः श्रियं पुष्यत्ययं गिरिः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Abounding in umbrageous trees laden with flowers and fruits and pleasing to the mind, the foremost of which are mangoes, rose-apples and Asanas, Lodhras, Priyālas (commonly called Payals), bread-fruit trees, Dhavas, Aṅkolas, Bhavyas and Tiniśas, Bilvas (Bel trees), Tindukas and bamboos, Kāśmarīs, margosas and Varaṇas, Madhūkas and Tilakas, jujube trees and trees bearing emblic myrobalans, Kadambas, cane, Dhanvanas and pomegranates, called Bījaka because they abound in seeds, this mountain thereby is enhancing its own beauty. (8–10)

verses.text:
शैलप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पश्येमान् कामहर्षणान्।
किंनरान् द्वन्द्वशो भद्रे रममाणान् मनस्विनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Behold these Kinnaras rejoicing at will and sporting in couples on the level grounds on the tops of this mountain with their minds focussed on each other. (11)

verses.text:
शाखावसक्तान् खड्गांश्च प्रवराण्यम्बराणि च।
पश्य विद्याधरस्त्रीणां क्रीडोद्देशान् मनोरमान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Also behold suspended on the boughs of trees the swords of the Kinnaras as also the excellent garments of Vidyādhara women as well as their sporting-grounds, so pleasing to the mind. (12)

verses.text:
जलप्रपातैरुद्भेदैर्निष्पन्दैश्च क्वचित् क्वचित्।
स्रवद्भिर्भात्ययं शैलः स्रवन्मद इव द्विपः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “With its cascades and springs flowing here and there this mountain looks like an elephant with ichor exuding from its temples. (13)

verses.text:
गुहासमीरणो गन्धान् नानापुष्पभवान् बहून्।
घ्राणतर्पणमभ्येत्य कं नरं न प्रहर्षयेत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “What man will the wind issuing from the caves, catching on its way numerous odours emanating from various flowers, not enrapture, regaling his olfactory sense? (14)

verses.text:
यदीह शरदोऽनेकास्त्वया सार्धमनिन्दिते।
लक्ष्मणेन च वत्स्यामि न मां शोकः प्रधर्षति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “If I dwell in this forest for many autumns with you and Lakṣmaṇa, O irreproachable lady, grief will not overpower me. (15)

verses.text:
बहुपुष्पफले रम्ये नानाद्विजगणायुते।
विचित्रशिखरे ह्यस्मिन् रतवानस्मि भामिनि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I am really enamoured of this enjoyable mountain containing abundant flowers and fruits, nay, inhabited by flocks of birds of every description and adorned with charming peaks, O proud lady ! (16)

verses.text:
अनेन वनवासेन मम प्राप्तं फलद्वयम्।
पितुश्चानृण्यता धर्मे भरतस्य प्रियं तथा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “A twofold gain has been secured by me through this exile of mine, viz., that I have got square with my father, who was devoted to piety in the form of truthfulness, and the pleasure of Bharata has been accomplished. (17)

verses.text:
वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह।
पश्यन्ती विविधान् भावान् मनोवाक्कायसम्मतान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Do you feel happy in Citrakūṭa with me, beholding various objects agreeable to your mind, speech and body? (18)

verses.text:
इदमेवामृतं प्राहू राज्ञि राजर्षयः परे।
वनवासं भवार्थाय प्रेत्य मे प्रपितामहाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “My forefathers, Manu and others, who were all foremost royal sages, O my queen, have pronounced such disciplined residence in the forest as nectar-like and as conducive to cessation from rebirth after death. (19)

verses.text:
शिलाः शैलस्य शोभन्ते विशालाः शतशोऽभितः।
बहुला बहुलैर्वर्णैर्नीलपीतसितारुणैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Large rocks of various sizes and shapes and distinguished by different colours such as blue, yellow, white and ruddy shine brightly in hundreds on every side of the mountain. (20)

verses.text:
निशि भान्त्यचलेन्द्रस्य हुताशनशिखा इव।
ओषध्यः स्वप्रभालक्ष्म्या भ्राजमानाः सहस्रशः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Shining with the wealth of their splendour, herbs in their thousands sparkle like flames of fire on the top of the mountain at night. (21)

verses.text:
केचित् क्षयनिभा देशाः केचिदुद्यानसंनिभाः।
केचिदेकशिला भान्ति पर्वतस्यास्य भामिनि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Some parts of this mountain consisting as they do of dense clusters of Palāsa trees, look like houses, while others, which abound in flowers, appear like gardens, while still others consist of huge single blocks of stone, O proud lady ! (22)

verses.text:
भित्त्वेव वसुधां भाति चित्रकूटः समुत्थितः।
चित्रकूटस्य कूटोऽयं दृश्यते सर्वतः शुभः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Citrakūṭa appears as though risen, having split the earth. Nay, this peak of Citrakūṭa looks charming on all sides. (23)

verses.text:
कुष्ठस्थगरपुंनागभूर्जपत्रोत्तरच्छदान्।
कामिनां स्वास्तरान् पश्य कुशेशयदलायुतान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Behold the cosy beds of voluptuaries covered with the leaves of lilies, Sthagara trees, Punnāga trees and Bhūrja trees as counterpane and overspread with lotus leaves. (24)

verses.text:
मृदिताश्चापविद्धाश्च दृश्यन्ते कमलस्रजः।
कामिभिर्वनिते पश्य फलानि विविधानि च॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Here are seen, O darling, wreaths of lotus flowers crushed and cast aside by voluptuaries and also behold fruits of various kinds enjoyed and thrown away by them. (25)

verses.text:
वस्वौकसारां नलिनीमतीत्यैवोत्तरान् कुरून्।
पर्वतश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ बहुमूलफलोदकः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Having abundant roots, fruit and water, the yonder Citrakūṭa mountain surpasses even Vaswaukasārā (more popularly known by the name of Alakā, the capital of Kubera, the god of riches), Nalinī, the capital of Indra, better known by the name of Amarāvatī and the territory of the Uttarakurus in loveliness. (26)

verses.text:
इमं तु कालं वनिते विजह्रिवां-
स्त्वया च सीते सह लक्ष्मणेन।
रतिं प्रपत्स्ये कुलधर्मवर्धिनीं
सतां पथि स्वैर्नियमैः परैः स्थितः॥ २७॥
verses.m: If for my part, O darling, I shall be able to spend this period of exile extending over fourteen years merrily as though in sport with you, O Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, adhering to the path trodden by the virtuous and conforming to the highest discipline imposed by myself, I shall derive joy enhancing the piety of my race.” (27)

verses.text:
अथ शैलाद् विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेश्वरः।
अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Then, turning away from the mountain, Śrī Rāma, the prospective ruler of the kingdom of Kosala, pointed out to Sītā, daughter of the king of Mithilā, the delightful river Mandākinī, carrying holy waters. (1)

verses.text:
अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां चन्द्रचारुनिभाननाम्।
विदेहराजस्य सुतां रामो राजीवलोचनः॥ २॥
verses.m: Nay, the lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma spoke as follows to Sītā, the daughter of the king of Videhas, of charming limbs and with a lovely countenance resembling the moon : (2)

verses.text:
विचित्रपुलिनां रम्यां हंससारससेविताम्।
कुसुमैरुपसम्पन्नां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्॥ ३॥
नानाविधैस्तीररुहैर्वृतां पुष्पफलद्रुमैः।
राजन्तीं राजराजस्य नलिनीमिव सर्वतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Behold the beautiful river Mandākinī with its delightful banks—a stream inhabited by swans and cranes and rich in flowers, nay, hemmed in with trees of various kinds growing on its banks and laden with flowers and fruits—and spreading its charms all round like the lake Saugandhika of Kubera, the ruler of Yakṣas. (3-4)

verses.text:
मृगयूथनिपीतानि कलुषाम्भांसि साम्प्रतम्।
तीर्थानि रमणीयानि रतिं संजनयन्ति मे॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The delightful fords, even though their waters are turbid just at present evidently because herds of deer have drunk their fill from them, exercise their charm on me. (5)

verses.text:
जटाजिनधराः काले वल्कलोत्तरवाससः।
ऋषयस्त्ववगाहन्ते नदीं मन्दाकिनीं प्रिये॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Sages, for their part, wearing matted locks and with deerskin wrapped about their loins and having the bark of trees for their upper garment take a dip in the river Mandākinī at the appointed hour, my darling ! (6)

verses.text:
आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते नियमादूर्ध्वबाहवः।
एते परे विशालाक्षि मुनयः संशितव्रताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Here are other ascetics of austere vows praying to the sun-god with uplifted arms according to the scriptural injunctions, O lady with big eyes ! (7)

verses.text:
मारुतोद्धूतशिखरैः प्रनृत्त इव पर्वतः।
पादपैः पुष्पपत्राणि सृजद्भिरभितो नदीम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “With its trees—whose tops are shaken by the wind—shedding flowers and leaves all along the river, the mountain looks as if it has started dancing. (8)

verses.text:
क्वचिन्मणिनिकाशोदां क्वचित् पुलिनशालिनीम्।
क्वचित् सिद्धजनाकीर्णां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Behold the river Mandākinī whose waters are sparkling like pearls at one place, nay, which looks charming with its sandy banks at another and which is crowded with Siddhas (a class of semi-divine beings endowed with mystic powers from their very birth) at a third place. (9)

verses.text:
निर्धूतान् वायुना पश्य विततान् पुष्पसंचयान्।
पोप्लूयमानानपरान् पश्य त्वं तनुमध्यमे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Behold you heaps of flowers shaken down by the wind and scattered on both the banks of the river and other heaps continuously floating along the current, O lady with a slender waist ! (10)

verses.text:
पश्यैतद्वल्गुवचसो रथाङ्गाह्वयना द्विजाः।
अधिरोहन्ति कल्याणि निष्कूजन्तः शुभा गिरः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Behold how these melodious Cakrawāka birds are ascending the banks uttering charming notes, O blessed lady ! (11)

verses.text:
दर्शनं चित्रकूटस्य मन्दाकिन्याश्च शोभने।
अधिकं पुरवासाच्च मन्ये तव च दर्शनात्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I value the sight of Citrakūṭa as well as of the Mandākinī more than even residence in the capital particularly because of your sight, O charming lady ! (12)

verses.text:
विधूतकल्मषैः सिद्धैस्तपोदमशमान्वितैः।
नित्यविक्षोभितजलां विगाहस्व मया सह॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Take a dip with me in this river, whose waters are ever agitated through daily bath by Siddhas endowed with austerity and control of the senses and mind and whose sins have been completely shaken off. (13)

verses.text:
सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्।
कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Nay, freely take a dip in the river Mandākinī even as a friend would sport in the company of her friend, submerging out of fun the red and white lotuses in which the river abounds, O proud lady ! (14)

verses.text:
त्वं पौरजनवद् व्यालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम्।
मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Esteem you ever the dwellers in the forest as you would the citizens of Ayodhyā, the mountain Citrakūṭa as the city of Ayodhyā, and this river Mandākinī as the Sarayū, my darling ! (15)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणश्चैव धर्मात्मा मन्निदेशे व्यवस्थितः।
त्वं चानुकूला वैदेहि प्रीतिं जनयती मम॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Not only is Lakṣmaṇa, whose mind is given to righteousness, fully determined to carry out my command, but you too, O princess of the Videha kingdom, favourably disposed towards me, causing delight to me. (16)

verses.text:
उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं मधुमूलफलाशनः।
नायोध्यायै न राज्याय स्पृहये च त्वया सह॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Bathing thrice a day (every morning, midday and evening) and living on honey, roots and fruits with you, I long neither for Ayodhyā nor for its sovereignty ! (17)

verses.text:
इमां हि रम्यां गजयूथलोडितां
निपीततोयां गजसिंहवानरैः।
सुपुष्पितां पुष्पभरैरलंकृतां
न सोऽस्ति यः स्यान्न गतक्लमः सुखी॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Surely there is no one who will not be relieved of his fatigue and feel refreshed on taking a dip in this delightful river which is churned by herds of elephants, whose waters are partaken of without interruption by elephants, lions and monkeys alike, which is hemmed with trees laden with blossom and as such remains decked with loads of flowers all through the year.” (18)

verses.text:
इतीव रामो बहुसंगतं वचः
प्रियासहायः सरितं प्रति ब्रुवन्।
चचार रम्यं नयनाञ्जनप्रभं
स चित्रकूटं रघुवंशवर्धनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Offering many such cogent remarks concerning the aforesaid river, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, the promoter of the race of Raghu, wandered in the company of his beloved spouse, Sītā, over the lovely Citrakūṭa, which shone like a heap of collyrium. (19)

verses.text:
तां तदा दर्शयित्वा तु मैथिलीं गिरिनिम्नगाम्।
निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे सीतां मांसेन छन्दयन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having shown on that occasion the hilly stream, Mandākinī, to the aforesaid Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, Śrī Rāma for his part sat down on a single flat rock humouring Sītā with a description of the pulp of fruits fit for the consumption of ascetics as follows : (1)

verses.text:
इदं मेध्यमिदं स्वादु निष्टप्तमिदमग्निना।
एवमास्ते स धर्मात्मा सीतया सह राघवः॥ २॥
verses.m: “This fruit is fit for being offered as an oblation into the sacred fire, this is luscious and this bulb has been roasted well in fire.” In this way the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, whose mind was devoted to righteousness, spent his time with Sītā. (2)

verses.text:
तथा तत्रासतस्तस्य भरतस्योपयायिनः।
सैन्यरेणुश्च शब्दश्च प्रादुरास्तां नभस्पृशौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: While he remained sitting there as aforesaid, the dust raised by the army of Bharata, who was approaching Śrī Rāma, as well as their tramp, rose to the skies. (3)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे त्रस्ताः शब्देन महता ततः।
अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ताः सयूथाद् दुद्रुवुर्दिशः॥ ४॥
verses.m: In the meantime alarmed and agitated by that great noise, the lordly elephants in rut ran away from their herd in various directions. (4)

verses.text:
स तं सैन्यसमुद्धूतं शब्दं शुश्राव राघवः।
तांश्च विप्रद्रुतान् सर्वान् यूथपानन्ववैक्षत॥ ५॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Śrī Rāma heard that noise caused by the army and also perceived all those leaders of herds of elephants that had taken flight from their herd. (5)

verses.text:
तांश्च विप्रद्रुतान् दृष्ट्वा तं च श्रुत्वा महास्वनम्।
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Seeing them run away and also hearing that great noise, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, of resplendent glory : (6)

verses.text:
हन्त लक्ष्मण पश्येह सुमित्रा सुप्रजास्त्वया।
भीमस्तनितगम्भीरं तुमुलः श्रूयते स्वनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Hullo Lakṣmaṇa, Sumitrā in this world is blessed with a worthy son in you. See how this confused noise is being heard, deep as a terrible crash of thunder. (7)

verses.text:
गजयूथानि वारण्ये महिषा वा महावने।
वित्रासिता मृगाः सिंहैः सहसा प्रद्रुता दिशः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “How is it that herds of elephants in the forest or wild buffaloes in the great forest or deer have all of a sudden taken to flight helter-skelter in various directions as though scared by lions? (8)

verses.text:
राजा वा राजपुत्रो वा मृगयामटते वने।
अन्यद्वा श्वापदं किंचित् सौमित्रे ज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Is any king or prince going about hunting in the forest? Or has any other beast of prey appeared here? You ought to find this out, O son of Sumitrā ! (9)

verses.text:
सुदुश्चरो गिरिश्चायं पक्षिणामपि लक्ष्मण।
सर्वमेतद् यथातत्त्वमभिज्ञातुमिहार्हसि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Moreover this mountain, O Lakṣmaṇa, is most difficult of access even to birds of other parts. You ought, therefore, to ascertain all this correctly here.” (10)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणः संत्वरितः सालमारुह्य पुष्पितम्।
प्रेक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वाः पूर्वां दिशमवैक्षत॥ ११॥
verses.m: Enjoined thus, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa climbed up with great expedition a sal tree in blossom and, surveying all the quarters, fixed his gaze on the eastern quarter. (11)

verses.text:
उदङ्मुखः प्रेक्षमाणो ददर्श महतीं चमूम्।
गजाश्वरथसम्बाधां यत्तैर्युक्तां पदातिभिः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Looking intently with his face now turned northward he espied a large army thick with elephants, horses and chariots and conjoined with vigilant foot-soldiers. (12)

verses.text:
तामश्वरथसम्पूर्णां रथध्वजविभूषिताम्।
शशंस सेनां रामाय वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: He announced to Śrī Rāma the approach of that army abounding in horses and chariots and adorned with ensigns borne on chariots, and made the following submission : (13)

verses.text:
अग्निं संशमयत्वार्यः सीता च भजतां गुहाम्।
सज्यं कुरुष्व चापं च शरांश्च कवचं तथा॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Let your worthy self fully extinguish the fire lest the smoke issuing from it should attract the army to this spot and let Sītā seek a cave. Nay, keep ready your bow, as well as arrows and armour.” (14)

verses.text:
तं रामः पुरुषव्याघ्रो लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाच ह।
अङ्गावेक्षस्व सौमित्रे कस्येमां मन्यसे चमूम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: To the said Lakṣmaṇa, they say, Śrī Rāma, a veritable tiger among men, replied as follows : “Dear Lakṣmaṇa, please look carefully at the device of the ensign and tell me whose army you consider it to be.” (15)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
दिधक्षन्निव तां सेनां रुषितः पावको यथा॥ १६॥
verses.m: Commanded thus by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa for his part submitted as follows, gazing at the army as though keen to consume it like an angry fire : (16)

verses.text:
सम्पन्नं राज्यमिच्छंस्तु व्यक्तं प्राप्याभिषेचनम्।
आवां हन्तुं समभ्येति कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Evidently having secured consecration on the throne of Ayodhyā and keen to attain undisputed sovereignty, Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, for his part, comes fully prepared to kill us both. (17)

verses.text:
एष वै सुमहान् श्रीमान् विटपी सम्प्रकाशते।
विराजत्युज्ज्वलस्कन्धः कोविदारध्वजो रथे॥ १८॥
verses.m: “An ensign bearing the device of a Kovidāra tree with a white trunk really shines prominently over there on a chariot standing where that gigantic tree, rich in flowers and fruits etc., is clearly visible. (18)

verses.text:
भजन्त्येते यथाकाममश्वानारुह्य शीघ्रगान्।
एते भ्राजन्ति संहृष्टा गजानारुह्य सादिनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Mounting swift-going horses as they would, these horsemen are heading towards this spot. Mounting elephants, these riders on elephants too appear highly rejoiced while marching towards this place. (19)

verses.text:
गृहीतधनुषावावां गिरिं वीर श्रयावहे।
अथवेहैव तिष्ठावः संनद्धावुद्यतायुधौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Taking up our bows let us both station ourselves on the summit of the mountain, O heroic prince ! Or clothed with mail, let us continue on this very spot with uplifted weapons. (20)

verses.text:
अपि नौ वशमागच्छेत् कोविदारध्वजो रणे।
अपि द्रक्ष्यामि भरतं यत्कृते व्यसनं महत्॥ २१॥
त्वया राघव सम्प्राप्तं सीतया च मया तथा।
यन्निमित्तं भवान् राज्याच्च्युतो राघव शाश्वतात्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The ensign bearing the device of a Kovidāra tree will surely be brought under our control, and I am glad I shall be able to see face to face Bharata, on whose account great suffering has been undergone by you, O scion of Raghu, as well as by Sītā and myself, and for whose sake, O Rāma, you have been deprived of a kingdom which was ever yours. (21-22)

verses.text:
सम्प्राप्तोऽयमरिर्वीर भरतो वध्य एव हि।
भरतस्य वधे दोषं नाहं पश्यामि राघव॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Bharata over there, who has arrived in state as an adversary, surely deserves to be killed outright, O heroic prince ! I see no wrong in killing Bharata, O scion of Raghu ! (23)

verses.text:
पूर्वापकारिणं हत्वा न ह्यधर्मेण युज्यते।
पूर्वापकारी भरतस्त्यागेऽधर्मश्च राघव॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Killing a man who has wronged one earlier, one surely does not get contaminated with sin. Bharata has wronged you heretofore; hence there is sin only in leaving him alive, O scion of Raghu ! (24)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन् निहते कृत्स्नामनुशाधि वसुंधराम्।
अद्य पुत्रं हतं संख्ये कैकेयी राज्यकामुका॥ २५॥
मया पश्येत् सुदुःखार्ता हस्तिभिन्नमिव द्रुमम्।
कैकेयीं च वधिष्यामि सानुबन्धां सबान्धवाम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “When Bharata has been killed, rule over the entire globe. Sore stricken with sorrow, Kaikeyī, who is covetous of sovereignty, will find her son killed in battle by me like a tree uprooted by an elephant. I shall kill Kaikeyī too with her dependants and relations. (25-26)

verses.text:
कलुषेणाद्य महता मेदिनी परिमुच्यताम्।
अद्येमं संयतं क्रोधमसत्कारं च मानद॥ २७॥
मोक्ष्यामि शत्रुसैन्येषु कक्षेष्विव हुताशनम्।
अद्यैव चित्रकूटस्य काननं निशितैः शरैः॥ २८॥
छिन्दन् शत्रुशरीराणि करिष्ये शोणितोक्षितम्।
शरैर्निभिन्नहृदयान् कुञ्जरांस्तुरगांस्तथा॥ २९॥
श्वापदाः परिकर्षन्तु नरांश्च निहतान् मया।
शराणां धनुषश्चाहमनृणोऽस्मिन् महावने।
ससैन्यं भरतं हत्वा भविष्यामि न संशयः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Let the earth be purged of this sin in the shape of Kaikeyī. Today I shall release my repressed fury and scorn in the shape of arrows against the enemy’s forces even as one would spit fire on dried bushes, O bestower of honour! Tearing to pieces the bodies of the enemies with sharp-pointed arrows, I shall this very day drench the forest of Citrakūṭa with blood. Let beasts of prey drag hither and thither the elephants and horses, whose heart is pierced through with arrows, as well as the men that will be slain by me. Having killed Bharata with his army in this great forest I shall get square with my arrows and bow by supplying them with abundant food: there is no doubt about it.” (27—30)

verses.text:
सुसंरब्धं तु भरतं लक्ष्मणं क्रोधमूर्च्छितम्।
रामस्तु परिसान्त्व्याथ वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, for his part, pacified in everyway Lakṣmaṇa, who actually bore an utterly bellicose attitude towards Bharata and was beside himself with rage, and then spoke to him as follows : (1)

verses.text:
किमत्र धनुषा कार्यमसिना वा सचर्मणा।
महाबले महोत्साहे भरते स्वयमागते॥ २॥
verses.m: “When the very mighty Bharata, full of great longing to see me, has turned up in person, what purpose will be served at this moment with a bow or with a sword accompanied by a shield? (2)

verses.text:
पितुः सत्यं प्रतिश्रुत्य हत्वा भरतमाहवे।
किं करिष्यामि राज्येन सापवादेन लक्ष्मण॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Having given, in the first instance, my word of honour to implement the pledge of my father and killed Bharata in an encounter, O Lakṣmaṇa, what shall I do with a kingdom stained with infamy (that will be occasioned by my going back upon my word of honour and robbing Bharata of the gift bestowed on him by our father)? (3)

verses.text:
यद् द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्।
नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I am not going to accept a fortune that will descend on the destruction of my kinsfolk or friends any more than one would partake of dishes mixed with poison. (4)

verses.text:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च पृथिवीं चापि लक्ष्मण।
इच्छामि भवतामर्थे एतत् प्रतिशृणोमि ते॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I seek virtue, fortune, gratification of senses and even sovereignty of the earth, O Lakṣmana, only for you people, my brothers, and not for any personal gain: I give this word of honour to you. (5)

verses.text:
भ्रातॄणां संग्रहार्थं च सुखार्थं चापि लक्ष्मण।
राज्यमप्यहमिच्छामि सत्येनायुधमालभे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I seek sovereignty too only for the protection and gratification of my brothers, O Lakṣmaṇa: I swear by my bow. (6)

verses.text:
नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा।
नहीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The sovereignty of this globe, hemmed in by the sea, O gentle brother, is not difficult for me to acquire; but I do not covet even the position of Indra through unrighteousness, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (7)

verses.text:
यद् विना भरतं त्वां च शत्रुघ्नं वापि मानद।
भवेन्मम सुखं किंचिद् भस्म तत् कुरुतां शिखी॥ ८॥
verses.m: “If any joy comes to me without Bharata and yourself, or even without Śatrughna, O respecter of others, let fire reduce it to ashes. (8)

verses.text:
मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः।
मम प्राणैः प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥ ९॥
श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्।
जानक्या सहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषोत्तम॥ १०॥
स्नेहेनाक्रान्तहृदयः शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः।
द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽऽगतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I believe, O gallant brother, that hearing, when back in Ayodhyā, of myself having been actually exiled with Sītā (daughter of Janaka) and yourself, and having proceeded to the forest, wearing matted locks and clad in the bark of trees, O jewel among men, Bharata, who is so fond of his brothers, and is dearer to me than life itself, must have found his heart overwhelmed with affection and his mind distracted through grief and has surely come all the way to see me, bearing in mind the usage of his race in the shape of installing the eldest son on the throne on the death of a king and that the said Bharata has not come with any other motive. (9—11)

verses.text:
अम्बां च केकयीं रुष्य भरतश्चाप्रियं वदन्।
प्रसाद्य पितरं श्रीमान् राज्यं मे दातुमागतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, getting angry with mother Kaikeyī and speaking unkind words to her and having obtained the consent of our father, the glorious Bharata has evidently come to offer the throne to me. (12)

verses.text:
प्राप्तकालं यथैषोऽस्मान् भरतो द्रष्टुमर्हति।
अस्मासु मनसाप्येष नाहितं किंचिदाचरेत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “It is but opportune that Bharata sees us—in fact, he deserves to see us. He would not do any harm to us even with his mind. (13)

verses.text:
विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा नु किम्।
ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं यद् विशङ्कसे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I wonder when and what offence was given to you by Bharata in the past and when any such alarming thing was said by him that you mistrust Bharata today. (14)

verses.text:
नहि ते निष्ठुरं वाच्यो भरतो नाप्रियं वचः।
अहं ह्यप्रियमुक्तः स्यां भरतस्याप्रिये कृते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Bharata should under no circumstances be spoken harshly to nor should unkind words be addressed to him. If any offence is given to Bharata, indeed it would mean that I am told unpleasant things. (15)

verses.text:
कथं नु पुत्राः पितरं हन्युः कस्यांचिदापदि।
भ्राता वा भ्रातरं हन्यात् सौमित्रे प्राणमात्मनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How on earth can sons take the life of their father in any trying situation or how can a brother kill his own brother, his very life, O son of Sumitrā? (16)

verses.text:
यदि राज्यस्य हेतोस्त्वमिमां वाचं प्रभाषसे।
वक्ष्यामि भरतं दृष्ट्वा राज्यमस्मै प्रदीयताम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “If you utter these words, signifying your intention to kill Bharata for the sake of sovereignty, I shall speak to Bharata as follows on seeing him: ‘Let the kingdom be given away for good to Lakṣmaṇa.’ (17)

verses.text:
उच्यमानो हि भरतो मया लक्ष्मण तद्वचः।
राज्यमस्मै प्रयच्छेति बाढमित्येव मंस्यते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Being addressed by me in the words ‘Bestow the kingdom on Lakṣmaṇa,’ Bharata, O Lakṣmaṇa, will surely accept my command saying “amen !” (18)

verses.text:
तथोक्तो धर्मशीलेन भ्रात्रा तस्य हिते रतः।
लक्ष्मणः प्रविवेशेव स्वानि गात्राणि लज्जया॥ १९॥
verses.m: Admonished thus by his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma, of virtuous disposition, Lakṣmaṇa, who was devoted to the interests of the latter, hid himself in his own limbs, as it were, out of shame. (19)

verses.text:
तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणः श्रुत्वा व्रीडितः प्रत्युवाच ह।
त्वां मन्ये द्रष्टुमायातः पिता दशरथः स्वयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Put out of countenance to hear the aforesaid admonition, Lakṣmaṇa, they say, submitted as follows : “I believe our father, Emperor Daśaratha himself, has come to see you.” (20)

verses.text:
व्रीडितं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह।
एष मन्ये महाबाहुरिहास्मान् द्रष्टुमागतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Finding Lakṣmaṇa abashed, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, they say, replied as follows : “I too believe that the mighty-armed Emperor has personally come to see us here. (21)

verses.text:
अथवा नौ ध्रुवं मन्ये मन्यमानः सुखोचितौ।
वनवासमनुध्याय गृहाय प्रतिनेष्यति॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Nay, considering us to be deserving of comfort and bearing in mind the privations attendant on residence in a forest, father will, I believe, surely take us back home. (22)

verses.text:
इमां चाप्येष वैदेहीमत्यन्तसुखसेविनीम्।
पिता मे राघवः श्रीमान् वनादादाय यास्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Again, my aforesaid father, the glorious Daśaratha, a scion of Raghu, will return to the capital taking with him from the forest this Sītā (a princess of the Videha kingdom) too, who has always enjoyed the utmost amenities of life. (23)

verses.text:
एतौ तौ सम्प्रकाशेते गोत्रवन्तौ मनोरमौ।
वायुवेगसमौ वीरौ जवनौ तुरगोत्तमौ॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Here are to be clearly seen the two spirited and excellent fleet horses of noble breed, pleasing to the mind and vying with the wind in swiftness. (24)

verses.text:
स एष सुमहाकायः कम्पते वाहिनीमुखे।
नागः शत्रुंजयो नाम वृद्धस्तातस्य धीमतः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Here is the well-known gigantic and aged elephant, Śatruñjaya by name, of our wise father, rocking about at the head of the army. (25)

verses.text:
न तु पश्यामि तच्छत्रं पाण्डुरं लोकविश्रुतम्।
पितुर्दिव्यं महाभाग संशयो भवतीह मे॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I, however, do not behold that white heavenly umbrella of my father, well-known in the world, O highly blessed one ! Doubt on this point fills my mind.” (26)

verses.text:
वृक्षाग्रादवरोह त्वं कुरु लक्ष्मण मद्वचः।
इतीव रामो धर्मात्मा सौमित्रिं तमुवाच ह॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Do my bidding, O Lakṣmaṇa, and climb you down from the tree-top.” In these precise words did Śrī Rāma, whose mind was given to piety, address the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā: so the tradition goes. (27)

verses.text:
अवतीर्य तु सालाग्रात् तस्मात् स समितिंजयः।
लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Getting down from that top of the sāl tree, the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa, the conqueror of hostile forces, for his part, stood by the side of Śrī Rāma with folded hands. (28)

verses.text:
भरतेनाथ संदिष्टा सम्मर्दो न भवेदिति।
समन्तात् तस्य शैलस्य सेना वासमकल्पयत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Admonished by Bharata in the words: “Let there be no molestation to the hermitage of Śrī Rāma”, his army encamped round-about that mountain. (29)

verses.text:
अध्यर्धमिक्ष्वाकुचमूर्योजनं पर्वतस्य ह।
पार्श्वे न्यविशदावृत्य गजवाजिनराकुला॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Occupying an area of one Yojana and a half, they say, the army of Bharata, of Ikṣwāku’s line, full of elephants, horses and men, encamped by the side of the mountain. (30)

verses.text:
सा चित्रकूटे भरतेन सेना
धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य विधूय दर्पम्।
प्रसादनार्थं रघुनन्दनस्य
विरोचते नीतिमता प्रणीता॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Brought with the purpose of propitiating Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, by Bharata, who was rich in the sense of propriety, placing righteousness in the forefront and shaking off vanity, the aforesaid army shone brightly in the vicinity of Citrakūṭa. (31)

verses.text:
निवेश्य सेनां तु विभुः पद्भ्यां पादवतां वरः।
अभिगन्तुं स काकुत्स्थमियेष गुरुवर्तकम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having encamped the army by the side of Citrakūṭa, the powerful Bharata, for his part, who was the foremost of those endowed with feet, desired to approach on foot Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who was implementing the words of his father.(1)

verses.text:
निविष्टमात्रे सैन्ये तु यथोद्देशं विनीतवत्।
भरतो भ्रातरं वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: The army having barely encamped in a well-behaved manner according to Bharata’s directions, Bharata for his part spoke the following words to his younger brother, Śatrughna : (2)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं वनमिदं सौम्य नरसंघैः समन्ततः।
लुब्धैश्च सहितैरेभिस्त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि॥ ३॥
verses.m: “With these multitudes of men forming your retinue, accompanied by the Niṣādas, the followers of Guha, O gentle brother, you ought quickly to search this forest all round. (3)

verses.text:
गुहो ज्ञातिसहस्रेण शरचापासिपाणिना।
समन्वेषतु काकुत्स्थावस्मिन् परिवृतः स्वयम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Let Guha, surrounded by a thousand of his clansmen, carrying each arrows, a bow and a sword in their hands, personally search for Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Kakutstha, in this forest. (4)

verses.text:
अमात्यैः सह पौरैश्च गुरुभिश्च द्विजातिभिः।
सह सर्वं चरिष्यामि पद्भ्यां परिवृतः स्वयम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “In the company of and surrounded by ministers and citizens, preceptors and other Brāhmaṇas, I shall personally go round the whole forest on foot. (5)

verses.text:
यावन्न रामं द्रक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मणं वा महाबलम्।
वैदेहीं वा महाभागां न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “There will be no peace to me until I see Śrī Rāma or the very mighty Lakṣmaṇa or the highly fortunate Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory. (6)

verses.text:
यावन्न चन्द्रसंकाशं तद् द्रक्ष्यामि शुभाननम्।
भ्रातुः पद्मविशालाक्षं न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “There will be no peace of mind to me until I look on the well-known blessed countenance of my elder brother, shining brightly like the full moon and distinguished by eyes big as the lotus. (7)

verses.text:
सिद्धार्थः खलु सौमित्रिर्यश्चन्द्रविमलोपमम्।
मुखं पश्यति रामस्य राजीवाक्षं महाद्युतिम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Accomplished of purpose, indeed, is Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, who beholds the highly resplendent face of Śrī Rāma, resembling the clear moon and marked with lotus-like eyes. (8)

verses.text:
यावन्न चरणौ भ्रातुः पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ।
शिरसा प्रग्रहीष्यामि न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “There will be no peace of mind for me until I hold firmly on my head the lotus-like feet of my elder brother, adorned with the marks of royalty (viz., the figures of a thunderbolt, flag, lotus, umbrella and so on), (9)

verses.text:
यावन्न राज्ये राज्यार्हः पितृपैतामहे स्थितः।
अभिषिक्तो जलक्लिन्नो न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “There will be no peace of mind to me until Śrī Rāma, who deserves the kingship, is installed on the ancestral throne, duly consecrated and wet with water after a ceremonial bath forming part of the consecration. (10)

verses.text:
कृतकृत्या महाभागा वैदेही जनकात्मजा।
भर्तारं सागरान्तायाः पृथिव्या यानुगच्छति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The highly blessed Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, the daughter of Janaka, who follows in the footsteps of her husband, the protector of the earth extending up to the ocean, has accomplished her object. (11)

verses.text:
सुशुभश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ गिरिराजसमो गिरिः।
यस्मिन् वसति काकुत्स्थः कुबेर इव नन्दने॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Highly blessed is this mountain Citrakūṭa, ranking with the Himalayan range, on which dwells Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) as does Kubera, the god of riches, in the Caitraratha garden, which delights him. (12)

verses.text:
कृतकार्यमिदं दुर्गवनं व्यालनिषेवितम्।
यदध्यास्ते महाराजो रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “This forest, which is difficult of access and is infested with beasts of prey, and which the great king Rāma, the foremost of those wielding arms, is occupying at present is surely accomplished of purpose.” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्भरतः पुरुषर्षभः।
पद्भ्यामेव महातेजाः प्रविवेश महद् वनम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying so, the mighty-armed Bharata, a jewel among men, who was endowed with exceptional glory, entered the great forest only on foot. (14)

verses.text:
स तानि द्रुमजालानि जातानि गिरिसानुषु।
पुष्पिताग्राणि मध्येन जगाम वदतां वरः॥ १५॥
verses.m: That jewel among the eloquent passed through clusters of trees grown on mountain-peaks—trees whose tops were full of blossom. (15)

verses.text:
स गिरेश्चित्रकूटस्य सालमारुह्य सत्वरम्।
रामाश्रमगतस्याग्नेर्ददर्श ध्वजमुच्छ्रितम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Hastily climbing up a sāla tree standing on the Citrakūṭa mountain, he saw a towering column of smoke issuing from fire in Śrī Rāma’s hermitage. (16)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरतः श्रीमान् मुमोद सहबान्धवः।
अत्र राम इति ज्ञात्वा गतः पारमिवाम्भसः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Perceiving the smoke and concluding that Śrī Rāma was there, the glorious Bharata with his kinsman, Śatrughna, rejoiced like one who had reached the end of an expanse of water. (17)

verses.text:
स चित्रकूटे तु गिरौ निशम्य
रामाश्रमं पुण्यजनोपपन्नम्।
गुहेन सार्धं त्वरितो जगाम
पुनर्निवेश्यैव चमूं महात्मा॥ १८॥
verses.m: Seeing on the Citrakūṭa mountain the hermitage of Śrī Rāma, frequented by holy men, and sending back to the camps the troops that had been sent by him in search of Śrī Rāma, the high-souled Bharata for his part proceeded with quick steps alongwith Guha to meet Śrī Rāma. (18)

verses.text:
निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्ततः।
जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुघ्नमनुदर्शयन्॥ १॥
verses.m: The army having encamped, Bharata for his part, keen as he was to see his elder brother, then proceeded to see him, pointing out on the way to Śatrughna the marks indicating the presence of a hermitage nearby. (1)

verses.text:
ऋषिं वसिष्ठं संदिश्य मातॄर्मे शीघ्रमानय।
इति त्वरितमग्रे स जगाम गुरुवत्सलः॥ २॥
verses.m: Requesting Sage Vasiṣṭha in the following words: “Pray, fetch my mothers promptly,” Bharata, who was fond of his elder brother, hastily pressed forward. (2)

verses.text:
सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शत्रुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत।
रामदर्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च॥ ३॥
verses.m: Sumantra too for his part closely followed Śatrughna; for an ardent longing for the sight of Śrī Rāma possessed his heart too, as Bharata’s. (3)

verses.text:
गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालयसंस्थिताम्।
भ्रातुः पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह॥ ४॥
verses.m: Even while proceeding, Bharata, who was now radiant with joy at the prospect of meeting Śrī Rāma, beheld the hut made of leafy twigs, belonging to his elder brother and built after the style of hermits’ dwellings, as well as another cottage enclosed with a wooden wall and provided with doors, intended for Sītā: so the tradition goes. (4)

verses.text:
शालायास्त्वग्रतस्तस्या ददर्श भरतस्तदा।
काष्ठानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्यपचितानि च॥ ५॥
verses.m: In front of that hut Bharata saw at that time hewn pieces of wood as well as flowers gathered for worship. (5)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाश्रममीयुषः।
कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरैः क्वचित् क्वचित्॥ ६॥
verses.m: He also perceived tokens for indicating the way made on trees here and there with blades of Kuśa grass and strips of cloth by Lakṣmaṇa and Śrī Rāma while returning to the hermitage from the riverside after a bath or with water fetched from the river. (6)

verses.text:
ददर्श च वने तस्मिन् महतः संचयान् कृतान्।
मृगाणां महिषाणां च करीषैः शीतकारणात्॥ ७॥
verses.m: He further beheld in the vicinity of that cottage large heaps made of the dried dung of deer and wild buffaloes for protection against cold. (7)

verses.text:
गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान् भरतस्तदा।
शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वशः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Nay, even while going, the mighty-armed Bharata, who was full of glory, spoke with delight as follows on that occasion to Śatrughna as well as to all those ministers that had accompanied him : (8)

verses.text:
मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्।
नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I believe we have reached that region of which Ṛṣi Bharadwāja spoke to us. I conclude the river Mandākinī to be not very far from this place. (9)

verses.text:
उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्।
अभिज्ञानकृतः पन्था विकाले गन्तुमिच्छता॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Since strips of cloth are seen fastened to the trees high up, this may be the path provided with identifications by Lakṣmaṇa wishing to go out for a bath or in order to bring water from the river at odd hours. (10)

verses.text:
इतश्चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्।
शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nay, on this side do swift-footed elephants, distinguished by huge tusks, roam about trumpeting at one another in the flanks of the mountain. (11)

verses.text:
यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसाः सततं वने।
तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूमः संकुलः कृष्णवर्त्मनः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “There can be seen the thick smoke of the sacred fire, which ascetics in a forest seek to preserve incessantly for pouring oblations into it both morning and evening. (12)

verses.text:
अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्।
आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टं महर्षिमिव राघवम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Here I shall be able to see Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, my elder brother, a veritable tiger among men, who shows respect to his elders, highly delighted like an eminent sage.” (13)

verses.text:
अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तं तु चित्रकूटं स राघवः।
मन्दाकिनीमनु प्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Then, going awhile, the celebrated Bharata, a scion of Raghu, for his part reached Citrakūṭa on the bank of the Mandākinī and spoke as follows to those men that had accompanied him : (14)

verses.text:
जगत्यां पुरुषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रतः।
जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Having reached a lonely place Śrī Rāma (a tiger among men), a ruler of the people, sits delighted on the bare ground in the posture of a hero (with his left foot placed on his right knee). Woe be to my birth alongwith my life ! (15)

verses.text:
मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युतिः।
सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य वने वसति राघवः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Fallen in adversity (in the shape of being deprived of his inheritance and exiled) on my account, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the protector of the world, who is possessed of great splendour, is dwelling in the forest, having completely given up all enjoyments. (16)

verses.text:
इति लोकसमाक्रुष्टः पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्।
रामं तस्य पतिष्यामि सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Reviled thus by the world, I shall fall at the feet of Śrī Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa today with a view to propitiating them.” (17)

verses.text:
एवं स विलपंस्तस्मिन् वने दशरथात्मजः।
ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्॥ १८॥
सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्।
विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे॥ १९॥
verses.m: Wailing as aforesaid, the celebrated Bharata (son of Daśaratha) beheld in that forest a large and holy hut of leafy twigs pleasing to the mind and thatched with abundant leaves of sāla, palmyra and Aśwakarṇa trees, and thus appearing from a distance like an extensive altar, softly overspread with blades of Kuśa grass in a sacrificial performance. (18-19)

verses.text:
शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः।
रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारैः शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: The hut was adorned with very strong bows, plated with gold at the back and shining like rainbows, nay, instrumental in accomplishing great deeds and capable of causing pain to the enemy. (20)

verses.text:
अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणगतैः शरैः।
शोभितां दीप्तवदनैः सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव॥ २१॥
verses.m: It was further graced with fearful arrows encased in quivers and shining like sunbeams, in the same way as Bhogavatī (the realm of Nāgas) is graced by serpents with incandescent hoods (21)

verses.text:
महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्।
रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: The hut was also decked with a couple of swords encased in sheaths of gold and further adorned with two shields emblazoned with flowers of gold. (22)

verses.text:
गोधाङ्गुलित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रकाञ्चनभूषितैः।
अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगैः सिंहगुहामिव॥ २३॥
verses.m: Distinguished by gloves of iguana skin decked with excellent gold and hanging on walls, the hut was unassailable by hordes of enemies even as the lair of a lion is incapable of being assailed by deer. (23)

verses.text:
प्रागुदक्प्रवणां वेदिं विशालां दीप्तपावकाम्।
ददर्श भरतस्तत्र पुण्यां रामनिवेशने॥ २४॥
verses.m: In that habitat of Śrī Rāma, Bharata also beheld a spacious holy altar inclining towards the south-east and with a lighted fire placed on it. (24)

verses.text:
निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम्।
उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Fixing his gaze awhile, Bharata for his part descried his elder brother, Śrī Rāma, seated in the hut wearing a rounded mass of matted hair on his head. (25)

verses.text:
कृष्णाजिनधरं तं तु चीरवल्कलवाससम्।
ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: He saw the said Śrī Rāma wearing the skin of a black buck and clad in a strip of bark and resembling fire in brilliance, seated closeby. (26)

verses.text:
सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्।
पृथिव्याः सागरान्ताया भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्॥ २७॥
उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्।
स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च॥ २८॥
verses.m: He saw the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, the protector of the earth extending up to the ocean, who had shoulders resembling a lion’s and eyes resembling a pair of lotuses and was given to the practice of virtue, seated like the eternal Brahmā (the creator) on a levelled and squared piece of ground strewn with blades of the sacred Kuśa grass, alongwith Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. (27-28)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरतः श्रीमान् शोकमोहपरिप्लुतः।
अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरतः केकयीसुतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Overwhelmed with agony and infatuation, the glorious Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, whose mind was given to piety, rushed towards him on seeing him. (29)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वैव विललापार्तो बाष्पसंदिग्धया गिरा।
अशक्नुवन् वारयितुं धैर्याद् वचनमब्रुवन्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Distressed at his very sight, he wailed as follows in a voice choked with tears, unable as he was to restrain his agony through firmness and failing to articulate words : (30)

verses.text:
यः संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद् युक्त उपासितुम्।
वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीनः सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रजः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Here is that very elder brother of mine sitting in the company of wild deer, who deserves to be attended upon by ministers in a royal assembly. (31)

verses.text:
वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचितः।
मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “The same exalted soul who was used to wearing clothes worth many thousands in the city of Ayodhyā, puts on in this forest today pieces of deerskin, one about his loins and the other as an upper garment, discharging his sacred obligation towards his father. (32)

verses.text:
अधारयद् यो विविधाश्चित्राः सुमनसः सदा।
सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं सहते राघवः कथम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “How does the selfsame Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who ever adorned his head with beautiful flowers of every description, endure now this burden of matted locks on his head? (33)

verses.text:
यस्य यज्ञैर्यथादिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य संचयः।
शरीरक्लेशसम्भूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “He who deserved to acquire merit through sacrificial performances undertaken as enjoined by the scriptures, is striving after merit earned through mortification of the flesh ! (34)

verses.text:
चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्।
मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “How is this person of my celebrated elder brother, which used to be adorned with sandal-paste of great value is now covered with dirt? (35)

verses.text:
मन्निमित्तमिदं दुःखं प्राप्तो रामः सुखोचितः।
धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, who deserves all kinds of comforts, has met with this misfortune on my account. Woe to my life, condemned by the world, cruel as I am.” (36)

verses.text:
इत्येवं विलपन् दीनः प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कजः।
पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Loudly wailing as aforesaid, Bharata, who was feeling miserable, his lotus-like countenance covered with perspiration, fell down crying, unable as he was to place his hands on the feet of Śrī Rāma. (37)

verses.text:
दुःखाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबलः।
उक्त्वाऽऽर्येति सकृद् दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किंचन॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Pitifully saying “O worshipful brother !” but once, the very mighty prince Bharata, tormented as he was with agony, said nothing further. (38)

verses.text:
बाष्पैः पिहितकण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्।
आर्येत्येवाभिसंक्रुश्य व्याहर्तुं नाशकत् ततः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Nay, crying at the top of his voice “My noble brother !” only, on perceiving the illustrious Śrī Rāma, he could not speak further, his throat choked with tears. (39)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नश्चापि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन्।
तावुभौ च समालिङ्ग्य रामोऽप्यश्रूण्यवर्तयत्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Shedding tears, Śatrughna as well bowed down at the feet of Śrī Rāma. And closely embracing them both, Śrī Rāma too began dropping tears. (40)

verses.text:
ततः सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव
समीयतू राजसुतावरण्ये।
दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च
यथाम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: The two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, then embraced Sumantra as well as Guha in the forest, even as the Sun and the Moon conjoin with Venus and Jupiter in the heavens. (41)

verses.text:
तान् पार्थिवान् वारणयूथपार्हान्
समागतांस्तत्र महत्यरण्ये।
वनौकसस्तेऽभिसमीक्ष्य सर्वे
त्वश्रूण्यमुञ्चन् प्रविहाय हर्षम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Perceiving the aforesaid princes, who deserved to ride on lordly elephants (lit., the leaders of herds of elephants), come together in that forest, all those dwellers in forests for their part began to shed tears totally giving up joy born of his blessed sight.(42)

verses.text:
जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि।
ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करं यथा॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma beheld Bharata fallen on the ground with folded hands, wearing matted locks on his head, clad in bark and as such painful to the sight like the sun at the time of universal destruction coming at the end of a cycle. (1)

verses.text:
कथंचिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम्।
भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिजग्राह पाणिना॥ २॥
verses.m: Anyhow recognizing his younger brother, Bharata, pale-faced and emaciated as he was, Śrī Rāma lifted him up with his hand. (2)

verses.text:
आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघवम्।
अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत सादरम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Smelling the head of Bharata as a token of affection and embracing the scion of Raghu, nay, placing him on his lap, Śrī Rāma tenderly questioned him as follows : (3)

verses.text:
क्व नु तेऽभूत् पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागतः।
न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Where, I wonder, has our father gone, my darling, that you have come all the way to the forest, leaving him alone? So long as he is alive, you ought not to have come to the forest under any circumstances. (4)

verses.text:
चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद् भरतमागतम्।
दुष्प्रतीकमरण्येऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I am glad I behold after a long time Bharata, though difficult to recognize because of his pale countenance and emaciated limbs, come to this forest from a distant land (the home of his maternal grandfather). How have you come to the forest, my darling? (5)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्नु धरते तात राजा यत् त्वमिहागतः।
कच्चिन्न दीनः सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Does the king, our father, survive, I ask you, that you have come to this place? I hope the miserable king has not departed to the other world all of a sudden. (6)

verses.text:
कच्चित् सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम्।
कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितुः सत्यपराक्रम॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I hope, O gentle brother, your sovereignty, which has come down from eternity, has not been lost, tender of age as you are? Are you rendering service to our father, my darling of unfailing prowess?(7)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् दशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसंगरः।
राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्ता धर्मनिश्चितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Is King Daśaratha, our father, who is true to his promise and has performed a number of Rājasūya and Aśwamedha sacrifices, and who is resolute upon righteousness, enjoying good health? (8)

verses.text:
स कच्चिद् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युतिः।
इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत् तात पूज्यते॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Is the celebrated Vasiṣṭha, the preceptor of the Ikṣwākus, who has realized Brahma, or is a mind-born son of Brahmā, is learned in all the branches of knowledge, ever devoted to virtue and possessed of great splendour, duly honoured by you, my darling? (9)

verses.text:
तात कच्चिच्च कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती।
सुखिनी कच्चिदार्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Is Kausalyā as well as Sumitrā, who is blessed with good progeny, happy? I hope the glorious mother Kaikeyī too is rejoicing (because of my exile and Your ascension to the throne of Ayodhyā). (10)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् विनयसम्पन्नः कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुतः।
अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Is your personal priest a son of Vasiṣṭha, who is rich in humility, born of a noble pedigree, a man of extensive learning, free from spite and skilled in all pious and sacred rites—treated with honour by you? (11)

verses.text:
कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजुः।
हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Does the priest, employed by you to look after the sacred fires, who is well-versed in the procedure of conducting sacrificial performances, is endowed with intelligence and guileless of disposition, invariably inform you in time about a sacred fire having already been or going to be fed with oblations? (12)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् देवान् पितॄन् भृत्यान् गुरून् पितृसमानपि।
वृद्धांश्च तात वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Do you hold in high esteem gods and manes, dependants, elders, kinsmen of your father’s age, the aged, the physicians as well as the Brāhmaṇas, my darling? (13)

verses.text:
इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्रविशारदम्।
सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित् त्वं तात मन्यसे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Do you respect Sudhanvā, your teacher of the science of archery, who is equipped with knowledge relating to the use of excellent arrows discharged without uttering spells and missiles propelled with the utterance of spells and well-versed in political economy? (14)

verses.text:
कच्चिदात्मसमाः शूराः श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः।
कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिणः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I hope counsellors who are valiant like you and full of learning, have controlled their senses, are born of a high pedigree and know the meaning of signs, have been secured by you, my darling ! (15)

verses.text:
मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव।
सुसंवृतो मन्त्रिधुरैरमात्यैः शास्त्रकोविदैः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “A secret well-guarded by ministers who are the foremost counsellors and well-versed in politics is the root of victory of kings, O scion of Raghu ! (16)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषि कच्चित् कालेऽवबुध्यसे।
कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तयस्यर्थनैपुणम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I hope you do not fall a prey to excess of sleep and wake betimes. And do you contemplate during the late hours of the night on the methods of acquiring wealth?(17)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह।
कच्चित् ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I hope you do not deliberate alone without consulting anyone nor do you take counsel with many. I hope the decision arrived at by you through deliberation with your counsellors does not reach the public before it is carried out. (18)

verses.text:
कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम्।
क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्म न दीर्घयसि राघव॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I hope, considering your interest fully, you launch an enterprise betimes with a modest beginning but pregnant with great potentialities, and do not defer it, O scion of Raghu? (19)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्नु सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुनः।
विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्तव्यानि पार्थिवाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I hope your vassals actually know of all your projects only when they have been duly carried out or at least well-nigh carried out and not so long as they are yet to be carried out. (20)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न तर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिताः।
त्वया वा तव वामात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I hope your deliberations, which have not been proclaimed are not known to others through surmises or reasoning and the deliberations of others are known (before they materialize) by yourself or by your ministers. (21)

verses.text:
कच्चित् सहस्रैर्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्।
पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्यान्निःश्रेयसं महत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I hope you prefer one learned man to thousands of fools inasmuch as a learned man is calculated to do immense good in financial crises. (22)

verses.text:
सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां यद्युपास्ते महीपतिः।
अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता॥ २३॥
verses.m: “If a king maintains thousands or even tens of thousands of fools, no assistance can be expected from them in times of need. (23)

verses.text:
एकोऽप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षणः।
राजानं राजपुत्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Even one minister who is talented, valiant, clever and well-versed in politics can bring a large fortune to a king or prince. (24)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्मुख्या महत्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमाः।
जघन्याश्च जघन्येषु भृत्यास्ते तात योजिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I hope high-class servants are entrusted by you with important duties, middling ones with second-rate affairs and third-grade servants with menial duties, my darling! (25)

verses.text:
अमात्यानुपधातीतान् पितृपैतामहान् शुचीन्।
श्रेष्ठान् श्रेष्ठेषु कच्चित् त्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I hope you entrust first-rate ministers, who are past all tests of loyalty, are hereditary servants of the crown and honest, with the highest duties. (26)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजिताः प्रजाः।
राष्ट्रे तवावजानन्ति मन्त्रिणः कैकयीसुत॥ २७॥
verses.m: “I hope, sore agitated by stern rule, the people in your state do not show disrespect to your ministers, O son of Kaikeyī? (27)

verses.text:
कच्चित् त्वां नावजानन्ति याजकाः पतितं यथा।
उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रियः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “I hope priests conducting sacrifices for the benefit of others do not disregard you (by refusing to officiate at your sacrifices) as they would a fallen man or even as matrons would despise their own husband who had taken to wife a lowborn woman and was excessively fond of her. (28)

verses.text:
उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसंदूषणे रतम्।
शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो हन्ति न स हन्यते॥ २९॥
verses.m: “He who does not get rid of a physician adept in devices of aggravating a malady, a servant intent on bringing disgrace (to his master) and a gallant warrior seeking kingly power is himself killed by these. (29)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् धृष्टश्च शूरश्च धृतिमान् मतिमान् शुचिः।
कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्षः सेनापतिः कृतः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “I hope a man, who is ever pleased and full of resolution, gallant and talented, spotless of character and well-born, devoted and clever, has been appointed by you as the generalissimo? (30)

verses.text:
बलवन्तश्च कच्चित् ते मुख्या युद्धविशारदाः।
दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्य मानिताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Have the foremost of your heroic warriors, who are possessed of might and skilled in warfare, and whose prowess has been treated with honour by you, after being politely received? (31)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्।
सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “I hope you distribute daily provisions and disburse the monthly salary due to them at the opportune time in a suitable manner and do not defer their payment. (32)

verses.text:
कालातिक्रमणे ह्येव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृताः।
भर्तुरप्यतिकुप्यन्ति सोऽनर्थः सुमहान् कृतः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Salaried servants surely and positively get enraged even at their master when the distribution of their provisions and the disbursal of their salary are delayed and that itself is a very great harm done to the State. (33)

verses.text:
कच्चित् सर्वेऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्राः प्रधानतः।
कच्चित् प्राणांस्तवार्थेषु संत्यजन्ति समाहिताः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “I hope all the principal members of your race, the Kṣatriyas, are devoted to you? And do they devoutly and cheerfully lay down their lives for your sake? (34)

verses.text:
कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान् दक्षिणः प्रतिभानवान्।
यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डितः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Has a man of your own state, who is learned, clever, ready-witted and capable of delivering messages correctly, nay, who is able to distinguish between right and wrong, been appointed by you as an ambassador, O Bharata? (35)

verses.text:
कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च।
त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकैः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Do you keep an eye on the eighteen functionaries* of the enemies and the fiteen functionaries of your own side through three unknown spies told off for each? (36)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् व्यपास्तानहितान् प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा।
दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्तसे रिपुसूदन॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “I hope you remain ever mindful of your enemies expelled from their home by you and since returned, even though they are apparently weak, O destroyer of foes ! (37)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न लोकायतिकान् ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे।
अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बालाः पण्डितमानिनः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “I hope you do not patronize atheistic Brāhmaṇs; O dear brother: for, ignorant and conceited as they are, they are skilled only in perverting the mind and thereby diverting people from the righteous path. (38)

verses.text:
धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः।
बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Banking solely on their logical acumen, these men of perverted intellect preach nonsense even in the presence of foremost books on Dharma (piety). (39)

verses.text:
वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः।
सत्यनामां दृढद्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसंकुलाम्॥ ४०॥
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः स्वकर्मनिरतैः सदा।
जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यैः सहस्रशः॥ ४१॥
प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्।
कच्चित् समुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसे॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I hope you protect on all sides the prosperous city of Ayodhyā, rightly so-called because of its being unassailable, which has been occupied in the past, O dear brother, by our heroic forbears, which is provided with strong gates and remains crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, which is inhabited in thousands by noble Brāhmaṇas (members of the priestly class), Kṣatriyas (members of the warrior class) and Vaiśyas (members of the agriculturist and trading classes)—who are ever devoted to their respective duties, have subdued their senses and are full of great zeal—nay, which is crowded with palatial buildings of various patterns and is thronged with learned men and full of highly contented people. (40—42)

verses.text:
कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्टः सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः।
देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः॥ ४३॥
प्रहृष्टनरनारीकः समाजोत्सवशोभितः।
सुकृष्टसीमापशुमान् हिंसाभिरभिवर्जितः॥ ४४॥
अदेवमातृको रम्यः श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः।
परित्यक्तो भयैः सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः॥ ४५॥
विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वैः सुरक्षितः।
कच्चिज्जनपदः स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “I hope the kingdom of Ayodhyā—which is overspread with hundreds of altars constructed for sacrificial performances and crowded with well-established men, which is adorned with temples, sheds where water is stocked for free distribution to passers-by and tanks, and peopled with highly delighted men and women, which is graced by social festivities and is full of well-cultivated fields and abounds in cattle, which is totally free from violence and does not depend exclusively on rains for its agricultural products, which is charming in point of topography and is purged of beasts of prey, which is completely rid of all fears and is studded with mines, nay, which is bereft of sinful men and was well-protected by our forbears—is prosperous and faring well, O scion of Raghu ! (43—46)

verses.text:
कच्चित् ते दयिताः सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः।
वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोकोऽयं सुखमेधते॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “I hope the Vaiśyas, who live by agriculture and rearing the bovine race, are all loved by you. Are these people, depending as they do on the vocation of a Vaiśya, viz., trade, agriculture and breeding of cattle, thriving well at present, O dear brother? (47)

verses.text:
तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित् ते भरणं कृतम्।
रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “I hope protection has been afforded by you to them by making available to them the objects desired by them and warding off evil; for all the inhabitants of one’s land deserve to be protected righteously by a king. (48)

verses.text:
कच्चित् स्त्रियः सान्त्वयसे कच्चित् तास्ते सुरक्षिताः।
कच्चिन्न श्रद्दधास्यासां कच्चिद् गुह्यं न भाषसे॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Do you keep your womenfolk pacified? Are they duly protected by you? I hope you do not repose excessive faith in them and do not confide your secrets to them. (49)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित् ते सन्ति धेनुकाः।
कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Are the forests which are the home of elephants preserved by you? Are milch cows in abundance with you? I hope you do not feel satisfied with the existing number of female elephants, horses and elephants owned by you. (50)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् दर्शयसे नित्यं मानुषाणां विभूषितम्।
उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Getting up regularly everyday do you show yourself well-adorned to the people in the assembly hall in the forenoon, O prince? (51)

verses.text:
कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ताः प्रत्यक्षास्तेऽविशङ्कया।
सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “I hope all your workmen do not appear unhesitatingly before you nor are they kept altogether out of your sight. In fact, a middle course is undoubtedly profitable in this behalf. (52)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् दुर्गाणि सर्वाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः।
यन्त्रैश्च प्रतिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Are all your fortifications fully supplied with wealth and provisions, arms and water, mechanical contrivances and equipped with artisans and bowmen? (53)

verses.text:
आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित् कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः।
अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित् कोषो गच्छति राघव॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Is your income sufficiently large to meet your expenses and your expenditure comparatively less? I hope your wealth does not go to undeserving men, O scion of Raghu! (54)

verses.text:
देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थे ब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च।
योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद् गच्छति ते व्ययः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “I further hope your wealth is expended exclusively in the cause of gods and manes as well as over the Brāhmaṇas and unexpected visitors, warriors and hosts of friends. (55)

verses.text:
कच्चिदार्योऽपि शुद्धात्मा क्षारितश्चापकर्मणा।
अदृष्टः शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद् बध्यते शुचिः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “I hope no pious soul, who is pure of mind and sinless, is convicted from greed, when charged with some offence, though not found guilty by those well-versed in law-books. (56)

verses.text:
गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टः सकारणः।
कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “I hope no thief who has been detected at the time of theft and apprehended on sufficient ground and also questioned and found guilty is released on account of greed of wealth, O jewel among men ! (57)

verses.text:
व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्बलस्य च राघव।
अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “In an unhappy contention between an affluent and a financially feeble man, O scion of Raghu, do your ministers of vast learning judge the case impartially? (58)

verses.text:
यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव।
तानि पुत्रपशून् घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “The tears that drop from the eyes of men falsely convicted, O scion of Raghu, destroy the sons and cattle of a king who rules the people merely for the sake of pleasure, caring little for equity and justice. (59)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यान् मुख्यांश्च राघव।
दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “Do you seek, O scion of Raghu, to win over the elders, children and foremost physicians by the following three means, viz., gifts, a loving mind and polite words? (60)

verses.text:
कच्चिद् गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन्।
चैत्यांश्च सर्वान् सिद्धार्थान् ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “Do you greet your teachers and elders, ascetics, deities and unexpected visitors as well as all the trees standing at crossroads and believed to be the abode of gods and Brāhmaṇas who have achieved the object of their life through their learning, character and austerities? (61)

verses.text:
कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुनः।
उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन न विबाधसे॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “I hope you do not cause interruption in your religious practices by your excessive devotion to wealth and devoting the morning hours and forenoon to the pursuit of wealth and other secular interests, nor do you mar your earthly interests by your over-emphasis on religion (and allowing your religious duties to encroach upon the midday hours and afternoon reserved for the pursuit of wealth and other secular interests) nor do you mar both your religious and secular interests by your self-indulgence in the form of avidity for gratification of the senses. (62)

verses.text:
कच्चिदर्थं च कामं च धर्मं च जयतां वर।
विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान् वरद सेवसे॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “Do you pursue all the three objects of human pursuit, viz., wealth and the delights of sense and religion only during the hours allotted to each,* O bestower of boons, * Our Smṛti texts enjoin the pursuit of religion during the morning hours and forenoon, the pursuit dividing them according to time, O jewel among the victorious, knowing as you do the time appropriate for each? (63)

verses.text:
कच्चित् ते ब्राह्मणाः शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदाः।
आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदैः सह॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “Do the Brāhmaṇas that have thoroughly grasped the meaning of all the scriptures pray for your welfare alongwith the citizens of Ayodhyā and the people of the countryside, O exceptionally wise prince? (64)

verses.text:
नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्।
अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्॥ ६५॥
एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्।
निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्॥ ६६॥
मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः।
कच्चित् त्वं वर्जयस्येतान् राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “Do you abjure the following fourteen failings of kings, viz., disbelief in the other world, mendacity (through greed etc.,) anger, neglect of kingly duties, procrastination, shunning the wise, sloth, thraldom of the five senses, devoting thought to the affairs of the State without seeking the advice of others (ministers etc.,) taking counsel with those of perverted insight, failure to launch projects already decided upon, failure to keep secrets, failure to utter auspicious words at the beginning of every undertaking and rising from one’s seat indiscriminately to receive all who happen to approach him? (65—67)

verses.text:
दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान् सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः।
अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव॥ ६८॥
इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्वा षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्।
कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्॥ ६९॥
यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी संधिविग्रहौ।
कच्चिदेतान् महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे॥ ७०॥
verses.m: “I hope you deal properly after knowing them in reality with the well-known ten evils born of concupiscence, the five kinds of fortifications, the four expedients recommended for kings, the seven important limbs of a state, the eight evils born of anger or the eight measures conducive to the welfare of a state, the three worldly objects of human pursuit, viz., religious merit, material wealth and sensuous enjoyment, or the three kinds of power (viz., energy or उत्साहशक्ति, the power of dominion or प्रभुशक्ति and the power of counsel or मन्त्रनाशक्ति), the three branches of learning (viz., the three Vedas or त्रयी, the knowledge relating to agriculture, commerce and other vocational pursuits or वार्ता and political science or दण्डनीति), subjugation of the senses, the six strategic expedients (viz., coming to terms with the enemy—संधि, waging war against him—विग्रह, marching against him—यानम्, biding one’s time to seek a favourable opportunity—आसनम्, causing dissension in the enemy’s ranks—द्वैधम् and seeking the protection of a powerful ally—आश्रय ; adversity brought about by divine agencies such as fire, water in the shape of excessive rains or floods, epidemic or endemic diseases, famine and pestilence, and by human agencies such as officials, thieves, enemies, a king’s favourites and the king himself when actuated by greed ; the stern duty of a king as dictated by policy, such as to win over enemy’s men whose emoluments have been withheld, who are greedy or haughty, who have suffered indignity at his hands, who are irate or have been provoked by him for no reason, who are afraid or have been intimidated, the following twenty types of monarchs who are not worth negotiating with, viz., 1. a king who is yet a child, or 2. aged, 3. who has been ailing for a long time, 4. who has been ostracised by his own kith and kin, 5. who is pusillanimous, or 6. is surrounded by cowards, 7. who is greedy, or 8. has greedy associates, 9. who has estranged his ministers and others, 10. who is extremely voluptuous, 11. who confers with fickle-minded persons, 12. who speaks ill of divine beings and Brāhmaṇas, 13. who is ill-fated and 14. a fatalist, 15. who is afflicted by famine, and 16. by military reverses, 17. who mostly remains away from home, 18. who has numerous enemies, 19. who is in the clutches of adverse times, and 20. who is not devoted to truth and piety*;
