the entire population of the State; setting forth on an expedition for conquest against an enemy; drawing up an army in battle-array; coming to terms with an enemy and waging war against him, the first of which serves as a ground for the two policies of duplicity and seeking the protection of a powerful enemy, while the other serves as a ground for the other two policies of marching against the enemy and biding time to seek a favourable opportunity to march against an enemy, O highly intelligent scion of Raghu ! (68—70)

verses.text:
मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टं चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा।
कच्चित् समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्रं मन्त्रयसे बुध॥ ७१॥
verses.m: “Do you hold consultation in accordance with scriptural injunctions with only four or three selected counsellors collectively or severally to guard against a split among them and to prevent the secrets from leaking out, O wise one? (71)

verses.text:
कच्चित् ते सफला वेदाः कच्चित् ते सफलाः क्रियाः।
कच्चित् ते सफला दाराः कच्चित् ते सफलं श्रुतम्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “Has your study of the Vedas borne fruit in the shape of moulding your conduct according to their injunctions? Are your undertakings fruitful? Has your spouse given birth to offspring? Has your learning borne fruit in the shape of culture and humility? (72)

verses.text:
कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव।
आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थसंहिता॥ ७३॥
verses.m: “I hope your conclusion is precisely the same as mine, which has been set forth in the foregoing verses, O scion of Raghu, and which is conducive to longevity and fame and is attended with religious merit, enjoyment and wealth. (73)

verses.text:
यां वृत्तिं वर्तते तातो यां च नः प्रपितामहः।
तां वृत्तिं वर्तसे कच्चिद् या च सत्पथगा शुभा॥ ७४॥
verses.m: “Do you follow the way of life which our father treads and which our forbears trod, nay, which is in accord with the way of the virtuous and which is righteous in itself? (74)

verses.text:
कच्चित् स्वादुकृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव।
कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्यः सम्प्रयच्छसि॥ ७५॥
verses.m: “I hope you do not partake by yourself of food nicely cooked. I hope you offer it to friends who seek it. (75)

verses.text:
राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा
महीपतिर्दण्डधरः प्रजानाम्।
अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथाव-
दितश्च्युतः स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान्॥ ७६॥
verses.m: “Having obtained as his share, and ruled in the right way over the entire globe, a wise Kṣatriya holds sway over the earth and administering justice to the people quite in consonance with righteousness surely ascends to heaven when detached from this mortal body.” (76)

verses.text:
तं तु रामः समाज्ञाय भ्रातरं गुरुवत्सलम्।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ १॥
verses.m: Concluding from his ascetic garb, the aforesaid Bharata to be full of love to himself (his elder brother), Śrī Rāma for his part alongwith Lakṣmaṇa duly started questioning Bharata as follows : (1)

verses.text:
किमेतदिच्छेयमहं श्रोतुं प्रव्याहृतं त्वया।
यस्मात् त्वमागतो देशमिमं चीरजटाजिनी॥ २॥
verses.m: “I wish to hear explained by you wherefore it is that you have come all the way to this region, clad in the bark of trees and deerskin and wearing matted locks on your head. (2)

verses.text:
यन्निमित्तमिमं देशं कृष्णाजिनजटाधरः।
हित्वा राज्यं प्रविष्टस्त्वं तत् सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि॥ ३॥
verses.m: “What for have you entered this region, wearing the skin of a black buck on your person and matted locks on your head, relinquishing the sovereignty? Please state all this clearly.” (3)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः केकयीपुत्रः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना।
प्रगृह्य बलवद् भूयः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Addressed in the aforesaid words once again by the high-souled Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) closely embracing him, Bharata (the son of Kaikeyī) made the following submission with folded hands : (4)

verses.text:
आर्य तातः परित्यज्य कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्।
गतः स्वर्गं महाबाहुः पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः॥ ५॥
स्त्रिया नियुक्तः कैकेय्या मम मात्रा परंतप।
चकार सा महत्पापमिदमात्मयशोहरम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Having performed a deed in the shape of disinheriting and exiling his own eldest son, most difficult to perform, as urged by his favourite spouse and my mother, Kaikeyī, and abandoning us all, our mighty-armed father ascended to heaven, sore stricken as he was with grief caused by separation from his most beloved son, O tormentor of foes ! In this way she perpetrated this great sin, that has taken away her own reputation, O noble brother ! (5-6)

verses.text:
सा राज्यफलमप्राप्य विधवा शोककर्शिता।
पतिष्यति महाघोरे नरके जननी मम॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Failing to gain the prize in the shape of sovereignty, my widowed mother, emaciated as she is with grief, will descend into a most frightful hell. (7)

verses.text:
तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।
अभिषिञ्चस्व चाद्यैव राज्येन मघवानिव॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Be pleased to bestow this favour on me, your notorious slave, and have yourself consecrated like Indra, the ruler of gods, for the kingship of Ayodhyā. (8)

verses.text:
इमाः प्रकृतयः सर्वा विधवा मातरश्च याः।
त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्ताः प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You ought to be gracious to these people as well as to my widowed mothers, who have sought your presence to propitiate you. (9)

verses.text:
तथानुपूर्व्या युक्तश्च युक्तं चात्मनि मानद।
राज्यं प्राप्नुहि धर्मेण सकामान् सुहृदः कुरु॥ १०॥
verses.m: “You are fitted for sovereignty by virtue of primogeniture and as such assume you the sovereignty, which is your due, conformably with the principles of righteousness and thereby enable your relations and friends to realize their ambition of seeing you installed on the throne of Ayodhyā, O respecter of others ! (10)

verses.text:
भवत्वविधवा भूमिः समग्रा पतिना त्वया।
शशिना विमलेनेव शारदी रजनी यथा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “With you as its lord, let the entire globe cease to be without a master even as and autumnal night ceases to be dismal when united with a bright moon. (11)

verses.text:
एभिश्च सचिवैः सार्धं शिरसा याचितो मया।
भ्रातुः शिष्यस्य दासस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Solicited by me with bent head in conjunction with these ministers, be pleased to show grace to this servant, who is at the same time your younger brother and pupil. (12)

verses.text:
तदिदं शाश्वतं पित्र्यं सर्वं सचिवमण्डलम्।
पूजितं पुरुषव्याघ्र नातिक्रमितुमर्हसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “You ought not to disregard the solicitation of this entire body of your father’s ministers, who are not only well-known but have continued through many past generations and are adored by you, O tiger among men !” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुः सबाष्पः कैकयीसुतः।
रामस्य शिरसा पादौ जग्राह भरतः पुनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying so, full of tears, the mighty armed Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, clasped the feet of Śrī Rāma once more, touching them with his head. (14)

verses.text:
तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः।
भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Embracing his younger brother, Bharata, who was sighing again and again like an elephant in rut, Śrī Rāma spoke to him as follows : (15)

verses.text:
कुलीनः सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः।
राज्यहेतोः कथं पापमाचरेन्मद्विधो जनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How can a man of noble descent, rich in Sattva goodness and dignified, and who has observed sacred vows like myself, perpetrate a sinful act for the sake of sovereignty? (16)

verses.text:
न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन।
न चापि जननीं बाल्यात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I do not discover even a minute fault in you, O destroyer of foes ! Nor should you reproach your mother through ignorance. (17)

verses.text:
कामकारो महाप्राज्ञ गुरूणां सर्वदानघ।
उपपन्नेषु दारेषु पुत्रेषु च विधीयते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Freedom of action on the part of elders with reference to their esteemed wife and progeny is always permitted by the scriptures, O sinless and highly intelligent brother. (18)

verses.text:
वयमस्य यथा लोके संख्याताः सौम्य साधुभिः।
भार्याः पुत्राश्च शिष्याश्च त्वमपि ज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “You, too, should know, O gentle brother, that we are held by holy men to be in the same position in the world with reference to the deceased king-emperor as the wives, progeny and pupils of a householder are considered as amenable to his control. (19)

verses.text:
वने वा चीरवसनं सौम्य कृष्णाजिनाम्बरम्।
राज्ये वापि महाराजो मां वासयितुमीश्वरः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The emperor, King Daśaratha, was perfectly within his rights to lodge me in a forest with the bark of trees wrapped about me and wearing the skin of a black buck about my loins or install me on the throne of Ayodhyā, O gentle brother ! (20)

verses.text:
यावत् पितरि धर्मज्ञ गौरवं लोकसत्कृते।
तावद् धर्मकृतां श्रेष्ठ जनन्यामपि गौरवम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The same degree of respect is due even to our mother, Kaikeyī, as is due to our father, who was honoured by the world, O knower of what is right and jewel among those practising virtue ! (21)

verses.text:
एताभ्यां धर्मशीलाभ्यां वनं गच्छेति राघव।
मातापितृभ्यामुक्तोऽहं कथमन्यत् समाचरे॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Commanded by these parents of mine, who are pious by disposition, in the words ‘Proceed to the forest,’ O scion of Raghu, how can I do anything else? (22)

verses.text:
त्वया राज्यमयोध्यायां प्राप्तव्यं लोकसत्कृतम्।
वस्तव्यं दण्डकारण्ये मया वल्कलवाससा॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Sovereignty in Ayodhyā, respected by the world, should be enjoyed by you, while I must dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest, clad in the bark of trees. (23)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाराजो विभागं लोकसंनिधौ।
व्यादिश्य च महाराजो दिवं दशरथो गतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Saying so and giving two different orders for us two in the presence of the people, Emperor Daśaratha ascended to heaven. (24)

verses.text:
स च प्रमाणं धर्मात्मा राजा लोकगुरुस्तव।
पित्रा दत्तं यथाभागमुपभोक्तुं त्वमर्हसि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Nay, that pious-minded king, the adored of the people, is your authority in this matter. You ought, therefore, to enjoy duly the share allotted to you by our high-souled father. (25)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश समाः सौम्य दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः।
उपभोक्ष्ये त्वहं दत्तं भागं पित्रा महात्मना॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Taking up my abode in the Daṇḍaka forest, O gentle brother, I for my part shall enjoy the share allotted to me by our high-souled father for fourteen years. (26)

verses.text:
यदब्रवीन्मां नरलोकसत्कृतः
पिता महात्मा विबुधाधिपोपमः।
तदेव मन्ये परमात्मनो हितं
न सर्वलोकेश्वरभावमव्ययम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “I consider that alone to be supremely good for me, which our high-souled father, who is respected by the world of human beings and is a compeer of Indra, the ruler of gods, has enjoined upon me, and not the state of Brahmā (the lord of all the worlds), which knows no decay.” (27)

verses.text:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह।
किं मे धर्माद् विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the exhortation of Śrī Rāma, Bharata, it is said, replied as follows : “How will the code of conduct prescribed for a king avail me, who stand outside the range of that code (disqualified as I am for sovereignty, being a younger issue of the king-emperor)? (1)

verses.text:
शाश्वतोऽयं सदा धर्मः स्थितोऽस्मासु नरर्षभ।
ज्येष्ठे पुत्रे स्थिते राजा न कनीयान् भवेन्नृपः॥ २॥
verses.m: “This has ever been the perpetual law amongst us (the Kṣatriyas of the solar dynasty), O jewel among men, that so long as the eldest prince is alive, a younger one can never be king. (2)

verses.text:
स समृद्धां मया सार्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव।
अभिषेचय चात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय नः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Therefore, return with me to the affluent city of Ayodhyā, O scion of Raghu, and get yourself consecrated for the kingship for the continuance of this race of ours. (3)

verses.text:
राजानं मानुषं प्राहुर्देवत्वे सम्मतो मम।
यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The king, whom the common people speak of as a human being and yet whose conduct, which goes hand in hand with righteousness and worldly prosperity, they declare as superhuman, is esteemed by me as verging on divinity. (4)

verses.text:
केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्यमाश्रिते।
धीमान् स्वर्गं गतो राजा यायजूकः सतां मतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “While I was away to the kingdom of Kekaya and you had proceeded to the forest, the sagacious king, who was given to the performance of sacrifices and was esteemed by the virtuous, ascended to heaven. (5)

verses.text:
निष्क्रान्तमात्रे भवति सहसीते सलक्ष्मणे।
दुःखशोकाभिभूतस्तु राजा त्रिदिवमभ्यगात्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, you had just gone out of Ayodhyā when, overwhelmed with sorrow and grief, the king departed for heaven. (6)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितुः।
अहं चायं च शत्रुघ्नः पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Get up, O tiger among men! Let water be offered to the spirit of our deceased father. Śatrughna standing here and myself too have already offered water to him. (7)

verses.text:
प्रियेण किल दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव।
अक्षयं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितुः प्रियः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “For, the knowers of Truth declare that water etc., offered by a beloved son surely becomes inexhaustible in the realm of manes, O scion of Raghu; and you are undoubtedly the beloved of our deceased father. (8)

verses.text:
त्वामेव शोचंस्तव दर्शनेप्सु-
स्त्वय्येव सक्तामनिवर्त्य बुद्धिम्।
त्वया विहीनस्तव शोकरुग्ण-
स्त्वां संस्मरन्नेव गतः पिता ते॥ ९ ॥
verses.m: “Bereft of you and stricken with grief caused by separation from you and unable to divert his mind, which was solely attached to you alone, our father departed from this world grieving only for you, longing for your sight and fondly remembering you alone.” (9)

verses.text:
तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्।
राघवो भरतेनोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the pathetic news relating to the death of his father, King Daśaratha, told by Bharata, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, fainted there. (1)

verses.text:
तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा।
वाग्वज्रं भरतेनोक्तममनोज्ञं परंतपः॥ २॥
प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वै पुष्पिताङ्ग इव द्रुमः।
वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid unpleasant and heart-rending news broken by Bharata, which was piercing like a thunderbolt discharged by Indra, the enemy of demons, on a field of battle, and raising his arms, Śrī Rāma, the scorcher of his enemies, for his part actually sank to the ground precisely like a tree with boughs full of blossom felled down with an axe in a forest : so it is said. (2-3)

verses.text:
तथा हि पतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम्।
कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्॥ ४॥
भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वतः शोककर्शितम्।
रुदन्तः सह वैदेह्या सिषिचुः सलिलेन वै॥ ५॥
verses.m: Weeping with Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, his celebrated brothers, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, promptly sprinkled water all over Śrī Rāma, the ruler of the earth and the wielder of a mighty bow, fallen on the ground, as aforesaid, blasted with grief, like an elephant exhausted by striking with his tusks against a river bank and lying fast asleep due to fatigue. (4-5)

verses.text:
स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामश्रुमुत्सृजन्।
उपाक्रामत काकुत्स्थः कृपणं बहु भाषितुम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Shortly regaining his consciousness, the aforesaid Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, for his part, began piteously to wail, dropping tears from his eyes. (6)

verses.text:
स रामः स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरं पृथिवीपतिम्।
उवाच भरतं वाक्यं धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing of the emperor, his father, having ascended to heaven, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, whose mind was given to piety, addressed the following words, consistent with righteousness, to Bharata : (7)

verses.text:
किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिं गते।
कस्तां राजवराद्धीनामयोध्यां पालयिष्यति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Father having reached the end of his life (the destiny assigned by Providence), what shall I do at Ayodhyā? Who will look after the said city of Ayodhyā, bereft of Daśaratha, the foremost of kings? (8)

verses.text:
किं नु तस्य मया कार्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मनः।
यो मृतो मम शोकेन स मया न च संस्कृतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “What purpose on earth of that high-souled monarch—who died of grief caused by separation from me, and who was not even cremated by me—was served by me, his hapless child? (9)

verses.text:
अहो भरत सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वयानघ।
शत्रुघ्नेन च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Oh sinless Bharata, accomplished of purpose are you, by whom, as well as by Śatrughna the king was paid homage to in all obsequial rites! (10)

verses.text:
निष्प्रधानामनेकाग्रां नरेन्द्रेण विना कृताम्।
निवृत्तवनवासोऽपि नायोध्यां गन्तुमुत्सहे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Even when the term of my exile has expired, I shall have no heart to return to Ayodhyā, which has been rendered destitute of its ruler and is, therefore, without a leader and agitated. (11)

verses.text:
समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायां परंतप।
कोऽनुशासिष्यति पुनस्ताते लोकान्तरं गते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Father having departed to the otherworld, O scorcher of enemies, who will give instructions to me hereafter about my duty when I am back in Ayodhyā, having completed the term of my exile in the forest? (12)

verses.text:
पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्।
वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “From whom shall I hear those words, pleasing to the ear, which father addressed to me in the past, speaking kindly to me, on seeing me of good conduct?” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वाथ भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघवः।
उवाच शोकसंतप्तः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Having spoken to Bharata as aforesaid, and turning to his consort, whose countenance resembled the full moon, as well as to Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was tormented with grief, said to her : (14)

verses.text:
सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुरः पितृहीनोऽसि लक्ष्मण।
भरतो दुःखमाचष्टे स्वर्गतिं पृथिवीपतेः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Your father-in-law is no more, O Sītā ! You are fatherless, O Lakṣmaṇa ! Bharata sorrowfully relates the emperor’s ascent to heaven.” (15)

verses.text:
ततो बहुगुणं तेषां बाष्पं नेत्रेष्वजायत।
तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: When Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) spoke as above, copious tears welled up in consequence in the eyes of those illustrious princes. (16)

verses.text:
ततस्ते भ्रातरः सर्वे भृशमाश्वास्य दुःखितम्।
अब्रुवञ्जगतीभर्तुः क्रियतामुदकं पितुः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having consoled their afflicted brother to the best of their ability, all the aforesaid brothers then said to him, “Let water be offered to the spirit of our imperial father.” (17)

verses.text:
सा सीता स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा श्वशुरं तं महानृपम्।
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां न शशाकेक्षितुं प्रियम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing of the celebrated emperor, her father-in-law, having ascended to heaven, the renowned Sītā with her eyes full of tears was not able to look at her beloved lord. (18)

verses.text:
सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदतीं जनकात्मजाम्।
उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दुःखितो दुःखितं वचः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Consoling the aforesaid Sītā (daughter of Janaka), who was weeping, the afficted Śrī Rāma for his part spoke as follows to the distressed Lakṣmaṇa on that very spot : (19)

verses.text:
आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम्।
जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मनः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Bring the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī, a piece of bark for being wrapped about my lions and another for being used as an upper garment. I shall proceed to the river bank to perform the rite of offering water to the spirit of our high-souled father. (20)

verses.text:
सीता पुरस्ताद् व्रजतु त्वमेनामभितो व्रज।
अहं पश्चाद् गमिष्यामि गतिर्ह्येषा सुदारुणा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā walk ahead and follow you at her heels. I shall follow in the rear; for such is the most painful procedure employed on occasions of mourning.” (21)

verses.text:
ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः।
मृदुर्दान्तश्च कान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्॥ २२॥
सुमन्त्रस्तैर्नृपसुतैः सार्धमाश्वास्य राघवम्।
अवतारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Consoling Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, alongwith those other princes, and holding the former by the hand, Sumantra, their hereditary servant—who had realized the Self, was possessed of great intelligence, gentle, self-controlled and glorious, and was full of unswerving devotion to Śrī Rāma—helped him descend to the blessed river, Mandākinī. (22-23)

verses.text:
ते सुतीर्थां ततः कृच्छ्रादुपगम्य यशस्विनः।
नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्॥ २४॥
शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्।
सिषिचुस्तूदकं राज्ञे तत एतद् भवत्विति॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having reached with difficulty (because of their inability to walk, overwhelmed as they were with grief caused by their father’s demise) the lovely and swift-flowing river Mandākinī—which was provided with easy descents for bathing purposes and was hemmed in with woodlands ever full of blossom—and, betaking themselves to a blessed descent free from mud, Śrī Rāma and others for their part offered water to the departed king, saying “Dear father, let this water reach you.” (24-25)

verses.text:
प्रगृह्य तु महीपालो जलापूरितमञ्जलिम्।
दिशं याम्यामभिमुखो रुदन् वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Holding together, in the form of a hollow, his palms full of water, and standing with his face turned towards the southern quarter presided over by Yama, the god of death, Śrī Rāma, the ruler of the earth, for his part spoke weeping as follows : (26)

verses.text:
एतत् ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम्।
पितृलोकगतस्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Let this limpid water offered by me today serve you, who have left for the world of manes, inexhaustibly, O tiger among kings !” (27)

verses.text:
ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरं प्रत्युत्तीर्य स राघवः।
पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निर्वापं भ्रातृभिः सह॥ २८॥
verses.m: Re-ascending to the bank of the Mandākinī the celebrated and glorious Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) then offered balls of food to his father alongwith his other three brothers. (28)

verses.text:
ऐङ्गुदं बदरैर्मिश्रं पिण्याकं दर्भसंस्तरे।
न्यस्य रामः सुदुःखार्तो रुदन् वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Serving the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī fruit mixed with the pulp of plums on a mat of Kuśa grass, Śrī Rāma, who was sore stricken with agony, spoke weeping as follows : (29)

verses.text:
इदं भुङ् क्ष्व महाराज प्रीतो यदशना वयम्।
यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Delightfully partake of this, which is our only food, O great monarch! Deties partake of the same food which a man worshipping them eats.” (30)

verses.text:
ततस्तेनैव मार्गेण प्रत्युत्तीर्य सरित्तटात्।
आरुरोह नरव्याघ्रो रम्यसानुं महीधरम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Moving up from the river bank once more by the same route along which he had descended, Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, then ascended the mountain Citrakūṭa, which was crowned with a lovely summit. (31)

verses.text:
ततः पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपतिः।
परिजग्राह पाणिभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Reaching the entrance of the hut of leafy twigs in which he dwelt, Śrī Rāma (the emperor) now clasped both Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa by his hands and wept loudly. (32)

verses.text:
तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात् प्रतिशब्दोऽभवद् गिरौ।
भ्रातॄणां सह वैदेह्या सिंहानां नर्दतामिव॥ ३३॥
verses.m: From the cry of those brothers with Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, which resembled the noise of roaring lions, rose an echo in the mountain. (33)

verses.text:
महाबलानां रुदतां कुर्वतामुदकं पितुः।
विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दं त्रस्ता भरतसैनिकाः॥ ३४॥
अब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरतः संगतो ध्रुवम्।
तेषामेव महान् शब्दः शोचतां पितरं मृतम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The troops of Bharata got alarmed to hear the confused noise of the four exceptionally mighty brothers, who, they thought were crying while offering water to the spirit of their deceased father, and said to one another, “Surely Prince Bharata has met Śrī Rāma. This is undoubtedly the loud cry of those four brothers mourning for their deceased father.” (34-35)•

verses.text:
अथ वाहान् परित्यज्य तं सर्वेऽभिमुखाः स्वनम्।
अप्येकमनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानं प्रधाविताः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Leaving their conveyances, all troops without exception ran fast with an undivided mind to the place from which the sound was coming, with their faces turned towards that sound. (36)

verses.text:
हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलंकृतैः।
सुकुमारास्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययुः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Some people, other than the troops, who were tender of body rode on horses, others on elephants and still others in chariots tastefully decorated; while still others went on foot alone. (37)

verses.text:
अचिरप्रोषितं रामं चिरविप्रोषितं यथा।
द्रष्टुकामो जनः सर्वो जगाम सहसाश्रमम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Eager to see Śrī Rāma, as though he had been away from his home, Ayodhyā, for a long time, although he had left his home not long before, all men rushed headlong to the hermitage of Śrī Rāma. (38)

verses.text:
भ्रातॄणां त्वरितास्ते तु द्रष्टुकामाः समागमम्।
ययुर्बहुविधैर्यानैः खुरनेमिसमाकुलैः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Keen to behold the meeting of the four brothers, they for their part hastily rode on hoofed animals and wheeled vehicles of various kinds. (39)

verses.text:
सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानै रथनेमिसमाहता।
मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Run over by many animals and vehicles and consequently struck against by hoofs and felloes, that land of Citrakūṭa produced a tumultuous noise as heavens do during the gathering of clouds. (40)

verses.text:
तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः।
आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनं ततः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Terrified by that noise, wild elephants accompanied by female elephants migrated to another forest from that place, perfuming the quarters with the scent of their ichor. (41)

verses.text:
वराहवृकसिंहाश्च महिषाः सृमरास्तथा।
व्याघ्रगोकर्णगवया वित्रेसुः पृषतैः सह॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Boars, wolves and lions, buffaloes, Sṛmaras and Gokarṇas, two distinctive species of deer, as well as tigers and Gavayas alongwith spotted deer felt stricken with terror. (42)

verses.text:
रथाह्वहंसानत्यूहाः प्लवाः कारण्डवाः परे।
तथा पुंस्कोकिलाः क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Cakrawākas, swans and waterfowl, Plavas (a kind of heron), Kāraṇḍavas (a sort of duck) and other aquatic birds, male cuckoos and cranes flew utterly confused in various directions. (43)

verses.text:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकाशं पक्षिभिर्वृतम्।
मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयं प्रबभौ तदा॥ ४४॥
verses.m: The sky was screened with birds terrified by that sound, while the land was covered with men; and both looked most charming on that occasion. (44)

verses.text:
ततस्तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं यशस्विनमकल्मषम्।
आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामं ददर्श सहसा जनः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: All of a sudden people now beheld the illustrious and sinless Śrī Rāma, that tiger among men, sitting on the altar. (45)

verses.text:
विगर्हमाणः कैकेयीं मन्थरासहितामपि।
अभिगम्य जनो रामं बाष्पपूर्णमुखोऽभवत्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Approaching Śrī Rāma, the people, who had been reproaching Kaikeyī, including Mantharā too, found their own face bathed in tears. (46)

verses.text:
तान् नरान् बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान् समीक्ष्याथ सुदुःखितान्।
पर्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञः पितृवन्मातृवच्च सः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Perceiving those men sore distressed with their eyes full of tears, Śrī Rāma, who knew what is right, presently embraced them like their father and mother. (47)

verses.text:
स तत्र कांश्चित् परिषस्वजे नरान्
नराश्च केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन्।
चकार सर्वान् सवयस्यबान्धवान्
यथार्हमासाद्य तदा नृपात्मजः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Nay, he embraced some men who deserved it, while others on that spot hailed him. Approaching them on that occasion, the princes received them all including his friends and relations according to the rank of each. (48)

verses.text:
ततः स तेषां रुदतां महात्मनां
भुवं च खं चानुविनादयन् स्वनः।
गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च संततं
मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिमो विशुश्रुवे॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Making the earth and the heavens as well as the mountain caves and the quarters incessantly resound, the aforesaid cry of those wailing high-souled men was continuously heard far and wide like the sound of a clay tomtom. (49)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठः पुरतः कृत्वा दारान् दशरथस्य च।
अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षितः॥ १॥
verses.m: Placing the widows of King Daśaratha in the forefront, Vasiṣṭha, who was feeling athirst for the sight of Śrī Rāma, proceeded to that region where Śrī Rāma was sojourning. (1)

verses.text:
राजपत्न्यश्च गच्छन्त्यो मन्दं मन्दाकिनीं प्रति।
ददृशुस्तत्र तत् तीर्थं रामलक्ष्मणसेवितम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Making their way with slow paces towards the river Mandākinī the dowager queens saw there a descent (suitable for bathing etc.) to the river resorted to by Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. (2)

verses.text:
कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता।
सुमित्रामब्रवीद् दीनां याश्चान्या राजयोषितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: With a withering face bathed in tears, Kausalyā spoke as follows to the afflicted Sumitrā and the other queens that were present there : (3)

verses.text:
इदं तेषामनाथानां क्लिष्टमक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्।
वने प्राक्कलनं तीर्थं ये ते निर्विषयीकृताः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Here is the descent selected for the first time by those fatherless children, who have been expelled from their kingdom and who are now living a hard life in the forest, though unwearied in action. (4)

verses.text:
इतः सुमित्रे पुत्रस्ते सदा जलमतन्द्रितः।
स्वयं हरति सौमित्रिर्मम पुत्रस्य कारणात्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Along this route, O Sumitrā, does your elder son, Lakṣmaṇa, ever unweariedly fetch water himself for the sake of my son (his elder brother). (5)

verses.text:
जघन्यमपि ते पुत्रः कृतवान् न तु गर्हितः।
भ्रातुर्यदर्थरहितं सर्वं तद् गर्हितं गुणैः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Your son has not been subjected to any reproach, even though he has done menial service to his elder brother. All that which is devoid of use to one’s elder brother, who is held to be on a par with one’s father, is censured by men possessed of noble qualities. (6)

verses.text:
अद्यायमपि ते पुत्रः क्लेशानामतथोचितः।
नीचानर्थसमाचारं सज्जं कर्म प्रमुञ्चतु॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Let this son of yours, too, who is undeserving of the hardships, which are being experienced by him, totally give up the work in hand whose execution is painful and fit for menials, now that his elder brother is soon returning to Ayodhyā.” (7)

verses.text:
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सा दर्दश महीतले।
पितुरिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं न्यस्तमायतलोचना॥ ८॥
verses.m: The large-eyed Kausalyā presently saw the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī fruits placed by Śrī Rāma on blades of Kuśa grass spread on the earth’s surface with their ends pointing to the south as an offering intended for the gratification of his deceased father. (8)

verses.text:
तं भूमौ पितुरार्तेन न्यस्तं रामेण वीक्ष्य सा।
उवाच देवी कौसल्या सर्वा दशरथस्त्रियः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Observing the said pulp placed on the ground by the afflicted Śrī Rāma for the gratification of his deceased father, the aforesaid Queen Kausalyā spoke as follows to all the other consorts of King Daśaratha : (9)

verses.text:
इदमिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः।
राघवेण पितुर्दत्तं पश्यतैतद् यथाविधि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Behold here this offering made in accordance with the scriptural ordinance by Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for the gratification of his high-souled father, the late King Daśaratha, also a scion of Raghu, the lord of the Ikṣwākus. (10)

verses.text:
तस्य देवसमानस्य पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः।
नैतदौपयिकं मन्ये भुक्तभोगस्य भोजनम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I do not consider this food (viz., the pulp of the Iṅgudī-fruit) to be fit for the consumption of that high-souled monarch, who vied with gods and had enjoyed all the luxuries of life. (11)

verses.text:
चतुरन्तां महीं भुक्त्वा महेन्द्रसदृशो भुवि।
कथमिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं स भुङ्क्ते वसुधाधिपः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Having ruled over the globe bounded by the four oceans, how will the emperor, who was a compeer on earth of the great Indra, be able to partake of the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī fruits? (12)

verses.text:
अतो दुःखतरं लोके न किंचित् प्रतिभाति मे।
यत्र रामः पितुर्दद्यादिङ्गुदीक्षोदमृद्धिमान्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nothing in the world appears more painful to me than the occasion when Rāma, who is full of riches of every description, should feel constrained to offer the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī fruits to the spirit of his deceased father. (13)

verses.text:
रामेणेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं पितुर्दत्तं समीक्ष्य मे।
कथं दुःखेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Why does my heart not get split into a thousand fragments through agony perceiving the crushed pulp of Iṅgudī fruits offered by Rāma to the spirit of his deceased father?” (14)

verses.text:
श्रुतिस्तु खल्वियं सत्या लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मे।
यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The popular saying that the deities of a man partake of the same food on which a man subsists, appears undoubtedly true to us.” (15)

verses.text:
एवमार्तां सपत्न्यस्ता जग्मुराश्वास्य तां तदा।
ददृशुश्चाश्रमे रामं स्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Comforting the afflicted Kausalyā in the foregoing words on that occassion, her aforesaid co-wives departed with Kausalyā and beheld Śrī Rāma seated in his hermitage like an immortal fallen from heaven. (16)

verses.text:
तं भोगैः सम्परित्यक्तं रामं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मातरः।
आर्ता मुमुचुरश्रूणि सस्वरं शोककर्शिताः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Distressed to observe the celebrated Śrī Rāma shorn of all luxuries, his mothers wept loudly, emaciated as they were through grief. (17)

verses.text:
तासां रामः समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणाम्बुजान्।
मातॄणां मनुजव्याघ्रः सर्वासां सत्यसंगरः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Duly rising from his seat, Śrī Rāma, a veritable tiger among men, who was true to his promise, clasped the lotus-like feet of all his aforesaid mothers. (18)

verses.text:
ताः पाणिभिः सुखस्पर्शैर्मृद्वङ्गुलितलैः शुभैः।
प्रममार्जू रजः पृष्ठाद् रामस्यायतलोचनाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: With their lovely hands, which were delightful to the touch and the base of whose fingers was exceptionally soft, those large-eyed ladies wiped the dust off Śrī Rāma’s back. (19)

verses.text:
सौमित्रिरपि ताः सर्वा मातॄः सम्प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितः।
अभ्यवादयदासक्तं शनै रामादनन्तरम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Distressed to perceive all the aforesaid mothers, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) too fondly greeted them immediately after Śrī Rāma. (20)

verses.text:
यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन् सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रियः।
वृत्तिं दशरथाज्जाते लक्ष्मणे शुभलक्षणे॥ २१॥
verses.m: All the ladies behaved towards the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, sprung from the loins of Daśaratha, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks, in the same way as they did towards Śrī Rāma. (21)

verses.text:
सीतापि चरणांस्तासामुपसंगृह्य दुःखिता।
श्वश्रूणामश्रुपूर्णाक्षी सम्बभूवाग्रतः स्थिता॥ २२॥
verses.m: Holding firmly the feet of the said mothers-in-law, Sītā too stood agonized before them with her eyes full of tears. (22)

verses.text:
तां परिष्वज्य दुःखार्ता माता दुहितरं यथा।
वनवासकृतां दीनां कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रतीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Embracing her, as a mother would embrace her own daughter, the sorrow-stricken Kausalyā spoke as follows to Sītā, who looked withered through exile in the forest : (23)

verses.text:
वैदेहराजन्यसुता स्नुषा दशरथस्य च।
रामपत्नी कथं दुःखं सम्प्राप्ता विजने वने॥ २४॥
verses.m: “I wonder how the consort of Rāma, daughter of Janaka (a royal personage of the Videha clan) and daughter-in-law of Emperor Daśaratha, has undergone suffering in a lonely forest. (24)

verses.text:
पद्ममातपसंतप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम्।
काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदैः॥ २५॥
मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाश्रयम्।
भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भवः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “The fire of grief produced by the firewood of adversity and existing in my mind, O princess of the Videha kingdom, burns me to the core even as the element of fire consumes the very substance that sustains it, when I gaze on your countenance resembling a lotus scorched by the sun, a crushed lily, gold soiled with dust and the moon obscured by clouds.” (25-26)

verses.text:
ब्रुवन्त्यामेवमार्तायां जनन्यां भरताग्रजः।
पादावासाद्य जग्राह वसिष्ठस्य च राघवः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Reaching the feet of Vasiṣṭha, while his distressed mother was speaking as aforesaid, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the elder brother of Bharata, clasped them. (27)

verses.text:
पुरोहितस्याग्निसमस्य तस्य वै
बृहस्पतेरिन्द्र इवामराधिपः।
प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजसः
सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघवः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Holding the feet of the said priest—who was possessed of very great splendour and resembled the fire-god—even as Indra, the ruler of gods, would clasp the feet of Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of gods, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) took his seat with Vasiṣṭha himself. (28)

verses.text:
ततो जघन्यं सहितैः स्वमन्त्रिभिः
पुरप्रधानैश्च तथैव सैनिकैः।
जनेन धर्मज्ञतमेन धर्मवा-
नुपोपविष्टो भरतस्तदाग्रजम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Thereupon alongwith his friends, counsellors and the foremost of citizens as well as with the troops and men who knew best what is right, the celebrated Bharata, who was full of piety, sat down on that occasion close to his elder brother, Śrī Rāma, at his back. (29)

verses.text:
उपोपविष्टस्तु तदातिवीर्यवां-
स्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम्।
श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरतः कृताञ्जलि-
र्यथा महेन्द्रः प्रयतः प्रजापतिम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Perceiving Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, blazing with glory in the garb of an ascetic, Bharata, for his part, who was seated closeby at that time and was exceedingly powerful, folded his hands in the same way as the mighty Indra submissively would before Brahmā, the lord of created beings. (30)

verses.text:
किमेष वाक्यं भरतोऽद्य राघवं
प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति।
इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो
बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा॥ ३१॥
verses.m: A great curiosity really arose at that moment in the mind of those worthies assembled there as to what submission yonder Bharata would now politely make after bowing low and paying his homage to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, that day. (31)

verses.text:
स राघवः सत्यधृतिश्च लक्ष्मणो
महानुभावो भरतश्च धार्मिकः।
वृताः सुहृद्भिश्च विरेजिरेऽध्वरे
यथा सदस्यैः सहितास्त्रयोऽग्नयः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Nay, surrounded by their near and dear ones, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who was firmly devoted to truthfulness, and the noble-minded Lakṣmaṇa and the pious Bharata shone brightly on the sacrificial ground like the three sacrificial fires (known by the names of Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇā) accompanied by the superintending priests. (32)

verses.text:
ततः पुरुषसिंहानां वृतानां तैः सुहृद्गणैः।
शोचतामेव रजनी दुःखेन व्यत्यवर्तत॥ १॥
verses.m: The night subsequently passed away in sorrow in the case of the said tigers among men, accompanied by those near and dear ones, while the former were grieving. (1)

verses.text:
रजन्यां सुप्रभातायां भ्रातरस्ते सुहृद्वृताः।
मन्दाकिन्यां हुतं जप्यं कृत्वा राममुपागमन्॥ २॥
verses.m: Having offered oblations into the sacred fire and muttered their prayers on the bank of the Mandākinī, when the night had been vividly relieved by dawn, the aforesaid brothers, accompanied by their near and dear ones, sought the presence of Śrī Rāma. (2)

verses.text:
तूष्णीं ते समुपासीना न कश्चित् किंचिदब्रवीत्।
भरतस्तु सुहृन्मध्ये रामं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: They all sat down mute, none spoke anything. Bharata for his part made the following submission to Śrī Rāma in the midst of his near and dear ones : (3)

verses.text:
सान्त्विता मामिका माता दत्तं राज्यमिदं मम।
तद् ददामि तवैवाहं भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “My mother Kaikeyī has been consoled by you and this kingdom of Ayodhyā bestowed on me. I hereby return it to your own self. Please enjoy it without impediment. (4)

verses.text:
महतेवाम्बुवेगेन भिन्नः सेतुर्जलागमे।
दुरावरं त्वदन्येन राज्यखण्डमिदं महत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Just as a dam breached by a mighty onrush of water during the rains cannot be easily repaired, this large state of Ayodhyā cannot be easily held in one’s sway by anyone other than you. (5)

verses.text:
गतिं खर इवाश्वस्य तार्क्ष्यस्येव पतत्त्रिणः।
अनुगन्तुं न शक्तिर्मे गतिं तव महीपते॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The power to emulate your ruling capacity does not lie in me, O ruler of the globe, any more than the power to emulate the gait of a horse in a donkey and the flight of Garuḍa, the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu, in a common bird. (6)

verses.text:
सुजीवं नित्यशस्तस्य यः परैरुपजीव्यते।
राम तेन तु दुर्जीवं यः परानुपजीवति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Know his life to be blessed from day to day, who is depended upon by others. Life is, however, dragged on with hardship by him who depends for his life upon others, O Rāma ! (7)

verses.text:
यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः।
ह्रस्वकेन दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “For example a tree planted and nurtured by a man develops in course of time into a mighty tree with a stout trunk, hard to scale for a dwarf. (8)

verses.text:
स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्।
स तां नानुभवेत् प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “But when, though laden with flowers, it does not bear fruit, the man does not experience the same delight which he expected from it due to his failure to reach the consummation for which it was planted with effort. (9)

verses.text:
एषोपमा महाबाहो तदर्थं वेत्तुमर्हसि।
यत्र त्वमस्मान् वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान् न शाधि हि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This is only an analogy, O mighty-armed brother: be pleased to make out its meaning, since you, our supreme master, do not care to instruct us, your servants, on this occasion when it becomes you to protect us. (10)

verses.text:
श्रेणयस्त्वां महाराज पश्यन्त्वग्र्याश्च सर्वशः।
प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं राज्यस्थितमरिंदमम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Let the guilds of traders (of every class) and their leaders behold you, the subduer of enemies, seated on the throne like the sun blazing on all sides, O great king ! (11)

verses.text:
तथानुयाने काकुत्स्थ मत्ता नर्दन्तु कुञ्जराः।
अन्तःपुरगता नार्यो नन्दन्तु सुसमाहिताः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Likewise, let the elephants in rut trumpet in the course of your return journey to Ayodhyā and let the ladies living in the royal gynaeceum, fully collected in mind, rejoice to see you returned.” (12)

verses.text:
तस्य साध्वनुमन्यन्त नागरा विविधा जनाः।
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामं प्रत्यनुयाचतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of the celebrated Bharata, supplicating as aforesaid Śrī Rāma, the citizens of every class, assembled at Citrakūṭa, acclaimed it in the words “Well said !” (13)

verses.text:
तमेवं दुःखितं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं यशस्विनम्।
रामः कृतात्मा भरतं समाश्वासयदात्मवान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Perceiving the said illustrious Bharata wailing as above, afflicted as he was, Śrī Rāma, who was self possessed and self-disciplined comforted him in the following words : (14)

verses.text:
नात्मनः कामकारो हि पुरुषोऽयमनीश्वरः।
इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Freedom of action does not belong to the embodied soul, since this soul is powerless (unlike God). Providence alone forcibly drags the soul hither and thither. (15)

verses.text:
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः।
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “All accumulations end in attenuation; all elevations end in degradation; all unions end in separation; all life has its end in death. (16)

verses.text:
यथा फलानां पक्वानां नान्यत्र पतनाद् भयम्।
एवं नरस्य जातस्य नान्यत्र मरणाद् भयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “As no fear from any quarter other than a fall awaits ripe fruits, so no fear from any quarter other than death awaits a man come into the world. (17)

verses.text:
यथाऽऽगारं दृढस्थूणं जीर्णं भूत्वोपसीदति।
तथावसीदन्ति नरा जरामृत्युवशंगताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Even as a house though supported by stout pillars collapses on getting old, so men fallen into the clutches of old age and death breathe their last. (18)

verses.text:
अत्येति रजनी या तु सा न प्रतिनिवर्तते।
यात्येव यमुना पूर्णं समुद्रमुदकार्णवम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The night that passes away does not return in any case; the Yamunā (river) meets without fail the all-sufficient ocean, abounding in water. (19)

verses.text:
अहोरात्राणि गच्छन्ति सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह।
आयूंषि क्षपयन्त्याशु ग्रीष्मे जलमिवांशवः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Passing days and nights quickly end the life-span of all living beings in this world, even as sunbeams suck up water in summer. (20)

verses.text:
आत्मानमनुशोच त्वं किमन्यमनुशोचसि।
आयुस्तु हीयते यस्य स्थितस्यास्य गतस्य च॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Grieve for yourself alone, why do you grieve for another? In fact, the life-span of each and every creature, whether staying at home or departed for another place, gets shortened every moment. (21)

verses.text:
सहैव मृत्युर्व्रजति सह मृत्युर्निषीदति।
गत्वा सुदीर्घमध्वानं सह मृत्युर्निवर्तते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Death ever walks with us when we are walking and remains seated with us while we are sitting. Nay, having travelled a very long distance with us death returns with us on our return. (22)

verses.text:
गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ताः श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः।
जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “When folds have appeared on the skin of the limbs and the hair have turned grey, by what expedient will a man, worn out with age, be able to control them?(23)

verses.text:
नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि।
आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Men rejoice when the sun has risen and also rejoice when the day has ended, but do not perceive the ebbing of their life. (24)

verses.text:
हृष्यन्त्यृतुमुखं दृष्ट्वा नवं नवमिवागतम्।
ऋतूनां परिवर्तेन प्राणिनां प्राणसंक्षयः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “People rejoice to see the approach of a season (say, the vernal season or the monsoon) as though it had appeared for the first time. But they forget that with a change of season comes about the gradual waning of life of living beings. (25)

verses.text:
यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे।
समेत्य तु व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कंचन॥ २६॥
एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च।
समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Even as two pieces of drift-wood come together on the surface of an ocean at a particular moment of time and, having come together in this way, drift apart on reaching a particular moment, so wives and sons as well as relations and riches part company after coming together; for inevitable is their separation. (26-27)

verses.text:
नात्र कश्चिद् यथाभावं प्राणी समतिवर्तते।
तेन तस्मिन् न सामर्थ्यं प्रेतस्यास्त्यनुशोचतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “No living being in this world can escape its destiny in the shape of birth and death when the time comes for it. Hence the power to avert his own death does not inhere in a man, even though mourning again and again for a dead person. (28)

verses.text:
यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात् कश्चित् पथि स्थितः।
अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवतामिति॥ २९॥
एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहैर्ध्रुवः।
तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद् यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “How can he who has got on the inevitable path trodden by his forbears, viz., his father, grandfather and so on, and from which there is no escape—even as one standing on the roadside would cry to a group of travellers passing by, ‘I shall also follow at your heels (and would forthwith follow them), mourn for his parents and other departed relations? (29-30)

verses.text:
वयसः पतमानस्य स्रोतसो वानिवर्तिनः।
आत्मा सुखे नियोक्तव्यः सुखभाजः प्रजाः स्मृताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Foreseeing the inevitable end of one’s ebbing life, which does not return any more than a stream, one’s own self should be employed in a pursuit leading to blessedness; for living beings are declared as pursuing happiness. (31)

verses.text:
धर्मात्मा सुशुभैः कृत्स्नैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः।
धूतपापो गतः स्वर्गं पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Our father, the king, the lord of the earth, was a virtuous person. He performed almost all extremely auspicious sacrifices and paid plentiful sacrificial fees to the officiating priests and Brahmins. All his sins were washed away and so he went to the heaven. (32)

verses.text:
भृत्यानां भरणात् सम्यक् प्रजानां परिपालनात्।
अर्थादानाच्च धर्मेण पिता नस्त्रिदिवं गतः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “On account of properly maintaining the servants, protecting and guarding the subjects and realising taxes in the manner prescribed by scriptures from them, our father has gone to the heaven. (33)

verses.text:
कर्मभिस्तु शुभैरिष्टैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः।
स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Our father, Daśaratha, the lord of the earth, has reached heaven on account of his performing all auspicious acts desirable, and performing many sacrifices involving heavy sacrificial fees. (34)

verses.text:
इष्ट्वा बहुविधैर्यज्ञैर्भोगांश्चावाप्य पुष्कलान्।
उत्तमं चायुरासाद्य स्वर्गतः पृथिवीपतिः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Having propitiated the Yajñapuruṣa by performing different types of sacrifices, enjoying worldly pleasures in plenty and having lived a long and virtuous life, the lord of the earth has gone to the heaven. (35)

verses.text:
आयुरुत्तममासाद्य भोगानपि च राघवः।
न स शोच्यः पिता तात स्वर्गतः सत्कृतः सताम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Having obtained a long life and worldly luxuries, the father, from the Raghu dynasty, has gone to the heaven coveted and honoured by the virtuous people, O dear ! He is not at all to be lamented upon. (36)

verses.text:
स जीर्णमानुषं देहं परित्यज्य पिता हि नः।
दैवीमृद्धिमनुप्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Having shed his worn-out human frame, our father has surely attained celestial wealth in the form of an ethereal body etc., which enables him to sport even in the realm of Brahmā (the highest heaven). (37)

verses.text:
तं तु नैवंविधः कश्चित् प्राज्ञः शोचितुमर्हसि।
त्वद्विधो मद्विधश्चापि श्रुतवान् बुद्धिमत्तरः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “No highly wise, learned and exceptionally clever man, such as you and I are, ought to grieve for the emperor. (38)

verses.text:
एते बहुविधाः शोका विलापरुदिते तदा।
वर्जनीया हि धीरेण सर्वावस्थासु धीमता॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “These manifold griefs as well as wailing and weeping should in that case undoubtedly be given up under all circumstances by a resolute man possessed of wisdom. (39)

verses.text:
स स्वस्थो भव मा शोको यात्वा चावस तां पुरीम्।
तथा पित्रा नियुक्तोऽसि वशिना वदतां वर॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “As such, be at ease; let not grief overpower you. And, returning home, dwell in that city of Ayodhyā. So have you been enjoined by father, a master of his will, O jewel among the eloquent ! (40)

verses.text:
यत्राहमपि तेनैव नियुक्तः पुण्यकर्मणा।
तत्रैवाहं करिष्यामि पितुरार्यस्य शासनम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “I too shall do the bidding of our noble father continuing in that very place where I have been enjoined to stay by that emperor of virtuous deeds. (41)

verses.text:
न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्यमरिंदम।
स त्वयापि सदा मान्यः स वै बन्धुः स नः पिता॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “It is not justifiable on my part to flout his command, O subduer of foes ! He ever deserved to be honoured even by you, since he was our friend, he was our (very) father. (42)

verses.text:
तद् वचः पितुरेवाहं सम्मतं धर्मचारिणाम्।
कर्मणा पालयिष्यामि वनवासेन राघव॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Through my action in the shape of sojourning in the forest, O scion of Raghu, I shall obey that very command of my father, which is thought highly of by those practising virtue. (43)

verses.text:
धार्मिकेणानृशंसेन नरेण गुरुवर्तिना।
भवितव्यं नरव्याघ्र परलोकं जिगीषता॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “A pious man seeking to conquer the other world, O tiger among men, ought to be kind-hearted and obedient to his elders, father and others. (44)

verses.text:
आत्मानमनुतिष्ठ त्वं स्वभावेन नरर्षभ।
निशाम्य तु शुभं वृत्तं पितुर्दशरथस्य नः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Keeping in view the virtuous conduct of our father, King Daśaratha, O jewel among men, direct your thoughts only towards the welfare in the other world of your spirit in consonance with your pious nature.” (45)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा
पितुर्निदेशप्रतिपालनार्थम्।
यवीयसं भ्रातरमर्थवच्च
प्रभुर्मुहूर्ताद् विरराम रामः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Having tendered to his younger brother, Bharata, in about an hour, the aforesaid significant advice, urging him to carry out the behests of their father, the high-souled and almighty Śrī Rāma became silent. (46)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु विरते रामे वचनमर्थवत्।
ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे रामं प्रकृतिवत्सलम्॥ १॥
उवाच भरतश्चित्रं धार्मिको धार्मिकं वचः।
को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृशस्त्वमरिंदम॥ २॥
verses.m: When Śrī Rāma became silent after making a significant speech as aforesaid, the pious Bharata for his part now addressed to Śrī Rāma, who was so fond of his people, the following agreeable and righteous submission on the bank of the Mandākinī: “Indeed, who can there be in this world such as you are, O tamer of foes? (1-2)

verses.text:
न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद् दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा न प्रहर्षयेत्।
सम्मतश्चापि वृद्धानां तांश्च पृच्छसि संशयान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Neither can sorrow torment you nor can joy exhilarate you. Though highly thought of by the elders, you nevertheless refer your doubts to them. (3)

verses.text:
यथा मृतस्तथा जीवन् यथासति तथा सति।
यस्यैष बुद्धिलाभः स्यात् परितप्येत केन सः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Wherefore should he grieve, he who has developed an attitude of mind by virtue of which, though living, he is as good as dead to the world and which makes him as indifferent to the existent as to the non-existent? (4)

verses.text:
परावरज्ञो यश्च स्याद् यथा त्वं मनुजाधिप।
स एव व्यसनं प्राप्य न विषीदितुमर्हति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “He who knows the Self as well as the non-Self as you do, O ruler of men, ought not to feel dejected even on meeting with adversity. (5)

verses.text:
अमरोपमसत्त्वस्त्वं महात्मा सत्यसंगरः।
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च बुद्धिमांश्चासि राघव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Possessed of valour comparing with that of gods, and endowed with great fortitude, you are true to your promise, all-knowing, all-seeing and wise too, O scion of Raghu ! (6)

verses.text:
न त्वामेवंगुणैर्युक्तं प्रभवाभवकोविदम्।
अविषह्यतमं दुःखमासादयितुमर्हति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Even affliction, which is most unbearable for us, ought not to assail you, endowed as you are with such virtues and conversant with the origin and end of living beings. (7)

verses.text:
प्रोषिते मयि यत् पापं मात्रा मत्कारणात् कृतम्।
क्षुद्रया तदनिष्टं मे प्रसीदतु भवान् मम॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The sinful deed in the shape of bringing about your exile which was perpetrated by my mean mother for my sake when I was away, was not to my liking. Therefore, be gracious to me. (8)

verses.text:
धर्मबन्धेन बद्धोऽस्मि तेनेमां नेह मातरम्।
हन्मि तीव्रेण दण्डेन दण्डार्हां पापकारिणीम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I am bound by fetters of morality which forbid a warrior to lay his finger upon a woman; hence I do not kill on the spot with a severe punishment my mother of sinful deeds, who is deserving of punishment. (9)

verses.text:
कथं दशरथाज्जातः शुभाभिजनकर्मणः।
जानन् धर्ममधर्मं च कुर्यां कर्म जुगुप्सितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: How can I, sprung as I am from the loins of Daśaratha of noble birth and deeds, and knowing as I do right and wrong, perpetrate an odious act like killing my own mother? (10)

verses.text:
गुरुः क्रियावान् वृद्धश्च राजा प्रेतः पितेति च।
तातं न परिगर्हेऽहं दैवतं चेति संसदि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I do not wish to denounce my father in an open assembly because he had a number of sacrificial performances to his credit, was aged and worthy of respect, has joined the majority and was my father and a deity to me. (11)

verses.text:
को हि धर्मार्थयोर्हीनमीदृशं कर्म किल्बिषम्।
स्त्रियः प्रियचिकीर्षुः सन् कुर्याद् धर्मज्ञ धर्मवित्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Indeed, what man, who knows the principles of morality, would perpetrate such a sinful act, unproductive of religious merit and worldly prosperity, with intent to please a woman, O knower of what is right? (12)

verses.text:
अन्तकाले हि भूतानि मुह्यन्तीति पुरा श्रुतिः।
राज्ञैवं कुर्वता लोके प्रत्यक्षा सा श्रुतिः कृता॥ १३॥
verses.m: “There is an old adage saying that living beings invariably get infatuated at the hour of death. That saying has been illustrated to the world by the king while acting as he has done. (13)

verses.text:
साध्वर्थमभिसंधाय क्रोधान्मोहाच्च साहसात्।
तातस्य यदतिक्रान्तं प्रत्याहरतु तद् भवान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Keeping in mind a noble purpose, nullify the transgression that has been committed by father for fear of wrath of Kaikeyī or through infatuation and precipitance. (14)

verses.text:
पितुर्हि समतिक्रान्तं पुत्रो यः साधु मन्यते।
तदपत्यं मतं लोके विपरीतमतोऽन्यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “A son who mends the arrant transgression of his father is accounted a son in the real acceptance of the term* in the world; he who acts otherwise than this is quite the reverse of a son. (15)

verses.text:
तदपत्यं भवानस्तु मा भवान् दुष्कृतं पितुः।
अति यत् तत् कृतं कर्म लोके धीरविगर्हितम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Therefore be you a true son; do not countenance the sinful act of our father by implementing his word. The act which has been perpetrated by him is in contravention of all principles of morality and is, therefore, utterly condemned in the world by the wise. (16)

verses.text:
कैकेयीं मां च तातं च सुहृदो बान्धवांश्च नः।
पौरजानपदान् सर्वांस्त्रातुं सर्वमिदं भवान्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Be pleased to grant all this prayer of mine in order to save Kaikeyī, myself, father, nay, our friends and relations as well as all the citizens and people of the country-side. (17)

verses.text:
क्व चारण्यं क्व च क्षात्रं क्व जटाः क्व च पालनम्।
ईदृशं व्याहतं कर्म न भवान् कर्तुमर्हति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “What congruity is there between forest life, on the one hand, and the duty of a Kṣatriya, on the other, between wearing matted locks on one’s head and protection of the people? You ought not to perpetrate such an incongruous act as may stand in the way of your discharging the duty of a Kṣatriya, viz., protection of the people. (18)

verses.text:
एष हि प्रथमो धर्मः क्षत्रियस्याभिषेचनम्।
येन शक्यं महाप्राज्ञ प्रजानां परिपालनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Indeed, it is the foremost duty of a Kṣatriya to get himself consecrated as a king, through which act alone it is possible to protect the people, O highly enlightened brother ! (19)

verses.text:
कश्च प्रत्यक्षमुत्सृज्य संशयस्थमलक्षणम्।
आयतिस्थं चरेद् धर्मं क्षत्रबन्धुरनिश्चितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, neglecting a duty yielding visible joy, what Kṣatriya esteemed by his race would practise a virtue which is of doubtful result, which does not promise happiness, which brings its reward in a future state only and which is undefined? (20)

verses.text:
अथ क्लेशजमेव त्वं धर्मं चरितुमिच्छसि।
धर्मेण चतुरो वर्णान् पालयन् क्लेशमाप्नुहि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “If you desire to pursue a virtue following from hardship alone, undergo suffering while protecting the four divisions of society by recourse to righteousness. (21)

verses.text:
चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमुत्तमम्।
आहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तुमिच्छसि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The knowers of what is right definitely declare the life of a householder to be the noblest and best of all the four stages of life, inasmuch as it is depended upon by all others; how then do you seek to abandon it, O knower of the principles of righteousness? (22)

verses.text:
श्रुतेन बालः स्थानेन जन्मना भवतो ह्यहम्।
स कथं पालयिष्यामि भूमिं भवति तिष्ठति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I am decidedly junior to you in point of learning, rank and date of brith. As such how shall I be able to rule over the earth when you are present? (23)

verses.text:
हीनबुद्धिगुणो बालो हीनस्थानेन चाप्यहम्।
भवता च विनाभूतो न वर्तयितुमुत्सहे॥ २४॥
verses.m: “A mere child as I am, of poor understanding and virtues, and also placed in an inferior position as compared to you, I cannot even live without you, much less rule over the people. (24)

verses.text:
इदं निखिलमप्यग्र्यं राज्यं पित्र्यमकण्टकम्।
अनुशाधि स्वधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ सह बान्धवैः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “O knower of what is right, rule with your kinsmen over the whole of this foremost ancestral kingdom, without opposition, according to the code of conduct prescribed for you. (25)

verses.text:
इहैव त्वाभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वाः प्रकृतयः सह।
ऋत्विजः सवसिष्ठाश्च मन्त्रविन्मन्त्रकोविदाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Let all the ministers as well as the priests including Vasiṣṭha, well-versed in sacred formulas, conjointly consecrate you as the king of Ayodhyā on this very spot, O knower of sacred texts ! (26)

verses.text:
अभिषिक्तस्त्वमस्माभिरयोध्यां पालने व्रज।
विजित्य तरसा लोकान् मरुद्भिरिव वासवः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Consecrated by us, as Indra by Maruts (the wind-gods), and having conquered the worlds by dint of your might, march you back to Ayodhyā in order to rule over it. (27)

verses.text:
ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकुर्वन् दुर्हृदः साधु निर्दहन्।
सुहृदस्तर्पयन् कामैस्त्वमेवात्रानुशाधि माम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Discharging the three obligations you owe to gods, Ṛṣis and manes severally by offering oblations, studying the Vedas and procreating children, completely destroying the foes and gratifying your near and dear ones through their desired objects, you instruct me at Ayodhyā itself.” (28)

verses.text:
अद्यार्य मुदिताः सन्तु सुहृदस्तेऽभिषेचने।
अद्य भीताः पलायन्तु दुष्प्रदास्ते दिशो दश॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Let those who are friendly to you feel rejoiced today on your consecration as the king of Ayodhyā, O noble brother ! Let those who are inclined to cause pain to you run frightened in every direction today. (29)

verses.text:
आक्रोशं मम मातुश्च प्रमृज्य पुरुषर्षभ।
अद्य तत्रभवन्तं च पितरं रक्ष किल्बिषात्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Wiping off the obloquy attaching to me as well as to my mother, O jewel among men, save our esteemed father as well from remorse today. (30)

verses.text:
शिरसा त्वाभियाचेऽहं कुरुष्व करुणां मयि।
बान्धवेषु च सर्वेषु भूतेष्विव महेश्वरः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “I implore you with my head bent low: pray, take pity on me as well as on all your kinsfolk even as Lord Śiva, the Supreme Deity, does on all created beings. (31)

verses.text:
अथवा पृष्ठतः कृत्वा वनमेव भवानितः।
गमिष्यति गमिष्यामि भवता सार्धमप्यहम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Else, if setting aside my request, you proceed from this place to a forest alone, I too shall depart with you.” (32)

verses.text:
तथाभिरामो भरतेन ताम्यता
प्रसाद्यमानः शिरसा महीपतिः।
न चैव चक्रे गमनाय सत्त्ववान्
मतिं पितुस्तद् वचने प्रतिष्ठितः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Even while being propitiated as above with bowed head by Bharata, who was sinking in spirit, the graceful Śrī Rāma, the ruler of the globe, who had a strong will and clung fast to the word of his father giving consent to his exile, did not feel inclined to proceed to Ayodhyā. (33)

verses.text:
तदद्भुतं स्थैर्यमवेक्ष्य राघवे
समं जनो हर्षमवाप दुःखितः।
न यात्ययोध्यामिति दुःखितोऽभवत्
स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वमवेक्ष्य हर्षितः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Perceiving such wonderful firmness in Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the people of Ayodhyā experienced joy and felt disconsolate at the same time. They were distressed to find that he was not going to Ayodhyā and felt rejoiced to note his firmness of resolve. (34)

verses.text:
तमृत्विजो नैगमयूथवल्लभा-
स्तथा विसंज्ञाश्रुकलाश्च मातरः।
तथा ब्रुवाणं भरतं प्रतुष्टुवुः
प्रणम्य रामं च ययाचिरे सह॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The priests, the citizens and the leaders of different bodies of men as well as the mothers of Śrī Rāma and others, who had all been rendered senseless, as it were, and had tear-drops in their eyes, complimented Bharata, who was speaking in that strain, and bowing down low to Śrī Rāma, joined Bharata in his supplication to Śrī Rāma. (35)

verses.text:
पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तं भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
प्रत्युवाच ततः श्रीमान् ज्ञातिमध्ये सुसत्कृतः॥ १॥
verses.m: Thereupon the glorious Śrī Rāma, eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa, highly respected among his clansmen, replied to the said Bharata, who was speaking again in that strain : (1)

verses.text:
उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं यस्त्वमेवमभाषथाः।
जातः पुत्रो दशरथात् कैकेय्यां राजसत्तमात्॥ २॥
verses.m: “The assertion that you—a son born of Daśaratha, the foremost of kings, through Kaikeyī—have made just now, as above, is reasonable. (2)

verses.text:
पुरा भ्रातः पिता नः स मातरं ते समुद्वहन्।
मातामहे समाश्रौषीद् राज्यशुल्कमनुत्तमम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “In the past, while marrying Kaikeyī your mother, O brother, our celebrated father promised to your maternal grandfather the kingdom of Ayodhyā in favour of her issue as the best price for the marriage. (3)

verses.text:
देवासुरे च संग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिवः।
सम्प्रहृष्टो ददौ राजा वरमाराधितः प्रभुः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Nay, propitiated by standing him in goodstead in a conflict between the gods and the demons, and immensely delighted, the powerful king, who held sway over the entire globe, granted a boon to your mother. (4)

verses.text:
ततः सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी।
अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी॥ ५॥
तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा।
तच्च राजा तथा तस्यै नियुक्तः प्रददौ वरम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Then, binding him with a solemn oath your aforesaid illustrious mother, who was endowed with an excellent complexion, sought the following two boons of Daśaratha, the foremost of men, viz., (1) rulership for you, O tiger among men, and (2) exile for me; and urged thus, the king granted the aforesaid boons to her. (5-6)

verses.text:
तेन पित्राहमप्यत्र नियुक्तः पुरुषर्षभ।
चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वरदानिकम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I, too, O jewel among men, have been enjoined by our aforesaid father to dwell here in the forest for fourteen years in consequence of the boon granted by our father to your mother. (7)

verses.text:
सोऽयं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वितः।
सीतया चाप्रतिद्वन्द्वः सत्यवादे स्थितः पितुः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “As such I, who have no rival in this world and stand by the veracity of my father, have come to this lonely forest accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā. (8)

verses.text:
भवानपि तथेत्येव पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।
कर्तुमर्हसि राजेन्द्र क्षिप्रमेवाभिषिञ्चनात्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You too, O ruler of kings, ought likewise, as enjoined by our father, to vindicate the truthfulness of our father by getting yourself consecrated on the throne of Ayodhyā immediately. (9)

verses.text:
ऋणान्मोचय राजानं मत्कृते भरत प्रभुम्।
पितरं त्राहि धर्मज्ञ मातरं चाभिनन्दय॥ १०॥
verses.m: “For my sake, O Bharata, exonerate the powerful king from the debt he owes to Kaikeyī. Save our father by redeeming his promise and delight your mother, O knower of what is right ! (10)

verses.text:
श्रूयते धीमता तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विना।
गयेन यजमानेन गयेष्वेव पितॄन् प्रति॥ ११॥
पुन्नाम्नो नरकाद् यस्मात् पितरं त्रायते सुतः।
तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः पितॄन् यः पाति सर्वतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The following utterance, which is held sacred as a Śruti text, is heard to have been addressed to the manes by the wise and illustrious king named Gaya, who is believed to have founded the city of Gayā, while performing sacrifices in the territory of Gaya (the region which is now covered by the district of Gayā) : ‘Since a son delivers his father from the hell named ‘Put’ he is designated as Putra. According to another interpretation, a son is he who protects his father in all possible ways. (11-12)

verses.text:
एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुताः।
तेषां वै समवेतानामपि कश्चिद् गयां व्रजेत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “A number of sons, endowed with virtues and versed in many Śāstras, should be desired so that at least one of them may proceed to Gayā and perform Śrāddha there.” (13)

verses.text:
एवं राजर्षयः सर्वे प्रतीता रघुनन्दन।
तस्मात् त्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात् प्रभो॥ १४॥
verses.m: “So did all royal sages believe, O powerful scion of Raghu ! Therefore, O jewel among men, protect your father from hell. (14)

verses.text:
अयोध्यां गच्छ भरत प्रकृतीरुपरञ्जय।
शत्रुघ्नसहितो वीर सह सर्वैर्द्विजातिभिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by Śatrughna and together with all Brāhmaṇas return, O gallant Bharata, to Ayodhyā and protect the people. (15)

verses.text:
प्रवेक्ष्ये दण्डकारण्यमहमप्यविलम्बयन्।
आभ्यां तु सहितो वीर वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I too, for my part, accompanied by these two, viz., Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, and Lakṣmaṇa, shall enter the Daṇḍaka forest without tarrying here any longer. (16)

verses.text:
त्वं राजा भरत भव स्वयं नराणां
वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम्।
गच्छ त्वं पुरवरमद्य सम्प्रहृष्टः
संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान् प्रवेक्ष्ये॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Be you, O Bharata, the ruler of the people themselves. I too shall be the emperor of wild beasts. Return you, extremely delighted, to Ayodhyā, the foremost of cities, this very day and I too shall enter the Daṇḍaka forest highly rejoiced. (17)

verses.text:
छायां ते दिनकरभाः प्रबाधमानं
वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम्।
एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां
छायां तामतिशयिनीं शनैः श्रयिष्ये॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Let the royal umbrella, O Bharata, repulsing the rays of the sun, spread a cool shade over your head. I too shall gradually seek that dense shade of these forest trees. (18)

verses.text:
शत्रुघ्नस्त्वतुलमतिस्तु ते सहायः
सौमित्रिर्मम विदितः प्रधानमित्रम्।
चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं
सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषीद॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Let Śatrughna of peerless wisdom for his part be your assistant and the well-known Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, be my chief friend. Let us, his four worthy sons, enable the king to adhere to truth. Do not feel dejected.” (19)

verses.text:
आश्वासयन्तं भरतं जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः।
उवाच रामं धर्मज्ञं धर्मापेतमिदं वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: To Śrī Rāma, the knower of what is right, who was comforting Bharata, Jābāli, a jewel among Brāhmaṇas, addressed the following words contrary to the Vedic religion : (1)

verses.text:
साधु राघव मा भूत् ते बुद्धिरेवं निरर्थिका।
प्राकृतस्य नरस्येव ह्यार्यबुद्धेस्तपस्विनः॥ २॥
verses.m: “You have spoken aright, O scion of Raghu; but such a vain resolution, akin to that of an ordinary man, ought not to have been made by you, who are endowed with a noble understanding and given to austerities. (2)

verses.text:
कः कस्य पुरुषो बन्धुः किमाप्यं कस्य केनचित्।
एको हि जायते जन्तुरेक एव विनश्यति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “No man is the friend of anyone, nor is anything to be gained by anyone through anyone; for, alone is a creature born and alone does it perish. (3)

verses.text:
तस्मान्माता पिता चेति राम सज्जेत यो नरः।
उन्मत्त इव स ज्ञेयो नास्ति कश्चिद्धि कस्यचित्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, the man who feels attached to anyone believing that the latter is his mother or father, O Rāma, should be reckoned on a par with a madman; for none is related to another. (4)

verses.text:
यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन् नरः कश्चिद् बहिर्वसेत्।
उत्सृज्य च तमावासं प्रतिष्ठेतापरेऽहनि॥ ५॥
एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु।
आवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “As while journeying to another distant village a man stays abroad in the course of his journey and, leaving that resting place behind, proceeds further the next day, even so, to men a father, mother, home and wealth are only a temporary shelter, O Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha); the wise do not get attached to these. (5-6)

verses.text:
पित्र्यं राज्यं समुत्सृज्य स नार्हसि नरोत्तम।
आस्थातुं कापथं दुःखं विषमं बहुकण्टकम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Relinquishing the kingdom of Ayodhyā, inherited from your father, O jewel among men, you as such ought not to tread the wrong path, which is painful, rugged and bristling with thorns. (7)

verses.text:
समृद्धायामयोध्यायामात्मानमभिषेचय।
एकवेणीधरा हि त्वा नगरी सम्प्रतीक्षते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Get yourself consecrated on the throne of the prosperous Ayodhyā; for the city eagerly awaits your return like a widow who wears a single braid of hair as a sign of mourning and desolation. (8)

verses.text:
राजभोगाननुभवन् महार्हान् पार्थिवात्मज।
विहर त्वमयोध्यायां यथा शक्रस्त्रिविष्टपे॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Enjoying kingly delights of great value, O prince, sport you in Ayodhyā as Indra does in heaven. (9)

verses.text:
न ते कश्चिद् दशरथस्त्वं च तस्य च कश्चन।
अन्यो राजा त्वमन्यस्तु तस्मात् कुरु यदुच्यते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Daśaratha was none to you nor were you related in anyway to him. The king was not you, while you are not the king Daśaratha; therefore do what is recommended to you. (10)

verses.text:
बीजमात्रं पिता जन्तोः शुक्रं शोणितमेव च।
संयुक्तमृतुमन्मात्रा पुरुषस्येह जन्म तत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The father is only an efficient cause of a creature; it is only the sperm and the ovum conjointly retained by a prospective mother during the nights favourable for conception that constitute the material cause of a human being in this world. (11)

verses.text:
गतः स नृपतिस्तत्र गन्तव्यं यत्र तेन वै।
प्रवृत्तिरेषा भूतानां त्वं तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid king has departed to the destination where he was bound to go, viz., back to the five elements, from which he had sprung up. Such is the natural way of created beings, while you are being harassed for no purpose.” (12)

verses.text:
अर्थधर्मपरा ये ये तांस्तान् शोचामि नेतरान्।
ते हि दुःखमिह प्राप्य विनाशं प्रेत्य लेभिरे॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I bewail only those whosoever are devoted to wealth and religious merit, not others, who are devoted to sense-enjoyment alone; for having undergone suffering in this life for the sake of wealth and religious merit, they have met with extermination even after death. (13)

verses.text:
अष्टकापितृदेवत्यमित्ययं प्रसृतो जनः।
अन्नस्योपद्रवं पश्य मृतो हि किमशिष्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “People here have taken to Śrāddha and other allied rites under the belief that Aṣṭakā, (a Śrāddha performed on the seventh, eighth and ninth days of the dark fortnights of the lunar months of Pauṣa, Māgha and Phālguna respectively) and other Śrāddhas are calculated to gratify the manes. Look at the wanton waste of food involved in these rites; for what will a dead man eat? (14)

verses.text:
यदि भुक्तमिहान्येन देहमन्यस्य गच्छति।
दद्यात् प्रवसतां श्राद्धं न तत् पथ्यशनं भवेत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “If the food eaten by one man here reaches the body of another in the other world, one might as well offer Śrāddha to those travelling from home; no provisions for journey should be necessary for them. (15)

verses.text:
दानसंवनना ह्येते ग्रन्था मेधाविभिः कृताः।
यजस्व देहि दीक्षस्व तपस्तप्यस्व संत्यज॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Enjoining us to worship gods, make gifts, get ourselves consecrated for a sacrificial performance, practise austerities and renounce our hearth and home, these books have been written by talented men with a view to exalting charity. (16)

verses.text:
स नास्ति परमित्येतत् कुरु बुद्धिं महामते।
प्रत्यक्षं यत् तदातिष्ठ परोक्षं पृष्ठतः कुरु॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Having known this truth, O highly intelligent prince, arrive at the conclusion that there is nothing beyond this visible universe. Depend upon that which meets the eye; discard that which is outside the ken of your senses. (17)

verses.text:
सतां बुद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वलोकनिदर्शिनीम्।
राज्यं स त्वं निगृह्णीष्व भरतेन प्रसादितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Respecting the judgment of the wise who believe that alone which meets the eye to be true—which serves as an authority for all men and propitiated by Bharata, accept you the kingdom.” (18)

verses.text:
जाबालेस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
उवाच परया सूक्त्या बुद्ध्याविप्रतिपन्नया॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Jābāli, Śrī Rāma, for his part, who was possessed of unfailing prowess, replied as follows in the commendable phraseology of the Vedas, armed as he was with a conviction opposed to Jābāli’s point of view: (1)

verses.text:
भवान् मे प्रियकामार्थं वचनं यदिहोक्तवान्।
अकार्यं कार्यसंकाशमपथ्यं पथ्य संनिभम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “The advice that you have tendered on this occasion in order to make available to me the pleasures of sense, which are agreeable to all, is not really worth following, although appearing as such, and is unwholesome, though appearing as wholesome. (2)

verses.text:
निर्मर्यादस्तु पुरुषः पापाचारसमन्वितः।
मानं न लभते सत्सु भिन्नचारित्रदर्शनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “A man who has transgressed the bounds of propriety and is characterized by a sinful conduct, and who is wedded to a moral philosophy different from the established ethical doctrines does not get recognition among the wise. (3)

verses.text:
कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्।
चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Conduct alone proclaims a man to be well-born or otherwise, gallant or only fancying himself to be gallant, honest or dishonest. (4)

verses.text:
अनार्यस्त्वार्य संस्थानः शौचाद्धीनस्तथा शुचिः।
लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुःशीलः शीलवानिव॥ ५॥
verses.m: “One following the way of life propounded by you will be ignoble, though appearing as noble, will be accepted as clean, though devoid of cleanliness, would pass for one endowed with auspicious bodily marks, though lacking in such marks, will appear as possessed of an amiable disposition, though ill-mannered. (5)

verses.text:
अधर्मं धर्मवेषेण यद्यहं लोकसंकरम्।
अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियां विधिविवर्जिताम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “If I embrace unrighteousness, cloaked in the garb of piety and leading to confusion or mixture of castes, I should be giving up the virtuous acts and taking to unauthorized action. (6)

verses.text:
कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः।
बहु मन्येत मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “What sensible man capable of discerning what ought to be done and what ought not to be done would hold me in high esteem in the world, knowing me to be vile of conduct and a corrupter of the people? (7)

verses.text:
कस्य यास्याम्यहं वृत्तं केन वा स्वर्गमाप्नुयाम्।
अनया वर्तमानोऽहं वृत्त्या हीनप्रतिज्ञया॥ ८॥
कामवृत्तोऽन्वयं लोकः कृत्स्नः समुपवर्तते।
यद्वृत्ताः सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ताः सन्ति हि प्रजाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Conducting myself according to the mode of life recommended by you in which my vow of remaining in exile in woods for fourteen years has to be abandoned, whose way of life shall I follow as an ideal so that I may attain heaven, since you tell me my father was none to me? By following your advice, I will act according to my own inclination (disregarding the authority of the Śāstras) and, following my example, the whole of this world too is likely to turn licentious; for people follow the same way of life as kings do. (8-9)

verses.text:
सत्यमेवानृशंसं च राजवृत्तं सनातनम्।
तस्मात् सत्यात्मकं राज्यं सत्ये लोकः प्रतिष्ठितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Truthfulness alone, which is divorced from cruelty, is the eternal way of life prescribed for kings. Therefore, truthfulness is the soul of a kingdom; nay, the world itself is founded on truth. (10)

verses.text:
ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च सत्यमेव हि मेनिरे।
सत्यवादी हि लोकेऽस्मिन् परं गच्छति चाक्षयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The seers of Vedic Mantras as well as gods have respected truthfulness alone. Indeed, a veracious man in this world attains the highest realm, which knows no decay. (11)

verses.text:
उद्विजन्ते यथा सर्पान्नरादनृतवादिनः।
धर्मः सत्यपरो लोके मूलं सर्वस्य चोच्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “People turn away in fear from a man telling lies in the same way as they do from a serpent. Virtue has its culmination in truthfulness; nay, it is declared to be the root of all. (12)

verses.text:
सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्ये धर्मः सदाश्रितः।
सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Truth alone is God in the world, piety ever hinges on truth. All have their root in truth; there is no goal higher than truth. (13)

verses.text:
दत्तमिष्टं हुतं चैव तप्तानि च तपांसि च।
वेदाः सत्यप्रतिष्ठानास्तस्मात् सत्यपरो भवेत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Charity, sacrificial performances, as well as offering oblations into the sacred fire, nay, austerities actually practised and the Vedas studied have their foundation on truth. Hence one should remain devoted to truth. (14)

verses.text:
एकः पालयते लोकमेकः पालयते कुलम्।
मज्जत्येको हि निरय एकः स्वर्गे महीयते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “According to the degree of virtue and sin practised in one’s past lives one rules over the world,another simply supports one’s race alone; a third actually sinks into hell, and yet another is respected in heaven.(15)

verses.text:
सोऽहं पितुर्निदेशं तु किमर्थं नानुपालये।
सत्यप्रतिश्रवः सत्यं सत्येन समयीकृतम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Wherefore, then, shall I, who know all this, not carry out the behest of my father, which was based on truth and solemnized through swearing by truth, true to my promise as I am? (16)

verses.text:
नैव लोभान्न मोहाद् वा न चाज्ञानात् तमोऽन्वितः।
सेतुं सत्यस्य भेत्स्यामि गुरोः सत्यप्रतिश्रवः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Neither from greed of sovereignty nor even from infatuation nor again from ignorance shall I, overpowered by obtuseness of understanding, violate the sanctity of my father’s pledge given to mother, Kaikeyī, true to my promise as I am. (17)

verses.text:
असत्यसंधस्य सतश्चलस्यास्थिरचेतसः।
नैव देवा न पितरः प्रतीच्छन्तीति नः श्रुतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “It has been heard by us that neither gods nor even manes accept the offerings of a man who is not true to his promise, and has thus deviated from truth and is of irresolute mind. (18)

verses.text:
प्रत्यगात्ममिमं धर्मं सत्यं पश्याम्यहं ध्रुवम्।
भारः सत्पुरुषैश्चीर्णस्तदर्थमभिनन्द्यते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I recognize this virtue in the form of truthfulness as binding on all embodied beings and foremost. The burden in the form of matted locks has been made much of by good men; hence it is welcomed by me. (19)

verses.text:
क्षात्रं धर्ममहं त्यक्ष्ये ह्यधर्मं धर्मसंहितम्।
क्षुद्रैर्नृशंसैर्लुब्धैश्च सेवितं पापकर्मभिः॥ २०॥
