verses.m: “I shall certainly renounce the duty of a Kṣatriya (in the shape of assuming the rulership of Ayodhyā in violation of my father’s injunction) which consists mostly of unrighteousness, though seemingly attended with an iota of virtue and which is followed generally by petty, cruel and greedy men of sinful deeds. (20)

verses.text:
कायेन कुरुते पापं मनसा सम्प्रधार्य तत्।
अनृतं जिह्वया चाह त्रिविधं कर्म पातकम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Having first resolved upon a sinful deed with the mind, a man speaks of his vile intention to his friends and associates with his tongue and then perpetrates it with his body with the help of others. In this way a sinful deed is accomplished in three ways, viz., by thought, word and deed. (21)

verses.text:
भूमिः कीर्तिर्यशो लक्ष्मीः पुरुषं प्रार्थयन्ति हि।
सत्यं समनुवर्तन्ते सत्यमेव भजेत् ततः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Land, renown, glory and fortune undoubtedly woo a man devoted to truth. The wise pursue truth, hence one should worship truth alone. (22)

verses.text:
श्रेष्ठं ह्यनार्यमेव स्याद् यद् भवानवधार्य माम्।
आह युक्तिकरैर्वाक्यैरिदं भद्रं कुरुष्व ह॥ २३॥
verses.m: “What you have recommended to me after concluding it to be the best for me in so many logical words, viz., ‘this sovereignty is good for you, unhesitatingly accept it,’ must be unquestionably improper for me. (23)

verses.text:
कथं ह्यहं प्रतिज्ञाय वनवासमिमं गुरोः।
भरतस्य करिष्यामि वचो हित्वा गुरोर्वचः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Having actually given my word of honour to my father to remain in exile in the woods for fourteen years, as I am doing, how shall I comply with the prayer of Bharata, flouting the command of my father? (24)

verses.text:
स्थिरा मया प्रतिज्ञाता प्रतिज्ञा गुरुसंनिधौ।
प्रहृष्टमानसा देवी कैकेयी चाभवत् तदा॥ २५॥
verses.m: “A firm vow was taken by me in the presence of my father and Queen Kaikeyī felt highly delighted at heart to hear it at that moment. How can I now go back upon my word of honour and cause sorrow to her?(25)

verses.text:
वनवासं वसन्नेव शुचिर्नियतभोजनः।
मूलपुष्पफलैः पुण्यैः पितॄन् देवांश्च तर्पयन्॥ २६॥
संतुष्टपञ्चवर्गोऽहं लोकयात्रां प्रवाहये।
अकुहः श्रद्दधानः सन् कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Having controlled my diet and propitiating gods as well as manes by means of sacred roots, flowers and fruits while continuing to reside in the forest only and remaining pure of body and mind, with all the five senses fully sated, nay, free from all viles, devout and fully cognizant of what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, I propose to discharge my worldly obligations in the form of carrying out the behest of my father. (26-27)

verses.text:
कर्मभूमिमिमां प्राप्य कर्तव्यं कर्म यच्छुभम्।
अग्निर्वायुश्च सोमश्च कर्मणां फलभागिनः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Having reached this terrestrial globe (the realm of action), virtuous action alone should be undertaken. The god of fire as well as the wind-god and the moon-god enjoy, in their respective realms, the fruit of their meritorious action. (28)

verses.text:
शतं क्रतूनामाहृत्य देवराट् त्रिदिवं गतः।
तपांस्युग्राणि चास्थाय दिवं प्राप्ता महर्षयः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Indra, the ruler of gods, was able to attain the sovereignty of heaven only after performing a hundred sacrifices. The eminent seers of Vedic Mantras too ascended to the ethereal regions (the realms even higher than heaven) after practising rigorous austerities only.” (29)

verses.text:
अमृष्यमाणः पुनरुग्रतेजा
निशम्य तन्नास्तिकवाक्यहेतुम्।
अथाब्रवीत् तं नृपतेस्तनूजो
विगर्हमाणो वचनानि तस्य॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Hearing the plea put forward by the aforesaid sage, Jābāli, in the form of a heretic utterance (denying the life beyond death) and resenting, nay, censuring his words, Śrī Rāma, son of King Daśaratha, who was endowed with a formidable spirit, forthwith spoke to him once again as follows : (30)

verses.text:
सत्यं च धर्मं च पराक्रमं च
भूतानुकम्पां प्रियवादितां च।
द्विजातिदेवातिथिपूजनं च
पन्थानमाहुस्त्रिदिवस्य सन्तः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The sages speak of truthfulness and piety and valour and compassion for created beings and polite speech and worship of Brāhmaṇas, gods and unexpected guests as a road to heaven. (31)

verses.text:
तेनैवमाज्ञाय यथावदर्थ-
मेकोदयं सम्प्रतिपद्य विप्राः।
धर्मं चरन्तः सकलं यथावत्
कांक्षन्ति लोकागममप्रमत्ताः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Scrupulously and duly practising virtue in all its aspects, having in the first instance correctly understood its meaning through the aforesaid utterance of sages and reached complete unanimity on the point, Brāhmaṇas seek to attain realms of their choice. (32)

verses.text:
निन्दाम्यहं कर्म कृतं पितुस्तद्
यस्त्वामगृह्णाद् विषमस्थबुद्धिम्।
बुद्ध्यानयैवंविधया चरन्तं
सुनास्तिकं धर्मपथादपेतम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “I denounce the action mentioned below, of my father, who picked up as his counsellor-priest you, a staunch unbeliever, who has not only strayed away from the path of righteousness but whose mind is set on a wrong path opposed to the Vedic path, nay, who is moving about in the world with such an ideology conforming to the doctrine of the atheistic Cārvāka, who believes only in the world of senses, as has been set forth in your foregoing speech. (33)

verses.text:
यथा हि चोरः स तथा हि बुद्ध-
स्तथागतं नास्तिकमत्र विद्धि।
तस्माद्धि यः शक्यतमः प्रजानां
स नास्तिके नाभिमुखो बुधः स्यात्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “It is a well-known fact that a follower of Buddha condemning the Vedas deserves to be punished precisely in the same way as a thief inasmuch as a heretic robs people of their faith; and know an unbeliever (a follower of the Cārvāka or materialistic school of philosophy) to be on a par with a Bauddha. Therefore, among such unbelievers he who is most tameable should undoubtedly be so punished in the interest of the people; in no other case should a wise man even stand face to face with an unbeliever, but should shun him. (34)

verses.text:
त्वत्तो जनाः पूर्वतरे द्विजाश्च
शुभानि कर्माणि बहूनि चक्रुः।
छित्त्वा सदेमं च परं च लोकं
तस्माद् द्विजाः स्वस्ति कृतं हुतं च॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Men that lived before you, as well as Brāhmaṇas ever performed numerous blessed deeds in obedience to the injunctions of the Vedas giving up all hopes of reward in this world as well as in the next. Hence following the injunctions of the Vedas, Brāhmaṇas pursue harmlessness, truthfulness and other virtues, perform noble deeds such as practice of austerities, making gifts, doing a good turn to others and so on and offer oblations into the sacred fire. (35)

verses.text:
धर्मे रताः सत्पुरुषैः समेता-
स्तेजस्विनो दानगुणप्रधानाः।
अहिंसका वीतमलाश्च लोके
भवन्ति पूज्या मुनयः प्रधानाः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Foremost sages, like Vasiṣṭha, who are devoted to righteousness, remain in communion with good men, are endowed with spiritual glory, have the virtue of munificence predominant in them, practise harmlessness and are entirely free from impurity of all kinds become worthy of adoration in the world.” (36)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवन्तं वचनं सरोषं
रामं महात्मानमदीनसत्त्वम्।
उवाच पथ्यं पुनरास्तिकं च
सत्यं वचः सानुनयं च विप्रः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: To the high-souled Śrī Rāma, who never felt dejected at heart and was speaking angrily as above, the Brāhmaṇa Jābāli now politely addressed the following wholesome and truthful words, which showed his belief in the authority of the Vedas, the otherworld and so on: (37)

verses.text:
न नास्तिकानां वचनं ब्रवीम्यहं
न नास्तिकोऽहं न च नास्ति किंचन।
समीक्ष्य कालं पुनरास्तिकोऽभवं
भवेय काले पुनरेव नास्तिकः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “I do not as a rule repeat the words of unbelievers nor am I an unbeliever at heart nor is it a fact that nothing exists beyond this visible universe. Perceiving the time opportune for it, now that I find you bent on implementing the pledge given to your father, I have become a believer once more and to suit the exigencies of the moment, may again pose as an unbeliever when the time comes for it. (38)

verses.text:
स चापि कालोऽयमुपागतः शनै-
र्यथा मया नास्तिकवागुदीरिता।
निवर्तनार्थं तव राम कारणात्
प्रसादनार्थं च मयैतदीरितम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “That time too had now come when a heretical speech was slowly made by me in order to deflect you from your purpose of remaining in exile in the forest and also from another motive viz., to establish your reputation as a great believer by evoking your opposition to the heretical view. Again, in order to pacify you when I found you angry has this revised utterance been made by me, O Rāma !” (39)

verses.text:
क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय रामं तु वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह।
जाबालिरपि जानीते लोकस्यास्य गतागतिम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving Śrī Rāma to be angry, Vasiṣṭha too pleaded with him (for Jābāli) as follows: “Jābāli also recognizes the departure of the human soul from this world and its return to the mortal plane. (1)

verses.text:
निवर्तयितुकामस्तु त्वामेतद् वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
इमां लोकसमुत्पत्तिं लोकनाथ निबोध मे॥ २॥
verses.m: He, however, spoke to you as aforesaid desirous as he was of persuading you to return to Ayodhyā. Pray, hear from me about the creation of worlds, O protector of the world ! (2)

verses.text:
सर्वं सलिलमेवासीत् पृथिवी तत्र निर्मिता।
ततः समभवद् ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्दैवतैः सह॥ ३॥
verses.m: “There was water alone in the beginning of creation, the earth was evolved in water. Next appeared the self-born Brahmā alongwith gods. (3)

verses.text:
स वराहस्ततो भूत्वा प्रोज्जहार वसुंधराम्।
असृजच्च जगत् सर्वं सह पुत्रैः कृतात्मभिः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Appearing as the Divine Boar, Brahmā, who is the same as Viṣṇu, the Protector, then lifted the earth out of the water into which it had disappeared and in conjunction with his sons (Marīci and others), who had subdued their mind, evolved the whole universe. (4)

verses.text:
आकाशप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्ययः।
तस्मान्मरीचिः संजज्ञे मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The eternal, everlasting and imperishable Brahmā sprang out of ether, which is no other than Brahma, the Absolute, from him came forth Marīci, and Kaśyapa was the son of Marīchi. (5)

verses.text:
विवस्वान् कश्यपाज्जज्ञे मनुर्वैवस्वतः स्वयम्।
स तु प्रजापतिः पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुस्तु मनोः सुतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Vivaswān, the sun-god, descended from Kaśyapa. Manu himself was the son of Vivaswān. Manu for his part was formerly a lord of creation, and Manu’s son was Ikṣwāku. (6)

verses.text:
यस्येयं प्रथमं दत्ता समृद्धा मनुना मही।
तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Know that Ikṣwāku to be the very first ruler of Ayodhyā, to whom this prosperous earth was entrusted for the first time by the said Manu. (7)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुतः श्रीमान् कुक्षिरित्येव विश्रुतः।
कुक्षेरथात्मजो वीरो विकुक्षिरुदपद्यत॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Ikṣwāku’s glorious son for his part became known simply by the name of Kukṣi; and from the loins of Kukṣi, O prince, sprang up gallant Vikukṣi. (8)

verses.text:
विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजाः बाणः पुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
बाणस्य च महाबाहुरनरण्यो महातपाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Vikukṣi’s son, on the other hand, was the mighty Bāṇa, who was endowed with exceptional glory; and Bāṇa’s son was the mighty-armed Anaraṇya, who practised great austerities. (9)

verses.text:
नानावृष्टिर्बभूवास्मिन् न दुर्भिक्षः सतां वरे।
अनरण्ये महाराजे तस्करो वापि कश्चन॥ १०॥
verses.m: “So long as this Anaraṇya, who was a jewel among the virtuous, continued to be the Emperor, there was neither a drought nor famine nor was a thief to be seen in Ayodhyā. (10)

verses.text:
अनरण्यान्महाराज पृथू राजा बभूव ह।
तस्मात् पृथोर्महातेजास्त्रिशङ्कुरुदपद्यत॥ ११॥
verses.m: “From the loins of Anaraṇya, O great king, they say, appeared King Pṛthu; from the said Pṛthu was descended Triśaṅku, who was possessed of great splendour. (11)

verses.text:
स सत्यवचनाद् वीरः सशरीरो दिवं गतः।
त्रिशङ्कोरभवत् सूनुर्धुन्धुमारो महायशाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Due to the unfailing vow of Viśwāmitra the aforesaid hero bodily ascended to heaven. Triśaṅku’s son was the highly illustrious Dhundhumāra. (12)

verses.text:
धुन्धुमारान्महातेजा युवनाश्वो व्यजायत।
युवनाश्वसुतः श्रीमान् मान्धाता समपद्यत॥ १३॥
verses.m: “From the loins of Dhundhumāra sprang up Yuvanāśwa, who was endowed with exceptional glory; the glorious Māndhātā was born as the son of Yuvanāśwa. (13)

verses.text:
मान्धातुस्तु महातेजाः सुसंधिरुदपद्यत।
सुसंधेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसंधिः प्रसेनजित्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Of Māndhātā, again, was born the highly glorious Susandhi; of Susandhi too there were two sons, Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit. (14)

verses.text:
यशस्वी ध्रुवसंधेस्तु भरतो रिपुसूदनः।
भरतात् तु महाबाहोरसितो नाम जायत॥ १५॥
यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रवः।
हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च शूराश्च शशबिन्दवः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Bharata, for his part, a destroyer of foes, was the illustrious son of Dhruvasandhi; and of the mighty-armed Bharata was born one Asita by name, of whom the following tributary chiefs, viz., the rulers of the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas and the gallant ruler of the Śaśabindus, came to be the enemies. (15-16)

verses.text:
तांस्तु सर्वान् प्रतिव्यूह्य युद्धे राजा प्रवासितः।
स च शैलवरे रम्ये बभूवाभिरतो मुनिः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “In spite of his having arrayed his army against all these, the king was routed and exiled. He, therefore, gladly took up his abode as an ascetic on a delightful and excellent mountain. (17)

verses.text:
द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुतिः।
तत्र चैका महाभागा भार्गवं देववर्चसम्॥ १८॥
ववन्दे पद्मपत्राक्षी कांक्षिणी पुत्रमुत्तमम्।
एका गर्भविनाशाय सपत्न्यै गरलं ददौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: “In course of time his two consorts came to be in the family way: so the tradition goes. Desiring to have an excellent son, one of them, who was highly fortunate and had eyes resembling the petals of a lotus, sought the presence of and bowed down to Sage Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu, who possessed the splendour of gods; while the other administered poison to her co-wife in order to destroy her foetus. (18-19)

verses.text:
भार्गवश्च्यवनो नाम हिमवन्तमुपाश्रितः।
तमृषिं साभ्युपागम्य कालिन्दी त्वभ्यवादयत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The sage named Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu, had betaken himself to the Himālayas. Approaching that sage, the said Kālindī for her part greeted him. (20)

verses.text:
स तामभ्यवदत् प्रीतो वरेप्सुं पुत्रजन्मनि।
पुत्रस्ते भविता देवि महात्मा लोकविश्रुतः॥ २१॥
धार्मिकश्च सुभीमश्च वंशकर्तारिसूदनः।
श्रुत्वा प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा मुनिं तमनुमान्य च॥ २२॥
पद्मपत्रसमानाक्षं पद्मगर्भसमप्रभम्।
ततः सा गृहमागम्य पत्नी पुत्रमजायत॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Gratified to receive her respects, he said to the queen, who sought from him a boon ensuring the birth of a son to her, ‘A lofty minded son, widely known in the world, pious and most formidable, the founder of a dynasty and the destroyer of his foes, will be born to you, O queen !’ Hearing this benediction, and going round the sage clockwise as a mark of respect and taking leave of him, and then returning home, the queen brought forth a son who had lotus-like eyes and shone like Brahmā, the lotus-born. (21—23)

verses.text:
सपत्न्या तु गरस्तस्यै दत्तो गर्भजिघांसया।
गरेण सह तेनैव तस्मात् स सगरोऽभवत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The boy was born alongwith that very poison that had actually been administered to the queen by her fellow-consort with the intention of destroying the foetus; hence he became known as Sagara (lit., with poison). (24)

verses.text:
स राजा सगरो नाम यः समुद्रमखानयत्।
इष्ट्वा पर्वणि वेगेन त्रासयान इमाः प्रजाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “King Sagara was he who, getting consecrated for a sacrifice on a full-moon day or new moon day, caused the ocean to be dug by his sons, sixteen thousand in number, causing fear to the people here by the speed of digging. (25)

verses.text:
असमञ्जस्तु पुत्रोऽभूत् सगरस्येति नः श्रुतम्।
जीवन्नेव स पित्रा तु निरस्तः पापकर्मकृत्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “It has been heard by us that Sagara’s eldest son, really speaking, was Asamañja. A perpetrator of sinful deeds as he was, he, however, was abandoned by his father, even when alive. (26)

verses.text:
अंशुमानपि पुत्रोऽभूदसमञ्जस्य वीर्यवान्।
दिलीपोंऽशुमतः पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Aṁśumān, again, who was full of valour, was the son of Asamañja. Dilīpa was the son of Aṁśumān and Bhagīratha, of Dilīpa. (27)

verses.text:
भगीरथात् ककुत्स्थश्च काकुत्स्था येन तु स्मृताः।
ककुत्स्थस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूद् रघुर्येन तु राघवाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Again, from the loins of Bhagīratha appeared Kakutstha, after whose name his descendants came to be called, Kākutsthas, the scions of Kakutstha. And Kakutstha’s son was Raghu, after whom his descendants were known as Rāghavas, the scions of Raghu. (28)

verses.text:
रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्धः पुरुषादकः।
कल्माषपादः सौदास इत्येवं प्रथितो भुवि॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Raghu’s glorious son for his part came to be known on earth by the names of Pravṛddha, Puruṣādaka (lit., a man-eater or ogre), Kalmāṣapāda and Saudāsa. (29)

verses.text:
कल्माषपादपुत्रोऽभूच्छङ्खणस्त्विति नः श्रुतम्।
यस्तु तद्वीर्यमासाद्य सहसैन्यो व्यनीनशत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “It has been heard by us that Kalmāṣapāda’s son was Śaṅkhaṇa, who, even on attaining remarkable valour on the field of battle, perished, army and all, in an encounter.” (30)

verses.text:
शङ्खणस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूच्छूरः श्रीमान् सुदर्शनः।
सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्ण अग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The glorious Sudarśana for his part was the heroic son of Śaṅkhaṇa. Agnivarṇa was the son of Sudarśana and Śīghraga, of Agnivarṇa. (31)

verses.text:
शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुवः।
प्रशुश्रुवस्य पुत्रोऽभूदम्बरीषो महामतिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Maru was the son of Śīghraga and Maru’s son was Praśuśruva. The highly intelligent Ambarīṣa was the son of Praśuśruva. (32)

verses.text:
अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोऽभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः।
नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Nahuṣa of unfailing prowess was the son of Ambarīṣa, while Nābhāga was the supremely pious son of Nahuṣa. (33)

verses.text:
अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ।
अजस्य चैव धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथः सुतः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Both Aja and Suvrata were the sons of Nābhāga and the pious King Daśaratha was the son of Aja. (34)

verses.text:
तस्य ज्येष्ठोऽसि दायादो राम इत्यभिविश्रुतः।
तद् गृहाण स्वकं राज्यमवेक्षस्व जगन्नृप॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “You are his eldest son known all round by the name of Rāma; therefore, accept this kingdom of your own and look after the world, O protector of men ! (35)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकूणां हि सर्वेषां राजा भवति पूर्वजः।
पूर्वजे नावरः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो राजाभिषिच्यते॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Among all the Ikṣwākus the eldest son undoubtedly becomes the ruler. While an elder son is present, a younger son is never consecrated as a king. The eldest alone is so consecrated. (36)

verses.text:
स राघवाणां कुलधर्ममात्मनः
सनातनं नाद्य विहन्तुमर्हसि।
प्रभूतरत्नामनुशाधि मेदिनीं
प्रभूतराष्ट्रां पितृवन्महायशः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Being one of the Rāghavas, you as such ought not to violate today the time-honoured usage of Your House according to which the throne goes to the eldest son alone. Like your father, highly illustrious as You are, rule the earth abounding in precious stones and consisting of numerous dominions.” (37)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठः स तदा राममुक्त्वा राजपुरोहितः।
अब्रवीद् धर्मसंयुक्तं पुनरेवापरं वचः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having spoken to Śrī Rāma as aforesaid on that occasion, the said Vasiṣṭha, the family-priest of the king, addressed to him once more the following words in consonance with righteousness : (1)

verses.text:
पुरुषस्येह जातस्य भवन्ति गुरवः सदा।
आचार्यश्चैव काकुत्स्थ पिता माता च राघव॥ २॥
verses.m: “The preceptor, O scion of Kakutstha, as well as one’s father and mother, O descendant of Raghu, ever come to be the adored of a man from the time he is born in this world. (2)

verses.text:
पिता ह्येनं जनयति पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
प्रज्ञां ददाति चाचार्यस्तस्मात् स गुरुरुच्यते॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The father only procreates and the mother brings forth a human being, O jewel among men; the preceptor, on the other hand, bestows wisdom on him, hence he is spoken of as Guru (superior even to the parents). (3)

verses.text:
स तेऽहं पितुराचार्यस्तव चैव परंतप।
मम त्वं वचनं कुर्वन् नातिवर्तेः सतां गतिम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I, for my part, am the preceptor not only of your father but yours too, O chastiser of foes ! Doing my bidding, therefore, you will not be transgressing the path of the virtuous. (4)

verses.text:
इमा हि ते परिषदो ज्ञातयश्च नृपास्तथा।
एषु तात चरन् धर्मं नातिवर्तेः सतां गतिम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Here indeed are your subjects, kinsmen and tributary princes too. Discharging your duty by them, you will not be transgressing the path of the virtuous. (5)

verses.text:
वृद्धाया धर्मशीलाया मातुर्नार्हस्यवर्तितुम्।
अस्या हि वचनं कुर्वन् नातिवर्तेः सतां गतिम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “You ought not to fail in your duty towards your aged mother, who is given to piety. Doing her bidding you will certainly not be transgressing the path of the virtuous. (6)

verses.text:
भरतस्य वचः कुर्वन् याचमानस्य राघव।
आत्मानं नातिवर्तेस्त्वं सत्यधर्मपराक्रम॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Granting the prayer of Bharata, who is supplicating you, you will not be overstepping your bounds, O scion of Raghu, who are ever united with truthfulness, piety and valour !” (7)

verses.text:
एवं मधुरमुक्तः स गुरुणा राघवः स्वयम्।
प्रत्युवाच समासीनं वसिष्ठं पुरुषर्षभः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Instructed thus in sweet words by his preceptor himself, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), a jewel among men, replied as follows to Vasiṣṭha, who was sitting at ease there : (8)

verses.text:
यन्मातापितरौ वृत्तं तनये कुरुतः सदा।
न सुप्रतिकरं तत् तु मात्रा पित्रा च यत्कृतम्॥ ९॥
यथाशक्तिप्रदानेन स्वापनोच्छादनेन च।
नित्यं च प्रियवादेन तथा संवर्धनेन च॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The service that the parents render to their son by giving him whatever they can, as well as by putting him to bed and rubbing his body with oil etc., nay, by speaking kindly to him every moment and, even so, by nourishing him, nay, whatever good is done by them cannot be easily requited. (9-10)

verses.text:
स हि राजा दशरथः पिता जनयिता मम।
आज्ञापयन्मां यत् तस्य न तन्मिथ्या भविष्यति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Indeed that which the celebrated King Daśaratha, my father, who brought me into being, has asked me to do shall not prove untrue.” (11)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण भरतः प्रत्यनन्तरम्।
उवाच विपुलोरस्कः सूतं परमदुर्मनाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: When Śrī Rāma had spoken thus, Bharata for his part, who was distinguished by a broad chest, and felt extremely sad at heart, commanded as follows Sumantra, the charioteer, who stood nearest to him : (12)

verses.text:
इह तु स्थण्डिले शीघ्रं कुशानास्तर सारथे।
आर्यं प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यामि यावन्मे सम्प्रसीदति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Speedily spread for your part blades of Kuśa grass on this piece of level ground, O charioteer ! I shall sit at the door of my elder brother in order to exert pressure on him until he gets fully propitiated and grants my request. (13)

verses.text:
निराहारो निरालोको धनहीनो यथा द्विजः।
शये पुरस्ताच्छालायां यावन्मां प्रतियास्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Like a destitute Brāhmaṇa, who has been deprived of his fortune by a debtor, failing to repay the debt as stipulated, I shall remain lying down in front of Śrī Rāma’s hut without food or drink and depriving myself of light by covering my face until he returns to Ayodhyā as a concession to me.” (14)

verses.text:
स तु राममवेक्षन्तं सुमन्त्रं प्रेक्ष्य दुर्मनाः।
कुशोत्तरमुपस्थाप्य भूमावेवास्थितः स्वयम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Perceiving Sumantra awaiting the pleasure of Śrī Rāma, Bharata for his part sat down disconsolate on the ground, spreading a mat of Kuśa grass with his own hands. (15)

verses.text:
तमुवाच महातेजा रामो राजर्षिसत्तमः।
किं मां भरत कुर्वाणं तात प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यसे॥ १६॥
verses.m: To him the highly glorious Śrī Rāma, the foremost of royal sages, said, “What wrong have I done to you, O Bharata, that you will sit at my door to exert pressure on me, my darling? (16)

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणो ह्येकपार्श्वेन नरान् रोद्धुमिहार्हति।
न तु मूर्धाभिषिक्तानां विधिः प्रत्युपवेशने॥ १७॥
verses.m: “A Brāhmaṇa alone ought to restrain people oppressing him by lying on one side at their door. Kṣatriyas, however, who are or deserve to be sprinkled with holy water on the head (when being installed as the head of a state) are not enjoined to sit at the door of anyone in this way. (17)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल हित्वैतद् दारुणं व्रतम्।
पुरवर्यामितः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां याहि राघव॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Get up, O tiger among men ! Giving up this terrible vow, return, O scion of Raghu, speedily to Ayodhyā, the foremost of cities, from this place.” (18)

verses.text:
आसीनस्त्वेव भरतः पौरजानपदं जनम्।
उवाच सर्वतः प्रेक्ष्य किमार्यं नानुशासथ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Gazing on all sides, Bharata, even while sitting, said to the citizens as well as to the people of the countryside, “Wherefore do you not plead with my elder brother?” (19)

verses.text:
ते तदोचुर्महात्मानं पौरजानपदा जनाः।
काकुत्स्थमभिजानीमः सम्यग् वदति राघवः॥ २०॥
verses.m: The people of the city as well as of the countryside then replied as follows to Bharata, an exalted soul : “We know full well that you, a scion of Raghu, speak aright to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha. (20)

verses.text:
एषोऽपि हि महाभागः पितुर्वचसि तिष्ठति।
अत एव न शक्ताः स्मो व्यावर्तयितुमञ्जसा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “This highly blessed prince, Śrī Rāma, too sincerely abides by the command of his father. For this very reason we are, truly speaking, not easily able to divert him from his purpose.” (21)

verses.text:
तेषामाज्ञाय वचनं रामो वचनमब्रवीत्।
एवं निबोध वचनं सुहृदां धर्मचक्षुषाम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing their submission Śrī Rāma addressed the following words to Bharata : “Listen to the foregoing words of our friends, who have their eyes fixed on what is right. (22)

verses.text:
एतच्चैवोभयं श्रुत्वा सम्यक् सम्पश्य राघव।
उत्तिष्ठ त्वं महाबाहो मां च स्पृश तथोदकम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Nay, hearing both these utterances (mine as well as that of these people) weigh them fully, O scion of Raghu. Get you up, O mighty-armed prince, and touch water in order to sip it as well as myself as an indication of your resolve to break the vow that you have just taken.” (23)

verses.text:
अथोत्थाय जलं स्पृष्ट्वा भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
शृण्वन्तु मे परिषदो मन्त्रिणः शृणुयुस्तथा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Getting up immediately and touching water, Bharata spoke as follows : “Let all the members of this assembly hear me. Let the king’s counsellors too listen. (24)

verses.text:
न याचे पितरं राज्यं नानुशासामि मातरम्।
एवं परमधर्मज्ञं नानुजानामि राघवम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “I never begged sovereignty of my father nor did I instruct my mother to do it on my behalf. Nor did I approve of this step of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), viz., that he should go into exile for fourteen years, he knows best what is right. (25)

verses.text:
यदि त्ववश्यं वस्तव्यं कर्तव्यं च पितुर्वचः।
अहमेव निवत्स्यामि चतुर्दश वने समाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “If the behest of our father must be carried out and if one must live in the forest at all events, I myself shall do so for a period of fourteen years.” (26)

verses.text:
धर्मात्मा तस्य सत्येन भ्रातुर्वाक्येन विस्मितः।
उवाच रामः सम्प्रेक्ष्य पौरजानपदं जनम्॥ २७॥
विक्रीतमाहितं क्रीतं यत् पित्रा जीवता मम।
न तल्लोपयितुं शक्यं मया वा भरतेन वा॥ २८॥
verses.m: Fixing his gaze on the citizens of Ayodhyā as well as on the people of the countryside, Śrī Rāma, whose mind is set on righteousness and who felt astonished at the sincere vow of his aforesaid brother, said “The sale, deposit or purchase effected by our father while alive cannot be nullified either by me or even by Bharata. (27-28)

verses.text:
उपाधिर्न मया कार्यो वनवासे जुगुप्सितः।
युक्तमुक्तं च कैकेय्या पित्रा मे सुकृतं कृतम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “No proxy should be sent by me into exile in the woods; for that would be a matter for reproach, since a proxy is allowed only in case the man replaced by him is unable to discharge the obligation imposed on him. The demand of Kaikeyī was but reasonable inasmuch as it was based firstly on the stipulation made by the king while marrying Kaikeyī that a son born to her alone would succeed him on the throne, and secondly on the debt the former owed to her for the invaluable service rendered by her on the field of battle; and only a virtuous act was done by our father in granting the boons asked by her. (29)

verses.text:
जानामि भरतं क्षान्तं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्।
सर्वमेवात्र कल्याणं सत्यसंधे महात्मनि॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “I know Bharata to be forgiving by nature and fond of paying respects to his elders. Indeed, all will be well with this high-souled prince, who is true to his promise. (30)

verses.text:
अनेन धर्मशीलेन वनात् प्रत्यागतः पुनः।
भ्रात्रा सह भविष्यामि पृथिव्याः पतिरुत्तमः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “When returned from the forest I shall indeed become the paramount ruler of the earth with this pious brother of mine. (31)

verses.text:
वृतो राजा हि कैकेय्या मया तद्वचनं कृतम्।
अनृतान्मोचयानेन पितरं तं महीपतिम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “As the king was solicited for a boon by Kaikeyī, his pledge given to her has been implemented by me by being in exile in the forest. Now, acquit the said king, our father, of the charge of falsehood by ruling over Ayodhyā and thereby discharging your part of the obligation.” (32)

verses.text:
तमप्रतिमतेजोभ्यां भ्रातृभ्यां रोमहर्षणम्।
विस्मिताः संगमं प्रेक्ष्य समुपेता महर्षयः॥ १॥
verses.m: The eminent sages who had assembled there were astonished to behold at close quarters that thrilling meeting of the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Bharata, who were endowed with matchless glory. (1)

verses.text:
अन्तर्हिता मुनिगणाः स्थिताश्च परमर्षयः।
तौ भ्रातरौ महाभागौ काकुत्स्थौ प्रशशंसिरे॥ २॥
verses.m: Hosts of sages who stood invisible in the air and most eminent Ṛṣis bodily present there applauded in the following words those two highly blessed brothers, Śrī Rāma and Bharata, the scions of Kakutstha : (2)

verses.text:
सदार्यौ राजपुत्रौ द्वौ धर्मज्ञौ धर्मविक्रमौ।
श्रुत्वा वयं हि सम्भाषामुभयोः स्पृहयामहे॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Ever noble are the two princes, Śrī Rāma and Bharata, who not only know what is right but also tread the path of virtue. Indeed, having heard the dialogue of the two, we long to hear it again and again.” (3)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वृषिगणाः क्षिप्रं दशग्रीववधैषिणः।
भरतं राजशार्दूलमित्यूचुः संगता वचः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Then the hosts of Ṛṣis for their part, who longed for the death of Rāvaṇa, hastily addressed with one voice the following exhortation to Bharata, a tiger among princes : (4)

verses.text:
कुले जात महाप्राज्ञ महावृत्त महायशः।
ग्राह्यं रामस्य वाक्यं ते पितरं यद्यवेक्षसे॥ ५॥
verses.m: “O prince of high birth, nay, endowed with exceptional intelligence, distinguished by a noble conduct and enjoying great renown, the advice of Śrī Rāma ought to be accepted by you, if you have the least regard for your father. (5)

verses.text:
सदानृणमिमं रामं वयमिच्छामहे पितुः।
अनृणत्वाच्च कैकेय्याः स्वर्गं दशरथो गतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “We wish to see Śrī Rāma absolved forever from all obligations to his father; for due to his getting square with Kaikeyī as a result of Śrī Rāma’s having readily offered to be in exile, King Daśaratha has ascended to heaven.” (6)

verses.text:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं गन्धर्वाः समहर्षयः।
राजर्षयश्चैव तथा सर्वे स्वां स्वां गतिं गताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Having uttered these few words, the Gandharvas alongwith the eminent sages as well as the royal sages and all others went each his own way. (7)

verses.text:
ह्लादितस्तेन वाक्येन शुशुभे शुभदर्शनः।
रामः संहृष्टवदनस्तानृषीनभ्यपूजयत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Gladdened by this observation, Śrī Rāma of blessed appearance looked brighter. Nay, his face thrilled with joy, he duly extolled the aforesaid Ṛṣis. (8)

verses.text:
त्रस्तगात्रस्तु भरतः स वाचा सज्जमानया।
कृताञ्जलिरिदं वाक्यं राघवं पुनरब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: The celebrated Bharata for his part, whose limbs were seized with a tremor, made the following submission to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) with folded hands in faltering accents : (9)

verses.text:
राम धर्ममिमं प्रेक्ष्य कुलधर्मानुसंततम्।
कर्तुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ मम मातुश्च याचनाम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Fully considering, O Rāma, this sacred obligation of getting yourself consecrated for the rulership of Ayodhyā and protecting the people, which is also linked with our family usage, you ought to fulfil it, O scion of Kakutstha, and grant my prayer as well as that of your mother, Kausalyā. (10)

verses.text:
रक्षितुं सुमहद् राज्यमहमेकस्तु नोत्सहे।
पौरजानपदांश्चापि रक्तान् रञ्जयितुं तदा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I for my part cannot protect the vast dominion single-handed, nor can I please the citizens and the people of the countryside, so devoted to you. (11)

verses.text:
ज्ञातयश्चापि योधाश्च मित्राणि सुहृदश्च नः।
त्वामेव हि प्रतीक्षन्ते पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Indeed our kinsmen, nay, warriors, friends and relations too wait for you alone as cultivators do for the rumbling cloud. (12)

verses.text:
इदं राज्यं महाप्राज्ञ स्थापय प्रतिपद्य हि।
शक्तिमान् स हि काकुत्स्थ लोकस्य परिपालने॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Accepting the kingdom, O highly intelligent brother, actually place it on a sound footing. Such as you are, you are capable of protecting the people on all sides, O scion of Kakutstha !” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वापतद् भ्रातुः पादयोर्भरतस्तदा।
भृशं सम्प्रार्थयामास राघवेऽतिप्रियं वदन्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying so, Bharata then fell at the feet of his elder brother and made a fervent appeal to him to accept the sovereignty, speaking in most endearing tones to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (14)

verses.text:
तमङ्के भ्रातरं कृत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्।
श्यामं नलिनपत्राक्षं मत्तहंसस्वरः स्वयम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Placing on his lap the aforesaid brother, Bharata, who was dark-brown of complexion and had eyes resembling the petals of a lotus, Śrī Rāma, who was himself endowed with a voice resembling the cackling of a swan in rut, replied to him as follows : (15)

verses.text:
आगता त्वामियं बुद्धिः स्वजा वैनयिकी च या।
भृशमुत्सहसे तात रक्षितुं पृथिवीमपि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “You can very well protect even the earth, to say nothing of Ayodhyā, through this innate wisdom in the shape of underestimation of your worth born of humility, that has dawned on you, my darling ! (16)

verses.text:
अमात्यैश्च सुहृद्भिश्च बुद्धिमद्भिश्च मन्त्रिभिः।
सर्वकार्याणि सम्मन्त्र्य महान्त्यपि हि कारय॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nay, coolly deliberating with your ministers, friends and wise counsellors too, get through even your major concerns. (17)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद् वा हिमवान् वा हिमं त्यजेत्।
अतीयात् सागरो वेलां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Splendour would sooner depart from the moon, nay, the Himalaya mountain would sooner shed its snow and the ocean would sooner transgress its limits than I shall violate the plighted word of my father. (18)

verses.text:
कामाद् वा तात लोभाद् वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्।
न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “No matter whether all this was wrought by your mother in your interest from affection for you or from greed of sovereignty through your installation as Prince-Regent, my darling, it should not be taken to heart by you and you should behave towards her as towards a mother.” (19)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं भरतः कौसल्यासुतमब्रवीत्।
तेजसाऽऽदित्यसंकाशं प्रतिपच्चन्द्रदर्शनम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: To Śrī Rāma, the son of Kausalyā—who was speaking as aforesaid, nay, who vied with the sun in glory, and who was pleasing to the sight as the new moon appearing on the first day of a bright fortnight—Bharata replied as follows : (20)

verses.text:
अधिरोहार्य पादाभ्यां पादुके हेमभूषिते।
एते हि सर्वलोकस्य योगक्षेमं विधास्यतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Pray, stand with your feet on the pair of wooden sandals embellished with gold placed before you, O noble brother ! Surely these will supply the needs and ensure the safety of men.” (21)

verses.text:
सोऽधिरुह्य नरव्याघ्रः पादुके व्यवमुच्य च।
प्रायच्छत् सुमहातेजा भरताय महात्मने॥ २२॥
verses.m: Placing his feet on the sandals and immediately leaving them, Śrī Rāma, a tiger among men, who was endowed with exceptional glory, gave them to the high-souled Bharata. (22)

verses.text:
स पादुके सम्प्रणम्य रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि जटाचीरधरो ह्यहम्॥ २३॥
फलमूलाशनो वीर भवेयं रघुनन्दन।
तवागमनमाकांक्षन् वसन् वै नगराद् बहिः॥ २४॥
तव पादुकयोर्न्यस्य राज्यतन्त्रं परंतप।
चतुर्दशे हि सम्पूर्णे वर्षेऽहनि रघूत्तम॥ २५॥
न द्रक्ष्यामि यदि त्वां तु प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्।
तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय तं परिष्वज्य सादरम्॥ २६॥
शत्रुघ्नं च परिष्वज्य वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।
मातरं रक्ष कैकेयीं मा रोषं कुरु तां प्रति॥ २७॥
verses.m: Reverentially bowing down to the wooden sandals, he spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma : “Indeed, having relegated the burden of rulership to the wooden sandals, O gallant brother, I should like to live on fruits and roots alone for fourteen years, O delight of the Raghus, wearing matted locks on my head and the bark of trees on my person and actually dwelling outside the city, longing for your return to the capital, O scorcher of enemies ! If, however, when the fourteenth year of your exile has fully ended, O jewel among the Raghus, I do not see you returned to Ayodhyā, the following day, I for my part shall enter the fire once for all.” Giving his approval in the words “So be it !” and embracing Bharata with love, nay, embracing Śatrughna as well, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows : “Take care of mother Kaikeyī; be not angry with her. (23—27)

verses.text:
मया च सीतया चैव शप्तोऽसि रघुनन्दन।
इत्युक्त्वाश्रुपरीताक्षो भ्रातरं विससर्ज ह॥ २८॥
verses.m: “You are hereby adjured to do so by me as well as by Sītā, O delight of the Raghus !” Saying so, his eyes suffused with tears, Śrī Rāma bade good-bye to Bharata. (28)

verses.text:
स पादुके ते भरतः स्वलंकृते
महोज्ज्वले सम्परिगृह्य धर्मवित्।
प्रदक्षिणं चैव चकार राघवं
चकार चैवोत्तमनागमूर्धनि॥ २९॥
verses.m: Receiving with reverence the aforesaid pair of exceedingly bright-ornate wooden sandals, the celebrated Bharata, who knew what is right, went clockwise round Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, and further placed the pair of sandals on the head of an excellent elephant. (29)

verses.text:
अथानुपूर्व्या प्रतिपूज्य तं जनं
गुरूंश्च मन्त्रीन् प्रकृतीस्तथानुजौ।
व्यसर्जयद् राघववंशवर्धनः
स्थितः स्वधर्मे हिमवानिवाचलः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Then, paying respects in the order of precedence to all those men who had gathered there as well as to his preceptors, counsellors, subjects and two younger brothers, Bharata and Śatrughna, who were going to Ayodhyā, Śrī Rāma, the promoter of Raghu’s race, who stood by his duty unshaken like the Himalaya mountain, bade them goodbye. (30)

verses.text:
तं मातरो बाष्पगृहीतकण्ठ्यो
दुःखेन नामन्त्रयितुं हि शेकुः।
स चैव मातॄरभिवाद्य सर्वा
रुदन् कुटीं स्वां प्रविवेश रामः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: His mothers, whose throat was choked with tears through agony, could not even speak to him. Greeting all his mothers, the celebrated Śrī Rāma too re-entered his hut weeping. (31)

verses.text:
ततः शिरसि कृत्वा तु पादुके भरतस्तदा।
आरुरोह रथं हृष्टः शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: Then, placing the pair of wooden sandals on his head, Bharata for his part, full of joy and accompanied by Śatrughna, forthwith ascended the chariot. (1)

verses.text:
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिश्च दृढव्रतः।
अग्रतः प्रययुः सर्वे मन्त्रिणो मन्त्रपूजिताः॥ २॥
verses.m: The counsellors, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and Jābāli of steadfast vows and all others, adored for their sage counsel, travelled in the forefront. (2)

verses.text:
मन्दाकिनीं नदीं रम्यां प्राङ्मुखास्ते ययुस्तदा।
प्रदक्षिणं च कुर्वाणाश्चित्रकूटं महागिरिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Keeping the lovely river Mandākinī and the great Citrakūṭa mountain to their right they then departed with their face turned towards the east. (3)

verses.text:
पश्यन् धातुसहस्राणि रम्याणि विविधानि च।
प्रययौ तस्य पार्श्वेन ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing on the way thousands of minerals of every description, which were charming too, Bharata, accompanied by his army, now proceeded along the (northern) side of the aforesaid mountain. (4)

verses.text:
अदूराच्चित्रकूटस्य ददर्श भरतस्तदा।
आश्रमं यत्र स मुनिर्भरद्वाजः कृतालयः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Not far from Citrakūṭa. Bharata now beheld the hermitage in which Sage Bharadwāja had taken up his abode.* (5)

verses.text:
स तमाश्रममागम्य भरद्वाजस्य वीर्यवान्।
अवतीर्य रथात् पादौ ववन्दे कुलनन्दनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Reaching the said hermitage of Bharadwāja and alighting from his chariot, the valiant Bharata, the delight of his race, saluted the sage’s feet. (6)

verses.text:
ततो हृष्टो भरद्वाजो भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
अपि कृत्यं कृतं तात रामेण च समागतम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Full of delight, Bharadwāja thereupon spoke to Bharata as follows : “Did you meet Śrī Rāma, my darling, and has your purpose been accomplished?” (7)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः स तु ततो भरद्वाजेन धीमता।
प्रत्युवाच भरद्वाजं भरतो धर्मवत्सलः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Questioned thus by the wise Bharadwāja, the celebrated Bharata for his part, who was lovingly devoted to righteousness, then replied to Bharadwāja as follows : (8)

verses.text:
स याच्यमानो गुरुणा मया च दृढविक्रमः।
राघवः परमप्रीतो वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Supremely delighted on being solicited by my preceptor and myself to return to Ayodhyā, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, of unrelenting prowess replied to Vasiṣṭha as follows : (9)

verses.text:
पितुः प्रतिज्ञां तामेव पालयिष्यामि तत्त्वतः।
चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि या प्रतिज्ञा पितुर्मम॥ १०॥
verses.m: “ ‘I shall without doubt unequivocally implement that pledge of my father given to my mother Kaikeyī, which was to the effect that I should actually remain in exile for fourteen years.’ (10)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो महाप्राज्ञो वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह।
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं राघवं वचनं महत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Spoken to as aforesaid, the highly enlightened Vasiṣṭha, who knows how to speak, actually addressed the following momentous words to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, who is an adept in expression : (11)

verses.text:
एते प्रयच्छ संहृष्टः पादुके हेमभूषिते।
अयोध्यायां महाप्राज्ञ योगक्षेमकरो भव॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Full of great delight, please gift these wooden sandals decked with gold to Bharata. Existing in the form of these sandals, supply the needs of the people in Ayodhyā and safeguard their interests, O highly intelligent prince !’ (12)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन राघवः प्राङ्मुखः स्थितः।
पादुके हेमविकृते मम राज्याय ते ददौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Requested in these words by Vasiṣṭha, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) stood on the sandals facing the east and allowed me to take the aforesaid pair of wooden sandals, adorned with gold, for carrying on the rule (on his behalf). (13)

verses.text:
निवृत्तोऽहमनुज्ञातो रामेण सुमहात्मना।
अयोध्यामेव गच्छामि गृहीत्वा पादुके शुभे॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Departed, as permitted by the exceptionally high-souled Śrī Rāma, I am returning to Ayodhyā itself taking the blessed pair of sandals with me.” (14)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः।
भरद्वाजः शुभतरं मुनिर्वाक्यमुदाहरत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Hearing this happy report of the high-souled Bharata, Sage Bharadwāja made the following reply, which was still more agreeable to hear : (15)

verses.text:
नैतच्चित्रं नरव्याघ्रे शीलवृत्तविदां वरे।
यदार्यं त्वयि तिष्ठेत्तु निम्नोत्सृष्टमिवोदकम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “It is no wonder that, even as water discharged from above collects into a depression, noble conduct for its part should find its place in you, a tiger among men and the foremost of those who know how to behave well and conduct themselves with propriety. (16)

verses.text:
अनृणः स महाबाहुः पिता दशरथस्तव।
यस्य त्वमीदृशः पुत्रो धर्मात्मा धर्मवत्सलः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Free from all debt is your mighty-armed father, the celebrated Daśaratha, of whom was born such a pious son as you, fondly devoted to virtue.” (17)

verses.text:
तमृषिं तु महाप्राज्ञमुक्तवाक्यं कृताञ्जलिः।
आमन्त्रयितुमारेभे चरणावुपगृह्य च॥ १८॥
verses.m: Bharata for his part stood with folded hands before the highly wise Ṛṣi, Sage Bharadwāja, who had spoken as above, and clasping his feet, proceeded to take leave of him. (18)

verses.text:
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा भरद्वाजं पुनः पुनः।
भरतस्तु ययौ श्रीमानयोध्यां सह मन्त्रिभिः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Going clockwise round Bharadwāja as a mark of respect, again and again, the glorious Bharata for his part then left for Ayodhyā alongwith his counsellors. (19)

verses.text:
यानैश्च शकटैश्चैव हयैर्नागैश्च सा चमूः।
पुनर्निवृत्ता विस्तीर्णा भरतस्यानुयायिनी॥ २०॥
verses.m: That large army following Bharata returned along the same route on chariots and bullock-carts as well as on horseback and on the back of elephants. (20)

verses.text:
ततस्ते यमुनां दिव्यां नदीं तीर्त्वोर्मिमालिनीम्।
ददृशुस्तां पुनः सर्वे गङ्गां शिवजलां नदीम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having crossed the divine river, Yamunā, adorned with a succession of waves, they all then beheld once more the river Gaṅgā, containing holy waters. (21)

verses.text:
तां रम्यजलसम्पूर्णां संतीर्य सहबान्धवः।
शृङ्गवेरपुरं रम्यं प्रविवेश ससैनिकः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having easily crossed with his kinsfolk the aforesaid river, which was brimful with delightful waters, Bharata, with his army men, duly entered the lovely town of Śṛngaverapura. (22)

verses.text:
शृङ्गवेरपुराद् भूय अयोध्यां संददर्श ह।
अयोध्यां तु तदा दृष्ट्वा पित्रा भ्रात्रा विवर्जिताम्॥ २३॥
भरतो दुःखसंतप्तः सारथिं चेदमब्रवीत्।
सारथे पश्य विध्वस्ता अयोध्या न प्रकाशते॥ २४॥
निराकारा निरानन्दा दीना प्रतिहतस्वना॥ २५॥
verses.m: Proceeding from Śṛngaverapura he vividly saw Ayodhyā once more: so the tradition goes. Seeing Ayodhyā deserted by his father and elder brother, Śrī Rāma, Bharata for his part felt sore stricken with agony at that moment and spoke as follows to the charioteer Sumantra : “Look, O charioteer ! Desolate and shorn of its grace, bereft of joy, wretched and lifeless, Ayodhyā does not look bright as before.” (23—25)

verses.text:
स्निग्धगम्भीरघोषेण स्यन्दनेनोपयान् प्रभुः।
अयोध्यां भरतः क्षिप्रं प्रविवेश महायशाः॥ १॥
verses.m: Journeying forth in a chariot which produced an agreeable deep sound, the powerful and highly illustrious Bharata duly entered Ayodhyā in no time. (1)

verses.text:
बिडालोलूकचरितामालीननरवारणाम्।
तिमिराभ्याहतां कालीमप्रकाशां निशामिव॥ २॥
verses.m: Haunted by cats and owls, obscured by darkness and devoid of light, with the house doors of its men closed, the city presented the appearance of a dark night. (2)

verses.text:
राहुशत्रोः प्रियां पत्नीं श्रिया प्रज्वलितप्रभाम्।
ग्रहेणाभ्युदितेनैकां रोहिणीमिव पीडिताम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: It looked desolate like Rohiṇī, the beloved consort of the moon-god (treated as an enemy by the demon Rāhu*), tormented in the form of her spouse whose better half she is by the planet Rāhu in the ascendant, though ordinarily invested with an exceedingly bright splendour by virtue of her glory. (3)

verses.text:
अल्पोष्णक्षुब्धसलिलां घर्मतप्तविहंगमाम्।
लीनमीनझषग्राहां कृशां गिरिनदीमिव॥ ४॥
verses.m: It further looked attenuated like a mountain-stream whose scanty waters had become hot and agitated due to the rays of the sun, birds living in which were scorched by the sun and whose fish, small and big, and alligators had disappeared into the mire. (4)

verses.text:
विधूमामिव हेमाभां शिखामग्नेः समुत्थिताम्।
हविरभ्युक्षितां पश्चाच्छिखां विप्रलयं गताम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: It resembled a fully developed tongue of fire, devoid of smoke and bright as gold, later reduced to extinction when sprinkled all over with milk. (5)

verses.text:
विध्वस्तकवचां रुग्णगजवाजिरथध्वजाम्।
हतप्रवीरामापन्नां चमूमिव महाहवे॥ ६॥
verses.m: It looked like an army which had met with reverses in a major conflict—whose armours had been shattered, whose ensigns borne on elephants, horses and chariots had been torn and whose foremost heroes had been killed. (6)

verses.text:
सफेनां सस्वनां भूत्वा सागरस्य समुत्थिताम्।
प्रशान्तमारुतोद्धूतां जलोर्मिमिव निःस्वनाम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: It presented the appearance of an oceanic wave which, though tossed very high by a strong gale with foam and a roar, is rendered noiseless when stirred by a quiet wind. (7)

verses.text:
त्यक्तां यज्ञायुधैः सर्वैरभिरूपैश्च याजकैः।
सुत्याकाले सुनिर्वृत्ते वेदिं गतरवामिव॥ ८॥
verses.m: It resembled an altar which, when the period of offering oblations into the sacred fire has completely expired, has been cleared * The demon presiding over a planet of the same name figuring in Indian astronomy and identified of all sacrificial implements and deserted by the learned priests, and where all sound has consequently ceased. (8)

verses.text:
गोष्ठमध्ये स्थितामार्तामचरन्तीं नवं तृणम्।
गोवृषेण परित्यक्तां गवां पत्नीमिवोत्सुकाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: It looked like a cow fit to be coveted by bulls and longing for copulation but bereft of an excellent bull and standing disconsolate in a cow-pen, refusing to feed on fresh grass. (9)

verses.text:
प्रभाकराद्यैः सुस्निग्धैः प्रज्वलद्भिरिवोत्तमैः।
वियुक्तां मणिभिर्जात्यैर्नवां मुक्तावलीमिव॥ १०॥
verses.m: It further resembled a new necklace of pearls stripped of its highly polished, dazzling, excellent rubies and other gems of superior quality. (10)

verses.text:
सहसाचरितां स्थानान्महीं पुण्यक्षयाद् गताम्।
संहृतद्युतिविस्तारां तारामिव दिवश्च्युताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Again, it presented the appearance of a meteor suddenly shifted from its position and fallen from the heavens, and consequently shorn of its expanse of light when descended on earth through exhaustion of its merit. (11)

verses.text:
पुष्पनद्धां वसन्तान्ते मत्तभ्रमरशालिनीम्।
द्रुतदावाग्निविप्लुष्टां क्लान्तां वनलतामिव॥ १२॥
verses.m: It further looked blighted in appearance like a forest creeper laden with blossom at the close of spring and appearing lovely with drunken bees surrounding it but later on scorched by a raging wild fire. (12)

verses.text:
सम्मूढनिगमां सर्वां संक्षिप्तविपणापणाम्।
प्रच्छन्नशशिनक्षत्रां द्यामिवाम्बुधरैर्युताम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: The entire city with its trafficless streets and markets carrying on a dull business resembled a cloudy sky with the moon and other stars obscured. (13)

verses.text:
क्षीणपानोत्तमैर्भग्नैः शरावैरभिसंवृताम्।
हतशौण्डामिव ध्वस्तां पानभूमिमसंस्कृताम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: With its streets and lanes unswept and full of rubbish, Ayodhyā presented the appearance of a deserted and uncleaned tavern strewn with broken vessels devoid of any excellent liquor, the wine-drinkers having been killed. (14)

verses.text:
वृक्णभूमितलां निम्नां वृक्णपात्रैः समावृताम्।
उपयुक्तोदकां भग्नां प्रपां निपतितामिव॥ १५॥
verses.m: Again it looked like a shed erected for storage and distribution of water, but now broken and collapsed with its platform razed and sunk, and covered with broken vessels, its water having been used up. (15)

verses.text:
विपुलां विततां चैव युक्तपाशां तरस्विनाम्।
भूमौ बाणैर्विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां ज्यामिवायुधात्॥ १६॥
verses.m: It further resembled a bow-string, broad and long (extended over the entire length of a bow) with a noose at both ends in order to fasten it to the bow, severed from the bow by the arrows of heroes and fallen to the ground. (16)

verses.text:
सहसा युद्धशौण्डेन हयारोहेण वाहिताम्।
निहतां प्रतिसैन्येन वडवामिव पातिताम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: It further resembled a mare spurred on precipitately by a horseman, skilled in warfare, and fallen down when killed by the opposite army. (17)

verses.text:
भरतस्तु रथस्थः सन् श्रीमान् दशरथात्मजः।
वाहयन्तं रथश्रेष्ठं सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Seated in his chariot, the glorious Bharata, son of Daśaratha, for his part, spoke as follows to the charioteer, Sumantra, who was driving the foremost of the king’s chariot : (18)

verses.text:
किं नु खल्वद्य गम्भीरो मूर्च्छितो न निशाम्यते।
यथापुरमयोध्यायां गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “How is it, I wonder, that the deep and resonant sound of vocal and instrumental music is not heard as before in Ayodhyā today? (19)

verses.text:
वारुणीमदगन्धश्च माल्यगन्धश्च मूर्च्छितः।
चन्दनागुरुगन्धश्च न प्रवाति समन्ततः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The intoxicating fragrance of spirituous liquor, the scent of flowers and the odour of sandalwood and aloewood, which once used to be spread on all sides, is not being wafted. (20)

verses.text:
यानप्रवरघोषश्च सुस्निग्धहयनिःस्वनः।
प्रमत्तगजनादश्च महांश्च रथनिःस्वनः॥ २१॥
नेदानीं श्रूयते पुर्यामस्यां रामे विवासिते।
चन्दनागुरुगन्धांश्च महार्हाश्च वनस्रजः॥ २२॥
गते रामे हि तरुणाः संतप्ता नोपभुञ्जते।
बहिर्यात्रां न गच्छन्ति चित्रमाल्यधरा नराः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma having been sent into exile, neither the noise of the foremost of chariots nor the most delightful neighing of horses, neither the trumpeting of highly excited elephants nor the great noise of chariots is heard in this city now. Sore distressed on Śrī Rāma having departed from Ayodhyā, indeed, young men here no longer use the paste of aloewood and sandalwood nor costly garlands of sylvan flowers to cool their body with; nor do men go out for excursion wearing wreaths of various flowers. (21—23)

verses.text:
नोत्सवाः सम्प्रवर्तन्ते रामशोकार्दिते पुरे।
सा हि नूनं मम भ्रात्रा पुरस्यास्य द्युतिर्गता॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Festivities no longer duly proceed in the capital, stricken, as it is, with grief caused by separation from Śrī Rāma; the former splendour of this city has, truly speaking, undoubtedly departed with my elder brother, Śrī Rāma. (24)

verses.text:
नहि राजत्ययोध्येयं सासारेवार्जुनी क्षपा।
कदा नु खलु मे भ्राता महोत्सव इवागतः॥ २५॥
जनयिष्यत्ययोध्यायां हर्षं ग्रीष्म इवाम्बुदः।
तरुणैश्चारुवेषैश्च नरैरुन्नतगामिभिः॥ २६॥
सम्पतद्भिरयोध्यायां नाभिभान्ति महापथाः।
इति ब्रुवन् सारथिना दुःखितो भरतस्तदा॥ २७॥
अयोध्यां सम्प्रविश्यैव विवेश वसतिं पितुः।
तेन हीनां नरेन्द्रेण सिंहहीनां गुहामिव॥ २८॥
verses.m: “This Ayodhyā, with tears flowing from the eyes of its citizens, does not look charming any more than the night of a bright fortnight, with a continuous shower. Oh, when will my elder brother, returned to Ayodhyā like a great festival, bring forth joy in Ayodhyā like a rainy cloud in summer? The highways no longer shine forth with youngmen, clad in an attractive garb and walking with a proud gait, pouring into Ayodhyā from outside.” Immediately on penetrating into the heart of Ayodhyā, Bharata, who was talking in the above strain with his charioteer, Sumantra, at that time, stricken as he was with agony, entered his father’s palace, which looked desolate like a cave without a lion, bereft as it was of that ruler of men. (25—28)

verses.text:
तदा तदन्तःपुरमुज्झितप्रभं
सुरैरिवोत्कृष्टमभास्करं दिनम्।
निरीक्ष्य सर्वत्र विभक्तमात्मवान्
मुमोच बाष्पं भरतः सुदुःखितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Sore distressed to gaze at that moment on the well-known gynaeceum—which, having shed its splendour, resembled a day without the sun, bewailed by gods*, and was untidy everywhere, Bharata, who though self-possessed, shed tears. (29) * The commentators refer here to a story in the Purāṇas, according to which, in the course of the

verses.text:
ततो निक्षिप्य मातॄस्ता अयोध्यायां दृढव्रतः।
भरतः शोकसंतप्तो गुरूनिदमथाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having brought his celebrated mothers back to Ayodhyā, Bharata of steadfast vows, sore stricken with grief as he was, then submitted to his preceptors (Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva and others) forthwith as follows : (1)

verses.text:
नन्दिग्रामं गमिष्यामि सर्वानामन्त्रयेऽत्र वः।
तत्र दुःखमिदं सर्वं सहिष्ये राघवं विना॥ २॥
verses.m: “I take leave of you all here: I shall at once proceed to Nandigrāma. Bereft of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, I shall endure all this suffering there. (2)

verses.text:
गतश्चाहो दिवं राजा वनस्थः स गुरुर्मम।
रामं प्रतीक्षे राज्याय स हि राजा महायशाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Alas, the king has ascended to heaven and that elder brother of mine has taken up his abode in the forest. I look forward to Śrī Rāma to take care of the kingdom; for he is the highly illustrious ruler of Ayodhyā.” (3)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः।
अब्रुवन् मन्त्रिणः सर्वे वसिष्ठश्च पुरोहितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing this blessed utterance of the high-souled Bharata, all his counsellors as well as Vasiṣṭha, the chief family-priest, replied as follows : (4)

verses.text:
सुभृशं श्लाघनीयं च यदुक्तं भरत त्वया।
वचनं भ्रातृवात्सल्यादनुरूपं तवैव तत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The statement that has been made by you through loving devotion to your elder brother is extremely laudable; nay, it is worthy of you alone. (5)

verses.text:
नित्यं ते बन्धुलुब्धस्य तिष्ठतो भ्रातृसौहृदे।
मार्गमार्यं प्रपन्नस्य नानुमन्येत कः पुमान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “What man would not approve of the resolution of Your Royal Highness, who are ever covetous of the welfare of your kinsmen and are steadfast in your affection for your brothers, nay, who have taken to the noble path, the path of virtue?” (6)

verses.text:
मन्त्रिणां वचनं श्रुत्वा यथाभिलषितं प्रियम्।
अब्रवीत् सारथिं वाक्यं रथो मे युज्यतामिति॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing the agreeable reply of the counsellors, which was in consonance with his desire, Bharata spoke as follows to the charioteer, Sumantra : “Let my chariot be got ready !” (7)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टवदनः सर्वा मातृः समभिभाष्य च।
आरुरोह रथं श्रीमान्शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having spoken kindly with a most cheerful countenance, to all his mothers and accompanied by Śatrughna, the glorious prince got into the chariot. (8)

verses.text:
आरुह्य तु रथं क्षिप्रं शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ।
ययतुः परमप्रीतौ वृतौ मन्त्रिपुरोहितैः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Mounting the chariot, supremely delighted and surrounded by the counsellors and family priests, both Bharata and Śatrughna for their part quickly departed. (9)

verses.text:
अग्रतो गुरवः सर्वे वसिष्ठप्रमुखा द्विजाः।
प्रययुः प्राङ्मुखाः सर्वे नन्दिग्रामो यतो भवेत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: All the preceptors, headed by Vasiṣṭha, and other Brāhmaṇas being in the forefront, all proceeded with their face turned eastward on the path by which Nandigrāma could be reached. (10)

verses.text:
बलं च तदनाहूतं गजाश्वरथसंकुलम्।
प्रययौ भरते याते सर्वे च पुरवासिनः॥ ११॥
verses.m: When Bharata had left, the army too, full of elephants, horses and chariots, marched, though not called by Bharata, as well as the citizens. (11)

verses.text:
रथस्थः स तु धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः।
नन्दिग्रामं ययौ तूर्णं शिरस्यादाय पादुके॥ १२॥
verses.m: Seated in his chariot, the celebrated Bharata, for his part, whose mind was given to piety and who was so lovingly devoted to his elder brother, drove fast to Nandigrāma, taking the pair of wooden sandals on his head. (12)

verses.text:
भरतस्तु ततः क्षिप्रं नन्दिग्रामं प्रविश्य सः।
अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णं गुरूनिदमभाषत॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having speedily entered Nandigrāma and quickly alighting from his chariot, the said Bharata for his part then submitted to his preceptors as follows : (13)

verses.text:
एतद् राज्यं मम भ्रात्रा दत्तं संन्यासमुत्तमम्।
योगक्षेमवहे चेमे पादुके हेमभूषिते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “This kingdom has been given to me by my elder brother, Śrī Rāma, as a foremost sacred trust, as well as these wooden sandals decked with gold, which will supply all our needs and bring security to us.” (14)

verses.text:
भरतः शिरसा कृत्वा संन्यासं पादुके ततः।
अब्रवीद् दुःखसंतप्तः सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having dedicated the sacred trust to the pair of wooden sandals with his head bent low, Bharata, who was sore stricken with agony, then spoke as follows to the entire body of his ministers : (15)

verses.text:
छत्रं धारयत क्षिप्रमार्यपादाविमौ मतौ।
आभ्यां राज्ये स्थितो धर्मः पादुकाभ्यां गुरोर्मम॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Hold the royal umbrella over these sandals; they are considered by me to be as good as the feet of my elder brother. By these wooden sandals of my elder brother will righteousness be established in the kingdom. (16)

verses.text:
भ्रात्रा तु मयि संन्यासो निक्षिप्तः सौहृदादयम्।
तमिमं पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनं प्रति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “From affection alone has this sacred trust been committed to my charge by my elder brother. I shall keep this aforesaid trust till the return of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (17)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं संयोजयित्वा तु राघवस्य पुनः स्वयम्।
चरणौ तौ तु रामस्य द्रक्ष्यामि सहपादुकौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having undoubtedly restored these wooden sandals to Śrī Rāma’s feet immediately on his return to the capital myself, I for my part shall behold those feet placed on the wooden sandals. (18)

verses.text:
ततो निक्षिप्तभारोऽहं राघवेण समागतः।
निवेद्य गुरवे राज्यं भजिष्ये गुरुवर्तिताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Having restored the kingdom to my elder brother, when re-united with Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, and thereby laid down the burden of responsibility, I shall then assume the role of a servant of my elder brother. (19)

verses.text:
राघवाय च संन्यासं दत्त्वेमे वरपादुके।
राज्यं चेदमयोध्यां च धूतपापो भवाम्यहम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, having given back to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, this kingdom, held as a trust till then, as well as the city of Ayodhyā and the pair of excellent wooden sandals, I shall have shaken off the stigma of having been instrumental in bringing about the exile of my elder brother. (20)

verses.text:
अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्स्थे प्रहृष्टमुदिते जने।
प्रीतिर्मम यशश्चैव भवेद् राज्याच्चतुर्गुणम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “After Śrī Rama, descendant of the Kakutstha lineage, is coronated on the throne and the subjects are blissfully happy, it will give me fourfold more fame and happiness than that from having obtained the kingdom.” (21)

verses.text:
एवं तु विलपन् दीनो भरतः स महायशाः।
नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद् राज्यं दुःखितो मन्त्रिभिः सह॥ २२॥
verses.m: Lamenting this way the dispirited Bharata of great fame, even though sad, looked after the state administration alongwith the council of ministers from Nandigrāma. (22)

verses.text:
स वल्कलजटाधारी मुनिवेषधरः प्रभुः।
नन्दिग्रामेऽवसद् धीरः ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Wearing the bark of trees on his person and matted locks on his head and thus assuming the garb of an ascetic, the said powerful and wise Bharata then lived at Nandigrāma with the army; (23)

verses.text:
रामागमनमाकांक्षन् भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः।
भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तदा।
पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत् तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Bharata, obedient to his elder brother, fulfiller of his vows, lover of his brothers, wishing always the return of Śrī Rāma, lived in Nandigrāma after coronating the wooden-sandals on the throne. (24)

verses.text:
सवालव्यजनं छत्रं धारयामास स स्वयम्।
भरतः शासनं सर्वं पादुकाभ्यां निवेदयन्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Committing the whole administration to the care of the wooden sandals, the celebrated Bharata himself held the royal umbrella alongwith the Chowrie over them as a mark of respect. (25)

verses.text:
ततस्तु भरतः श्रीमानभिषिच्यार्यपादुके।
तदधीनस्तदा राज्यं कारयामास सर्वदा॥ २६॥
verses.m: Having then consecrated the wooden sandals of his elder brother on the throne of Ayodhyā, the glorious Bharata for his part now carried on the rule, being always subordinate to them. (26)

verses.text:
तदा हि यत् कार्यमुपैति किंचि-
दुपायनं चोपहृतं महार्हम्।
स पादुकाभ्यां प्रथमं निवेद्य
चकार पश्चाद् भरतो यथावत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Submitting in the first instance to the wooden sandals whatever affair of the State came up before him, nay, whatever highly valuable present was offered to the State, the said Bharata dealt with it in the proper way afterwards. (27)

verses.text:
प्रतियाते तु भरते वसन् रामस्तदा वने।
लक्षयामास सोद्वेगमथौत्सुक्यं तपस्विनाम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Living in the forest when Bharata had returned to Ayodhyā, Śrī Rāma for his part forthwith noticed during that period anxiety accompanied by perturbation among the ascetics. (1)

verses.text:
ये तत्र चित्रकूटस्य पुरस्तात् तापसाश्रमे।
राममाश्रित्य निरतास्तानलक्षयदुत्सुकान्॥ २॥
verses.m: He perceived the ascetics, who looked formerly quite pleased in that hermitage at Citrakūṭa, depending, as they did, on Śrī Rāma, anxious. (2)

verses.text:
नयनैर्भ्रुकुटीभिश्च रामं निर्दिश्य शङ्किताः।
अन्योन्यमुपजल्पन्तः शनैश्चक्रुर्मिथः कथाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Making references to Śrī Rāma through the movements of their eyes and eyebrows and calling one another, full of misgiving, they whispered among themselves. (3)

verses.text:
तेषामौत्सुक्यमालक्ष्य रामस्त्वात्मनि शङ्कितः।
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमृषिं कुलपतिं ततः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Perceiving their anxiety, Śrī Rāma was filled with apprehension about himself and accordingly submitted with folded hands as follows to the Ṛṣi (a seer of Vedic Mantras) who presided over the hermitage : (4)

verses.text:
न कश्चिद् भगवन् किंचित् पूर्ववृत्तमिदं मयि।
दृश्यते विकृतं येन विक्रियन्ते तपस्विनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “I fear, O venerable sir, the conduct of my forefathers is not seen in me here, or there is some change for the worse in me, due to which the ascetics feel agitated. (5)

verses.text:
प्रमादाच्चरितं किंचित् कच्चिन्नावरजस्य मे।
लक्ष्मणस्यर्षिभिर्दृष्टं नानुरूपं महात्मनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I hope no lapse, unbecoming of an exalted soul, on the part of my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, has been detected by the sages. (6)

verses.text:
कच्चिच्छुश्रूषमाणा वः शुश्रूषणपरा मयि।
प्रमदाभ्युचितां वृत्तिं सीता युक्तां न वर्तते॥ ७॥
verses.m: “While attending on you, Sītā, who remains solely devoted to my service, does not, I am afraid, follow the conduct wholly worthy of a young lady and showing due respect to you.” (7)

verses.text:
अथर्षिर्जरया वृद्धस्तपसा च जरां गतः।
वेपमान इवोवाच रामं भूतदयापरम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: The Ṛṣi, who was not only worn out from age but had also attained ripeness through askesis, replied as follows, as though quaking, to Śrī Rāma, who regarded compassion for created beings as the highest virtue : (8)

verses.text:
कुतः कल्याणसत्त्वायाः कल्याणाभिरतेः सदा।
चलनं तात वैदेह्यास्तपस्विषु विशेषतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “How can there be any aberration, my darling, on the part of Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, who has a benign disposition and is ever devoted to goodness, particularly in her attitude towards ascetics? (9)

verses.text:
त्वन्निमित्तमिदं तावत् तापसान् प्रति वर्तते।
रक्षोभ्यस्तेन संविग्नाः कथयन्ति मिथः कथाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This peril from the Rākṣasas threatens the ascetics because of you, who are kindly disposed to the latter. Alarmed by it, they hold conversation among themselves. (10)

verses.text:
रावणावरजः कश्चित् खरो नामेह राक्षसः।
उत्पाट्य तापसान् सर्वाञ्जनस्थाननिवासिनः॥ ११॥
धृष्टश्च जितकाशी च नृशंसः पुरुषादकः।
अवलिप्तश्च पापश्च त्वां च तात न मृष्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Having uprooted all the ascetics in Janasthāna (a portion of the Daṇḍaka forest), a man-eating Rākṣasa, Khara by name—who is a younger brother of Rāvaṇa and is presumptuous, victorious in battle, brutal, haughty and sinful—is intolerant of you too, my darling ! (11-12)

verses.text:
त्वं यदाप्रभृति ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रमे तात वर्तसे।
तदाप्रभृति रक्षांसि विप्रकुर्वन्ति तापसान्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Ever since, O darling, you are in this hermitage, the ogres continue to ill-treat the ascetics. (13)

verses.text:
दर्शयन्ति हि बीभत्सैः क्रूरैर्भीषणकैरपि।
नानारूपैर्विरूपैश्च रूपैरसुखदर्शनैः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “They reveal themselves in diverse odious, savage, hideous and ugly forms, whose very sight brings sorrow in its wake. (14)

verses.text:
अप्रशस्तैरशुचिभिः सम्प्रयुज्य च तापसान्।
प्रतिघ्नन्त्यपरान् क्षिप्रमनार्याः पुरतः स्थितान्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Nay, forcibly bringing the ascetics into touch with forbidden and impure substances, the ignoble fellows quickly dispose of others standing in front of them. (15)

verses.text:
तेषु तेष्वाश्रमस्थानेष्वबुद्धमवलीय च।
रमन्ते तापसांस्तत्र नाशयन्तोऽल्पचेतसः॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘They incognito hide themselves in this hermitage and killing the dull-witted and unconscious ascetics, move about there in glee. (16)

verses.text:
अवक्षिपन्ति स्रुग्भाण्डानग्नीन् सिञ्चन्ति वारिणा।
कलशांश्च प्रमर्दन्ति हवने समुपस्थिते॥ १७॥
verses.m: “When the time of pouring oblations into the sacred fire has approached, they fling away sacrificial vessels such as the ladle, sprinkle the fires with water and smash the water-pots. (17)

verses.text:
तैर्दुरात्मभिराविष्टानाश्रमान् प्रजिहासवः।
गमनायान्यदेशस्य चोदयन्त्यृषयोऽद्य माम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Desirous of leaving for good the hermitages defiled by those evil-minded fellows, the sages urge me to shift to another region today. (18)

verses.text:
तत् पुरा राम शारीरीमुपहिंसां तपस्विषु।
दर्शयन्ति हि दुष्टास्ते त्यक्ष्याम इममाश्रमम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O Rāma, we shall certainly abandon this hermitage before those wicked fellows exhibit bodily violence towards the ascetics. (19)

verses.text:
बहुमूलफलं चित्रमविदूरादितो वनम्।
अश्वस्याश्रममेवाहं श्रयिष्ये सगणः पुनः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I shall then resort with my followers to the hermitage of Sage Aśwa (lit., who does not lay by anything for the morrow), consisting of an excellent woodland abounding in roots and fruits, not very far from this place. (20)

verses.text:
खरस्त्वय्यपि चायुक्तं पुरा राम प्रवर्तते।
सहास्माभिरितो गच्छ यदि बुद्धिः प्रवर्तते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “If your mind feels so inclined, O Rāma, depart from this place alongwith us before Khara proceeds unjustly with you as well, O Rāma ! (21)

verses.text:
सकलत्रस्य संदेहो नित्यं युक्तस्य राघव।
समर्थस्यापि हि सतो वासो दुःखमिहाद्य ते॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Your continuance too at this place, O scion of Raghu, with your consort, although you are ever alert and even though you are powerful enough to put him down, is attended with peril and conducive to misery now.”(22)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तवन्तं रामस्तं राजपुत्रस्तपस्विनम्।
न शशाकोत्तरैर्वाक्यैरवबद्धुं समुत्सुकम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Prince Rāma could not with counter-arguments check the said ascetic when he had spoken as above, impatient as he was to leave the place. (23)

verses.text:
अभिनन्द्य समापृच्छ्य समाधाय च राघवम्।
स जगामाश्रमं त्यक्त्वा कुलैः कुलपतिः सह॥ २४॥
verses.m: Extolling, duly taking leave of and consoling Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the aforesaid leader of the sages departed with the hosts of sages, leaving the hermitage.(24)

verses.text:
रामः संसाध्य ऋषिगणमनुगमनाद्
देशात् तस्मात् कुलपतिमभिवाद्य ऋषिम्।
सम्यक्प्रीतैस्तैरनुमत उपदिष्टार्थः
पुण्यं वासाय स्वनिलयमुपसम्पेदे॥ २५॥
verses.m: Seeing off the multitude of sages from that area by following them to a distance, and greeting the Ṛṣi who presided over the entire host, nay, instructed by the sages about his duty, Śrī Rāma, when permitted by them, who were highly pleased with him, returned to his sacred dwelling for rest. (25)

verses.text:
आश्रममृषिविरहितं प्रभुः
क्षणमपि न जहौ स राघवः।
राघवं हि सततमनुगता-
स्तापसाश्चार्षचरिते धृतगुणाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: The powerful Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, referred to above, did not leave the hermitage, now bereft of the sages, even for a moment; while the ascetics, who had fixed their mind on Śrī Rāma, who followed the conduct of sages, constantly followed Śrī Rāma, with their mind. (26)

verses.text:
राघवस्त्वपयातेषु सर्वेष्वनुविचिन्तयन्।
न तत्रारोचयद् वासं कारणैर्बहुभिस्तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: Reflecting again and again, when all the ascetics had left, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part did not like to continue his stay there any more for many reasons. (1)

verses.text:
इह मे भरतो दृष्टो मातरश्च सनागराः।
सा च मे स्मृतिरन्वेति तान् नित्यमनुशोचतः॥ २॥
verses.m: “At this place was Bharata seen by me as well as my mothers with the people of Ayodhyā. Nay, that memory still haunts me, and I mourn for them daily. (2)

verses.text:
स्कन्धावारनिवेशेन तेन तस्य महात्मनः।
हयहस्तिकरीषैश्च उपमर्दः कृतो भृशम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Moreover much impurity has been caused to the land by the dry dung of horses and elephants due to the camping, referred to above, of the army of that high-souled prince, Bharata. (3)

verses.text:
तस्मादन्यत्र गच्छाम इति संचिन्त्य राघवः।
प्रातिष्ठत स वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च संगतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “We shall, therefore, move elsewhere !” Pondering thus, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, accompanied by Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, and Lakṣmaṇa, departed from Citrakūṭa. (4)

verses.text:
सोऽत्रेराश्रममासाद्य तं ववन्दे महायशाः।
तं चापि भगवानत्रिः पुत्रवत् प्रत्यपद्यत॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having reached the hermitage of Sage Atri, that highly illustrious prince saluted him; and the glorious Atri too received him as his own son. (5)

verses.text:
स्वयमातिथ्यमादिश्य सर्वमस्य सुसत्कृतम्।
सौमित्रिं च महाभागं सीतां च समसान्त्वयत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having personally shown every hospitality with full honours to him, he comforted the highly blessed Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā too. (6)

verses.text:
पत्नीं च तामनुप्राप्तां वृद्धामामन्त्र्य सत्कृताम्।
सान्त्वयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥ ७॥
अनसूयां महाभागां तापसीं धर्मचारिणीम्।
प्रतिगृह्णीष्व वैदेहीमब्रवीदृषिसत्तमः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Calling by name his aged and highly blessed wife, Anasūyā, who had reached his presence and was received with attentions by him, and who was given to austerities and the practice of virtue, Atri, the foremost of sages, who knew what is right and was devoted to the good of all created beings, spoke kindly to her, and said, “Welcome Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom.” (7-8)

verses.text:
रामाय चाचचक्षे तां तापसीं धर्मचारिणीम्।
दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्॥ ९ ॥
यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता।
उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलंकृता॥ १०॥
दश वर्षसहस्राणि यया तप्तं महत् तपः।
अनसूयाव्रतैस्तात प्रत्यूहाश्च निबर्हिताः॥ ११॥
देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया संत्वरमाणया।
दशरात्रं कृता रात्रिः सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ॥ १२॥
verses.m: He further introduced to Śrī Rāma as follows the aforesaid lady, who was given to austerities and the practice of virtue : “Like a mother to you, O sinless prince, is this celebrated Anasūyā, distinguished by severe asceticism and adorned with sacred vows, by whom roots and fruits were produced and the river Gaṅgā, a foster-daughter of the royal king Jahnu, was made to flow close to my hermitage by virtue of her asceticism at a time when the world had been dried up by a drought continuing for ten years without break, nay, by whom great askesis were practised for ten thousand years and obstacles in the way of Ṛṣis were done away with and by whom for the purpose* of gods in a great hurry ten nights were reduced to one night. (9—12)

verses.text:
तामिमां सर्वभूतानां नमस्कार्यां तपस्विनीम्।
अभिगच्छतु वैदेही वृद्धामक्रोधनां सदा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, meekly approach this celebrated * We read in the Purāṇas how Sage Māṇḍavya once pronounced a curse against a hermitess, Śāṇḍili and aged hermitess, who is worth saluting in the eyes of all created beings, and is ever free from anger.” (13)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं तथेत्युक्त्वा स राघवः।
सीतामालोक्य धर्मज्ञामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying “Amen!” to the aforesaid Ṛṣi, who was speaking in this strain and looking at Sītā, who knew what is right, the celebrated Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) addressed the following words to her : 14)

verses.text:
राजपुत्रि श्रुतं त्वेतन्मुनेरस्य समीरितम्।
श्रेयोऽर्थमात्मनः शीघ्रमभिगच्छ तपस्विनीम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The foregoing utterance of this sage has surely been heard by you, O princess! For your own good, therefore, quickly approach the hermitess with reverence. (15)

verses.text:
अनसूयेति या लोके कर्मभिः ख्यातिमागता।
तां शीघ्रमभिगच्छ त्वमभिगम्यां तपस्विनीम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Speedily seek you respectfully the ascetic lady, who is worth approaching with reverence and who has attained celebrity in the world through her actions under the name of Anasūyā (lit., free from jealousy).” (16)

verses.text:
सीता त्वेतद् वचः श्रुत्वा राघवस्य यशस्विनी।
तामत्रिपत्नीं धर्मज्ञामभिचक्राम मैथिली॥ १७॥
शिथिलां वलितां वृद्धां जरापाण्डुरमूर्धजाम्।
सततं वेपमानाङ्गीं प्रवाते कदलीमिव॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing this exhortation of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the illustrious Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, for her part proceeded to meet the celebrated and aged consort of Atri, who knew what is right, nay, who was feeble of body and wrinkled, with her hair turned grey due to old age, and whose frame constantly shook like a banana tree in a storm. (17-18)

verses.text:
तां तु सीता महाभागामनसूयां पतिव्रताम्।
अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रा स्वं नाम समुदाहरत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Sītā for her part calmly greeted the highly blessed Anasūyā, devoted to her husband, and duly uttered her own name by way of introduction. (19)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्य च वैदेही तापसीं तां दमान्विताम्।
बद्धाञ्जलिपुटा हृष्टा पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Nay, having greeted that hermitess, who was endowed with self-restraint, Sītā (a princess of the Videha kingdom), full of joy, enquired after her health with folded hands. (20)

verses.text:
ततः सीतां महाभागां दृष्ट्वा तां धर्मचारिणीम्।
सान्त्वयन्त्यब्रवीद् वृद्धा दिष्ट्या धर्ममवेक्षसे॥ २१॥
verses.m: Seeing the highly blessed and celebrated Sītā, who was given to the practice of virtue, the old lady, thereupon, comfortingly said to her, “Luckily enough, you have your eyes fixed on righteousness. (21)

verses.text:
त्यक्त्वा ज्ञातिजनं सीते मानवृद्धिं च मानिनि।
अवरुद्धं वने रामं दिष्ट्या त्वमनुगच्छसि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having forsaken your relations and given up your exaltation, O proud Sītā, I am glad, you are following your husband, Śrī Rāma, who has been exiled into the forest. (22)

verses.text:
नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा शुभो वा यदि वाशुभः।
यासां स्त्रीणां प्रियो भर्ता तासां लोका महोदयाः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Worlds that are attended with great prosperity await those women to whom their husband is dear, no matter whether he lives in a city or in a forest, whether he is propitious or adverse. (23)

verses.text:
दुःशीलः कामवृत्तो वा धनैर्वा परिवर्जितः।
स्त्रीणामार्यस्वभावानां परमं दैवतं पतिः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “In the eyes of women who are blessed with a noble disposition the husband is the highest deity, no matter whether he is ill-mannered or licentious or entirely devoid of riches. (24)

verses.text:
नातो विशिष्टं पश्यामि बान्धवं विमृशन्त्यहम्।
सर्वत्र योग्यं वैदेहि तपःकृतमिवाव्ययम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Though deeply pondering, I do not see for a woman a friend greater than the husband and more capable of yielding one’s desired object at all places like the imperishable fruit of one’s austerities, O princess of the Videha kingdom ! (25)

verses.text:
न त्वेवमनुगच्छन्ति गुणदोषमसत्स्त्रियः।
कामवक्तव्यहृदया भर्तृनाथाश्चरन्ति याः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Those evil women, however, whose hearts are swayed by desire, nay, who lord it over their husband, having no sense of virtue and vice, and move about at will, do not follow him in the aforesaid manner. (26)

verses.text:
प्राप्नुवन्त्ययशश्चैव धर्मभ्रंशं च मैथिलि।
अकार्यवशमापन्नाः स्त्रियो याः खलु तद्विधाः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Indeed, fallen a prey to concupiscence, which is worth giving up, women who belong to that category, O princess of Mithilā, meet with a fall from virtue and also reap infamy. (27)

verses.text:
त्वद्विधास्तु गुणैर्युक्ता दृष्टलोकपरावराः।
स्त्रियः स्वर्गे चरिष्यन्ति यथा पुण्यकृतस्तथा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Women like you, on the other hand, who are adorned with virtues like devotion to their husband and have discovered what is good and evil in the world, will hereafter dwell in heaven in the same way as those who have performed meritorious deeds. (28)

verses.text:
तदेवमेतं त्वमनुव्रता सती
पतिप्रधाना समयानुवर्तिनी।
भव स्वभर्तुः सहधर्मचारिणी
यशश्च धर्मं च ततः समाप्स्यसि॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Therefore, remaining devoted to the service of this prince, nay, looking upon your husband as the foremost object of your worship and attending on him at the proper time, practise virtue in co-operation with your husband. Thereby you will easily attain fame as well as religious merit.” (29) Thus end Canto One hundred and seventeen in the Ayodhyākāṇḍa of the glorious Rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, the work of a Ṛṣi and the oldest epic.

verses.text:
सा त्वेवमुक्ता वैदेही त्वनसूयानसूयया।
प्रतिपूज्य वचो मन्दं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ १॥
verses.m: Applauding her speech when instructed in the foregoing words by Anasūyā, Sītā, a princess of the Videha kingdom, for her part, who was free from the carping spirit, actually began slowly to reply as follows : (1)

verses.text:
नैतदाश्चर्यमार्यायां यन्मां त्वमनुभाषसे।
विदितं तु ममाप्येतद् यथा नार्याः पतिर्गुरुः॥ २॥
verses.m: “This instruction which you have given to me is no matter for wonder on Your Holiness’ part. It is, however, already known to me as well how the husband is the adored of a matron. (2)

verses.text:
यद्यप्येष भवेद् भर्ता अनार्यो वृत्तिवर्जितः।
अद्वैधमत्र वर्तव्यं यथाप्येष मया भवेत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Even if this husband of mine were ignoble and without any means of livelihood, I ought to have nonetheless conducted myself just in the same way without any hesitation or scruple towards him: this was my duty. (3)

verses.text:
किं पुनर्यो गुणश्लाघ्यः सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रियः।
स्थिरानुरागो धर्मात्मा मातृवत्पितृवत्प्रियः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “How much more worthy of devotion then is he who is deserving of praise by virtue of his excellences and full of compassion, nay, who has controlled all his senses including the mind, the inner sense, who is constant in his love, whose mind is set on righteousness and who is loving both as a mother and father combined ! (4)

verses.text:
यां वृत्तिं वर्तते रामः कौसल्यायां महाबलः।
तामेव नृपनारीणामन्यासामपि वर्तते॥ ५॥
